He cried out to the LORD, and the LORD showed him a piece of wood. He threw it into the water, and the water became sweet. There the LORD gave them a decree and a ruling, and there he tested them.

He said, "If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and do what is right in his eyes, if you pay attention to his commands and keep all his decrees, I will not bring on you any of the diseases I brought on the Egyptians, for I am the LORD who heals you."
Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there by the water.

They set out from Elim, and the whole community of the Israelites came to the wilderness of Sin, which is between Elim and Sinai, on the fifteenth day of the second month after they had come out of the land of Egypt.
In the wilderness the whole community of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron.

The Israelites said to them, "If only we had died by the hand of the LORD in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the pots of meat and ate all the bread we wanted! But you have brought us out into this wilderness to kill this whole assembly with hunger."

Then the LORD said to Moses, "I am going to rain down bread from heaven for you. The people are to go out each day and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test them, to see whether they will follow my instructions or not.
On the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on other days."
So Moses and Aaron said to all the Israelites, "This evening you will know that it was the LORD who brought you out of the land of Egypt,
and in the morning you will see the glory of the LORD, because he has heard your grumbling against the LORD. Who are we, that you grumble against us?"

Moses also said, "You will know it when the LORD gives you meat to eat in the evening and all the bread you want in the morning, because the LORD has heard the grumbling you are directing against him. Who are we? Your grumbling is not against us, but against the LORD."
Then Moses said to Aaron, "Say to the whole community of the Israelites, 'Come near before the LORD, for he has heard your grumbling.'"
While Aaron was speaking to the whole community of the Israelites, they turned toward the wilderness, and there was the glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud.
"I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites. Tell them, 'At twilight you will eat meat, and in the morning you will have your fill of bread. Then you will know that I am the LORD your God.'"
That evening quail came up and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
When the layer of dew had gone, there on the surface of the wilderness was something fine and flaky, as fine as frost on the ground.
When the Israelites saw it, they said to one another, "What is it?" For they did not know what it was. Moses said to them, "It is the bread that the LORD has given you to eat.
This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Each of you is to gather as much of it as he needs to eat, an omer for each person. Each of you is to take it for the number of people in his tent.'"
The Israelites did so. Some gathered more and some less.
When they measured it by the omer, those who had gathered much had nothing left over, and those who had gathered little did not have too little. Each had gathered as much as he needed to eat.
Moses said to them, "No one is to keep any of it until morning."
But they did not listen to Moses. Some of them kept part of it until morning, and it became full of maggots and began to stink. And Moses was angry with them.
Every morning each of them gathered as much as he needed to eat, and when the sun grew hot, it melted.
On the sixth day they gathered twice as much bread, two omers for each person. All the leaders of the community came and told Moses.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD said: 'Tomorrow is a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. Bake what you want to bake and boil what you want to boil, and set aside whatever is left over to be kept until morning.'"
So they set it aside until morning, as Moses had commanded, and it did not stink, and there were no maggots in it.
Moses said, "Eat it today, because today is a Sabbath to the LORD. Today you will not find any in the field.
For six days you are to gather it, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none."
Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather it, but they found none.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "How long will you all refuse to keep my commands and my instructions?
See, the LORD has given you the Sabbath. That is why on the sixth day he gives you bread for two days. Each of you is to stay where he is. No one is to leave his place on the seventh day."
So the people rested on the seventh day.
The house of Israel called it manna. It was like coriander seed, white, and it tasted like wafers made with honey.

Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded: 'Keep a full omer of it throughout your generations, so that they can see the bread I fed you in the wilderness when I brought you out of the land of Egypt.'"
So Moses said to Aaron, "Take a jar and put a full omer of manna in it. Then place it before the LORD, to be kept throughout your generations."
As the LORD had commanded Moses, Aaron placed it in front of the testimony, to be kept.
The Israelites ate manna for forty years, until they came to a land where people lived. They ate manna until they came to the border of the land of Canaan.
An omer is a tenth of an ephah.
The whole community of the Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sin, moving from place to place as the LORD commanded. They camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for the people to drink.
So the people quarreled with Moses and said, "Give us water to drink." Moses said to them, "Why are you quarreling with me? Why are you testing the LORD?"
But the people were thirsty for water there, and the people grumbled against Moses. They said, "Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to kill us and our children and our livestock with thirst?"
Then Moses cried out to the LORD, "What am I to do with this people? A little more and they will stone me!"
The LORD said to Moses, "Go on ahead of the people, and take some of the elders of Israel with you. Take in your hand the staff with which you struck the Nile, and go.
I will stand there in front of you on the rock at Horeb. Strike the rock, and water will come out of it, and the people will drink." Moses did so in the sight of the elders of Israel.
He named the place Massah and Meribah, because the Israelites quarreled and because they tested the LORD, saying, "Is the LORD among us or not?"
Then Amalek came and fought against Israel at Rephidim.
Moses said to Joshua, "Choose men for us, and go out and fight against Amalek. Tomorrow I will stand on the top of the hill with the staff of God in my hand."
Joshua did as Moses had told him and fought against Amalek, while Moses, Aaron and Hur went up to the top of the hill.
Whenever Moses held up his hand, Israel was winning, and whenever he lowered his hand, Amalek was winning.

When Moses' hands grew tired, they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other, so that his hands stayed steady until the sun went down.
So Joshua defeated Amalek and his army with the sword.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "Write this in a book to be remembered, and make sure that Joshua hears it: I will completely wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven."
Moses built an altar and named it The LORD Is My Banner.
He said, "A hand was raised against the throne of the LORD! The LORD will be at war with Amalek from generation to generation."
Jethro, the priest of Midian and Moses' father-in-law, heard about everything God had done for Moses and for his people Israel, how the LORD had brought Israel out of Egypt.
So Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, took Zipporah, Moses' wife, after Moses had sent her away,
and her two sons. One of them was named Gershom, for Moses said, "I have become a foreigner in a foreign land."
The other was named Eliezer, for he said, "The God of my father was my help; he rescued me from Pharaoh's sword."
Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came with Moses' sons and wife to Moses in the wilderness, where he was camped at the mountain of God.
He sent word to Moses, "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you, with your wife and her two sons."
Moses went out to meet his father-in-law. He bowed down and kissed him, and they asked each other how they were. Then they went into the tent.
Moses told his father-in-law everything the LORD had done to Pharaoh and to the Egyptians for Israel's sake, all the hardships that had come on them along the way, and how the LORD had rescued them.
Jethro rejoiced over all the good that the LORD had done for Israel in rescuing them from the power of the Egyptians.
Jethro said, "Blessed be the LORD, who has rescued you from the power of the Egyptians and from the power of Pharaoh, who has rescued the people from under the power of the Egyptians.
Now I know that the LORD is greater than all the gods, because of what happened when they acted arrogantly against them."
Then Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, brought a burnt offering and sacrifices to God, and Aaron came with all the elders of Israel to eat a meal with Moses' father-in-law in the presence of God.
The next day Moses sat down to judge the people, and the people stood around Moses from morning until evening.

When Moses' father-in-law saw all that he was doing for the people, he said, "What is this you are doing for the people? Why do you sit alone, while all the people stand around you from morning until evening?"
Moses said to his father-in-law, "Because the people come to me to inquire of God.
Whenever they have a dispute, it comes to me, and I decide between one person and another. And I make known to them God's decrees and his instructions."
Moses' father-in-law said to him, "What you are doing is not good.
You will wear yourself out, both you and these people who are with you, for the task is too heavy for you. You cannot do it alone.
Now listen to me. I will give you advice, and may God be with you. You are to represent the people before God and bring their cases to God.
Teach them the decrees and the instructions, and show them the way they are to live and the things they are to do.

But look among all the people for capable men who fear God, trustworthy men who hate dishonest gain. Appoint them over the people as officials over thousands, officials over hundreds, officials over fifties and officials over tens.
Let them judge the people at all times. Every major case they are to bring to you, but every minor case they can decide themselves. That will make your load lighter, and they will carry it with you.
If you do this, and God so commands you, you will be able to stand the strain, and all these people too will go home in peace."
Moses listened to his father-in-law and did everything he had said.
Moses chose capable men from all Israel and made them heads over the people, officials over thousands, officials over hundreds, officials over fifties and officials over tens.
They judged the people at all times. The difficult cases they brought to Moses, but every minor case they decided themselves.
Then Moses let his father-in-law go, and he went back to his own land.
In the third month after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, on that very day, they came to the wilderness of Sinai.
They had set out from Rephidim, and they came to the wilderness of Sinai and camped in the wilderness. Israel camped there in front of the mountain.
Then Moses went up to God, and the LORD called to him from the mountain: "This is what you are to say to the house of Jacob and tell the Israelites:
'You have seen for yourselves what I did to the Egyptians, and how I carried you on eagles' wings and brought you to myself.
Now if you truly obey me and keep my covenant, you will be my own treasured possession out of all the peoples, for the whole earth is mine.
You will be for me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.' These are the words you are to speak to the Israelites."
So Moses came and summoned the elders of the people and set before them all these words that the LORD had commanded him.
All the people answered together, "We will do everything the LORD has said." And Moses took the people's answer back to the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "I am going to come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people will hear when I speak with you, and will always believe you." Then Moses told the LORD what the people had said.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go to the people and consecrate them today and tomorrow. Have them wash their clothes
and be ready by the third day, for on the third day the LORD will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.
Set limits for the people all around, and say, 'Be careful not to go up the mountain or touch its edge. Whoever touches the mountain must be put to death.
No hand is to touch him. He must be stoned or shot with arrows. Whether animal or person, he must not live.' Only when the ram's horn sounds a long blast may they go up the mountain."
So Moses went down from the mountain to the people. He consecrated the people, and they washed their clothes.
He said to the people, "Be ready by the third day. Do not go near a woman."
On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning, with a thick cloud on the mountain and a very loud blast of the ram's horn, and all the people in the camp trembled.
Then Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
Mount Sinai was all in smoke, because the LORD had come down on it in fire. Its smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, and the whole mountain shook violently.
As the sound of the ram's horn grew louder and louder, Moses spoke, and God answered him in thunder.
The LORD came down on Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain. The LORD called Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down and warn the people not to force their way through to the LORD to look, or many of them will die.
Even the priests who come near the LORD must consecrate themselves, or the LORD will break out against them."
Moses said to the LORD, "The people cannot come up Mount Sinai, for you yourself warned us, 'Set limits around the mountain and make it holy.'"
The LORD said to him, "Go down, and then come up, you and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people must not force their way through to come up to the LORD, or he will break out against them."
So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.
Then God spoke all these words:
"I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery.
You must have no other gods besides me.
You must not make for yourself an idol, or an image of anything in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

You must not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God. I punish children for the wrongdoing of their parents, to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me,
but I show faithful love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commands.
You must not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who misuses his name.
Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy.
For six days you are to work and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you must not do any work, neither you, nor your son or your daughter, nor your male or female slave, nor your livestock, nor the foreigner who lives in your towns.
For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, the sea and everything in them, and he rested on the seventh day. That is why the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and made it holy.
Honor your father and your mother, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You must not give false testimony against your neighbor.
You must not covet your neighbor's house. You must not covet your neighbor's wife, or his male or female slave, or his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor."
All the people saw the thunder and the lightning, the sound of the ram's horn and the mountain smoking. When the people saw it, they trembled and stood at a distance.
They said to Moses, "You speak to us, and we will listen. But do not let God speak to us, or we will die."
Moses said to the people, "Do not be afraid. God has come to test you, so that the fear of him will be with you and keep you from sinning."
So the people stood at a distance, while Moses went near to the thick darkness where God was.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "This is what you are to say to the Israelites: 'You have seen for yourselves that I have spoken to you from heaven.
You must not make anything to set beside me. You must not make for yourselves gods of silver or gods of gold.

Make an altar of earth for me, and sacrifice on it your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings, your sheep and goats and your cattle. In every place where I cause my name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.
If you make me an altar of stones, do not build it of cut stones, for if you use a tool on it, you will defile it.
And do not go up to my altar by steps, so that your nakedness is not exposed on it.'"
These are the rulings you are to set before them.
If you buy a Hebrew slave, he is to serve for six years, but in the seventh year he is to go free, without paying anything.
If he came in single, he is to go out single. If he had a wife when he came, his wife is to go out with him.
If his master gives him a wife and she bears him sons or daughters, the wife and her children will belong to her master, and he is to go out alone.
But if the slave declares, "I love my master, my wife and my children. I will not go free,"
then his master must bring him to God. He is to bring him to the door or the doorpost, and his master is to pierce his ear with an awl. Then he will be his slave for life.
If a man sells his daughter as a slave woman, she is not to go free as the male slaves do.
If she does not please her master, who has designated her for himself, he must let her be bought back. He has no right to sell her to foreigners, since he has broken faith with her.
If he designates her for his son, he must treat her as he would a daughter.
If he takes another wife for himself, he must not reduce her food, her clothing or her marital rights.
If he does not provide her with these three things, she is to go free, without paying any money.
Whoever strikes a person so that he dies must be put to death.
But if he did not lie in wait for him, and God let him fall into his hands, I will appoint a place for you to which he may flee.
But if someone plots against his neighbor and kills him by treachery, you must take him even from my altar to be put to death.
Whoever strikes his father or his mother must be put to death.
Whoever kidnaps someone must be put to death, whether he has sold him or the person is still found in his possession.
Whoever curses his father or his mother must be put to death.
If men quarrel and one strikes the other with a stone or with his fist, and he does not die but has to stay in bed,
then if he gets up and walks around outside with the help of a staff, the one who struck him will not be held liable. He must only pay for the time he lost and see that he is fully healed.
If a man strikes his male or female slave with a rod, and the slave dies at his hand, the slave must be avenged.
But if the slave survives a day or two, he is not to be avenged, for the slave is his property.

If men are fighting and they hit a pregnant woman so that her children come out, but there is no further harm, the one responsible must be fined whatever the woman's husband demands of him, and he is to pay as the judges decide.
But if there is further harm, you are to give life for life,
eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot,
burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.
If a man strikes the eye of his male or female slave and destroys it, he must let the slave go free to make up for the eye.
And if he knocks out the tooth of his male or female slave, he must let the slave go free to make up for the tooth.
If an ox gores a man or a woman to death, the ox must be stoned, and its meat must not be eaten, but the owner of the ox will not be held liable.

But if the ox has been in the habit of goring, and its owner has been warned but has not kept it under control, and it kills a man or a woman, the ox must be stoned, and its owner too must be put to death.
If a ransom is set for him instead, he must pay whatever is set for him to redeem his life.
If it gores a son or a daughter, the same ruling applies.
If the ox gores a male or female slave, the owner must pay thirty shekels of silver to the slave's master, and the ox must be stoned.
If a man opens a pit, or digs a pit and does not cover it, and an ox or a donkey falls into it,
the owner of the pit must make good the loss. He must pay money to its owner, and the dead animal will be his.
If a man's ox injures his neighbor's ox and it dies, they are to sell the live ox and divide the money, and they are to divide the dead animal as well.
But if it was known that the ox had been in the habit of goring, and its owner did not keep it under control, he must pay in full, ox for ox, and the dead animal will be his.
If a man steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he must repay five cattle for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is caught breaking in, and he is struck so that he dies, there is no bloodguilt for him.
But if the sun has risen on him, there is bloodguilt for him. A thief must make full restitution. If he has nothing, he is to be sold to pay for what he stole.
If the stolen animal is found alive in his possession, whether ox or donkey or sheep, he must pay back double.

If a man lets his animals graze in a field or vineyard, and lets his livestock loose so that they graze in someone else's field, he must make restitution from the best of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and catches in thornbushes, so that stacked grain or standing grain or the field is burned up, the one who started the fire must make full restitution.
If a man gives his neighbor money or goods to keep safe, and they are stolen from that man's house, then if the thief is caught, he must pay back double.
If the thief is not caught, the owner of the house is to come before God to show that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property.

In every case of a disputed wrong, whether it concerns an ox, a donkey, a sheep, a garment, or anything lost of which someone says, "This is mine," the case of both parties is to come before God. The one whom God declares guilty must pay back double to his neighbor.
If a man gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep or any other animal to keep safe, and it dies or is injured or is carried off while no one is looking,
an oath before the LORD is to settle the matter between them, that he has not laid his hand on his neighbor's property. Its owner must accept this, and he does not have to make restitution.
But if it was actually stolen from him, he must make restitution to its owner.
If it was torn to pieces by a wild animal, he is to bring it as evidence. He does not have to make restitution for what was torn.
If a man borrows an animal from his neighbor, and it is injured or dies while its owner is not with it, he must make full restitution.
If its owner was with it, he does not have to make restitution. If it was hired, the hiring fee covers the loss.
If a man seduces a virgin who is not engaged to be married and sleeps with her, he must pay the bride-price for her and make her his wife.
If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still pay money equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You must not let a sorceress live.
Whoever has sexual relations with an animal must be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than the LORD alone must be destroyed.
You must not mistreat or oppress a foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
You must not mistreat any widow or orphan.
If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to me, I will certainly hear their cry.
My anger will burn, and I will kill you with the sword. Then your wives will become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend money to my people, to a poor person among you, do not act like a moneylender toward him. You must not charge him interest.
If you ever take your neighbor's cloak as security for a debt, give it back to him before sunset,
because it is his only covering. It is the cloak for his body. What else will he sleep in? When he cries out to me, I will listen, for I am gracious.
You must not curse God, and you must not curse a leader of your people.
You must not hold back the best of your harvest and of your wine and oil. You must give me the firstborn of your sons.
You must do the same with your cattle and your sheep. The firstborn may stay with its mother seven days, but on the eighth day you must give it to me.
You are to be holy people for me. You must not eat the meat of an animal torn by wild animals in the field. Throw it to the dogs.
Do not spread a false report. Do not join hands with a wicked person by being a malicious witness.
Do not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you give evidence in a lawsuit, do not side with the majority to twist justice.
And do not show favor to a poor person in his lawsuit.
If you come across your enemy's ox or donkey wandering off, you must take it back to him.
If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying down under its load, do not walk away and leave him with it. You must help him with it.
Do not twist justice for the poor among you in their lawsuits.
Keep far away from a false charge. Do not put an innocent or righteous person to death, for I will not acquit the guilty.
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see clearly and twists the words of those who are in the right.
Do not oppress a foreigner. You yourselves know how a foreigner feels, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
For six years you are to sow your land and gather in its produce,

but in the seventh year you must let it rest and leave it alone. Then the poor among your people may eat from it, and the wild animals may eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
For six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you must stop, so that your ox and your donkey may rest, and the son of your slave woman and the foreigner may be refreshed.
Pay attention to everything I have said to you. Do not call on the names of other gods. Do not even let them be heard on your lips.
Three times a year you are to hold a festival for me.

Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in that month you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.

Keep the Festival of Harvest, with the first produce of your work, of what you sow in the field. And keep the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in the produce of your work from the field.
Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD.
Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything that contains yeast. And the fat of my festival offering must not be left overnight until morning.
Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Look, I am sending an angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared.
Pay attention to him and listen to his voice. Do not rebel against him, for he will not pardon your wrongdoing, because my name is in him.
But if you listen carefully to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes.
For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and I will wipe them out.
Do not bow down to their gods or serve them, and do not follow their practices. You must tear them down completely and smash their standing stones to pieces.
Serve the LORD your God, and he will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from among you.
No woman in your land will miscarry or be unable to have children. I will give you a full life span.
I will send my terror ahead of you. I will throw into confusion every people you come against, and I will make all your enemies turn their backs and run from you.
I will send the hornet ahead of you, and it will drive the Hivites, the Canaanites and the Hittites out of your way.
I will not drive them out from before you in a single year, or the land would become a wasteland and the wild animals would become too many for you.
Little by little I will drive them out from before you, until you have grown in number and can take possession of the land.

I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the River. For I will hand over to you the people who live in the land, and you will drive them out from before you.
Do not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They must not live in your land, or they will make you sin against me. For if you serve their gods, it will be a trap for you.
Then he said to Moses, "Come up to the LORD, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel. Bow down in worship at a distance.
Moses alone is to come near to the LORD. The others must not come near, and the people must not come up with him."
Moses came and told the people all the LORD's words and all the rulings. All the people answered with one voice, "We will do everything the LORD has said."
Then Moses wrote down all the LORD's words. He got up early in the morning and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and set up twelve standing stones for the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent some young men of the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed bulls to the LORD as fellowship offerings.
Moses took half of the blood and put it in bowls, and the other half of the blood he splashed against the altar.
Then he took the Book of the Covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, "We will do everything the LORD has said, and we will obey."
Moses took the blood and splashed it on the people. He said, "This is the blood of the covenant that the LORD has made with you on the basis of all these words."
Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
They saw the God of Israel. Under his feet was something like a pavement made of lapis lazuli, as clear as the sky itself.
But God did not lay a hand on these leaders of the Israelites. They saw God, and they ate and drank.
The LORD said to Moses, "Come up to me on the mountain and stay there. I will give you the stone tablets with the instruction and the commandment that I have written to teach them."
So Moses set out with Joshua his assistant, and Moses went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, "Wait here for us until we come back to you. Aaron and Hur are with you. Anyone who has a dispute can go to them."
When Moses went up the mountain, the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of the LORD settled on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day he called to Moses from inside the cloud.
To the Israelites, the glory of the LORD looked like a consuming fire on the top of the mountain.
Moses went into the cloud and went up the mountain. He was on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
"Tell the Israelites to bring me a contribution. You are to receive my contribution from everyone whose heart moves them to give.
This is the contribution you are to receive from them: gold, silver and bronze;
blue, purple and scarlet yarn; fine linen; goats' hair;
rams' skins dyed red; fine leather; acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
Have them make a sanctuary for me, so that I may live among them.
Make it exactly like the pattern I am showing you, the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings.
"They are to make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide and one and a half cubits high.
Overlay it with pure gold. Overlay it inside and out, and make a gold molding all around it.
Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
Make poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, so that the ark can be carried with them.
The poles are to stay in the rings of the ark. They must not be removed from it.
Put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
"Make an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Make two cherubim of gold. Make them of hammered work at the two ends of the atonement cover.
Make one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. Make the cherubim of one piece with the atonement cover, at its two ends.
The cherubim are to have their wings spread out upward, sheltering the atonement cover with their wings. They are to face each other, with their faces turned toward the atonement cover.
Put the atonement cover on top of the ark, and put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.

There I will meet with you. From above the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, I will speak with you about everything I command you for the Israelites.
"Make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide and one and a half cubits high.
Overlay it with pure gold, and make a gold molding all around it.
Make a rim a handbreadth wide all around it, and make a gold molding all around its rim.
Make four gold rings for it, and fasten the rings to the four corners, where its four legs are.
The rings are to be close to the rim, to hold the poles for carrying the table.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold. The table is to be carried with them.
Make its plates and its dishes, and its jars and its bowls for pouring out drink offerings. Make them of pure gold.
Put the bread of the Presence on the table, to be in front of me always.
"Make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand is to be made of hammered work. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its buds and its blossoms are to be of one piece with it.
Six branches are to come out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

On one branch there are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a blossom, and on the next branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a blossom. It is to be the same for the six branches that come out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and its blossoms.

There is to be a bud under the first pair of branches that come out from it, a bud under the second pair of branches, and a bud under the third pair of branches: so for the six branches that come out from the lampstand.
Their buds and their branches are to be of one piece with it. The whole of it is to be a single piece of hammered work of pure gold.
Make its seven lamps. Its lamps are to be set up so that they give light to the space in front of it.
Its tongs and its trays are to be of pure gold.
It is to be made from a talent of pure gold, together with all these utensils.
See that you make them according to the pattern you are being shown on the mountain.
"Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled designer.
Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains are to be the same size.
Five of the curtains are to be joined to one another, and the other five curtains are to be joined to one another.
Make loops of blue yarn on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
Make fifty loops on the one curtain, and make fifty loops on the edge of the curtain at the end of the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
Make fifty gold clasps, and join the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle becomes a single whole.
"Make curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle. Make eleven of these curtains.
Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains are to be the same size.
Join five of the curtains together by themselves, and six of the curtains by themselves. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent.
Make fifty loops on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.
Make fifty bronze clasps. Put the clasps into the loops and join the tent together, so that it becomes a single whole.
As for the extra length that is left over in the curtains of the tent, the half curtain that is left over is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle.
The cubit on one side and the cubit on the other side that is left over in the length of the curtains of the tent is to hang down over the sides of the tabernacle, on both sides, to cover it.
Make a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
"Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame is to be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Each frame is to have two tenons, joined to each other. Do this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
Make the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side,
and make forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
For the back of the tabernacle, toward the west, make six frames.
Make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the back.
They are to be double at the bottom, and together they are to be complete up to the top, to the first ring. Both of them are to be made this way. They will form the two corners.
So there will be eight frames, with their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
"Make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the tabernacle,
five crossbars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the frames of the side of the tabernacle at the back, toward the west.
The middle crossbar is to run halfway up the frames, from one end to the other.
Overlay the frames with gold, and make their rings of gold to hold the crossbars. Overlay the crossbars with gold as well.
Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you were shown on the mountain.
"Make a veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled designer.
Hang it on four posts of acacia wood overlaid with gold, with gold hooks, standing on four silver bases.
Hang the veil under the clasps, and bring the ark of the testimony in there, behind the veil. The veil will separate the holy place from the most holy place for you.
Put the atonement cover on the ark of the testimony in the most holy place.
Place the table outside the veil, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle. Put the table on the north side.
"For the entrance of the tent, make a screen of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer.
Make five posts of acacia wood for the screen and overlay them with gold, with gold hooks. And cast five bronze bases for them.
"Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar is to be square, and it is to be three cubits high.
Make horns for it on its four corners. Its horns are to be of one piece with it. Then overlay it with bronze.
Make its pots for removing its ashes, and its shovels, its bowls, its forks and its firepans. Make all its utensils of bronze.
Make a grating for it, a network of bronze, and on the network make four bronze rings at its four corners.
Put the grating under the ledge of the altar, below it, so that the network reaches halfway up the altar.
Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and overlay them with bronze.
Its poles are to be put through the rings, so that the poles are on the two sides of the altar when it is carried.
Make it hollow, out of boards. They are to make it just as you were shown on the mountain.
"Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard is to have hangings of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long for that side,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands are to be of silver.
In the same way, on the north side there are to be hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands are to be of silver.
Across the width of the courtyard on the west side there are to be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases.
The width of the courtyard on the east side, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits.
On one side of the entrance there are to be hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
For the gate of the courtyard there is to be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases.
All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and silver hooks, and bronze bases.
The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with hangings of fine twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases.
All the utensils of the tabernacle, for all its service, and all its tent pegs and all the tent pegs of the courtyard are to be of bronze.
"Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that a lamp can be kept burning always.

In the tent of meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the testimony, Aaron and his sons are to keep it burning before the LORD from evening until morning. This is a permanent decree for the Israelites, for all their generations.
"Bring your brother Aaron near to you, together with his sons, from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests: Aaron, and Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's sons.
Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron, to give him dignity and splendor.
Speak to all who are skilled, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aaron's garments, to consecrate him to serve me as priest.

These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a tunic of checkered weave, a turban and a sash. They are to make sacred garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so that he may serve me as priest.
They are to use gold, and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
"They are to make the ephod of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled designer.
It is to have two shoulder pieces attached to its two edges, so that it can be joined together.
The woven waistband on it is to be made in the same way and of one piece with it: of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen.
"Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel,
six of their names on one stone and the names of the remaining six on the other stone, in the order of their birth.
Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones as a gem cutter engraves a seal. Mount them in settings of gold.
Put the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as stones of remembrance for the Israelites. Aaron is to carry their names before the LORD on his two shoulders as a reminder.
and two chains of pure gold, twisted like cords, and fasten the corded chains to the settings.
"Make a breastpiece of judgment, the work of a skilled designer. Make it in the same way as the ephod: make it of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen.
It is to be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide.
Mount on it a setting of stones, four rows of stones. The first row is to be a carnelian, a chrysolite and an emerald;
the second row a turquoise, a lapis lazuli and a moonstone;
the third row a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a beryl, an onyx and a jasper. They are to be mounted in gold settings in their places.
There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each is to be engraved like a seal with its name, for the twelve tribes.
"For the breastpiece make chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
Make two gold rings for the breastpiece, and fasten the two rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
Fasten the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and fasten the other two ends of the two cords to the two settings. In this way attach them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front.
Make two gold rings and put them on the other two corners of the breastpiece, on its inside edge, next to the ephod.
Make two more gold rings and fasten them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to its seam, just above the woven waistband of the ephod.
The breastpiece is to be tied by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it lies on the woven waistband of the ephod. Then the breastpiece will not come loose from the ephod.
"So Aaron will carry the names of the sons of Israel on the breastpiece of judgment over his heart whenever he goes into the holy place, as a reminder before the LORD at all times.

Put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece of judgment, so that they will be over Aaron's heart when he goes in before the LORD. So Aaron will always carry the means of judgment for the Israelites over his heart before the LORD.
"Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue.
It is to have an opening for the head in the middle of it. Around the opening there is to be a woven binding, like the opening of a coat of armor, so that it will not tear.
On its hem make pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, all around its hem, with gold bells between them all around:
a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe.
Aaron is to wear it when he serves. Its sound will be heard when he goes into the holy place before the LORD and when he comes out, so that he will not die.
"Make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it, as on a seal, 'Holy to the LORD.'
Fasten it to a cord of blue, so that it is on the turban. It is to be on the front of the turban.

It will be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron will bear the guilt connected with the holy things that the Israelites consecrate, all their holy gifts. It is to be on his forehead always, so that they may be accepted before the LORD.
"Weave the tunic of fine linen in a checkered pattern. Make a turban of fine linen, and make a sash, the work of an embroiderer.
For Aaron's sons make tunics, and make sashes for them, and make caps for them, to give them dignity and splendor.
Dress your brother Aaron and his sons with him in these garments. Anoint them, ordain them and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
Make linen undergarments for them to cover their naked bodies. They are to reach from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons are to wear them when they go into the tent of meeting or when they come near the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they do not incur guilt and die. This is to be a permanent decree for Aaron and for his descendants after him.
"This is what you are to do to consecrate them to serve me as priests. Take one young bull and two rams without defect,
and bread made without yeast, cakes made without yeast mixed with oil, and wafers made without yeast spread with oil. Make them of fine wheat flour.
Put them in one basket and present them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Take the garments and dress Aaron in the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod and the breastpiece. Fasten the ephod on him with its woven waistband.
Put the turban on his head and put the holy crown on the turban.
Take the anointing oil, pour it on his head and anoint him.
Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
Wrap sashes around them, Aaron and his sons, and tie caps on them. The priesthood will be theirs by a permanent decree. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.
"Bring the bull to the front of the tent of meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on the bull's head.
Slaughter the bull before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Take some of the bull's blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the blood at the base of the altar.
Take all the fat that covers the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar.
But burn the bull's flesh, its skin and its dung with fire outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
"Take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on the ram's head.
Slaughter the ram, take its blood and splash it against the altar on all sides.
Cut the ram into its pieces. Wash its internal organs and its legs, and put them with its pieces and its head.
Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
"Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on the ram's head.

Slaughter the ram and take some of its blood. Put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear and on the lobes of his sons' right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then splash the blood against the altar on all sides.

Take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and his sons' garments. Then he and his garments will be holy, and his sons and his sons' garments with him.

"Take the fat from the ram: the fat tail, the fat that covers the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh. For it is a ram of ordination.
Also take one loaf of bread, one cake of bread made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of bread made without yeast that is before the LORD.
Put all these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering, as a pleasing aroma before the LORD. It is an offering by fire to the LORD.
Take the breast of Aaron's ram of ordination and wave it as a wave offering before the LORD. It will be your share.
"Consecrate the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution, the parts that were waved and lifted up from the ram of ordination, from what belongs to Aaron and to his sons.

This is to be the permanent share of Aaron and his sons from the Israelites, for it is a contribution. It will be a contribution from the Israelites from their fellowship sacrifices, their contribution to the LORD.
"Aaron's sacred garments are to belong to his sons after him, so that they can be anointed and ordained in them.
The son who becomes priest in his place and comes into the tent of meeting to serve in the holy place is to wear them for seven days.
"Take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons are to eat the ram's meat and the bread that is in the basket, at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
They are to eat the things by which atonement was made for them when they were ordained and consecrated. But no one else may eat them, because they are holy.
If any of the meat of ordination or any of the bread is left over until morning, burn what is left over. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.
"Do this for Aaron and his sons, just as I have commanded you. Spend seven days ordaining them.
Each day offer a bull as a sin offering to make atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days make atonement for the altar and consecrate it. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches the altar will become holy.
"This is what you are to offer on the altar: two lambs a year old, every day, regularly.
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other lamb at twilight.
With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
Offer the other lamb at twilight. Offer with it the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
This is to be a regular burnt offering for all your generations, at the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, where I will meet with you, to speak to you there.
There I will meet with the Israelites, and it will be made holy by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of meeting and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I will live among the Israelites and be their God.
They will know that I am the LORD their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I might live among them. I am the LORD their God.
"Make an altar for burning incense. Make it of acacia wood.
It is to be square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and it is to be two cubits high. Its horns are to be of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold, its top, its sides all around and its horns, and make a gold molding all around it.
Make two gold rings for it below its molding. Make them on its two sides, on opposite sides, to hold the poles for carrying it.
Make the poles of acacia wood and overlay them with gold.
Put it in front of the veil that is in front of the ark of the testimony, in front of the atonement cover that is over the testimony, where I will meet with you.
Aaron is to burn fragrant incense on it. Every morning, when he tends the lamps, he is to burn it.
And when Aaron lights the lamps at twilight, he is to burn it. This is to be a regular offering of incense before the LORD for all your generations.
Do not offer on it any unauthorized incense, or a burnt offering or a grain offering, and do not pour a drink offering on it.

Once a year Aaron is to make atonement on its horns. Once a year he is to make atonement for it with the blood of the sin offering of atonement, for all your generations. It is most holy to the LORD."
"When you take a census of the Israelites to count them, each man must pay the LORD a ransom for his life when they are counted. Then no plague will come on them when they are counted.
Everyone who crosses over to those already counted is to give this: half a shekel, by the sanctuary shekel (a shekel is twenty gerahs). This half shekel is a contribution to the LORD.
Everyone who crosses over to those counted, twenty years old and over, is to give the LORD's contribution.
When you give the LORD's contribution to make atonement for your lives, the rich must not give more and the poor must not give less than half a shekel.
Take the atonement money from the Israelites and use it for the service of the tent of meeting. It will be a reminder of the Israelites before the LORD, to make atonement for your lives."
"Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand, for washing. Put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and their feet with water from it.
Whenever they go into the tent of meeting, they are to wash with water, so that they will not die. And when they come near the altar to serve, to burn an offering by fire to the LORD,
they are to wash their hands and their feet, so that they will not die. This is to be a permanent decree for them, for Aaron and for his descendants, for all their generations."
"Take the finest spices: 500 shekels of liquid myrrh, half as much fragrant cinnamon, 250 shekels, 250 shekels of fragrant cane,
and five hundred shekels of cassia, by the sanctuary shekel, and a hin of olive oil.
Make these into a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer. It will be a sacred anointing oil.
Use it to anoint the tent of meeting and the ark of the testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand.
Consecrate them, so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them will become holy.
Anoint Aaron and his sons, and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
Say to the Israelites, 'This is to be my sacred anointing oil for all your generations.
It must not be poured on anyone's body, and you must not make anything like it with the same formula. It is holy, and it is to be holy to you.
Anyone who mixes perfume like it, or puts any of it on someone who is not a priest, is to be cut off from his people.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "Take fragrant spices: gum resin, onycha and galbanum, fragrant spices together with pure frankincense, all in equal amounts.
Make them into incense, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer, salted, pure and holy.
Grind some of it into fine powder and put some of it in front of the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with you. It is to be most holy to you.
As for the incense you are to make, do not make any for yourselves with the same formula. You are to treat it as holy to the LORD.
Anyone who makes anything like it, to enjoy its fragrance, is to be cut off from his people."
"See, I have chosen by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
I have filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding and knowledge, and with ability in every kind of craft,
to make artistic designs, to work in gold, silver and bronze,
to cut stones for setting, to carve wood, and to work in every kind of craft.
And I myself have appointed Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, to work with him. I have given skill to all who are skilled, so that they can make everything I have commanded you:
the tent of meeting, the ark of the testimony and the atonement cover on it, and all the furnishings of the tent;
the table and its utensils, the pure gold lampstand and all its utensils, the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils, the basin and its stand;
the woven garments, that is, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons for serving as priests;
and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the holy place. They are to make them just as I have commanded you."
"Tell the Israelites, 'Above all, you must keep my Sabbaths. For this is a sign between me and you for all your generations, so that you may know that I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
Keep the Sabbath, because it is holy for you. Anyone who profanes it must be put to death. Whoever does any work on it, that person must be cut off from among his people.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, holy to the LORD. Anyone who does any work on the Sabbath day must be put to death.
The Israelites must keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath for all their generations as a permanent covenant.
It is a sign between me and the Israelites forever. For in six days the LORD made the heavens and the earth, and on the seventh day he stopped working and was refreshed.'"
When he had finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two tablets of the testimony, tablets of stone written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said to him, "Come, make us gods who will go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we don't know what has happened to him."
Aaron said to them, "Take off the gold rings that are in the ears of your wives, your sons and your daughters, and bring them to me."
So all the people took off the gold rings that were in their ears and brought them to Aaron.
He took the gold from them, shaped it with a tool and made it into a calf of cast metal. Then they said, "These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt."
When Aaron saw this, he built an altar in front of it. Aaron made a proclamation: "Tomorrow there will be a festival to the LORD."
Early the next day they got up and offered burnt offerings and brought fellowship offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and then got up to revel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Go down at once, because your people, whom you brought up out of the land of Egypt, have acted corruptly.

They have been quick to turn away from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a calf of cast metal. They have bowed down to it and sacrificed to it, and they have said, 'These are your gods, Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.'"
The LORD said to Moses, "I have seen this people, and they are a stiff-necked people.
Now leave me alone, so that my anger may burn against them and I may destroy them. Then I will make you into a great nation."
But Moses pleaded with the LORD his God. He said, "LORD, why should your anger burn against your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt with great power and a strong hand?

Why should the Egyptians say, 'He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the face of the earth'? Turn from your fierce anger, and relent from bringing disaster on your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac and Israel, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself. You said to them, 'I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars of the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have spoken of, and they will possess it forever.'"
So the LORD relented from the disaster he had said he would bring on his people.
Moses turned and went down the mountain with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands. The tablets were written on both sides. They were written on the front and on the back.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was the writing of God, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the noise of the people shouting, he said to Moses, "There is a sound of war in the camp."
But Moses said, "It is not the sound of victors shouting, and it is not the sound of the defeated crying out. It is the sound of singing that I hear."
As soon as he came near the camp and saw the calf and the dancing, Moses' anger burned. He threw the tablets from his hands and broke them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made and burned it in the fire. Then he ground it until it was powder, scattered it on the water and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, "What did this people do to you, that you have brought such a great sin on them?"
Aaron said, "Do not let my lord's anger burn. You know the people yourself, how set on evil they are.
They said to me, 'Make us gods who will go ahead of us. As for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we don't know what has happened to him.'
So I said to them, 'Whoever has any gold, take it off.' They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and out came this calf!"
Moses saw that the people were running wild, for Aaron had let them run wild, and they had become an object of scorn among their enemies.
So Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, "Whoever is on the LORD's side, come to me!" And all the Levites gathered around him.

He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Each of you, strap your sword to your side. Go back and forth through the camp from gate to gate, and each of you kill his brother, his friend and his neighbor.'"
The Levites did as Moses said, and about three thousand of the people died that day.
Moses said, "Dedicate yourselves to the LORD today, because each of you has gone against his own son and his own brother. So he will give you a blessing today."
The next day Moses said to the people, "You have committed a great sin. But now I will go up to the LORD. Perhaps I can make atonement for your sin."
So Moses went back to the LORD and said, "Oh, this people has committed a great sin! They have made themselves gods of gold.
But now, if you will forgive their sin… But if not, please wipe me out of the book you have written."
The LORD said to Moses, "Whoever has sinned against me, I will wipe out of my book.
Now go, lead the people to the place I told you about. Look, my angel will go ahead of you. But when the day comes for me to punish, I will punish them for their sin."
And the LORD struck the people with a plague because they had made the calf, the one Aaron made.

The LORD said to Moses, "Go, leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of the land of Egypt. Go up to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.'
I will send an angel ahead of you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up among you, because you are a stiff-necked people, and I might destroy you on the way."
When the people heard this bad news, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.

The LORD said to Moses, "Say to the Israelites, 'You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up among you for a single moment, I would destroy you. So now take off your ornaments, and I will decide what to do with you.'"
So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments from Mount Horeb onward.

Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, some distance from the camp. He called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wanted to seek the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would get up and stand at the entrances of their tents, watching Moses until he went into the tent.
When Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stand at the entrance of the tent, and he would speak with Moses.
When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would all get up and bow down, each at the entrance of his tent.
The LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as someone speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his assistant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, would not leave the tent.

Moses said to the LORD, "Look, you keep telling me, 'Lead these people up,' but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, 'I know you by name, and you have found favor in my sight.'
Now, if I have found favor in your sight, please let me know your ways, so that I may know you and keep on finding favor in your sight. And remember that this nation is your people."
He said, "My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest."
Moses said to him, "If your presence does not go with us, do not lead us up from here.

How else will it be known that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Is it not by your going with us, so that we are set apart, I and your people, from all the peoples on the face of the earth?"
The LORD said to Moses, "I will do this very thing you have asked, because you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name."
Moses said, "Please show me your glory."

He said, "I will make all my goodness pass in front of you, and I will proclaim my name, the LORD, before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show compassion to whom I will show compassion."
But he said, "You cannot see my face, for no human being can see me and live."
The LORD said, "Look, there is a place beside me. Stand on the rock,
and when my glory passes by, I will put you in a crevice in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back. But my face must not be seen."
The LORD said to Moses, "Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready in the morning. In the morning come up Mount Sinai and present yourself to me there on the top of the mountain.
No one is to come up with you, and no one is to be seen anywhere on the mountain. Not even the flocks or the herds may graze in front of that mountain."
So Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the LORD had commanded him, and he took the two stone tablets in his hand.
The LORD came down in the cloud and stood there with him, and he proclaimed the name, the LORD.
The LORD passed by in front of him and proclaimed, "The LORD, the LORD, a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in faithful love and faithfulness,

keeping faithful love for thousands, forgiving wrongdoing, rebellion and sin. Yet he does not let the guilty go unpunished. He punishes the children and the grandchildren for the wrongdoing of their fathers, to the third and the fourth generation."
At once Moses bowed down to the ground and worshiped.
He said, "If I have found favor in your sight, Lord, please let the Lord go among us. This is a stiff-necked people, but forgive our wrongdoing and our sin, and take us as your own possession."

He said, "Look, I am making a covenant. In front of all your people I will do wonders such as have never been done in all the earth or in any nation. All the people among whom you live will see the work of the LORD, for what I am going to do with you is awesome.
Be careful to do what I command you today. Look, I am going to drive out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
Be careful not to make a covenant with the people who live in the land you are going into, or it will become a trap among you.
Instead, tear down their altars, smash their standing stones and cut down their Asherah poles.
You must not bow down to any other god, for the LORD, whose name is Jealous, is a jealous God.

Do not make a covenant with the people who live in the land. Otherwise, when they prostitute themselves to their gods and sacrifice to their gods, someone will invite you, and you will eat from his sacrifice.
And you will take some of their daughters as wives for your sons, and their daughters will prostitute themselves to their gods and make your sons prostitute themselves to their gods too.
Do not make yourself any gods of cast metal.

"Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, for in the month of Abib you came out of Egypt.
Every firstborn belongs to me, including every male among your livestock, the firstborn of cattle and of sheep.
Redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If you do not redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn of your sons. No one is to appear before me empty-handed.
"For six days you are to work, but on the seventh day you must rest. Even at plowing time and harvest you must rest.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks with the firstfruits of the wheat harvest, and the Festival of Ingathering at the turn of the year.
Three times a year all your males are to appear before the Lord GOD, the God of Israel.
For I will drive out nations before you and enlarge your territory. No one will covet your land when you go up three times a year to appear before the LORD your God.
"Do not offer the blood of my sacrifice with anything that contains yeast, and the sacrifice of the Passover festival must not be left until morning.
Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk."
The LORD said to Moses, "Write down these words, for on the basis of these words I have made a covenant with you and with Israel."
Moses was there with the LORD for forty days and forty nights. He did not eat bread or drink water. And he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.

When Moses came down from Mount Sinai with the two tablets of the testimony in his hand, as he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that the skin of his face was shining because he had been speaking with him.
When Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, the skin of his face was shining, and they were afraid to come near him.
But Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the community came back to him, and Moses spoke to them.
After that all the Israelites came near, and he gave them all the commands that the LORD had spoken to him on Mount Sinai.
When Moses had finished speaking with them, he put a covering over his face.
But whenever Moses went in before the LORD to speak with him, he would take the covering off until he came out. When he came out, he would tell the Israelites what he had been commanded.
The Israelites would see Moses' face, that the skin of Moses' face was shining. Then Moses would put the covering back over his face until he went in to speak with him.
Moses assembled the whole community of the Israelites and said to them, "These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is to be holy for you, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Anyone who does any work on it must be put to death.
Do not light a fire in any of your homes on the Sabbath day."
Moses said to the whole community of the Israelites, "This is what the LORD has commanded:
Take from among you a contribution for the LORD. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring it as the LORD's contribution: gold, silver and bronze;
blue, purple and scarlet yarn; fine linen; goats' hair;
rams' skins dyed red; fine leather; acacia wood;
oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
onyx stones and other stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece.
"Let all who are skilled among you come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
the tabernacle, with its tent and its covering, its clasps and its frames, its crossbars, its posts and its bases;
the ark with its poles, the atonement cover, and the veil that screens it off;
the table with its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the lampstand for the light with its utensils and its lamps, and the oil for the light;
the altar of incense with its poles, the anointing oil and the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance, at the entrance of the tabernacle;
the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;
the hangings of the courtyard, its posts and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard;
the tent pegs of the tabernacle and the tent pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests."
Then the whole community of the Israelites left Moses' presence.
Everyone whose heart stirred him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought the LORD's contribution for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the sacred garments.
They came, men and women alike, all who were willing. They brought brooches, earrings, rings and necklaces, all kinds of gold jewelry. Everyone presented gold as a wave offering to the LORD.
Everyone who had blue, purple or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats' hair, rams' skins dyed red or fine leather brought them.
Everyone who could make a contribution of silver or bronze brought it as the LORD's contribution, and everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
All the skilled women spun with their own hands and brought what they had spun: blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
All the women whose hearts stirred them and who had the skill spun the goats' hair.
The leaders brought the onyx stones and the other stones for setting, for the ephod and for the breastpiece,
and the spices and the oil for the light, for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense.

All the men and women whose hearts moved them to bring something for all the work that the LORD had commanded through Moses to be done brought it. The Israelites brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
Then Moses said to the Israelites, "See, the LORD has chosen by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with skill, understanding and knowledge, and with ability in every kind of craft,
to make artistic designs, to work in gold, silver and bronze,
to cut stones for setting, to carve wood, and to work in every kind of artistic craft.
And he has given him the ability to teach others, both him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with skill to do every kind of work as craftsmen, as designers, as embroiderers in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and as weavers. They can do every kind of work and make artistic designs.

So Bezalel and Oholiab and all the skilled people to whom the LORD has given skill and understanding, to know how to do all the work for the service of the sanctuary, are to do the work just as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and all the skilled people to whom the LORD had given skill, everyone whose heart stirred him to come and do the work.

They received from Moses all the contributions that the Israelites had brought for doing the work for the service of the sanctuary. But the people kept bringing him more freewill offerings, morning after morning.
So all the skilled workers who were doing all the work on the sanctuary left the work each of them was doing and came
and said to Moses, "The people are bringing much more than enough for doing the work that the LORD commanded us to do."
So Moses gave an order, and they sent a message throughout the camp: "No man or woman is to make anything more as a contribution for the sanctuary." So the people were stopped from bringing more.
What they had was enough for doing all the work, and more than enough.

All the skilled people among those doing the work made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn. He made them with cherubim worked into them by a skilled designer.
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains were the same size.
He joined five of the curtains to one another, and he joined the other five curtains to one another.
