He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and he did the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set.
He made fifty loops on the one curtain, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain at the end of the second set, with the loops opposite one another.
He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle became a single whole.
He made curtains of goats' hair for a tent over the tabernacle. He made eleven of these curtains.
Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains were the same size.
He joined five of the curtains together by themselves, and six of the curtains by themselves.
He made fifty loops on the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and he made fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.
He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together, so that it became a single whole.
He made a covering for the tent of rams' skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
He made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
Each frame was ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
Each frame had two tenons, joined to each other. He did this for all the frames of the tabernacle.
He made the frames for the tabernacle: twenty frames for the south side,
and he made forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons, and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, he made twenty frames,
with their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
For the back of the tabernacle, toward the west, he made six frames.
He made two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the back.
They were double at the bottom, and together they were complete up to the top, to the first ring. He made both of them this way, for the two corners.
So there were eight frames, with their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases under each frame.
He made crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames of one side of the tabernacle,
five crossbars for the frames of the second side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the frames of the tabernacle at the back, toward the west.
He made the middle crossbar to run halfway up the frames, from one end to the other.
He overlaid the frames with gold, and he made their rings of gold to hold the crossbars. He overlaid the crossbars with gold as well.
He made the veil of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. He made it with cherubim worked into it by a skilled designer.
He made four posts of acacia wood for it and overlaid them with gold, with gold hooks, and he cast four silver bases for them.
For the entrance of the tent he made a screen of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer,
with its five posts and their hooks. He overlaid their tops and their bands with gold, and their five bases were of bronze.
Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide and one and a half cubits high.
He overlaid it with pure gold, inside and out, and made a gold molding all around it.
He cast four gold rings for it, for its four feet, with two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the ark, for carrying the ark.
He made an atonement cover of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
He made two cherubim of gold. He made them of hammered work at the two ends of the atonement cover,
one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other end. He made the cherubim of one piece with the atonement cover, at its two ends.
The cherubim had their wings spread out upward, sheltering the atonement cover with their wings. They faced each other, with their faces turned toward the atonement cover.
He made the table of acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide and one and a half cubits high.
He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding all around it.
He made a rim a handbreadth wide all around it, and made a gold molding all around its rim.
He cast four gold rings for it and fastened the rings to the four corners, where its four legs were.
The rings were close to the rim, to hold the poles for carrying the table.
He made the poles for carrying the table of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He made the utensils that were to be on the table of pure gold: its plates and its dishes, its bowls and its jars for pouring out drink offerings.
He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work. Its base and its shaft, its cups, its buds and its blossoms were of one piece with it.
Six branches came out from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

On one branch there were three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a blossom, and on the next branch three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a blossom. It was the same for the six branches that came out from the lampstand.
On the lampstand itself there were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and its blossoms.

There was a bud under the first pair of branches that came out from it, a bud under the second pair of branches, and a bud under the third pair of branches: so for the six branches that came out from it.
Their buds and their branches were of one piece with it. The whole of it was a single piece of hammered work of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, and its tongs and its trays, of pure gold.
He made the lampstand and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
He made the altar of incense of acacia wood. It was square, a cubit long and a cubit wide, and it was two cubits high. Its horns were of one piece with it.
He overlaid it with pure gold, its top, its sides all around and its horns, and he made a gold molding all around it.
He made two gold rings for it below its molding, on its two sides, on opposite sides, to hold the poles for carrying it.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
He also made the sacred anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
He made the altar of burnt offering of acacia wood. It was square, five cubits long and five cubits wide, and it was three cubits high.
He made horns for it on its four corners. Its horns were of one piece with it, and he overlaid it with bronze.
He made all the utensils of the altar: the pots, the shovels, the bowls, the forks and the firepans. He made all its utensils of bronze.
He made a grating for the altar, a network of bronze, under its ledge, below it, reaching halfway up.
He cast four rings for the four corners of the bronze grating, to hold the poles.
He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
He put the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, for carrying it. He made it hollow, out of boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze stand from the mirrors of the women who served at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He made the courtyard. On the south side the hangings of the courtyard were of fine twisted linen, a hundred cubits long,
with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the north side the hangings were a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the west side there were hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases. The hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver.
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the courtyard was fifty cubits wide.
There were hangings fifteen cubits long on one side of the entrance, with three posts and three bases,
and on the other side, so that there were hangings on both sides of the gate of the courtyard, hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard were of fine twisted linen.
The bases for the posts were of bronze. The hooks of the posts and their bands were of silver, and their tops were overlaid with silver. All the posts of the courtyard had silver bands.

The screen for the gate of the courtyard was the work of an embroiderer, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. It was twenty cubits long and five cubits high, matching the hangings of the courtyard.
It had four posts and four bronze bases. Their hooks were of silver, and the overlay of their tops and their bands were of silver.
All the tent pegs for the tabernacle and for the courtyard around it were of bronze.
This is the inventory of the tabernacle, the tabernacle of the testimony, which was recorded at Moses' command, as the work of the Levites under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, made everything the LORD had commanded Moses.
With him was Oholiab son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, a craftsman and designer, and an embroiderer in blue, purple and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
All the gold that was used for the work, in all the work on the sanctuary, the gold of the wave offering, came to twenty-nine talents and 730 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
The silver from those of the community who were counted came to 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
That was a beka for each person, that is, half a shekel by the sanctuary shekel, for everyone who crossed over to those counted, from twenty years old and over: 603,550 in all.
The hundred talents of silver were used to cast the bases of the sanctuary and the bases of the veil: a hundred bases from the hundred talents, a talent for each base.
From the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the posts, overlaid their tops and made bands for them.
The bronze of the wave offering came to seventy talents and 2,400 shekels.
With it he made the bases for the entrance of the tent of meeting, the bronze altar with its bronze grating, and all the utensils of the altar,
the bases around the courtyard and the bases for the gate of the courtyard, and all the tent pegs of the tabernacle and all the tent pegs around the courtyard.
From the blue, purple and scarlet yarn they made woven garments for serving in the holy place. They also made the sacred garments for Aaron, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the ephod of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen.
They hammered out thin sheets of gold and cut them into threads, to work them into the blue, purple and scarlet yarn and the fine linen, the work of a skilled designer.
They made shoulder pieces for the ephod, attached to its two edges, so that it was joined together.
The woven waistband on it was of one piece with it and made in the same way: of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They prepared the onyx stones, mounted in settings of gold and engraved like a seal with the names of the sons of Israel.
He put them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece, the work of a skilled designer, in the same way as the ephod: of gold, of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, and of fine twisted linen.
It was square. They made the breastpiece folded double, a span long and a span wide, folded double.
They mounted on it four rows of stones. The first row was a carnelian, a chrysolite and an emerald;
the second row a turquoise, a lapis lazuli and a moonstone;
the third row a jacinth, an agate and an amethyst;
and the fourth row a beryl, an onyx and a jasper. They were mounted in settings of gold in their places.
There were twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel. Each was engraved like a seal with its name, for the twelve tribes.
For the breastpiece they made chains of pure gold, twisted like cords.
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, and fastened the two rings to the two corners of the breastpiece.
They fastened the two gold cords to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece,
and they fastened the other two ends of the two cords to the two settings. In this way they attached them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at the front.
They made two gold rings and put them on the other two corners of the breastpiece, on its inside edge, next to the ephod.
They made two more gold rings and fastened them to the bottom of the two shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, close to its seam, just above the woven waistband of the ephod.

They tied the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a cord of blue, so that it lay on the woven waistband of the ephod and the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He made the robe of the ephod, the work of a weaver, entirely of blue.
The opening of the robe was in the middle of it, like the opening of a coat of armor, with a binding around the opening, so that it would not tear.
On the hem of the robe they made pomegranates of blue, purple and scarlet yarn, twisted.
They made bells of pure gold and put the bells between the pomegranates, all around the hem of the robe, between the pomegranates:
a bell and a pomegranate, a bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe, to be worn for serving, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the tunics of fine linen, the work of a weaver, for Aaron and his sons,
and the turban of fine linen, the decorated caps of fine linen, and the linen undergarments of fine twisted linen,
and the sash of fine twisted linen and blue, purple and scarlet yarn, the work of an embroiderer, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
They made the plate, the holy crown, of pure gold, and wrote on it an inscription, engraved like a seal: "Holy to the LORD."
They fastened a cord of blue to it, to attach it to the turban above, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
So all the work on the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, was finished. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. That is what they did.
Then they brought the tabernacle to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, its clasps, its frames, its crossbars, its posts and its bases;
the covering of rams' skins dyed red, the covering of fine leather, and the veil that screens off;
the ark of the testimony with its poles, and the atonement cover;
the table, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
the pure gold lampstand with its lamps, the lamps set in their places, and all its utensils, and the oil for the light;
the gold altar, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the screen for the entrance of the tent;
the bronze altar with its bronze grating, its poles and all its utensils; the basin with its stand;

the hangings of the courtyard, its posts and its bases, and the screen for the gate of the courtyard, its ropes and its tent pegs, and all the utensils for the service of the tabernacle, for the tent of meeting;
the woven garments for serving in the holy place, the sacred garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for serving as priests.
The Israelites had done all the work just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Moses saw all the work, and they had done it just as the LORD had commanded. That is what they had done. And Moses blessed them.
"On the first day of the first month, set up the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
Put the ark of the testimony in it, and screen off the ark with the veil.
Bring in the table and set out the things that belong on it. Bring in the lampstand and set up its lamps.
Place the gold altar for incense in front of the ark of the testimony, and put up the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle.
Place the altar of burnt offering in front of the entrance of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting.
Place the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it.
Set up the courtyard all around, and put up the screen at the gate of the courtyard.
"Take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. Consecrate it and all its furnishings, and it will be holy.
Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils. Consecrate the altar, and the altar will be most holy.
Anoint the basin and its stand, and consecrate it.
"Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of meeting and wash them with water.
Dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him and consecrate him, so that he may serve me as priest.
Bring his sons and dress them in tunics.
Anoint them as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing will make them a priesthood that lasts forever, for all their generations."
Moses did everything just as the LORD had commanded him. That is what he did.
So on the first day of the first month in the second year, the tabernacle was set up.
Moses set up the tabernacle. He put its bases in place, set up its frames, put in its crossbars and set up its posts.
He spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering of the tent on top of it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and put it into the ark. He put the poles on the ark, and he put the atonement cover on top of the ark.
He brought the ark into the tabernacle and hung the veil that screens it off, and so he screened off the ark of the testimony, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the table in the tent of meeting, on the north side of the tabernacle, outside the veil.
He set out the bread on it in order before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the lampstand in the tent of meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the tabernacle.
He set up the lamps before the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put the gold altar in the tent of meeting, in front of the veil,
and burned fragrant incense on it, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He put up the screen at the entrance of the tabernacle.
He placed the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the tabernacle, the tent of meeting, and offered on it the burnt offering and the grain offering, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it for washing.
Moses and Aaron and his sons would wash their hands and their feet with water from it.
Whenever they went into the tent of meeting, and whenever they came near the altar, they would wash, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard around the tabernacle and the altar, and put up the screen at the gate of the courtyard. So Moses finished the work.
Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Moses could not go into the tent of meeting, because the cloud had settled on it, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle, the Israelites would set out. So it was in all their journeys.
But if the cloud did not lift, they did not set out until the day it lifted.
For the cloud of the LORD was over the tabernacle by day, and there was fire in it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel, in all their journeys.
The LORD called to Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any of you brings an offering to the LORD, you are to bring your offering from the livestock, from the herd or from the flock.
If his offering is a burnt offering from the herd, he is to offer a male without defect. He is to bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting, so that he may be accepted before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the burnt offering, and it will be accepted on his behalf to make atonement for him.

He is to slaughter the young bull before the LORD. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, are to present the blood and splash the blood against all sides of the altar that is at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to skin the burnt offering and cut it into its pieces.
The sons of Aaron the priest are to put fire on the altar and arrange wood on the fire.
Then Aaron's sons, the priests, are to arrange the pieces, with the head and the fat, on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He is to wash its internal organs and its legs with water, and the priest is to burn all of it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
"If his offering for a burnt offering is from the flock, from the sheep or from the goats, he is to offer a male without defect.
He is to slaughter it on the north side of the altar before the LORD, and Aaron's sons, the priests, are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
He is to cut it into its pieces, with its head and its fat, and the priest is to arrange them on the wood that is on the fire on the altar.
He is to wash the internal organs and the legs with water. Then the priest is to offer all of it and burn it on the altar. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
"If his offering to the LORD is a burnt offering of birds, he is to bring his offering from the turtledoves or from the young pigeons.
The priest is to bring it to the altar, wring off its head and burn it on the altar. Its blood is to be drained out against the side of the altar.
He is to remove its crop with its contents and throw it beside the altar, on the east side, in the place for the ashes.

He is to tear it open by its wings without dividing it in two. Then the priest is to burn it on the altar, on the wood that is on the fire. It is a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
"When anyone brings a grain offering to the LORD, his offering is to be of fine flour. He is to pour oil on it and put frankincense on it.

He is to bring it to Aaron's sons, the priests, and the priest is to take from it a full handful of its fine flour and its oil, together with all its frankincense. Then the priest is to burn it on the altar as the memorial portion of the offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy, a portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD.
"When you bring a grain offering baked in an oven, it is to be of fine flour: cakes made without yeast and mixed with oil, or wafers made without yeast and spread with oil.
"If your offering is a grain offering made on a griddle, it is to be of fine flour mixed with oil, made without yeast.
Break it into pieces and pour oil on it. It is a grain offering.
"If your offering is a grain offering made in a pan, it is to be made of fine flour with oil.
You are to bring the grain offering made from these things to the LORD. It is to be presented to the priest, and he is to bring it to the altar.
The priest is to take the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons. It is most holy, a portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD.
No grain offering that you bring to the LORD is to be made with yeast, for you must not burn any yeast or any honey as an offering by fire to the LORD.
You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of the first produce, but they must not be offered up on the altar as a pleasing aroma.
You must season every grain offering of yours with salt. Do not leave the salt of the covenant of your God out of your grain offering. You are to offer salt with all your offerings.
"If you bring a grain offering of firstfruits to the LORD, you are to bring fresh ears of grain roasted in the fire, crushed kernels of new grain, as the grain offering of your firstfruits.
Put oil on it and lay frankincense on it. It is a grain offering.
The priest is to burn its memorial portion, some of its crushed grain and some of its oil, together with all its frankincense, as an offering by fire to the LORD.
"If his offering is a fellowship offering, and he offers an animal from the herd, whether male or female, he is to offer one without defect before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it at the entrance of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, are to splash the blood against all sides of the altar.
From the fellowship offering he is to present an offering by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the internal organs and all the fat that is on the internal organs,
the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
Aaron's sons are to burn it on the altar on top of the burnt offering, which is on the wood on the fire, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
"If his offering for a fellowship offering to the LORD is from the flock, whether male or female, he is to offer one without defect.
If he offers a lamb as his offering, he is to present it before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on the head of his offering and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.

From the fellowship offering he is to present its fat as an offering by fire to the LORD: the whole fat tail, which he is to remove close to the backbone, the fat that covers the internal organs and all the fat that is on the internal organs,
the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn it on the altar as food, an offering by fire to the LORD.
"If his offering is a goat, he is to present it before the LORD.
He is to lay his hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the tent of meeting. Then Aaron's sons are to splash its blood against all sides of the altar.
From it he is to present his offering as an offering by fire to the LORD: the fat that covers the internal organs and all the fat that is on the internal organs,
the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn them on the altar as food, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma. All the fat belongs to the LORD.
This is a permanent decree for all your generations, wherever you live: you must not eat any fat or any blood."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When anyone sins unintentionally by doing any one of the things that the LORD has commanded must not be done,
if it is the anointed priest who sins, bringing guilt on the people, then for the sin he has committed he is to offer to the LORD a young bull without defect as a sin offering.
He is to bring the bull to the entrance of the tent of meeting before the LORD, lay his hand on the bull's head and slaughter the bull before the LORD.
Then the anointed priest is to take some of the bull's blood and bring it into the tent of meeting.
The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting. He is to pour out all the bull's blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to remove all the fat from the bull of the sin offering: the fat that covers the internal organs and all the fat that is on the internal organs,
the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he is to remove with the kidneys,
just as these are removed from the ox of the fellowship offering. Then the priest is to burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
But the bull's skin and all its flesh, with its head and its legs, its internal organs and its dung,

the whole bull, he is to take outside the camp to a ritually clean place, where the ashes are poured out. There he is to burn it up on a wood fire. It is to be burned up where the ashes are poured out.

"If the whole community of Israel goes astray unintentionally, and the matter escapes the notice of the assembly, and they do any one of the things that the LORD has commanded must not be done, and they realize their guilt,
when the sin they have committed becomes known, the assembly is to offer a young bull as a sin offering. They are to bring it in front of the tent of meeting.
The elders of the community are to lay their hands on the bull's head before the LORD, and the bull is to be slaughtered before the LORD.
Then the anointed priest is to bring some of the bull's blood into the tent of meeting.
The priest is to dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times before the LORD, in front of the veil.

He is to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar that stands before the LORD in the tent of meeting, and he is to pour out all the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
He is to remove all its fat from it and burn it on the altar.
He is to do with this bull just as he did with the bull of the sin offering. He is to do the same with it. So the priest will make atonement for them, and they will be forgiven.
He is to take the bull outside the camp and burn it up, just as he burned up the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
"When a leader sins, and unintentionally does any one of the things that the LORD his God has commanded must not be done, and he realizes his guilt,
or the sin he has committed is made known to him, he is to bring as his offering a male goat without defect.
He is to lay his hand on the goat's head and slaughter it in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered before the LORD. It is a sin offering.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he is to pour out its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
He is to burn all its fat on the altar, like the fat of the fellowship offering. So the priest will make atonement for him for his sin, and he will be forgiven.
"If one of the ordinary people sins unintentionally by doing any one of the things that the LORD has commanded must not be done, and he realizes his guilt,
or the sin he has committed is made known to him, he is to bring as his offering a female goat without defect, for the sin he has committed.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter the sin offering in the place of the burnt offering.
The priest is to take some of its blood with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he is to pour out all its blood at the base of the altar.

He is to remove all its fat, just as the fat is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma to the LORD. So the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
"If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he is to bring a female without defect.
He is to lay his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it as a sin offering in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered.
The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering, and he is to pour out all its blood at the base of the altar.

He is to remove all its fat, just as the fat of the lamb is removed from the fellowship offering, and the priest is to burn it on the altar on top of the offerings by fire to the LORD. So the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

"If anyone sins in this way: he hears a public call for witnesses, and he is a witness, because he has seen or knows about the matter, but he does not speak up, he will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing.

Or if anyone touches anything unclean, whether the carcass of an unclean wild animal, or the carcass of unclean livestock, or the carcass of an unclean swarming creature, and it escapes his notice that he has become unclean, and then he realizes his guilt;
or if he touches human uncleanness, any kind of uncleanness by which a person becomes unclean, and it escapes his notice, and then he learns of it and realizes his guilt;

or if anyone thoughtlessly swears an oath with his lips to do harm or to do good, in any matter about which people swear thoughtlessly, and it escapes his notice, and then he learns of it and realizes his guilt in any of these matters;
when he realizes his guilt in any one of these matters, he must confess the sin he has committed.
He must bring to the LORD his penalty for the sin he has committed: a female from the flock, a lamb or a female goat, as a sin offering. So the priest will make atonement for him for his sin.

"If he cannot afford a sheep or a goat, he is to bring to the LORD, as the penalty for the sin he has committed, two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering.
He is to bring them to the priest, who is to offer first the one for the sin offering. He is to wring its head at the back of its neck, without severing it.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood is to be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering.
The second he is to offer as a burnt offering, according to the regulation. So the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven.

"But if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons, he is to bring as his offering for the sin he has committed a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He must not put oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a sin offering.
He is to bring it to the priest, and the priest is to take a full handful of it as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar on top of the offerings by fire to the LORD. It is a sin offering.
So the priest will make atonement for him for the sin he has committed in any one of these matters, and he will be forgiven. The rest is to belong to the priest, as with the grain offering."

"When anyone acts unfaithfully and sins unintentionally in regard to any of the LORD's holy things, he is to bring to the LORD as his guilt offering a ram without defect from the flock, valued in silver shekels by the sanctuary shekel, as a guilt offering.

He must make good what he has failed to give from the holy things, add a fifth of its value to it, and give it to the priest. The priest will make atonement for him with the ram of the guilt offering, and he will be forgiven.
"If anyone sins by doing any one of the things that the LORD has commanded must not be done, even though he does not know it, he is guilty and will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing.

He is to bring to the priest a ram without defect from the flock, at the value you set, as a guilt offering. So the priest will make atonement for him for the error he committed unintentionally without knowing it, and he will be forgiven.
It is a guilt offering. He was certainly guilty before the LORD."
"When anyone sins and acts unfaithfully against the LORD by deceiving his neighbor about something entrusted to him or left in his care, or about something stolen, or if he has cheated his neighbor,
or has found something that was lost and lied about it, and has sworn falsely about any one of the things that people do and so sin,
then, when he has sinned and realizes his guilt, he must give back what he stole, or what he got by cheating, or what was entrusted to him, or the lost thing he found,
or anything at all about which he swore falsely. He must repay it in full and add a fifth to it. He must give it to its owner on the day he presents his guilt offering.
He is to bring to the priest, as his guilt offering to the LORD, a ram without defect from the flock, at the value you set, as a guilt offering.
So the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD, and he will be forgiven for any one of all the things he may have done that made him guilty."

"Command Aaron and his sons: These are the instructions for the burnt offering. The burnt offering is to stay on its hearth on the altar all night until morning, and the fire of the altar is to be kept burning on it.

The priest is to put on his linen garment, with linen undergarments next to his body. He is to remove the ashes of the burnt offering that the fire has consumed on the altar, and put them beside the altar.
Then he is to take off his garments and put on other garments, and carry the ashes outside the camp to a ritually clean place.

The fire on the altar is to be kept burning on it. It must not go out. Every morning the priest is to burn wood on it, arrange the burnt offering on it, and burn the fat of the fellowship offerings on it.
A fire is to be kept burning on the altar continually. It must not go out.
"These are the instructions for the grain offering. Aaron's sons are to present it before the LORD, in front of the altar.

One of them is to take from it a handful of the fine flour of the grain offering and of its oil, with all the frankincense that is on the grain offering, and burn it on the altar as a pleasing aroma, its memorial portion for the LORD.
Aaron and his sons are to eat what is left of it. It is to be eaten without yeast in a holy place. They are to eat it in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
It must not be baked with yeast. I have given it to them as their share of my offerings by fire. It is most holy, like the sin offering and the guilt offering.
Any male among Aaron's descendants may eat it. It is their permanent share, for all your generations, from the offerings by fire to the LORD. Whatever touches them will become holy."

"This is the offering that Aaron and his sons are to present to the LORD on the day he is anointed: a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a regular grain offering, half of it in the morning and half of it in the evening.
It is to be prepared with oil on a griddle. Bring it well soaked, and present the grain offering in broken pieces as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
The priest from among his sons who is anointed to succeed him is to prepare it. It is a permanent decree: it is to be burned completely for the LORD.
Every grain offering of a priest is to be burned completely. It must not be eaten."

"Speak to Aaron and his sons: These are the instructions for the sin offering. The sin offering is to be slaughtered before the LORD in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered. It is most holy.
The priest who offers it as a sin offering is to eat it. It is to be eaten in a holy place, in the courtyard of the tent of meeting.
Whatever touches its meat will become holy. If any of its blood is spattered on a garment, you must wash the spattered part in a holy place.
The clay pot in which it is boiled must be broken. But if it is boiled in a bronze pot, the pot is to be scoured and rinsed with water.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It is most holy.
But no sin offering whose blood is brought into the tent of meeting to make atonement in the holy place may be eaten. It must be burned up in the fire.
"These are the instructions for the guilt offering. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is to be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood is to be splashed against all sides of the altar.
All its fat is to be offered from it: the fat tail, the fat that covers the internal organs,
the two kidneys with the fat that is on them, by the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which is to be removed with the kidneys.
The priest is to burn them on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a guilt offering.
Any male among the priests may eat it. It is to be eaten in a holy place. It is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering: there is one rule for both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
The priest who offers anyone's burnt offering is to have for himself the skin of the burnt offering he has offered.
Every grain offering that is baked in an oven, and every one prepared in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it.
Every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all of Aaron's sons, to each one equally.
"These are the instructions for the fellowship offering that is offered to the LORD.

If someone offers it as an expression of thanks, then along with the thanksgiving sacrifice he is to offer cakes made without yeast and mixed with oil, wafers made without yeast and spread with oil, and cakes of fine flour well soaked and mixed with oil.
He is to present his offering with cakes of bread made with yeast, along with his thanksgiving fellowship offering.
From each kind of offering he is to present one as a contribution to the LORD. It belongs to the priest who splashes the blood of the fellowship offering.
The meat of his thanksgiving fellowship offering must be eaten on the day it is offered. He must not leave any of it until morning.
But if the sacrifice he offers is a vow offering or a freewill offering, it is to be eaten on the day he offers his sacrifice, and what is left of it may be eaten the next day.
Any meat of the sacrifice that is left on the third day must be burned up in the fire.

If any of the meat of his fellowship offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offered it. It is spoiled meat, and the person who eats any of it will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten. It must be burned up in the fire. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But if anyone eats meat from the fellowship offering that belongs to the LORD while he is unclean, that person must be cut off from his people.

If anyone touches anything unclean, whether human uncleanness or an unclean animal or any unclean detestable creature, and then eats any of the meat of the fellowship offering that belongs to the LORD, that person must be cut off from his people."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: You must not eat any fat of an ox, a sheep or a goat.
The fat of an animal that has died and the fat of an animal torn by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must certainly not eat it.
Anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which an offering by fire may be presented to the LORD, the person who eats it must be cut off from his people.
You must not eat any blood, whether of a bird or of an animal, wherever you live.
Anyone who eats any blood, that person must be cut off from his people."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Whoever offers his fellowship offering to the LORD must bring part of his fellowship offering as his offering to the LORD.
His own hands are to bring the offerings by fire to the LORD. He is to bring the fat together with the breast, so that the breast may be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest is to burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You are to give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your fellowship offerings.
The one among Aaron's sons who offers the blood and the fat of the fellowship offering is to have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the Israelites, from their fellowship offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and his sons as their permanent share from the Israelites.
This is the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons from the offerings by fire to the LORD, from the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
The LORD commanded that the Israelites should give it to them from the day he anointed them. It is a permanent decree for all their generations."
These are the instructions for the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering and the fellowship offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day he commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings to the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai.
"Take Aaron and his sons with him, the garments, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams and the basket of bread made without yeast,
and assemble the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him, and the community assembled at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Moses said to the community, "This is what the LORD has commanded to be done."
Then Moses brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
He put the tunic on Aaron, wrapped the sash around him, clothed him with the robe and put the ephod on him. He tied the woven waistband of the ephod around him, fastening the ephod to him with it.
He put the breastpiece on him, and put the Urim and the Thummim into the breastpiece.
He put the turban on his head, and on the turban, at the front, he put the gold plate, the holy crown, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the tabernacle and everything in it, and so consecrated them.
He sprinkled some of the oil on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand, to consecrate them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head and anointed him to consecrate him.
Then Moses brought Aaron's sons forward, clothed them with tunics, wrapped sashes around them and tied caps on them, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he brought the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull for the sin offering.

He slaughtered it, and Moses took the blood and put it with his finger on the horns of the altar all around, and so purified the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar. So he consecrated it, to make atonement for it.
Moses took all the fat that was on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.
But the bull, with its skin, its flesh and its dung, he burned up in the fire outside the camp, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram's head.
He slaughtered it, and Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
He cut the ram into its pieces, and Moses burned the head, the pieces and the fat.

He washed the internal organs and the legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then he presented the other ram, the ram of ordination, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the ram's head.
He slaughtered it, and Moses took some of its blood and put it on the lobe of Aaron's right ear, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.

Then he brought Aaron's sons forward, and Moses put some of the blood on the lobes of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands and on the big toes of their right feet. Then Moses splashed the blood against all sides of the altar.
He took the fat: the fat tail, all the fat that was on the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.

From the basket of bread made without yeast that was before the LORD, he took one cake made without yeast, one cake of bread made with oil and one wafer, and he put them on the fat portions and on the right thigh.
He put all these in the hands of Aaron and in the hands of his sons, and waved them as a wave offering before the LORD.
Then Moses took them from their hands and burned them on the altar on top of the burnt offering. They were an ordination offering, a pleasing aroma. It was an offering by fire to the LORD.
Moses took the breast and waved it as a wave offering before the LORD. It was Moses' portion from the ram of ordination, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.

Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and his sons' garments with him. So he consecrated Aaron and his garments, and his sons and his sons' garments with him.

Moses said to Aaron and his sons, "Boil the meat at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and eat it there with the bread that is in the basket of the ordination offerings, just as I commanded: 'Aaron and his sons are to eat it.'
Whatever is left over of the meat and the bread you must burn up in the fire.
Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting for seven days, until the time of your ordination is completed, for your ordination will take seven days.
What has been done today, the LORD has commanded to be done, to make atonement for you.
You must stay at the entrance of the tent of meeting day and night for seven days and keep the LORD's charge, so that you do not die, for that is what I have been commanded."
So Aaron and his sons did everything that the LORD had commanded through Moses.
On the eighth day Moses summoned Aaron and his sons and the elders of Israel.
He said to Aaron, "Take a young calf for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering, both without defect, and present them before the LORD.
And tell the Israelites: 'Take a male goat for a sin offering, and a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defect, for a burnt offering,
and an ox and a ram for fellowship offerings, to sacrifice before the LORD, and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the LORD will appear to you.'"
They brought what Moses had commanded to the front of the tent of meeting, and the whole community came near and stood before the LORD.
Moses said, "This is what the LORD has commanded you to do, so that the glory of the LORD may appear to you."

Then Moses said to Aaron, "Come near to the altar and offer your sin offering and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself and for the people. Then offer the people's offering and make atonement for them, just as the LORD has commanded."
So Aaron came near to the altar and slaughtered the calf of the sin offering that was for himself.
Aaron's sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the altar. He poured out the blood at the base of the altar.
The fat, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering he burned on the altar, just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But the meat and the skin he burned up in the fire outside the camp.
Then he slaughtered the burnt offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
They handed him the burnt offering piece by piece, with the head, and he burned them on the altar.
He washed the internal organs and the legs and burned them on top of the burnt offering on the altar.
Then he presented the people's offering. He took the goat for the people's sin offering, slaughtered it and offered it as a sin offering, as he had done with the first.
He presented the burnt offering and offered it according to the regulation.
He presented the grain offering, took a handful of it and burned it on the altar, in addition to the morning burnt offering.
He slaughtered the ox and the ram, the people's fellowship offering. Aaron's sons handed him the blood, and he splashed it against all sides of the altar.
They also handed him the fat portions from the ox and from the ram: the fat tail, the fat that covers the organs, the kidneys and the long lobe of the liver.
They put the fat portions on the breasts, and he burned the fat portions on the altar.
Aaron waved the breasts and the right thigh as a wave offering before the LORD, just as Moses had commanded.
Then Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people and blessed them. And he came down from offering the sin offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings.
Moses and Aaron went into the tent of meeting. When they came out, they blessed the people, and the glory of the LORD appeared to all the people.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed the burnt offering and the fat portions on the altar. When all the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell on their faces.
Aaron's sons Nadab and Abihu each took his firepan, put fire in it and laid incense on it. They offered before the LORD unauthorized fire, which he had not commanded them to offer.
Fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them, and they died before the LORD.
Then Moses said to Aaron, "This is what the LORD meant when he said, 'Among those who are near me I will show myself holy, and before all the people I will be glorified.'" And Aaron was silent.
Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, the sons of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, and said to them, "Come here and carry your relatives away from the front of the sanctuary, outside the camp."
So they came and carried them, still in their tunics, outside the camp, as Moses had said.

Then Moses said to Aaron and to his sons Eleazar and Ithamar, "Do not let your hair hang loose, and do not tear your clothes, or you will die, and the LORD will be angry with the whole community. But your relatives, the whole house of Israel, may mourn over the burning that the LORD has sent.
Do not leave the entrance of the tent of meeting, or you will die, for the LORD's anointing oil is on you." So they did as Moses said.
"You and your sons with you must not drink wine or beer when you go into the tent of meeting, or you will die. This is a permanent decree for all your generations.
You are to distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean,
and you are to teach the Israelites all the rules that the LORD has spoken to them through Moses."

Moses said to Aaron and to his surviving sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, "Take the grain offering that is left over from the offerings by fire to the LORD, and eat it without yeast beside the altar, for it is most holy.
Eat it in a holy place, because it is your share and your sons' share of the offerings by fire to the LORD. That is what I have been commanded.

But the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution you may eat in a ritually clean place, you and your sons and your daughters with you, for they have been given as your share and your sons' share from the fellowship offerings of the Israelites.

The thigh of the contribution and the breast of the wave offering are to be brought together with the fat portions for the offerings by fire, to be waved as a wave offering before the LORD. They will belong to you and to your sons with you as a permanent share, just as the LORD has commanded."
Then Moses searched carefully for the goat of the sin offering, and found that it had been burned up. He was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's surviving sons, and said,
"Why did you not eat the sin offering in the holy area? It is most holy, and it was given to you to take away the guilt of the community, to make atonement for them before the LORD.
Look, its blood was not brought inside the holy place. You should certainly have eaten it in the holy area, as I commanded."

Aaron replied to Moses, "Look, today they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the LORD, and yet things like these have happened to me. If I had eaten the sin offering today, would that have been pleasing in the LORD's sight?"
When Moses heard this, he was satisfied.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are the creatures you may eat, of all the animals that live on land.
You may eat any animal that has divided hooves, completely split in two, and that chews the cud.
But among those that chew the cud or have divided hooves, you must not eat these: the camel, because although it chews the cud, it does not have divided hooves. It is unclean for you.
The rock badger, because although it chews the cud, it does not have divided hooves. It is unclean for you.
The hare, because although it chews the cud, it does not have divided hooves. It is unclean for you.
And the pig, because although it has divided hooves, completely split in two, it does not chew the cud. It is unclean for you.
You must not eat their meat, and you must not touch their carcasses. They are unclean for you.
"Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat these: you may eat anything in the water that has fins and scales, whether in the seas or in the rivers.
But anything in the seas or in the rivers that does not have fins and scales, among all the swarming creatures in the water and all the living creatures that are in the water, is detestable to you.
They are to remain detestable to you. You must not eat their meat, and you must detest their carcasses.
Anything in the water that does not have fins and scales is detestable to you.
"These are the birds you are to detest. They must not be eaten, because they are detestable: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the kite, every kind of falcon,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the gull, every kind of hawk,
the little owl, the cormorant, the great owl,
the white owl, the pelican, the carrion vulture,
the stork, every kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
"All winged swarming creatures that walk on all fours are detestable to you.
But among all the winged swarming creatures that walk on all fours, you may eat those that have jointed legs above their feet, with which to leap on the ground.
Of these you may eat: every kind of locust, every kind of bald locust, every kind of cricket and every kind of grasshopper.
But all other winged swarming creatures that have four legs are detestable to you.
"You will become unclean by these. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
Whoever carries any part of their carcasses must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
Every animal that has hooves but whose hooves are not completely split, and that does not chew the cud, is unclean for you. Whoever touches them will become unclean.
All the four-footed animals that walk on their paws are unclean for you. Whoever touches their carcasses will be unclean until evening.
Whoever carries their carcasses must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening. They are unclean for you.
"These are unclean for you among the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground: the mole rat, the mouse, every kind of great lizard,
the gecko, the monitor lizard, the lizard, the skink and the chameleon.
These are the ones that are unclean for you among all the swarming creatures. Whoever touches them when they are dead will be unclean until evening.

Anything on which one of them falls when they are dead will become unclean, whether it is any article of wood, or clothing, or leather, or sackcloth, any article that is used for any work. It must be put into water, and it will be unclean until evening. Then it will be clean.
If any of them falls into a clay pot, everything in it will become unclean, and you must break the pot.
Any food that may be eaten will become unclean if water from such a pot has come on it, and any liquid that may be drunk will become unclean in any such pot.
Anything on which any part of their carcass falls will become unclean. An oven or a stove must be broken down. They are unclean, and they must remain unclean for you.
However, a spring or a cistern that collects water will remain clean, but whoever touches their carcass in it will become unclean.
If any part of their carcass falls on any seed that is to be sown, the seed remains clean.
But if water has been put on the seed and any part of their carcass falls on it, it is unclean for you.
"If any animal that you may eat dies, whoever touches its carcass will be unclean until evening.
Whoever eats any of its carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries its carcass must wash his clothes and will be unclean until evening.
"Every swarming creature that swarms on the ground is detestable. It must not be eaten.
Whatever moves on its belly, whatever walks on all fours, or whatever has many feet, among all the swarming creatures that swarm on the ground, you must not eat them, because they are detestable.
Do not make yourselves detestable by any swarming creature that swarms. Do not make yourselves unclean by them, so that you become unclean through them.
For I am the LORD your God. Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am holy. Do not make yourselves unclean by any swarming creature that moves on the ground.
For I am the LORD, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt to be your God. So be holy, because I am holy.
"These are the instructions about land animals, birds, every living creature that moves in the water and every creature that swarms on the ground,
to distinguish between the unclean and the clean, and between the living creatures that may be eaten and the living creatures that may not be eaten."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When a woman conceives and gives birth to a boy, she will be unclean for seven days. She will be unclean just as during the days of her monthly period.
On the eighth day the flesh of the boy's foreskin is to be circumcised.
Then she is to remain for thirty-three days in the blood of her purification. She must not touch anything holy or come into the sanctuary until the days of her purification are completed.
If she gives birth to a girl, she will be unclean for two weeks, as during her monthly period. Then she is to remain for sixty-six days in the blood of her purification.

"When the days of her purification are completed, whether for a son or for a daughter, she is to bring to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting a lamb a year old for a burnt offering, and a young pigeon or a turtledove for a sin offering.
He is to offer it before the LORD and make atonement for her, and she will be clean from her flow of blood. These are the instructions for a woman who gives birth to a boy or a girl.

If she cannot afford a lamb, she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons, one for a burnt offering and the other for a sin offering. So the priest will make atonement for her, and she will be clean."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

"When someone has a swelling, a scab or a shiny spot on the skin of his body, and it could be a mark of skin disease on the skin of his body, he is to be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons, the priests.

The priest is to examine the mark on the skin of his body. If the hair in the mark has turned white, and the mark appears to be deeper than the skin of his body, it is a mark of skin disease. When the priest has examined him, he is to pronounce him unclean.

But if the shiny spot on the skin of his body is white, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest is to isolate the person with the mark for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to examine him. If in his view the mark has not changed and the mark has not spread in the skin, the priest is to isolate him for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest is to examine him again. If the mark has faded and the mark has not spread in the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. It is only a scab. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
But if the scab spreads further in the skin after he has shown himself to the priest to be pronounced clean, he must show himself to the priest again.
The priest is to examine him, and if the scab has spread in the skin, the priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a skin disease.
"When someone has a mark of skin disease, he is to be brought to the priest.
The priest is to examine him. If there is a white swelling in the skin, and it has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling,
it is a chronic skin disease in the skin of his body. The priest is to pronounce him unclean. He is not to isolate him, because he is unclean.
If the skin disease breaks out all over the skin, so that the skin disease covers all the skin of the person with the mark from his head to his feet, wherever the priest looks,
the priest is to examine him. If the skin disease has covered his whole body, he is to pronounce the person with the mark clean. He has turned all white; he is clean.
But on the day raw flesh appears on him, he will be unclean.
The priest is to examine the raw flesh and pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.
But if the raw flesh changes again and turns white, he is to go to the priest.
The priest is to examine him, and if the mark has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the person with the mark clean. He is clean.
"When someone has a boil on the skin of his body and it has healed,
and in the place of the boil there is a white swelling or a reddish-white shiny spot, he must show himself to the priest.

The priest is to examine it. If it appears to be lower than the skin, and its hair has turned white, the priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a mark of skin disease that has broken out in the boil.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in it, and it is not lower than the skin, and it has faded, the priest is to isolate him for seven days.
If it spreads further in the skin, the priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a mark of disease.
But if the shiny spot stays where it is and does not spread, it is only the scar of the boil, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
"Or when someone has a burn on his skin, and the raw flesh of the burn becomes a shiny spot, reddish-white or white,

the priest is to examine it. If the hair in the shiny spot has turned white, and it appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a mark of skin disease.
But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the shiny spot, and it is not lower than the skin, and it has faded, the priest is to isolate him for seven days.
The priest is to examine him on the seventh day. If it has spread further in the skin, the priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a mark of skin disease.
But if the shiny spot stays where it is and has not spread in the skin, and it has faded, it is the swelling from the burn. The priest is to pronounce him clean, because it is the scar of the burn.
"When a man or a woman has a mark on the head or in the beard,

the priest is to examine the mark. If it appears to be deeper than the skin, and there is thin yellow hair in it, the priest is to pronounce him unclean. It is a scaly patch, a skin disease of the head or of the beard.

But if the priest examines the mark of the scaly patch, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest is to isolate the person with the scaly patch for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to examine the mark. If the scaly patch has not spread, and there is no yellow hair in it, and the scaly patch does not appear to be deeper than the skin,
the person is to shave himself, but he must not shave the scaly patch. Then the priest is to isolate the person with the scaly patch for another seven days.

On the seventh day the priest is to examine the scaly patch. If the scaly patch has not spread in the skin, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
But if the scaly patch spreads further in the skin after he has been pronounced clean,
the priest is to examine him. If the scaly patch has spread in the skin, the priest does not need to look for yellow hair. He is unclean.
But if in his view the scaly patch has not changed, and black hair has grown in it, the scaly patch has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
"When a man or a woman has shiny spots on the skin of their body, white shiny spots,
the priest is to examine them. If the shiny spots on the skin of their body are dull white, it is a rash that has broken out on the skin. That person is clean.
"When a man loses the hair of his head, he is bald, but he is clean.
If he loses the hair from the front of his head, he is bald on the forehead, but he is clean.
But if there is a reddish-white mark on the bald head or the bald forehead, it is a skin disease breaking out on his bald head or his bald forehead.
The priest is to examine him. If the swelling of the mark on his bald head or his bald forehead is reddish-white, like the appearance of skin disease on the skin of the body,
he is a man with a skin disease. He is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean. His mark is on his head.
"The person with the skin disease, who has the mark, must wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head hang loose. He must cover his upper lip and cry out, 'Unclean! Unclean!'
He will remain unclean as long as he has the mark. He is unclean. He must live alone; his home must be outside the camp.
"When a garment has a mark of mold, whether it is a garment of wool or of linen,
in the warp or the weft of linen or of wool, or in leather or anything made of leather,
if the mark in the garment or the leather, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather, is greenish or reddish, it is a mark of mold, and it must be shown to the priest.
The priest is to examine the mark and isolate the article with the mark for seven days.

On the seventh day he is to examine the mark. If the mark has spread in the garment, in the warp or the weft, or in the leather, whatever the leather is used for, the mark is a persistent mold. It is unclean.
He must burn up the garment, or the warp or the weft, of wool or of linen, or any article of leather that has the mark, because it is a persistent mold. It must be burned up in the fire.
But if the priest examines it and the mark has not spread in the garment, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather,
the priest is to order them to wash the article that has the mark, and he is to isolate it for another seven days.

After the mark has been washed, the priest is to examine it. If the mark has not changed its appearance, even though the mark has not spread, it is unclean. You must burn it up in the fire. It is rot, whether on its back or on its front.
But if the priest examines it and the mark has faded after it has been washed, he is to tear the affected part out of the garment, or out of the leather, or out of the warp or the weft.
If it appears again in the garment, or in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather, it is breaking out. You must burn up in the fire whatever has the mark.
But the garment, or the warp or the weft, or any article of leather, that you wash and from which the mark disappears, is to be washed a second time, and it will be clean.
These are the instructions for a mark of mold in a garment of wool or of linen, in the warp or the weft, or in any article of leather, for pronouncing it clean or unclean."
"These are to be the instructions for the person with a skin disease on the day he is to be made clean. He is to be brought to the priest.
The priest is to go outside the camp and examine him. If the mark of skin disease in the diseased person has healed,
the priest is to order that two live clean birds, some cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop be brought for the one who is to be cleansed.
The priest is to order that one of the birds be slaughtered in a clay pot over fresh water.
He is to take the live bird, together with the cedar wood, the scarlet yarn and the hyssop, and dip them and the live bird in the blood of the bird that was slaughtered over the fresh water.
He is to sprinkle it seven times on the one who is to be cleansed from the skin disease, and pronounce him clean. Then he is to let the live bird go free in the open country.

The one who is being cleansed must wash his clothes, shave off all his hair and bathe in water, and he will be clean. After that he may come into the camp, but he must stay outside his tent for seven days.

On the seventh day he must shave off all his hair. He must shave his head, his beard and his eyebrows; he must shave off all his hair. He must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he will be clean.

"On the eighth day he is to take two male lambs without defect and one ewe lamb a year old without defect, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and one log of oil.
The priest who performs the cleansing is to place the man who is being cleansed, together with these offerings, before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to take one of the male lambs and offer it as a guilt offering, together with the log of oil, and wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He is to slaughter the lamb in the place where the sin offering and the burnt offering are slaughtered, in the holy area. For the guilt offering, like the sin offering, belongs to the priest. It is most holy.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering, and the priest is to put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
Then the priest is to take some of the log of oil and pour it into the palm of his own left hand.
The priest is to dip his right finger in the oil that is in his left palm, and with his finger sprinkle some of the oil seven times before the LORD.

From the rest of the oil in his palm, the priest is to put some on the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on top of the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest's palm he is to put on the head of the one who is being cleansed. So the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD.
"Then the priest is to offer the sin offering and make atonement for the one who is being cleansed from his uncleanness. After that he is to slaughter the burnt offering.
The priest is to offer up the burnt offering and the grain offering on the altar. So the priest will make atonement for him, and he will be clean.

"But if he is poor and cannot afford these, he is to take one male lamb as a guilt offering to be waved, to make atonement for him, and one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering, and a log of oil,
and two turtledoves or two young pigeons, whichever he can afford, one to be a sin offering and the other a burnt offering.
On the eighth day he is to bring them for his cleansing to the priest, at the entrance of the tent of meeting, before the LORD.
The priest is to take the lamb of the guilt offering and the log of oil, and the priest is to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD.

He is to slaughter the lamb of the guilt offering, and the priest is to take some of the blood of the guilt offering and put it on the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot.
The priest is to pour some of the oil into the palm of his own left hand,
and with his right finger the priest is to sprinkle some of the oil that is in his left palm seven times before the LORD.

The priest is to put some of the oil in his palm on the lobe of the right ear of the one who is being cleansed, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, on the places where he put the blood of the guilt offering.
The rest of the oil in the priest's palm he is to put on the head of the one who is being cleansed, to make atonement for him before the LORD.
Then he is to offer one of the turtledoves or one of the young pigeons, from whatever he can afford.

From what he can afford, he is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, together with the grain offering. So the priest will make atonement before the LORD for the one who is being cleansed.
These are the instructions for someone who has a mark of skin disease and cannot afford the usual offerings for his cleansing."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"When you come into the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as your property, and I put a mark of mold in a house in the land you possess,
the owner of the house is to come and tell the priest, 'Something like a mark has appeared in my house.'
The priest is to order the house to be emptied before he comes to examine the mark, so that nothing in the house becomes unclean. After that the priest is to go in to examine the house.
He is to examine the mark. If the mark on the walls of the house consists of greenish or reddish hollows that appear to be lower than the surface of the wall,
the priest is to go out of the house to the doorway of the house and close up the house for seven days.
On the seventh day the priest is to come back and examine it. If the mark has spread on the walls of the house,
the priest is to order that the stones with the mark in them be pulled out and thrown into an unclean place outside the town.
He is to have the inside of the house scraped all around, and the plaster that is scraped off is to be dumped in an unclean place outside the town.
Then they are to take other stones and put them in place of the old stones, and he is to take other plaster and replaster the house.
"If the mark comes back and breaks out in the house after the stones have been pulled out, and after the house has been scraped and replastered,
the priest is to come and examine it. If the mark has spread in the house, it is a persistent mold in the house. It is unclean.
The house must be torn down, its stones, its timbers and all the plaster of the house, and taken outside the town to an unclean place.
Anyone who goes into the house while it is closed up will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who lies down in the house must wash his clothes, and anyone who eats in the house must wash his clothes.
"But if the priest comes and examines it, and the mark has not spread in the house after the house has been replastered, the priest is to pronounce the house clean, because the mark has gone.
To purify the house he is to take two birds, cedar wood, scarlet yarn and hyssop.
He is to slaughter one of the birds in a clay pot over fresh water.
He is to take the cedar wood, the hyssop, the scarlet yarn and the live bird, and dip them in the blood of the slaughtered bird and in the fresh water, and sprinkle the house seven times.
He is to purify the house with the blood of the bird and the fresh water, with the live bird, the cedar wood, the hyssop and the scarlet yarn.
Then he is to let the live bird go free outside the town in the open country. So he will make atonement for the house, and it will be clean.
"These are the instructions for any mark of skin disease, for a scaly patch,
for mold in a garment or in a house,
for a swelling, a scab or a shiny spot,
to teach when something is unclean and when it is clean. These are the instructions about skin disease and mold."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When any man has a discharge from his body, his discharge is unclean.
This is his uncleanness from his discharge: whether his body runs with his discharge or his body is blocked by his discharge, it is his uncleanness.
Every bed on which the man with the discharge lies will be unclean, and everything on which he sits will be unclean.
