Anyone who touches his bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever sits on anything on which the man with the discharge has sat must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whoever touches the body of the man with the discharge must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
If the man with the discharge spits on someone who is clean, that person must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any saddle on which the man with the discharge rides will be unclean.
Whoever touches anything that was under him will be unclean until evening, and whoever carries such things must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone whom the man with the discharge touches without having rinsed his hands in water must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
A clay pot that the man with the discharge touches must be broken, and any wooden article must be rinsed in water.

"When the man with the discharge becomes clean from his discharge, he is to count off seven days for his cleansing. Then he must wash his clothes and bathe his body in fresh water, and he will be clean.
On the eighth day he is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and come before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and give them to the priest.
The priest is to offer them, one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. So the priest will make atonement for him before the LORD because of his discharge.
"When a man has an emission of semen, he must bathe his whole body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Any garment or any leather on which there is semen must be washed with water, and it will be unclean until evening.
When a man lies with a woman and there is an emission of semen, they must both bathe in water, and they will be unclean until evening.
"When a woman has a discharge, and the discharge from her body is blood, she will be in her menstrual impurity for seven days, and anyone who touches her will be unclean until evening.
Anything she lies on during her menstrual impurity will be unclean, and anything she sits on will be unclean.
Anyone who touches her bed must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Anyone who touches anything she sits on must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
Whether it is on the bed or on anything on which she is sitting, when someone touches it, he will be unclean until evening.
If a man lies with her, and her menstrual impurity comes on him, he will be unclean for seven days, and every bed he lies on will be unclean.

"When a woman has a discharge of blood for many days, not at the time of her monthly period, or if she has a discharge that continues beyond her period, she will be unclean for all the days of her unclean discharge, just as during the days of her period. She is unclean.
Any bed she lies on during all the days of her discharge will be to her like her bed during her period, and anything she sits on will be unclean, as in her menstrual impurity.
Anyone who touches them will be unclean. He must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening.
When she becomes clean from her discharge, she is to count off seven days, and after that she will be clean.
On the eighth day she is to take two turtledoves or two young pigeons and bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. So the priest will make atonement for her before the LORD because of her unclean discharge.
"In this way you are to keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die in their uncleanness by making my tabernacle, which is among them, unclean.
These are the instructions for the man with a discharge, and for the man who has an emission of semen that makes him unclean,
for the woman who is in her menstrual period, for anyone with a discharge, whether male or female, and for a man who lies with a woman who is unclean."
The LORD spoke to Moses after the death of Aaron's two sons, who died when they came near before the LORD.

The LORD said to Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that he must not come at just any time into the holy place inside the veil, in front of the atonement cover that is on the ark, or he will die. For I appear in the cloud over the atonement cover.
This is how Aaron is to come into the holy place: with a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

He is to put on the holy linen tunic, with linen undergarments next to his body. He is to tie the linen sash around him and wrap the linen turban around his head. These are holy garments. He must bathe his body in water and then put them on.
From the community of the Israelites he is to take two male goats for a sin offering and one ram for a burnt offering.
Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household.
Then he is to take the two goats and set them before the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
Aaron is to cast lots for the two goats, one lot for the LORD and the other lot for Azazel.
Aaron is to present the goat on which the lot for the LORD falls and offer it as a sin offering.
But the goat on which the lot for Azazel falls is to be set alive before the LORD, to make atonement with it, by sending it away into the wilderness to Azazel.
"Aaron is to present the bull for his own sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household. He is to slaughter the bull for his own sin offering.
He is to take a firepan full of burning coals from the altar before the LORD, and two handfuls of finely ground fragrant incense, and bring them inside the veil.
He is to put the incense on the fire before the LORD, so that the cloud of incense covers the atonement cover that is over the testimony, or he will die.

He is to take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it with his finger on the front of the atonement cover, on the east side. And in front of the atonement cover he is to sprinkle some of the blood with his finger seven times.

"Then he is to slaughter the goat for the people's sin offering and bring its blood inside the veil. He is to do with its blood as he did with the bull's blood, sprinkling it on the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

So he will make atonement for the holy place because of the uncleanness of the Israelites and because of their rebellious acts, all their sins. He is to do the same for the tent of meeting, which stays with them in the midst of their uncleanness.

No one is to be in the tent of meeting from the time he goes in to make atonement in the holy place until he comes out. So he will make atonement for himself, for his household and for the whole assembly of Israel.
Then he is to go out to the altar that is before the LORD and make atonement for it. He is to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood and put it on all the horns of the altar.
He is to sprinkle some of the blood on it with his finger seven times, and so cleanse it and consecrate it from the uncleanness of the Israelites.
"When he has finished making atonement for the holy place, the tent of meeting and the altar, he is to present the live goat.

Aaron is to lay both his hands on the head of the live goat and confess over it all the wrongdoings of the Israelites and all their rebellious acts, all their sins. He is to put them on the goat's head and send it away into the wilderness in the care of a man who stands ready.
The goat will carry all their wrongdoings on itself into a remote land. He is to let the goat go in the wilderness.
"Then Aaron is to go into the tent of meeting, take off the linen garments that he put on when he went into the holy place, and leave them there.

He is to bathe his body in water in a holy place and put on his own garments. Then he is to come out and offer his burnt offering and the people's burnt offering, and make atonement for himself and for the people.
He is to burn the fat of the sin offering on the altar.
The man who sent the goat away to Azazel must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come into the camp.

The bull for the sin offering and the goat for the sin offering, whose blood was brought in to make atonement in the holy place, are to be taken outside the camp, and their skins, their flesh and their dung are to be burned up in the fire.
The one who burns them must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come into the camp.

"This is to be a permanent decree for you: in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, you must deny yourselves and not do any work, whether you are native-born or a foreigner who lives among you.
For on this day atonement will be made for you, to make you clean. You will be clean from all your sins before the LORD.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. It is a permanent decree.
The priest who is anointed and ordained to serve as priest in his father's place is to make atonement. He is to put on the linen garments, the holy garments.
He is to make atonement for the holy sanctuary, and he is to make atonement for the tent of meeting and the altar, and he is to make atonement for the priests and for all the people of the assembly.
This is to be a permanent decree for you, to make atonement for the Israelites once a year for all their sins." And he did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and tell them: This is what the LORD has commanded.
Any Israelite who slaughters an ox, a lamb or a goat in the camp, or who slaughters it outside the camp,

and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to present it as an offering to the LORD in front of the LORD's tabernacle, that man will be held guilty of bloodshed. He has shed blood, and that man must be cut off from among his people.

This is so that the Israelites will bring to the LORD the sacrifices that they have been sacrificing in the open fields. They are to bring them to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting and sacrifice them as fellowship offerings to the LORD.
The priest is to splash the blood against the LORD's altar at the entrance of the tent of meeting and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
They must no longer offer their sacrifices to the goat-demons, after whom they have prostituted themselves. This is to be a permanent decree for them, for all their generations.
"Tell them also: Any Israelite, or any foreigner who lives among them, who offers a burnt offering or a sacrifice
and does not bring it to the entrance of the tent of meeting to offer it to the LORD, that man must be cut off from his people.
"Any Israelite, or any foreigner who lives among them, who eats any blood, I will set my face against that person who eats the blood, and I will cut him off from among his people.
For the life of a creature is in the blood, and I have given it to you on the altar to make atonement for your lives, because it is the blood that makes atonement by means of the life.
That is why I have said to the Israelites, 'None of you may eat blood, and no foreigner who lives among you may eat blood.'
"Any Israelite, or any foreigner who lives among them, who hunts and catches a wild animal or a bird that may be eaten must pour out its blood and cover it with earth.

For the life of every creature is its blood; its blood is its life. That is why I have said to the Israelites, 'You must not eat the blood of any creature, because the life of every creature is its blood. Anyone who eats it must be cut off.'

"Anyone, whether native-born or foreigner, who eats an animal that has died or that was torn by wild beasts must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and he will be unclean until evening. Then he will be clean.
But if he does not wash his clothes or bathe his body, he will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: I am the LORD your God.
You must not do as they do in the land of Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their customs.
You are to carry out my rulings and keep my decrees, and live by them. I am the LORD your God.
Keep my decrees and my rulings, for the person who does them will live by them. I am the LORD.
"None of you is to approach any close relative to have sexual relations. I am the LORD.
Do not have sexual relations with your father or with your mother. She is your mother; do not have sexual relations with her.
Do not have sexual relations with your father's wife. That would dishonor your father.
Do not have sexual relations with your sister, your father's daughter or your mother's daughter, whether she was born in the same household or elsewhere.
Do not have sexual relations with your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, for that would dishonor you.
Do not have sexual relations with the daughter of your father's wife, born to your father. She is your sister; do not have sexual relations with her.
Do not have sexual relations with your father's sister. She is your father's close relative.
Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister, for she is your mother's close relative.
Do not dishonor your father's brother: do not approach his wife. She is your aunt.
Do not have sexual relations with your daughter-in-law. She is your son's wife; do not have sexual relations with her.
Do not have sexual relations with your brother's wife. That would dishonor your brother.
Do not have sexual relations with a woman and her daughter. Do not marry her son's daughter or her daughter's daughter to have sexual relations with her. They are close relatives. It is depravity.
Do not marry a woman as a rival to her sister, having sexual relations with her while her sister is still alive.
Do not approach a woman to have sexual relations with her while she is unclean during her monthly period.
Do not have sexual intercourse with your neighbor's wife and so make yourself unclean with her.
Do not give any of your children to be handed over to Molech, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not lie with a male as one lies with a woman. It is a detestable act.
Do not have sexual intercourse with any animal and so make yourself unclean with it. No woman is to present herself to an animal to mate with it. It is a perversion.
"Do not make yourselves unclean by any of these things, for by all these things the nations that I am driving out before you made themselves unclean.
The land became unclean, so I punished it for its wrongdoing, and the land vomited out its inhabitants.
But you must keep my decrees and my rulings, and you must not do any of these detestable things, neither the native-born nor the foreigner who lives among you.
For the people of the land who were there before you did all these detestable things, and the land became unclean.
Then the land will not vomit you out for making it unclean, as it vomited out the nation that was there before you.
Whoever does any of these detestable things, the people who do them must be cut off from among their people.
So keep my charge, and do not follow any of the detestable customs that were practiced before you, and do not make yourselves unclean by them. I am the LORD your God."
"Speak to the whole community of the Israelites and tell them: Be holy, because I, the LORD your God, am holy.
Each of you must respect his mother and his father, and you must keep my Sabbaths. I am the LORD your God.
Do not turn to idols, and do not make gods of cast metal for yourselves. I am the LORD your God.
"When you sacrifice a fellowship offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in such a way that you will be accepted.
It must be eaten on the day you sacrifice it or on the next day. Whatever is left over until the third day must be burned up in the fire.
If any of it is eaten on the third day, it is spoiled meat; it will not be accepted.
Whoever eats it will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing, because he has profaned what is holy to the LORD. That person must be cut off from his people.
"When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest.
Do not go back over your vineyard, and do not gather the grapes that have fallen in your vineyard. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God.
"Do not steal. Do not deceive or lie to one another.
Do not swear falsely by my name, and so profane the name of your God. I am the LORD.
Do not oppress your neighbor or rob him. Do not keep back the wages of a hired worker overnight until morning.
Do not curse the deaf or put a stumbling block in front of the blind. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
"Do not do wrong in judging. Do not show partiality to the poor or favor to the powerful. Judge your neighbor fairly.
Do not go around spreading slander among your people. Do not stand by when your neighbor's life is at stake. I am the LORD.
Do not hate your brother in your heart. Rebuke your neighbor frankly, so that you do not incur sin because of him.
Do not take revenge or bear a grudge against any of your people, but love your neighbor as yourself. I am the LORD.
"Keep my decrees. Do not let two different kinds of your livestock mate. Do not sow your field with two kinds of seed. Do not wear a garment made of two kinds of material.

"If a man lies with a woman and has sexual intercourse with her, and she is a slave woman promised to another man, but she has not been ransomed or given her freedom, there must be an inquiry. They are not to be put to death, because she had not been freed.
He is to bring his guilt offering to the LORD at the entrance of the tent of meeting, a ram as a guilt offering.
With the ram of the guilt offering the priest is to make atonement for him before the LORD for the sin he has committed, and he will be forgiven for the sin he has committed.
"When you come into the land and plant any kind of fruit tree, regard its fruit as forbidden. For three years it is to be forbidden to you. It must not be eaten.
In the fourth year all its fruit is to be holy, an offering of praise to the LORD.
But in the fifth year you may eat its fruit, so that its yield will increase for you. I am the LORD your God.
"Do not eat anything with the blood. Do not practice divination or sorcery.
Do not round off the hair at the sides of your head, or ruin the edges of your beard.
Do not make cuts in your bodies for the dead, or put tattoo marks on yourselves. I am the LORD.
Do not profane your daughter by making her a prostitute, or the land will turn to prostitution and the land will be full of depravity.
Keep my Sabbaths, and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
Do not turn to mediums or to spiritists. Do not seek them out, and so become unclean through them. I am the LORD your God.
Stand up in the presence of the gray-haired, and show respect to the elderly. Fear your God. I am the LORD.
"When a foreigner lives with you in your land, do not mistreat him.
The foreigner who lives with you is to be treated like the native-born among you. Love him as yourself, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
Do not do wrong in judging, or in measures of length, weight or quantity.
You are to have honest scales, honest weights, an honest ephah and an honest hin. I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
Keep all my decrees and all my rulings, and do them. I am the LORD."
"Tell the Israelites: Any Israelite, or any foreigner who lives in Israel, who gives any of his children to Molech must be put to death. The people of the land are to stone him.
I myself will set my face against that man and cut him off from among his people, because he has given some of his children to Molech, and so made my sanctuary unclean and profaned my holy name.
If the people of the land close their eyes to that man when he gives any of his children to Molech, and do not put him to death,
I myself will set my face against that man and against his family. I will cut off from among their people both him and all who follow him in prostituting themselves to Molech.
If anyone turns to mediums and spiritists, prostituting himself by following them, I will set my face against that person and cut him off from among his people.
Consecrate yourselves and be holy, because I am the LORD your God.
Keep my decrees and do them. I am the LORD, who makes you holy.
"Anyone who curses his father or his mother must be put to death. He has cursed his father or his mother; his blood is on his own head.
If a man commits adultery with another man's wife, if he commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the man and the woman who commit adultery must be put to death.
If a man lies with his father's wife, he has dishonored his father. Both of them must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with his daughter-in-law, both of them must be put to death. They have committed a perversion; their blood is on their own heads.
If a man lies with a male as one lies with a woman, both of them have done a detestable thing. They must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.
If a man marries a woman and her mother, it is depravity. He and they must be burned in the fire, so that there will be no depravity among you.
If a man has sexual intercourse with an animal, he must be put to death, and you must kill the animal.
If a woman approaches any animal to mate with it, you must kill the woman and the animal. They must be put to death; their blood is on their own heads.

If a man marries his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and they have sexual relations, it is a disgrace. They must be cut off in the sight of their people. He has had sexual relations with his sister; he will bear the consequences of his wrongdoing.

If a man lies with a woman during her monthly period and has sexual relations with her, he has laid bare the source of her flow, and she has exposed the source of her blood. Both of them must be cut off from among their people.
Do not have sexual relations with your mother's sister or your father's sister, for that is to lay bare one's own close relative. They will bear the consequences of their wrongdoing.
If a man lies with his aunt, he has dishonored his uncle. They will bear the consequences of their sin; they will die childless.
If a man marries his brother's wife, it is an impurity. He has dishonored his brother. They will be childless.
"Keep all my decrees and all my rulings, and do them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live will not vomit you out.
Do not follow the customs of the nation that I am driving out before you. Because they did all these things, I loathed them.
But I have said to you, 'You will take possession of their land. I will give it to you to possess, a land flowing with milk and honey.' I am the LORD your God, who has set you apart from the peoples.

So you must distinguish between the clean and the unclean animals, and between the unclean and the clean birds. Do not make yourselves detestable by any animal or bird or anything that moves on the ground, which I have set apart for you as unclean.
You are to be holy to me, because I, the LORD, am holy, and I have set you apart from the peoples to be mine.
"A man or a woman who is a medium or a spiritist must be put to death. They are to be stoned; their blood is on their own heads."
The LORD said to Moses, "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and tell them: A priest must not make himself unclean for a dead person among his people,
except for a close relative: his mother or his father, his son or his daughter, his brother,
or his unmarried sister, who is close to him because she has no husband. For her he may make himself unclean.
He must not make himself unclean as a husband among his people, and so profane himself.
Priests must not shave bald patches on their heads or shave off the edges of their beards or make cuts in their bodies.
They are to be holy to their God and must not profane the name of their God, because they present the offerings by fire to the LORD, the food of their God. So they must be holy.
They must not marry a woman who is a prostitute or who has been defiled, and they must not marry a woman divorced from her husband, for the priest is holy to his God.
You are to treat him as holy, because he offers the food of your God. He is to be holy to you, because I, the LORD, who make you holy, am holy.
If a priest's daughter profanes herself by prostitution, she profanes her father. She must be burned in the fire.

"The priest who is highest among his brothers, on whose head the anointing oil has been poured and who has been ordained to wear the garments, must not let the hair of his head hang loose or tear his clothes.
He must not go near any dead body. He must not make himself unclean even for his father or his mother.
He must not leave the sanctuary, or profane the sanctuary of his God, because the consecration of the anointing oil of his God is on him. I am the LORD.
He is to marry a woman who is a virgin.
He must not marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman defiled by prostitution. He is to marry only a virgin from his own people,
so that he does not profane his descendants among his people, for I am the LORD, who makes him holy."
"Speak to Aaron and tell him: None of your descendants in any generation who has a defect is to come near to offer the food of his God.
For no man who has a defect may come near: no man who is blind or lame, or who has a disfigured face or a deformed limb,
or a man who has a broken foot or a broken hand,
or who is hunchbacked or a dwarf, or who has a spot in his eye, or who has a festering rash or scabs, or crushed testicles.
No man among the descendants of Aaron the priest who has a defect is to come near to present the offerings by fire to the LORD. He has a defect; he must not come near to offer the food of his God.
He may eat the food of his God, both the most holy and the holy things.
But he must not go near the veil or come near the altar, because he has a defect. He must not profane my holy places, for I am the LORD, who makes them holy."
So Moses spoke to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites.
"Tell Aaron and his sons to treat with care the holy offerings of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name. I am the LORD.

Say to them: In all your generations, if any of your descendants comes near the holy offerings that the Israelites consecrate to the LORD while he is unclean, that person must be cut off from my presence. I am the LORD.

None of Aaron's descendants who has a skin disease or a discharge may eat any of the holy offerings until he is clean. If anyone touches anything made unclean by a dead body, or a man has an emission of semen,
or a man touches any swarming creature that makes him unclean, or any person who makes him unclean, whatever his uncleanness may be,
the person who touches any such thing will be unclean until evening. He must not eat any of the holy offerings unless he has bathed his body in water.
When the sun has set, he will be clean, and after that he may eat the holy offerings, for they are his food.
He must not eat an animal that has died or that was torn by wild beasts, and so make himself unclean by it. I am the LORD.
The priests are to keep my charge, so that they do not incur sin because of it and die for it when they profane it. I am the LORD, who makes them holy.
"No outsider may eat any holy offering. Neither a priest's resident guest nor a hired worker may eat a holy offering.
But if a priest buys someone with his money, that person may eat it, and those born in his household may eat his food.
If a priest's daughter marries an outsider, she must not eat any of the holy contributions.

But if a priest's daughter becomes a widow or is divorced, and she has no children, and she returns to her father's household as in her youth, she may eat her father's food. But no outsider may eat it.
"If anyone eats a holy offering unintentionally, he must add a fifth of its value to it and give the holy offering to the priest.
The priests must not profane the holy offerings of the Israelites, which they set apart for the LORD,
by letting them eat their holy offerings and so bringing on them guilt that requires a penalty. For I am the LORD, who makes them holy."

"Speak to Aaron and his sons and to all the Israelites and tell them: Any Israelite, or any foreigner in Israel, who presents his offering as a burnt offering to the LORD, whether for any of their vows or as any of their freewill offerings,
must offer a male without defect from the cattle, the sheep or the goats, so that you may be accepted.
Do not offer anything that has a defect, because it will not be accepted on your behalf.

When anyone presents a fellowship offering to the LORD to fulfill a vow or as a freewill offering, from the herd or from the flock, it must be without defect to be accepted. There must be no defect in it.

You must not offer to the LORD anything blind, injured or maimed, or anything with a running sore, a festering rash or scabs. You must not put any of these on the altar as an offering by fire to the LORD.
You may present as a freewill offering an ox or a sheep that has a limb too long or too short, but it will not be accepted for a vow.
You must not offer to the LORD an animal whose testicles are bruised, crushed, torn or cut. You must not do this in your land.
You must not accept any such animals from a foreigner and offer them as the food of your God. They are damaged; they have a defect. They will not be accepted on your behalf."
"When an ox, a sheep or a goat is born, it is to stay with its mother for seven days. From the eighth day on, it will be accepted as an offering by fire to the LORD.
But do not slaughter a cow or a ewe and its young on the same day.
When you sacrifice a thanksgiving offering to the LORD, sacrifice it in such a way that you will be accepted.
It must be eaten the same day. Do not leave any of it until morning. I am the LORD.
"Keep my commandments and do them. I am the LORD.
Do not profane my holy name. I must be treated as holy among the Israelites. I am the LORD, who makes you holy,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: These are the LORD's appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim as holy assemblies. These are my appointed festivals.
For six days work may be done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest, a holy assembly. You must not do any work. It is a Sabbath to the LORD wherever you live.
"These are the LORD's appointed festivals, the holy assemblies that you are to proclaim at their appointed times.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at twilight, is the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of the same month is the LORD's Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast.
On the first day you are to hold a holy assembly. You must not do any regular work.
For seven days you are to present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the seventh day there is to be a holy assembly. You must not do any regular work."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you come into the land that I am giving you and reap its harvest, you are to bring to the priest a sheaf of the first of your harvest.
He is to wave the sheaf before the LORD so that you may be accepted. The priest is to wave it on the day after the Sabbath.
On the day you wave the sheaf, you are to offer a male lamb a year old without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD,
with its grain offering of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering by fire to the LORD, a pleasing aroma, and its drink offering of a quarter of a hin of wine.

You must not eat any bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until this very day, until you have brought the offering of your God. This is a permanent decree for all your generations, wherever you live.
"From the day after the Sabbath, the day you bring the sheaf of the wave offering, you are to count off seven full weeks.
Count fifty days, to the day after the seventh Sabbath. Then present a new grain offering to the LORD.
From wherever you live, bring two loaves of bread as a wave offering, made of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour and baked with yeast, as firstfruits to the LORD.

Along with the bread, present seven male lambs a year old without defect, one young bull and two rams. They are to be a burnt offering to the LORD, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
You are also to offer one male goat as a sin offering and two male lambs a year old as a fellowship offering.
The priest is to wave them, together with the bread of the firstfruits, as a wave offering before the LORD, along with the two lambs. They are to be holy to the LORD, for the priest.
On that same day you are to make a proclamation: there is to be a holy assembly for you. You must not do any regular work. This is a permanent decree for all your generations, wherever you live.

"When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap all the way to the edges of your field as you reap, and do not gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the foreigner. I am the LORD your God."

"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you are to have a day of complete rest, a day of remembrance announced with blasts of the horn, a holy assembly.
You must not do any regular work, and you are to present an offering by fire to the LORD."
"But the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It is to be a holy assembly for you. You must deny yourselves, and you are to present an offering by fire to the LORD.
Do not do any work on that same day, because it is a Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.
Anyone who does not deny himself on that same day must be cut off from his people.
Anyone who does any work on that same day, I will destroy that person from among his people.
You must not do any work. This is a permanent decree for all your generations, wherever you live.
It is a Sabbath of complete rest for you, and you must deny yourselves. From the evening of the ninth day of the month until the following evening you are to keep your Sabbath."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the LORD's Festival of Shelters, for seven days.
On the first day there is to be a holy assembly. You must not do any regular work.

For seven days you are to present an offering by fire to the LORD. On the eighth day you are to hold a holy assembly and present an offering by fire to the LORD. It is a closing assembly. You must not do any regular work.

"These are the LORD's appointed festivals, which you are to proclaim as holy assemblies for presenting offerings by fire to the LORD: burnt offerings and grain offerings, sacrifices and drink offerings, each on its own day.
They are in addition to the LORD's Sabbaths, and in addition to your gifts, all your vow offerings and all your freewill offerings that you give to the LORD.

"So on the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in the produce of the land, you are to celebrate the LORD's festival for seven days. The first day is to be a day of complete rest, and the eighth day is to be a day of complete rest.

On the first day you are to take for yourselves the fruit of majestic trees, palm fronds, branches of leafy trees and willows from the stream, and you are to rejoice before the LORD your God for seven days.
You are to celebrate it as a festival to the LORD for seven days each year. This is a permanent decree for all your generations. You are to celebrate it in the seventh month.
You are to live in shelters for seven days. All the native-born in Israel are to live in shelters,
so that your descendants may know that I made the Israelites live in shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."
So Moses announced the LORD's appointed festivals to the Israelites.
"Command the Israelites to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that a lamp can be kept burning regularly.
Outside the veil of the testimony in the tent of meeting, Aaron is to keep it in order before the LORD regularly, from evening until morning. This is a permanent decree for all your generations.
He is to keep the lamps on the pure gold lampstand in order before the LORD regularly.
"Take fine flour and bake twelve loaves with it, using two-tenths of an ephah for each loaf.
Set them in two rows, six to a row, on the pure gold table before the LORD.
Put pure frankincense on each row, to be a memorial portion for the bread, an offering by fire to the LORD.
Every Sabbath day he is to set it out before the LORD regularly. It is an everlasting covenant on the part of the Israelites.
It is to belong to Aaron and his sons, and they are to eat it in a holy place, because it is most holy for him, a portion of the offerings by fire to the LORD. It is a permanent share."
Now the son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian, went out among the Israelites. A fight broke out in the camp between the son of the Israelite woman and an Israelite man.
The son of the Israelite woman blasphemed the Name and cursed. So they brought him to Moses. His mother's name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.
They put him in custody until the will of the LORD should be made clear to them.
Then the LORD said to Moses,
"Take the man who cursed outside the camp. All who heard him are to lay their hands on his head, and the whole community is to stone him.
And tell the Israelites: Anyone who curses his God will bear the consequences of his sin.
Whoever blasphemes the name of the LORD must be put to death. The whole community must stone him. Whether he is a foreigner or native-born, when he blasphemes the Name, he must be put to death.
"Anyone who takes the life of any human being must be put to death.
Anyone who takes the life of an animal must make it good, life for life.
If anyone injures his neighbor, whatever he has done must be done to him:
fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever injury he has caused to someone must be caused to him.
Whoever kills an animal must make it good, but whoever kills a human being must be put to death.
You are to have one law for the foreigner and for the native-born alike, for I am the LORD your God."
Then Moses spoke to the Israelites, and they took the man who had cursed outside the camp and stoned him. The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai. He said,
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you come into the land that I am giving you, the land itself is to keep a Sabbath to the LORD.
For six years you are to sow your field, and for six years you are to prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.
But in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of complete rest, a Sabbath to the LORD. Do not sow your field or prune your vineyard.
Do not reap what grows by itself from your harvest, and do not gather the grapes of your untended vines. It is to be a year of complete rest for the land.
What the land produces during its Sabbath will be food for you: for you, for your male and female slaves, and for your hired workers and the temporary residents who live with you,
and for your livestock and for the wild animals in your land. All its produce may be eaten.
"You are to count off seven Sabbaths of years, seven times seven years, so that the period of seven Sabbaths of years amounts to forty-nine years.
Then on the tenth day of the seventh month you are to sound the ram's horn loudly. On the Day of Atonement you are to sound the horn throughout your land.

You are to consecrate the fiftieth year and proclaim freedom throughout the land to all its inhabitants. It is to be a jubilee for you. Each of you is to return to his own property, and each of you is to return to his family.
The fiftieth year is to be a jubilee for you. Do not sow, and do not reap what grows by itself, and do not gather the grapes of the untended vines.
For it is a jubilee. It is to be holy to you. You are to eat what the fields produce.
In this year of jubilee each of you is to return to his property.
"If you sell anything to your neighbor or buy anything from your neighbor, do not cheat one another.
You are to buy from your neighbor on the basis of the number of years since the jubilee, and he is to sell to you on the basis of the number of years of harvests that remain.
If there are many years, you are to increase the price, and if there are few years, you are to reduce the price, because what he is selling you is a number of harvests.
Do not cheat one another, but fear your God, for I am the LORD your God.
"Carry out my decrees, and keep my rulings and do them, and you will live securely in the land.
The land will yield its fruit, and you will eat your fill and live there securely.
If you ask, 'What will we eat in the seventh year, if we may not sow or gather in our produce?'
I will send my blessing on you in the sixth year, so that the land will produce enough for three years.
When you sow in the eighth year, you will still be eating from the old produce. Until the ninth year, until its produce comes in, you will eat the old.
"The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine. You are foreigners and temporary residents with me.
Throughout the land you hold as property, you must allow the land to be redeemed.
"If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his property, his nearest redeemer is to come and redeem what his brother has sold.
If a man has no one to redeem it, but he himself prospers and finds enough to redeem it,
he is to calculate the years since he sold it and refund the balance to the man he sold it to. Then he may return to his property.
But if he does not find enough to pay him back, what he sold will remain in the hands of the buyer until the year of jubilee. In the jubilee it is to be released, and he may return to his property.
"If a man sells a house to live in, in a walled city, he has the right to redeem it until a full year after its sale. His right of redemption lasts a year.
If it is not redeemed before a full year has passed, the house in the walled city will belong permanently to the buyer and his descendants. It is not to be released in the jubilee.
But houses in villages that have no walls around them are to be counted as open country. They may be redeemed, and they are to be released in the jubilee.
As for the cities of the Levites, the houses in the cities they hold as property, the Levites always have the right to redeem them.

Whatever is redeemed from the Levites, a house sold in a city that they hold as property, is to be released in the jubilee, because the houses in the cities of the Levites are their property among the Israelites.
But the pastureland around their cities must not be sold, for it is their permanent property.
"If your brother becomes poor and cannot support himself among you, you are to help him as you would a foreigner or a temporary resident, so that he may continue to live among you.
Do not take interest or profit from him, but fear your God, so that your brother may continue to live among you.
Do not lend him your money at interest or give him your food for profit.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of Canaan and to be your God.
"If your brother becomes poor among you and sells himself to you, do not make him work as a slave.
He is to be with you like a hired worker or a temporary resident. He is to work for you until the year of jubilee.
Then he and his children with him are to go free from you, and he is to return to his family and to the property of his ancestors.
For they are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. They must not be sold as slaves are sold.
Do not rule over him harshly, but fear your God.
"As for the male and female slaves you may have, you may buy male and female slaves from the nations around you.
You may also buy them from the children of the temporary residents who live among you, and from their families who are with you, who were born in your land. They may become your property.
You may leave them to your children after you to inherit as property. You may make them your slaves for life. But as for your brothers the Israelites, you must not rule over one another harshly.

"If a foreigner or temporary resident among you becomes rich, and your brother becomes poor beside him and sells himself to the foreigner or temporary resident among you, or to a member of the foreigner's family,
he has the right to be redeemed after he has sold himself. One of his brothers may redeem him,
or his uncle or his uncle's son may redeem him, or any close relative from his family may redeem him. Or if he prospers, he may redeem himself.

He and his buyer are to count the time from the year he sold himself to him until the year of jubilee. The price of his sale is to be based on the number of years, as if he had been with him for the time of a hired worker.
If many years still remain, he must pay for his redemption a share of the price he was bought for, in proportion to them.
If only a few years remain until the year of jubilee, he is to calculate it, and he must pay for his redemption in proportion to his years.
He is to be with him as a worker hired from year to year. The buyer must not rule over him harshly in your sight.
If he is not redeemed in any of these ways, he and his children with him are to go free in the year of jubilee.
For the Israelites are my servants. They are my servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. I am the LORD your God.
"Do not make idols for yourselves, and do not set up a carved image or a standing stone for yourselves. Do not place a carved stone in your land to bow down to it, for I am the LORD your God.
Keep my Sabbaths, and revere my sanctuary. I am the LORD.
"If you follow my decrees and keep my commandments and do them,
I will give you your rains at the right time, the land will yield its crops, and the trees of the field will yield their fruit.
Your threshing will last until the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will last until sowing time. You will eat your fill of food and live securely in your land.
I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down with no one to make you afraid. I will rid the land of dangerous animals, and the sword will not pass through your land.
You will chase your enemies, and they will fall before you by the sword.
Five of you will chase a hundred, and a hundred of you will chase ten thousand, and your enemies will fall before you by the sword.
I will turn toward you and make you fruitful and multiply you, and I will uphold my covenant with you.
You will still be eating last year's harvest when you have to clear out the old to make room for the new.
I will put my dwelling place among you, and I will not reject you.
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be my people.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt so that you would no longer be their slaves. I broke the bars of your yoke and made you walk upright.
"But if you do not listen to me and do not carry out all these commandments,
if you reject my decrees and loathe my rulings, so that you do not carry out all my commandments and you break my covenant,

then I in turn will do this to you: I will bring sudden terror on you, wasting disease and fever that make the eyes fail and the life ebb away. You will sow your seed in vain, because your enemies will eat it.
I will set my face against you, and you will be defeated by your enemies. Those who hate you will rule over you, and you will flee when no one is pursuing you.
"And if after all this you still do not listen to me, I will go on to discipline you seven times over for your sins.
I will break your proud strength. I will make your sky like iron and your land like bronze.
Your strength will be spent in vain, because your land will not yield its crops, and the trees of the land will not yield their fruit.
"If you continue to walk in opposition to me and refuse to listen to me, I will go on to strike you seven times over, as your sins deserve.
I will send wild animals against you, and they will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock and make you few in number, so that your roads will be deserted.
"If in spite of these things you do not accept my discipline, but continue to walk in opposition to me,
then I too will walk in opposition to you, and I myself will strike you seven times over for your sins.
I will bring a sword on you to take vengeance for the covenant. When you gather in your cities, I will send a plague among you, and you will be handed over to the enemy.
When I cut off your supply of bread, ten women will bake your bread in a single oven, and they will dole out your bread by weight. You will eat, but you will not be satisfied.
"If in spite of this you still do not listen to me, but continue to walk in opposition to me,
then I will walk in opposition to you in fury, and I myself will discipline you seven times over for your sins.
You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.
I will destroy your high places, cut down your incense altars and pile your corpses on the corpses of your idols, and I will reject you.
I will turn your cities into ruins and make your sanctuaries desolate, and I will not take pleasure in your pleasing aromas.
I myself will make the land desolate, so that your enemies who come to live in it will be appalled at it.
I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw the sword and pursue you. Your land will become desolate, and your cities will become ruins.
Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths all the time that it lies desolate and you are in the land of your enemies. Then the land will rest and enjoy its Sabbaths.
All the time that it lies desolate it will have rest, the rest it did not have during your Sabbaths when you lived in it.

"As for those of you who are left, I will bring fear into their hearts in the lands of their enemies. The sound of a windblown leaf will put them to flight. They will flee as one flees from the sword, and they will fall when no one is pursuing them.
They will stumble over one another as if fleeing from the sword, though no one is pursuing. You will not be able to stand before your enemies.
You will perish among the nations, and the land of your enemies will devour you.
Those of you who are left will waste away in the lands of your enemies because of their wrongdoing. And because of the wrongdoing of their ancestors also, they will waste away like them.
"But if they confess their wrongdoing and the wrongdoing of their ancestors, the unfaithfulness they committed against me, and also how they walked in opposition to me,
so that I in turn walked in opposition to them and brought them into the land of their enemies, if then their uncircumcised hearts are humbled and they pay for their wrongdoing,
then I will remember my covenant with Jacob. I will remember also my covenant with Isaac and also my covenant with Abraham, and I will remember the land.

For the land will be left behind by them, and it will enjoy its Sabbaths while it lies desolate without them, and they will pay for their wrongdoing, because they rejected my rulings and loathed my decrees.
Yet in spite of this, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or loathe them so as to destroy them completely and break my covenant with them, for I am the LORD their God.
For their sake I will remember the covenant with their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, to be their God. I am the LORD."
These are the decrees, the rulings and the instructions that the LORD established between himself and the Israelites on Mount Sinai through Moses.
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When anyone makes a special vow to give the value of a person to the LORD,
the value of a male from twenty to sixty years old is to be fifty shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel.
If it is a female, the value is to be thirty shekels.
If the person is from five to twenty years old, the value of a male is to be twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.
If the person is from a month to five years old, the value of a male is to be five shekels of silver, and the value of a female three shekels of silver.
If the person is sixty years old or more, the value of a male is to be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

But if the one making the vow is too poor to pay the value, the person is to be presented to the priest, and the priest is to set a value for him. The priest is to set the value according to what the one making the vow can afford.
"If the vow concerns an animal of a kind that may be presented as an offering to the LORD, every such animal that is given to the LORD becomes holy.
He must not exchange it or substitute another for it, a good one for a bad one or a bad one for a good one. If he does substitute one animal for another, both it and its substitute will become holy.
If the vow concerns any unclean animal, of a kind that may not be presented as an offering to the LORD, the animal is to be presented to the priest.
The priest is to set its value, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets, so it is to be.
If he wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth to its value.
"When anyone consecrates his house as holy to the LORD, the priest is to set its value, whether good or bad. Whatever value the priest sets, so it will stand.
If the one who consecrated it wishes to redeem his house, he must add a fifth to its value in silver, and it will be his again.

"If anyone consecrates to the LORD part of the land that he holds as family property, its value is to be set according to the seed needed to sow it: fifty shekels of silver for a homer of barley seed.
If he consecrates his field from the year of jubilee onward, it is to stand at the full value.
But if he consecrates his field after the jubilee, the priest is to calculate the price for him according to the years that remain until the year of jubilee, and it is to be deducted from the value.
If the one who consecrated the field wishes to redeem it, he must add a fifth to its value in silver, and it will remain his.
But if he does not redeem the field, or if he has sold the field to someone else, it can no longer be redeemed.
When the field is released in the jubilee, it will be holy to the LORD, like a field that has been devoted. It will become the priest's property.
If anyone consecrates to the LORD a field that he has bought, which is not part of the land he holds as family property,
the priest is to calculate for him the amount of its value up to the year of jubilee, and he must pay its value on that day as a holy gift to the LORD.
In the year of jubilee the field is to return to the person from whom he bought it, the one to whom the land belongs as family property.
Every value is to be set by the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
"But no one may consecrate the firstborn of an animal, since as a firstborn it already belongs to the LORD. Whether ox or sheep, it is the LORD's.
If it is an unclean animal, he may buy it back at its value, adding a fifth to it. If it is not redeemed, it is to be sold at its value.
"But nothing that anyone devotes to the LORD from all that he has, whether a person or an animal or family land, may be sold or redeemed. Everything devoted is most holy to the LORD.
No person who has been devoted to destruction may be ransomed. He must be put to death.
"A tenth of everything from the land, whether grain from the soil or fruit from the trees, belongs to the LORD. It is holy to the LORD.
If anyone wishes to redeem any of his tenth, he must add a fifth to it.
Every tenth of the herd and the flock, every tenth animal that passes under the shepherd's rod, is to be holy to the LORD.
He must not look to see whether it is good or bad, and he must not substitute another for it. If he does substitute one, both it and its substitute will become holy. It cannot be redeemed."
These are the commandments that the LORD gave Moses for the Israelites on Mount Sinai.
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt. He said,
"Take a census of the whole community of the Israelites by their clans and their ancestral families, counting the names of every male, one by one.
You and Aaron are to register them by their divisions, all those in Israel who are twenty years old or more and able to serve in the army.
A man from each tribe is to be with you, each of them the head of his ancestral family.
These are the names of the men who are to stand with you: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar;
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the sons of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
from Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran;
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan."
These were the men chosen from the community, the leaders of their ancestral tribes. They were the heads of the clans of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named,

and on the first day of the second month they assembled the whole community. The people recorded their descent by their clans and their ancestral families, and those twenty years old or more were counted by name, one by one,
as the LORD had commanded Moses. So he registered them in the wilderness of Sinai.

From the descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, every male twenty years old or more who was able to serve in the army was counted by name, one by one.
Those registered from the tribe of Reuben numbered 46,500.

From the descendants of Simeon, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, those registered were counted by name, one by one: every male twenty years old or more who was able to serve in the army.
Those registered from the tribe of Simeon numbered 59,300.

From the descendants of Gad, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Gad numbered 45,650.

From the descendants of Judah, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Judah numbered 74,600.

From the descendants of Issachar, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Issachar numbered 54,400.

From the descendants of Zebulun, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Zebulun numbered 57,400.

From the sons of Joseph: from the descendants of Ephraim, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Ephraim numbered 40,500.

From the descendants of Manasseh, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Manasseh numbered 32,200.

From the descendants of Benjamin, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Benjamin numbered 35,400.

From the descendants of Dan, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Dan numbered 62,700.

From the descendants of Asher, according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Asher numbered 41,500.

The descendants of Naphtali: according to their records of descent by their clans and their ancestral families, all those twenty years old or more who were able to serve in the army were counted by name.
Those registered from the tribe of Naphtali numbered 53,400.
These were the men registered by Moses and Aaron and the leaders of Israel, twelve men, each one representing his ancestral family.
All the Israelites registered by their ancestral families, those twenty years old or more, everyone in Israel who was able to serve in the army,
But the Levites were not registered among them by their ancestral tribe.
"Only the tribe of Levi you are not to register. Do not include them in the census among the Israelites.

Instead, put the Levites in charge of the tabernacle of the testimony, all its furnishings and everything that belongs to it. They are to carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings. They are to serve in it, and they are to camp around the tabernacle.
Whenever the tabernacle sets out, the Levites are to take it down. Whenever the tabernacle is to be pitched, the Levites are to set it up. Any outsider who comes near it is to be put to death.
The Israelites are to camp by their divisions, each man in his own camp and each under his own banner.
But the Levites are to camp around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that wrath will not fall on the community of the Israelites. The Levites are to take charge of the tabernacle of the testimony."
The Israelites did this. They did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"The Israelites are to camp each man under his own banner, with the emblems of their ancestral families. They are to camp around the tent of meeting, facing it at a distance.
On the east side, toward the sunrise, the banner of the camp of Judah is to camp by its divisions. The leader of the people of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab.
The tribe of Issachar is to camp next to him. The leader of the people of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar.
Then the tribe of Zebulun. The leader of the people of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon.
All those registered for the camp of Judah, by their divisions, number 186,400. They are to set out first.
On the south side is to be the banner of the camp of Reuben by its divisions. The leader of the people of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
The tribe of Simeon is to camp next to him. The leader of the people of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
Then the tribe of Gad. The leader of the people of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
All those registered for the camp of Reuben, by their divisions, number 151,450. They are to set out second.
Then the tent of meeting is to set out, with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They are to set out in the same order as they camp, each man in his place, under their banners.
On the west side is to be the banner of the camp of Ephraim by its divisions. The leader of the people of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
Next to him is the tribe of Manasseh. The leader of the people of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
Then the tribe of Benjamin. The leader of the people of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
All those registered for the camp of Ephraim, by their divisions, number 108,100. They are to set out third.
On the north side is to be the banner of the camp of Dan by its divisions. The leader of the people of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
The tribe of Asher is to camp next to him. The leader of the people of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran.
Then the tribe of Naphtali. The leader of the people of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
All those registered for the camp of Dan number 157,600. They are to set out last, under their banners."
These were the Israelites registered by their ancestral families. All those registered in the camps, by their divisions, numbered 603,550.
But the Levites were not registered among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses. That is how they camped under their banners, and that is how they set out, each man by his clan, with his ancestral family.
These are the generations of Aaron and Moses at the time when the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed priests, whom he ordained to serve as priests.

But Nadab and Abihu died in the LORD's presence when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai, and they had no sons. So Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests during the lifetime of their father Aaron.
"Bring the tribe of Levi near and present them to Aaron the priest, to assist him.
They are to carry out duties for him and for the whole community in front of the tent of meeting, doing the work of the tabernacle.
They are to take care of all the furnishings of the tent of meeting and carry out the duties of the Israelites, doing the work of the tabernacle.
Give the Levites to Aaron and his sons. They are given wholly to him from among the Israelites.
Appoint Aaron and his sons to carry out their priesthood. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death."
"Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn, the first to open the womb among the Israelites. The Levites are mine,

for every firstborn is mine. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for myself every firstborn in Israel, both human and animal, as holy. They are to be mine. I am the LORD."
The LORD said to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai,
"Register the Levites by their ancestral families and their clans. Register every male a month old or more."
So Moses registered them at the command of the LORD, as he had been commanded.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath and Merari.
These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans: Amram, Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
The sons of Merari by their clans: Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites by their ancestral families.
To Gershon belonged the clan of the Libnites and the clan of the Shimeites. These were the clans of the Gershonites.
Those registered, counting every male a month old or more, numbered 7,500.
The clans of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle, on the west.
The leader of the ancestral family of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
At the tent of meeting the Gershonites were responsible for the tabernacle and the tent, its covering, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,
the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, and its ropes: all the work connected with these.
To Kohath belonged the clan of the Amramites, the clan of the Izharites, the clan of the Hebronites and the clan of the Uzzielites. These were the clans of the Kohathites.
Counting every male a month old or more, there were 8,600. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
The clans of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.
The leader of the ancestral family of the clans of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, the holy utensils used in the service, and the screen: all the work connected with these.
The chief leader of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He had oversight of those responsible for the care of the sanctuary.
To Merari belonged the clan of the Mahlites and the clan of the Mushites. These were the clans of Merari.
Those registered from them, counting every male a month old or more, numbered 6,200.
The leader of the ancestral family of the clans of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. They were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.
The Merarites were appointed to take charge of the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its posts, its bases and all its equipment, all the work connected with these,
and the posts of the courtyard all around, with their bases, their tent pegs and their ropes.

Those who were to camp in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting toward the sunrise, were Moses and Aaron and his sons. They were responsible for the care of the sanctuary, carrying out the duty owed by the Israelites. Any outsider who came near was to be put to death.
All the Levites registered, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the command of the LORD by their clans, every male a month old or more, numbered twenty-two thousand.
The LORD said to Moses, "Register every firstborn male among the Israelites a month old or more, and count the number of their names.
Take the Levites for me in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the livestock of the Israelites. I am the LORD."
So Moses registered all the firstborn among the Israelites, as the LORD had commanded him.
All the firstborn males a month old or more, counted by name as they were registered, numbered 22,273.
"Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of their livestock. The Levites are to be mine. I am the LORD.
As the redemption price for the 273 firstborn of the Israelites who outnumber the Levites,
collect five shekels for each one. Collect it by the sanctuary shekel, twenty gerahs to the shekel.
Give the money to Aaron and his sons as the redemption price for those of them who are in excess."
So Moses collected the redemption money from those who were in excess of those redeemed by the Levites.
From the firstborn of the Israelites he collected the money: 1,365 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons at the command of the LORD, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Take a census of the Kohathites from among the Levites, by their clans and their ancestral families,
all those from thirty to fifty years old who enter the service to do work at the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the Kohathites at the tent of meeting: the most holy things.
When the camp is to set out, Aaron and his sons are to go in and take down the screening veil and cover the ark of the testimony with it.
Then they are to put a covering of fine leather over it, spread a cloth made entirely of blue on top, and put its poles in place.
Over the table of the Presence they are to spread a blue cloth and put on it the plates, the dishes, the bowls and the jars for drink offerings. The regular bread is to remain on it.
They are to spread a scarlet cloth over them, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand for the light, with its lamps, its tongs, its trays, and all the jars for its oil that are used in tending it.
They are to put it and all its utensils in a covering of fine leather and put it on a carrying frame.
Over the gold altar they are to spread a blue cloth, cover it with a covering of fine leather, and put its poles in place.
They are to take all the utensils used for serving in the sanctuary, put them in a blue cloth, cover them with a covering of fine leather, and put them on a carrying frame.
They are to clear the ashes from the altar and spread a purple cloth over it.

They are to put on it all the utensils used in serving at it: the firepans, the forks, the shovels and the basins, all the utensils of the altar. They are to spread a covering of fine leather over it and put its poles in place.

"When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the holy utensils, as the camp is about to set out, the Kohathites are to come and carry them. But they must not touch the holy things, or they will die. These are the things in the tent of meeting that the Kohathites are to carry.

"Eleazar son of Aaron the priest is to have charge of the oil for the light, the fragrant incense, the regular grain offering and the anointing oil. He is to have charge of the whole tabernacle and everything in it, the sanctuary and its furnishings."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Do not let the tribe of the clans of the Kohathites be cut off from among the Levites.
Do this for them, so that they will live and not die when they come near the most holy things: Aaron and his sons are to go in and assign each of them to his work and to what he is to carry.
But the Kohathites must not go in to look at the holy things even for a moment, or they will die."
"Take a census of the Gershonites as well, by their ancestral families and their clans.
Register those from thirty to fifty years old, all who enter to serve in the work force and do the work at the tent of meeting.
This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites, in serving and in carrying:
they are to carry the curtains of the tabernacle and the tent of meeting, its covering and the covering of fine leather on top of it, the screen for the entrance of the tent of meeting,

the hangings of the courtyard, the screen for the entrance of the gate of the courtyard that surrounds the tabernacle and the altar, their ropes and all the equipment for their service. They are to do all the work that needs to be done with these.
All the service of the Gershonites, all that they carry and all their work, is to be under the direction of Aaron and his sons. You are to assign to them as their duty all that they are to carry.
This is the work of the clans of the Gershonites at the tent of meeting. Their duties are to be under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
"As for the Merarites, register them by their clans and their ancestral families.
Register those from thirty to fifty years old, all who enter the service to do the work of the tent of meeting.
This is what they are responsible for carrying, as all their work at the tent of meeting: the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its posts and its bases,

and the posts of the courtyard all around with their bases, their tent pegs and their ropes, with all their equipment and all the work connected with them. Assign to each man by name the items he is responsible for carrying.
This is the work of the clans of the Merarites, all their work at the tent of meeting, under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest."
So Moses and Aaron and the leaders of the community registered the Kohathites by their clans and their ancestral families,
those from thirty to fifty years old, all who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting.
Those registered by their clans numbered 2,750.
These were those registered from the clans of the Kohathites, all who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the command of the LORD through Moses.
Those registered from the Gershonites by their clans and their ancestral families,
those from thirty to fifty years old, all who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting,
those registered by their clans and their ancestral families, numbered 2,630.
These were those registered from the clans of the Gershonites, all who served at the tent of meeting, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the command of the LORD.
Those registered from the clans of the Merarites by their clans and their ancestral families,
those from thirty to fifty years old, all who entered the service for work at the tent of meeting,
those registered by their clans, numbered 3,200.
These were those registered from the clans of the Merarites, whom Moses and Aaron registered at the command of the LORD through Moses.
All those registered from the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron and the leaders of Israel registered by their clans and their ancestral families,
those from thirty to fifty years old, all who entered to do the work of serving and the work of carrying at the tent of meeting,
At the command of the LORD through Moses they were registered, each man according to his work and what he was to carry. So they were registered as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with a skin disease, everyone who has a discharge, and everyone who is unclean through contact with a dead body.
Send out both male and female. Send them outside the camp, so that they do not make their camp unclean, where I live among them."
The Israelites did so and sent them outside the camp. The Israelites did just as the LORD had told Moses.
"Tell the Israelites: When a man or a woman commits any of the sins that people commit, and so is unfaithful to the LORD, that person is guilty.
They are to confess the sin they have committed. The guilty person is to repay in full what is owed for the wrong, add a fifth to it, and give it to the one who was wronged.

But if that person has no close relative to whom the repayment can be made, the repayment for the wrong belongs to the LORD, for the priest. This is in addition to the ram of atonement with which atonement is made for the guilty person.
Every contribution among all the holy gifts that the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to him.
The holy gifts of each person are his own, but what anyone gives to the priest belongs to the priest."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Suppose a man's wife goes astray and is unfaithful to him,

and another man has sexual relations with her, but it is hidden from her husband and she remains undetected, though she has made herself unclean. There is no witness against her, and she was not caught in the act.

And suppose a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, and she has made herself unclean; or a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he is jealous of his wife, though she has not made herself unclean.

Then the man is to bring his wife to the priest. He is to bring the offering required for her: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He must not pour oil on it or put frankincense on it, because it is a grain offering for jealousy, a grain offering of remembrance, which brings wrongdoing to remembrance.
