"The priest is to bring her near and have her stand before the LORD.
The priest is to take holy water in a clay jar, and take some of the dust from the floor of the tabernacle and put it in the water.

When the priest has had the woman stand before the LORD, he is to loosen the hair of her head and put in her hands the grain offering of remembrance, which is the grain offering for jealousy. The priest himself is to hold the bitter water that brings the curse.

Then the priest is to put her under oath and say to the woman, 'If no man has had sexual relations with you, and if you have not gone astray into uncleanness while under your husband's authority, may you be free from this bitter water that brings the curse.
But if you have gone astray while under your husband's authority, and if you have made yourself unclean, and a man other than your husband has had sexual relations with you,'

then the priest is to put the woman under the oath of the curse, and the priest is to say to the woman, 'May the LORD make you a curse and an oath among your people, by making your thigh fall away and your belly swell.
May this water that brings the curse enter your body and make your belly swell and your thigh fall away.' And the woman is to say, 'Amen, amen.'
"The priest is to write these curses on a scroll and wash them off into the bitter water.
He is to make the woman drink the bitter water that brings the curse, and the water that brings the curse will enter her and cause bitter pain.
The priest is to take the grain offering for jealousy from the woman's hand, wave the grain offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
The priest is to take a handful of the grain offering as its memorial portion and burn it on the altar. After that he is to make the woman drink the water.

When he has made her drink the water, then if she has made herself unclean and has been unfaithful to her husband, the water that brings the curse will enter her and cause bitter pain. Her belly will swell and her thigh will fall away, and the woman will become a curse among her people.
But if the woman has not made herself unclean, and she is clean, she will be free and will be able to conceive children.
"This is the law for cases of jealousy, when a wife goes astray while under her husband's authority and makes herself unclean,
or when a spirit of jealousy comes over a man and he is jealous of his wife. He is to have the woman stand before the LORD, and the priest is to carry out for her this whole law.
The man will be free from guilt, but that woman will bear the consequences of her guilt."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When a man or a woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to dedicate themselves to the LORD,
he is to keep away from wine and strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or vinegar made from strong drink. He must not drink any grape juice, or eat grapes, fresh or dried.
As long as he is a Nazirite, he must not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or the skins.

"As long as his vow of separation lasts, no razor is to touch his head. Until the time for which he has dedicated himself to the LORD is completed, he is to be holy. He is to let the hair of his head grow long.
"As long as he is dedicated to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
Even if his father or his mother, his brother or his sister dies, he must not make himself unclean for them, because the sign of his dedication to his God is on his head.
As long as he is a Nazirite, he is holy to the LORD.
"If someone dies suddenly beside him, and so makes his consecrated head unclean, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing. He is to shave it on the seventh day.
On the eighth day he is to bring two doves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the tent of meeting.

The priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering, and make atonement for him, because he incurred sin through the dead body. That same day he is to consecrate his head again.
He must dedicate to the LORD his days as a Nazirite again and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. The earlier days do not count, because his consecration was made unclean.
"This is the law for the Nazirite when the time of his separation is completed. He is to be brought to the entrance of the tent of meeting,

and he is to present his offering to the LORD: one year-old male lamb without defect as a burnt offering, one year-old female lamb without defect as a sin offering, one ram without defect as a fellowship offering,
and a basket of unleavened bread, loaves made of fine flour mixed with oil, and wafers of unleavened bread spread with oil, together with their grain offerings and their drink offerings.
The priest is to present them before the LORD and offer his sin offering and his burnt offering.
He is to offer the ram as a fellowship sacrifice to the LORD, together with the basket of unleavened bread. The priest is also to offer its grain offering and its drink offering.

"Then at the entrance of the tent of meeting the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head. He is to take the hair from his consecrated head and put it on the fire that is under the fellowship sacrifice.

The priest is to take the boiled shoulder of the ram, one loaf of unleavened bread from the basket and one wafer of unleavened bread, and put them in the hands of the Nazirite after he has shaved off his consecrated hair.

The priest is to wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. They are holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast that is waved and the thigh that is presented. After that the Nazirite may drink wine.

"This is the law for the Nazirite who makes a vow, and for his offering to the LORD for his separation, in addition to whatever else he can afford. He must carry out the vow he has made, in keeping with the law of his separation."
"Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
'May the LORD bless you and keep you.
May the LORD make his face shine on you and be gracious to you.
May the LORD turn his face toward you and give you peace.'
So they will put my name on the Israelites, and I myself will bless them."
On the day Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed it and consecrated it and all its furnishings, and the altar and all its utensils. When he had anointed them and consecrated them,
the leaders of Israel, the heads of their ancestral families, made an offering. They were the leaders of the tribes, the men who had supervised the registration.
They brought their offering before the LORD: six covered carts and twelve oxen, a cart for every two leaders and an ox for each one. They presented them in front of the tabernacle.
"Accept these from them, so that they may be used for the work of the tent of meeting. Give them to the Levites, to each group as its work requires."
So Moses took the carts and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two carts and four oxen to the Gershonites, as their work required,
and he gave four carts and eight oxen to the Merarites, as their work required, under the supervision of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave none to the Kohathites, because they were responsible for the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders.
The leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders presented their offering in front of the altar.
The LORD said to Moses, "Each day one leader, one leader each day, is to present his offering for the dedication of the altar."
The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of Issachar, presented an offering.

He presented as his offering one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
On the third day it was the leader of the people of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day it was the leader of the people of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day it was the leader of the people of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day it was the leader of the people of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.
On the seventh day it was the leader of the people of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day it was the leader of the people of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day it was the leader of the people of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day it was the leader of the people of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day it was the leader of the people of Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.
On the twelfth day it was the leader of the people of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
His offering was one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing seventy shekels, by the sanctuary shekel, both of them full of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering;
one gold dish weighing ten shekels, full of incense;
one young bull, one ram and one year-old male lamb as a burnt offering;
one male goat as a sin offering;
and as the fellowship sacrifice, two head of cattle, five rams, five male goats and five year-old male lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar from the leaders of Israel on the day it was anointed: twelve silver plates, twelve silver basins and twelve gold dishes.
Each silver plate weighed 130 shekels and each basin seventy. All the silver of the vessels came to 2,400 shekels, by the sanctuary shekel.
The twelve gold dishes full of incense weighed ten shekels each, by the sanctuary shekel. All the gold of the dishes came to 120 shekels.
All the cattle for the burnt offering came to twelve bulls, together with twelve rams and twelve year-old male lambs, with their grain offerings, and twelve male goats as a sin offering.

All the cattle for the fellowship sacrifice came to twenty-four bulls, together with sixty rams, sixty male goats and sixty year-old male lambs. This was the dedication offering for the altar after it was anointed.

When Moses went into the tent of meeting to speak with him, he heard the voice speaking to him from above the atonement cover that was on the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim. And he spoke to him.
"Speak to Aaron and tell him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps are to give light in front of the lampstand."
Aaron did so. He set up its lamps to give light in front of the lampstand, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
This is how the lampstand was made. It was hammered work of gold, from its base to its blossoms. It was hammered work. The lampstand was made according to the pattern that the LORD had shown Moses.
"Take the Levites from among the Israelites and make them clean.
This is what you are to do to them to make them clean: sprinkle the water of purification on them, and have them shave their whole bodies and wash their clothes, and so make themselves clean.
Then they are to take a young bull with its grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil, and you are to take a second young bull as a sin offering.
Bring the Levites to the front of the tent of meeting, and assemble the whole community of the Israelites.
When you bring the Levites before the LORD, the Israelites are to lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron is to present the Levites before the LORD as a wave offering from the Israelites, so that they may do the work of the LORD.
"Then the Levites are to lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and you are to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the LORD, to make atonement for the Levites.
Have the Levites stand before Aaron and his sons, and present them as a wave offering to the LORD.
In this way you are to set the Levites apart from among the Israelites, and the Levites will be mine.
After that the Levites may go in to serve at the tent of meeting. You are to make them clean and present them as a wave offering,
for they are wholly given to me from among the Israelites. I have taken them for myself in place of all who first open the womb, the firstborn of all the Israelites.
For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day I struck down every firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart for myself as holy.
And I have taken the Levites in place of all the firstborn among the Israelites.

From among the Israelites I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and his sons, to do the work for the Israelites at the tent of meeting and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no plague will strike the Israelites when the Israelites come near the sanctuary."
Moses and Aaron and the whole community of the Israelites did this to the Levites. The Israelites did to them everything that the LORD had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.
The Levites purified themselves from sin and washed their clothes. Aaron presented them as a wave offering before the LORD, and Aaron made atonement for them to make them clean.
After that the Levites went in to do their work at the tent of meeting under Aaron and his sons. They did to the Levites just as the LORD had commanded Moses concerning them.
"This is what applies to the Levites. From the age of twenty-five a man is to enter the service and do the work of the tent of meeting.
From the age of fifty he is to retire from the service of the work and work no longer.
He may assist his brothers at the tent of meeting in carrying out their duties, but he must not do the work himself. This is how you are to arrange the duties of the Levites."
The LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai in the first month of the second year after they came out of the land of Egypt. He said,
"Let the Israelites keep the Passover at its appointed time.
Keep it at its appointed time, at twilight on the fourteenth day of this month. Keep it in keeping with all its statutes and all its regulations."
So Moses told the Israelites to keep the Passover,
and they kept the Passover in the first month, at twilight on the fourteenth day of the month, in the wilderness of Sinai. The Israelites did everything just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
But there were some men who were unclean because of a dead body, so they could not keep the Passover on that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day,
and those men said to him, "We are unclean because of a dead body. Why should we be kept from presenting the LORD's offering at its appointed time with the other Israelites?"
Moses said to them, "Wait, and I will hear what the LORD commands concerning you."
"Tell the Israelites: If any of you or your descendants is unclean because of a dead body, or is away on a distant journey, he may still keep the Passover to the LORD.
They are to keep it in the second month, at twilight on the fourteenth day. They are to eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They must not leave any of it until morning, and they must not break any of its bones. They are to keep it in keeping with every statute of the Passover.

But if anyone who is clean and is not on a journey fails to keep the Passover, that person is to be cut off from his people, because he did not present the LORD's offering at its appointed time. That man will bear the consequences of his sin.

"If a foreigner living among you wants to keep the Passover to the LORD, he is to keep it in keeping with the statute and the regulation for the Passover. You are to have one statute for the foreigner and for the native-born."
On the day the tabernacle was set up, the cloud covered the tabernacle, the tent of the testimony. From evening until morning it would be over the tabernacle, looking like fire.
That is how it always was. The cloud covered it, and at night it looked like fire.
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the tent, the Israelites would set out after it, and in the place where the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.
At the LORD's command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD's command they camped. As long as the cloud stayed over the tabernacle, they remained in camp.
When the cloud remained over the tabernacle for many days, the Israelites kept the LORD's charge and did not set out.
Sometimes the cloud was over the tabernacle only for a few days. At the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out.
Sometimes the cloud stayed only from evening until morning, and when the cloud lifted in the morning, they set out. Or if it stayed for a day and a night, when the cloud lifted, they set out.

Whether it was two days or a month or a longer time, as long as the cloud remained over the tabernacle, resting on it, the Israelites remained in camp and did not set out. But when it lifted, they set out.
At the LORD's command they camped, and at the LORD's command they set out. They kept the LORD's charge, at the LORD's command through Moses.
"Make two silver trumpets. Make them of hammered work. You are to use them for calling the community together and for setting the camps on the move.
When both are blown, the whole community is to gather before you at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
If only one is blown, the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel, are to gather before you.
When you sound an alarm, the camps on the east side are to set out.
When you sound a second alarm, the camps on the south side are to set out. An alarm is to be sounded whenever they are to set out.
But when the assembly is to be gathered, you are to blow the trumpets without sounding an alarm.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to blow the trumpets. This is to be a permanent statute for you throughout your generations.
When you go to war in your land against an enemy who is oppressing you, sound an alarm on the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before the LORD your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.

Also on your days of rejoicing, at your appointed festivals and at the beginning of your months, blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your fellowship sacrifices. They will be a reminder of you before your God. I am the LORD your God."
In the second year, on the twentieth day of the second month, the cloud lifted from above the tabernacle of the testimony.
The Israelites set out from the wilderness of Sinai, journeying in stages, and the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran.
They set out for the first time at the LORD's command through Moses.
The banner of the camp of Judah set out first, by their divisions. Nahshon son of Amminadab was over its division.
Nethanel son of Zuar was over the division of the tribe of Issachar,
and Eliab son of Helon was over the division of the tribe of Zebulun.
Then the tabernacle was taken down, and the Gershonites and the Merarites, who carried the tabernacle, set out.
Next the banner of the camp of Reuben set out, by their divisions. Elizur son of Shedeur was over its division.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was over the division of the tribe of Simeon,
and Eliasaph son of Deuel was over the division of the tribe of Gad.
Then the Kohathites set out, carrying the holy things. The tabernacle was to be set up before they arrived.
Next the banner of the camp of Ephraim set out, by their divisions. Elishama son of Ammihud was over its division.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was over the division of the tribe of Manasseh,
and Abidan son of Gideoni was over the division of the tribe of Benjamin.
Then the banner of the camp of Dan set out, by their divisions, as the rear guard for all the camps. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was over its division.
Pagiel son of Ochran was over the division of the tribe of Asher,
and Ahira son of Enan was over the division of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the order of march of the Israelites by their divisions when they set out.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses' father-in-law, "We are setting out for the place about which the LORD said, 'I will give it to you.' Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the LORD has promised good things to Israel."
But he said to him, "I will not go. I will go back to my own land and my own relatives."
Moses said, "Please do not leave us. You know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes.
If you come with us, whatever good the LORD does for us, we will do the same for you."
So they set out from the mountain of the LORD and traveled for three days. The ark of the covenant of the LORD went ahead of them during those three days to look for a place for them to rest.
The cloud of the LORD was over them by day when they set out from the camp.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, "Rise up, LORD! May your enemies be scattered, and may those who hate you flee before you."
And whenever it came to rest, he would say, "Return, LORD, to the countless thousands of Israel."
The people began complaining about their hardships in the hearing of the LORD. When the LORD heard it, his anger burned. Fire from the LORD burned among them and consumed the outskirts of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses, Moses prayed to the LORD, and the fire died down.
So that place was named Taberah, because fire from the LORD had burned among them.
The mixed crowd among them had a strong craving, and the Israelites also began weeping again. They said, "If only we had meat to eat!
We remember the fish we used to eat in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers, the melons, the leeks, the onions and the garlic.
But now our appetite is gone. There is nothing at all, nothing for us to look at but this manna!"
The manna was like coriander seed, and it looked like bdellium.
The people went around gathering it. They ground it in hand mills or crushed it in a mortar, boiled it in a pot, and made it into cakes. It tasted like something made with olive oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna fell with it.
Moses heard the people weeping, family by family, each at the entrance of his tent. The LORD became very angry, and Moses was troubled.
Moses said to the LORD, "Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in your eyes, that you put the burden of all this people on me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should say to me, 'Carry them in your arms, as a nurse carries a nursing baby,' to the land you swore to give their ancestors?
Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? They keep weeping to me and saying, 'Give us meat to eat!'
I cannot carry all this people by myself. It is too heavy for me.
If this is how you are going to treat me, please kill me at once, if I have found favor in your eyes, and do not let me see my own misery."

The LORD said to Moses, "Gather for me seventy men from the elders of Israel, men you know to be elders of the people and officials over them. Bring them to the tent of meeting, and have them stand there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is on you and put it on them. They will carry the burden of the people with you, so that you will not have to carry it alone.

"And say to the people: 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, and you will eat meat. You wept in the hearing of the LORD and said, "If only we had meat to eat! We were better off in Egypt!" So the LORD will give you meat, and you will eat it.
You will eat it not just for one day, or two days, or five days, or ten days, or twenty days,

but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and you are sick of it, because you have rejected the LORD who is among you, and you have wept before him, saying, "Why did we ever leave Egypt?"'"
But Moses said, "The people I am among number six hundred thousand men on foot, and you say, 'I will give them meat, and they will eat it for a whole month'!
Could enough flocks and herds be slaughtered for them to have enough? Could all the fish of the sea be caught for them to have enough?"
The LORD said to Moses, "Is the LORD's arm too short? Now you will see whether or not what I say will happen to you."
So Moses went out and told the people the LORD's words. He gathered seventy men from the elders of the people and had them stand around the tent.

Then the LORD came down in the cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders. When the spirit rested on them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

Two men had stayed behind in the camp. One was named Eldad and the other Medad. The spirit rested on them too. They were among those whose names had been written down, but they had not gone out to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and told Moses, "Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!"
Joshua son of Nun, who had been Moses' assistant since his youth, spoke up and said, "Moses, my lord, stop them!"
But Moses said to him, "Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!"
Then Moses went back to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.

A wind went out from the LORD and drove quail in from the sea. It brought them down all around the camp, about a day's journey on one side and a day's journey on the other, about two cubits deep on the ground.
All that day and all night and all the next day the people went out and gathered the quail. No one gathered less than ten homers. They spread them out for themselves all around the camp.
But while the meat was still between their teeth, before it was chewed, the LORD's anger burned against the people, and the LORD struck the people with a very severe plague.
So that place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, because there they buried the people who had had the craving.
From Kibroth-hattaavah the people set out for Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had married a Cushite woman.
They said, "Has the LORD spoken only through Moses? Has he not spoken through us as well?" And the LORD heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more humble than anyone else on the face of the earth.
Suddenly the LORD said to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, "Come out to the tent of meeting, all three of you." So the three of them went out.
The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud and stood at the entrance of the tent. He called Aaron and Miriam, and they both came forward.
He said, "Listen to my words. When there is a prophet among you, I, the LORD, make myself known to him in a vision; I speak to him in a dream.
Not so with my servant Moses. He is trusted in all my house.
With him I speak face to face, plainly and not in riddles, and he sees the form of the LORD. So why were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?"
The LORD's anger burned against them, and he left.
When the cloud moved away from above the tent, there was Miriam, stricken with a skin disease, as white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam and saw that she had the disease.
Aaron said to Moses, "Please, my lord, do not hold against us the sin we have so foolishly committed.
Do not let her be like a stillborn child, whose flesh is half eaten away when it comes out of its mother's womb."
So Moses cried out to the LORD, "O God, please heal her!"
The LORD said to Moses, "If her father had spat in her face, would she not be in disgrace for seven days? Let her be shut outside the camp for seven days. After that she may be brought back."
So Miriam was shut outside the camp for seven days, and the people did not set out until Miriam was brought back.
After that the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
"Send men to explore the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites. Send one man from each ancestral tribe, each of them a leader among them."
So at the LORD's command Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran. All of them were men who were heads of the Israelites.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori;
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, that is, the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
from the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli;
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses gave Hoshea son of Nun the name Joshua.
When Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan, he said to them, "Go up through the Negev, and go up into the hill country.
See what the land is like, and whether the people who live in it are strong or weak, few or many;
whether the land they live in is good or bad; and whether the towns they live in are open camps or fortified.
See whether the land is rich or poor, and whether there are trees in it or not. Be brave, and bring back some of the fruit of the land." It was the season of the first ripe grapes.
So they went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin as far as Rehob, toward Lebo-hamath.
They went up through the Negev and came to Hebron, where Ahiman, Sheshai and Talmai, the descendants of Anak, lived. Hebron had been built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.
They came to the Valley of Eshcol, and there they cut off a branch with a single cluster of grapes. Two of them carried it on a pole, along with some pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the Valley of Eshcol because of the cluster that the Israelites cut off there.
At the end of forty days they returned from exploring the land.

They came back to Moses and Aaron and the whole community of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They brought back a report to them and to the whole community, and showed them the fruit of the land.
They told Moses, "We went into the land where you sent us. It does indeed flow with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
But the people who live in the land are strong, and the towns are fortified and very large. We even saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the land of the Negev. The Hittites, the Jebusites and the Amorites live in the hill country, and the Canaanites live by the sea and along the Jordan."
Then Caleb quieted the people before Moses and said, "Let us go up at once and take possession of it, for we can certainly overcome it."
But the men who had gone up with him said, "We cannot go up against those people, for they are stronger than we are."

So they spread among the Israelites a bad report about the land they had explored. They said, "The land we passed through to explore is a land that devours those who live in it. All the people we saw in it are men of great size.
We saw the Nephilim there, the descendants of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. In our own eyes we seemed like grasshoppers, and that is how we seemed to them."
Then the whole community raised a loud cry, and the people wept that night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole community said to them, "If only we had died in the land of Egypt! Or if only we had died in this wilderness!
Why is the LORD bringing us into this land, only for us to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will be taken as plunder. Wouldn't it be better for us to go back to Egypt?"
And they said to one another, "Let us choose a leader and go back to Egypt."
Then Moses and Aaron fell face down in front of the whole assembly of the community of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored the land, tore their clothes
and said to the whole community of the Israelites, "The land we passed through to explore is an exceedingly good land.
If the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us into this land and give it to us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not be afraid of the people of the land, for we will devour them. Their protection has left them, and the LORD is with us. Do not be afraid of them."
But the whole community talked of stoning them. Then the glory of the LORD appeared at the tent of meeting to all the Israelites.
The LORD said to Moses, "How long will this people treat me with contempt? How long will they refuse to trust me, in spite of all the signs I have done among them?
I will strike them with a plague and disinherit them, and I will make you into a nation greater and mightier than they are."
But Moses said to the LORD, "Then the Egyptians will hear of it, for by your power you brought this people up from among them.

They will tell the people who live in this land. They have heard that you, LORD, are among this people, that you, LORD, are seen face to face, that your cloud stands over them, and that you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.
If you put this people to death all at once, the nations who have heard reports about you will say,
'The LORD was not able to bring this people into the land he swore to give them, so he slaughtered them in the wilderness.'
"So now, please let the power of the Lord be great, just as you have said:

'The LORD is slow to anger and abounding in faithful love, forgiving wrongdoing and rebellion. Yet he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. He punishes the children for the wrongdoing of their fathers, to the third and the fourth generation.'
Please forgive the wrongdoing of this people, in keeping with the greatness of your faithful love, just as you have forgiven this people from Egypt until now."
The LORD said, "I have forgiven them, as you asked.
But as surely as I live, and as surely as the whole earth will be filled with the glory of the LORD,
not one of the men who have seen my glory and the signs I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and yet have tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice,
will see the land I swore to give their ancestors. None of those who treated me with contempt will see it.
But because my servant Caleb has a different spirit and has followed me wholeheartedly, I will bring him into the land he went to, and his descendants will possess it.
Now the Amalekites and the Canaanites live in the valley. Tomorrow turn back and set out for the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea."
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"How long must I put up with this wicked community that keeps grumbling against me? I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites, which they keep making against me.
Say to them: 'As surely as I live, declares the LORD, I will do to you exactly what I heard you say.
Your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness, all of you who were registered, by your full number, those twenty years old or more who have grumbled against me.
Not one of you will enter the land where I swore to settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But your little ones, who you said would be taken as plunder, I will bring in, and they will come to know the land you have rejected.
But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will be shepherds in the wilderness for forty years. They will suffer for your unfaithfulness until the last of your dead bodies lies in the wilderness.
You explored the land for forty days. For forty years, a year for each day, you will bear the consequences of your wrongdoing, and you will know what it is to have me against you.
I, the LORD, have spoken. I will certainly do this to this whole wicked community that has banded together against me. In this wilderness they will come to an end, and there they will die.'"
The men Moses had sent to explore the land, who returned and made the whole community grumble against him by spreading a bad report about the land,
those men who spread the bad report about the land died of a plague before the LORD.
Of the men who went to explore the land, only Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh remained alive.
When Moses told these words to all the Israelites, the people mourned bitterly.
Early the next morning they set out to go up to the heights of the hill country. They said, "Here we are. We will go up to the place the LORD spoke of, for we have sinned."
But Moses said, "Why are you disobeying the LORD's command? It will not succeed.
Do not go up, for the LORD is not with you. Do not let yourselves be struck down by your enemies.
For the Amalekites and the Canaanites are there ahead of you, and you will fall by the sword. Because you have turned back from following the LORD, the LORD will not be with you."
But they defiantly went up to the heights of the hill country, though neither the ark of the covenant of the LORD nor Moses left the camp.
Then the Amalekites and the Canaanites who lived in that hill country came down and struck them and beat them down as far as Hormah.
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land where you are to live, which I am giving you,

and you present to the LORD an offering by fire, whether a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a special vow or as a freewill offering or at your appointed festivals, to make a pleasing aroma for the LORD from the herd or from the flock,
the one who brings his offering is to present to the LORD a grain offering of a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil.
With each lamb for the burnt offering or the sacrifice, you are also to prepare a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering.
For a ram, prepare a grain offering of two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil,
and present a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
When you prepare a young bull as a burnt offering or a sacrifice, to fulfill a special vow or as a fellowship offering to the LORD,
you are to present with the young bull a grain offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil,
and you are to present half a hin of wine as a drink offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
This is how it is to be done for each bull or each ram, or for each lamb or young goat.
However many you prepare, do this for each one, according to their number.
Everyone who is native-born is to do these things in this way when he presents an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
If a foreigner is living with you, or anyone else who is among you throughout your generations, and he presents an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, he is to do just as you do.

For the assembly there is to be one statute for you and for the foreigner who lives among you. It is a permanent statute throughout your generations: you and the foreigner are to be alike before the LORD.
There is to be one law and one regulation for you and for the foreigner who lives among you."
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you come into the land where I am bringing you
and you eat the food of the land, you are to set aside a contribution for the LORD.
From the first of your dough you are to set aside a loaf as a contribution. Set it aside just as you do the contribution from the threshing floor.
Throughout your generations you are to give the LORD a contribution from the first of your dough.
"But suppose you unintentionally fail to keep all these commands that the LORD gave Moses,
everything that the LORD has commanded you through Moses, from the day the LORD gave his commands and on throughout your generations.

If it was done unintentionally, without the community being aware of it, the whole community is to offer one young bull as a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma to the LORD, with its grain offering and its drink offering as prescribed, and one male goat as a sin offering.

The priest is to make atonement for the whole community of the Israelites, and they will be forgiven, because it was unintentional, and they have brought their offering, an offering by fire to the LORD, and their sin offering before the LORD for their unintentional wrong.
The whole community of the Israelites will be forgiven, and the foreigner who lives among them, because all the people were involved in the unintentional wrong.
"If one person sins unintentionally, he is to present a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest is to make atonement before the LORD for the person who has done wrong by sinning unintentionally, to make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
You are to have one law for anyone who acts unintentionally, whether he is a native-born Israelite or a foreigner who lives among them.
But anyone who acts defiantly, whether native-born or foreigner, is insulting the LORD. That person is to be cut off from among his people.
Because he has despised the word of the LORD and broken his command, that person must certainly be cut off. His guilt remains on him."
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him gathering wood brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the whole community.
They put him in custody, because it had not been made clear what should be done to him.
Then the LORD said to Moses, "The man must be put to death. The whole community is to stone him outside the camp."
So the whole community took him outside the camp and stoned him to death, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
"Speak to the Israelites and tell them to make tassels on the corners of their garments throughout their generations, and to put a blue cord on the tassel at each corner.
You will have the tassel so that when you see it you will remember all the LORD's commands and do them, and not go about following your own heart and your own eyes, which lead you to be unfaithful.
So you will remember and do all my commands, and you will be holy to your God.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the LORD your God."
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, took action, together with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, who were descendants of Reuben.
They rose up against Moses, along with 250 Israelite men, leaders of the community, chosen from the assembly, men of renown.

They assembled against Moses and Aaron and said to them, "You have gone too far! The whole community is holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them. So why do you set yourselves above the assembly of the LORD?"
When Moses heard this, he fell face down.

Then he said to Korah and all his followers, "In the morning the LORD will make known who belongs to him and who is holy, and he will let that one come near to him. The one he chooses he will let come near to him.
Do this, Korah and all your followers: take censers.
Tomorrow put fire in them and put incense on them before the LORD. The man the LORD chooses will be the one who is holy. You have gone too far, you Levites!"
Moses said to Korah, "Listen, you Levites!

Is it not enough for you that the God of Israel has set you apart from the community of Israel to bring you near to himself, to do the work of the LORD's tabernacle, and to stand before the community and serve them?
He has brought you near, and all your fellow Levites with you, and now you are seeking the priesthood as well?
So it is against the LORD that you and all your followers have banded together. As for Aaron, who is he, that you grumble against him?"
Then Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, "We will not come up!
Is it not enough that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey to kill us in the wilderness? Must you also make yourself a prince over us?
What is more, you have not brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, or given us an inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you gouge out the eyes of these men? We will not come up!"
Moses became very angry and said to the LORD, "Do not accept their offering. I have not taken a single donkey from them, and I have not harmed any one of them."
Moses said to Korah, "You and all your followers are to appear before the LORD tomorrow, you and they and Aaron.
Each of you is to take his censer and put incense on it, and each of you is to present his censer before the LORD, 250 censers. You and Aaron are also to bring your censers."
So each man took his censer, put fire in it and placed incense on it, and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting with Moses and Aaron.
When Korah had gathered the whole community against them at the entrance of the tent of meeting, the glory of the LORD appeared to the whole community.
The LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Separate yourselves from this community, so that I may destroy them in an instant."
But they fell face down and said, "O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, when one man sins, will you be angry with the whole community?"
"Tell the community: 'Move away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram.'"
Then Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
He said to the community, "Move away from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything that belongs to them, or you will be swept away because of all their sins."

So they moved away from around the dwelling of Korah, Dathan and Abiram. Dathan and Abiram had come out and were standing at the entrance of their tents with their wives, their children and their little ones.
Moses said, "This is how you will know that the LORD has sent me to do all these things, and that it was not my own idea.
If these men die a natural death, as all people do, and if they suffer the fate of all people, then the LORD has not sent me.

But if the LORD brings about something new, and the ground opens its mouth and swallows them and everything that belongs to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then you will know that these men have treated the LORD with contempt."
As soon as he had finished saying all these words, the ground under them split open.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and their households, and all the people who belonged to Korah, and all their possessions.
They and everything that belonged to them went down alive into Sheol. The earth closed over them, and they vanished from among the assembly.
All the Israelites who were around them fled at their cry, for they said, "The earth may swallow us too!"
And fire came out from the LORD and consumed the 250 men who were offering the incense.
"Tell Eleazar son of Aaron the priest to take the censers out of the blaze, and to scatter the coals some distance away, for the censers are holy.

Take the censers of these men who sinned at the cost of their own lives, and have them hammered into thin sheets as plating for the altar. They were presented before the LORD, and so they have become holy. Let them be a sign to the Israelites."
So Eleazar the priest took the bronze censers that had been presented by those who were burned, and they were hammered out as plating for the altar,

as a reminder to the Israelites that no outsider, no one who is not a descendant of Aaron, should come near to burn incense before the LORD, so that he would not become like Korah and his followers. This was as the LORD had told him through Moses.
The next day the whole community of the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron. "You have killed the LORD's people," they said.
But when the community had assembled against Moses and Aaron, they turned toward the tent of meeting, and there was the cloud covering it, and the glory of the LORD appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the tent of meeting,
and the LORD said to Moses,
"Get away from this community, so that I may destroy them in an instant." And they fell face down.

Moses said to Aaron, "Take the censer, put fire from the altar in it, and put incense on it. Then go quickly to the community and make atonement for them, for wrath has gone out from the LORD. The plague has begun."
Aaron took it, as Moses had said, and ran into the middle of the assembly. The plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.
Those who died in the plague numbered 14,700, besides those who had died because of Korah.
Then Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance of the tent of meeting, for the plague had been stopped.
"Speak to the Israelites and get a staff from them for each ancestral family, one from each of their leaders by their ancestral families, twelve staffs. Write each man's name on his staff.
Write Aaron's name on the staff of Levi, for there is to be one staff for the head of each ancestral family.
Place them in the tent of meeting in front of the testimony, where I meet with you.
The staff of the man I choose will sprout. In this way I will rid myself of the grumbling of the Israelites, which they keep making against you."
So Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him a staff, one for each leader, by their ancestral families, twelve staffs. Aaron's staff was among their staffs.
Moses placed the staffs before the LORD in the tent of the testimony.
The next day Moses went into the tent of the testimony, and there was Aaron's staff, the staff for the house of Levi. It had sprouted. It had put out buds, produced blossoms and borne ripe almonds.
Then Moses brought out all the staffs from the LORD's presence to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his own staff.
The LORD said to Moses, "Put Aaron's staff back in front of the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the rebels, so that you may put an end to their grumbling against me, and they will not die."
Moses did so. He did just as the LORD had commanded him.
The Israelites said to Moses, "We are going to die! We are lost, all of us lost!
Everyone who comes near, anyone who comes near to the LORD's tabernacle, will die. Are we all going to perish?"

The LORD said to Aaron, "You and your sons and your father's family with you will bear the guilt for offenses against the sanctuary, and you and your sons with you will bear the guilt for offenses against your priesthood.
Bring with you also your relatives, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, so that they may join you and serve you while you and your sons with you are in front of the tent of the testimony.
They are to carry out their duties to you and their duties for the whole tent. But they must not come near the holy furnishings or the altar, or both they and you will die.
They are to join you and carry out the duties of the tent of meeting, all the work of the tent. No outsider may come near you.
You are to carry out the duties of the sanctuary and the duties of the altar, so that wrath will not come on the Israelites again.
I myself have taken your relatives the Levites from among the Israelites. They are a gift to you, given to the LORD, to do the work of the tent of meeting.

But you and your sons with you are to carry out your priesthood in everything that concerns the altar and what is inside the veil. You are to do this service. I am giving you your priesthood as a gift. Any outsider who comes near is to be put to death."

Then the LORD spoke to Aaron: "I myself have put you in charge of the contributions made to me. All the holy gifts of the Israelites I have given to you and to your sons as your portion, as your permanent share.

This will be yours from the most holy offerings, kept back from the fire: every offering of theirs, every grain offering, every sin offering and every guilt offering that they give back to me. It is most holy, for you and for your sons.
You are to eat it as a most holy thing. Every male may eat it. It is to be holy to you.

This also is yours: the contribution from their gifts, all the wave offerings of the Israelites. I have given them to you, and to your sons and your daughters with you, as your permanent share. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the best of the fresh olive oil and all the best of the new wine and the grain, the first portion of them that they give to the LORD, I have given to you.
The first ripe fruits of everything in their land, which they bring to the LORD, will be yours. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat them.
Everything in Israel that is devoted will be yours.

Every firstborn of every living creature that is offered to the LORD, whether human or animal, will be yours. But you must redeem the firstborn of human beings, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
As for their redemption price, you are to redeem them from the age of one month, at the fixed value: five shekels of silver, by the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty gerahs.

But you must not redeem the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat. They are holy. Splash their blood against the altar, and burn their fat as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
Their meat will be yours, just as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours.

All the holy contributions that the Israelites present to the LORD I have given to you, and to your sons and your daughters with you, as your permanent share. It is a covenant of salt forever before the LORD, for you and for your descendants with you."
The LORD said to Aaron, "You will have no inheritance in their land, and you will have no share among them. I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.
"To the Levites I have given every tithe in Israel as their inheritance, in return for the work they do, the work of the tent of meeting.
The Israelites must never again come near the tent of meeting, or they will incur sin and die.

The Levites are the ones who are to do the work of the tent of meeting, and they will bear their guilt. This is a permanent decree for all your generations. They will have no inheritance among the Israelites.

For I have given to the Levites as their inheritance the tithe of the Israelites, which they present to the LORD as a contribution. That is why I have said of them, 'They will have no inheritance among the Israelites.'"

"Speak to the Levites and tell them: 'When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your inheritance, you are to present a contribution from it to the LORD, a tenth of the tithe.
Your contribution will be counted for you as if it were grain from the threshing floor or the full yield of the winepress.
In the same way you too are to present a contribution to the LORD from all the tithes that you receive from the Israelites. From them you are to give the LORD's contribution to Aaron the priest.
From all the gifts you receive you are to present every contribution due to the LORD, from all the best of it, the part of it that is holy.'
"Say to them, 'When you present the best of it, it will be counted for the Levites as the produce of the threshing floor and the produce of the winepress.
You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, because it is your wages in return for your work at the tent of meeting.
You will not incur sin because of it once you have presented the best of it. But you must not profane the holy gifts of the Israelites, so that you will not die.'"
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron:
"This is the rule of the law that the LORD has commanded: Tell the Israelites to bring you a red heifer without defect, which has no blemish and has never been under a yoke.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. It is to be taken outside the camp and slaughtered in his presence.
Eleazar the priest is to take some of its blood on his finger and sprinkle some of its blood seven times toward the front of the tent of meeting.
Then the heifer is to be burned while he watches. Its hide, its flesh and its blood are to be burned, together with its dung.
The priest is to take cedar wood, hyssop and scarlet yarn, and throw them into the fire where the heifer is burning.
Then the priest must wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. After that he may come into the camp, but the priest will be unclean until evening.
The one who burns the heifer must also wash his clothes in water and bathe his body in water, and he will be unclean until evening.

"A man who is clean is to gather up the ashes of the heifer and put them in a clean place outside the camp. They are to be kept for the community of the Israelites for the water for impurity. It is a sin offering.

The one who gathers up the ashes of the heifer must wash his clothes, and he will be unclean until evening. This is to be a permanent decree for the Israelites and for the foreigner who lives among them.
"Whoever touches the dead body of any human being will be unclean for seven days.

He must purify himself with the water on the third day and on the seventh day, and then he will be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he will not be clean.

Whoever touches a dead body, the body of any human being who has died, and does not purify himself, defiles the tabernacle of the LORD. That person is to be cut off from Israel. Because the water for impurity has not been splashed on him, he is unclean. His uncleanness is still on him.
"This is the law when someone dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent and everyone who is in the tent will be unclean for seven days.
Every open container that has no lid fastened on it will be unclean.
And anyone out in the open who touches someone killed by the sword, or someone who has died, or a human bone, or a grave, will be unclean for seven days.
"For the unclean person, they are to take some of the ashes from the burning of the sin offering and pour fresh water over them in a container.

Then a man who is clean is to take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the furnishings, and on the people who were there. He is also to sprinkle it on anyone who touched the bone, or the one who was killed, or the one who died, or the grave.

The clean person is to sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day. On the seventh day he is to purify him. Then the person being purified must wash his clothes and bathe in water, and in the evening he will be clean.

But anyone who becomes unclean and does not purify himself is to be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD. The water for impurity has not been splashed on him. He is unclean.
This is to be a permanent decree for them. The one who sprinkles the water for impurity must wash his clothes, and whoever touches the water for impurity will be unclean until evening.
Anything that the unclean person touches will be unclean, and anyone who touches it will be unclean until evening."
The Israelites, the whole community, came into the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the community, and they gathered together against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses. They said, "If only we had died when our brothers died before the LORD!
Why have you brought the LORD's assembly into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die here?
Why did you bring us up out of Egypt, to bring us to this terrible place? It is no place for grain, or figs, or vines, or pomegranates, and there is no water to drink!"
Moses and Aaron went away from the assembly to the entrance of the tent of meeting and fell face down. Then the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

"Take the staff, and gather the community together, you and Aaron your brother. Speak to the rock while they watch, and it will give out its water. So you will bring water out of the rock for them, and give the community and their livestock water to drink."
So Moses took the staff from before the LORD, as he had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly together in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, "Listen, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?"
Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff. Water came out in abundance, and the community and their livestock drank.
But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "Because you did not trust me enough to show my holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them."
These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and he showed his holiness among them.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom: "This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has come upon us.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt, and we lived in Egypt for a long time. The Egyptians treated us and our ancestors badly.
We cried out to the LORD, and he heard our voice and sent an angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now here we are at Kadesh, a town on the edge of your territory.

Please let us pass through your land. We will not go through any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from any well. We will keep to the King's Highway. We will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory."
But Edom answered him, "You will not pass through my land, or I will come out against you with the sword."
The Israelites said to him, "We will go up by the main road. If we drink any of your water, I and my livestock, I will pay for it. Let me only pass through on foot. That is all."
But Edom said, "You will not pass through." And Edom came out against them with a large army and a strong force.
So Edom refused to let Israel pass through its territory, and Israel turned away from it.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole community, came to Mount Hor.
At Mount Hor, on the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,
"Aaron is to be gathered to his people. He will not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you both rebelled against my command at the waters of Meribah.
Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up Mount Hor.
Take Aaron's garments off him and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there."
Moses did as the LORD had commanded. They went up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole community.
Moses took Aaron's garments off him and put them on Eleazar his son, and Aaron died there on the top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
When the whole community saw that Aaron had died, all the house of Israel mourned for Aaron thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev, heard that Israel was coming by the road to Atharim. He fought against Israel and took some of them captive.
Then Israel made a vow to the LORD: "If you will hand this people over to me, I will completely destroy their towns."
The LORD listened to Israel's voice and handed the Canaanites over. They completely destroyed them and their towns, and the place was named Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor by the road to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom. But the people grew impatient on the way.
The people spoke against God and against Moses: "Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? There is no bread and there is no water, and we are sick of this miserable food!"
Then the LORD sent fiery snakes among the people. They bit the people, and many of the people of Israel died.
The people came to Moses and said, "We have sinned, because we have spoken against the LORD and against you. Pray to the LORD to take the snakes away from us." So Moses prayed for the people.
The LORD said to Moses, "Make a fiery snake and put it on a pole. Anyone who has been bitten can look at it and live."
So Moses made a bronze snake and put it on the pole. Whenever a snake bit someone, and he looked at the bronze snake, he lived.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, in the wilderness that faces Moab, toward the sunrise.
From there they set out and camped in the Zered Valley.

From there they set out and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the wilderness that extends from the territory of the Amorites. For the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites.
That is why it is said in the Book of the Wars of the LORD: "… Waheb in Suphah, and the valleys of the Arnon,
and the slope of the valleys that stretches toward the settlement of Ar and lies along the border of Moab."
From there they went on to Beer. That is the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water."
Then Israel sang this song: "Spring up, O well! Sing to it!
The well that the princes dug, that the nobles of the people hollowed out with the scepter, with their staffs." From the wilderness they went on to Mattanah,
from Mattanah to Nahaliel, from Nahaliel to Bamoth,
and from Bamoth to the valley in the country of Moab, by the top of Pisgah, which looks down over the wasteland.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying,

"Let me pass through your land. We will not turn aside into any field or vineyard, and we will not drink water from any well. We will keep to the King's Highway until we have passed through your territory."
But Sihon would not let Israel pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness against Israel. He came to Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel struck him down with the sword and took possession of his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for the border of the Ammonites was strongly held.
Israel took all these towns, and Israel settled in all the towns of the Amorites, in Heshbon and all its villages.
For Heshbon was the city of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had fought against the former king of Moab and taken all his land from him as far as the Arnon.
That is why the poets say: "Come to Heshbon! Let it be rebuilt! Let the city of Sihon be restored!
For fire went out from Heshbon, a flame from the town of Sihon. It consumed Ar of Moab, the lords of the heights of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You are destroyed, people of Chemosh! He has made his sons fugitives and given his daughters into captivity to Sihon king of the Amorites.
But we shot them down. Heshbon is destroyed as far as Dibon. We laid waste as far as Nophah, which reaches to Medeba."
So Israel settled in the land of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to spy out Jazer, and they captured its villages and drove out the Amorites who were there.
Then they turned and went up by the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against them, he and all his people, to do battle at Edrei.
The LORD said to Moses, "Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon."
So they struck him down, with his sons and all his people, until no survivor was left to him. And they took possession of his land.
Then the Israelites set out and camped in the plains of Moab, on the other side of the Jordan from Jericho.
Balak son of Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amorites.
Moab was terrified of the people, because there were so many of them. Moab was filled with dread because of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, "This horde will now lick up everything around us, as an ox licks up the grass of the field." Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab at that time.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which is by the River, in the land of his own people, to summon him. He said, "Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They cover the face of the land, and they have settled opposite me.

Now please come and curse this people for me, for they are too strong for me. Perhaps I will be able to defeat them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless is blessed, and whoever you curse is cursed."
So the elders of Moab and the elders of Midian set out, with the fee for divination in their hands. They came to Balaam and told him what Balak had said.
Balaam said to them, "Stay here tonight, and I will bring you back whatever answer the LORD gives me." So the officials of Moab stayed with Balaam.
Then God came to Balaam and said, "Who are these men with you?"
Balaam said to God, "Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, has sent them to me with this message:
'Look, the people that has come out of Egypt covers the face of the land. Now come and put a curse on them for me. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them and drive them out.'"
But God said to Balaam, "Do not go with them. You must not curse the people, for they are blessed."
Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak's officials, "Go back to your own country, for the LORD has refused to let me go with you."
So the officials of Moab got up and went back to Balak and said, "Balaam refused to come with us."
Balak sent officials once again, more of them and more distinguished than the first.
They came to Balaam and said to him, "This is what Balak son of Zippor says: Please do not let anything stop you from coming to me.
For I will reward you very richly, and I will do whatever you tell me. Please come and put a curse on this people for me."
But Balaam answered Balak's servants, "Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD my God to do anything, small or great.
Now please stay here tonight as well, so that I may find out what more the LORD will say to me."
God came to Balaam at night and said to him, "If the men have come to summon you, get up and go with them. But you must do only what I tell you."
So Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with the officials of Moab.
But God's anger burned because he was going, and the angel of the LORD took his stand in the road to oppose him. Balaam was riding on his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

The donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand, so the donkey turned off the road and went into the field. Balaam beat the donkey to turn her back onto the road.
Then the angel of the LORD stood in a narrow path between the vineyards, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she pressed herself against the wall and crushed Balaam's foot against the wall. So he beat her again.
Then the angel of the LORD went on ahead and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn aside, either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she lay down under Balaam. Balaam's anger burned, and he beat the donkey with his stick.
Then the LORD opened the donkey's mouth, and she said to Balaam, "What have I done to you, that you have beaten me these three times?"
Balaam said to the donkey, "You have made a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would kill you right now."
The donkey said to Balaam, "Am I not your donkey, which you have ridden all your life until this day? Have I ever been in the habit of doing this to you?" "No," he said.
Then the LORD opened Balaam's eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with his sword drawn in his hand. He bowed down and fell face down to the ground.
The angel of the LORD said to him, "Why have you beaten your donkey these three times? I have come out to oppose you, because your way is reckless before me.
The donkey saw me and turned aside from me these three times. If she had not turned aside from me, I would certainly have killed you by now and let her live."
Balaam said to the angel of the LORD, "I have sinned. I did not know that you were standing in the road against me. Now if this displeases you, I will go back."
The angel of the LORD said to Balaam, "Go with the men, but you must say only what I tell you." So Balaam went with Balak's officials.
When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went out to meet him at Ir-moab, which is on the Arnon border, at the farthest edge of the territory.
Balak said to Balaam, "Did I not send for you urgently to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Am I really not able to reward you?"
Balaam said to Balak, "Well, I have come to you now. But do I have the power to say anything at all? I can speak only the word that God puts in my mouth."
Then Balaam went with Balak, and they came to Kiriath-huzoth.
Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep, and sent some to Balaam and to the officials who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to Bamoth-baal. From there he could see the edge of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and Balak and Balaam offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Then Balaam said to Balak, "Stand beside your burnt offering while I go. Perhaps the LORD will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me, I will tell you." And he went off to a bare height.
God met Balaam, and Balaam said to him, "I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered a bull and a ram on each altar."
The LORD put a word in Balaam's mouth and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
So he went back to him, and there was Balak, standing beside his burnt offering, he and all the officials of Moab.
Then Balaam spoke his oracle: "Balak has brought me from Aram, the king of Moab from the mountains of the east. 'Come, curse Jacob for me! Come, denounce Israel!'
How can I curse those whom God has not cursed? How can I denounce those whom the LORD has not denounced?
From the top of the rocks I see them; from the hills I watch them. Here is a people that lives apart, and does not count itself among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob, or number a fourth part of Israel? Let me die the death of the upright, and let my end be like theirs!"
Balak said to Balaam, "What have you done to me? I brought you to curse my enemies, and instead you have done nothing but bless them!"
