He answered, "Must I not take care to say what the LORD puts in my mouth?"
Then Balak said to him, "Please come with me to another place, where you can see them. You will see only the edge of them; you will not see all of them. Curse them for me from there."
So he took him to the Field of Zophim, on the top of Pisgah. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
Balaam said to Balak, "Stand here beside your burnt offering while I meet with him over there."
The LORD met Balaam and put a word in his mouth, and said, "Go back to Balak, and this is what you are to say."
So he came to him, and there was Balak, standing beside his burnt offering, with the officials of Moab. Balak asked him, "What did the LORD say?"
Then Balaam spoke his oracle: "Get up, Balak, and listen! Hear me, son of Zippor!
God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he said it, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not carry it out?
Look, I have received a command to bless. He has blessed, and I cannot turn it back.
He sees no wrongdoing in Jacob; he finds no trouble in Israel. The LORD their God is with them, and the shout of a king is among them.
God is bringing them out of Egypt; they have the strength of a wild ox.
For there is no omen against Jacob, no divination against Israel. Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel, 'See what God has done!'
Look, a people rises up like a lioness, and raises itself like a lion. It does not lie down until it has eaten its prey and drunk the blood of the slain."
Then Balak said to Balaam, "Do not curse them at all, and do not bless them at all!"
Balaam answered Balak, "Did I not tell you, 'Whatever the LORD says, that is what I must do'?"
Balak said to Balaam, "Please come, and I will take you to another place. Perhaps it will be right in God's eyes for you to curse them for me from there."
So Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which looks down over the wasteland.
Balaam said to Balak, "Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here."
Balak did as Balaam had said, and offered a bull and a ram on each altar.
When Balaam saw that it pleased the LORD to bless Israel, he did not go as at the other times to look for omens. Instead he turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam looked up and saw Israel camped tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
Then he spoke his oracle: "The utterance of Balaam son of Beor, the utterance of the man whose eye is opened,
the utterance of one who hears the words of God, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down, yet with his eyes uncovered:
How beautiful are your tents, Jacob, your dwelling places, Israel!
Like valleys they stretch out, like gardens beside a river, like aloes that the LORD has planted, like cedars beside the waters.
Water will flow from his buckets, and his seed will be by abundant waters. His king will be greater than Agag, and his kingdom will be exalted.
God is bringing him out of Egypt; he has the strength of a wild ox. He will devour the nations that are his enemies; he will crush their bones and pierce them with his arrows.
He crouches, he lies down like a lion, like a lioness: who dares to rouse him? Blessed is everyone who blesses you, and cursed is everyone who curses you!"
Balak's anger burned against Balaam, and he struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, "I summoned you to curse my enemies, and instead you have blessed them these three times!
Now go back home at once! I said I would reward you richly, but the LORD has kept you from being rewarded."
Balaam said to Balak, "Did I not also tell the messengers you sent to me,
'Even if Balak gave me his house full of silver and gold, I could not go beyond the command of the LORD to do anything good or bad of my own will. Whatever the LORD says, that is what I will say'?
Now I am going back to my people. Come, let me tell you what this people will do to your people in days to come."
Then he spoke his oracle: "The utterance of Balaam son of Beor, the utterance of the man whose eye is opened,
the utterance of one who hears the words of God, who has knowledge from the Most High, who sees the vision of the Almighty, who falls down, yet with his eyes uncovered:
I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not near. A star will march out of Jacob; a scepter will rise out of Israel. He will crush the foreheads of Moab, and tear down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will become a conquered land; Seir, his enemy, will become a conquered land, while Israel acts with strength.
One from Jacob will rule, and destroy the survivors of the city."
Then Balaam saw Amalek and spoke his oracle: "Amalek was the first of the nations, but its end will be destruction."
Then he saw the Kenites and spoke his oracle: "Your dwelling place is secure, and your nest is set in the rock.
Yet Kain will be burned. How long until Asshur takes you captive?"
Then he spoke his oracle: "Alas, who can survive when God does this?
Ships will come from the coast of Kittim. They will humble Asshur and humble Eber, but he too will come to destruction."
Then Balaam got up and went back to his place, and Balak also went his way.
While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people began to commit sexual immorality with the women of Moab.
The women invited the people to the sacrifices to their gods, and the people ate and bowed down to their gods.
So Israel joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor, and the LORD's anger burned against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, "Take all the leaders of the people and execute them before the LORD in broad daylight, so that the LORD's fierce anger may turn away from Israel."
So Moses said to the judges of Israel, "Each of you must kill those of his men who have joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor."

Just then one of the Israelites came and brought a Midianite woman to his family, in the sight of Moses and in the sight of the whole community of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance of the tent of meeting.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he got up from among the community and took a spear in his hand.
He went after the Israelite man into the inner tent and drove the spear through both of them, the Israelite man and the woman, through her belly. Then the plague on the Israelites was stopped.
Those who died in the plague numbered 24,000.
"Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the Israelites, because he was zealous with my zeal among them, so that I did not wipe out the Israelites in my zeal.
Therefore say: 'I am giving him my covenant of peace.
It will be for him and for his descendants after him a covenant of a permanent priesthood, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.'"
The name of the Israelite man who was killed, who was killed with the Midianite woman, was Zimri son of Salu, the leader of an ancestral family of the Simeonites.
The name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur. He was the tribal head of an ancestral family in Midian.
"Treat the Midianites as enemies and strike them down,

because they treated you as enemies by the tricks they used to deceive you in the matter of Peor, and in the matter of Cozbi, the daughter of a leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the plague that came because of Peor."
The LORD said to Moses and to Eleazar son of Aaron the priest,
"Take a census of the whole community of the Israelites, those twenty years old or more, by their ancestral families: everyone in Israel who is able to serve in the army."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest spoke with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho. They said,
"Take a census of those twenty years old or more, as the LORD commanded Moses." The Israelites who came out of the land of Egypt were these:
Reuben was Israel's firstborn. The descendants of Reuben: of Hanoch, the clan of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These were the clans of the Reubenites. Those registered numbered 43,730.
The son of Pallu was Eliab.

The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan and Abiram. These were the same Dathan and Abiram, chosen men of the community, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron with Korah's followers, when they rebelled against the LORD.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up together with Korah, when his followers died, when the fire consumed 250 men. They became a warning.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
The descendants of Simeon by their clans: of Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites;
of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These were the clans of the Simeonites: 22,200.
The descendants of Gad by their clans: of Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites;
of Ozni, the clan of the Oznites; of Eri, the clan of the Erites;
of Arod, the clan of the Arodites; of Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Gad. Those registered numbered 40,500.
The sons of Judah were Er and Onan, but Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
The descendants of Judah by their clans were: of Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; of Perez, the clan of the Perezites; of Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
The descendants of Perez were: of Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These were the clans of Judah. Those registered numbered 76,500.
The descendants of Issachar by their clans: of Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the clan of the Punites;
of Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These were the clans of Issachar. Those registered numbered 64,300.
The descendants of Zebulun by their clans: of Sered, the clan of the Seredites; of Elon, the clan of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These were the clans of the Zebulunites. Those registered numbered 60,500.
The descendants of Joseph by their clans were Manasseh and Ephraim.
The descendants of Manasseh: of Machir, the clan of the Machirites. Machir was the father of Gilead. Of Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.
These were the descendants of Gilead: of Iezer, the clan of the Iezerites; of Helek, the clan of the Helekites;
of Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; of Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites;
of Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; of Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
Zelophehad son of Hepher had no sons, only daughters. The names of Zelophehad's daughters were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
These were the clans of Manasseh. Those registered numbered 52,700.
These were the descendants of Ephraim by their clans: of Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the clan of the Becherites; of Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
These were the descendants of Shuthelah: of Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These were the clans of the descendants of Ephraim. Those registered numbered 32,500. These were the descendants of Joseph by their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin by their clans: of Bela, the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites;
of Shephupham, the clan of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the clan of the Huphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman: the clan of the Ardites; of Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These were the descendants of Benjamin by their clans. Those registered numbered 45,600.
These were the descendants of Dan by their clans: of Shuham, the clan of the Shuhamites. These were the clans of Dan, by their clans.
All the clans of the Shuhamites, those registered, numbered 64,400.
The descendants of Asher by their clans: of Imnah, the clan of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
Of the descendants of Beriah: of Heber, the clan of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
The name of Asher's daughter was Serah.
These were the clans of the descendants of Asher. Those registered numbered 53,400.
The descendants of Naphtali by their clans: of Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the clan of the Gunites;
of Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These were the clans of Naphtali by their clans. Those registered numbered 45,400.
"The land is to be divided among these as their inheritance, according to the number of names.
To a large group you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a small group a smaller inheritance. Each is to be given its inheritance according to the number of those registered in it.
But the land is to be divided by lot. They are to receive their inheritance according to the names of their ancestral tribes.
Each inheritance is to be divided by lot, between the larger and the smaller."
These were the Levites registered by their clans: of Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; of Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These were the clans of Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mahlites, the clan of the Mushites, the clan of the Korahites. Kohath was the father of Amram.
The name of Amram's wife was Jochebed daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi in Egypt. She bore to Amram Aaron and Moses and their sister Miriam.
To Aaron were born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar.
But Nadab and Abihu died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD.
Those registered numbered 23,000, every male a month old or more. They were not registered among the Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites.
These were the people registered by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who registered the Israelites in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
Among them there was not one of those registered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they registered the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the LORD had said of them, "They will certainly die in the wilderness." Not one of them was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Then the daughters of Zelophehad came forward. Zelophehad was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh son of Joseph. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, Eleazar the priest, the leaders and the whole community at the entrance of the tent of meeting, and said,
"Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the group that gathered together against the LORD in Korah's company. He died because of his own sin, and he had no sons.
Why should our father's name disappear from his clan because he had no son? Give us property among our father's brothers."
So Moses brought their case before the LORD.
"The daughters of Zelophehad are right in what they say. You must give them property as an inheritance among their father's brothers, and pass on their father's inheritance to them.
And tell the Israelites: 'If a man dies and has no son, you are to pass on his inheritance to his daughter.
If he has no daughter, you are to give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to his father's brothers.

If his father has no brothers, you are to give his inheritance to the nearest relative in his clan, and he is to take possession of it.' This is to be a rule of law for the Israelites, as the LORD commanded Moses."
The LORD said to Moses, "Go up this mountain in the Abarim range and look at the land that I have given to the Israelites.
When you have seen it, you too will be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered.

For in the wilderness of Zin, when the community quarreled, you both rebelled against my command to show my holiness at the waters before their eyes." These were the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin.
Moses spoke to the LORD, saying,
"May the LORD, the God of the spirits of all living beings, appoint a man over the community
who will go out before them and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the LORD's community will not be like sheep that have no shepherd."
The LORD said to Moses, "Take Joshua son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community, and commission him in their sight.
Give him some of your authority, so that the whole community of the Israelites will obey him.

He is to stand before Eleazar the priest, who will ask for him the decision of the Urim before the LORD. At his word they will go out, and at his word they will come in, he and all the Israelites with him, the whole community."
Moses did as the LORD commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole community.
He laid his hands on him and commissioned him, as the LORD had said through Moses.
"Command the Israelites and say to them: 'Be careful to present to me at its appointed time my offering, my food for my offerings by fire, a pleasing aroma to me.'
Say to them: 'This is the offering by fire that you are to present to the LORD: two male lambs a year old without defect, every day, as a regular burnt offering.
Offer one lamb in the morning, and offer the other lamb at twilight,
with a tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives.
It is the regular burnt offering that was instituted at Mount Sinai, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
Its drink offering is to be a quarter of a hin for each lamb. Pour out the drink offering of fermented drink to the LORD in the holy place.
Offer the other lamb at twilight. Offer it with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD.
"'On the Sabbath day: two male lambs a year old without defect, and two tenths of fine flour as a grain offering, mixed with oil, with its drink offering.
This is the burnt offering for every Sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
"'At the beginning of each month you are to present a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, without defect,
with three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each bull, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for the one ram,
and a tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering for each lamb. It is a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.

Their drink offerings are to be half a hin of wine for each bull, a third of a hin for the ram, and a quarter of a hin for each lamb. This is the burnt offering for each new month, for all the months of the year.
One male goat is to be offered to the LORD as a sin offering, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
"'On the fourteenth day of the first month is the LORD's Passover.
On the fifteenth day of this month there is to be a festival. For seven days bread made without yeast is to be eaten.
On the first day you are to hold a sacred assembly. Do no regular work.
Present to the LORD an offering by fire, a burnt offering: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old. They must be without defect.
With them offer their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for the ram.
Offer a tenth for each lamb, for each of the seven lambs.
Offer one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.
Offer these in addition to the morning burnt offering, which belongs to the regular burnt offering.

In this way you are to offer every day for seven days the food of the offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD. It is to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its drink offering.
On the seventh day you are to hold a sacred assembly. Do no regular work.
"'On the day of the firstfruits, when you present to the LORD an offering of new grain at your Festival of Weeks, you are to hold a sacred assembly. Do no regular work.
Present a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven male lambs a year old,
with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the one ram,
and a tenth for each lamb, for each of the seven lambs;
and one male goat to make atonement for you.
Offer them, with their drink offerings, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering. They must be without defect.
"'On the first day of the seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly. Do no regular work. It is to be a day of trumpet blasts for you.
Offer a burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the ram,
and one tenth for each lamb, for each of the seven lambs;
and one male goat as a sin offering, to make atonement for you.

These are in addition to the burnt offering of the new month and its grain offering, and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings, as prescribed for them, as a pleasing aroma, an offering by fire to the LORD.
"'On the tenth day of this seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly. You are to deny yourselves, and do no work at all.
Present to the LORD a burnt offering, a pleasing aroma: one young bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old. They must be without defect.
With them offer their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the one ram,
and a tenth for each lamb, for each of the seven lambs;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the sin offering for atonement, and the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
"'On the fifteenth day of the seventh month you are to hold a sacred assembly. Do no regular work. Celebrate a festival to the LORD for seven days.
Present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: thirteen young bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old. They must be without defect.
With them offer their grain offering of fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each of the thirteen bulls, two tenths for each of the two rams,
and a tenth for each of the fourteen lambs;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"'On the second day: twelve young bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering, and their drink offerings.
"'On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"'On the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"'On the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.
"'On the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offerings.
"'On the seventh day: seven bulls, two rams and fourteen male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bulls, the rams and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed for them;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering, its grain offering and its drink offering.
"'On the eighth day you are to hold a closing assembly. Do no regular work.
Present a burnt offering, an offering by fire, a pleasing aroma to the LORD: one bull, one ram and seven male lambs a year old, without defect,
with their grain offering and their drink offerings for the bull, the ram and the lambs, according to their number, as prescribed;
and one male goat as a sin offering. These are in addition to the regular burnt offering and its grain offering and its drink offering.

"'These are what you are to offer to the LORD at your appointed festivals, in addition to your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, whether burnt offerings, grain offerings, drink offerings or fellowship offerings.'"
So Moses told the Israelites everything that the LORD had commanded him.
Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the Israelites: "This is what the LORD has commanded.
If a man makes a vow to the LORD, or swears an oath to bind himself by a pledge, he must not break his word. He must do everything he has said.
"If a woman makes a vow to the LORD and binds herself by a pledge while she is young and living in her father's house,
and her father hears of her vow or of the pledge by which she has bound herself, and says nothing to her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her father forbids her on the day he hears of it, none of her vows or the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand. The LORD will forgive her, because her father has forbidden her.
"If she marries while her vows are on her, or a rash promise by which she has bound herself,
and her husband hears of it and says nothing to her on the day he hears of it, then her vows will stand, and the pledges by which she has bound herself will stand.
But if her husband forbids her on the day he hears of it, he cancels the vow she is under and the rash promise by which she has bound herself, and the LORD will forgive her.
"But the vow of a widow or of a divorced woman, everything by which she has bound herself, will stand against her.
"If a woman made a vow in her husband's house, or bound herself by a pledge with an oath,
and her husband heard of it and said nothing to her and did not forbid her, then all her vows will stand, and every pledge by which she bound herself will stand.

But if her husband cancels them on the day he hears of them, then nothing that came from her lips, whether her vows or the pledge by which she bound herself, will stand. Her husband has canceled them, and the LORD will forgive her.
Any vow, and any sworn pledge to deny herself, her husband may confirm or her husband may cancel.

But if her husband says nothing at all to her from one day to the next, then he confirms all her vows, or all the pledges that are on her. He has confirmed them, because he said nothing to her on the day he heard of them.
But if he cancels them some time after he has heard of them, he will bear her guilt."
These are the rules that the LORD commanded Moses about a man and his wife, and about a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father's house.
"Take vengeance for the Israelites on the Midianites. After that you will be gathered to your people."
So Moses said to the people, "Arm some of your men for war, so that they may go against Midian to carry out the LORD's vengeance on Midian.
Send a thousand men from each tribe, from all the tribes of Israel, to the war."
So from the clans of Israel 1,000 were provided from each tribe, 12,000 men armed for war.
Moses sent them to the war, a thousand from each tribe, together with Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest, who took with him the holy objects and the trumpets for sounding the alarm.
They made war on Midian, as the LORD had commanded Moses, and killed every male.
Along with the others they killed, they killed the kings of Midian: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword.
The Israelites took the women of Midian and their little ones captive, and they carried off as plunder all their animals, all their herds and flocks, and all their goods.
They burned with fire all the towns where they had settled and all their encampments.
They took all the spoil and all the plunder, both people and animals.
They brought the captives, the plunder and the spoil to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the community of the Israelites, at the camp on the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
Moses, Eleazar the priest and all the leaders of the community went out to meet them outside the camp.
Moses was angry with the officers of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, who had come back from the campaign.
Moses said to them, "Have you let all the women live?
These were the very ones who, on Balaam's advice, caused the Israelites to be unfaithful to the LORD in the matter of Peor, so that the plague came on the LORD's community.
Now kill every male among the little ones, and kill every woman who has slept with a man.
But keep alive for yourselves all the girls who have not slept with a man.

As for you, stay outside the camp for seven days. All of you who have killed anyone or touched anyone who was killed must purify yourselves on the third day and on the seventh day, you and your captives.
Purify every garment, every article of leather, everything made of goats' hair, and every article of wood."
Then Eleazar the priest said to the soldiers who had gone into battle, "This is the rule of the law that the LORD commanded Moses:
Only the gold, the silver, the bronze, the iron, the tin and the lead,

everything that can stand fire, you must pass through the fire, and it will be clean. But it must also be purified with the water for impurity. And everything that cannot stand fire you must pass through the water.
On the seventh day wash your clothes, and you will be clean. After that you may come into the camp."
"You and Eleazar the priest and the heads of the ancestral families of the community are to count the plunder that was captured, both people and animals.
Divide the plunder into two halves, between the warriors who went out to battle and the whole community.
From the soldiers who went out to battle, set aside a tribute for the LORD: one life out of every five hundred, whether of people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the LORD's contribution.

From the Israelites' half, take one out of every fifty, whether of people, cattle, donkeys, or sheep and goats, of all the animals, and give them to the Levites, who carry out the duties of the LORD's tabernacle."
So Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the LORD commanded Moses.
The plunder, what remained of the spoil that the soldiers had taken, was 675,000 sheep and goats,
and 32,000 people in all, women who had not slept with a man.
The half that was the share of those who had gone out to battle was 337,500 sheep and goats,
and the tribute for the LORD from the sheep and goats was 675;
36,000 cattle, and the tribute from them for the LORD was seventy-two;
30,500 donkeys, and the tribute from them for the LORD was sixty-one;
and 16,000 people, and the tribute from them for the LORD was thirty-two people.
Moses gave the tribute, the LORD's contribution, to Eleazar the priest, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
From the Israelites' half, which Moses had separated from that of the men who had fought,
the community's half was 337,500 sheep and goats,

From the Israelites' half Moses took one out of every fifty, of people and of animals, and gave them to the Levites, who carry out the duties of the LORD's tabernacle, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then the officers who were over the units of the army, the commanders of thousands and the commanders of hundreds, came to Moses
and said to him, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing.
So we have brought as an offering to the LORD what each man found, articles of gold: armlets, bracelets, signet rings, earrings and pendants, to make atonement for ourselves before the LORD."
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it crafted articles.
All the gold of the contribution that they presented to the LORD, from the commanders of thousands and from the commanders of hundreds, came to 16,750 shekels.
The soldiers had each taken plunder for themselves.
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from the commanders of thousands and of hundreds and brought it into the tent of meeting as a reminder for the Israelites before the LORD.
The Reubenites and the Gadites had a very great number of livestock. They saw that the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead was a good place for livestock.
So the Gadites and the Reubenites came to Moses, to Eleazar the priest and to the leaders of the community, and said,
"Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sebam, Nebo and Beon,
the land that the LORD struck down before the community of Israel, is a land for livestock, and your servants have livestock."
They said, "If we have found favor in your eyes, let this land be given to your servants as our property. Do not make us cross the Jordan."
Moses said to the Gadites and the Reubenites, "Are your brothers to go to war while you stay here?
Why would you discourage the Israelites from crossing over into the land that the LORD has given them?
That is what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh-barnea to look at the land.
They went up as far as the Valley of Eshcol and saw the land, and then they discouraged the Israelites from going into the land that the LORD had given them.
The LORD's anger burned that day, and he swore an oath:
'Not one of the men twenty years old or more who came up out of Egypt will see the land that I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, because they have not followed me wholeheartedly,
none except Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite and Joshua son of Nun, because they have followed the LORD wholeheartedly.'
The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until the whole generation that had done evil in the LORD's sight was gone.
And now here you are, standing up in your fathers' place, a brood of sinful men, to add still more to the LORD's fierce anger against Israel!
If you turn away from following him, he will once again leave them in the wilderness, and you will bring destruction on this whole people."
Then they came up to him and said, "We will build sheep pens here for our livestock, and towns for our little ones.

But we ourselves will arm ourselves and go quickly ahead of the Israelites, until we have brought them to their place. Meanwhile our little ones will live in the fortified towns, safe from the people who live in the land.
We will not return to our homes until every one of the Israelites has taken possession of his inheritance.
For we will not take an inheritance with them across the Jordan and beyond, because our inheritance has come to us on the east side of the Jordan."
Moses said to them, "If you will do this, if you will arm yourselves to go before the LORD into battle,
and every one of your armed men will cross the Jordan before the LORD, until he has driven out his enemies from before him,

and the land is brought under control before the LORD, then after that you may return. You will be free of your obligation to the LORD and to Israel, and this land will be your property before the LORD.
But if you do not do this, you will have sinned against the LORD. And be sure that your sin will find you out.
Build towns for your little ones and pens for your flocks, but do what you have promised."
The Gadites and the Reubenites said to Moses, "Your servants will do as my lord commands.
Our little ones, our wives, our flocks and all our livestock will stay there in the towns of Gilead,
but your servants, every man armed for war, will cross over before the LORD to the battle, just as my lord says."
So Moses gave orders about them to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of the Israelites.

Moses said to them, "If the Gadites and the Reubenites cross the Jordan with you, every man armed for battle before the LORD, and the land is brought under control before you, then you are to give them the land of Gilead as their property.
But if they do not cross over with you armed, they must receive their property among you in the land of Canaan."
The Gadites and the Reubenites answered, "What the LORD has said to your servants, that is what we will do.
We will cross over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, but the property we inherit will remain ours across the Jordan."

So Moses gave to the Gadites, the Reubenites and the half-tribe of Manasseh son of Joseph the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan: the land with its towns and their territories, the towns of the land all around.
The Gadites built Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer,
Beth-nimrah and Beth-haran, as fortified towns, and sheep pens.
The Reubenites built Heshbon, Elealeh, Kiriathaim,
Nebo and Baal-meon (their names were changed), and Sibmah. They gave new names to the towns they built.
The descendants of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it, and drove out the Amorites who were there.
So Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages, and he called them Havvoth-jair.
Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and he called it Nobah, after his own name.
These were the journeys of the Israelites when they went out of the land of Egypt by their divisions, under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
At the LORD's command Moses recorded the places they set out from, stage by stage. These were their journeys, by the places they set out from.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover the Israelites went out boldly in the sight of all the Egyptians,
while the Egyptians were burying all their firstborn, whom the LORD had struck down among them. The LORD had also carried out judgments on their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, which is on the edge of the wilderness.
They set out from Etham and turned back to Pi-hahiroth, which faces Baal-zephon, and they camped in front of Migdol.
They set out from before Hahiroth and passed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. They went three days' journey in the wilderness of Etham and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and came to Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and they camped there.
They set out from Elim and camped by the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
They set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at Kibroth-hattaavah.
They set out from Kibroth-hattaavah and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
They set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
They set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Hor-haggidgad.
They set out from Hor-haggidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin, that is, Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, on the edge of the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up Mount Hor at the LORD's command, and he died there in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of the land of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the Negev in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the border of Moab.
They set out from Iyim and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
They set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, in front of Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
They camped along the Jordan from Beth-jeshimoth as far as Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
In the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
you must drive out all the inhabitants of the land before you. Destroy all their carved stones, destroy all their images of cast metal, and demolish all their high places.
Take possession of the land and settle in it, for I have given you the land to possess.

Divide the land among your clans by lot as your inheritance. To a larger clan you are to give a larger inheritance, and to a smaller clan a smaller inheritance. Wherever the lot falls for anyone, that will be his. You are to receive your inheritance by your ancestral tribes.

But if you do not drive out the inhabitants of the land before you, those you allow to remain will be like barbs in your eyes and thorns in your sides. They will harass you in the land where you live.
And then I will do to you what I planned to do to them.'"
"Command the Israelites and say to them: 'When you enter the land of Canaan, this is the land that will fall to you as an inheritance: the land of Canaan with its borders.
Your southern side will extend from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom. Your southern border will begin in the east at the end of the Salt Sea.
Your border will turn south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its far end will be south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go out to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
From Azmon the border will turn to the Wadi of Egypt, and its far end will be at the sea.
"'As for the western border, the Great Sea and its coast will be your border. This will be your western border.
"'This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea mark out your line to Mount Hor.
From Mount Hor mark it out to Lebo-hamath, and the far end of the border will be at Zedad.
Then the border will go out to Ziphron, and its far end will be at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
"'For your eastern border, mark out your line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
The border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. Then the border will go down and reach the slope east of the Sea of Kinnereth.
Then the border will go down along the Jordan, and its far end will be at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, with its borders all around.'"
Moses commanded the Israelites: "This is the land that you are to receive as your inheritance by lot, which the LORD has commanded to be given to the nine and a half tribes.

For the tribe of the Reubenites by their ancestral families and the tribe of the Gadites by their ancestral families have received their inheritance, and the half-tribe of Manasseh has received its inheritance.
The two and a half tribes have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, to the east, toward the sunrise."
"These are the names of the men who are to divide the land among you as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Also take one leader from each tribe to divide the land as an inheritance.
These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of the Simeonites, Shemuel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of the Danites, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli;
from the sons of Joseph: from the tribe of the Manassites, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod;
and from the tribe of the Ephraimites, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;
from the tribe of the Zebulunites, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach;
from the tribe of the Issacharites, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan;
from the tribe of the Asherites, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi;
from the tribe of the Naphtalites, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
These are the men whom the LORD commanded to divide the inheritance among the Israelites in the land of Canaan.
In the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho, the LORD said to Moses,
"Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from the inheritance they will possess. You are also to give the Levites pasturelands around the towns.
The towns will be theirs to live in, and their pasturelands will be for their cattle, their goods and all their animals.
The pasturelands of the towns that you give to the Levites are to extend a thousand cubits from the town wall outward, all around.

Measure outside the town two thousand cubits on the east side, two thousand cubits on the south side, two thousand cubits on the west side and two thousand cubits on the north side, with the town in the middle. This will be the pastureland of their towns.

"Among the towns you give to the Levites will be the six cities of refuge, which you are to provide so that anyone who has killed someone may flee there. In addition to them you are to give forty-two towns.
All the towns you give to the Levites will be forty-eight towns, together with their pasturelands.

The towns you give from the property of the Israelites are to be in proportion: take more from a tribe that has more, and fewer from a tribe that has fewer. Each is to give some of its towns to the Levites in proportion to the inheritance it receives."
"Speak to the Israelites and say to them: 'When you cross the Jordan into the land of Canaan,
select towns to be your cities of refuge, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake may flee there.
The towns will be a refuge for you from the avenger, so that the killer will not die until he has stood trial before the community.
The towns you give will be your six cities of refuge.
Give three towns across the Jordan and three towns in the land of Canaan. They will be cities of refuge.
These six towns will be a refuge for the Israelites, and for the foreigner and the temporary resident among them, so that anyone who kills a person by mistake may flee there.
"'But if someone strikes a person with an iron object and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If someone strikes a person with a stone in his hand that could cause death, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
Or if someone strikes a person with a wooden object in his hand that could cause death, and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself is to put the murderer to death. When he meets him, he is to put him to death.
If someone pushes another out of hatred, or throws something at him with intent, and he dies,
or strikes him with his hand out of hostility, and he dies, then the one who struck him must be put to death. He is a murderer. The avenger of blood is to put the murderer to death when he meets him.
"'But if someone pushes another suddenly, without hostility, or throws any object at him without intent,
or, without seeing him, drops on him a stone that could cause death, and he dies, though he was not his enemy and did not seek to harm him,
then the community must judge between the one who struck him and the avenger of blood according to these rules.

The community must rescue the killer from the hand of the avenger of blood and return him to the city of refuge to which he fled. He must live there until the death of the high priest, who was anointed with the holy oil.
But if the killer ever goes outside the boundary of the city of refuge to which he fled,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundary of his city of refuge, and the avenger of blood kills the killer, he is not guilty of bloodshed.
For the killer must live in his city of refuge until the death of the high priest. After the death of the high priest the killer may return to the land he owns.
"'These are to be legal rules for you for all your generations, wherever you live.
"'If anyone kills a person, the murderer is to be put to death on the evidence of witnesses. But one witness alone may not testify against a person to have him put to death.
Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer who is guilty and deserves to die. He must be put to death.
And do not accept a ransom for anyone who has fled to his city of refuge, so that he may return and live in the land before the death of the priest.
Do not defile the land where you are, for blood defiles the land, and no atonement can be made for the land for the blood that has been shed on it, except by the blood of the one who shed it.
Do not make the land where you live unclean, the land where I live, for I, the LORD, live among the Israelites.'"

The heads of the ancestral families of the clan of the descendants of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the clans of the descendants of Joseph, came forward. They spoke before Moses and before the leaders, the heads of the ancestral families of the Israelites.

They said, "The LORD commanded my lord to give the land to the Israelites as an inheritance by lot, and my lord was commanded by the LORD to give the inheritance of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

But if they marry men from any of the other tribes of the Israelites, their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestors and added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into. So it will be taken away from the inheritance allotted to us.

And when the Jubilee comes for the Israelites, their inheritance will be added to the inheritance of the tribe they marry into, and their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of our ancestral tribe."
Then at the LORD's command Moses commanded the Israelites: "What the tribe of the descendants of Joseph says is right.
This is what the LORD commands concerning the daughters of Zelophehad: They may marry anyone they please, but they must marry within a clan of their father's tribe.
No inheritance of the Israelites may pass from tribe to tribe, for each of the Israelites is to keep hold of the inheritance of his ancestral tribe.

Every daughter who inherits property in any of the tribes of the Israelites must marry someone from a clan of her father's tribe, so that each of the Israelites may possess the inheritance of his ancestors.
No inheritance may pass from one tribe to another, for each of the tribes of the Israelites is to keep hold of its own inheritance."
The daughters of Zelophehad did just as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, married the sons of their uncles.
They married into the clans of the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, and their inheritance remained with the tribe of their father's clan.
These are the commands and the rules that the LORD gave to the Israelites through Moses in the plains of Moab by the Jordan, across from Jericho.
These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel east of the Jordan, in the wilderness, in the Arabah opposite Suph, between Paran and Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth and Di-zahab.
It is eleven days' journey from Horeb to Kadesh-barnea by the Mount Seir road.
In the fortieth year, on the first day of the eleventh month, Moses spoke to the Israelites, telling them everything the LORD had commanded him to tell them.
This was after he had defeated Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon, and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth, at Edrei.
East of the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses began to explain this law. He said:
"The LORD our God spoke to us at Horeb. He said, 'You have stayed at this mountain long enough.

Turn and set out. Go to the hill country of the Amorites and to all their neighbors in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the western foothills, in the Negev and along the seacoast: the land of the Canaanites, and Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates.
See, I have set the land before you. Go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to give to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, and to their descendants after them.'
At that time I said to you, 'I cannot carry you by myself.
The LORD your God has multiplied you, and here you are today, as many as the stars of the sky.
May the LORD, the God of your ancestors, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you as he has promised you.
How can I bear by myself the weight of you, the burden of you and your quarrels?
Choose wise, discerning and respected men from each of your tribes, and I will make them your leaders.'
You answered me, 'What you have told us to do is good.'

So I took the leaders of your tribes, wise and respected men, and made them leaders over you: commanders of thousands, commanders of hundreds, commanders of fifties and commanders of tens, and officials for your tribes.

At that time I gave your judges this command: 'Hear the disputes between your fellow Israelites, and judge fairly between one person and another, whether a fellow Israelite or a foreigner who lives among you.
Do not show partiality in judging. Hear the small and the great alike. Do not be afraid of anyone, for judgment belongs to God. Bring to me any case that is too hard for you, and I will hear it.'
At that time I commanded you all the things you were to do.

Then we set out from Horeb and went through all that great and terrible wilderness that you saw, on the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as the LORD our God had commanded us. And we came to Kadesh-barnea.
I said to you, 'You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which the LORD our God is giving us.
See, the LORD your God has set the land before you. Go up and take possession of it, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has told you. Do not be afraid or discouraged.'
Then all of you came to me and said, 'Let us send men ahead of us to explore the land for us. Let them bring us back a report about the route we should take up and the cities we will come to.'
The idea seemed good to me, so I took twelve men from among you, one man from each tribe.
They turned and went up into the hill country and came to the Valley of Eshcol, and they spied out the land.
They took some of the fruit of the land in their hands and brought it down to us. They brought us back a report and said, 'The land that the LORD our God is giving us is good.'
But you were not willing to go up. You rebelled against the command of the LORD your God.
You grumbled in your tents and said, 'The LORD hates us. That is why he brought us out of the land of Egypt, to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us.

Where can we go up to? Our brothers have made our hearts melt. They say, "The people are bigger and taller than we are. The cities are large, with walls up to the sky. And we even saw the Anakim there."'
Then I said to you, 'Do not be terrified or afraid of them.
The LORD your God, who is going ahead of you, will himself fight for you, just as he did for you in Egypt before your eyes,
and in the wilderness. There you saw how the LORD your God carried you, as a man carries his son, all the way you went until you came to this place.'
Yet in spite of this, you did not trust the LORD your God,
who went ahead of you on the way to look for a place for you to camp, in fire by night to show you the way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
When the LORD heard what you said, he was angry, and he swore,
'Not one of these men, this evil generation, will see the good land that I swore to give to your ancestors,
except Caleb son of Jephunneh. He will see it, and I will give him and his children the land he has walked on, because he followed the LORD completely.'
Because of you, the LORD was angry with me too. He said, 'You will not enter it either.
Joshua son of Nun, who serves you, will enter it. Encourage him, for he will lead Israel to take possession of it.

And your little ones, who you said would be taken as plunder, and your children, who today do not yet know good from bad, they will enter it. I will give it to them, and they will take possession of it.
But as for you, turn around and set out for the wilderness, by the road to the Red Sea.'

Then you answered me, 'We have sinned against the LORD. We will go up and fight, just as the LORD our God commanded us.' Each of you put on his weapons, and you thought it easy to go up into the hill country.
But the LORD said to me, 'Tell them, "Do not go up and do not fight, for I am not with you. You will be defeated by your enemies."'
So I told you, but you would not listen. You rebelled against the LORD's command, and in your arrogance you went up into the hill country.
The Amorites who lived in that hill country came out against you and chased you like a swarm of bees. They struck you down in Seir as far as Hormah.
You came back and wept before the LORD, but the LORD did not listen to your voice or pay any attention to you.
So you stayed in Kadesh for a long time, all the time that you stayed there.
"Then we turned and set out for the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea, as the LORD had told me. For a long time we went around the hill country of Seir.
Then the LORD said to me,
'You have been going around this hill country long enough. Turn north.
Give the people this command: "You are about to pass through the territory of your relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir. They will be afraid of you, but be very careful.
Do not start a fight with them, for I will not give you any of their land, not even enough to put your foot on. I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau as his possession.
You are to buy food from them with money, so that you may eat, and you are also to buy water from them with money, so that you may drink.

For the LORD your God has blessed you in all the work of your hands. He has watched over your journey through this great wilderness. For these forty years the LORD your God has been with you, and you have not lacked anything."'

So we went on past our relatives, the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, away from the Arabah road, away from Elath and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and went along the road to the wilderness of Moab.
The LORD said to me, 'Do not harass Moab or start a war with them, for I will not give you any of their land as a possession. I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as their possession.'
(The Emim used to live there, a people great and numerous, and as tall as the Anakim.
Like the Anakim, they too were counted as Rephaim, but the Moabites call them Emim.

The Horites also used to live in Seir, but the descendants of Esau drove them out. They destroyed them and settled in their place, just as Israel did in the land that the LORD gave them as their possession.)
'Now get up and cross the Zered Valley.' So we crossed the Zered Valley.
From the time we left Kadesh-barnea until we crossed the Zered Valley was thirty-eight years, until the whole generation of fighting men had died out from the camp, as the LORD had sworn to them.
Indeed, the hand of the LORD was against them, to wipe them out from the camp until they were all gone.
When the last of the fighting men among the people had died,
'Today you are to cross the border of Moab at Ar.

When you come near the Ammonites, do not harass them or start a fight with them, for I will not give you any of the land of the Ammonites as a possession. I have given it to the descendants of Lot as their possession.'
(That too was counted as a land of the Rephaim. Rephaim used to live there, but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim,
a people great and numerous, and as tall as the Anakim. But the LORD destroyed them before the Ammonites, who drove them out and settled in their place.
He had done the same for the descendants of Esau, who live in Seir, when he destroyed the Horites before them. They drove them out and have lived in their place to this day.
And as for the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who came from Caphtor, destroyed them and settled in their place.)
'Get up, set out and cross the Arnon Valley. See, I have handed over to you Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land. Begin to take possession of it. Go to war against him.
This very day I will begin to put the dread and fear of you on the peoples everywhere under heaven. When they hear the report of you, they will tremble and be in anguish because of you.'
So I sent messengers from the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with an offer of peace. I said,
'Let me pass through your land. I will keep strictly to the road. I will not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Sell me food for money, so that I may eat, and give me water for money, so that I may drink. Only let me pass through on foot,
as the descendants of Esau who live in Seir and the Moabites who live in Ar did for me, until I cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD our God is giving us.'
But Sihon king of Heshbon was not willing to let us pass through his land, for the LORD your God had made his spirit stubborn and his heart hard, to hand him over to you, as he has now done.
The LORD said to me, 'See, I have begun to hand Sihon and his land over to you. Begin to take possession, so that you may possess his land.'
Then Sihon came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Jahaz.
The LORD our God handed him over to us, and we struck him down, together with his sons and all his people.
At that time we captured all his towns and devoted every town to destruction, men, women and children. We left no survivors.
We kept only the livestock as plunder for ourselves, along with the spoil of the towns we had captured.
From Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the town in the valley, as far as Gilead, there was not one town too strong for us. The LORD our God handed them all over to us.
But you did not go near the land of the Ammonites: the whole bank of the Jabbok River, the towns of the hill country, or any place that the LORD our God had forbidden.
"Then we turned and went up the road to Bashan, and Og king of Bashan came out against us, he and all his people, to fight at Edrei.
The LORD said to me, 'Do not be afraid of him, for I have handed him over to you, with all his people and his land. Do to him what you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.'
So the LORD our God also handed over to us Og king of Bashan and all his people. We struck him down until no survivor was left to him.
At that time we captured all his towns. There was not a town that we did not take from them: sixty towns, the whole region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan.
All these were towns fortified with high walls, gates and bars, not counting a great many unwalled villages.
We devoted them to destruction, as we had done to Sihon king of Heshbon, devoting every town to destruction, men, women and children.
But all the livestock and the spoil of the towns we took as plunder for ourselves.
So at that time we took the land from the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon.
(The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)
We took all the towns of the plateau, all Gilead and all Bashan as far as Salecah and Edrei, towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan.

(Only Og king of Bashan was left of the remnant of the Rephaim. His bed was made of iron. Isn't it still in Rabbah of the Ammonites? It is nine cubits long and four cubits wide, by the standard cubit.)
So we took possession of this land at that time. I gave the Reubenites and the Gadites the land from Aroer, by the Arnon Valley, and half the hill country of Gilead with its towns.
The rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (The whole region of Argob, all that part of Bashan, is called the land of the Rephaim.
Jair, a descendant of Manasseh, took the whole region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites. He named Bashan after himself, Havvoth-jair, as it is called to this day.)

To the Reubenites and the Gadites I gave the territory from Gilead as far as the Arnon Valley, with the middle of the valley as the border, and as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites.
Their territory also included the Arabah, with the Jordan as its border, from Kinnereth to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, below the slopes of Pisgah on the east.
At that time I commanded you, 'The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. All your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your fellow Israelites.
Only your wives, your little ones and your livestock (I know you have a great deal of livestock) may stay in the towns I have given you,

until the LORD gives your relatives rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them on the other side of the Jordan. Then each of you may return to the possession I have given you.'
At that time I commanded Joshua, 'Your own eyes have seen everything the LORD your God has done to these two kings. The LORD will do the same to all the kingdoms you are crossing over into.
Do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God is the one who fights for you.'
At that time I pleaded with the LORD:
'Lord GOD, you have begun to show your servant your greatness and your mighty hand. What god is there in heaven or on earth who can do deeds and mighty acts like yours?
Please let me cross over and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan, that good hill country, and Lebanon.'
But the LORD was angry with me because of you, and he would not listen to me. The LORD said to me, 'That is enough! Do not speak to me about this matter again.
Go up to the top of Pisgah and look west, north, south and east. See it with your own eyes, for you will not cross this Jordan.
Give Joshua his orders. Encourage him and strengthen him, for he will cross over at the head of this people, and he will lead them to take possession of the land that you will see.'
So we stayed in the valley opposite Beth-peor.

"Now, Israel, listen to the decrees and the rulings that I am teaching you to follow, so that you may live, and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.
Do not add anything to what I command you, and do not take anything away from it. Keep the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you.
You saw with your own eyes what the LORD did at Baal-peor. The LORD your God destroyed from among you everyone who followed the Baal of Peor.
But all of you who held fast to the LORD your God are alive today.
See, I have taught you decrees and rulings, as the LORD my God commanded me, so that you may follow them in the land you are entering to take possession of.

Keep them and follow them, for this will show your wisdom and understanding to the peoples. When they hear about all these decrees, they will say, 'Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.'
For what great nation has a god so near to it as the LORD our God is to us whenever we call on him?
And what great nation has decrees and rulings as righteous as this whole law that I am setting before you today?

Only be careful, and watch yourselves closely, so that you do not forget the things your eyes have seen, and so that they do not slip from your heart as long as you live. Make them known to your children and your grandchildren:

the day you stood before the LORD your God at Horeb, when the LORD said to me, 'Assemble the people for me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me as long as they live on the earth, and may teach their children.'
You came near and stood at the foot of the mountain, while the mountain blazed with fire up to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud and thick gloom.
Then the LORD spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words, but you saw no form. There was only a voice.
He declared to you his covenant, which he commanded you to keep: the Ten Commandments. And he wrote them on two stone tablets.
At that time the LORD commanded me to teach you decrees and rulings, for you to follow in the land you are crossing over into to take possession of.
So watch yourselves very carefully. Since you saw no form of any kind on the day the LORD spoke to you at Horeb out of the fire,
do not act corruptly by making for yourselves an idol in the form of any figure: the likeness of a male or a female,
the likeness of any animal on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky,
the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, or the likeness of any fish in the waters below the earth.

And when you look up to the sky and see the sun, the moon and the stars, the whole array of heaven, do not be drawn away to bow down to them and serve them. The LORD your God has allotted them to all the peoples everywhere under heaven.
But you are the ones the LORD took and brought out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be the people of his inheritance, as you are today.
The LORD was angry with me because of you, and he swore that I would not cross the Jordan or enter the good land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
For I am going to die in this land. I will not cross the Jordan. But you are going to cross over and take possession of this good land.
Be careful not to forget the covenant that the LORD your God made with you. Do not make for yourselves an idol in the form of anything that the LORD your God has forbidden you.
For the LORD your God is a consuming fire, a jealous God.

When you have had children and grandchildren and have been in the land a long time, if you act corruptly by making an idol in the form of anything, and do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God, provoking him to anger,

I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that you will soon perish completely from the land you are crossing the Jordan to take possession of. You will not live long on it, but will be utterly destroyed.
The LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will be left among the nations where the LORD will drive you.
There you will serve gods made by human hands, of wood and stone, which cannot see or hear or eat or smell.
But from there you will seek the LORD your God, and you will find him, if you search for him with all your heart and with all your soul.
When you are in distress and all these things have happened to you, in days to come, you will return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice.
For the LORD your God is a compassionate God. He will not abandon you or destroy you, and he will not forget the covenant with your ancestors that he swore to them.

Ask now about the former days, the days before you, from the day God created human beings on the earth. Ask from one end of heaven to the other: has anything as great as this ever happened, or has anything like it ever been heard of?
Has any people ever heard the voice of God speaking out of fire, as you have heard it, and lived?

Or has any god ever tried to go and take for himself one nation from within another nation, by trials, by signs and wonders, by war, by a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, and by great and terrifying deeds, as the LORD your God did for you in Egypt before your eyes?
You were shown these things so that you would know that the LORD is God. There is no other besides him.
From heaven he let you hear his voice to discipline you, and on earth he let you see his great fire, and you heard his words out of the fire.
Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them, and he himself brought you out of Egypt by his great power,
to drive out before you nations greater and stronger than you, to bring you in and give you their land as an inheritance, as it is today.
So know today, and take it to heart, that the LORD is God in heaven above and on the earth below. There is no other.

Keep his decrees and his commands, which I am giving you today, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you for all time."
Then Moses set apart three cities east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
for anyone who had killed someone to flee to: anyone who had killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having been his enemy before. He could flee to one of these cities and save his life.
These were Bezer in the wilderness, on the plateau, for the Reubenites; Ramoth in Gilead for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan for the Manassites.
This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites.
These are the statutes, the decrees and the rulings that Moses spoke to the Israelites after they came out of Egypt,
east of the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites defeated him after they came out of Egypt,
and they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who were east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.
Their land stretched from Aroer, on the edge of the Arnon Valley, as far as Mount Sion, that is, Hermon,
together with all the Arabah east of the Jordan, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, "Hear, Israel, the decrees and the rulings that I am speaking in your hearing today. Learn them and be careful to follow them.
The LORD our God made a covenant with us at Horeb.
It was not with our ancestors that the LORD made this covenant, but with us, all of us who are alive here today.
The LORD spoke with you face to face at the mountain, out of the fire.
At that time I was standing between the LORD and you to tell you the word of the LORD, because you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain. He said:
'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery.
You must have no other gods besides me.
You must not make for yourself an idol, an image of anything in the heavens above, or on the earth below, or in the waters under the earth.

You must not bow down to them or serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God. I punish children for the wrongdoing of their parents, to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me,
but I show faithful love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commands.
You must not misuse the name of the LORD your God, for the LORD will not leave unpunished anyone who misuses his name.
Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the LORD your God has commanded you.
For six days you are to work and do all your work,

but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God. On it you must not do any work, neither you, nor your son or your daughter, nor your male or female slave, nor your ox or your donkey or any of your livestock, nor the foreigner who lives in your towns, so that your male and female slaves may rest as you do.

Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm. That is why the LORD your God has commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
Honor your father and your mother, as the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live long, and so that it may go well with you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
You must not give false testimony against your neighbor.
You must not covet your neighbor's wife. You must not desire your neighbor's house, his field, his male or female slave, his ox or his donkey, or anything that belongs to your neighbor.'

These are the words that the LORD spoke with a loud voice to your whole assembly at the mountain, out of the fire, the cloud and the thick darkness, and he added nothing more. He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.
When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was blazing with fire, all the heads of your tribes and your elders came to me

and said, 'See, the LORD our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the fire. Today we have seen that God can speak with a human being and that person still live.
But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us. If we hear the voice of the LORD our God any longer, we will die.
For who among all humankind has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of fire, as we have, and lived?
You go near and listen to everything that the LORD our God says. Then tell us everything that the LORD our God tells you, and we will listen and do it.'
The LORD heard what you said when you spoke to me, and the LORD said to me, 'I have heard what this people said to you. Everything they have said is good.
If only they would always have a heart like this, to fear me and keep all my commands, so that it might go well with them and with their children forever!
Go and tell them, "Return to your tents."
But you, stand here with me, and I will tell you the whole command, the decrees and the rulings that you are to teach them, so that they may follow them in the land that I am giving them to possess.'
So be careful to do as the LORD your God has commanded you. Do not turn aside to the right or to the left.
Walk in all the way that the LORD your God has commanded you, so that you may live and prosper, and live long in the land you will possess.
