"This is the command, the decrees and the rulings, that the LORD your God commanded me to teach you, for you to follow in the land you are crossing over into to take possession of,

so that you may fear the LORD your God all the days of your life, you and your children and your grandchildren, by keeping all his decrees and his commands that I am giving you, and so that you may live long.

Listen, Israel, and be careful to follow them, so that it may go well with you and you may increase greatly in number, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has promised you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
Hear, Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is one.
You shall love the LORD your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
These words that I am commanding you today are to be on your heart.
Impress them on your children. Talk about them when you sit in your house and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Tie them as a sign on your hand, and let them be a band on your forehead.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, to give you: a land with large and fine cities that you did not build,
houses full of all kinds of good things that you did not fill, cisterns cut in the rock that you did not dig, and vineyards and olive trees that you did not plant. When you eat and are satisfied,
be careful not to forget the LORD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery.
Fear the LORD your God. Serve him, and swear by his name.
Do not follow other gods, the gods of the peoples around you,
for the LORD your God, who is among you, is a jealous God. Otherwise the anger of the LORD your God will burn against you, and he will wipe you off the face of the earth.
Do not put the LORD your God to the test as you tested him at Massah.
Be sure to keep the commands of the LORD your God, and the statutes and decrees he has commanded you.
Do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD, so that it may go well with you, and so that you may go in and take possession of the good land that the LORD swore to give your ancestors,
by driving out all your enemies before you, as the LORD has promised.
In the future, when your son asks you, 'What is the meaning of the statutes, the decrees and the rulings that the LORD our God has commanded you?'
then tell your son, 'We were Pharaoh's slaves in Egypt, but the LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Before our eyes the LORD did great and terrible signs and wonders against Egypt, against Pharaoh and against all his household.
But he brought us out from there, to bring us in and give us the land he swore to give our ancestors.
The LORD commanded us to follow all these decrees and to fear the LORD our God, for our own good always, so that he might keep us alive, as we are today.
And it will be righteousness for us if we are careful to follow all this command before the LORD our God, as he has commanded us.'

"When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of, he will drive out many nations before you: the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, seven nations larger and stronger than you.
When the LORD your God hands them over to you and you defeat them, you must devote them completely to destruction. Do not make a covenant with them, and show them no mercy.
Do not intermarry with them. Do not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons,
for they would turn your children away from following me, to serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD would burn against you, and he would quickly destroy you.
Instead, this is what you are to do to them: tear down their altars, smash their standing stones, cut down their Asherah poles and burn their idols in the fire.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD your God has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his people, his treasured possession.
It was not because you were more numerous than all the other peoples that the LORD set his heart on you and chose you, for you were the fewest of all peoples.

It was because the LORD loved you, and because he kept the oath that he swore to your ancestors, that the LORD brought you out with a mighty hand and redeemed you from the place of slavery, from the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt.
So know that the LORD your God is God. He is the faithful God, who keeps his covenant and his faithful love for a thousand generations with those who love him and keep his commands,
but who repays those who hate him to their face by destroying them. He will not be slow to repay anyone who hates him; he will repay him to his face.
So keep the command, the decrees and the rulings that I am giving you today, and follow them.
If you listen to these rulings, and keep them and follow them, then the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the faithful love that he swore to your ancestors.

He will love you, bless you and multiply you. He will bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your ground, your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks, in the land that he swore to your ancestors to give you.
You will be blessed more than all the peoples. There will be no infertile male or female among you or among your livestock.
The LORD will take away from you every sickness. He will not put on you any of the dreadful diseases of Egypt that you know, but he will lay them on all who hate you.
You must destroy all the peoples that the LORD your God is handing over to you. Do not look on them with pity, and do not serve their gods, for that would be a trap for you.
You may say to yourself, 'These nations are more numerous than I am. How can I drive them out?'
But do not be afraid of them. Remember well what the LORD your God did to Pharaoh and to all Egypt:

the great trials that your eyes saw, the signs and the wonders, and the mighty hand and the outstretched arm by which the LORD your God brought you out. The LORD your God will do the same to all the peoples you are afraid of.
The LORD your God will also send the hornet among them, until those who are left and those who hide from you are destroyed.
Do not be terrified of them, for the LORD your God is among you, a great and awesome God.
The LORD your God will drive out those nations before you little by little. You will not be able to make an end of them quickly, or the wild animals would become too many for you.
But the LORD your God will hand them over to you, and throw them into great confusion until they are destroyed.
He will hand their kings over to you, and you will wipe out their names from under heaven. No one will be able to stand against you until you have destroyed them.
Burn the idols of their gods in the fire. Do not covet the silver or the gold on them, and do not take it for yourself, or you will be trapped by it, for it is detestable to the LORD your God.
Do not bring anything detestable into your house, or you will be set apart for destruction like it. You must utterly abhor it and detest it, for it is set apart for destruction.
"Be careful to follow every command that I am giving you today, so that you may live and multiply, and go in and take possession of the land that the LORD swore to give your ancestors.

Remember the whole way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, to humble you and to test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commands or not.

He humbled you and let you go hungry, and then he fed you with manna, which neither you nor your ancestors had known, to teach you that people do not live on bread alone, but on everything that comes from the mouth of the LORD.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell, these forty years.
Know then in your heart that the LORD your God disciplines you as a man disciplines his son.
Keep the commands of the LORD your God by walking in his ways and fearing him.
For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land of streams of water, of springs and deep waters that flow out in the valleys and in the hills,
a land of wheat and barley, of vines, fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive oil and honey,
a land where you will eat food without scarcity, where you will lack nothing, a land whose stones are iron and from whose hills you can dig copper.
When you have eaten and are satisfied, you will bless the LORD your God for the good land he has given you.
Be careful not to forget the LORD your God by failing to keep his commands, his rulings and his decrees that I am giving you today.
Otherwise, when you have eaten and are satisfied, when you have built fine houses and live in them,
and when your herds and your flocks have grown large, and your silver and gold have increased, and everything you have has increased,
your heart will become proud, and you will forget the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery.
He led you through the great and terrible wilderness, with its poisonous snakes and scorpions, a thirsty land where there was no water. He brought water out for you from the flint rock.
He fed you in the wilderness with manna, which your ancestors had not known, to humble you and to test you, so that in the end he might do you good.
You might say to yourself, 'My power and the strength of my hand have gained me this wealth.'
But remember the LORD your God, for it is he who gives you the power to gain wealth, so that he may confirm his covenant that he swore to your ancestors, as he is doing today.
If you ever forget the LORD your God and follow other gods, and serve them and bow down to them, I warn you today that you will surely perish.
Like the nations that the LORD is destroying before you, so you will perish, because you would not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
"Hear, Israel. Today you are about to cross the Jordan, to go in and dispossess nations greater and stronger than you, with large cities that have walls up to the sky,
a people great and tall, the Anakim. You know about them, and you have heard it said, 'Who can stand up to the Anakim?'

Know then today that the LORD your God is the one who is crossing over ahead of you, a consuming fire. He will destroy them, and he will bring them down before you. You will drive them out and destroy them quickly, as the LORD has promised you.

When the LORD your God has driven them out before you, do not say to yourself, 'It is because of my righteousness that the LORD has brought me in to take possession of this land.' It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD is driving them out before you.

It is not because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart that you are going in to take possession of their land. It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God is driving them out before you, and in order to fulfill the promise that the LORD swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
So know that it is not because of your righteousness that the LORD your God is giving you this good land to possess, for you are a stubborn people.

Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the LORD your God to anger in the wilderness. From the day you left the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebels against the LORD.
At Horeb you provoked the LORD to anger, and the LORD was angry enough with you to destroy you.

When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the LORD made with you, I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water.
The LORD gave me the two stone tablets, written with the finger of God. On them were all the words that the LORD had spoken to you at the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly.
At the end of the forty days and forty nights, the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

Then the LORD said to me, 'Get up, go down from here at once, for your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way I commanded them. They have made themselves a cast idol.'
The LORD also said to me, 'I have seen this people, and they are indeed a stubborn people.
Leave me alone, so that I may destroy them and wipe out their name from under heaven. Then I will make you into a nation stronger and more numerous than they are.'
So I turned and went down from the mountain, while the mountain was blazing with fire. The two tablets of the covenant were in my two hands.
I looked, and there you were: you had sinned against the LORD your God. You had made yourselves a calf, a cast idol. You had quickly turned aside from the way that the LORD had commanded you.
So I took hold of the two tablets and threw them out of my two hands, and I broke them before your eyes.

Then I lay face down before the LORD, as I had the first time, for forty days and forty nights. I ate no bread and drank no water, because of all the sin you had committed, doing what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and provoking him to anger.
For I was afraid of the anger and the fury that the LORD felt against you, enough to destroy you. But the LORD listened to me that time too.
The LORD was very angry with Aaron, enough to destroy him, and at that time I prayed for Aaron too.

Then I took the sinful thing you had made, the calf, and burned it in the fire. I crushed it, grinding it thoroughly until it was as fine as dust, and I threw its dust into the stream that flowed down from the mountain.
At Taberah, at Massah and at Kibroth-hattaavah you also provoked the LORD to anger.

And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh-barnea and said, 'Go up and take possession of the land I have given you,' you rebelled against the command of the LORD your God. You did not trust him or listen to his voice.
You have been rebels against the LORD from the day I first knew you.
So I lay face down before the LORD for those forty days and forty nights, because the LORD had said he would destroy you.
I prayed to the LORD and said, 'Lord GOD, do not destroy your people, your inheritance, whom you redeemed by your greatness and brought out of Egypt with a mighty hand.
Remember your servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. Do not look at the stubbornness of this people, or at their wickedness, or at their sin.

Otherwise the land you brought us out of will say, "It was because the LORD was not able to bring them into the land he had promised them, and because he hated them, that he brought them out to kill them in the wilderness."
But they are your people, your inheritance, whom you brought out by your great power and your outstretched arm.'
"At that time the LORD said to me, 'Cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and come up to me on the mountain. Also make yourself an ark of wood.
I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke, and you are to put them in the ark.'
So I made an ark of acacia wood and cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hand.
He wrote on the tablets the same words as before, the Ten Commandments that the LORD had spoken to you at the mountain, out of the fire, on the day of the assembly. And the LORD gave them to me.
Then I turned and went down from the mountain, and I put the tablets in the ark that I had made. And they are there, as the LORD commanded me.
(The Israelites set out from Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah. There Aaron died, and he was buried there, and his son Eleazar became priest in his place.
From there they set out to Gudgodah, and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah, a land of streams of water.
At that time the LORD set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the ark of the LORD's covenant, to stand before the LORD to serve him, and to bless in his name, as they still do today.
That is why Levi has no share or inheritance among his brothers. The LORD is his inheritance, as the LORD your God told him.)
I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights, as I had the first time, and the LORD listened to me that time too. The LORD was not willing to destroy you.
Then the LORD said to me, 'Get up, set out at the head of the people, so that they may go in and take possession of the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.'

And now, Israel, what does the LORD your God ask of you? Only to fear the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to love him, and to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul,
and to keep the commands and decrees of the LORD that I am giving you today, for your own good.
See, the heavens, even the highest heavens, belong to the LORD your God, and the earth and everything in it.
Yet the LORD set his heart on your ancestors and loved them, and he chose their descendants after them, you, out of all the peoples, as you are today.
So circumcise your hearts, and do not be stubborn any longer.
For the LORD your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great God, mighty and awesome, who shows no partiality and takes no bribe.
He secures justice for the fatherless and the widow, and he loves the foreigner, giving him food and clothing.
So you too must love the foreigner, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
Fear the LORD your God. Serve him, hold fast to him, and swear by his name.
He is your praise, and he is your God, who has done for you these great and awesome things that your own eyes have seen.
Your ancestors went down to Egypt seventy persons in all, and now the LORD your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the sky.
"Love the LORD your God, and always keep his charge, his decrees, his rulings and his commands.
Know today that it is not your children I am speaking to, who have not known or seen the discipline of the LORD your God: his greatness, his mighty hand and his outstretched arm,
his signs and the deeds he did in Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt and to all his land,
what he did to the army of Egypt, to its horses and its chariots, when he made the waters of the Red Sea flow over them as they pursued you, and the LORD destroyed them, as can be seen to this day,
what he did for you in the wilderness until you came to this place,

and what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, son of Reuben, when the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, with their households, their tents and every living thing that belonged to them, in the middle of all Israel.
For it is your own eyes that have seen all the great work that the LORD has done.
So keep the whole command that I am giving you today, so that you may be strong, and go in and take possession of the land you are crossing over into to possess,
and so that you may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give to them and to their descendants, a land flowing with milk and honey.
For the land you are entering to take possession of is not like the land of Egypt, from which you have come, where you sowed your seed and watered it with your foot, like a vegetable garden.
The land you are crossing over into to possess is a land of hills and valleys, which drinks water from the rain of the sky,
a land that the LORD your God cares for. The eyes of the LORD your God are always on it, from the beginning of the year to the end of the year.
If you truly listen to my commands that I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul,
then I will give the rain for your land in its season, the autumn rain and the spring rain, and you will gather in your grain, your new wine and your olive oil.
I will give grass in your fields for your livestock, and you will eat and be satisfied.
Be careful, or your hearts will be led astray, and you will turn aside and serve other gods and bow down to them.

Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you. He will shut up the sky so that there is no rain, and the ground will not yield its produce, and you will quickly perish from the good land that the LORD is giving you.
Fix these words of mine in your hearts and in your souls. Tie them as a sign on your hands, and let them be a band on your foreheads.
Teach them to your children, talking about them when you sit in your house and when you walk along the road, when you lie down and when you get up.
Write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates,
so that you and your children may live long in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give them, as long as the heavens are above the earth.
For if you are careful to keep all this command that I am giving you to follow, to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways and to hold fast to him,
then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, and you will dispossess nations greater and stronger than you.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours. Your territory will reach from the wilderness and Lebanon, and from the river, the river Euphrates, as far as the western sea.
No one will be able to stand against you. The LORD your God will put the dread and the fear of you on all the land you tread on, as he has promised you.
See, I am setting before you today a blessing and a curse:
the blessing, if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today,
and the curse, if you do not listen to the commands of the LORD your God, but turn aside from the way that I am commanding you today, to follow other gods that you have not known.
When the LORD your God brings you into the land you are entering to take possession of, you are to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.
Are they not on the other side of the Jordan, beyond the road to the west, in the land of the Canaanites who live in the Arabah, opposite Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
For you are about to cross the Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you. When you have taken possession of it and are living in it,
be careful to follow all the decrees and the rulings that I am setting before you today.
These are the decrees and the rulings that you must be careful to follow in the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you to possess, all the days you live on the earth.
You must completely destroy all the places where the nations you are dispossessing served their gods, on the high mountains, on the hills and under every leafy tree.
Tear down their altars, smash their standing stones, burn their Asherah poles in the fire, and cut down the idols of their gods. Wipe out their names from that place.
You must not worship the LORD your God in their way.
Instead, you must seek the place that the LORD your God will choose out of all your tribes to put his name there, for his dwelling, and you must go there.
There you are to bring your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and your contributions, your vow offerings and your freewill offerings, and the firstborn of your herds and your flocks.
There you and your households are to eat before the LORD your God, and rejoice in everything you have set your hand to, because the LORD your God has blessed you.
You must not do as we are doing here today, each of us doing whatever seems right in his own eyes,
for you have not yet come to the place of rest and the inheritance that the LORD your God is giving you.
But you will cross the Jordan and live in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance. He will give you rest from all your enemies around you, and you will live in safety.

Then you are to bring everything I command you to the place that the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and your contributions, and all the choice offerings you vow to the LORD.

And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your male and female slaves, and the Levite who lives in your towns, since he has no share or inheritance among you.
Be careful not to offer your burnt offerings in any place you happen to see.
Only in the place that the LORD will choose in one of your tribes, there you are to offer your burnt offerings, and there you are to do everything I command you.

However, you may slaughter and eat meat in any of your towns, as much as you want, according to the blessing that the LORD your God has given you. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
But you must not eat the blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.

In your towns you may not eat the tithe of your grain, your new wine or your olive oil, or the firstborn of your herds or your flocks, or any of the offerings you vow, or your freewill offerings, or your contributions.

Instead, you are to eat them before the LORD your God in the place that the LORD your God will choose, you and your son and your daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite who lives in your towns. And you are to rejoice before the LORD your God in everything you set your hand to.
Be careful not to neglect the Levite as long as you live in your land.
When the LORD your God enlarges your territory, as he has promised you, and you say, "I want to eat meat," because you long to eat meat, you may eat as much meat as you want.

If the place that the LORD your God will choose to put his name is too far from you, you may slaughter animals from the herds and flocks that the LORD has given you, as I have commanded you, and you may eat as much as you want in your towns.
Eat it just as a gazelle or a deer is eaten. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it.
But be sure not to eat the blood, for the blood is the life, and you must not eat the life with the meat.
Do not eat it. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Do not eat it, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you, because you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
But take the holy things that are yours to give, and your vow offerings, and go to the place that the LORD will choose.

Offer your burnt offerings, both the meat and the blood, on the altar of the LORD your God. The blood of your sacrifices is to be poured out on the altar of the LORD your God, but you may eat the meat.

Be careful to obey all these words that I am commanding you, so that it may go well with you and with your children after you forever, because you will be doing what is good and right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
When the LORD your God cuts off before you the nations you are going in to dispossess, and you dispossess them and live in their land,

be careful not to be trapped into following their ways after they have been destroyed before you. Do not inquire about their gods, saying, "How did these nations serve their gods? I will do the same."

You must not worship the LORD your God in their way, for they have done for their gods every detestable thing that the LORD hates. They even burn their sons and their daughters in the fire for their gods.
Be careful to do everything I command you. Do not add to it or take anything away from it.
If a prophet or someone who has dreams appears among you and gives you a sign or a wonder,
and the sign or wonder he told you about comes true, and he says, "Let us follow other gods," gods you have not known, "and let us serve them,"
do not listen to the words of that prophet or that dreamer. For the LORD your God is testing you, to find out whether you love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
You must follow the LORD your God and fear him. Keep his commands and listen to his voice. Serve him and hold fast to him.

That prophet or that dreamer must be put to death, because he has preached rebellion against the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the place of slavery. He has tried to lead you away from the way that the LORD your God commanded you to walk in. So you must purge the evil from among you.

Your brother, your mother's son, or your son or your daughter, or the wife you embrace, or your friend who is as dear to you as your own life, may secretly entice you, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods," gods that neither you nor your ancestors have known,
some of the gods of the peoples around you, whether near you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other.
Do not give in to him or listen to him. Show him no pity. Do not spare him or shield him.
You must kill him. Your hand must be the first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people.
Stone him to death, because he tried to lead you away from the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery.
Then all Israel will hear and be afraid, and no one among you will ever again do such an evil thing.
You may hear it said about one of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you to live in
that worthless men have gone out from among you and have led the people of their town astray, saying, "Let us go and serve other gods," gods you have not known.
Then you must inquire, investigate and ask thoroughly. If it is true and certain that this detestable thing has been done among you,
you must put the inhabitants of that town to the sword. Devote it to destruction, with everything in it, and put its livestock to the sword.

Gather all its plunder into the middle of its public square, and burn the town and all its plunder in the fire as a whole offering to the LORD your God. It must remain a ruin mound forever. It must never be rebuilt.

Nothing that is set apart for destruction must stick to your hand, so that the LORD may turn from his burning anger, and show you mercy and have compassion on you, and multiply you, as he swore to your ancestors,
because you listen to the voice of the LORD your God, keeping all his commands that I am giving you today, and doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD your God.
You are the children of the LORD your God. Do not cut yourselves or shave the front of your heads for the dead.
For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. The LORD has chosen you out of all the peoples on the face of the earth to be his people, his treasured possession.
These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat,
the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep.
You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof, split in two, and that chews the cud.

But of those that chew the cud or that have a divided, split hoof, you must not eat these: the camel, the hare and the hyrax. Although they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof. They are unclean for you.
And the pig is unclean for you, because although it has a divided hoof, it does not chew the cud. You must not eat their meat or touch their carcasses.
Of all the creatures that live in the water, you may eat these: you may eat anything that has fins and scales.
But you must not eat anything that does not have fins and scales. It is unclean for you.
You may eat any clean bird.
But these are the ones you must not eat: the eagle, the bearded vulture, the black vulture,
the red kite, the black kite, any kind of falcon,
the ostrich, the nighthawk, the seagull, any kind of hawk,
the little owl, the great owl, the white owl,
the desert owl, the carrion vulture, the cormorant,
the stork, any kind of heron, the hoopoe and the bat.
All winged swarming creatures are unclean for you. They must not be eaten.
You may eat any clean winged creature.

Do not eat anything that has died by itself. You may give it to the foreigner who lives in your towns, and he may eat it, or you may sell it to an outsider. For you are a people holy to the LORD your God. Do not boil a young goat in its mother's milk.
Each year you must set aside a tenth of all the produce of your seed that comes from the field.

In the presence of the LORD your God, at the place he will choose as a dwelling for his name, you are to eat the tithe of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the firstborn of your herds and your flocks, so that you may learn to fear the LORD your God always.
But the LORD your God may bless you so much that the journey is too long for you to carry the tithe, because the place where the LORD your God will choose to put his name is too far from you.
Then exchange it for money. Wrap up the money and take it with you, and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
Spend the money on whatever you want: cattle or sheep, wine or beer, or anything you wish. Eat it there in the presence of the LORD your God, and rejoice, you and your household.
And do not neglect the Levite who lives in your towns, for he has no share or inheritance among you.
At the end of every three years, bring out the whole tithe of your produce for that year and store it in your towns.

Then the Levite, who has no share or inheritance among you, and the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow who live in your towns, may come and eat and be satisfied, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work you do with your hands.
At the end of every seven years you must grant a release.

This is how the release is to be done: every creditor is to cancel the loan he has made to his neighbor. He must not press his neighbor, his fellow Israelite, for payment, because a release has been proclaimed for the LORD.
You may press a foreigner for payment, but you must cancel whatever your fellow Israelite owes you.
However, there should be no poor among you, for the LORD will richly bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess,
if only you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and are careful to follow all this command that I am giving you today.
For the LORD your God will bless you, as he has promised you. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow. You will rule over many nations, but they will not rule over you.

If there is a poor person among you, one of your fellow Israelites, in any of your towns in the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not be hardhearted or tightfisted toward your poor brother.
Instead, open your hand to him freely, and lend him enough for whatever he needs.

Be careful not to harbor this wicked thought: "The seventh year, the year of release, is near," and so look grudgingly on your poor brother and give him nothing. He may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Give to him generously, and do not give with a grudging heart, for because of this the LORD your God will bless you in all your work and in everything you set your hand to.
For there will never cease to be poor people in the land. That is why I command you: open your hand freely to your brother, to the needy and the poor in your land.
If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or a Hebrew woman, is sold to you and serves you for six years, then in the seventh year you must set that person free.
And when you set him free, do not send him away empty-handed.
Supply him generously from your flock, your threshing floor and your winepress. Give to him as the LORD your God has blessed you.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you. That is why I am giving you this command today.
But if he says to you, "I do not want to leave you," because he loves you and your household and is well off with you,
then take an awl and drive it through his ear into the door, and he will be your slave for life. Do the same for your female slave.
Do not consider it a hardship to set him free, for his six years of service to you have been worth twice the wages of a hired worker. And the LORD your God will bless you in everything you do.
Set apart for the LORD your God every firstborn male born in your herd and in your flock. Do not put the firstborn of your oxen to work, and do not shear the firstborn of your sheep.
Each year you and your household are to eat them before the LORD your God, in the place that the LORD will choose.
But if an animal has a defect, if it is lame or blind or has any serious defect, you must not sacrifice it to the LORD your God.
Eat it in your towns. Both the unclean and the clean may eat it, as they would a gazelle or a deer.
But you must not eat its blood. Pour it out on the ground like water.
Observe the month of Abib and keep the Passover for the LORD your God, for in the month of Abib the LORD your God brought you out of Egypt by night.
Sacrifice the Passover animal for the LORD your God from your flock or your herd, at the place that the LORD will choose as a dwelling for his name.

Do not eat anything made with yeast with it. For seven days eat bread made without yeast with it, the bread of hardship, because you left the land of Egypt in haste. Do this so that all the days of your life you may remember the day you left the land of Egypt.
No yeast is to be found among you anywhere in your territory for seven days, and none of the meat you sacrifice on the evening of the first day is to be left overnight until morning.
You may not sacrifice the Passover in just any of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you,
but only at the place that the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name. There you are to sacrifice the Passover in the evening, at sunset, at the time when you came out of Egypt.
Cook it and eat it at the place that the LORD your God will choose. Then in the morning turn and go back to your tents.
For six days eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day hold a solemn assembly for the LORD your God. Do no work on that day.
Count seven weeks. Begin to count the seven weeks from the time you first put the sickle to the standing grain.
Then keep the Festival of Weeks for the LORD your God with a freewill offering from your hand, given in proportion to how the LORD your God has blessed you.

Rejoice before the LORD your God at the place that the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name, you and your son and your daughter, your male and female slaves, the Levite who lives in your towns, and the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow who live among you.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and be careful to follow these decrees.
Keep the Festival of Shelters for seven days, when you have gathered in the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress.
Rejoice at your festival, you and your son and your daughter, your male and female slaves, and the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow who live in your towns.

For seven days keep the festival for the LORD your God at the place that the LORD will choose, for the LORD your God will bless you in all your harvest and in all the work of your hands, and you will be full of joy.

Three times a year all your males are to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks and at the Festival of Shelters. No one is to appear before the LORD empty-handed.
Each of you is to give as he is able, according to the blessing that the LORD your God has given you.
Appoint judges and officials for your tribes in all the towns that the LORD your God is giving you, and they are to judge the people with righteous judgment.
Do not twist justice. Do not show partiality. Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and twists the words of those who are in the right.
Pursue justice, justice alone, so that you may live and possess the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Do not plant any kind of tree as an Asherah pole beside the altar you build for the LORD your God.
And do not set up a standing stone, which the LORD your God hates.
Do not sacrifice to the LORD your God an ox or a sheep that has a defect or anything wrong with it, for that is detestable to the LORD your God.
Suppose a man or a woman is found among you, in one of the towns that the LORD your God is giving you, who does what is evil in the eyes of the LORD your God by breaking his covenant.
That person has gone and served other gods and bowed down to them, or to the sun or the moon or any of the host of heaven, which I have forbidden.
If you are told about it and hear of it, you must investigate thoroughly. If it is true and certain that this detestable thing has been done in Israel,
you must bring out to your town gates the man or the woman who has done this evil thing, the man or the woman, and stone that person to death.
The one who is to die must be put to death on the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses. No one is to be put to death on the testimony of only one witness.
The hands of the witnesses must be the first against him to put him to death, and then the hands of all the people. So you must purge the evil from among you.

If a case comes before you that is too hard for you to judge, whether it concerns bloodshed, a legal claim or an assault, or any dispute in your towns, then get up and go to the place that the LORD your God will choose.
Go to the Levitical priests and to the judge who is in office at that time. Inquire of them, and they will declare the verdict to you.
You must act according to the verdict they declare to you at the place that the LORD will choose. Be careful to do everything they instruct you.
Act according to the instruction they give you and the ruling they tell you. Do not turn aside from the verdict they declare to you, either to the right or to the left.
Anyone who acts presumptuously and will not listen to the priest who stands there to serve the LORD your God, or to the judge, must die. So you must purge the evil from Israel.
Then all the people will hear and be afraid, and they will not act presumptuously again.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and have taken possession of it and settled in it, you may say, "Let me set a king over me, like all the nations around me."
Then be sure to set over you a king whom the LORD your God will choose. You are to set over you a king from among your own people. You may not put a foreigner over you, one who is not your brother.
But he must not acquire many horses for himself, or make the people go back to Egypt to acquire many horses, for the LORD has said to you, "You must never go back that way again."
He must not take many wives for himself, or his heart will turn away. And he must not acquire great amounts of silver and gold for himself.
When he sits on the throne of his kingdom, he is to write for himself on a scroll a copy of this law, taken from the one kept by the Levitical priests.
It is to be with him, and he is to read from it all the days of his life, so that he may learn to fear the LORD his God by keeping all the words of this law and these decrees and doing them,

so that his heart will not be lifted up above his brothers, and so that he will not turn aside from the command, to the right or to the left. Then he and his sons will reign long over his kingdom in Israel.
The Levitical priests, the whole tribe of Levi, are to have no share or inheritance with Israel. They are to eat the food offerings for the LORD, which are his inheritance.
They will have no inheritance among their brothers. The LORD is their inheritance, as he promised them.
This is what is due to the priests from the people, from those who offer a sacrifice, whether an ox or a sheep: they are to give the priest the shoulder, the two cheeks and the stomach.
You are to give him the first of your grain, your new wine and your olive oil, and the first wool from the shearing of your sheep.
For the LORD your God has chosen him and his sons out of all your tribes to stand and serve in the name of the LORD for all time.
If a Levite comes from one of your towns anywhere in Israel where he is living, he may come whenever he wishes to the place that the LORD will choose,
and serve in the name of the LORD his God like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the LORD.
They are to have equal portions to eat, besides what he receives from the sale of his family property.
When you come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, do not learn to imitate the detestable practices of those nations.
There must not be found among you anyone who makes his son or his daughter pass through the fire, or who practices divination, or tells fortunes, or interprets omens, or practices sorcery,
or casts spells, or consults ghosts or spirits, or inquires of the dead.
For anyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD, and it is because of these detestable practices that the LORD your God is driving those nations out before you.
You must be blameless before the LORD your God.
These nations you are about to dispossess listen to fortune-tellers and diviners. But as for you, the LORD your God has not allowed you to do so.
The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among you, from your own people. You must listen to him.

This is just what you asked of the LORD your God at Horeb on the day of the assembly, when you said, "Let me not hear the voice of the LORD my God again, or see this great fire any more, or I will die."
And the LORD said to me, "What they have said is good.
I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people. I will put my words in his mouth, and he will tell them everything I command him.
If anyone does not listen to my words that he speaks in my name, I myself will hold him accountable.
But a prophet who presumes to speak in my name a word I have not commanded him to speak, or who speaks in the name of other gods, that prophet must die."
You may say to yourself, "How can we know which word the LORD has not spoken?"
If a prophet speaks in the name of the LORD and the thing does not happen or come true, that is a word the LORD has not spoken. The prophet has spoken it presumptuously. Do not be afraid of him.
When the LORD your God has cut off the nations whose land the LORD your God is giving you, and you have dispossessed them and settled in their towns and their houses,
set apart for yourself three cities in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
Prepare the roads, and divide into three parts the territory of the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, so that anyone who has killed someone can flee there.
This is the rule for someone who kills another person and flees there to save his life: he must have killed his neighbor unintentionally, without having been his enemy before.

For example, a man goes into the forest with his neighbor to cut wood. As he swings the axe to cut down a tree, the head flies off the handle and hits his neighbor, and he dies. That man may flee to one of these cities and save his life.

Otherwise the avenger of blood, in hot anger, might pursue the killer and overtake him because the distance is great, and kill him, though he did not deserve to die, since he had not been his enemy before.
That is why I command you to set apart for yourself three cities.
The LORD your God may enlarge your territory, as he swore to your ancestors, and give you all the land he promised to give your ancestors,
if you are careful to keep all this command that I am giving you today, to love the LORD your God and to walk in his ways always. Then you are to add three more cities to these three.
This is so that innocent blood will not be shed in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and you will not be guilty of bloodshed.
But suppose someone hates his neighbor, lies in wait for him, attacks him and kills him, and then flees to one of these cities.
The elders of his town are to send for him and bring him back from there, and hand him over to the avenger of blood to be put to death.
Show him no pity. You must purge the guilt of innocent blood from Israel, so that it may go well with you.
Do not move your neighbor's boundary marker, set up by those who came before you, in the inheritance you will receive in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.
A single witness is not enough to convict anyone of any wrongdoing or any sin, whatever sin he may have committed. A matter must be established on the testimony of two witnesses or three witnesses.
If a malicious witness comes forward against someone to accuse him of wrongdoing,
the two people involved in the dispute must stand before the LORD, before the priests and the judges who are in office at that time.
The judges must investigate thoroughly. If the witness turns out to be a false witness, who has given false testimony against his brother,
then do to him what he intended to do to his brother. So you must purge the evil from among you.
The rest of the people will hear and be afraid, and such an evil thing will never again be done among you.
Show no pity: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

When you go out to war against your enemies and see horses and chariots and an army larger than yours, do not be afraid of them, for the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt, is with you.
When you are about to go into battle, the priest is to come forward and speak to the army.
He is to say to them, "Hear, Israel. Today you are going into battle against your enemies. Do not lose heart. Do not be afraid, or alarmed, or terrified of them.
For the LORD your God is the one who goes with you, to fight for you against your enemies and to give you victory."
Then the officials are to say to the army, "Has anyone built a new house and not yet dedicated it? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in battle and someone else dedicate it.
Has anyone planted a vineyard and not yet begun to enjoy its fruit? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in battle and someone else enjoy it.
Has anyone become engaged to a woman and not yet married her? Let him go back to his house, or he may die in battle and someone else marry her."
Then the officials are to speak further to the army and say, "Is anyone afraid or fainthearted? Let him go back to his house, so that he does not make his brothers lose heart as he has."
When the officials have finished speaking to the army, commanders are to be appointed at the head of the troops.
When you approach a town to attack it, first offer it terms of peace.
If it accepts your terms and opens its gates to you, all the people found in it are to become forced laborers for you and serve you.
But if it does not make peace with you and goes to war with you, then lay siege to it.
When the LORD your God hands it over to you, put all its males to the sword.

But the women, the children, the livestock and everything else in the town, all its plunder, you may take as spoil for yourselves. And you may enjoy the spoil of your enemies that the LORD your God has given you.
This is what you are to do to all the towns that are very far away from you, which are not among the towns of these nations.
But in the towns of these peoples that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, you must not leave alive anything that breathes.
You must devote them completely to destruction: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, as the LORD your God has commanded you,
so that they will not teach you to do all the detestable things they do for their gods, and so cause you to sin against the LORD your God.

When you besiege a town for a long time, fighting against it to capture it, do not destroy its trees by swinging an axe against them. You may eat from them, but you must not cut them down. Are the trees of the field human beings, that you should besiege them?
Only the trees that you know are not fruit trees may you destroy and cut down, to build siege works against the town that is at war with you, until it falls.
If someone is found killed, lying in the open country in the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess, and it is not known who killed him,
your elders and your judges are to go out and measure the distance to the towns around the body.
The elders of the town nearest to the body are to take a heifer that has never been worked and has never pulled in a yoke.
The elders of that town are to bring the heifer down to a valley with a stream that never runs dry, which has not been plowed or sown, and there in the valley they are to break the heifer's neck.

Then the priests, the sons of Levi, are to come forward, for the LORD your God has chosen them to serve him and to bless in the name of the LORD, and by their word every dispute and every case of assault is to be settled.
All the elders of the town nearest to the body are to wash their hands over the heifer whose neck was broken in the valley,
and they are to declare, "Our hands did not shed this blood, and our eyes did not see it.
LORD, forgive your people Israel, whom you have redeemed, and do not hold the guilt of innocent blood against your people Israel." Then the bloodshed will be forgiven them.
So you will purge the guilt of innocent blood from among you, for you will be doing what is right in the eyes of the LORD.
When you go out to war against your enemies, and the LORD your God hands them over to you and you take some of them captive,
you may see among the captives a beautiful woman, and desire her, and want to take her as your wife.
Bring her into your house. She is to shave her head and trim her nails,

and take off the clothes she was wearing when she was captured. She is to live in your house and mourn her father and her mother for a full month. After that you may go to her and be her husband, and she will be your wife.
But if you are no longer pleased with her, let her go wherever she wishes. You must not sell her for money or treat her as a slave, because you have dishonored her.
If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and both the loved wife and the unloved wife bear him sons, and the firstborn son is the son of the unloved wife,
then on the day he divides his property among his sons as their inheritance, he may not treat the son of the loved wife as his firstborn in place of the son of the unloved wife, who is the firstborn.

He must acknowledge the son of the unloved wife as the firstborn by giving him a double share of everything he has, for he is the first sign of his father's strength. The right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If someone has a stubborn and rebellious son who will not obey his father or his mother, and will not listen to them even when they discipline him,
his father and his mother are to take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his town, at the gate of the place where he lives.
They are to say to the elders of his town, "This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious. He will not obey us. He is a glutton and a drunkard."
Then all the men of his town are to stone him to death. So you must purge the evil from among you, and all Israel will hear and be afraid.
If someone has committed a sin that deserves the death penalty and has been put to death, and you hang his body on a tree,

his body must not remain on the tree overnight. You must bury him that same day, for anyone who is hung on a tree is cursed by God. You must not defile the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
If you see a fellow Israelite's ox or sheep wandering off, do not ignore it. You must take it back to him.
If he does not live near you, or you do not know who he is, bring the animal home and keep it with you until he comes looking for it. Then give it back to him.
Do the same with his donkey, and with his cloak, and with anything else he has lost that you find. You must not ignore it.
If you see a fellow Israelite's donkey or ox fallen on the road, do not ignore it. You must help him get it back on its feet.
A woman must not wear a man's things, and a man must not put on a woman's clothing, for anyone who does these things is detestable to the LORD your God.

If you come across a bird's nest beside the road, in any tree or on the ground, with young birds or eggs, and the mother sitting on the young or on the eggs, do not take the mother along with the young.
You must let the mother go, but you may take the young for yourself, so that it may go well with you and you may live long.
When you build a new house, make a railing around your roof, so that you will not bring the guilt of bloodshed on your house if someone falls from it.
Do not sow your vineyard with a second kind of seed, or the whole crop, both the seed you have sown and the fruit of the vineyard, will be forfeited.
Do not plow with an ox and a donkey together.
Do not wear clothing of mixed material, wool and linen together.
Make tassels on the four corners of the cloak you wrap yourself in.
Suppose a man marries a woman and sleeps with her, and then turns against her.
He makes up charges against her and gives her a bad name, saying, "I married this woman, but when I came near her I did not find the evidence of her virginity."
Then the young woman's father and mother are to take the evidence of her virginity and bring it out to the elders of the town at the gate.
The young woman's father is to say to the elders, "I gave my daughter to this man as his wife, but he has turned against her.

Now he has made up charges against her, saying, 'I did not find the evidence of your daughter's virginity.' But here is the evidence of my daughter's virginity." Then they are to spread out the cloth before the elders of the town.
The elders of that town are to take the man and punish him.

They are to fine him a hundred shekels of silver and give it to the young woman's father, because the man has given an Israelite virgin a bad name. She will remain his wife, and he may not divorce her as long as he lives.
But if the charge is true, and no evidence of the young woman's virginity is found,

they are to bring the young woman out to the door of her father's house, and the men of her town are to stone her to death. She has done a disgraceful thing in Israel by being promiscuous while in her father's house. So you must purge the evil from among you.
If a man is found sleeping with another man's wife, both of them must die, the man who slept with the woman and the woman. So you must purge the evil from Israel.
If a young woman who is a virgin is engaged to a man, and another man meets her in the town and sleeps with her,

you are to take both of them out to the gate of that town and stone them to death: the young woman because she did not cry for help in the town, and the man because he violated his neighbor's wife. So you must purge the evil from among you.
But if the man meets the engaged young woman in the open country, and seizes her and sleeps with her, only the man who slept with her must die.
Do nothing to the young woman. She has committed no sin that deserves death. This case is like that of a man who attacks his neighbor and murders him.
For he met her in the open country, and though the engaged young woman cried out, there was no one to rescue her.
If a man meets a young woman who is a virgin and is not engaged, and seizes her and sleeps with her, and they are found out,
the man who slept with her must give the young woman's father fifty shekels of silver, and she must become his wife. Because he has violated her, he may not divorce her as long as he lives.
A man must not marry his father's wife. He must not uncover his father's garment.
No one whose testicles are crushed or whose penis is cut off may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No one born of a forbidden union may enter the assembly of the LORD. Even to the tenth generation, none of his descendants may enter the assembly of the LORD.
No Ammonite or Moabite may enter the assembly of the LORD. Even to the tenth generation, none of their descendants may ever enter the assembly of the LORD,
because they did not come to meet you with food and water on the way when you came out of Egypt, and because Moab hired Balaam son of Beor, from Pethor in Aram-naharaim, to curse you.
But the LORD your God would not listen to Balaam. The LORD your God turned the curse into a blessing for you, because the LORD your God loves you.
Never seek their peace or their prosperity, as long as you live.
Do not abhor an Edomite, for he is your brother. Do not abhor an Egyptian, because you were a foreigner in his land.
The children born to them in the third generation may enter the assembly of the LORD.
When you go out as an army against your enemies, keep away from everything improper.
If one of your men is unclean because of an emission during the night, he must go outside the camp. He must not come inside the camp.
As evening approaches he is to wash himself with water, and at sunset he may come back into the camp.
You are to have a place outside the camp, and you are to go out there to relieve yourself.
Among your equipment you are to have a digging tool. When you squat outside, dig a hole with it, and then turn and cover your excrement.

For the LORD your God walks about in the middle of your camp to rescue you and to hand over your enemies to you. So your camp must be holy, so that he does not see anything indecent among you and turn away from you.
If a slave has escaped from his master and taken refuge with you, do not hand him over to his master.
Let him live among you, in whatever place he chooses in one of your towns, wherever he likes. Do not oppress him.
No daughter of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute, and no son of Israel is to be a shrine prostitute.
Do not bring the earnings of a prostitute or the wages of a dog into the house of the LORD your God to pay any vow, for both of them are detestable to the LORD your God.
Do not charge interest to your fellow Israelite, whether on money or on food or on anything else that can earn interest.

You may charge interest to a foreigner, but not to your fellow Israelite, so that the LORD your God may bless you in everything you set your hand to in the land you are entering to take possession of.
If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to fulfill it, for the LORD your God will certainly require it of you, and you will be guilty of sin.
But if you refrain from making a vow, you will not be guilty of sin.
Be careful to do what has passed your lips, just as you freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth.
When you go into your neighbor's vineyard, you may eat as many grapes as you want, until you are satisfied, but you must not put any in your basket.
When you go into your neighbor's standing grain, you may pick the ears with your hand, but you must not put a sickle to your neighbor's standing grain.

Suppose a man marries a woman and becomes her husband, and she does not please him because he has found something indecent about her. He writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her away from his house.
She leaves his house and goes and becomes another man's wife.
Then the second man turns against her, writes her a certificate of divorce, puts it in her hand and sends her away from his house, or the second man who married her dies.

In that case her first husband, who sent her away, may not take her back to be his wife, since she has been defiled, for that would be detestable to the LORD. You must not bring sin on the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance.
When a man has newly married, he is not to go out with the army or be given any other duty. He is to be free to stay at home for one year and bring joy to the wife he has married.
No one is to take a pair of millstones, or even the upper millstone, as security for a debt, for that would be taking a life as security.
If someone is found kidnapping a fellow Israelite and treating him as a slave or selling him, that kidnapper must die. So you must purge the evil from among you.
In cases of skin disease, be very careful to do everything the Levitical priests instruct you. Be careful to do as I have commanded them.
Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam on the way when you came out of Egypt.
When you make your neighbor a loan of any kind, do not go into his house to take what he offers as security.
Stay outside, and let the man to whom you are making the loan bring the security out to you.
If he is poor, do not go to sleep with his security in your keeping.
Be sure to give it back to him at sunset, so that he may sleep in his cloak and bless you. And it will be counted as righteousness for you before the LORD your God.
Do not take advantage of a hired worker who is poor and needy, whether he is a fellow Israelite or a foreigner who lives in your land, in one of your towns.
Pay him his wages each day before sunset, because he is poor and is counting on it. Otherwise he may cry out to the LORD against you, and you will be guilty of sin.
Parents are not to be put to death for their children, and children are not to be put to death for their parents. Each is to be put to death for his own sin.
Do not deny justice to the foreigner or the fatherless, and do not take a widow's cloak as security.
Remember that you were a slave in Egypt, and the LORD your God redeemed you from there. That is why I command you to do this.

When you reap the harvest in your field and forget a sheaf in the field, do not go back to get it. It is to be for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, so that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hands.
When you beat your olive trees, do not go over the branches a second time. What is left is to be for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow.
When you gather the grapes of your vineyard, do not go over it a second time. What is left is to be for the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow.
Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt. That is why I command you to do this.
If there is a dispute between people, and they go to court and the judges decide between them, they are to acquit the innocent and condemn the guilty.
If the guilty one deserves to be beaten, the judge is to make him lie down and have him beaten in his presence with the number of lashes his crime deserves.
He may be given forty lashes, but no more. If he is beaten with many more lashes than these, your fellow Israelite will be degraded before your eyes.
Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain.

If brothers live together and one of them dies without a son, the dead man's widow must not marry outside the family, to a stranger. Her husband's brother is to go to her and take her as his wife, and do the duty of a husband's brother to her.
The first son she bears is to carry on the name of the dead brother, so that his name will not be wiped out from Israel.

But if the man does not want to marry his brother's widow, she is to go up to the elders at the gate and say, "My husband's brother refuses to keep his brother's name alive in Israel. He is not willing to do the duty of a husband's brother to me."
Then the elders of his town are to summon him and speak to him. If he stands firm and says, "I do not want to marry her,"

his brother's widow is to go up to him in the presence of the elders, pull his sandal off his foot, spit in his face, and declare, "This is what is done to the man who will not build up his brother's family."
And his family will be known in Israel as "The house of the man whose sandal was pulled off."
If two men are fighting each other, and the wife of one of them comes near to rescue her husband from the man who is hitting him, and she reaches out and seizes him by his private parts,
you are to cut off her hand. Show her no pity.
Do not have two different weights in your bag, one heavy and one light.
Do not have two different measures in your house, one large and one small.
You must have a full and honest weight and a full and honest measure, so that you may live long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
For anyone who does such things, anyone who acts dishonestly, is detestable to the LORD your God.
Remember what Amalek did to you on the way when you came out of Egypt,
how he met you on the way when you were faint and weary, and cut off all the stragglers at your rear. He did not fear God.

So when the LORD your God has given you rest from all your enemies around you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess, you must wipe out the memory of Amalek from under heaven. Do not forget!
When you have come into the land that the LORD your God is giving you as an inheritance, and have taken possession of it and settled in it,

take some of the first of all the produce of the soil that you bring in from the land that the LORD your God is giving you, and put it in a basket. Then go to the place that the LORD your God will choose as a dwelling for his name.
Go to the priest who is in office at that time and say to him, "I declare today to the LORD your God that I have come into the land that the LORD swore to our ancestors to give us."
The priest is to take the basket from your hand and set it down in front of the altar of the LORD your God.

Then you are to declare before the LORD your God, "My father was a wandering Aramean. He went down to Egypt with only a few people and lived there as a foreigner, and there he became a great nation, mighty and numerous.
But the Egyptians treated us harshly and oppressed us, and they imposed hard labor on us.
Then we cried out to the LORD, the God of our ancestors, and the LORD heard our voice and saw our misery, our toil and our oppression.
The LORD brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm, with great terror, and with signs and wonders.
He brought us to this place and gave us this land, a land flowing with milk and honey.
And now, here I have brought the first of the produce of the soil that you, LORD, have given me." Then set it down before the LORD your God, and bow down before the LORD your God.
Then you and the Levite and the foreigner who lives among you are to rejoice in all the good things that the LORD your God has given to you and your household.

When you have finished setting aside the whole tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe, and have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, so that they may eat in your towns and be satisfied,

then say before the LORD your God, "I have removed the holy portion from my house, and I have given it to the Levite, the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, just as you commanded me. I have not turned aside from any of your commands, and I have not forgotten them.

I have not eaten any of it while I was in mourning, or removed any of it while I was unclean, or given any of it for the dead. I have listened to the voice of the LORD my God. I have done everything you commanded me.
Look down from your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless your people Israel and the land you have given us, as you swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey."
This day the LORD your God commands you to follow these decrees and rulings. Be careful to follow them with all your heart and with all your soul.
Today you have declared that the LORD is your God, and that you will walk in his ways, and keep his decrees, his commands and his rulings, and listen to his voice.
And today the LORD has declared that you are his people, his treasured possession, as he promised you, and that you are to keep all his commands,
and that he will set you high above all the nations he has made, for praise, fame and honor, and that you will be a people holy to the LORD your God, as he promised.
Then Moses and the elders of Israel commanded the people, "Keep the whole command that I am giving you today.
On the day you cross the Jordan into the land that the LORD your God is giving you, set up some large stones and coat them with plaster.

Write on them all the words of this law when you have crossed over, so that you may enter the land that the LORD your God is giving you, a land flowing with milk and honey, as the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has promised you.
When you have crossed the Jordan, set up these stones on Mount Ebal, as I am commanding you today, and coat them with plaster.
Build an altar there to the LORD your God, an altar of stones. Do not use any iron tool on them.
Build the altar of the LORD your God with uncut stones, and offer burnt offerings on it to the LORD your God.
Sacrifice fellowship offerings and eat them there, and rejoice before the LORD your God.
And write very clearly on the stones all the words of this law."
Then Moses and the Levitical priests spoke to all Israel, "Be silent and listen, Israel. This day you have become the people of the LORD your God.
So listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and follow his commands and his decrees that I am giving you today."
That day Moses gave the people this command:
"When you have crossed the Jordan, these tribes are to stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph and Benjamin.
And these tribes are to stand on Mount Ebal for the curse: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan and Naphtali.
The Levites are to proclaim in a loud voice to all the people of Israel:
'Cursed is anyone who makes a carved or cast idol, something detestable to the LORD, the work of a craftsman's hands, and sets it up in secret.' And all the people are to respond, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who treats his father or his mother with contempt.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who moves his neighbor's boundary marker.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who leads a blind person astray on the road.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who denies justice to the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his father's wife, for he uncovers his father's garment.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who has sexual relations with any animal.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his sister, the daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who sleeps with his mother-in-law.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who strikes down his neighbor in secret.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who accepts a bribe to kill an innocent person.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'
'Cursed is anyone who does not uphold the words of this law by doing them.' And all the people are to say, 'Amen.'

"If you listen carefully to the voice of the LORD your God and are careful to follow all his commands that I am giving you today, the LORD your God will set you high above all the nations of the earth.
All these blessings will come on you and overtake you, if you listen to the voice of the LORD your God:
You will be blessed in the city, and blessed in the country.
The fruit of your womb will be blessed, and the fruit of your ground and the fruit of your livestock, the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be blessed.
You will be blessed when you come in, and blessed when you go out.
The LORD will make your enemies who rise up against you be defeated before you. They will come out against you by one road, and flee from you by seven roads.
The LORD will command the blessing to be with you in your barns and in everything you set your hand to. He will bless you in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
The LORD will establish you as a people holy to himself, as he swore to you, if you keep the commands of the LORD your God and walk in his ways.
Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will be afraid of you.
The LORD will make you abound in good things: in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground, in the land that the LORD swore to your ancestors to give you.
The LORD will open for you his rich storehouse, the heavens, to give rain to your land in its season and to bless all the work of your hands. You will lend to many nations, but you will not borrow.

The LORD will make you the head and not the tail. You will always be at the top and never at the bottom, if you listen to the commands of the LORD your God that I am giving you today, and are careful to follow them,
and if you do not turn aside from any of the words that I am commanding you today, to the right or to the left, to follow other gods and serve them.

But if you do not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, and are not careful to follow all his commands and his decrees that I am giving you today, then all these curses will come on you and overtake you:
You will be cursed in the city, and cursed in the country.
Your basket and your kneading bowl will be cursed.
The fruit of your womb will be cursed, and the fruit of your ground, the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks.
You will be cursed when you come in, and cursed when you go out.
The LORD will send on you curse, confusion and rebuke in everything you set your hand to, until you are destroyed and quickly perish because of the evil of your deeds, because you have abandoned me.
The LORD will make disease cling to you until he has wiped you out from the land you are entering to take possession of.
The LORD will strike you with wasting disease, fever and inflammation, with scorching heat and drought, and with blight and mildew. They will pursue you until you perish.
The sky over your head will be bronze, and the earth under you iron.
The LORD will turn the rain of your land into powder and dust. It will come down on you from the sky until you are destroyed.
The LORD will make you be defeated before your enemies. You will go out against them by one road, and flee from them by seven roads. You will become a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
Your dead bodies will be food for all the birds of the sky and the wild animals, and there will be no one to frighten them away.
The LORD will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, with festering sores and with the itch, and you will not be able to be healed.
The LORD will strike you with madness, blindness and confusion of mind.

At noon you will grope about, as a blind person gropes in the darkness. You will not succeed in anything you do. You will be nothing but oppressed and robbed all the time, and there will be no one to rescue you.
You will become engaged to a woman, but another man will sleep with her. You will build a house, but you will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard, but you will not enjoy its fruit.

Your ox will be slaughtered before your eyes, but you will not eat any of it. Your donkey will be taken from you by force and will not be given back. Your sheep will be given to your enemies, and no one will rescue you.
Your sons and your daughters will be given to another people, while your eyes look on and grow weary with longing for them all day long, and you will be powerless.
A people you have not known will eat the fruit of your ground and everything you have worked for. You will be nothing but oppressed and crushed all the time.
You will be driven mad by the sights your eyes will see.
