The LORD will strike you on the knees and on the legs with painful boils that cannot be healed, from the sole of your foot to the top of your head.
The LORD will bring you, and the king you set over you, to a nation that neither you nor your ancestors have known. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone.
You will become a horror, a proverb and a byword among all the peoples where the LORD will drive you.
You will take much seed out to the field but gather little in, for the locusts will devour it.
You will plant vineyards and work them, but you will not drink the wine or gather the grapes, for the worms will eat them.
You will have olive trees throughout your territory, but you will not anoint yourself with the oil, for your olives will drop off.
You will have sons and daughters, but they will not be yours, for they will go into captivity.
Swarming locusts will take over all your trees and the fruit of your ground.
The foreigner who lives among you will rise higher and higher above you, while you sink lower and lower.
He will lend to you, but you will not lend to him. He will be the head, and you will be the tail.

All these curses will come on you. They will pursue you and overtake you until you are destroyed, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God, to keep his commands and his decrees that he commanded you.
They will be a sign and a wonder against you and your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the LORD your God with joy and gladness of heart when you had plenty of everything,
you will serve the enemies whom the LORD will send against you, in hunger and thirst, in nakedness and in lack of everything. He will put an iron yoke on your neck until he has destroyed you.
The LORD will bring against you a nation from far away, from the end of the earth, swooping down like an eagle, a nation whose language you do not understand,
a fierce-looking nation, which shows no respect for the old and no mercy to the young.

It will eat the young of your livestock and the produce of your ground until you are destroyed. It will leave you no grain, new wine or olive oil, no calves of your herds or lambs of your flocks, until it has ruined you.

It will besiege you in all your towns, until the high, fortified walls that you trust in come down throughout your land. It will besiege you in all your towns throughout the land that the LORD your God has given you.
In the siege and the distress that your enemy will bring on you, you will eat the fruit of your womb, the flesh of your sons and your daughters whom the LORD your God has given you.
Even the most gentle and refined man among you will look grudgingly at his brother, at the wife he embraces, and at the last of his children who are left,
refusing to give any of them the flesh of his children that he is eating, because he has nothing else left in the siege and the distress that your enemy will bring on you in all your towns.

The most gentle and refined woman among you, so gentle and refined that she would not think of setting the sole of her foot on the ground, will look grudgingly at the husband she embraces, at her son and at her daughter,

and at the afterbirth that comes out from between her legs and at the children she bears. For she will eat them in secret, because she lacks everything, in the siege and the distress that your enemy will bring on you in your towns.
If you are not careful to follow all the words of this law that are written in this book, and to fear this glorious and awesome name, the LORD your God,
the LORD will strike you and your descendants with extraordinary plagues, great and lasting plagues, and severe and lasting illnesses.
He will bring back on you all the diseases of Egypt that you dreaded, and they will cling to you.
The LORD will also bring on you every sickness and every plague that is not written in the book of this law, until you are destroyed.
You who were as numerous as the stars of the sky will be left few in number, because you did not listen to the voice of the LORD your God.
Just as the LORD delighted in doing you good and multiplying you, so the LORD will delight in ruining you and destroying you. You will be torn from the land you are entering to take possession of.
The LORD will scatter you among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other. There you will serve other gods, gods of wood and stone, which neither you nor your ancestors have known.
Among those nations you will find no rest, no resting place for the sole of your foot. There the LORD will give you an anxious heart, eyes that fail with longing, and a despairing spirit.
Your life will hang in doubt before you. You will be afraid night and day, and you will never be sure of your life.
In the morning you will say, 'If only it were evening!' and in the evening you will say, 'If only it were morning!' because of the dread that fills your heart and the sights your eyes will see.

The LORD will bring you back to Egypt in ships, by the way that I told you you would never see again. There you will offer yourselves for sale to your enemies as male and female slaves, but no one will buy you."
These are the words of the covenant that the LORD commanded Moses to make with the Israelites in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant he had made with them at Horeb.
Moses summoned all Israel and said to them, "You have seen all that the LORD did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land:
the great trials that your eyes saw, those great signs and wonders.
But to this day the LORD has not given you a mind to understand, or eyes to see, or ears to hear.
I led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your sandals did not wear out on your feet.
You did not eat bread, and you did not drink wine or beer, so that you might know that I am the LORD your God.
When you came to this place, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan came out against us to fight, but we defeated them.
We took their land and gave it as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
So be careful to follow the words of this covenant, so that you may succeed in everything you do.
All of you are standing today before the LORD your God: your leaders and your tribes, your elders and your officials, all the men of Israel,
your little ones, your wives, and the foreigners who live in your camp, from those who cut your wood to those who draw your water,
so that you may enter into the covenant of the LORD your God, and into the oath that the LORD your God is making with you today,
in order to establish you today as his people, and so that he may be your God, as he promised you and as he swore to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob.
It is not with you alone that I am making this covenant and this oath,
but with those who are standing here with us today before the LORD our God, and also with those who are not here with us today.
For you know how we lived in the land of Egypt, and how we passed through the middle of the nations you passed through.
You saw their detestable things and their idols, of wood and stone, of silver and gold, which they had among them.

Make sure that there is no man or woman, no clan or tribe, among you whose heart turns away today from the LORD our God, to go and serve the gods of those nations. Make sure that there is no root among you that bears poisonous and bitter fruit.

When such a person hears the words of this oath, he may bless himself in his heart and think, 'I will be safe, though I follow my own stubborn heart.' That would sweep away the watered land and the dry alike.

The LORD will never be willing to forgive him. Instead, the anger and jealousy of the LORD will smoke against that man. Every curse written in this book will settle on him, and the LORD will wipe out his name from under heaven.
The LORD will single him out from all the tribes of Israel for disaster, according to all the curses of the covenant written in this book of the law.

The generation to come, your children who rise up after you, and the foreigner who comes from a distant land, will speak about it, when they see the plagues of that land and the diseases that the LORD has brought on it:

the whole land burned out with sulfur and salt, nothing sown, nothing growing, no plant coming up on it, like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim, which the LORD overthrew in his anger and his fury.
All the nations will say, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land? Why this great, burning anger?'
And people will say, 'It is because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt.
They went and served other gods and bowed down to them, gods they had not known, and that he had not given to them.
So the anger of the LORD burned against that land, and he brought on it every curse written in this book.
The LORD uprooted them from their land in anger, in fury and in great rage, and threw them into another land, as it is today.'
The secret things belong to the LORD our God, but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, so that we may follow all the words of this law.
"When all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse that I have set before you, and you take them to heart among all the nations where the LORD your God has driven you,
and you return to the LORD your God and listen to his voice, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul, just as I am commanding you today,
then the LORD your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you. He will gather you again from all the peoples where the LORD your God has scattered you.
Even if you have been driven away to the farthest edge of the heavens, from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there he will bring you back.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land that your ancestors possessed, and you will possess it. He will make you more prosperous and more numerous than your ancestors.
The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so that you will love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul, and live.
The LORD your God will put all these curses on your enemies and on those who hate you and persecuted you.
And you will again listen to the voice of the LORD and follow all his commands that I am giving you today.

The LORD your God will make you prosper abundantly in all the work of your hands, in the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your ground. For the LORD will again delight in you and make you prosper, as he delighted in your ancestors,

when you listen to the voice of the LORD your God by keeping his commands and his decrees that are written in this book of the law, when you turn back to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
For this command that I am giving you today is not too hard for you, and it is not far away.
It is not in heaven, so that you should say, 'Who will go up to heaven for us and bring it to us, and tell it to us so that we may do it?'
And it is not beyond the sea, so that you should say, 'Who will cross the sea for us and bring it to us, and tell it to us so that we may do it?'
No, the word is very near you. It is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you can do it.
See, today I have set before you life and good, death and evil.

For I am commanding you today to love the LORD your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commands, his decrees and his rulings. Then you will live and multiply, and the LORD your God will bless you in the land you are entering to take possession of.
But if your heart turns away and you do not listen, and you are drawn away to bow down to other gods and serve them,
I declare to you today that you will surely perish. You will not live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to enter and possess.
I call heaven and earth as witnesses against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessing and curse. So choose life, so that you and your descendants may live,

by loving the LORD your God, listening to his voice and holding fast to him. For he is your life and the length of your days, so that you may live in the land that the LORD swore to give to your ancestors, to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob."
Then Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel.
He said to them, "I am 120 years old today. I am no longer able to lead you, and the LORD has said to me, 'You will not cross this Jordan.'
The LORD your God himself will cross over ahead of you. He will destroy these nations before you, and you will dispossess them. Joshua will cross over ahead of you, as the LORD has said.
The LORD will do to them as he did to Sihon and Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land, when he destroyed them.
The LORD will hand them over to you, and you must do to them everything I have commanded you.
Be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or terrified of them, for the LORD your God is the one who goes with you. He will not fail you or abandon you."

Then Moses summoned Joshua and said to him in the sight of all Israel, "Be strong and courageous, for you will go with this people into the land that the LORD swore to their ancestors to give them, and you will divide it among them as their inheritance.
The LORD himself goes ahead of you. He will be with you. He will not fail you or abandon you. Do not be afraid or discouraged."
So Moses wrote down this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant, and to all the elders of Israel.
Moses commanded them, "At the end of every seven years, at the set time in the year of release, at the Festival of Shelters,
when all Israel comes to appear before the LORD your God at the place he will choose, you are to read this law aloud before all Israel, in their hearing.

Assemble the people, the men, the women and the children, and the foreigners who live in your towns, so that they may listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, and be careful to follow all the words of this law.
Their children, who do not know it, must also listen and learn to fear the LORD your God, as long as you live in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."

Then the LORD said to Moses, "The day of your death is near. Call Joshua, and present yourselves at the tent of meeting, so that I may give him his orders." So Moses and Joshua went and presented themselves at the tent of meeting.
The LORD appeared at the tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the entrance of the tent.

The LORD said to Moses, "You are about to rest with your ancestors. Then this people will rise up and prostitute themselves to the foreign gods of the land they are entering. They will abandon me and break my covenant that I made with them.

On that day my anger will burn against them. I will abandon them and hide my face from them, and they will be devoured. Many disasters and troubles will come on them, and on that day they will say, 'Haven't these disasters come on us because our God is not among us?'
And I will surely hide my face on that day, because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods.
So now write down this song for yourselves and teach it to the Israelites. Have them sing it, so that this song may be my witness against the Israelites.

When I have brought them into the land flowing with milk and honey that I swore to give their ancestors, and they eat their fill and grow fat, they will turn to other gods and serve them. They will despise me and break my covenant.

And when many disasters and troubles have come on them, this song will testify against them as a witness, for it will not be forgotten from the mouths of their descendants. For I know what they are inclined to do even now, before I have brought them into the land that I swore to give them."
So Moses wrote down this song that day and taught it to the Israelites.
Then he gave Joshua son of Nun his orders: "Be strong and courageous, for you will bring the Israelites into the land that I swore to give them, and I will be with you."
When Moses had finished writing the words of this law in a book, to the very end,
Moses gave this command to the Levites who carried the ark of the LORD's covenant:
"Take this book of the law and put it beside the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God. Let it remain there as a witness against you.
For I know how rebellious and stubborn you are. Even now, while I am still alive with you, you have been rebels against the LORD. How much more after my death!
Assemble before me all the elders of your tribes and your officials, so that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth as witnesses against them.

For I know that after my death you will act very corruptly and turn aside from the way I have commanded you. In days to come, disaster will come on you, because you will do what is evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger by what your hands have made."
Then Moses recited the words of this song to the very end, in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel:
Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
Let my teaching fall like rain, my words come down like dew, like gentle rain on new grass, like showers on green plants.
For I will proclaim the name of the LORD. Ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock: his work is perfect, for all his ways are just. A faithful God, without wrong, righteous and upright is he.
They have acted corruptly toward him; they are not his children, because of their flaw. They are a crooked and twisted generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Remember the days of old; consider the years of generation after generation. Ask your father, and he will tell you, your elders, and they will explain to you.
When the Most High gave the nations their inheritance, when he divided humankind, he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the sons of Israel.
For the LORD's portion is his people, Jacob his allotted inheritance.
He found him in a desert land, in an empty, howling wasteland. He surrounded him and cared for him; he guarded him like the pupil of his eye.
Like an eagle that stirs up its nest and hovers over its young, he spread out his wings and took him up; he carried him on his feathers.
The LORD alone guided him; no foreign god was with him.
He made him ride on the heights of the land, and he ate the produce of the field. He nursed him with honey from the rock, and oil from the flint rock,
with curds from the herd and milk from the flock, with the fat of lambs, with rams of Bashan's breed and goats, with the finest of the wheat. And you drank the blood of the grape, foaming wine.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, you grew thick, you were gorged! He abandoned the God who made him, and scorned the Rock of his salvation.
They made him jealous with strange gods; with detestable things they provoked him to anger.
They sacrificed to demons that were not God, to gods they had not known, new gods that had come lately, gods your ancestors had not feared.
You neglected the Rock who fathered you; you forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw it and spurned them, because his sons and his daughters provoked him.
He said: I will hide my face from them; I will see what their end will be. For they are a perverse generation, children who cannot be trusted.
They made me jealous with what is no god; they provoked me with their worthless idols. So I will make them jealous with what is no people; I will provoke them with a foolish nation.
For a fire has been kindled by my anger, and it burns to the depths of Sheol. It devours the earth and its produce, and sets fire to the foundations of the mountains.
I will heap disasters on them; I will spend my arrows on them.
They will be wasted by hunger, consumed by plague and bitter destruction. I will send the teeth of wild beasts against them, with the venom of creatures that crawl in the dust.
Outside, the sword will bereave them, and in the inner rooms, terror, for young man and young woman alike, for the nursing child and the gray-haired man.
I said I would cut them to pieces and wipe out their memory from humankind,
had I not feared the enemy's taunts, that their adversaries might misunderstand, that they might say, "Our hand has triumphed; it was not the LORD who did all this."
For they are a nation without sense, and there is no understanding in them.
If they were wise, they would understand this; they would see what their end will be.
How could one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight, unless their Rock had sold them, unless the LORD had handed them over?
For their rock is not like our Rock, as even our enemies must judge.
For their vine comes from the vine of Sodom, and from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are grapes of poison; their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the venom of serpents, the deadly poison of cobras.
Is this not stored up with me, sealed up in my storehouses?
Vengeance is mine, and repayment, for the time when their foot slips. For the day of their disaster is near, and their doom comes swiftly.
For the LORD will vindicate his people and have compassion on his servants, when he sees that their strength is gone, and no one is left, slave or free.
Then he will say: Where are their gods, the rock they took refuge in,
who ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their drink offerings? Let them rise up and help you! Let them be your shelter!
See now that I, I am he, and there is no god beside me. I put to death and I bring to life; I have wounded and I will heal, and no one can rescue from my hand.
For I lift up my hand to heaven and declare: As surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold of judgment, I will take vengeance on my adversaries and repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword will devour flesh, with the blood of the slain and the captives, from the long-haired heads of the enemy.
Praise his people, you nations, for he will avenge the blood of his servants. He will take vengeance on his adversaries and make atonement for his land, his people.
Moses came and recited all the words of this song in the hearing of the people, he and Hoshea son of Nun.
When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel,
he said to them, "Take to heart all the words I am solemnly declaring to you today, so that you may command your children to be careful to follow all the words of this law.
For this is no empty word for you; it is your life. By this word you will live long in the land you are crossing the Jordan to possess."
That same day the LORD said to Moses,
"Go up into these mountains of the Abarim, to Mount Nebo in the land of Moab, opposite Jericho, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites as their possession.
You will die on the mountain you go up, and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
For both of you broke faith with me among the Israelites at the waters of Meribath-kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not treat me as holy among the Israelites.
You will see the land from a distance, but you will not enter it, the land that I am giving to the Israelites."
This is the blessing with which Moses, the man of God, blessed the Israelites before his death.
He said: The LORD came from Sinai and dawned on them from Seir; he shone out from Mount Paran. He came from among ten thousands of holy ones, with a fiery law for them at his right hand.
Truly he loves the peoples; all his holy ones are in your hand. They bow down at your feet; each receives your words.
Moses gave us a law, a possession for the assembly of Jacob.
He became king in Jeshurun, when the leaders of the people gathered, the tribes of Israel together.
Let Reuben live and not die, though his men be few.
And this he said about Judah: Hear, LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him to his people. With his own hands he fights for himself; be a help to him against his adversaries.
About Levi he said: Your Thummim and your Urim belong to your faithful one, whom you tested at Massah, with whom you quarreled at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father and his mother, "I do not regard them." He did not acknowledge his brothers, or recognize his own children. For they kept your word and guarded your covenant.
They teach your rulings to Jacob and your law to Israel. They put incense before you and whole burnt offerings on your altar.
Bless his strength, LORD, and accept the work of his hands. Crush the loins of those who rise up against him, of those who hate him, so that they rise no more.
About Benjamin he said: The one the LORD loves will live securely beside him. He shields him all day long, and he dwells between his shoulders.
About Joseph he said: May his land be blessed by the LORD with the choicest gifts of heaven, with the dew, and with the deep waters that lie below,
with the choicest of what the sun brings forth, and the choicest of what the months bring out,
with the best of the ancient mountains, and the choicest of the everlasting hills,
with the choicest gifts of the earth and all that fills it, and with the favor of him who dwelt in the bush. Let these rest on the head of Joseph, on the brow of the one set apart among his brothers.

His firstborn bull has majesty, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox. With them he gores the peoples, all of them together, to the ends of the earth. Such are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and such are the thousands of Manasseh.
About Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out, and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call peoples to the mountain; there they will offer right sacrifices. For they will draw from the abundance of the seas, and from the treasures hidden in the sand.
About Gad he said: Blessed is he who enlarges Gad! Gad lies down like a lion, and tears at arm and head.
He chose the best land for himself, for there a commander's portion was kept for him. He came with the leaders of the people; he carried out the justice of the LORD, and his rulings for Israel.
About Dan he said: Dan is a lion's cub, leaping out from Bashan.
About Naphtali he said: Naphtali, satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD, take possession of the sea and the south.
About Asher he said: Most blessed of sons is Asher. May he be the favorite of his brothers, and may he dip his foot in oil.
Your bolts will be iron and bronze, and your strength will last as long as your days.
There is none like God, Jeshurun, who rides through the heavens to help you, through the skies in his majesty.
The eternal God is your refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms. He drove out the enemy before you, and said, "Destroy!"
So Israel lives in safety, the spring of Jacob alone, in a land of grain and new wine, where the heavens drip with dew.

How happy you are, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the LORD? He is the shield that helps you, the sword of your triumph. Your enemies will cringe before you, and you will tread on their backs.
Then Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, opposite Jericho. And the LORD showed him the whole land: Gilead as far as Dan,
all Naphtali, the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, all the land of Judah as far as the western sea,
the Negev, and the plain of the valley of Jericho, the city of palm trees, as far as Zoar.

Then the LORD said to him, "This is the land I swore to Abraham, to Isaac and to Jacob, when I said, 'I will give it to your descendants.' I have let you see it with your own eyes, but you will not cross over into it."
So Moses the servant of the LORD died there in the land of Moab, as the LORD had said.
He buried him in the valley in the land of Moab, opposite Beth-peor, and to this day no one knows where his grave is.
Moses was 120 years old when he died. His eyesight was not dim, and his vigor had not left him.
The Israelites wept for Moses in the plains of Moab for thirty days. Then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses came to an end.
Joshua son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, because Moses had laid his hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Never since has a prophet arisen in Israel like Moses, whom the LORD knew face to face,
in all the signs and wonders that the LORD sent him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh and to all his servants and to all his land,
and in all the mighty power and all the great and terrifying deeds that Moses performed in the sight of all Israel.
After the death of Moses the servant of the LORD, the LORD said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses' assistant,
"Moses my servant is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all this people, into the land that I am giving to them, to the Israelites.
I have given you every place where the sole of your foot treads, as I promised Moses.
From the wilderness and this Lebanon as far as the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and as far as the Great Sea in the west, will be your territory.
No one will be able to stand against you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you or abandon you.
Be strong and courageous, for you are the one who will lead this people to take possession of the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous, and be careful to do everything in the law that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.

This book of the law must not depart from your mouth. Meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything that is written in it. For then you will make your way prosper, and then you will succeed.
Have I not commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Do not be terrified or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go."
So Joshua commanded the officials of the people,

"Go through the camp and command the people: 'Get provisions ready for yourselves, for in three days you will cross this Jordan to go in and take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving you to possess.'"
To the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh Joshua said,
"Remember the command that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: 'The LORD your God is giving you rest, and he will give you this land.'
Your wives, your little ones and your livestock may stay in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan. But all your fighting men are to cross over armed ahead of your brothers and help them,

until the LORD gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too take possession of the land that the LORD your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land that is your possession and take possession of it, the land that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise."
They answered Joshua, "Everything you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go.
Just as we obeyed Moses in everything, so we will obey you. Only may the LORD your God be with you as he was with Moses.
Anyone who rebels against your command and does not obey your words, whatever you command him, is to be put to death. Only be strong and courageous."

Joshua son of Nun secretly sent two men from Shittim as spies. "Go and look over the land," he said, "and Jericho." So they went and came to the house of a prostitute named Rahab, and they stayed there.
The king of Jericho was told, "Look, some men from the Israelites have come here tonight to search out the land."
So the king of Jericho sent word to Rahab: "Bring out the men who came to you, who came into your house, for they have come to search out the whole land."
But the woman had taken the two men and hidden them. She said, "Yes, the men came to me, but I did not know where they were from.
When the gate was about to be shut at dark, the men went out. I do not know where the men went. Chase after them quickly, for you will catch up with them."
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them under the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
The men chased after them on the road to the Jordan, as far as the fords. And as soon as the pursuers had gone out after them, the gate was shut.
Before the men lay down for the night, she went up to them on the roof
and said to the men, "I know that the LORD has given you the land, that terror of you has fallen on us, and that all who live in the land are melting in fear before you.

For we have heard how the LORD dried up the water of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom you devoted to destruction.
When we heard it, our hearts melted, and no one had any courage left because of you, for the LORD your God is God in the heavens above and on the earth below.
So now, please swear to me by the LORD that, since I have shown you faithful love, you will also show faithful love to my father's household. Give me a sure sign
that you will spare the lives of my father and my mother, my brothers and my sisters, and everyone who belongs to them, and that you will save our lives from death."

The men said to her, "Our lives for yours, even to death! If you do not tell anyone about this business of ours, then when the LORD gives us the land, we will treat you with faithful love and faithfulness."
Then she let them down by a rope through the window, for her house was built into the town wall, and she lived in the wall.
She said to them, "Go to the hill country, so that the pursuers do not come across you. Hide there for three days, until the pursuers return. After that you can go on your way."
The men said to her, "We will be free of this oath of yours that you have made us swear.

When we come into the land, you must tie this cord of scarlet thread in the window through which you let us down, and you must gather your father and your mother, your brothers and all your father's household into the house with you.

If anyone goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his own head, and we will be free of guilt. But if a hand is laid on anyone who is with you in the house, his blood will be on our heads.
And if you tell anyone about this business of ours, we will be free of the oath you have made us swear."
She said, "Let it be as you say." She sent them away, and they left. And she tied the scarlet cord in the window.
They went and came to the hill country, and they stayed there three days, until the pursuers had returned. The pursuers searched all along the road but did not find them.
Then the two men turned back. They came down from the hill country, crossed the river and came to Joshua son of Nun, and they told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, "The LORD has given the whole land into our hands. All who live in the land are melting in fear before us."
Early in the morning Joshua got up, and they set out from Shittim and came to the Jordan, he and all the Israelites. They camped there for the night before they crossed over.
At the end of three days the officials went through the camp
and commanded the people, "When you see the ark of the covenant of the LORD your God, with the Levitical priests carrying it, you are to set out from your place and follow it.
But keep a distance between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure. Do not come near it. Then you will know the way you are to go, for you have not passed this way before."
Joshua said to the people, "Consecrate yourselves, for tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among you."
Joshua said to the priests, "Take up the ark of the covenant and cross over ahead of the people." So they took up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I will begin to make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you.
You are to command the priests who carry the ark of the covenant: 'When you come to the edge of the water of the Jordan, stand still in the Jordan.'"
Joshua said to the Israelites, "Come here and listen to the words of the LORD your God."

Joshua said, "By this you will know that the living God is among you, and that he will certainly drive out before you the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Hivites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Amorites and the Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is crossing over ahead of you into the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men from the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

When the soles of the feet of the priests who carry the ark of the LORD, the Lord of all the earth, come to rest in the water of the Jordan, the water of the Jordan will be cut off. The water flowing down from upstream will stand up in a single heap."
So the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, with the priests carrying the ark of the covenant ahead of the people.

Now the Jordan overflows all its banks throughout the time of harvest. But as soon as those carrying the ark came to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests carrying the ark dipped into the edge of the water,

the water flowing down from upstream stood still. It rose up in a single heap a great distance away, from Adam, the town beside Zarethan, while the water flowing down to the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, was completely cut off. And the people crossed over opposite Jericho.

The priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD stood firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan, while all Israel crossed over on dry ground, until the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan.
When the whole nation had finished crossing the Jordan, the LORD said to Joshua,
"Choose twelve men from the people, one man from each tribe,

and command them, 'Take up twelve stones from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from the place where the priests' feet stood firm. Carry them over with you and put them down at the place where you camp tonight.'"
So Joshua called the twelve men he had appointed from the Israelites, one man from each tribe.
Joshua said to them, "Cross over ahead of the ark of the LORD your God into the middle of the Jordan. Each of you is to lift a stone onto his shoulder, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites,
so that this may be a sign among you. In time to come, when your children ask, 'What do these stones mean to you?'

you are to tell them that the water of the Jordan was cut off before the ark of the covenant of the LORD. When it crossed the Jordan, the water of the Jordan was cut off. These stones are to be a memorial for the Israelites forever."

The Israelites did as Joshua commanded. They took up twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, one for each of the tribes of the Israelites, as the LORD had told Joshua. They carried them over with them to the camp and put them down there.
Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, at the place where the feet of the priests who carried the ark of the covenant had stood. They are there to this day.

The priests who carried the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done that the LORD had commanded Joshua to tell the people, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. And the people crossed over in haste.
When all the people had finished crossing, the ark of the LORD and the priests crossed over in front of the people.
The Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had told them.
About forty thousand men equipped for war crossed over before the LORD for battle, to the plains of Jericho.
On that day the LORD made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they held him in awe all the days of his life, as they had held Moses in awe.
"Command the priests who carry the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan."
So Joshua commanded the priests, "Come up out of the Jordan."

When the priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD came up from the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests' feet stepped out onto dry ground, the water of the Jordan returned to its place and flowed over all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and they camped at Gilgal, on the eastern edge of Jericho.
Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, "In time to come, when your children ask their fathers, 'What are these stones?'
you are to tell your children, 'Israel crossed this Jordan on dry ground.'
For the LORD your God dried up the water of the Jordan before you until you had crossed over, just as the LORD your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up before us until we had crossed over,
so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the hand of the LORD is strong, and so that you may fear the LORD your God forever."

All the kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan and all the kings of the Canaanites along the sea heard how the LORD had dried up the water of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed over. Their hearts melted, and they had no courage left because of the Israelites.
At that time the LORD said to Joshua, "Make flint knives and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time."
So Joshua made flint knives and circumcised the Israelites at Gibeath-haaraloth.
This is why Joshua circumcised them. All the people who came out of Egypt, the males, all the men of war, had died in the wilderness on the way after they came out of Egypt.
All the people who came out had been circumcised, but none of the people born in the wilderness on the way after they came out of Egypt had been circumcised.

For the Israelites walked for forty years in the wilderness, until the whole nation, the men of war who came out of Egypt, had died off, because they had not obeyed the voice of the LORD. The LORD had sworn to them that he would not let them see the land that the LORD had sworn to their ancestors to give us, a land flowing with milk and honey.
So it was their sons, whom he raised up in their place, that Joshua circumcised. They were uncircumcised, because they had not been circumcised on the way.
When the whole nation had been circumcised, they stayed where they were in the camp until they had healed.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the disgrace of Egypt from you." So the place has been called Gilgal to this day.
While the Israelites were camped at Gilgal, they kept the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, in the plains of Jericho.
On the day after the Passover, that very day, they ate some of the produce of the land: unleavened bread and roasted grain.
The manna stopped on the day after, when they ate some of the produce of the land. The Israelites no longer had manna, and that year they ate from the crops of the land of Canaan.
When Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua went up to him and said to him, "Are you for us or for our enemies?"
"No," he said, "I am the commander of the LORD's army. I have come now." Joshua fell with his face to the ground and bowed down, and he said to him, "What does my lord have to say to his servant?"
The commander of the LORD's army said to Joshua, "Take your sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy." And Joshua did so.
Now Jericho was shut up tight because of the Israelites. No one went out and no one came in.
The LORD said to Joshua, "See, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and its mighty warriors.
You are to march around the town, all the men of war, going around the town once. Do this for six days.
Seven priests are to carry seven rams' horns ahead of the ark. On the seventh day you are to march around the town seven times, and the priests are to blow the rams' horns.

When they sound a long blast on the ram's horn and you hear the sound of the horn, all the people are to give a loud shout. Then the wall of the town will fall down flat, and the people are to go up into the town, each man straight ahead."
So Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, "Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests carry seven rams' horns ahead of the ark of the LORD."
And he said to the people, "Go forward and march around the town, and let the armed men go ahead of the ark of the LORD."
When Joshua had spoken to the people, the seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns before the LORD went forward and blew the rams' horns, and the ark of the covenant of the LORD followed them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests who blew the rams' horns, and the rear guard followed the ark, while the horns kept sounding.
But Joshua had commanded the people, "Do not shout or let your voice be heard. Do not let a word come out of your mouth until the day I tell you to shout. Then you are to shout."
So he had the ark of the LORD go around the town, circling it once. Then they came back to the camp and spent the night in the camp.
Joshua got up early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the LORD.

The seven priests carrying the seven rams' horns ahead of the ark of the LORD went on, blowing the horns as they went. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard followed the ark of the LORD, while the horns kept sounding.
On the second day they marched around the town once and returned to the camp. They did this for six days.
On the seventh day they got up early, at the break of dawn, and marched around the town in the same way seven times. That was the only day they marched around the town seven times.
The seventh time, when the priests blew the rams' horns, Joshua said to the people, "Shout! For the LORD has given you the town.
The town and everything in it is to be devoted to the LORD for destruction. Only Rahab the prostitute is to live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers we sent.

But you must keep away from what is devoted to destruction. Otherwise you will devote it and then take some of what is devoted, and so make the camp of Israel something devoted to destruction and bring disaster on it.
All the silver and gold, and the articles of bronze and iron, are holy to the LORD. They must go into the LORD's treasury."

So the people shouted, and the rams' horns were blown. As soon as the people heard the sound of the horn, the people gave a loud shout, and the wall fell down flat. The people went up into the town, each man straight ahead, and they captured the town.
They devoted to destruction everything in the town, men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep and donkeys, putting them to the sword.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, "Go into the prostitute's house, and bring the woman out of it with everyone who belongs to her, as you swore to her."

So the young men who had been spies went in and brought out Rahab, her father and her mother, her brothers and everyone who belonged to her. They brought out all her relatives and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
Then they burned the town with fire, and everything in it. Only the silver and gold and the articles of bronze and iron they put into the treasury of the house of the LORD.

But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father's household and everyone who belonged to her. She has lived among the Israelites to this day, because she hid the messengers Joshua had sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua made them take an oath: "Cursed before the LORD is the man who sets out to rebuild this town, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he will lay its foundations, and at the cost of his youngest son he will set up its gates."
So the LORD was with Joshua, and his fame spread through the whole land.

But the Israelites acted unfaithfully in the matter of what was devoted to destruction. Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted, and the anger of the LORD burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is near Beth-aven, east of Bethel, and said to them, "Go up and spy out the land." So the men went up and spied out Ai.

They came back to Joshua and said to him, "Not all the people need to go up. Let about two thousand or three thousand men go up and attack Ai. Do not make all the people toil up there, for the people of Ai are few."
So about three thousand men from the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai struck down about thirty-six of them. They chased them from the gate as far as Shebarim, and struck them down on the slope. The hearts of the people melted and became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell face down on the ground before the ark of the LORD until evening, he and the elders of Israel, and they threw dust on their heads.

Joshua said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Why did you bring this people across the Jordan at all, only to hand us over to the Amorites to destroy us? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
Please, Lord, what can I say, now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all who live in the land will hear of it, and they will surround us and wipe our name off the earth. Then what will you do for your great name?"
The LORD said to Joshua, "Get up! Why are you lying face down like this?

Israel has sinned. They have broken my covenant, which I commanded them to keep. They have taken some of what was devoted to destruction. They have stolen it, they have lied about it, and they have put it among their own belongings.

That is why the Israelites cannot stand against their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they themselves have become devoted to destruction. I will not be with you any more unless you destroy what is devoted to destruction from among you.

Get up and consecrate the people. Say, 'Consecrate yourselves for tomorrow, for this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: "Things devoted to destruction are among you, Israel. You cannot stand against your enemies until you remove what is devoted to destruction from among you."'

In the morning you are to come forward tribe by tribe. The tribe that the LORD takes is to come forward clan by clan. The clan that the LORD takes is to come forward household by household. And the household that the LORD takes is to come forward man by man.
The one who is taken with the devoted things is to be burned with fire, he and everything he has, because he has broken the covenant of the LORD and has done a disgraceful thing in Israel."
Joshua got up early in the morning and had Israel come forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was taken.
He had the clans of Judah come forward, and the clan of the Zerahites was taken. He had the clan of the Zerahites come forward man by man, and Zabdi was taken.
He had Zabdi's household come forward man by man, and Achan son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, was taken.
Joshua said to Achan, "My son, give glory to the LORD, the God of Israel, and give him praise. Tell me what you have done. Do not hide it from me."
Achan answered Joshua, "It is true. I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel. This is what I did.

Among the spoil I saw a beautiful robe from Shinar, two hundred shekels of silver, and a bar of gold weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. They are hidden in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath."
So Joshua sent messengers, and they ran to the tent. There it was, hidden in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took the things out of the tent, brought them to Joshua and all the Israelites, and laid them out before the LORD.

Then Joshua, and all Israel with him, took Achan son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the bar of gold, his sons and his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys and his flock, his tent and everything he had, and they brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said, "Why have you brought disaster on us? The LORD will bring disaster on you today." And all Israel stoned him. They burned them with fire and stoned them with stones.
They raised over him a great heap of stones, which is there to this day. Then the LORD turned from his burning anger. That is why the place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.

The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Take all the fighting men with you, and get up and go up to Ai. See, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, his people, his town and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king, except that you may take its spoil and its livestock as plunder for yourselves. Set an ambush against the town, behind it."
So Joshua and all the fighting men got up to go up to Ai. Joshua chose thirty thousand mighty warriors and sent them out by night.
He commanded them, "Listen. You are to lie in ambush against the town, behind it. Do not go very far from the town, and all of you be ready.
I and all the people with me will approach the town. When they come out against us as they did the first time, we will flee from them.
They will come out after us until we have drawn them away from the town, for they will say, 'They are fleeing from us as they did the first time.' While we flee from them,
you are to rise up from the ambush and take possession of the town. The LORD your God will give it into your hand.
When you have seized the town, set it on fire. Do as the LORD has said. See, I have given you your orders."
So Joshua sent them out, and they went to the place of ambush and waited between Bethel and Ai, west of Ai. But Joshua spent that night among the people.
Early in the morning Joshua got up and mustered the people, and he and the elders of Israel went up ahead of the people to Ai.
All the fighting men who were with him went up and drew near until they came in front of the town. They camped north of Ai, with the valley between them and Ai.
He took about five thousand men and set them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the town.
So they stationed the people, the main camp north of the town and its rear guard west of the town. That night Joshua went into the middle of the valley.

When the king of Ai saw this, the men of the town hurried and got up early and went out to meet Israel in battle, the king and all his people, at the appointed place facing the Arabah. But he did not know that an ambush was waiting for him behind the town.
Joshua and all Israel let themselves be beaten back before them, and they fled along the road to the wilderness.
All the people who were in Ai were called out to chase them. They chased Joshua and were drawn away from the town.
Not a man was left in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the town open and chased Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Stretch out the javelin in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand." So Joshua stretched out the javelin in his hand toward the town.
As soon as he stretched out his hand, the men in ambush rose quickly from their place and ran. They entered the town and captured it, and they quickly set the town on fire.

The men of Ai looked back and saw the smoke of the town rising to the sky, and they had no strength to flee this way or that. Then the people who had fled toward the wilderness turned back on their pursuers.
When Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had captured the town and that the smoke of the town was rising, they turned back and struck down the men of Ai.

The others came out of the town against them, so that the men of Ai were caught in the middle of Israel, some on this side and some on that. Israel struck them down until not one survivor or fugitive was left.
But they took the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

When Israel had finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the open country, in the wilderness where they had chased them, and every one of them had fallen by the sword, all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
All who fell that day, men and women, numbered twelve thousand, all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not draw back the hand with which he held out the javelin until he had devoted to destruction all the inhabitants of Ai.
Only the livestock and the spoil of that town Israel took as plunder for themselves, in keeping with the word of the LORD that he had commanded Joshua.
So Joshua burned Ai and made it a ruin mound forever, a desolate place to this day.

He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening. At sunset Joshua gave the command, and they took his body down from the tree and threw it down at the entrance of the town gate. They raised over it a great heap of stones, which is there to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal,

as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses: an altar of uncut stones, on which no one had used an iron tool. On it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD and sacrificed fellowship offerings.
There on the stones he wrote a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the Israelites.

All Israel, with their elders, officials and judges, stood on both sides of the ark, facing the Levitical priests who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, foreigners as well as native-born. Half of them stood in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded earlier, to bless the people of Israel.
After that, Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, in keeping with everything written in the book of the law.
There was not a word of all that Moses had commanded that Joshua did not read before the whole assembly of Israel, including the women, the little ones and the foreigners who lived among them.

All the kings west of the Jordan heard of this, those in the hill country, in the western foothills and all along the coast of the Great Sea as far as Lebanon: the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
They gathered together to fight as one against Joshua and Israel.
But when the inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Jericho and to Ai,
they too acted with cunning. They went and disguised themselves as envoys. They took worn-out sacks for their donkeys, and wineskins that were worn out, split and patched up,
worn-out, patched sandals on their feet and worn-out clothes on their bodies. All the bread they had brought as provisions was dry and crumbly.
They went to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the men of Israel, "We have come from a distant land. Now make a covenant with us."
The men of Israel said to the Hivites, "Perhaps you live among us. How then can we make a covenant with you?"
They said to Joshua, "We are your servants." Joshua said to them, "Who are you, and where do you come from?"
They said to him, "Your servants have come from a very distant land because of the name of the LORD your God. For we have heard reports of him, and of everything he did in Egypt,
and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites east of the Jordan, Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth.
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land said to us, 'Take provisions with you for the journey. Go to meet them and say to them, "We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us."'
This bread of ours was warm when we took it from our houses as provisions on the day we set out to come to you. But now look, it is dry and crumbly.
These wineskins were new when we filled them, and look, they are split. And these clothes and sandals of ours are worn out from the very long journey."
The men of Israel took some of their provisions, but they did not ask for the LORD's direction.
Joshua made peace with them and made a covenant with them to let them live, and the leaders of the community swore an oath to them.
Three days after they had made a covenant with them, the Israelites heard that they were their neighbors and lived among them.
So the Israelites set out and came to their towns on the third day. Their towns were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth and Kiriath-jearim.
But the Israelites did not attack them, because the leaders of the community had sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole community grumbled against the leaders.
But all the leaders said to the whole community, "We have sworn to them by the LORD, the God of Israel, and now we cannot touch them.
This is what we will do to them: we will let them live, so that wrath does not come on us because of the oath we swore to them."
The leaders said to them, "Let them live." So they became woodcutters and water carriers for the whole community, as the leaders had said about them.
Joshua summoned them and said to them, "Why did you deceive us by saying, 'We live very far from you,' when you live among us?
Now you are cursed. Some of you will always be slaves, woodcutters and water carriers for the house of my God."

They answered Joshua, "Your servants were told plainly that the LORD your God had commanded his servant Moses to give you the whole land and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land before you. So we were very much afraid for our lives because of you, and we did this.
Now we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good and right to you."
So he did this for them: he rescued them from the hands of the Israelites, and they did not kill them.
That day Joshua made them woodcutters and water carriers for the community and for the altar of the LORD at the place he would choose, as they are to this day.

Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and devoted it to destruction, doing to Ai and its king as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them.
He and his people were very much afraid, because Gibeon was a great town, like one of the royal towns. It was greater than Ai, and all its men were warriors.
So Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent word to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish and Debir king of Eglon:
"Come up to me and help me, and let us attack Gibeon, for it has made peace with Joshua and the Israelites."

So the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon, gathered and went up, they and all their armies. They camped against Gibeon and attacked it.

The men of Gibeon sent word to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal: "Do not abandon your servants. Come up to us quickly, save us and help us, for all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us."
So Joshua went up from Gilgal, he and all the fighting men with him, all the mighty warriors.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for I have given them into your hand. Not one of them will be able to stand against you."
Joshua came on them suddenly, having marched all night from Gilgal.

The LORD threw them into confusion before Israel, and he struck them down in a great slaughter at Gibeon. He chased them along the road that goes up to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel, while they were on the way down from Beth-horon, the LORD threw huge stones down on them from the sky all the way to Azekah, and they died. More of them died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.
Then Joshua spoke to the LORD, on the day the LORD gave the Amorites over to the Israelites, and he said in the sight of Israel: "Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and moon, over the Valley of Aijalon!"

So the sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the nation took vengeance on its enemies. Is this not written in the Book of Jashar? The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There has been no day like it before or since, when the LORD listened to the voice of a man, for the LORD fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
Now these five kings had fled and hidden in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua was told, "The five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah."
Joshua said, "Roll large stones against the mouth of the cave, and post men by it to guard them.
But you must not stop. Chase your enemies and attack them from the rear. Do not let them get into their towns, for the LORD your God has given them into your hand."
Joshua and the Israelites finished striking them down in a very great slaughter, until they were wiped out, though some survivors escaped from them and reached the fortified towns.
Then all the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp at Makkedah. No one dared to say a word against the Israelites.
Joshua said, "Open the mouth of the cave and bring those five kings out of the cave to me."
They did so. They brought those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish and the king of Eglon.

When they had brought these kings out to Joshua, Joshua summoned all the men of Israel and said to the commanders of the fighting men who had gone with him, "Come here and put your feet on the necks of these kings." So they came and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua said to them, "Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous. For this is what the LORD will do to all the enemies you are fighting."
After this Joshua struck them down and put them to death, and he hanged them on five trees. They were left hanging on the trees until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave the command, and they took them down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They put large stones over the mouth of the cave, which are there to this very day.

That day Joshua captured Makkedah and put it and its king to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, with every person in it. He left no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Makkedah to Libnah and fought against Libnah.
The LORD gave it also, with its king, into the hand of Israel. He put it and every person in it to the sword. He left no survivor in it. He did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish. He camped against it and attacked it.
The LORD gave Lachish into the hand of Israel, and he captured it on the second day. He put it and every person in it to the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish, but Joshua struck him and his people down until he had left him no survivor.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon. They camped against it and attacked it.
They captured it that same day and put it to the sword. He devoted to destruction every person in it that day, just as he had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it.
They captured it and put it to the sword, with its king, all its towns and every person in it. He left no survivor, just as he had done to Eglon. He devoted it and every person in it to destruction.
Then Joshua and all Israel with him turned back to Debir and attacked it.

He captured it, with its king and all its towns. They put them to the sword and devoted to destruction every person in it. He left no survivor. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, just as he had done to Libnah and its king.

So Joshua struck the whole land, the hill country, the Negev, the western foothills and the slopes, with all their kings. He left no survivor. He devoted to destruction everything that breathed, as the LORD, the God of Israel, had commanded.
Joshua struck them from Kadesh-barnea to Gaza, and the whole land of Goshen as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their land at one time, because the LORD, the God of Israel, fought for Israel.
Then Joshua returned, and all Israel with him, to the camp at Gilgal.
When Jabin king of Hazor heard of this, he sent word to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings in the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Kinnereth, in the western foothills and in Naphoth-dor on the west,
to the Canaanites in the east and in the west, to the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites and the Jebusites in the hill country, and to the Hivites below Hermon in the land of Mizpah.
They came out, they and all their armies with them, a great horde, as many as the sand on the seashore, with a very great number of horses and chariots.
All these kings joined forces. They came and camped together at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, "Do not be afraid of them, for tomorrow at this time I will hand all of them over to Israel, slain. You are to hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire."
So Joshua and all the fighting men with him came against them suddenly at the waters of Merom and fell on them.

The LORD gave them into the hand of Israel. They struck them down and chased them as far as Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and as far as the Valley of Mizpeh to the east. They struck them down until no survivor was left.
Joshua did to them as the LORD had told him. He hamstrung their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor, and he put its king to the sword, for Hazor had formerly been the head of all these kingdoms.
They put every person in it to the sword, devoting them to destruction. Nothing that breathed was left, and he burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the towns of these kings and all their kings, and he put them to the sword. He devoted them to destruction, as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded.
But Israel did not burn any of the towns that stood on their mounds, except Hazor alone, which Joshua burned.

The Israelites took all the spoil of these towns and the livestock as plunder for themselves. But they put every human being to the sword until they had destroyed them. They left nothing that breathed.
As the LORD had commanded his servant Moses, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
So Joshua took this whole land: the hill country, the whole Negev, the whole land of Goshen, the western foothills, the Arabah, and the hill country of Israel with its foothills,
from Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir, as far as Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings and struck them down and put them to death.
Joshua waged war against all these kings for a long time.
Not one town made peace with the Israelites except the Hivites who lived in Gibeon. They took them all in battle.
For it was the LORD's doing to harden their hearts to meet Israel in battle, so that they would be devoted to destruction and receive no mercy, but be destroyed, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and wiped out the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, from all the hill country of Judah and from all the hill country of Israel. Joshua devoted them and their towns to destruction.
No Anakim were left in the land of the Israelites. Only in Gaza, in Gath and in Ashdod did some remain.
So Joshua took the whole land, just as the LORD had told Moses, and Joshua gave it as an inheritance to Israel, tribe by tribe, according to their divisions. And the land had rest from war.

These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites struck down, and whose land they took possession of east of the Jordan, toward the sunrise, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon, with all the Arabah on the east:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon. He ruled from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and from the middle of the valley, over half of Gilead as far as the Jabbok River, the border of the Ammonites,

and over the Arabah as far as the Sea of Kinnereth on the east, and as far as the Sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, on the east, on the road to Beth-jeshimoth, and on the south below the slopes of Pisgah.
Also the territory of Og king of Bashan, one of the last of the Rephaim, who lived in Ashtaroth and in Edrei.
He ruled over Mount Hermon, Salecah and all Bashan, as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and over half of Gilead, as far as the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of the LORD and the Israelites struck them down, and Moses the servant of the LORD gave their land as a possession to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites struck down west of the Jordan, from Baal-gad in the Valley of Lebanon to Mount Halak, which rises toward Seir. Joshua gave their land to the tribes of Israel as a possession according to their divisions,

in the hill country, the western foothills, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness and the Negev, the land of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites:
the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron-meron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in Naphath-dor, one; the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one. In all, thirty-one kings.
Joshua was old, advanced in years, and the LORD said to him, "You are old and advanced in years, and a great deal of the land remains to be taken over.
This is the land that remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the land of the Geshurites,

from the Shihor, which is east of Egypt, northward to the border of Ekron, which is counted as Canaanite: the five rulers of the Philistines, those of Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath and Ekron; and the Avvim
in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah, which belongs to the Sidonians, as far as Aphek, to the border of the Amorites;
the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, from Baal-gad below Mount Hermon to Lebo-hamath.

All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim, all the Sidonians, I myself will drive them out before the Israelites. Only allot the land to Israel as an inheritance, as I have commanded you.
So now divide this land as an inheritance among the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh."
With the other half of Manasseh, the Reubenites and the Gadites had received the inheritance that Moses gave them east of the Jordan, as Moses the servant of the LORD had given it to them:
from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town that is in the middle of the valley, and the whole plateau of Medeba as far as Dibon,
and all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the border of the Ammonites;
and Gilead, and the territory of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah,
the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei. He was one of the last of the Rephaim. Moses had struck them down and driven them out.
But the Israelites did not drive out the Geshurites or the Maacathites, so Geshur and Maacath live among Israel to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi he gave no inheritance. The offerings by fire to the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as he promised them.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of the Reubenites, clan by clan.
Their territory was from Aroer, which is on the edge of the Arnon Valley, and the town that is in the middle of the valley, and the whole plateau by Medeba,
Heshbon and all its towns on the plateau: Dibon, Bamoth-baal, Beth-baal-meon,
Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth-shahar on the hill in the valley,
Beth-peor, the slopes of Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth,

all the towns of the plateau, and the whole kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses had struck him down, together with the leaders of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lived in the land.
Along with the others they killed, the Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword.
The border of the Reubenites was the Jordan and its bank. This was the inheritance of the Reubenites, clan by clan, the towns and their villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the Gadites, clan by clan.
Their territory was Jazer and all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites as far as Aroer, which faces Rabbah,
and from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir,

and in the valley, Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, with the Jordan and its bank as the border, up to the end of the Sea of Kinnereth, east of the Jordan.
This was the inheritance of the Gadites, clan by clan, the towns and their villages.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It was for half the tribe of the Manassites, clan by clan.
Their territory was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, the whole kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all Havvoth-jair, which is in Bashan, sixty towns,
and half of Gilead, with Ashtaroth and Edrei, the towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan. These were for the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, for half of the descendants of Machir, clan by clan.
These are the inheritances that Moses gave out in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho.
But to the tribe of Levi Moses gave no inheritance. The LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he promised them.

These are the inheritances that the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the families of the tribes of the Israelites gave out to them.
Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses, for the nine and a half tribes.
For Moses had given the two and a half tribes their inheritance east of the Jordan, but he had given no inheritance among them to the Levites.

For the descendants of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. And the Levites were given no share in the land, only towns to live in, with their pasturelands for their livestock and their possessions.
