The Israelites did as the LORD had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
The people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to him, "You know what the LORD said to Moses the man of God about you and me at Kadesh-barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses the servant of the LORD sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back a report of what I truly believed.
But my brothers who went up with me made the people's hearts melt, while I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
On that day Moses swore, 'The land on which your foot has walked will surely be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you have followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.'

Now look, the LORD has kept me alive, as he promised, these forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, while Israel journeyed in the wilderness. And now here I am today, eighty-five years old.
I am still as strong today as I was on the day Moses sent me. As my strength was then, so my strength is now, for war and for going out and coming in.

So now give me this hill country that the LORD spoke of on that day. For you heard on that day that the Anakim were there, with great fortified towns. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I will drive them out, as the LORD said."
Joshua blessed him and gave Hebron to Caleb son of Jephunneh as an inheritance.
So Hebron has belonged to Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite as an inheritance to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
The name of Hebron was formerly Kiriath-arba. Arba was the greatest man among the Anakim. And the land had rest from war.
The allotment for the tribe of the people of Judah, clan by clan, reached southward to the border of Edom, to the wilderness of Zin at the far south.
Their southern border ran from the end of the Salt Sea, from the bay that faces south.
It went out south of the Ascent of Akrabbim, passed along to Zin, went up south of Kadesh-barnea, passed along to Hezron, went up to Addar and turned toward Karka.
It passed along to Azmon and went out to the Brook of Egypt, and the border ended at the sea. This will be your southern border.
The eastern border was the Salt Sea, as far as the mouth of the Jordan. The border on the north side ran from the bay of the sea at the mouth of the Jordan.
The border went up to Beth-hoglah and passed along north of Beth-arabah. The border went up to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.

The border went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and turned north toward Gilgal, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim, south of the valley. The border passed along to the waters of En-shemesh and ended at En-rogel.

The border went up by the Valley of the Son of Hinnom along the southern slope of the Jebusite town, that is, Jerusalem. The border went up to the top of the hill that faces the Valley of Hinnom on the west, at the northern end of the Valley of Rephaim.
From the top of the hill the border curved to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, went out to the towns of Mount Ephron, and curved to Baalah, that is, Kiriath-jearim.
From Baalah the border turned west to Mount Seir, passed along to the northern slope of Mount Jearim, that is, Chesalon, went down to Beth-shemesh and passed along to Timnah.
The border went out to the northern slope of Ekron, curved to Shikkeron, passed along to Mount Baalah and went out to Jabneel, and the border ended at the sea.
The western border was the Great Sea and its coast. This is the border all around the people of Judah, clan by clan.
Joshua gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a share among the people of Judah, as the LORD had commanded him: Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron. Arba was the father of Anak.
From there Caleb drove out the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai, the descendants of Anak.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water as well." So he gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
This is the inheritance of the tribe of the people of Judah, clan by clan.
The towns at the far end of the tribe of the people of Judah, toward the border of Edom in the Negev, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,
Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain and Rimmon: in all, twenty-nine towns, with their villages.
In the western foothills: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,
Shaaraim, Adithaim, Gederah and Gederothaim: fourteen towns, with their villages.
Gederoth, Beth-dagon, Naamah and Makkedah: sixteen towns, with their villages.
Keilah, Achzib and Mareshah: nine towns, with their villages.
Ekron, with its surrounding towns and its villages;
from Ekron to the sea, all the towns near Ashdod, with their villages;
Ashdod, with its surrounding towns and its villages; Gaza, with its surrounding towns and its villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt and the Great Sea with its coast.
In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,
Goshen, Holon and Giloh: eleven towns, with their villages.
Humtah, Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, and Zior: nine towns, with their villages.
Kain, Gibeah and Timnah: ten towns, with their villages.
Maarath, Beth-anoth and Eltekon: six towns, with their villages.
Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, and Rabbah: two towns, with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, Secacah,
Nibshan, Ir-hamelah and En-gedi: six towns, with their villages.
But the people of Judah could not drive out the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem. So the Jebusites live with the people of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
The allotment for the descendants of Joseph went from the Jordan at Jericho, east of the waters of Jericho, through the wilderness that goes up from Jericho into the hill country to Bethel.
From Bethel it went out to Luz and passed along to the territory of the Archites at Ataroth.
It went down westward to the territory of the Japhletites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Gezer, and it ended at the sea.
So the descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
This was the territory of the Ephraimites, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance on the east was Ataroth-addar, as far as Upper Beth-horon.
The border went out westward, with Michmethath on the north. The border turned eastward to Taanath-shiloh and passed by it on the east to Janoah.
From Janoah it went down to Ataroth and to Naarah, reached Jericho and went out at the Jordan.
From Tappuah the border went westward to the Kanah Valley and ended at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the Ephraimites, clan by clan,
together with the towns that were set apart for the Ephraimites within the inheritance of the Manassites, all those towns with their villages.
But they did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer. So the Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day, and they were made to do forced labor.
This was the allotment for the tribe of Manasseh, for he was Joseph's firstborn. Machir, Manasseh's firstborn and the father of Gilead, had received Gilead and Bashan, because he was a warrior.

The allotment was also for the rest of the Manassites, clan by clan: for the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, clan by clan.
Now Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the leaders, and said, "The LORD commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers." So, as the LORD had commanded, Joshua gave them an inheritance among their father's brothers.
So ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is east of the Jordan,
because the daughters of Manasseh received an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belonged to the rest of the Manassites.
The territory of Manasseh went from Asher to Michmethath, which faces Shechem. Then the border went south to the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but Tappuah itself, on the border of Manasseh, belonged to the Ephraimites.

The border went down to the Kanah Valley. South of the valley, these towns belonged to Ephraim, among the towns of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh ran along the north side of the valley and ended at the sea.
The land to the south belonged to Ephraim and the land to the north to Manasseh, with the sea as its border. They reached Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.

Within Issachar and Asher, Manasseh had Beth-shean and its surrounding towns, Ibleam and its surrounding towns, the inhabitants of Dor and its surrounding towns, the inhabitants of En-dor and its surrounding towns, the inhabitants of Taanach and its surrounding towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its surrounding towns: the three heights.
But the Manassites could not take possession of these towns, for the Canaanites were determined to live in that land.
When the Israelites grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, "Why have you given us only one allotment and one portion as an inheritance? We are a numerous people, for the LORD has blessed us so much."

Joshua said to them, "If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest and clear land for yourselves there, in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, since the hill country of Ephraim is too small for you."

The descendants of Joseph said, "The hill country is not enough for us, and all the Canaanites who live in the valley land have chariots of iron, both those in Beth-shean and its surrounding towns and those in the Valley of Jezreel."
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to Ephraim and Manasseh, "You are a numerous people and very strong. You will not have only one allotment.

The hill country will be yours. Though it is forest, you will clear it, and it will be yours to its farthest limits. For you will drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron and though they are strong."
The whole community of the Israelites assembled at Shiloh, and they set up the tent of meeting there. The land lay subdued before them.
Seven tribes remained among the Israelites that had not yet been given their inheritance.
So Joshua said to the Israelites, "How long will you put off going in to take possession of the land that the LORD, the God of your ancestors, has given you?

Appoint three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They are to set out and go through the land and write a description of it, with a view to their inheritance. Then they are to come back to me.
They are to divide it into seven portions. Judah will stay in its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph will stay in its territory in the north.
You are to write a description of the land in seven portions and bring it here to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.

For the Levites have no share among you, because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. And Gad, Reuben and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them."

So the men set out and went. Joshua commanded those who went to write a description of the land: "Go and walk through the land and write a description of it, then come back to me, and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh."
So the men went and passed through the land, and they wrote a description of it in a scroll, town by town, in seven portions. Then they came back to Joshua at the camp at Shiloh.
Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD, and there Joshua divided the land among the Israelites according to their divisions.
The lot for the tribe of the Benjaminites came up, clan by clan. The territory of their allotment lay between the people of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.
On the north side their border began at the Jordan. The border went up to the slope north of Jericho, went up westward through the hill country, and ended at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the border passed along to Luz, to the slope south of Luz, that is, Bethel. Then the border went down to Ataroth-addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.

On the west side the border curved and turned south, from the hill that faces Beth-horon on the south, and it ended at Kiriath-baal, that is, Kiriath-jearim, a town of the people of Judah. This was the west side.
The south side began at the edge of Kiriath-jearim. The border went out westward and went out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah.

The border went down to the edge of the hill that faces the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, at the north end of the Valley of Rephaim. It went down the Valley of Hinnom to the southern slope of the Jebusite town and went down to En-rogel.
It curved northward, went out to En-shemesh, and went out to Geliloth, which is opposite the Ascent of Adummim. Then it went down to the Stone of Bohan son of Reuben.
It passed along to the northern slope opposite the Arabah, and went down into the Arabah.
The border passed along to the northern slope of Beth-hoglah, and the border ended at the northern bay of the Salt Sea, at the southern end of the Jordan. This was the southern border.
The Jordan formed its border on the east side. This was the inheritance of the Benjaminites, clan by clan, with its borders all around.
The towns of the tribe of the Benjaminites, clan by clan, were: Jericho, Beth-hoglah, Emek-keziz,
Chephar-ammonah, Ophni and Geba: twelve towns, with their villages.
Zela, Haeleph, the Jebusite town, that is, Jerusalem, Gibeath and Kiriath: fourteen towns, with their villages. This was the inheritance of the Benjaminites, clan by clan.
The second lot came out for Simeon, for the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan. Their inheritance lay within the inheritance of the people of Judah.
For their inheritance they had Beersheba, Sheba, Moladah,
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: thirteen towns, with their villages;
Ain, Rimmon, Ether and Ashan: four towns, with their villages;
and all the villages around these towns as far as Baalath-beer, Ramah of the Negev. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Simeonites, clan by clan.

The inheritance of the Simeonites was taken from the share of the people of Judah, because the portion of the people of Judah was too large for them. So the Simeonites received their inheritance within Judah's inheritance.
The third lot came up for the Zebulunites, clan by clan. The border of their inheritance went as far as Sarid.
Their border went up westward to Maralah, touched Dabbesheth, and touched the valley that faces Jokneam.
From Sarid it turned east, toward the sunrise, to the border of Chisloth-tabor, went out to Daberath and went up to Japhia.
From there it passed along eastward, toward the sunrise, to Gath-hepher and Eth-kazin, went out to Rimmon and turned toward Neah.
Then the border went around it on the north to Hannathon, and it ended at the Valley of Iphtah-el.
It included Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah and Bethlehem: twelve towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the Zebulunites, clan by clan, these towns with their villages.
The fourth lot came out for Issachar, for the Issacharites, clan by clan.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,
The border touched Tabor, Shahazimah and Beth-shemesh, and their border ended at the Jordan: sixteen towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Issacharites, clan by clan, the towns with their villages.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the Asherites, clan by clan.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,
Allammelech, Amad and Mishal. On the west it touched Carmel and Shihor-libnath.
Then it turned toward the sunrise to Beth-dagon, touched Zebulun and the Valley of Iphtah-el on the north at Beth-emek and Neiel, and went out to Cabul on the north,
Ebron, Rehob, Hammon and Kanah, as far as Greater Sidon.
Then the border turned to Ramah and to the fortified town of Tyre. The border turned to Hosah, and it ended at the sea in the region of Achzib,
Ummah, Aphek and Rehob: twenty-two towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Asherites, clan by clan, these towns with their villages.
The sixth lot came out for the Naphtalites, for the Naphtalites clan by clan.
Their border ran from Heleph, from the oak at Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb and Jabneel as far as Lakkum, and it ended at the Jordan.
The border turned westward to Aznoth-tabor, went out from there to Hukkok, touched Zebulun on the south and Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise.
The fortified towns were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Kinnereth,
Iron, Migdal-el, Horem, Beth-anath and Beth-shemesh: nineteen towns, with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Naphtalites, clan by clan, the towns with their villages.
The seventh lot came out for the tribe of the Danites, clan by clan.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir-shemesh,
Me-jarkon and Rakkon, with the territory facing Joppa.

But the territory of the Danites slipped out of their hands. So the Danites went up and fought against Leshem. They captured it, put it to the sword, took possession of it and settled in it, and they named Leshem Dan, after their ancestor Dan.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the Danites, clan by clan, these towns with their villages.
When they had finished dividing up the land as inheritances by its borders, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
As the LORD had commanded, they gave him the town he asked for, Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He rebuilt the town and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun and the heads of the families of the tribes of the Israelites gave out by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
"Tell the Israelites: 'Designate the towns of refuge that I spoke to you about through Moses,
so that anyone who kills a person by mistake, without meaning to, may flee there. They will be a refuge for you from the avenger of blood.

He is to flee to one of these towns, stand at the entrance of the town gate and state his case to the elders of that town. Then they are to take him into the town with them and give him a place, and he will live among them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not hand the killer over to him, because he struck down his neighbor without meaning to, and he had not been his enemy before.

He is to stay in that town until he has stood trial before the community, until the death of the high priest who is serving at that time. Then the killer may go back to his own town and his own home, to the town he fled from.'"
So they set apart Kedesh in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

East of the Jordan, across from Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness on the plateau, from the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead from the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the designated towns for all the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them, so that anyone who killed a person by mistake could flee there and not die at the hand of the avenger of blood before he had stood trial before the community.
The heads of the families of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest, to Joshua son of Nun and to the heads of the families of the tribes of the Israelites
at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, and said to them, "The LORD commanded through Moses that we be given towns to live in, with their pasturelands for our livestock."
So, as the LORD had commanded, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns with their pasturelands out of their own inheritance.

The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites. The descendants of Aaron the priest, who were among the Levites, received by lot thirteen towns from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon and the tribe of Benjamin.
The rest of the Kohathites received by lot ten towns from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
The Gershonites received by lot thirteen towns from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
The Merarites, clan by clan, received twelve towns from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and the tribe of Zebulun.
So the Israelites gave these towns with their pasturelands to the Levites by lot, as the LORD had commanded through Moses.
From the tribe of the people of Judah and the tribe of the people of Simeon they gave the following towns, which are mentioned here by name.
They went to the descendants of Aaron, who belonged to the clans of the Kohathites among the Levites, because the first lot fell to them.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, that is, Hebron, in the hill country of Judah, with the pasturelands around it. Arba was the father of Anak.
But the fields of the town and its villages they had given to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his possession.
To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, the town of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, Libnah with its pasturelands,
Jattir with its pasturelands, Eshtemoa with its pasturelands,
Holon with its pasturelands, Debir with its pasturelands,
Ain with its pasturelands, Juttah with its pasturelands and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands: nine towns from these two tribes.
From the tribe of Benjamin they gave Gibeon with its pasturelands, Geba with its pasturelands,
Anathoth with its pasturelands and Almon with its pasturelands: four towns.
The towns of the descendants of Aaron, the priests, came to thirteen towns in all, with their pasturelands.
The rest of the Kohathites, the clans of the Kohathites who were Levites, received their towns by lot from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem, the town of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, with its pasturelands in the hill country of Ephraim, Gezer with its pasturelands,
Kibzaim with its pasturelands and Beth-horon with its pasturelands: four towns.
From the tribe of Dan they gave Elteke with its pasturelands, Gibbethon with its pasturelands,
Aijalon with its pasturelands and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: four towns.
From the half-tribe of Manasseh they gave Taanach with its pasturelands and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: two towns.
The towns of the clans of the rest of the Kohathites came to ten in all, with their pasturelands.

To the Gershonites, of the clans of the Levites, they gave from the half-tribe of Manasseh Golan in Bashan, the town of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, and Beeshterah with its pasturelands: two towns.
From the tribe of Issachar they gave Kishion with its pasturelands, Daberath with its pasturelands,
Jarmuth with its pasturelands and En-gannim with its pasturelands: four towns.
From the tribe of Asher they gave Mishal with its pasturelands, Abdon with its pasturelands,
Helkath with its pasturelands and Rehob with its pasturelands: four towns.

From the tribe of Naphtali they gave Kedesh in Galilee, the town of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, Hammoth-dor with its pasturelands and Kartan with its pasturelands: three towns.
The towns of the Gershonites, clan by clan, came to thirteen towns in all, with their pasturelands.
To the clans of the Merarites, the rest of the Levites, they gave from the tribe of Zebulun Jokneam with its pasturelands, Kartah with its pasturelands,
Dimnah with its pasturelands and Nahalal with its pasturelands: four towns.
From the tribe of Reuben they gave Bezer with its pasturelands, Jahaz with its pasturelands,
Kedemoth with its pasturelands and Mephaath with its pasturelands: four towns.
From the tribe of Gad they gave Ramoth in Gilead, the town of refuge for anyone who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, Mahanaim with its pasturelands,
Heshbon with its pasturelands and Jazer with its pasturelands: four towns in all.
All the towns given by lot to the Merarites, clan by clan, the rest of the clans of the Levites, were twelve towns.
The towns of the Levites within the possession of the Israelites came to forty-eight towns in all, with their pasturelands.
Each of these towns had its pasturelands around it. It was the same with all these towns.
So the LORD gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give to their ancestors, and they took possession of it and settled in it.
The LORD gave them rest on every side, just as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of all their enemies could stand against them. The LORD gave all their enemies into their hand.
Not one word of all the good promises that the LORD had made to the house of Israel failed. Every one came true.
Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
and said to them, "You have kept everything that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have obeyed me in everything I commanded you.
All this long time, up to this day, you have not abandoned your brothers, and you have faithfully kept the command of the LORD your God.

Now the LORD your God has given your brothers rest, as he promised them. So now turn and go to your homes, to the land that is your possession, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave you east of the Jordan.

Only be very careful to keep the command and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commands, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul."
Then Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their homes.

To one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to the other half Joshua had given land with their brothers west of the Jordan. When Joshua sent them away to their homes, he blessed them

and said to them, "Go back to your homes with great wealth: with a very large number of livestock, with silver, gold, bronze and iron, and with a great quantity of clothing. Share the spoil of your enemies with your brothers."

So the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their own possession, which they had acquired at the LORD's command through Moses.
When they came to Geliloth by the Jordan in the land of Canaan, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, a large altar, impressive to look at.

The Israelites heard it said, "Look, the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar on the frontier of the land of Canaan, at Geliloth by the Jordan, on the Israelites' side."
When the Israelites heard it, the whole community of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go up and make war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead,
and with him ten leaders, one leader for each family of all the tribes of Israel. Each of them was the head of his family among the clans of Israel.
They came to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead and said to them,

"This is what the whole community of the LORD says: 'What is this unfaithfulness you have committed against the God of Israel, turning away today from following the LORD by building yourselves an altar, and so rebelling today against the LORD?
Was the wrongdoing at Peor not enough for us? We have not cleansed ourselves of it to this day, even though a plague came on the community of the LORD.
And now you are turning away today from following the LORD! If you rebel against the LORD today, tomorrow he will be angry with the whole community of Israel.

But if the land you possess is unclean, cross over into the land that the LORD possesses, where the LORD's tabernacle stands, and take possession of land among us. Only do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us, by building yourselves an altar other than the altar of the LORD our God.

When Achan son of Zerah acted unfaithfully in the matter of what was devoted to destruction, did not wrath fall on the whole community of Israel? And he was not the only one to die for his wrongdoing.'"
Then the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered the heads of the clans of Israel:
"The Mighty One, God, the LORD! The Mighty One, God, the LORD! He knows, and let Israel know! If this was in rebellion or in unfaithfulness against the LORD, do not spare us today.

If we have built ourselves an altar to turn away from following the LORD, or to offer burnt offerings and grain offerings on it, or to make fellowship sacrifices on it, may the LORD himself call us to account.
No, we did it because we were anxious about something. In time to come your descendants might say to our descendants, 'What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
The LORD has made the Jordan a border between us and you, you Reubenites and Gadites. You have no share in the LORD.' So your descendants might make our descendants stop fearing the LORD.
So we said, 'Let us now build an altar, not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices,

but to be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we will worship the LORD in his presence with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices and our fellowship offerings. Then your descendants will not be able to say to our descendants in time to come, "You have no share in the LORD."'

And we said, 'If they ever say this to us or to our descendants in time to come, we will say, "Look at this copy of the altar of the LORD, which our ancestors made, not for burnt offerings or for sacrifices, but as a witness between us and you."'

Far be it from us to rebel against the LORD and turn away today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offerings, grain offerings or sacrifices, other than the altar of the LORD our God that stands in front of his tabernacle!"
Phinehas the priest, the leaders of the community and the heads of the clans of Israel who were with him heard what the Reubenites, the Gadites and the Manassites said, and they were satisfied.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the Reubenites, the Gadites and the Manassites, "Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this unfaithfulness against the LORD. Now you have rescued the Israelites from the hand of the LORD."
Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the Reubenites and the Gadites in the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought back word to them.
The Israelites were satisfied with the report, and the Israelites blessed God. They spoke no more of going up to make war against them, to destroy the land where the Reubenites and the Gadites lived.
The Reubenites and the Gadites gave the altar its name: "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."
A long time afterward, when the LORD had given Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and Joshua was old and advanced in years,
Joshua summoned all Israel, their elders, their leaders, their judges and their officials, and said to them, "I am old and advanced in years.
You yourselves have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to all these nations for your sake, for it is the LORD your God who has fought for you.
See, I have allotted to you as an inheritance for your tribes these nations that remain, as well as all the nations I have wiped out, from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west.
The LORD your God himself will push them back before you and drive them out of your way, and you will take possession of their land, as the LORD your God promised you.
So be very strong, and be careful to do everything that is written in the book of the law of Moses, without turning aside from it to the right or to the left.
Do not mix with these nations, these that remain among you. Do not call on the names of their gods, or make anyone swear by them. Do not serve them or bow down to them.
But hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
The LORD has driven out before you great and powerful nations, and as for you, no one has been able to stand against you to this day.
One of you puts a thousand to flight, for it is the LORD your God who fights for you, as he promised you.
So for your own sake take great care to love the LORD your God.
For if you ever turn back and cling to the rest of these nations, these that remain among you, and intermarry with them, and you mix with them and they with you,

know for certain that the LORD your God will no longer drive these nations out before you. They will be a snare and a trap for you, a whip on your sides and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.

Now I am about to go the way of all the earth. You know with all your heart and all your soul that not one word has failed of all the good promises that the LORD your God made concerning you. All of them have come true for you. Not one word of them has failed.

But just as every good promise that the LORD your God made to you has come true for you, so the LORD will bring on you every evil he has threatened, until he has destroyed you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you,

if you break the covenant of the LORD your God, which he commanded you to keep, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land that he has given you."
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He summoned the elders, the leaders, the judges and the officials of Israel, and they presented themselves before God.
Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Long ago your ancestors, Terah the father of Abraham and of Nahor, lived beyond the River, and they served other gods.
But I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him through all the land of Canaan. I made his descendants many, and I gave him Isaac.
To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave the hill country of Seir to possess, but Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
Then I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with plagues by what I did among them, and afterward I brought you out.
I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

They cried out to the LORD, and he put darkness between you and the Egyptians. He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did in Egypt. Then you lived in the wilderness for a long time.
I brought you to the land of the Amorites, who lived east of the Jordan. They fought against you, but I gave them into your hand. You took possession of their land, and I destroyed them before you.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, set out to fight against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I would not listen to Balaam. He blessed you again and again, and I rescued you from his hand.

Then you crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The leaders of Jericho fought against you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, but I gave them into your hand.
I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out before you, the two kings of the Amorites. It was not by your sword or your bow.
I gave you a land you had not toiled over, and towns you had not built, and you live in them. You eat from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.'
So now fear the LORD and serve him with integrity and faithfulness. Put away the gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.

But if you think it wrong to serve the LORD, choose today whom you will serve, whether the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you are living. But as for me and my household, we will serve the LORD."
The people answered, "Far be it from us to abandon the LORD to serve other gods!

For it is the LORD our God who brought us and our ancestors up from the land of Egypt, out of the place of slavery, and who did those great signs before our eyes. He protected us all along the way we traveled, and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
The LORD drove out before us all the peoples, and the Amorites who lived in the land. We too will serve the LORD, for he is our God."
Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins.
If you abandon the LORD and serve foreign gods, he will turn and bring disaster on you and make an end of you, after he has done you good."
The people said to Joshua, "No! We will serve the LORD."
Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen the LORD, to serve him." They said, "We are witnesses."
"Then put away the foreign gods that are among you, and turn your hearts to the LORD, the God of Israel."
The people said to Joshua, "We will serve the LORD our God, and we will obey his voice."
So on that day Joshua made a covenant for the people, and there at Shechem he set out for them a decree and a ruling.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up there, under the oak that was by the sanctuary of the LORD.

Joshua said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all the words that the LORD spoke to us. It will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny your God."
Then Joshua sent the people away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.
They buried him within the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua and who had known all the work that the LORD had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the piece of land that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred qesitah. It became an inheritance of the descendants of Joseph.
Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah, the town of his son Phinehas, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the LORD, "Which of us is to go up first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?"
The LORD said, "Judah is to go up. I have handed the land over to him."

Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into my allotted territory, and let us fight against the Canaanites. Then I too will go with you into your allotted territory." So Simeon went with him.
Judah went up, and the LORD handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over to them. They defeated ten thousand men at Bezek.
At Bezek they found Adoni-bezek and fought against him, and they defeated the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
Adoni-bezek fled, but they chased him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to pick up scraps under my table. As I have done, so God has paid me back." They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
The people of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it. They put it to the sword and set the city on fire.
Afterward the people of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, in the Negev and in the western foothills.
Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron (Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba), and they defeated Sheshai, Ahiman and Talmai.
From there Judah went against the people living in Debir. (Debir was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.)
Caleb said, "Whoever attacks Kiriath-sepher and captures it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife."
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she came to him, she urged him to ask her father for a field. She got down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What do you want?"
She said to him, "Give me a blessing. Since you have given me land in the Negev, give me springs of water too." So Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

The descendants of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up with the people of Judah from the City of Palms into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev near Arad. They went and settled among the people.
Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they defeated the Canaanites who lived in Zephath. They devoted the city to destruction, and so it was named Hormah.
Judah also captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
The LORD was with Judah, and Judah took possession of the hill country. But they could not drive out the people living in the plain, because they had iron chariots.
Hebron was given to Caleb, as Moses had promised, and he drove out from there the three sons of Anak.
But the Benjaminites did not drive out the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. So the Jebusites have lived with the Benjaminites in Jerusalem to this day.
The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
The house of Joseph sent men to spy out Bethel. (The city was formerly called Luz.)
The men keeping watch saw a man coming out of the city, and they said to him, "Please show us the way into the city, and we will treat you kindly."
He showed them the way into the city, and they put the city to the sword, but they let the man and his whole family go.
The man went to the land of the Hittites and built a city. He named it Luz, and that is its name to this day.

But Manasseh did not drive out Beth-shean and its villages, or Taanach and its villages, or the people living in Dor and its villages, or the people living in Ibleam and its villages, or the people living in Megiddo and its villages. The Canaanites were determined to stay in that land.
When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they did not drive them out completely.
Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived among them in Gezer.
Zebulun did not drive out the people living in Kitron or the people living in Nahalol. So the Canaanites lived among them, and they became forced laborers.
Asher did not drive out the people living in Acco or the people living in Sidon, or Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik or Rehob.
So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the people of the land, because they did not drive them out.

Naphtali did not drive out the people living in Beth-shemesh or the people living in Beth-anath. So they lived among the Canaanites, the people of the land, but the people of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became forced laborers for them.
The Amorites pressed the Danites back into the hill country. They did not let them come down into the plain.
The Amorites were determined to stay in Har-heres, in Aijalon and in Shaalbim. But the house of Joseph gained the upper hand, and they became forced laborers.
The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela, and upward.

The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you up from Egypt and brought you into the land that I promised on oath to your ancestors. I said, 'I will never break my covenant with you,
and you must not make a covenant with the people who live in this land. You must tear down their altars.' But you have not obeyed me. What is this you have done?
So I also say this: I will not drive them out before you. They will become thorns in your sides, and their gods will be a trap for you."
When the angel of the LORD had spoken these words to all the Israelites, the people wept aloud.
They named that place Bochim, and they offered sacrifices there to the LORD.
When Joshua had sent the people away, the Israelites went, each to his own inheritance, to take possession of the land.
The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlived Joshua, who had seen all the great work that the LORD had done for Israel.
Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at the age of 110.
They buried him in the territory he had inherited, at Timnath-heres in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
That whole generation also was gathered to its ancestors, and after them another generation grew up who did not know the LORD or the work he had done for Israel.
Then the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals.

They abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt. They followed other gods, gods of the peoples around them, and bowed down to them, and they provoked the LORD to anger.
They abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtoreths.

The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he handed them over to raiders, who plundered them. He sold them into the power of their enemies all around, and they could no longer stand up to their enemies.
Whenever they went out to fight, the hand of the LORD was against them to bring them disaster, just as the LORD had said and as the LORD had sworn to them. They were in great distress.
Then the LORD raised up judges, and they saved them from the power of those who plundered them.

But they would not listen even to their judges. They prostituted themselves to other gods and bowed down to them. They were quick to turn aside from the way their ancestors had walked in obedience to the LORD's commands. They did not do as their ancestors did.

Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and saved them from the power of their enemies as long as the judge lived. For the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who oppressed them and crushed them.

But when the judge died, they would turn back and act more corruptly than their ancestors, following other gods to serve them and bow down to them. They did not give up any of their practices or their stubborn ways.
So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he said, "This nation has broken my covenant, which I commanded their ancestors, and has not obeyed me.
So I in turn will no longer drive out before them any of the nations that Joshua left when he died.
I will use them to test Israel, to see whether they will keep the way of the LORD and walk in it, as their ancestors kept it, or not."
So the LORD left those nations in the land. He did not drive them out quickly, and he did not hand them over to Joshua.
These are the nations that the LORD left in the land to test Israel by them, all those Israelites who had not known any of the wars of Canaan.
It was only so that the generations of the Israelites would know war, to teach war to those who had not known it before.
They were the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites who lived in the mountains of Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon to Lebo-hamath.
They were there to test Israel by them, to find out whether they would obey the commands of the LORD, which he had given their ancestors through Moses.
So the Israelites lived among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites.
They took their daughters as wives for themselves and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherahs.
The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the power of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim. The Israelites served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the Israelites, who saved them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The Spirit of the LORD came on him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD handed Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram over to him, and he overpowered Cushan-rishathaim.
Then the land had peace for forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Once again the Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD made Eglon king of Moab strong against Israel, because they had done what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
Eglon brought the Ammonites and the Amalekites together with him. He went and defeated Israel, and they took possession of the City of Palms.
The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.

Then the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, a Benjaminite, a man who was left-handed. The Israelites sent tribute by him to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud made himself a sword with two edges, a gomed long, and he strapped it on his right thigh under his clothes.
He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
When Ehud had finished presenting the tribute, he sent away the people who had carried it.
But he himself turned back at the carved images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret message for you, Your Majesty." The king said, "Silence!" And all his attendants went out from his presence.
Ehud came to him as he was sitting alone in his cool upper room. Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." And the king rose from his seat.
Ehud reached out with his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and plunged it into his belly.
Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, because he did not pull the sword out of his belly. And the dung came out.
Then Ehud went out into the porch. He shut the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
After he had gone, the king's servants came. They saw that the doors of the upper room were locked, and they said, "He must be relieving himself in the inner room of the cool chamber."
They waited until they were embarrassed, but still he did not open the doors of the upper room. So they took the key and opened them, and there was their master, fallen to the floor, dead.
Ehud had escaped while they waited. He passed the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
When he arrived, he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went down with him from the hill country, with Ehud at their head.

He said to them, "Follow me, for the LORD has handed your enemies, the Moabites, over to you." So they went down after him and seized the fords of the Jordan leading to Moab, and they did not let anyone cross.
At that time they struck down about ten thousand Moabites, all of them sturdy and strong men. Not one escaped.
So that day Moab was brought down under the power of Israel, and the land had peace for eighty years.
After him came Shamgar son of Anath. He struck down six hundred Philistines with an ox goad, and he too saved Israel.
After Ehud died, the Israelites again did what was evil in the sight of the LORD.
So the LORD sold them into the power of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his army was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-ha-goiim.
The Israelites cried out to the LORD, because Jabin had nine hundred iron chariots, and he had cruelly oppressed the Israelites for twenty years.
Now Deborah, a prophet, the wife of Lappidoth, was judging Israel at that time.
She used to sit under the Palm of Deborah, between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites went up to her to have their disputes decided.

She sent for Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali and said to him, "The LORD, the God of Israel, has commanded you, 'Go, gather your men at Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun.
I will draw Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, out to meet you at the Kishon River, with his chariots and his troops, and I will hand him over to you.'"
Barak said to her, "If you go with me, I will go. But if you don't go with me, I won't go."

She said, "I will certainly go with you. But the road you are taking will not bring you honor, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the power of a woman." Then Deborah got up and went with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak called out Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh. Ten thousand men went up under his command, and Deborah went up with him.
Now Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far away as the oak at Zaanannim, near Kedesh.
Sisera was told that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
So Sisera called out all his chariots, nine hundred iron chariots, and all the troops who were with him, from Harosheth-ha-goiim to the Kishon River.

Deborah said to Barak, "Get up! This is the day the LORD has handed Sisera over to you. Hasn't the LORD gone out ahead of you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men following him.
Before Barak, the LORD threw Sisera, all his chariots and his whole army into panic and put them to the sword. Sisera got down from his chariot and fled on foot.
Barak chased the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-ha-goiim, and Sisera's whole army fell by the sword. Not a single man was left.
But Sisera fled on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the family of Heber the Kenite.
Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Come in, my lord. Come in here with me. Don't be afraid." So he went into her tent, and she covered him with a rug.
He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." She opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him again.
He said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent. If anyone comes and asks you, 'Is there a man here?' say, 'No.'"

But Jael, Heber's wife, took a tent peg and picked up a hammer. She went to him quietly and drove the peg through his temple, and it went down into the ground. He was fast asleep and exhausted, and he died.

Just then Barak came by, chasing Sisera. Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, I will show you the man you are looking for." He went in with her, and there was Sisera lying dead, with the tent peg in his temple.
So on that day God brought Jabin king of Canaan low before the Israelites.
The Israelites pressed harder and harder on Jabin king of Canaan, until they had destroyed Jabin king of Canaan.
On that day Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang this song:
"When the leaders took the lead in Israel, when the people offered themselves willingly, bless the LORD!
Hear, you kings! Listen, you rulers! I, to the LORD, I will sing; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
LORD, when you went out from Seir, when you marched from the land of Edom, the earth shook, and the heavens poured, and the clouds poured down water.
The mountains quaked before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the roads were deserted, and travelers went by winding paths.
The villagers ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I, Deborah, arose, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
They chose new gods; then there was war in the gates. Was a shield or a spear to be seen among forty thousand in Israel?
My heart is with the commanders of Israel, who offered themselves willingly among the people. Bless the LORD!
You who ride on white donkeys, you who sit on saddle blankets, and you who walk along the road, tell of it!

At the sound of those who divide the flocks at the watering places, there they recount the victories of the LORD, the victories of his villagers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, sing a song! Rise up, Barak! Lead away your captives, son of Abinoam!
Then the survivors came down to the nobles; the people of the LORD came down to me against the warriors.
From Ephraim came those whose roots are in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, with your people. From Machir came down commanders, and from Zebulun those who carry the officer's staff.
The princes of Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was true to Barak; into the valley they rushed at his heels. Among the clans of Reuben there were great resolves of heart.
Why did you stay among the sheepfolds, to hear the shepherds piping for the flocks? Among the clans of Reuben there was great searching of heart.
Gilead stayed on the far side of the Jordan. And Dan, why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat still at the seashore and stayed by his landing places.
Zebulun is a people who risked their lives to the death, Naphtali too, on the heights of the field.
Kings came, they fought; then the kings of Canaan fought, at Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. They carried off no plunder of silver.
From heaven they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
The Kishon River swept them away, the ancient river, the Kishon River. March on, my soul, with strength!
Then the horses' hooves hammered with the galloping, the galloping of his stallions.
'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the LORD, 'bitterly curse its people, because they did not come to help the LORD, to help the LORD against the warriors.'
Most blessed of women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, most blessed of women who live in tents.
He asked for water; she gave him milk. In a bowl fit for nobles she brought him curds.
She reached out her hand for the tent peg, her right hand for the workman's hammer. She hammered Sisera, she crushed his head, she shattered and pierced his temple.
Between her feet he sank down, he fell, he lay still. Between her feet he sank down, he fell. Where he sank down, there he fell, destroyed.
Through the window she looked out; Sisera's mother cried out through the lattice: 'Why is his chariot so slow to come? Why are the hoofbeats of his chariots so late?'
The wisest of her ladies answer her; and she answers herself again and again:

'Aren't they finding and dividing the plunder? A girl, two girls for every warrior; plunder of dyed cloth for Sisera, plunder of dyed cloth, embroidered, dyed cloth, two pieces of embroidery for the necks of the plunderer.'
So may all your enemies perish, LORD! But may those who love him be like the sun when it rises in its strength." And the land had peace for forty years.
The Israelites did what was evil in the sight of the LORD, and the LORD handed them over to Midian for seven years.
Midian's power was too strong for Israel. Because of Midian the Israelites made for themselves the hiding places in the mountains, the caves and the strongholds.
Whenever Israel had sown their crops, Midian, Amalek and the people of the east would come up and attack them.
They would camp against them and destroy the produce of the land all the way to Gaza. They left nothing to live on in Israel, no sheep, no ox and no donkey.
For they would come up with their livestock and their tents, coming like swarms of locusts. They and their camels were too many to count, and they came into the land to ruin it.
Israel was brought very low because of Midian, and the Israelites cried out to the LORD.
When the Israelites cried out to the LORD because of Midian,
the LORD sent a prophet to the Israelites. He said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'I brought you up from Egypt and brought you out of the place of slavery.
I rescued you from the power of Egypt and from the power of all who oppressed you. I drove them out before you and gave you their land.
I said to you, "I am the LORD your God. Do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you are living." But you have not obeyed me.'"
Then the angel of the LORD came and sat under the oak at Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite. His son Gideon was threshing wheat in the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites.
The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, mighty warrior."

Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord, but if the LORD is with us, why has all this happened to us? Where are all his wonders that our ancestors told us about, when they said, 'Didn't the LORD bring us up from Egypt?' But now the LORD has abandoned us and handed us over to Midian."
The LORD turned to him and said, "Go in this strength of yours, and save Israel from the power of Midian. Am I not sending you?"
He said to him, "Pardon me, Lord, but how can I save Israel? My clan is the weakest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my family."
The LORD said to him, "I will be with you, and you will strike down the Midianites as if they were one man."
He said to him, "If I have found favor with you, give me a sign that it is you who are speaking with me.
Please do not leave here until I come back to you and bring out my offering and set it before you." He said, "I will stay until you come back."

So Gideon went in and prepared a young goat, and unleavened bread from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and the broth in a pot, and he brought them out to him under the oak and presented them.
The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened bread, put them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.

Then the angel of the LORD reached out the tip of the staff in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened bread. Fire flared up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened bread, and the angel of the LORD vanished from his sight.
When Gideon saw that it was the angel of the LORD, Gideon said, "Oh no, Lord GOD! For I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!"
But the LORD said to him, "Peace be with you. Do not be afraid. You will not die."
So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and named it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it still stands at Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

That same night the LORD said to him, "Take your father's young bull, the second bull, seven years old. Tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah pole beside it.

Then build an altar to the LORD your God on the top of this stronghold, with the stones laid in proper order. Take the second bull and offer it as a burnt offering, using the wood of the Asherah pole that you cut down."
So Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did as the LORD had told him. But he was too afraid of his family and of the men of the town to do it by day, so he did it at night.
When the men of the town got up early in the morning, there was the altar of Baal torn down, and the Asherah pole beside it cut down, and the second bull offered on the altar that had been built.
They said to one another, "Who has done this?" They asked around and searched, and they were told, "Gideon son of Joash has done this."
The men of the town said to Joash, "Bring out your son. He must die, because he has torn down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah pole beside it."

But Joash said to all who stood against him, "Are you going to plead Baal's case? Are you going to save him? Whoever pleads his case will be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him plead his own case, since someone has torn down his altar."
So that day Gideon was named Jerubbaal, for people said, "Let Baal plead his case against him, because he has torn down his altar."
Then all Midian, Amalek and the people of the east joined forces. They crossed over and camped in the Valley of Jezreel.
But the Spirit of the LORD took possession of Gideon, and he blew the ram's horn, and the Abiezrites were called out to follow him.
He sent messengers throughout Manasseh, and they too were called out to follow him. He also sent messengers to Asher, Zebulun and Naphtali, and they went up to meet them.
Then Gideon said to God, "If you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said,
look, I am putting a fleece of wool on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone, and all the ground is dry, then I will know that you will save Israel by my hand, as you have said."
And so it was. He got up early the next day and squeezed the fleece, and he wrung dew out of the fleece, a bowlful of water.

Then Gideon said to God, "Do not be angry with me, but let me speak just once more. Please let me make just one more test with the fleece. Let the fleece alone be dry, and let there be dew on all the ground."
God did so that night. Only the fleece was dry, and there was dew on all the ground.
Early in the morning Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, and all the people with him camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was to the north of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.
The LORD said to Gideon, "You have too many people with you for me to hand Midian over to them. Israel might boast against me, 'My own hand has saved me.'
Now announce to the people, 'Whoever is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" So twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.

The LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many people. Take them down to the water, and I will sift them for you there. If I say to you, 'This one is to go with you,' he is to go with you. But anyone of whom I say to you, 'This one is not to go with you,' is not to go."

So he took the people down to the water, and the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps the water with his tongue, as a dog laps, you are to set apart by himself, and also everyone who kneels down to drink."
The number of those who lapped, putting their hands to their mouths, was three hundred men. All the rest of the people knelt down to drink water.
The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will save you, and I will hand Midian over to you. Let all the rest of the people go home."

So the people took provisions in their hands, and their rams' horns. Gideon sent all the other Israelites away, each to his own tent, but he kept the three hundred men. The camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
That night the LORD said to him, "Get up and go down against the camp, for I have handed it over to you.
But if you are afraid to go down, go down to the camp with Purah your servant.
Listen to what they are saying, and afterward you will have the courage to go down against the camp." So he went down with Purah his servant to the outposts of the armed men in the camp.
Midian, Amalek and all the people of the east lay spread out in the valley, as thick as locusts. Their camels were too many to count, as many as the sand on the seashore.

When Gideon arrived, there was a man telling his friend a dream. He said, "Listen, I had a dream. A round loaf of barley bread came tumbling into the camp of Midian. It came to the tent and struck it, and it fell. It turned it upside down, and the tent collapsed."
His friend answered, "This can be nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has handed Midian and the whole camp over to him."

When Gideon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down in worship. He went back to the camp of Israel and said, "Get up, for the LORD has handed the camp of Midian over to you."
He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put rams' horns and empty jars into the hands of all of them, with torches inside the jars.
He said to them, "Watch me and do the same. When I come to the edge of the camp, do just as I do.
When I and all who are with me blow the ram's horn, then you too blow your rams' horns all around the camp, and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at about ten at night, just after the guards had been posted. They blew the rams' horns and smashed the jars that were in their hands.

All three companies blew the rams' horns and broke the jars. They held the torches in their left hands and in their right hands the rams' horns to blow, and they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp, and the whole camp ran. They cried out and fled.

When the three hundred blew the rams' horns, the LORD set every man's sword against his comrade throughout the whole camp. The army fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the edge of Abel-meholah, near Tabbath.
The men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, from Asher and from all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.

Gideon sent messengers throughout the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against Midian, and seize the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan too." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they seized the waters as far as Beth-barah, and the Jordan.

They captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the Rock of Oreb, and they killed Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb. They pursued Midian, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon on the other side of the Jordan.
Then the men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they quarreled with him fiercely.
He said to them, "What have I done now compared with you? Isn't the gleaning of Ephraim's grapes better than the whole grape harvest of Abiezer?
God handed the commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb, over to you. What was I able to do compared with you?" When he said this, their anger against him died down.
Gideon came to the Jordan and crossed over, he and the three hundred men with him, exhausted but still pursuing.
He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give some loaves of bread to the people who are following me, for they are exhausted, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
But the officials of Succoth said, "Do you already have the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?"
Gideon said, "Because of that, when the LORD has handed Zebah and Zalmunna over to me, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers."
From there he went up to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way, and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered.
So he said to the men of Penuel too, "When I come back safely, I will tear down this tower."
Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor with their army, about 15,000 men, all who were left of the whole army of the people of the east. Those who had fallen were 120,000 men who carried the sword.
Gideon went up by the route of the tent-dwellers, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and he attacked the army while it felt secure.
Zebah and Zalmunna fled, but he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and he threw the whole army into panic.
Then Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the Ascent of Heres.
He caught a young man from Succoth and questioned him, and the young man wrote down for him the officials and elders of Succoth, seventy-seven men.

Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Do you already have the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna in your hand, that we should give bread to your exhausted men?'"
He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth a lesson.
He also tore down the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "What about the men you killed at Tabor?" They said, "They were like you, every one of them, like the sons of a king."
He said, "They were my brothers, my mother's sons. As surely as the LORD lives, if you had let them live, I would not kill you."
He said to Jether, his firstborn, "Get up and kill them." But the boy did not draw his sword, because he was afraid, for he was still only a boy.

Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Get up yourself and strike us down, for as the man is, so is his strength." So Gideon got up and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on their camels' necks.
The men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you and your son and your grandson too, for you have saved us from the power of Midian."
But Gideon said to them, "I will not rule over you, and my son will not rule over you. The LORD will rule over you."
Then Gideon said to them, "I have one request to make of you. Each of you give me an earring from his plunder." (The enemy had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)
They said, "We will gladly give them." So they spread out a cloak, and each man threw on it an earring from his plunder.

The weight of the gold earrings that he asked for was 1,700 shekels of gold, besides the crescent ornaments, the pendants and the purple garments worn by the kings of Midian, and besides the chains on their camels' necks.
Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his town, in Ophrah. All Israel prostituted themselves to it there, and it became a trap for Gideon and his family.
So Midian was brought low before the Israelites, and they did not raise their heads again. The land had peace for forty years in the days of Gideon.
Jerubbaal son of Joash went back and lived in his own house.
Gideon had seventy sons, his own offspring, for he had many wives.
His concubine who lived in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.
Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
As soon as Gideon was dead, the Israelites again prostituted themselves to the Baals, and they made Baal-berith their god.
The Israelites did not remember the LORD their God, who had rescued them from the power of all their enemies all around.
And they did not show faithful kindness to the family of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, in return for all the good he had done for Israel.
Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem, to his mother's brothers, and he said to them and to the whole clan of his mother's family,

"Please ask all the leaders of Shechem, 'Which is better for you: for seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, to rule over you, or for one man to rule over you?' Remember that I am your own flesh and blood."
His mother's brothers spoke all these words on his behalf to all the leaders of Shechem, and their hearts leaned toward Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
They gave him seventy pieces of silver from the temple of Baal-berith, and with it Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, who followed him.
He went to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone. But Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, was left alive, because he hid.
Then all the leaders of Shechem and all Beth-millo gathered together. They went and made Abimelech king beside the oak of the standing stone at Shechem.
When Jotham was told about it, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim and called out in a loud voice. He said to them, "Listen to me, leaders of Shechem, so that God may listen to you.
Once the trees went out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
But the olive tree said to them, 'Should I give up my rich oil, by which gods and people are honored, and go to sway over the trees?'
Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'You come and reign over us.'
But the fig tree said to them, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good fruit, and go to sway over the trees?'
Then the trees said to the vine, 'You come and reign over us.'
But the vine said to them, 'Should I give up my wine, which cheers gods and people, and go to sway over the trees?'
Then all the trees said to the thornbush, 'You come and reign over us.'
The thornbush said to the trees, 'If you really mean to anoint me king over you, come and take shelter in my shade. But if not, let fire come out of the thornbush and consume the cedars of Lebanon.'
Now then, did you act in good faith and with integrity when you made Abimelech king? Have you dealt well with Jerubbaal and his family, and done to him as his deeds deserved?
My father fought for you. He risked his life and rescued you from the power of Midian.

But today you have risen up against my father's family. You have killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and you have made Abimelech, the son of his slave woman, king over the leaders of Shechem, because he is your brother.
So if you have acted in good faith and with integrity toward Jerubbaal and his family today, then may you find joy in Abimelech, and may he find joy in you.
But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and consume the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire come out from the leaders of Shechem and from Beth-millo and consume Abimelech."
Then Jotham ran away and escaped. He went to Beer and lived there, out of the reach of his brother Abimelech.
Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem betrayed Abimelech.

This happened so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come back, and their blood would be laid on their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who helped him kill his brothers.
The leaders of Shechem set men to lie in wait against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road. And Abimelech was told about it.
Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers, and they moved into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem put their trust in him.
They went out into the fields, gathered the grapes from their vineyards and trod them, and held a festival of praise. They went into the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn't he the son of Jerubbaal, and isn't Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?
If only this people were under my command! Then I would get rid of Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Muster your army and come out!"
When Zebul, the governor of the city, heard what Gaal son of Ebed had said, he was furious.
He sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, "Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and they are stirring up the city against you.
Now get up during the night, you and the troops with you, and lie in wait in the fields.
In the morning, as soon as the sun rises, get up early and rush against the city. When he and the people with him come out against you, do to him whatever you are able."
So Abimelech and all the troops with him got up during the night and lay in wait against Shechem in four companies.
