He served Baal and bowed down to him, and he provoked the LORD, the God of Israel, to anger, just as his father had done.
After Ahab's death, Moab rebelled against Israel.

Ahaziah had fallen through the lattice of his upper room in Samaria and was injured. So he sent messengers and told them, "Go and consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover from this injury."

But the angel of the LORD said to Elijah the Tishbite, "Get up, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and say to them, 'Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are going to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron?
Therefore this is what the LORD says: You will not come down from the bed you have gone up to. You will certainly die.'" So Elijah went.
The messengers went back to the king, and he said to them, "Why have you come back?"

They said to him, "A man came up to meet us and said to us, 'Go back to the king who sent you and say to him, "This is what the LORD says: Is it because there is no God in Israel that you are sending to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to. You will certainly die."'"
He asked them, "What was the man like who came up to meet you and told you these things?"
They said to him, "He was a hairy man, with a leather belt fastened around his waist." He said, "It was Elijah the Tishbite."
Then the king sent a captain of fifty with his fifty men to Elijah. The captain went up to him, and there he was, sitting on top of the hill. He said to him, "Man of God, the king says, 'Come down!'"
Elijah answered the captain of fifty, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty!" Then fire came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.
Again the king sent another captain of fifty with his fifty men to him. He spoke to Elijah and said, "Man of God, this is what the king says: 'Come down at once!'"
Elijah answered them, "If I am a man of God, let fire come down from heaven and consume you and your fifty!" Then the fire of God came down from heaven and consumed him and his fifty.

Again the king sent a third captain of fifty with his fifty men. The third captain of fifty went up, came and fell on his knees in front of Elijah, and begged him, "Man of God, please let my life and the lives of these fifty servants of yours be precious in your sight.
Look, fire came down from heaven and consumed the first two captains of fifty and their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your sight."
Then the angel of the LORD said to Elijah, "Go down with him. Do not be afraid of him." So he got up and went down with him to the king.

He said to the king, "This is what the LORD says: You sent messengers to consult Baal-zebub, the god of Ekron, as if there were no God in Israel whose word you could consult. Therefore you will not come down from the bed you have gone up to. You will certainly die."
So Ahaziah died, as the LORD had said through Elijah. Because he had no son, Jehoram became king in his place, in the second year of Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah.
As for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah, and what he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
When the LORD was about to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha were on their way from Gilgal.
Elijah said to Elisha, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to Bethel." But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they went down to Bethel.
The company of prophets who were at Bethel came out to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" He said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Elijah said to him, "Elisha, please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to Jericho." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So they came to Jericho.
The company of prophets who were at Jericho came up to Elisha and said to him, "Do you know that today the LORD is going to take your master away from you?" He said, "Yes, I know. Be quiet."
Then Elijah said to him, "Please stay here, for the LORD has sent me on to the Jordan." But he said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So the two of them went on.
Fifty men of the company of prophets went too, and they stood at a distance, facing them, while the two of them stood by the Jordan.
Elijah took his cloak, rolled it up and struck the water. The water divided to one side and the other, and the two of them crossed over on dry ground.
When they had crossed, Elijah said to Elisha, "Tell me what I can do for you before I am taken from you." Elisha said, "Please let me have a double share of your spirit."
Elijah said, "You have asked for something hard. If you see me as I am taken from you, it will be yours. But if not, it will not."
As they were walking along and talking, suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared and separated the two of them, and Elijah went up to heaven in the whirlwind.
Elisha saw it, and he cried out, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" And he saw him no more. Then he took hold of his own clothes and tore them in two.
He picked up Elijah's cloak, which had fallen from him, and went back and stood on the bank of the Jordan.

He took Elijah's cloak that had fallen from him and struck the water. He said, "Where is the LORD, the God of Elijah?" When he too had struck the water, it divided to one side and the other, and Elisha crossed over.
The company of prophets from Jericho, who were facing him, saw him and said, "The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha." They came to meet him and bowed down to the ground before him.

They said to him, "Look, your servants have fifty strong men with them. Please let them go and search for your master. Perhaps the Spirit of the LORD has picked him up and thrown him down on one of the mountains or in one of the valleys." He said, "Do not send them."
But they kept pressing him until he was embarrassed to refuse, and he said, "Send them." So they sent fifty men, and they searched for three days but did not find him.
They came back to Elisha while he was staying at Jericho, and he said to them, "Didn't I tell you not to go?"
The men of the city said to Elisha, "Look, the city is well situated, as my lord can see, but the water is bad and the land is unfruitful."
He said, "Bring me a new bowl and put salt in it." So they brought it to him.
He went out to the spring and threw the salt into it, and said, "This is what the LORD says: I have healed this water. Never again will it cause death or unfruitfulness."
And the water has stayed healed to this day, just as Elisha had said.
From there Elisha went up to Bethel. As he was going up the road, some young boys came out of the town and jeered at him. They said to him, "Go on up, baldhead! Go on up, baldhead!"
He turned around, looked at them and cursed them in the name of the LORD. Then two female bears came out of the woods and mauled forty-two of the youths.
From there he went on to Mount Carmel, and from there he returned to Samaria.
Jehoram son of Ahab became king over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigned twelve years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, but not like his father and his mother. He removed the standing stone of Baal that his father had made.
But he held on to the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit. He did not turn away from them.
Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, and he used to pay the king of Israel a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams.
But when Ahab died, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.
So at that time King Jehoram set out from Samaria and mustered all Israel.

He went and sent this message to Jehoshaphat king of Judah: "The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me to war against Moab?" Jehoshaphat said, "I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses."
He asked, "Which way shall we go up?" He answered, "By the road through the wilderness of Edom."
So the king of Israel set out, with the king of Judah and the king of Edom. They marched around for seven days, and there was no water for the army or for the animals that followed them.
The king of Israel said, "Oh no! The LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab!"

But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no prophet of the LORD here, so that we may consult the LORD through him?" One of the officers of the king of Israel answered, "Elisha son of Shaphat is here, who used to pour water on Elijah's hands."
Jehoshaphat said, "The word of the LORD is with him." So the king of Israel, Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom went down to him.

Elisha said to the king of Israel, "What do you want with me? Go to your father's prophets and your mother's prophets." But the king of Israel said to him, "No, for the LORD has called these three kings together to hand them over to Moab."
Elisha said, "As the LORD of Armies lives, whom I serve, if I did not have respect for Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or even notice you.
But now bring me a musician." And while the musician was playing, the hand of the LORD came on Elisha.
He said, "This is what the LORD says: Dig this valley full of ditches.
For this is what the LORD says: You will see no wind and you will see no rain, yet this valley will be filled with water, and you will drink, you and your livestock and your other animals.
This is a small thing in the eyes of the LORD. He will also hand Moab over to you.
You will strike down every fortified city and every choice city. You will cut down every good tree, stop up all the springs of water and ruin every good field with stones."
In the morning, at the time when the grain offering is presented, water suddenly came flowing from the direction of Edom, and the land was filled with water.
Now all Moab had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. So every man old enough to bear arms was called out, and they took their stand at the border.
When they got up early in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, and the Moabites saw the water across from them, red as blood.
They said, "This is blood! The kings must have fought each other and killed one another. Now, Moab, to the plunder!"
But when they came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and struck down the Moabites, and they fled before them. Then the Israelites struck at the land, slaughtering Moab.

They tore down the cities, and on every good field each man threw his stone, until they had filled it. They stopped up every spring of water and cut down every good tree. Only in Kir-hareseth were its stones left standing, but the slingers surrounded it and attacked it.
When the king of Moab saw that the battle was going against him, he took seven hundred swordsmen with him to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not.

Then he took his firstborn son, who was to become king in his place, and offered him as a burnt offering on the wall. And there was great anger against Israel, so they withdrew from him and returned to their own land.

The wife of one of the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, "Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD. But now the creditor has come to take my two children as his slaves."
Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" She said, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house except a small jar of oil."
He said, "Go and borrow containers from outside, from all your neighbors, empty containers. Don't get just a few.
Then go in and shut the door behind you and your sons. Pour oil into all these containers, and as each one is filled, set it aside."
So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They kept bringing containers to her, and she kept pouring.
When the containers were full, she said to her son, "Bring me another container." But he said to her, "There are no more containers." Then the oil stopped flowing.
She went and told the man of God, and he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt. You and your sons can live on what is left."
One day Elisha went over to Shunem. A wealthy woman lived there, and she urged him to stay for a meal. So whenever he passed by, he would stop there for a meal.
She said to her husband, "Look, I am sure that this man who keeps passing our way is a holy man of God.
Let us make a small walled room on the roof and put a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp there for him. Then whenever he comes to us, he can stay there."
One day he came there, and he went into the upper room and lay down there.
He said to Gehazi his servant, "Call this Shunammite woman." He called her, and she stood before him.

Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tell her, 'Look, you have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Can we speak on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She said, "I live among my own people."
Elisha said, "Then what can be done for her?" Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
Elisha said, "Call her." He called her, and she stood in the doorway.
Elisha said, "At this season next year, you will be holding a son in your arms." She said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your servant!"
But the woman became pregnant, and she gave birth to a son at that season the following year, as Elisha had told her.
The child grew. One day he went out to his father, who was with the reapers.
He said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father said to a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
The servant picked him up and brought him to his mother. The boy sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God. Then she shut the door on him and went out.
She called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I can hurry to the man of God and come back."
He said, "Why are you going to him today? It is not the New Moon or the Sabbath." She said, "All is well."
She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on fast. Do not slow down for me unless I tell you."
So she set out and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite.
Now run to meet her and ask her, 'Is all well with you? Is all well with your husband? Is all well with the child?'" She said, "All is well."

But when she came to the man of God on the mountain, she took hold of his feet. Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Leave her alone, for she is in bitter distress, and the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me."
She said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Didn't I say, 'Do not raise my hopes'?"
Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck up your robe, take my staff in your hand and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet him, and if anyone greets you, do not answer him. Lay my staff on the boy's face."
But the boy's mother said, "As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave you." So he got up and followed her.
Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the staff on the boy's face, but there was no sound and no sign of life. So he went back to meet Elisha and told him, "The boy has not woken up."
When Elisha came into the house, there was the boy, dead, laid on his bed.
He went in and shut the door on the two of them, and he prayed to the LORD.
Then he got up on the bed and lay on the child. He put his mouth on his mouth, his eyes on his eyes and his hands on his hands, and as he stretched himself out over him, the child's body grew warm.
Elisha got up again and walked once back and forth in the house. Then he went up and stretched himself out over him again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
Elisha called Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." He called her, and when she came to him, he said, "Pick up your son."
She came in, fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground. Then she picked up her son and went out.

Elisha returned to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. While the company of prophets was sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire and cook stew for the company of prophets."

One of them went out into the field to gather herbs and found a wild vine. From it he gathered wild gourds, as many as his garment could hold. He came back and cut them up into the pot of stew, though they did not know what they were.
They poured it out for the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" And they could not eat it.
Elisha said, "Bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Pour it out for the people to eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.

A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread from the first of the harvest: twenty loaves of barley bread, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."
His attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" He said, "Give it to the people to eat, for this is what the LORD says: They will eat and have some left over."
So he set it before them, and they ate and had some left over, as the LORD had said.

Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Aram, was a great man in his master's eyes and highly honored, because through him the LORD had given victory to Aram. He was a mighty warrior, but he had a skin disease.
Raiding bands from Aram had gone out and taken a young girl captive from the land of Israel, and she served Naaman's wife.
She said to her mistress, "If only my master were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would cure him of his skin disease."
Naaman went and told his master, "This is what the girl from the land of Israel said."
The king of Aram said, "Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel." So he went, taking with him ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold and ten changes of clothes.
He brought the letter to the king of Israel. It said, "Now, with this letter, I am sending my servant Naaman to you, so that you may cure him of his skin disease."

When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes and said, "Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends word to me to cure a man of his skin disease? Just look and see how he is trying to pick a quarrel with me!"

When Elisha the man of God heard that the king of Israel had torn his clothes, he sent this message to the king: "Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel."
So Naaman came with his horses and his chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
Elisha sent a messenger to him to say, "Go and wash seven times in the Jordan. Your flesh will be restored, and you will be clean."
But Naaman was angry and went away. He said, "I thought he would surely come out to me, stand and call on the name of the LORD his God, wave his hand over the place and cure the skin disease.
Aren't the Amana and the Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn't I wash in them and be clean?" So he turned and went away in a rage.
But his servants came up to him and said, "My father, if the prophet had told you to do something great, wouldn't you have done it? How much more, then, when he tells you, 'Wash and be clean'!"
So he went down and dipped himself in the Jordan seven times, as the man of God had said. His flesh was restored and became like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.

Then he went back to the man of God, he and all his company. He came and stood before him and said, "Now I know that there is no God in all the earth except in Israel. So please accept a gift from your servant."
But Elisha said, "As the LORD lives, whom I serve, I will not accept anything." Naaman urged him to accept it, but he refused.

Naaman said, "If not, then please let your servant be given as much earth as a pair of mules can carry. For your servant will never again offer burnt offering or sacrifice to other gods, but only to the LORD.

But may the LORD pardon your servant for this one thing: when my master goes into the temple of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my arm, and I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, when I bow down in the temple of Rimmon, may the LORD pardon your servant for this."
Elisha said to him, "Go in peace." So Naaman went away from him some distance.

Then Gehazi, the servant of Elisha the man of God, said to himself, "Look, my master has let this Aramean Naaman off without accepting from him what he brought. As the LORD lives, I will run after him and take something from him."
So Gehazi hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw someone running after him, he got down from the chariot to meet him and said, "Is everything all right?"

He said, "Everything is all right. My master has sent me to say, 'Just now two young men from the company of prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothes.'"

Naaman said, "Please, take two talents." He urged him to take them, and he tied up two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothes. He gave them to two of his servants, and they carried them ahead of Gehazi.
When Gehazi came to the hill, he took the things from them and put them away in the house. Then he sent the men away, and they left.
He went in and stood before his master, and Elisha said to him, "Where have you been, Gehazi?" He said, "Your servant hasn't gone anywhere."

But Elisha said to him, "Wasn't my heart there when a man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is this the time to accept money and to accept clothes, olive groves and vineyards, sheep and cattle, male and female servants?
Naaman's skin disease will cling to you and to your descendants forever." And Gehazi went out from his presence with a skin disease, white as snow.
The company of prophets said to Elisha, "Look, the place where we live under your leadership is too small for us.
Let us go to the Jordan, and let each of us get a beam from there, and let us make ourselves a place to live there." He said, "Go."
Then one of them said, "Please be willing to go with your servants." He said, "I will go."
So he went with them. When they came to the Jordan, they began cutting down trees.
As one of them was felling a beam, the iron axe head fell into the water. He cried out, "Oh no, my lord! It was borrowed!"
The man of God said, "Where did it fall?" When he showed him the place, Elisha cut off a stick, threw it in there and made the iron float.
He said, "Pick it up." So the man reached out his hand and took it.
Now the king of Aram was at war with Israel. He consulted with his officers and said, "My camp will be at such and such a place."
But the man of God sent word to the king of Israel: "Be careful not to pass that place, because the Arameans are going down there."
So the king of Israel sent word to the place the man of God had told him about. Elisha would warn him, and the king would be on his guard there. This happened more than once or twice.
The king of Aram was enraged by this. He called his officers and said to them, "Won't you tell me which of us is on the side of the king of Israel?"
One of his officers said, "No one, my lord the king. It is Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel. He tells the king of Israel the words you speak in your bedroom."
The king said, "Go and find out where he is, so that I can send men and seize him." He was told, "He is in Dothan."
So he sent horses and chariots and a strong force there. They came by night and surrounded the city.
The attendant of the man of God got up early and went out, and there was an army surrounding the city with horses and chariots. His servant said to him, "Oh no, my lord! What shall we do?"
He said, "Do not be afraid, for there are more with us than with them."
Then Elisha prayed and said, "LORD, please open his eyes so that he may see." The LORD opened the servant's eyes, and he saw that the hill was full of horses and chariots of fire all around Elisha.
As the Arameans came down toward him, Elisha prayed to the LORD and said, "Please strike this nation with blindness." So he struck them with blindness, as Elisha had asked.
Elisha said to them, "This is not the road, and this is not the city. Follow me, and I will lead you to the man you are looking for." And he led them to Samaria.
As soon as they had come into Samaria, Elisha said, "LORD, open the eyes of these men so that they may see." The LORD opened their eyes, and they saw that they were inside Samaria.
When the king of Israel saw them, he said to Elisha, "Shall I strike them down, my father? Shall I strike them down?"

He said, "Do not strike them down. Would you strike down those you have taken captive with your own sword and bow? Set food and water before them, so that they may eat and drink and go back to their master."
So he prepared a great feast for them, and they ate and drank. Then he sent them away, and they went back to their master. And the raiding bands of Aram did not come into the land of Israel again.
Some time later Ben-hadad king of Aram gathered his whole army, marched up and laid siege to Samaria.
There was a great famine in Samaria. They besieged it until a donkey's head sold for eighty shekels of silver, and a quarter of a kab of dove's dung for five shekels of silver.
As the king of Israel was walking along the wall, a woman cried out to him, "Help, my lord the king!"
He said, "If the LORD does not help you, how can I help you? With grain from the threshing floor, or with wine from the winepress?"
Then the king asked her, "What is the matter?" She said, "This woman said to me, 'Give up your son, so that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.'
So we cooked my son and ate him. The next day I said to her, 'Give up your son, so that we may eat him.' But she has hidden her son."
When the king heard the woman's words, he tore his clothes. As he was walking along the wall, the people looked, and there was sackcloth underneath, on his body.
He said, "May God do this to me, and more, if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on his shoulders today!"

Elisha was sitting in his house, and the elders were sitting with him. The king sent a man ahead of him, but before the messenger reached him, Elisha said to the elders, "Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent someone to take off my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door and hold the door shut against him. Isn't the sound of his master's footsteps behind him?"
While he was still speaking with them, the messenger came down to him. And he said, "This disaster is from the LORD. Why should I wait for the LORD any longer?"

Elisha said, "Hear the word of the LORD. This is what the LORD says: About this time tomorrow, a seah of fine flour will sell for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, at the gate of Samaria."

The officer on whose arm the king leaned answered the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in the sky, could this happen?" Elisha said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
Now there were four men with a skin disease at the entrance to the gate. They said to one another, "Why are we sitting here until we die?

If we say, 'Let's go into the city,' the famine is in the city, and we will die there. And if we stay here, we will die. So come, let's go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live, and if they kill us, we will die."
So they got up at dusk to go to the Aramean camp. When they came to the edge of the Aramean camp, there was no one there.

For the Lord had made the Aramean army hear the sound of chariots and the sound of horses, the sound of a great army. They had said to one another, "Look, the king of Israel has hired the kings of the Hittites and the kings of Egypt to attack us."
So they had got up and fled at dusk. They had abandoned their tents, their horses and their donkeys, the camp just as it was, and fled for their lives.

When these men with skin disease came to the edge of the camp, they went into one tent and ate and drank. They carried off silver, gold and clothes from it, and went and hid them. Then they came back and went into another tent, carried things off from it, and went and hid them too.

Then they said to one another, "We are not doing right. This is a day of good news, and we are keeping quiet. If we wait until morning light, we will be punished. So come, let's go and tell the king's household."

So they went and called out to the gatekeepers of the city and told them, "We went to the Aramean camp, and there was no one there, not a human voice. There were only the horses tied up, the donkeys tied up, and the tents just as they were."
The gatekeepers shouted the news, and it was reported inside the king's palace.

The king got up in the night and said to his officers, "Let me tell you what the Arameans have done to us. They know that we are starving, so they have left the camp to hide in the open country. They are thinking, 'When they come out of the city, we will take them alive and get into the city.'"

One of his officers answered, "Let some men take five of the horses that are left, the ones still left in the city. They are like the whole crowd of Israel who are left in it; they are like the whole crowd of Israel who have already died. Let us send them and see."
So they took two chariots with their horses, and the king sent them after the Aramean army, saying, "Go and see."
They followed them as far as the Jordan, and the whole road was strewn with clothes and equipment that the Arameans had thrown away in their haste. The messengers returned and told the king.
Then the people went out and plundered the Aramean camp. So a seah of fine flour sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, as the LORD had said.
Now the king had put the officer on whose arm he leaned in charge of the gate. The people trampled him in the gate, and he died, just as the man of God had said when the king came down to him.
For when the man of God had said to the king, "Two seahs of barley will sell for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, about this time tomorrow at the gate of Samaria,"

the officer had answered the man of God, "Look, even if the LORD were to make windows in the sky, could such a thing happen?" And Elisha had said, "You will see it with your own eyes, but you will not eat any of it."
And that is what happened to him. The people trampled him in the gate, and he died.

Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had brought back to life, "Get up and go, you and your household, and live wherever you can, for the LORD has called for a famine, and it will come on the land for seven years."
The woman got up and did as the man of God had said. She went with her household and lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
At the end of the seven years, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines and went to appeal to the king for her house and her land.
Now the king was talking with Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, and saying, "Tell me all the great things Elisha has done."

Just as Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead back to life, the woman whose son he had brought back to life came to appeal to the king for her house and her land. Gehazi said, "My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is her son whom Elisha brought back to life."

The king questioned the woman, and she told him about it. Then the king assigned an official to her and said, "Give back everything that was hers, along with all the produce of her land from the day she left the country until now."
Elisha came to Damascus. Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick, and he was told, "The man of God has come here."
The king said to Hazael, "Take a gift with you and go to meet the man of God. Consult the LORD through him and ask, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"

So Hazael went to meet him, taking with him a gift of every good thing of Damascus, forty camel loads. He came and stood before him and said, "Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to you to ask, 'Will I recover from this illness?'"
Elisha said to him, "Go and tell him, 'You will certainly recover.' But the LORD has shown me that he will certainly die."
He kept his face fixed and stared until the other was ashamed. Then the man of God wept.

Hazael said, "Why is my lord weeping?" He said, "Because I know the harm you will do to the Israelites. You will set their fortresses on fire, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little children to pieces and rip open their pregnant women."
Hazael said, "But what is your servant, a mere dog, that he should do this great thing?" Elisha said, "The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram."
Then Hazael left Elisha and went back to his master, who said to him, "What did Elisha say to you?" He said, "He told me you would certainly recover."
But the next day he took the blanket, dipped it in water and spread it over his face, and he died. And Hazael became king in his place.
In the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, when Jehoshaphat was king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.
He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD was not willing to destroy Judah, for the sake of his servant David, since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants forever.
In his days Edom rebelled against Judah's rule and set up a king of their own.
So Joram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. He rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots, and the army fled to their homes.
So Edom has been in rebellion against Judah's rule to this day. Libnah also rebelled at that time.
As for the rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
Joram slept with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. And his son Ahaziah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah daughter of Omri king of Israel.
He walked in the way of the house of Ahab and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for he was related by marriage to the house of Ahab.
He went with Joram son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

King Joram went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to see Joram son of Ahab, because he was wounded.
Elisha the prophet called one of the company of prophets and said to him, "Tuck up your robe, take this flask of oil with you and go to Ramoth-gilead.
When you get there, look for Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi. Go in, get him to leave his companions, and take him into an inner room.
Then take the flask of oil, pour it on his head and say, 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.' Then open the door and run. Do not wait."
So the young man, the young prophet, went to Ramoth-gilead.
When he arrived, the commanders of the army were sitting together. He said, "I have a message for you, commander." Jehu said, "For which one of us?" He said, "For you, commander."

Jehu got up and went into the house, and the young man poured the oil on his head and said to him, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I anoint you king over the people of the LORD, over Israel.
You are to strike down the house of Ahab your master, and I will avenge on Jezebel the blood of my servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD.
The whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab every male in Israel, whether slave or free.
I will make the house of Ahab like the house of Jeroboam son of Nebat and like the house of Baasha son of Ahijah.
And the dogs will eat Jezebel on the plot of ground at Jezreel, and no one will bury her." Then he opened the door and ran.
When Jehu came out to his master's officers, someone said to him, "Is everything all right? Why did this madman come to you?" He said to them, "You know the man and the way he talks."
They said, "That's a lie! Tell us." He said, "This is what he said to me: 'This is what the LORD says: I anoint you king over Israel.'"
At once each of them took his cloak and spread it under him on the bare steps. They blew the ram's horn and said, "Jehu is king!"
So Jehu son of Jehoshaphat son of Nimshi conspired against Joram. Now Joram, with all Israel, had been guarding Ramoth-gilead against Hazael king of Aram,

but King Jehoram had gone back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds the Arameans had given him when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Jehu said, "If you agree, let no one slip out of the city to go and tell the news in Jezreel."
Then Jehu got into his chariot and went to Jezreel, because Joram was lying there. And Ahaziah king of Judah had come down to see Joram.

The watchman standing on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's troops coming, and he said, "I see a company of troops." Jehoram said, "Take a horseman and send him to meet them, and let him ask, 'Is it peace?'"

So the horseman went to meet him and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me." The watchman reported, "The messenger has reached them, but he is not coming back."
Then the king sent a second horseman. He came to them and said, "This is what the king says: 'Is it peace?'" Jehu said, "What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me."
The watchman reported, "He has reached them, but he is not coming back. And the driving is like the driving of Jehu son of Nimshi, for he drives like a madman."

Jehoram said, "Harness the chariot." When his chariot was harnessed, Jehoram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah set out, each in his own chariot. They went out to meet Jehu and found him at the plot of ground belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite.
When Jehoram saw Jehu, he said, "Is it peace, Jehu?" He answered, "How can there be peace, as long as the prostitution and the many sorceries of your mother Jezebel go on?"
Jehoram turned his chariot around and fled, calling out to Ahaziah, "Treachery, Ahaziah!"
Then Jehu drew his bow with all his strength and shot Jehoram between the shoulders. The arrow came out through his heart, and he slumped down in his chariot.

Jehu said to Bidkar his officer, "Pick him up and throw him onto the plot of ground belonging to Naboth the Jezreelite. Remember how you and I were riding side by side behind Ahab his father, when the LORD pronounced this oracle against him:

'As surely as I saw the blood of Naboth and the blood of his sons yesterday, declares the LORD, I will repay you on this plot of ground, declares the LORD.' So now pick him up and throw him onto the plot of ground, as the LORD said."

When Ahaziah king of Judah saw this, he fled by the road to Beth-haggan. Jehu chased after him and said, "Strike him down too!" And they struck him in his chariot on the ascent to Gur, which is near Ibleam. He fled to Megiddo and died there.
His servants carried him in a chariot to Jerusalem and buried him in his tomb with his ancestors in the City of David.
Ahaziah had become king over Judah in the eleventh year of Joram son of Ahab.
Then Jehu came to Jezreel. When Jezebel heard about it, she painted her eyes, arranged her hair and looked down through the window.
As Jehu came in through the gate, she said, "Is it peace, Zimri, murderer of your master?"
He looked up at the window and said, "Who is on my side? Who?" Two or three officials looked down at him.
He said, "Throw her down!" So they threw her down, and some of her blood spattered on the wall and on the horses, and he trampled her.
Then he went in and ate and drank. He said, "See to this cursed woman and bury her, for she was a king's daughter."
But when they went to bury her, they found nothing of her except the skull, the feet and the palms of her hands.

They came back and told him, and he said, "This is the word of the LORD, which he spoke through his servant Elijah the Tishbite: 'On the plot of ground at Jezreel the dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel.
Jezebel's corpse will be like dung on the surface of the field on the plot of ground at Jezreel, so that no one will be able to say, "This is Jezebel."'"
Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab's sons. They said,
"Now, as soon as this letter reaches you, since your master's sons are with you, and you have the chariots and the horses, a fortified city and the weapons,
choose the best and most capable of your master's sons, set him on his father's throne, and fight for your master's house."
But they were terrified and said, "Look, two kings could not stand against him. How can we stand?"

So the palace administrator, the governor of the city, the elders and the guardians sent this message to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do everything you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think best."

Then he wrote them a second letter, saying, "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of your master's sons and come to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy of them, were with the leading men of the city, who were bringing them up.
When the letter reached them, they took the king's sons and slaughtered all seventy of them. They put their heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu at Jezreel.
The messenger came and told him, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." He said, "Put them in two piles at the entrance to the gate until morning."
In the morning he went out, stood before all the people and said to them, "You are innocent. It was I who conspired against my master and killed him. But who struck down all these?
Know, then, that nothing the LORD has spoken against the house of Ahab will fail. The LORD has done what he said through his servant Elijah."
So Jehu struck down all who were left of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his leading men, his close friends and his priests, until he left him no survivor.
Then he set out and went toward Samaria. On the way, at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,
Jehu met the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah. He said, "Who are you?" They said, "We are Ahaziah's brothers, and we have come down to greet the king's sons and the sons of the queen mother."
He said, "Take them alive." So they took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men. He did not leave a single one of them.

When he left there, he met Jehonadab son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart true to mine, as mine is to yours?" Jehonadab said, "It is." "If it is," said Jehu, "give me your hand." So he gave him his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot with him.
He said, "Come with me and see my zeal for the LORD." So they had him ride in his chariot.
When Jehu came to Samaria, he struck down all who were left of Ahab's family in Samaria, until he had destroyed them, according to the word the LORD had spoken to Elijah.
Then Jehu gathered all the people together and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him a lot.

So now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I am holding a great sacrifice for Baal. Anyone who is missing will not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning, in order to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
Jehu said, "Proclaim a solemn assembly for Baal." So they proclaimed it.

Jehu sent word throughout Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came. Not one was left who did not come. They came into the temple of Baal, and the temple of Baal was filled from one end to the other.
Jehu said to the man in charge of the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for all the worshipers of Baal." So he brought out robes for them.

Then Jehu went into the temple of Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab, and he said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and make sure that there are no worshipers of the LORD here with you, only worshipers of Baal."
They went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed eighty men outside and had said, "If any of the men I am handing over to you escapes, it will be your life for his life."

As soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu said to the guards and the officers, "Go in and kill them. Let no one get out." So they killed them with the sword. The guards and the officers threw the bodies out and went into the inner shrine of the temple of Baal.
They brought out the standing stones of the temple of Baal and burned them.
They demolished the standing stone of Baal and tore down the temple of Baal, and they made it a latrine, as it is to this day.
So Jehu wiped out Baal from Israel.
But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit: the golden calves that were at Bethel and in Dan.

The LORD said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what is right in my eyes, and have done to the house of Ahab all that was in my heart, your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."
But Jehu was not careful to walk in the law of the LORD, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, which he had caused Israel to commit.
In those days the LORD began to cut away parts of Israel. Hazael defeated the Israelites throughout their territory,
from the Jordan eastward: all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the Arnon Valley, including Gilead and Bashan.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did and all his mighty deeds, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Jehu slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. And his son Jehoahaz became king in his place.
The time that Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria was twenty-eight years.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she set out to destroy the whole royal family.

But Jehosheba, King Joram's daughter and Ahaziah's sister, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death. She put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So they hid him from Athaliah, and he was not put to death.
He remained with her, hidden in the house of the LORD, for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada sent for the commanders of hundreds of the Carites and of the guards, and had them come to him in the house of the LORD. He made a covenant with them and put them under oath in the house of the LORD. Then he showed them the king's son.
He commanded them, "This is what you are to do. A third of you, those who come on duty on the Sabbath, are to keep guard over the king's palace,
a third are to be at the Sur Gate, and a third at the gate behind the guards. So you will keep guard over the palace as a barrier.
And your two divisions, all those who go off duty on the Sabbath, are to keep guard over the house of the LORD for the king.
Surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who comes into the ranks is to be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."

The commanders of hundreds did everything Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath together with those going off duty on the Sabbath, and they came to Jehoiada the priest.
The priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears and the shields that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of the LORD.
The guards stood, each with his weapons in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side, by the altar and the house, all around the king.
Then Jehoiada brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the statutes. They made him king and anointed him, and they clapped their hands and said, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the noise of the guards and the people, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there was the king, standing by the pillar, as the custom was. The commanders and the trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest commanded the commanders of hundreds, who were in charge of the army, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to death with the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "She must not be put to death in the house of the LORD."
So they seized her, and she went by the way of the horses' entrance to the king's palace, and there she was put to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between the LORD and the king and the people, that they would be the LORD's people, and also between the king and the people.

Then all the people of the land went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images to pieces, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars. And the priest posted guards over the house of the LORD.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the Carites, the guards and all the people of the land, and they brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They went by the way of the Gate of the Guards to the king's palace, and he took his seat on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword at the king's palace.
Jehoash was seven years old when he became king.
In the seventh year of Jehu, Jehoash became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Jehoash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all his days, because Jehoiada the priest instructed him.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.

Jehoash said to the priests, "All the money from the holy gifts that is brought into the house of the LORD, the money from the census, the money each person pays at his assessed value, and all the money that anyone freely chooses to bring into the house of the LORD,
let the priests take it, each from his donor, and let them repair the damage to the house wherever any damage is found."
But by the twenty-third year of King Jehoash, the priests had still not repaired the damage to the house.

So King Jehoash summoned Jehoiada the priest and the other priests and said to them, "Why are you not repairing the damage to the house? Now take no more money from your donors, but hand it over for the damage to the house."
The priests agreed that they would take no more money from the people, and that they would not repair the damage to the house themselves.

Then Jehoiada the priest took a chest, bored a hole in its lid and set it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into the house of the LORD. The priests who guarded the threshold put into it all the money that was brought into the house of the LORD.

Whenever they saw that there was a large amount of money in the chest, the king's secretary and the high priest came up, and they tied up and counted the money that was found in the house of the LORD.

They would give the money that had been weighed out into the hands of the men doing the work, who had been put in charge of the house of the LORD. They paid it out to the carpenters and the builders who worked on the house of the LORD,
to the masons and the stonecutters, and for buying timber and dressed stone to repair the damage to the house of the LORD, and for everything else that was spent on repairing the house.

But no silver basins, wick trimmers, sprinkling bowls or trumpets, or any articles of gold or articles of silver, were made for the house of the LORD from the money brought into the house of the LORD.
It was given to the workers, and with it they repaired the house of the LORD.
They did not require an accounting from the men to whom they handed the money to pay the workers, for they dealt honestly.
The money from the guilt offerings and the money from the sin offerings was not brought into the house of the LORD. It belonged to the priests.
At that time Hazael king of Aram went up and fought against Gath and captured it. Then Hazael turned to go up against Jerusalem.

Jehoash king of Judah took all the holy things that his ancestors Jehoshaphat, Jehoram and Ahaziah, kings of Judah, had dedicated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that was found in the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's palace, and he sent them to Hazael king of Aram. Then Hazael withdrew from Jerusalem.
As for the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
His officers rose up and formed a conspiracy, and they struck down Joash at Beth-millo, on the road that goes down to Silla.
His officers Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of Shomer struck him, and he died. They buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. And his son Amaziah became king in his place.
In the twenty-third year of Joash son of Ahaziah king of Judah, Jehoahaz son of Jehu became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned seventeen years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit. He did not turn away from them.
So the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and he handed them over to Hazael king of Aram and to Ben-hadad son of Hazael, again and again.
Then Jehoahaz pleaded with the LORD, and the LORD listened to him, for he saw the oppression of Israel, how the king of Aram oppressed them.
The LORD gave Israel a deliverer, and they escaped from the power of Aram. So the Israelites lived in their homes as they had before.
But they did not turn away from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, which he had caused Israel to commit. They went on in them. And the Asherah pole also remained standing in Samaria.
For the king of Aram had left Jehoahaz an army of no more than fifty horsemen, ten chariots and ten thousand foot soldiers, because he had destroyed them and made them like the dust at threshing.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, all that he did and his mighty deeds, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Jehoahaz slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in Samaria. And his son Joash became king in his place.
In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash son of Jehoahaz became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned sixteen years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit, but went on in them.
As for the rest of the acts of Joash, all that he did and his mighty deeds, how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Joash slept with his ancestors, and Jeroboam sat on his throne. Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
Now Elisha had fallen sick with the illness from which he would die. Joash king of Israel went down to him and wept over him, saying, "My father, my father! The chariots of Israel and its horsemen!"
Elisha said to him, "Take a bow and arrows." So he took a bow and arrows.
Then he said to the king of Israel, "Put your hand on the bow." So he put his hand on it, and Elisha put his hands on the king's hands.

He said, "Open the window toward the east." So he opened it. Elisha said, "Shoot!" And he shot. Elisha said, "The LORD's arrow of victory, the arrow of victory over Aram! You will strike down Aram at Aphek until you have made an end of them."
Then he said, "Take the arrows." So he took them. He said to the king of Israel, "Strike the ground." He struck it three times and stopped.

The man of God was angry with him and said, "You should have struck five or six times. Then you would have struck down Aram until you had made an end of it. But now you will strike down Aram only three times."
Elisha died, and they buried him. Now Moabite raiding bands used to come into the land at the coming of the year.

Once, as some men were burying a man, they suddenly saw a raiding band, and they threw the man into Elisha's tomb. When the man went down and touched Elisha's bones, he came to life and stood up on his feet.
Hazael king of Aram oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

But the LORD was gracious to them and had compassion on them. He turned toward them because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. He was not willing to destroy them, and he has not cast them out of his presence until now.
Hazael king of Aram died, and his son Ben-hadad became king in his place.

Then Jehoash son of Jehoahaz took back from Ben-hadad son of Hazael the cities that he had taken in war from his father Jehoahaz. Three times Joash defeated him, and he recovered the cities of Israel.
In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel, Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not like his ancestor David. He did everything his father Joash had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he struck down his officials who had struck down his father the king.

But he did not put to death the sons of the murderers, in keeping with what is written in the book of the Law of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Fathers are not to be put to death for their sons, and sons are not to be put to death for their fathers. Each is to be put to death for his own sin."
He struck down ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and he captured Sela in battle and called it Joktheel, the name it has to this day.
Then Amaziah sent messengers to Jehoash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other."

Jehoash king of Israel sent this reply to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thornbush in Lebanon sent word to a cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
You have indeed struck down Edom, and your heart has made you proud. Enjoy your glory, and stay at home. Why stir up trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his home.

Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Jehoash son of Ahaziah, at Beth-shemesh. Then he came to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.
He took all the gold and silver and all the articles that were found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's palace, as well as hostages, and he returned to Samaria.
As for the rest of the acts of Jehoash, what he did and his mighty deeds, and how he fought against Amaziah king of Judah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Jehoash slept with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. And his son Jeroboam became king in his place.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
As for the rest of the acts of Amaziah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
They formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They brought him back on horses, and he was buried in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.
Then all the people of Judah took Azariah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He was the one who rebuilt Elath and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his ancestors.
In the fifteenth year of Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel became king in Samaria, and he reigned forty-one years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from all the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.

He restored the border of Israel from Lebo-hamath to the Sea of the Arabah, according to the word of the LORD, the God of Israel, which he spoke through his servant Jonah son of Amittai, the prophet from Gath-hepher.
For the LORD saw that the suffering of Israel was very bitter. There was no one left, slave or free, and there was no one to help Israel.
The LORD had not said that he would blot out the name of Israel from under heaven, so he saved them through Jeroboam son of Joash.

As for the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, all that he did and his mighty deeds, how he fought, and how he recovered for Israel Damascus and Hamath, which had belonged to Judah, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Jeroboam slept with his ancestors, with the kings of Israel. And his son Zechariah became king in his place.
In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah became king.
He was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places.
The LORD struck the king, and he had a skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, and Jotham the king's son was in charge of the palace, governing the people of the land.
As for the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
Azariah slept with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the City of David. And his son Jotham became king in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah son of Jeroboam became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned six months.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestors had done. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.
Shallum son of Jabesh conspired against him. He struck him down in front of the people and killed him, and he became king in his place.
As for the rest of the acts of Zechariah, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
This was the word of the LORD that he spoke to Jehu: "Your descendants to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel." And so it came to pass.
Shallum son of Jabesh became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned one full month in Samaria.
Then Menahem son of Gadi went up from Tirzah and came to Samaria. He struck down Shallum son of Jabesh in Samaria and killed him, and he became king in his place.
As for the rest of the acts of Shallum, and the conspiracy he formed, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.

At that time Menahem, setting out from Tirzah, attacked Tiphsah and everyone in it and its territory, because they would not open the gates to him. He attacked it and ripped open all its pregnant women.
In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem son of Gadi became king over Israel, and he reigned ten years in Samaria.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. All his days he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.
Pul king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul a thousand talents of silver, so that he would support him and strengthen his hold on the kingdom.

Menahem raised the money from Israel, from all the wealthy men, fifty shekels of silver from each man, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back and did not stay there in the land.
As for the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel?
Menahem slept with his ancestors, and his son Pekahiah became king in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah son of Menahem became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned two years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.

Pekah son of Remaliah, his officer, conspired against him. With fifty men of Gilead, he struck him down in Samaria, in the citadel of the king's palace, along with Argob and Arieh. He killed him and became king in his place.
As for the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah son of Remaliah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned twenty years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he had caused Israel to commit.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria came and captured Ijon, Abel-beth-maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali, and he deported the people to Assyria.
Then Hoshea son of Elah formed a conspiracy against Pekah son of Remaliah. He struck him down and killed him, and he became king in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham son of Uzziah.
As for the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, they are written in the book of the annals of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham son of Uzziah king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerusha daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. He did everything his father Uzziah had done.
But the high places were not removed. The people still sacrificed and burned incense at the high places. He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD.
As for the rest of the acts of Jotham, and what he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
In those days the LORD began to send Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham slept with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David his ancestor. And his son Ahaz became king in his place.
In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah became king.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God, as his ancestor David had done.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel. He even made his son pass through the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.
Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to make war. They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.
At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram and drove the people of Judah out of Elath. Then the Edomites came to Elath, and they have lived there to this day.
Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria to say, "I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the power of the king of Aram and the king of Israel, who are attacking me."
Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's palace, and sent it as a payment to the king of Assyria.
The king of Assyria listened to him. The king of Assyria went up against Damascus and captured it. He deported its people to Kir, and he killed Rezin.

When King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, he saw the altar that was in Damascus. King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a model of the altar and a plan of it, with all the details of its construction.
Uriah the priest built the altar. He made it according to everything King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and Uriah the priest had it finished by the time King Ahaz came back from Damascus.
When the king came back from Damascus, the king saw the altar. The king approached the altar and went up on it.
He burned his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and splashed the blood of his fellowship offerings against the altar.
As for the bronze altar that stood before the LORD, he moved it from the front of the house, from between the new altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of the new altar.

King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, "On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering and the evening grain offering, the king's burnt offering and his grain offering, and the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their grain offering and their drink offerings. Splash against it all the blood of the burnt offerings and all the blood of the sacrifices. But the bronze altar will be for me to inquire by."
Uriah the priest did everything King Ahaz commanded.
King Ahaz cut off the frames of the stands and removed the basins from them. He took down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone pavement.
Because of the king of Assyria, he removed from the house of the LORD the covered way for the Sabbath that had been built in the house, and the king's outer entrance.
As for the rest of the acts of Ahaz, what he did, are they not written in the book of the annals of the kings of Judah?
Ahaz slept with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. And his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea son of Elah became king over Israel in Samaria, and he reigned nine years.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, but not like the kings of Israel who were before him.
Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against him, and Hoshea became his vassal and paid him tribute.

But the king of Assyria discovered that Hoshea was conspiring against him, for he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt and had not paid tribute to the king of Assyria as he had done year by year. So the king of Assyria arrested him and put him in prison.
The king of Assyria invaded the whole land. He came up to Samaria and besieged it for three years.
In the ninth year of Hoshea, the king of Assyria captured Samaria. He deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes.
This happened because the Israelites had sinned against the LORD their God, who had brought them up out of the land of Egypt, from under the power of Pharaoh king of Egypt. They worshiped other gods.
They followed the customs of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites, and the customs that the kings of Israel had introduced.
The Israelites secretly did things against the LORD their God that were not right. They built themselves high places in all their towns, from watchtower to fortified city.
They set up standing stones and Asherah poles for themselves on every high hill and under every green tree.
There they burned incense at all the high places, like the nations whom the LORD had driven into exile before them. They did evil things, provoking the LORD to anger.
They served idols, though the LORD had said to them, "You must not do this."

Yet the LORD warned Israel and Judah through every prophet and every seer: "Turn from your evil ways, and keep my commands and my decrees, in keeping with all the law that I commanded your ancestors and sent to you through my servants the prophets."
But they would not listen. They were as stubborn as their ancestors, who did not trust in the LORD their God.

They rejected his decrees and his covenant that he had made with their ancestors, and the statutes with which he had warned them. They went after worthless things and became worthless themselves. They followed the nations around them, although the LORD had commanded them not to do as they did.
They abandoned all the commands of the LORD their God and made themselves images of cast metal, two calves. They made an Asherah pole, bowed down to all the host of heaven and served Baal.

They made their sons and their daughters pass through the fire. They practiced divination and interpreted omens, and they sold themselves to do what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, provoking him to anger.
So the LORD was very angry with Israel and removed them from his presence. No one was left but the tribe of Judah alone.
Judah too did not keep the commands of the LORD their God, but followed the customs that Israel had introduced.
So the LORD rejected all the descendants of Israel. He afflicted them and handed them over to plunderers, until he had cast them out of his presence.
When he tore Israel away from the house of David, they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam drove Israel away from following the LORD and made them commit a great sin.
The Israelites walked in all the sins that Jeroboam had committed. They did not turn away from them,
until the LORD removed Israel from his presence, as he had said through all his servants the prophets. So Israel went into exile from their own land to Assyria, and they are there to this day.

The king of Assyria brought people from Babylon, Cuthah, Avva, Hamath and Sepharvaim and settled them in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites. They took possession of Samaria and lived in its towns.
When they first lived there, they did not worship the LORD, so the LORD sent lions among them, and they killed some of them.

So the king of Assyria was told, "The nations you deported and settled in the towns of Samaria do not know what the god of the land requires. So he has sent lions among them, and they are killing them, because they do not know what the god of the land requires."
Then the king of Assyria gave this command: "Send back there one of the priests you deported from there. Let him go and live there, and let him teach them what the god of the land requires."
So one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria came and lived in Bethel, and he taught them how they should worship the LORD.
But each nation made its own gods and set them up in the shrines of the high places that the people of Samaria had made, each nation in the towns where they lived.
The people of Babylon made Succoth-benoth, the people of Cuth made Nergal, and the people of Hamath made Ashima.
The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak, and the Sepharvites burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim.
They also worshiped the LORD, and they appointed all sorts of people from among themselves as priests for the high places, who served for them in the shrines of the high places.
They worshiped the LORD, but they also served their own gods, following the custom of the nations from which they had been deported.

To this day they follow their former customs. They do not worship the LORD, and they do not follow the decrees and rulings given to them, or the law and the command that the LORD gave to the descendants of Jacob, whom he named Israel.
The LORD had made a covenant with them and commanded them, "Do not worship other gods. Do not bow down to them, serve them or sacrifice to them.
But the LORD, who brought you up from the land of Egypt with great power and an outstretched arm, is the one you must worship. To him you must bow down, and to him you must sacrifice.
The decrees and the rulings, the law and the command that he wrote for you, you must always be careful to keep. Do not worship other gods.
Do not forget the covenant I have made with you, and do not worship other gods.
But worship the LORD your God, and he will rescue you from the power of all your enemies."
But they would not listen. Instead they went on following their former custom.
So these nations worshiped the LORD, but they also served their carved images. Their children and their grandchildren have done as their ancestors did, to this day.
In the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz king of Judah became king.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abi daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his ancestor David had done.

He removed the high places, smashed the standing stones and cut down the Asherah pole. He broke into pieces the bronze snake that Moses had made, for until those days the Israelites had been burning incense to it. It was called Nehushtan.
He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel. There was no one like him among all the kings of Judah after him, or among those who were before him.
He held fast to the LORD and did not turn away from following him. He kept the commands that the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD was with him, and he succeeded in everything he undertook. He rebelled against the king of Assyria and would not serve him.
He defeated the Philistines as far as Gaza and its territory, from watchtower to fortified city.
In the fourth year of King Hezekiah, which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria and besieged it.
At the end of three years they captured it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which was the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria was captured.
The king of Assyria deported Israel to Assyria and settled them in Halah, on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the towns of the Medes,
because they had not obeyed the LORD their God, but had broken his covenant, all that Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded. They would neither listen nor obey.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.

Then Hezekiah king of Judah sent this message to the king of Assyria at Lachish: "I have done wrong. Withdraw from me, and I will pay whatever you demand of me." The king of Assyria required of Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
Hezekiah gave him all the silver that was found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king's palace.
