He built Tadmor in the wilderness and all the storage cities that he built in Hamath.
He built Upper Beth-horon and Lower Beth-horon, fortified cities with walls, gates and bars,

and Baalath, and all the storage cities that Solomon had, all the cities for the chariots and the cities for the horsemen, and whatever Solomon desired to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon and in all the land under his rule.
As for all the people who were left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, who were not of Israel,
their descendants who were left after them in the land, whom the Israelites had not wiped out, Solomon conscripted them as forced labor, as they are to this day.
But Solomon did not make slaves of any of the Israelites for his work. They were his soldiers, the commanders of his officers, and the commanders of his chariots and his horsemen.
These were King Solomon's chief officers, 250 of them, who directed the people.

Solomon brought Pharaoh's daughter up from the City of David to the house he had built for her, for he said, "My wife must not live in the house of David king of Israel, for the places to which the ark of the LORD has come are holy."
Then Solomon offered burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of the LORD that he had built in front of the porch,

as each day required, offering them according to the command of Moses for the Sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed festivals three times a year: the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks and the Festival of Shelters.

Following the ruling of his father David, he appointed the divisions of the priests for their service, and the Levites for their duties of praising and ministering beside the priests, as each day required, and the gatekeepers by their divisions for each gate, for this was what David the man of God had commanded.
They did not turn aside from the king's command to the priests and the Levites in any matter, including the treasuries.
So all Solomon's work was carried out, from the day the foundation of the house of the LORD was laid until it was finished. The house of the LORD was complete.
Then Solomon went to Ezion-geber and to Eloth on the seashore, in the land of Edom.
Huram sent him ships by his servants, with servants who knew the sea. They went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and took from there 450 talents of gold, which they brought to King Solomon.

The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame, and she came to Jerusalem to test Solomon with hard questions. She came with a very great retinue, with camels carrying spices, a great quantity of gold, and precious stones. When she came to Solomon, she talked with him about everything that was on her mind.
Solomon answered all her questions. Nothing was hidden from Solomon that he could not explain to her.
When the queen of Sheba saw Solomon's wisdom, the house he had built,

the food on his table, the seating of his officials, the attendance of his servants and their clothing, his cupbearers and their clothing, and the ascent by which he went up to the house of the LORD, it took her breath away.
She said to the king, "The report I heard in my own country about your words and your wisdom was true.
But I did not believe their reports until I came and saw it with my own eyes. And look, not even half the greatness of your wisdom was told me. You go beyond the report I heard.
How happy your men must be! How happy these servants of yours, who stand before you continually and hear your wisdom!

Blessed be the LORD your God, who has delighted in you and set you on his throne as king for the LORD your God! Because your God loves Israel and will establish them forever, he has made you king over them, to do justice and what is right."
Then she gave the king 120 talents of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. There were never such spices as those the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brought gold from Ophir, also brought algum wood and precious stones.
The king used the algum wood to make steps for the house of the LORD and for the king's house, and lyres and harps for the singers. Nothing like them had been seen before in the land of Judah.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired, whatever she asked for, besides what she had brought to the king. Then she turned and went back to her own country, she and her servants.
The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was 666 talents of gold,
besides what the traders and the merchants brought. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the land also brought gold and silver to Solomon.
King Solomon made two hundred large shields of hammered gold. Six hundred shekels of hammered gold went into each shield.
He also made three hundred small shields of hammered gold. Three hundred shekels of gold went into each shield. The king put them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king also made a great throne of ivory and overlaid it with pure gold.
The throne had six steps, and a footstool of gold was attached to the throne. There were armrests on each side of the seat, with two lions standing beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood there on the six steps, one on each side. Nothing like it had ever been made in any kingdom.
All King Solomon's drinking vessels were gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were pure gold. Silver was considered of no value in Solomon's days.
For the king had ships that went to Tarshish with Huram's servants. Once every three years the Tarshish ships came, bringing gold and silver, ivory, apes and baboons.
So King Solomon was greater than all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought an audience with Solomon to hear the wisdom God had put in his heart.
Each of them brought his gift: articles of silver and articles of gold, garments, weapons and spices, horses and mules, so much year by year.
Solomon had four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, and he stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem.
He ruled over all the kings from the River to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt.
The king made silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he made cedar as plentiful as the sycamore-fig trees in the Shephelah.
Horses were imported for Solomon from Egypt and from all the lands.

As for the rest of the acts of Solomon, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Nathan the prophet, in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat?
Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years.
Solomon slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of his father David. And his son Rehoboam became king in his place.
Rehoboam went to Shechem, for all Israel had come to Shechem to make him king.
When Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it, he was in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon, and Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
They sent and summoned him, and Jeroboam and all Israel came and said to Rehoboam,
"Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten the hard service your father demanded and the heavy yoke he put on us, and we will serve you."
He said to them, "Come back to me in three days." So the people went away.
King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served his father Solomon while he was alive. He asked, "How do you advise me to answer this people?"
They said to him, "If you are kind to this people and please them and speak kind words to them, they will be your servants forever."
But he rejected the advice the elders gave him, and he consulted the young men who had grown up with him and who served him.
He said to them, "What do you advise that we answer this people, who have said to me, 'Lighten the yoke your father put on us'?"

The young men who had grown up with him said to him, "This is what you should say to the people who said to you, 'Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must make it lighter for us.' This is what you should tell them: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's waist.
My father loaded you with a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.'"
So Jeroboam and all the people came to Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them: "Come back to me on the third day."
The king answered them harshly. King Rehoboam rejected the advice of the elders
and spoke to them as the young men advised: "I will make your yoke heavy, and I will add to it. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions."
So the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events came from God, so that the LORD might fulfill his word that he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam son of Nebat.

As for all Israel, when the king did not listen to them, the people answered the king: "What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, every one of you, Israel! Now look after your own house, David!" So all Israel went to their tents.
But as for the Israelites who lived in the towns of Judah, Rehoboam reigned over them.
Then King Rehoboam sent Hadoram, who was in charge of the forced labor, but the Israelites stoned him to death. King Rehoboam managed to get into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
So Israel has been in rebellion against the house of David to this day.
When Rehoboam arrived in Jerusalem, he assembled the house of Judah and Benjamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight against Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam.
But the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah the man of God:
"Say to Rehoboam son of Solomon king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin,

'This is what the LORD says: Do not go up or fight against your relatives. Go home, every one of you, for this thing is from me.'" So they listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam lived in Jerusalem, and he built cities for defense in Judah.
Zorah, Aijalon and Hebron, which are in Judah and Benjamin, fortified cities.
He strengthened the fortresses and put commanders in them, with stores of food, oil and wine.
In every city he put large shields and spears, and he made them very strong. So Judah and Benjamin were his.
The priests and the Levites who were in all Israel came over to him from all their territories.
The Levites left their pasturelands and their property and came to Judah and Jerusalem, because Jeroboam and his sons had rejected them from serving as priests of the LORD.
He appointed his own priests for the high places, for the goat-demons and for the calves he had made.
After them, those from all the tribes of Israel who had set their hearts on seeking the LORD, the God of Israel, came to Jerusalem to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
They strengthened the kingdom of Judah, and they supported Rehoboam son of Solomon for three years, for they walked in the way of David and Solomon for three years.
Rehoboam married Mahalath daughter of Jerimoth son of David, and of Abihail daughter of Eliab son of Jesse.
She bore him sons: Jeush, Shemariah and Zaham.
After her he married Maacah daughter of Absalom, and she bore him Abijah, Attai, Ziza and Shelomith.

Rehoboam loved Maacah daughter of Absalom more than all his other wives and concubines. He had married eighteen wives and taken sixty concubines, and he fathered twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters.
Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief, the leader among his brothers, for he intended to make him king.
He acted wisely and distributed some of his sons through all the districts of Judah and Benjamin, in all the fortified cities. He gave them abundant provisions and sought many wives for them.
When Rehoboam's kingdom was established and he had become strong, he abandoned the law of the LORD, and all Israel with him.
In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem, because they had been unfaithful to the LORD,
with 1,200 chariots and 60,000 horsemen. The people who came with him from Egypt were beyond number: Libyans, Sukkites and Cushites.
He captured the fortified cities of Judah and came as far as Jerusalem.

Then Shemaiah the prophet came to Rehoboam and the leaders of Judah, who had gathered at Jerusalem because of Shishak, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD says: You have abandoned me, so I have abandoned you into the hand of Shishak."
Then the leaders of Israel and the king humbled themselves and said, "The LORD is righteous."

When the LORD saw that they had humbled themselves, the word of the LORD came to Shemaiah: "They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them. I will soon give them some deliverance, and my wrath will not be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak.
But they will become his servants, so that they may learn the difference between serving me and serving the kingdoms of other lands."

So Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem. He took away the treasures of the house of the LORD and the treasures of the king's house. He took everything. He also took the gold shields that Solomon had made.
So King Rehoboam made bronze shields to replace them, and he entrusted them to the commanders of the guard who kept watch at the entrance of the king's house.
Whenever the king went into the house of the LORD, the guards came and carried them, and then they brought them back to the guardroom.
Because he humbled himself, the anger of the LORD turned away from him, so as not to destroy him completely. Indeed, there was still some good in Judah.

King Rehoboam established himself firmly in Jerusalem and reigned. Rehoboam was forty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city the LORD had chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother's name was Naamah the Ammonite.
He did what was evil, because he did not set his heart on seeking the LORD.

As for the acts of Rehoboam, from first to last, are they not written in the records of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogies? There were wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually.
Rehoboam slept with his ancestors and was buried in the City of David. And his son Abijah became king in his place.
In the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam, Abijah became king over Judah.
He reigned three years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Micaiah daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There was war between Abijah and Jeroboam.
Abijah went into battle with an army of valiant warriors, four hundred thousand chosen men, and Jeroboam drew up his battle line against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, mighty warriors.
Abijah stood up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and said, "Listen to me, Jeroboam and all Israel!
Don't you know that the LORD, the God of Israel, gave the kingship over Israel to David forever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt?
Yet Jeroboam son of Nebat, a servant of Solomon son of David, rose up and rebelled against his master.
Worthless men, scoundrels, gathered around him and prevailed against Rehoboam son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and inexperienced and could not stand up to them.

And now you think you can stand up to the kingdom of the LORD, which is in the hands of the sons of David. You are a great multitude, and you have with you the gold calves that Jeroboam made to be your gods.

Haven't you driven out the priests of the LORD, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves like the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes to be ordained with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of what are not gods.
But as for us, the LORD is our God, and we have not abandoned him. Priests who are sons of Aaron minister to the LORD, and the Levites are at their work.

Every morning and every evening they burn burnt offerings and fragrant incense to the LORD. They set out the rows of bread on the pure table, and they light the gold lampstand with its lamps every evening. For we keep the charge of the LORD our God, but you have abandoned him.

Look, God is with us at our head, and his priests with their battle trumpets to sound the alarm against you. Israelites, do not fight against the LORD, the God of your ancestors, for you will not succeed."
But Jeroboam had sent an ambush around to come up behind them, so that his troops were in front of Judah and the ambush was behind them.
When Judah turned, there was the battle, in front of them and behind them. They cried out to the LORD, and the priests blew the trumpets.
Then the men of Judah raised the battle cry. And when the men of Judah raised the battle cry, God struck down Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah.
The Israelites fled before Judah, and God handed them over to them.
Abijah and his people struck them with a great slaughter, and five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fell slain.
So the Israelites were subdued at that time, and the people of Judah prevailed, because they relied on the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Abijah pursued Jeroboam and took cities from him: Bethel and its villages, Jeshanah and its villages, and Ephrain and its villages.
Jeroboam did not regain his strength in the days of Abijah. The LORD struck him down, and he died.
But Abijah grew strong. He married fourteen wives, and he fathered twenty-two sons and sixteen daughters.
The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways and his sayings, are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Abijah slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in the City of David. And his son Asa became king in his place. In his days the land had peace for ten years.
Asa did what was good and right in the eyes of the LORD his God.
He removed the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles.
He commanded Judah to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and to carry out the law and the command.
He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom had peace under him.
He built fortified cities in Judah, for the land had peace. There was no war against him in those years, because the LORD had given him rest.

He said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround them with walls and towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, because we have sought the LORD our God. We sought him, and he has given us rest on every side." So they built and prospered.
Asa had an army of 300,000 from Judah, carrying large shields and spears, and 280,000 from Benjamin, carrying shields and drawing bows. All these were mighty warriors.
Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a million and three hundred chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.
Asa went out to meet him, and they drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

Asa called to the LORD his God and said, "LORD, there is no one like you to help the powerless against the mighty. Help us, LORD our God, for we rely on you, and in your name we have come against this multitude. LORD, you are our God. Do not let mere mortals prevail against you."
So the LORD struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

Asa and the people with him pursued them as far as Gerar. So many Cushites fell that they could not recover, for they were shattered before the LORD and his army. The people of Judah carried off a very great amount of plunder.
They attacked all the cities around Gerar, for the terror of the LORD had fallen on them. They plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.
They also attacked the tents of the herdsmen and carried off sheep and goats in abundance, and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
The Spirit of God came on Azariah son of Oded.

He went out to meet Asa and said to him, "Listen to me, Asa and all Judah and Benjamin. The LORD is with you when you are with him. If you seek him, he will be found by you, but if you abandon him, he will abandon you.
For a long time Israel was without the true God, without a priest to teach, and without instruction.
But in their distress they turned to the LORD, the God of Israel. They sought him, and he was found by them.
In those times there was no peace for anyone who went out or came in, for great turmoil afflicted all the inhabitants of the lands.
They were crushed, nation against nation and city against city, for God troubled them with every kind of distress.
But as for you, be strong and do not lose heart, for your work will be rewarded."

When Asa heard these words and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he took courage. He removed the detestable idols from the whole land of Judah and Benjamin and from the cities he had captured in the hill country of Ephraim. And he restored the altar of the LORD that was in front of the porch of the house of the LORD.
He gathered all Judah and Benjamin, and those from Ephraim, Manasseh and Simeon who were living among them, for many had deserted to him from Israel when they saw that the LORD his God was with him.
They gathered in Jerusalem in the third month of the fifteenth year of Asa's reign.
On that day they sacrificed to the LORD, from the plunder they had brought, seven hundred cattle and seven thousand sheep and goats.
They entered into a covenant to seek the LORD, the God of their ancestors, with all their heart and with all their soul.
Anyone who would not seek the LORD, the God of Israel, was to be put to death, whether small or great, man or woman.
They swore an oath to the LORD with a loud voice, with shouting, and with trumpets and rams' horns.
All Judah rejoiced over the oath, for they had sworn with all their heart and sought him with all their desire, and he was found by them. So the LORD gave them rest on every side.
King Asa even removed Maacah, his mother, from being queen mother, because she had made an obscene image for Asherah. Asa cut down her obscene image, crushed it and burned it in the Kidron Valley.
But the high places were not taken away from Israel. Yet Asa's heart was fully devoted all his days.
He brought into the house of God the things his father had dedicated and the things he himself had dedicated: silver, gold and utensils.
There was no more war until the thirty-fifth year of Asa's reign.
In the thirty-sixth year of Asa's reign, Baasha king of Israel came up against Judah and fortified Ramah, to prevent anyone from going out or coming in to Asa king of Judah.
Then Asa brought out silver and gold from the treasuries of the house of the LORD and of the king's house and sent them to Ben-hadad king of Aram, who lived in Damascus, saying,

"There is a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, so that he will withdraw from me."
Ben-hadad listened to King Asa and sent the commanders of his armies against the cities of Israel. They struck Ijon, Dan, Abel-maim and all the storehouses in the cities of Naphtali.
When Baasha heard of it, he stopped fortifying Ramah and gave up his work.
Then King Asa took all Judah, and they carried away the stones and timber of Ramah, with which Baasha had been building. With them he fortified Geba and Mizpah.

At that time Hanani the seer came to Asa king of Judah and said to him, "Because you relied on the king of Aram and did not rely on the LORD your God, the army of the king of Aram has escaped from your hand.
Were not the Cushites and the Libyans a vast army, with very many chariots and horsemen? Yet because you relied on the LORD, he handed them over to you.
For the eyes of the LORD range throughout the whole earth, to show his strength for those whose hearts are fully devoted to him. You have acted foolishly in this. From now on you will have wars."
Asa was angry with the seer and put him in the stocks, for he was enraged with him over this. At that time Asa also oppressed some of the people.
The acts of Asa, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
In the thirty-ninth year of his reign Asa was diseased in his feet, and his disease became very severe. Yet even in his disease he did not seek the LORD, but only the physicians.
Asa slept with his ancestors. He died in the forty-first year of his reign.

They buried him in the tomb he had cut for himself in the City of David. They laid him on a bier filled with spices and various kinds of ointments blended by the perfumer's art, and they made a very great fire in his honor.
His son Jehoshaphat became king in his place, and he strengthened himself against Israel.
He stationed troops in all the fortified cities of Judah and placed garrisons in the land of Judah and in the cities of Ephraim that his father Asa had captured.
The LORD was with Jehoshaphat, because he walked in the earlier ways of his ancestor David. He did not seek the Baals,
but sought the God of his father and walked in his commands, and not according to the practices of Israel.
So the LORD established the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brought gifts to Jehoshaphat, and he had great riches and honor.
His heart was bold in the ways of the LORD, and he also removed the high places and the Asherah poles from Judah.
In the third year of his reign he sent his officials Ben-hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel and Micaiah to teach in the cities of Judah.
With them were the Levites Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah and Tob-adonijah, the Levites, and with them Elishama and Jehoram the priests.
They taught in Judah, having with them the book of the law of the LORD. They went around through all the cities of Judah and taught among the people.
The terror of the LORD fell on all the kingdoms of the lands around Judah, and they did not make war against Jehoshaphat.
Some of the Philistines brought Jehoshaphat gifts and silver as tribute, and the Arabs brought him flocks: 7,700 rams and 7,700 male goats.
Jehoshaphat grew steadily greater, and he built fortresses and storage cities in Judah.
He carried out many works in the cities of Judah, and he had soldiers, mighty warriors, in Jerusalem.
This was their enrollment by their ancestral families. From Judah, the commanders of thousands: Adnah the commander, and with him 300,000 mighty warriors;
next to him Jehohanan the commander, and with him 280,000;
next to him Amasiah son of Zichri, who volunteered for the service of the LORD, and with him 200,000 mighty warriors.
From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty warrior, and with him 200,000 armed with bow and shield;
next to him Jehozabad, and with him 180,000 equipped for war.
These were the men who served the king, besides those the king had placed in the fortified cities throughout Judah.
Jehoshaphat had great riches and honor, and he made a marriage alliance with Ahab.
Some years later he went down to Ahab in Samaria. Ahab slaughtered sheep and cattle in abundance for him and for the people who were with him, and he persuaded him to go up against Ramoth-gilead.
Ahab king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, "Will you go with me to Ramoth-gilead?" He answered him, "I am as you are, my people as your people. We will be with you in the battle."
But Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel, "Please inquire first for the word of the LORD."

So the king of Israel gathered the prophets, four hundred men, and said to them, "Shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" They said, "Go up, for God will hand it over to the king."
But Jehoshaphat said, "Is there no other prophet of the LORD here, so that we can inquire of him?"

The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "There is still one man through whom we can inquire of the LORD, but I hate him, because he never prophesies anything good about me, but always disaster. He is Micaiah son of Imla." Jehoshaphat said, "The king should not say that."
So the king of Israel called an officer and said, "Bring Micaiah son of Imla quickly."

The king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah were sitting each on his throne, dressed in their robes. They were sitting at the threshing floor at the entrance of the gate of Samaria, and all the prophets were prophesying before them.
Zedekiah son of Chenaanah had made himself horns of iron, and he said, "This is what the LORD says: With these you will gore the Arameans until they are destroyed."
All the prophets were prophesying the same, saying, "Go up to Ramoth-gilead and succeed. The LORD will hand it over to the king."

The messenger who had gone to summon Micaiah said to him, "Look, the prophets with one voice are speaking favorably to the king. Please let your word be like that of one of them, and speak favorably."
But Micaiah said, "As the LORD lives, whatever my God says, that is what I will speak."
When he came to the king, the king said to him, "Micah, shall we go to battle against Ramoth-gilead, or shall I hold back?" He said, "Go up and succeed. They will be handed over to you."
But the king said to him, "How many times must I make you swear to tell me nothing but the truth in the name of the LORD?"
Then he said, "I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, like sheep that have no shepherd. And the LORD said, 'These have no master. Let each of them go home in peace.'"
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "Didn't I tell you he would not prophesy anything good about me, only disaster?"
Micaiah said, "Therefore hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on his throne, with the whole host of heaven standing on his right and on his left.
And the LORD said, 'Who will entice Ahab king of Israel to go up and fall at Ramoth-gilead?' One said one thing, and another said another.
Then a spirit came forward and stood before the LORD and said, 'I will entice him.' The LORD said to him, 'How?'
He said, 'I will go out and be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.' The LORD said, 'You will entice him, and you will succeed. Go and do it.'
So now, the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these prophets of yours. The LORD has pronounced disaster against you."
Then Zedekiah son of Chenaanah came up and struck Micaiah on the cheek and said, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when he left me to speak to you?"
Micaiah said, "You will see on the day when you go into an inner room to hide."
The king of Israel said, "Take Micaiah and bring him back to Amon the governor of the city and to Joash the king's son,
and say, 'This is what the king says: Put this fellow in prison and feed him on scant bread and water until I come back safely.'"
Micaiah said, "If you ever come back safely, the LORD has not spoken through me." And he said, "Listen, all you peoples!"
So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat king of Judah went up to Ramoth-gilead.
The king of Israel said to Jehoshaphat, "I will disguise myself and go into battle, but you wear your robes." So the king of Israel disguised himself, and they went into battle.
Now the king of Aram had commanded his chariot commanders, "Do not fight with anyone, small or great, except the king of Israel alone."

When the chariot commanders saw Jehoshaphat, they said, "That is the king of Israel," and they turned to fight against him. But Jehoshaphat cried out, and the LORD helped him. God drew them away from him.
When the chariot commanders saw that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back from pursuing him.
But a man drew his bow at random and struck the king of Israel between the joints of his armor. He said to his chariot driver, "Turn around and get me out of the fighting, for I am wounded."
The battle grew fierce that day, and the king of Israel propped himself up in his chariot facing the Arameans until evening. At sunset he died.
Jehoshaphat king of Judah returned safely to his house in Jerusalem.
Jehu son of Hanani the seer went out to meet him and said to King Jehoshaphat, "Should you help the wicked and love those who hate the LORD? Because of this, wrath from the LORD is on you.
Nevertheless, some good is found in you, for you have removed the Asherah poles from the land and have set your heart on seeking God."
Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem. Then he went out again among the people, from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brought them back to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
He appointed judges in the land, in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.
He said to the judges, "Consider what you are doing, for you do not judge for human beings but for the LORD. He is with you when you give judgment.
Now let the fear of the LORD be on you. Be careful what you do, for with the LORD our God there is no injustice, no partiality and no taking of bribes."

In Jerusalem, too, Jehoshaphat appointed some of the Levites and the priests and of the heads of the ancestral families of Israel, to give judgment for the LORD and to settle disputes. Then they returned to Jerusalem.
He commanded them: "This is how you must act: in the fear of the LORD, faithfully and with a whole heart.

In every dispute that comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities, whether it concerns bloodshed or law and command, decrees and rulings, you must warn them so that they do not incur guilt before the LORD, and wrath come on you and on your brothers. Do this, and you will not incur guilt.

Look, Amariah the chief priest is over you in every matter of the LORD, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, the leader of the house of Judah, in every matter of the king. The Levites will serve you as officials. Be strong and act, and may the LORD be with those who do good."
After this the Moabites and the Ammonites, and with them some of the Ammonites, came to make war against Jehoshaphat.
Messengers came and told Jehoshaphat, "A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea, from Aram. They are already in Hazazon-tamar," that is, En-gedi.
Jehoshaphat was afraid, and he set himself to seek the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah.
Judah gathered to seek help from the LORD. From all the cities of Judah they came to seek the LORD.
Jehoshaphat stood in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in the house of the LORD, in front of the new courtyard,
and said, "LORD, God of our ancestors, are you not God in heaven? You rule over all the kingdoms of the nations. Power and might are in your hand, and no one can stand against you.
Did you not, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it forever to the descendants of Abraham your friend?
They have lived in it and have built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying,

'If disaster comes on us, sword, judgment, plague or famine, we will stand before this house and before you, for your name is in this house, and we will cry out to you in our distress, and you will hear and save us.'
Now here are the Ammonites, Moab and Mount Seir, whom you did not let Israel invade when they came from the land of Egypt. They turned away from them and did not destroy them.
Look how they are repaying us by coming to drive us out of your possession, which you gave us to inherit.
Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no strength to face this great multitude that is coming against us. We do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you."
All Judah was standing before the LORD, with their little ones, their wives and their children.
Then the Spirit of the LORD came on Jahaziel son of Zechariah, son of Benaiah, son of Jeiel, son of Mattaniah, a Levite of the descendants of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly.

He said, "Listen, all Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and King Jehoshaphat. This is what the LORD says to you: Do not be afraid or dismayed because of this great multitude, for the battle is not yours but God's.
Tomorrow go down against them. They will be coming up by the Ascent of Ziz, and you will find them at the end of the valley, facing the wilderness of Jeruel.

You will not need to fight in this battle. Take your positions, stand still and see the deliverance the LORD will give you, Judah and Jerusalem. Do not be afraid or dismayed. Tomorrow go out to face them, and the LORD will be with you."
Jehoshaphat bowed down with his face to the ground, and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before the LORD to worship the LORD.
Then the Levites, from the Kohathites and the Korahites, stood up to praise the LORD, the God of Israel, with a very loud voice.

Early in the morning they went out to the wilderness of Tekoa. As they went out, Jehoshaphat stood and said, "Listen to me, Judah and you inhabitants of Jerusalem. Believe in the LORD your God, and you will be established. Believe his prophets, and you will succeed."

After consulting with the people, he appointed singers to the LORD, and those who praised him in holy splendor, to go out ahead of the army, saying, "Give thanks to the LORD, for his faithful love endures forever."
As soon as they began to sing and praise, the LORD set ambushes against the Ammonites, Moab and Mount Seir, who had come against Judah, and they were defeated.

The Ammonites and Moab rose up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to destroy them completely and wipe them out. When they had finished off the inhabitants of Seir, they turned on one another and destroyed each other.
When Judah came to the watchtower overlooking the wilderness and looked toward the multitude, there were dead bodies lying on the ground. No one had escaped.

When Jehoshaphat and his people came to take their plunder, they found among them a great amount of goods, corpses and precious things. They stripped them for themselves until they could carry no more. They spent three days taking the plunder, because there was so much.
On the fourth day they assembled in the Valley of Beracah, for there they blessed the LORD. That is why that place is called the Valley of Beracah to this day.
Then all the men of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat at their head, returned to Jerusalem with joy, for the LORD had given them joy over their enemies.
They came to Jerusalem with harps, lyres and trumpets, to the house of the LORD.
The fear of God fell on all the kingdoms of the lands when they heard that the LORD had fought against the enemies of Israel.
So the kingdom of Jehoshaphat was at peace, for his God gave him rest on every side.
Jehoshaphat reigned over Judah. He was thirty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Azubah daughter of Shilhi.
He walked in the way of his father Asa and did not turn aside from it, doing what was right in the eyes of the LORD.
But the high places were not taken away, and the people had not yet set their hearts on the God of their ancestors.
The rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, from first to last, are written in the records of Jehu son of Hanani, which are included in the book of the kings of Israel.
After this Jehoshaphat king of Judah allied himself with Ahaziah king of Israel, who acted wickedly.
He joined with him in building ships to go to Tarshish, and they built the ships at Ezion-geber.

Then Eliezer son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesied against Jehoshaphat, saying, "Because you have allied yourself with Ahaziah, the LORD has broken down what you have made." The ships were wrecked and were not able to go to Tarshish.
Jehoshaphat slept with his ancestors and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. And his son Jehoram became king in his place.
He had brothers, sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael and Shephatiah. All these were sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel.
Their father gave them many gifts of silver, gold and precious things, along with fortified cities in Judah, but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
When Jehoram had taken over his father's kingdom and had made himself strong, he killed all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the leaders of Israel.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
He walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as the house of Ahab had done, for a daughter of Ahab was his wife. He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
But the LORD was not willing to destroy the house of David, because of the covenant he had made with David, and since he had promised to give a lamp to him and to his descendants forever.
In his days Edom rebelled against Judah's rule and set up a king of their own.
So Jehoram crossed over with his commanders, and all his chariots with him. He rose by night and struck the Edomites who had surrounded him and the commanders of the chariots.
So Edom has been in rebellion against Judah's rule to this day. Libnah also rebelled against his rule at that time, because he had abandoned the LORD, the God of his ancestors.
He also made high places in the hills of Judah, and he led the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful and led Judah astray.

A letter came to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, "This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: Because you have not walked in the ways of your father Jehoshaphat or in the ways of Asa king of Judah,

but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have led Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to be unfaithful, as the house of Ahab did, and have also killed your brothers, your own father's family, who were better than you,
the LORD is about to strike your people, your sons, your wives and all your possessions with a great blow.
And you yourself will suffer severe sickness, a disease of your bowels, until your bowels come out because of the disease, day after day."
The LORD stirred up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines and of the Arabs who live near the Cushites.
They came up against Judah, broke into it and carried off all the possessions found in the king's house, and also his sons and his wives. Not a son was left to him except Jehoahaz, his youngest son.
After all this the LORD struck him in his bowels with an incurable disease.
In the course of time, at the end of two years, his bowels came out because of his disease, and he died in great pain. His people made no fire in his honor like the fire made for his ancestors.

He was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He passed away, and no one was sorry. They buried him in the City of David, but not in the tombs of the kings.

The inhabitants of Jerusalem made Ahaziah, his youngest son, king in his place, for the raiding band that came with the Arabs to the camp had killed all the older sons. So Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah became king.
Ahaziah was forty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned one year in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Athaliah daughter of Omri.
He too walked in the ways of the house of Ahab, for his mother was his counselor in doing evil.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, as the house of Ahab had done, for after his father's death they were his counselors, to his ruin.
He also followed their advice and went with Jehoram son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.

He went back to Jezreel to recover from the wounds they had given him at Ramah, when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. And Azariah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to see Jehoram son of Ahab, because he was sick.
Ahaziah's downfall came from God, through his visit to Joram. When he arrived, he went out with Jehoram to meet Jehu son of Nimshi, whom the LORD had anointed to cut off the house of Ahab.
While Jehu was executing judgment on the house of Ahab, he found the leaders of Judah and the sons of Ahaziah's brothers, who were serving Ahaziah, and he killed them.

He searched for Ahaziah, and they captured him while he was hiding in Samaria. They brought him to Jehu and put him to death. They buried him, for they said, "He is the grandson of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart." So there was no one in the house of Ahaziah strong enough to rule the kingdom.
When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mother, saw that her son was dead, she set out to destroy the whole royal family of the house of Judah.

But Jehoshabeath, the king's daughter, took Joash son of Ahaziah and stole him away from among the king's sons who were being put to death. She put him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of King Jehoram and the wife of Jehoiada the priest, since she was Ahaziah's sister, hid him from Athaliah, and Athaliah did not put him to death.
He remained with them, hidden in the house of God, for six years, while Athaliah reigned over the land.

In the seventh year Jehoiada took courage and made a covenant with the commanders of hundreds: Azariah son of Jeroham, Ishmael son of Jehohanan, Azariah son of Obed, Maaseiah son of Adaiah and Elishaphat son of Zichri.
They went around through Judah and gathered the Levites from all the cities of Judah, and the heads of the ancestral families of Israel, and they came to Jerusalem.
The whole assembly made a covenant with the king in the house of God. Jehoiada said to them, "Here is the king's son! He shall reign, as the LORD promised concerning the sons of David.
This is what you are to do. A third of you, priests and Levites who come on duty on the Sabbath, are to be gatekeepers at the thresholds,
a third are to be at the king's palace, and a third at the Foundation Gate, and all the people are to be in the courtyards of the house of the LORD.
No one is to enter the house of the LORD except the priests and those of the Levites who minister. They may enter, for they are holy, but all the people are to keep the charge of the LORD.
The Levites are to surround the king on every side, each man with his weapons in his hand. Anyone who enters the house is to be put to death. Stay with the king wherever he goes."

The Levites and all Judah did everything Jehoiada the priest commanded. Each took his men, those coming on duty on the Sabbath together with those going off duty on the Sabbath, for Jehoiada the priest had not dismissed the divisions.
Jehoiada the priest gave the commanders of hundreds the spears, the small shields and the quivers that had belonged to King David, which were in the house of God.
He stationed all the people, each man with his weapon in his hand, from the south side of the house to the north side, by the altar and the house, all around the king.
Then they brought out the king's son and put the crown on him and gave him the statutes, and they made him king. Jehoiada and his sons anointed him, and they said, "Long live the king!"
When Athaliah heard the noise of the people running and praising the king, she came to the people at the house of the LORD.

She looked, and there was the king, standing by his pillar at the entrance. The commanders and the trumpeters were beside the king, and all the people of the land were rejoicing and blowing trumpets, and the singers with their musical instruments were leading the praise. Athaliah tore her clothes and cried out, "Treason! Treason!"

Jehoiada the priest brought out the commanders of hundreds, who were in charge of the army, and said to them, "Bring her out between the ranks, and put to death with the sword anyone who follows her." For the priest had said, "Do not put her to death in the house of the LORD."
So they seized her, and she went into the entrance of the Horse Gate of the king's palace, and there they put her to death.
Jehoiada made a covenant between himself and all the people and the king, that they would be the LORD's people.
Then all the people went to the temple of Baal and tore it down. They smashed its altars and its images, and they killed Mattan the priest of Baal in front of the altars.

Jehoiada put the oversight of the house of the LORD into the hands of the Levitical priests, whom David had organized in divisions over the house of the LORD, to offer the burnt offerings of the LORD as it is written in the Law of Moses, with rejoicing and singing, as David had directed.
He stationed the gatekeepers at the gates of the house of the LORD, so that no one who was unclean in any way could enter.

He took the commanders of hundreds, the nobles, the rulers of the people and all the people of the land, and he brought the king down from the house of the LORD. They went through the Upper Gate to the king's palace, and they seated the king on the royal throne.
All the people of the land rejoiced, and the city was quiet, for they had put Athaliah to death with the sword.
Joash was seven years old when he became king, and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Zibiah, from Beersheba.
Joash did what was right in the eyes of the LORD all the days of Jehoiada the priest.
Jehoiada took two wives for him, and he fathered sons and daughters.
Some time later Joash set his heart on restoring the house of the LORD.

He gathered the priests and the Levites and said to them, "Go out to the cities of Judah and collect money from all Israel to repair the house of your God year by year. Do it quickly." But the Levites did not act quickly.

So the king summoned Jehoiada the chief priest and said to him, "Why have you not required the Levites to bring in from Judah and Jerusalem the tax that Moses the servant of the LORD and the assembly of Israel imposed, for the tent of the testimony?"
For the sons of that wicked woman Athaliah had broken into the house of God and had even used all the holy things of the house of the LORD for the Baals.
At the king's command they made a chest and set it outside, at the gate of the house of the LORD.
A proclamation was issued in Judah and Jerusalem to bring to the LORD the tax that Moses the servant of God had imposed on Israel in the wilderness.
All the officials and all the people rejoiced, and they brought their money and threw it into the chest until it was full.

Whenever the chest was brought by the Levites to the king's officials, and they saw that there was a large amount of money, the king's secretary and the officer of the chief priest would come and empty the chest, then carry it back to its place. They did this day after day and collected a great deal of money.

The king and Jehoiada gave it to those who did the work of the service of the house of the LORD. They hired stonecutters and carpenters to restore the house of the LORD, and also workers in iron and bronze to repair the house of the LORD.
The workmen did their work, and the repairs went forward in their hands. They restored the house of God to its proper design and strengthened it.

When they had finished, they brought the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, and with it utensils were made for the house of the LORD: utensils for the service and for the burnt offerings, dishes, and articles of gold and silver. They offered burnt offerings in the house of the LORD continually, all the days of Jehoiada.
Jehoiada grew old and full of days, and he died. He was 130 years old when he died.
They buried him in the City of David with the kings, because he had done good in Israel, for God and for his house.
After the death of Jehoiada the officials of Judah came and bowed down to the king. Then the king listened to them.
They abandoned the house of the LORD, the God of their ancestors, and served the Asherah poles and the idols. Because of this guilt of theirs, wrath came on Judah and Jerusalem.
Yet he sent prophets among them to bring them back to the LORD. They warned them, but they would not listen.

Then the Spirit of God clothed Zechariah son of Jehoiada the priest. He stood up above the people and said to them, "This is what God says: Why do you transgress the commands of the LORD, so that you cannot prosper? Because you have abandoned the LORD, he has abandoned you."
But they conspired against him, and at the king's command they stoned him to death in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.
King Joash did not remember the faithful love that Zechariah's father Jehoiada had shown him, but killed his son. As he was dying, he said, "May the LORD see and call you to account!"

At the turn of the year the army of Aram came up against Joash. They came to Judah and Jerusalem and destroyed all the leaders of the people from among the people, and they sent all their plunder to the king of Damascus.

Although the army of Aram came with only a few men, the LORD handed over to them a very great army, because Judah had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors. So they executed judgment on Joash.

When they withdrew from him, they left him severely wounded. His servants conspired against him because of the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and they killed him on his bed, and he died. They buried him in the City of David, but they did not bury him in the tombs of the kings.
These were the ones who conspired against him: Zabad son of Shimeath the Ammonite woman, and Jehozabad son of Shimrith the Moabite woman.
As for his sons, the many oracles against him, and the rebuilding of the house of God, they are written in the commentary on the book of the kings. And his son Amaziah became king in his place.
Amaziah was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jehoaddan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not with a whole heart.
As soon as the kingdom was firmly in his hand, he killed his officials who had struck down his father the king.

But he did not put their sons to death, in keeping with what is written in the Law, in the book of Moses, where the LORD commanded, "Fathers are not to die for their sons, and sons are not to die for their fathers. Each is to die for his own sin."

Amaziah gathered Judah and organized them by ancestral families, under commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds, for all Judah and Benjamin. He mustered those twenty years old and upward, and he found that there were three hundred thousand chosen men fit for war, able to handle spear and large shield.
He also hired a hundred thousand mighty warriors from Israel for a hundred talents of silver.
But a man of God came to him and said, "O king, do not let the army of Israel go with you, for the LORD is not with Israel, with any of the people of Ephraim.
Even if you go and fight bravely in battle, God will make you fall before the enemy, for God has the power to help and to make fall."
Amaziah said to the man of God, "But what shall we do about the hundred talents I have given to the troops of Israel?" The man of God said, "The LORD is able to give you much more than this."
So Amaziah discharged the troops that had come to him from Ephraim and sent them home. They were very angry with Judah, and they returned home in fierce anger.
Amaziah took courage and led out his people. He went to the Valley of Salt and struck down ten thousand of the people of Seir.
The people of Judah captured another ten thousand alive. They brought them to the top of the Rock and threw them down from the top of the Rock, and they were all dashed to pieces.

Meanwhile the troops that Amaziah had sent back, so that they did not go with him to battle, raided the cities of Judah from Samaria to Beth-horon. They struck down three thousand of their people and took a great amount of plunder.
After Amaziah came back from striking down the Edomites, he brought the gods of the people of Seir and set them up as his own gods. He bowed down before them and burned incense to them.
The anger of the LORD burned against Amaziah, and he sent a prophet to him, who said to him, "Why have you sought the gods of a people who could not rescue their own people from your hand?"

While he was speaking to him, the king said to him, "Have we made you a counselor to the king? Stop! Why should you be struck down?" So the prophet stopped, but he said, "I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this and have not listened to my counsel."
Then Amaziah king of Judah took counsel and sent messengers to Joash son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, "Come, let us face each other."

Joash king of Israel sent this reply to Amaziah king of Judah: "A thornbush in Lebanon sent word to a cedar in Lebanon, 'Give your daughter to my son as his wife.' Then a wild animal in Lebanon passed by and trampled the thornbush.
You tell yourself that you have struck down Edom, and your heart has made you proud, so that you seek glory. Now stay at home. Why stir up trouble, so that you fall, you and Judah with you?"
But Amaziah would not listen, for this was from God, in order to hand them over, because they had sought the gods of Edom.
So Joash king of Israel went up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah faced each other at Beth-shemesh, which belongs to Judah.
Judah was defeated by Israel, and every man fled to his home.

Joash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah, son of Joash son of Jehoahaz, at Beth-shemesh. He brought him to Jerusalem and broke down the wall of Jerusalem from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate, four hundred cubits.

He took all the gold and silver and all the articles that were found in the house of God in the care of Obed-edom, and the treasuries of the king's palace, as well as hostages, and he returned to Samaria.
Amaziah son of Joash king of Judah lived fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel.
The rest of the acts of Amaziah, from first to last, are they not written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel?
From the time that Amaziah turned away from following the LORD, they formed a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he fled to Lachish. But they sent men after him to Lachish and killed him there.
They brought him back on horses and buried him with his ancestors in the city of Judah.
Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in place of his father Amaziah.
He was the one who rebuilt Eloth and restored it to Judah, after the king slept with his ancestors.
Uzziah was sixteen years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jecoliah, from Jerusalem.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Amaziah had done.
He set himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who had understanding in the visions of God. As long as he sought the LORD, God made him prosper.
He went out and made war against the Philistines and broke down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh and the wall of Ashdod. He built cities near Ashdod and elsewhere among the Philistines.
God helped him against the Philistines, and against the Arabs who lived in Gur-baal, and the Meunites.
The Ammonites paid tribute to Uzziah, and his fame spread as far as the border of Egypt, for he became very strong.
Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem at the Corner Gate, at the Valley Gate and at the Angle, and he fortified them.

He built towers in the wilderness and dug many cisterns, for he had much livestock in the Shephelah and in the plain. He had farmers and vinedressers in the hills and in the fertile lands, for he loved the soil.

Uzziah had an army of fighting men who went out to war by divisions, according to the number of their muster made by Jeiel the secretary and Maaseiah the officer, under the direction of Hananiah, one of the king's commanders.
The total number of the heads of ancestral families, mighty warriors, was 2,600.
Under their command was an army of 307,500, who made war with mighty power to help the king against the enemy.
Uzziah provided for the whole army shields, spears, helmets, coats of armor, bows and sling stones.

In Jerusalem he made devices designed by skilled men, to be on the towers and on the corners, for shooting arrows and great stones. His fame spread far, for he was marvelously helped until he became strong.
But when he had become strong, his heart grew proud, to his own ruin. He was unfaithful to the LORD his God, and he entered the temple of the LORD to burn incense on the altar of incense.
Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him eighty priests of the LORD, men of courage.

They stood against King Uzziah and said to him, "It is not for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to the LORD, but for the priests, the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have been unfaithful, and it will bring you no honor from the LORD God."

Uzziah was furious. He had a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he was raging at the priests, a skin disease broke out on his forehead, in front of the priests in the house of the LORD, beside the altar of incense.

When Azariah the chief priest and all the priests looked at him, there he was with a skin disease on his forehead. They hurried him out of there, and he himself hastened to go out, because the LORD had struck him.

King Uzziah had a skin disease until the day of his death. He lived in a separate house, with his skin disease, for he was excluded from the house of the LORD. His son Jotham was in charge of the palace, governing the people of the land.
The rest of the acts of Uzziah, from first to last, Isaiah the prophet son of Amoz wrote down.

Uzziah slept with his ancestors, and they buried him with his ancestors in the burial field that belonged to the kings, for they said, "He has a skin disease." And his son Jotham became king in his place.
Jotham was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Jerushah daughter of Zadok.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his father Uzziah had done, except that he did not enter the temple of the LORD. But the people still acted corruptly.
He built the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD, and he did much building on the wall of Ophel.
He built cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the wooded areas he built fortresses and towers.

He fought with the king of the Ammonites and prevailed over them. That year the Ammonites gave him a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand kors of wheat and ten thousand of barley. The Ammonites paid him the same in the second and the third years.
Jotham became strong, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God.
The rest of the acts of Jotham, all his wars and his ways, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Jotham slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in the City of David. And his son Ahaz became king in his place.
Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD, as his ancestor David had done.
He walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, and he even made cast images for the Baals.
He burned incense in the Valley of Ben-hinnom and burned his sons in the fire, following the detestable practices of the nations whom the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.
He sacrificed and burned incense at the high places, on the hills and under every green tree.

So the LORD his God handed him over to the king of Aram. They defeated him and took many of his people captive and brought them to Damascus. He was also handed over to the king of Israel, who struck him with a great slaughter.
Pekah son of Remaliah killed 120,000 in Judah in one day, all of them valiant men, because they had abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Zichri, a mighty warrior of Ephraim, killed Maaseiah the king's son, Azrikam the official in charge of the palace, and Elkanah, who was second to the king.
The Israelites took captive from their relatives two hundred thousand women, sons and daughters. They also took a great amount of plunder from them, and they brought the plunder to Samaria.

But a prophet of the LORD was there, whose name was Oded. He went out to meet the army as it came to Samaria and said to them, "Look, because the LORD, the God of your ancestors, was angry with Judah, he handed them over to you. But you have killed them in a rage that has reached up to heaven.
And now you intend to make the people of Judah and Jerusalem your male and female slaves. But are you yourselves not guilty of sins against the LORD your God?
Now listen to me, and send back the captives you have taken from your relatives, for the burning anger of the LORD is on you."

Then some of the leaders of the Ephraimites, Azariah son of Johanan, Berechiah son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah son of Shallum and Amasa son of Hadlai, stood up against those who were coming back from the campaign.

They said to them, "You must not bring the captives here, for you intend to bring guilt on us before the LORD, adding to our sins and our guilt. Our guilt is already great, and there is burning anger against Israel."
So the armed men left the captives and the plunder before the officials and the whole assembly.

Then the men who had been named got up and took charge of the captives. With the plunder they clothed all who were naked among them. They gave them clothes and sandals, gave them food and drink, and anointed them with oil. They put all who were weak on donkeys and brought them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their relatives. Then they returned to Samaria.
At that time King Ahaz sent to the kings of Assyria for help.
Again the Edomites had come and attacked Judah and carried away captives.

The Philistines had raided the cities of the Shephelah and the Negev of Judah. They had captured Beth-shemesh, Aijalon and Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages and Gimzo with its villages, and they settled there.
For the LORD humbled Judah because of Ahaz king of Israel, for he had let Judah run wild and had been very unfaithful to the LORD.
Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria came against him and oppressed him instead of strengthening him.
For Ahaz took a share from the house of the LORD, from the king's house and from the officials, and gave it to the king of Assyria, but it did not help him.
In the time of his distress he became even more unfaithful to the LORD, this same King Ahaz.

He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus, who had defeated him, for he said, "Because the gods of the kings of Aram help them, I will sacrifice to them so that they will help me." But they were the ruin of him and of all Israel.

Ahaz gathered together the utensils of the house of God and cut the utensils of the house of God in pieces. He shut the doors of the house of the LORD, and he made himself altars on every street corner in Jerusalem.
In every city of Judah he made high places to burn incense to other gods, and he provoked the LORD, the God of his ancestors, to anger.
The rest of his acts and all his ways, from first to last, are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel.
Ahaz slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city, in Jerusalem, but they did not bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel. And his son Hezekiah became king in his place.
Hezekiah became king when he was twenty-five years old, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Abijah daughter of Zechariah.
He did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, just as his ancestor David had done.
In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opened the doors of the house of the LORD and repaired them.
He brought in the priests and the Levites and gathered them in the square on the east.
He said to them, "Listen to me, Levites! Consecrate yourselves now, and consecrate the house of the LORD, the God of your ancestors. Carry the filth out of the holy place.

For our ancestors were unfaithful and did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD our God. They abandoned him. They turned their faces away from the dwelling place of the LORD and turned their backs on it.
They also shut the doors of the porch and put out the lamps. They did not burn incense or offer burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel.
So the wrath of the LORD came on Judah and Jerusalem, and he made them an object of terror, horror and hissing, as you see with your own eyes.
Look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons, our daughters and our wives are in captivity because of this.
Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with the LORD, the God of Israel, so that his burning anger may turn away from us.
My sons, do not be negligent now, for the LORD has chosen you to stand before him and serve him, and to be his ministers and burn incense."

Then the Levites set to work: Mahath son of Amasai and Joel son of Azariah, of the descendants of Kohath; of the descendants of Merari, Kish son of Abdi and Azariah son of Jehallelel; of the Gershonites, Joah son of Zimmah and Eden son of Joah;
of the descendants of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeiel; of the descendants of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah;
of the descendants of Heman, Jehiel and Shimei; and of the descendants of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel.
They gathered their brothers and consecrated themselves, and they came, as the king had commanded by the words of the LORD, to purify the house of the LORD.

The priests went into the inner part of the house of the LORD to purify it, and they brought out into the courtyard of the house of the LORD all the unclean things they found in the temple of the LORD. The Levites took them and carried them out to the Kidron Valley.

They began the consecration on the first day of the first month, and on the eighth day of the month they reached the porch of the LORD. They consecrated the house of the LORD for eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finished.

Then they went in to King Hezekiah and said, "We have purified the whole house of the LORD, the altar of burnt offering with all its utensils, and the table for the rows of bread with all its utensils.
All the utensils that King Ahaz discarded during his reign, in his unfaithfulness, we have prepared and consecrated. They are now in front of the altar of the LORD."
Early the next morning King Hezekiah gathered the officials of the city and went up to the house of the LORD.

They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs and seven male goats as a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary and for Judah. He told the priests, the descendants of Aaron, to offer them on the altar of the LORD.

So they slaughtered the bulls, and the priests received the blood and splashed it on the altar. They slaughtered the rams and splashed the blood on the altar. They slaughtered the lambs and splashed the blood on the altar.
Then they brought the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly, and they laid their hands on them.
The priests slaughtered them and made a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel, for the king had ordered the burnt offering and the sin offering for all Israel.

He stationed the Levites in the house of the LORD with cymbals, harps and lyres, as commanded by David, by Gad the king's seer and by Nathan the prophet, for the command came from the LORD through his prophets.
The Levites stood with the instruments of David, and the priests with the trumpets.

Then Hezekiah gave the order to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering began, the song of the LORD began too, with the trumpets, accompanied by the instruments of David king of Israel.
The whole assembly was bowing down, the singers were singing and the trumpeters were sounding. All this continued until the burnt offering was finished.
When the offering was finished, the king and all who were present with him knelt down and worshiped.
King Hezekiah and the officials told the Levites to praise the LORD with the words of David and of Asaph the seer. So they sang praises with joy, and they bowed down and worshiped.

Then Hezekiah said, "Now you have consecrated yourselves to the LORD. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings to the house of the LORD." So the assembly brought sacrifices and thank offerings, and all who were willing in heart brought burnt offerings.
The number of the burnt offerings that the assembly brought was seventy bulls, a hundred rams and two hundred lambs. All these were for a burnt offering to the LORD.
The consecrated offerings were six hundred cattle and three thousand sheep and goats.

But the priests were too few, and they could not skin all the burnt offerings. So their relatives the Levites helped them until the work was finished and until the other priests had consecrated themselves, for the Levites had been more conscientious in consecrating themselves than the priests.
Besides, there were burnt offerings in abundance, with the fat of the fellowship offerings and with the drink offerings for the burnt offerings. So the service of the house of the LORD was restored.
Hezekiah and all the people rejoiced over what God had prepared for the people, for it had come about suddenly.

Hezekiah sent word to all Israel and Judah, and he also wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh, for them to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel.
The king and his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem had decided to keep the Passover in the second month,
for they had not been able to keep it at the proper time, because not enough priests had consecrated themselves, and the people had not gathered in Jerusalem.
The plan seemed right to the king and to the whole assembly.

So they decided to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, for the people to come to keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel, in Jerusalem, for they had not kept it in great numbers, as it is written.

The couriers went throughout all Israel and Judah with letters from the king and his officials, as the king had commanded, saying, "Israelites, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, so that he may return to those of you who are left, who have escaped from the hand of the kings of Assyria.
Do not be like your ancestors and your brothers, who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their ancestors, so that he made them an object of horror, as you see.

Now do not be stiff-necked, as your ancestors were. Submit to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever, and serve the LORD your God, so that his burning anger may turn away from you.

For if you return to the LORD, your brothers and your children will find compassion with their captors and will return to this land. For the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate, and he will not turn his face away from you if you return to him."
So the couriers went from city to city through the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, as far as Zebulun, but people laughed at them and mocked them.
Yet some men from Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem.
In Judah also the hand of God was at work, giving them one heart to carry out the command of the king and the officials, by the word of the LORD.
A large crowd gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month, a very great assembly.
They set to work and removed the altars that were in Jerusalem. They also removed all the incense altars and threw them into the Kidron Valley.

They slaughtered the Passover lamb on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites were ashamed, and they consecrated themselves and brought burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.
They took their places according to their regulations, following the Law of Moses the man of God. The priests splashed the blood that they received from the Levites.
For many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, so the Levites were in charge of slaughtering the Passover lambs for everyone who was not clean, to consecrate them to the LORD.

For most of the people, many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar and Zebulun, had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover, contrary to what is written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the LORD, who is good, provide atonement for
everyone who has set his heart on seeking God, the LORD, the God of his ancestors, even if he is not clean by the rules of purity for the holy place."
The LORD listened to Hezekiah and healed the people.

The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with great joy. The Levites and the priests praised the LORD day after day with loud instruments for the LORD.

Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed good understanding in the service of the LORD. They ate the festival meals for the seven days, offering fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors.
Then the whole assembly decided to keep the festival for another seven days, and they kept another seven days with joy.

For Hezekiah king of Judah gave the assembly a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep and goats, and the officials gave the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep and goats. And a great number of priests consecrated themselves.

The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced, together with the priests and the Levites, and the whole assembly that came from Israel, and the foreigners who came from the land of Israel and those who lived in Judah.
There was great joy in Jerusalem, for since the days of Solomon son of David king of Israel there had been nothing like this in Jerusalem.
Then the Levitical priests stood up and blessed the people. Their voice was heard, and their prayer reached his holy dwelling place in heaven.

When all this was finished, all Israel who were present went out to the cities of Judah. They smashed the standing stones, cut down the Asherah poles, and tore down the high places and the altars throughout all Judah and Benjamin, and in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they had destroyed them all. Then all the Israelites returned to their cities, each to his own property.

Hezekiah appointed the divisions of the priests and the Levites, division by division, each according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for the burnt offerings and the fellowship offerings, to minister, to give thanks and to praise in the gates of the camp of the LORD.

The king's share from his own possessions was for the burnt offerings: the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, the new moons and the appointed festivals, as it is written in the law of the LORD.
He told the people, those who lived in Jerusalem, to give the share due to the priests and the Levites, so that they could devote themselves to the law of the LORD.
As soon as the word spread, the Israelites gave in abundance the firstfruits of grain, new wine, olive oil, honey and all the produce of the field. They brought in a tithe of everything in abundance.

The people of Israel and Judah who lived in the cities of Judah also brought a tithe of cattle and sheep, and a tithe of the holy things that had been consecrated to the LORD their God, and they laid them in heaps.
In the third month they began to lay the foundations of the heaps, and they finished in the seventh month.
When Hezekiah and the officials came and saw the heaps, they blessed the LORD and his people Israel.
Hezekiah asked the priests and the Levites about the heaps.
