If I called and he answered me, I would not believe that he was listening to my voice.
For he crushes me with a storm and multiplies my wounds for no reason.
He will not let me catch my breath, but fills me with bitterness.
If it is a matter of strength, look, he is mighty! If it is a matter of justice, who can summon him?
Even if I were in the right, my own mouth would condemn me; if I were blameless, it would declare me crooked.
I am blameless. I do not care about myself; I loathe my life.
It is all one; that is why I say, 'He destroys the blameless and the wicked alike.'
When a scourge brings sudden death, he mocks at the despair of the innocent.
The earth is handed over to the wicked; he covers the faces of its judges. If it is not he, then who is it?
My days are swifter than a runner; they flee away without seeing any good.
They glide by like boats of reed, like an eagle swooping on its prey.
If I say, 'I will forget my complaint, I will change my expression and be cheerful,'
I still dread all my sufferings, for I know you will not hold me innocent.
I will be counted guilty anyway. Why then should I struggle in vain?
If I washed myself with snow water and cleansed my hands with lye,
even then you would plunge me into a pit, and my own clothes would detest me.
For he is not a man like me, that I could answer him, that we could go to court together.
There is no arbiter between us, who might lay his hand on us both.
Let him take his rod away from me, and let not dread of him terrify me.
Then I would speak without fear of him, for I am not like that in myself.
"I am sick of my life. I will give free rein to my complaint; I will speak in the bitterness of my soul.
I will say to God: Do not condemn me; let me know why you contend with me.
Does it seem good to you to oppress, to reject the work of your hands and smile on the plans of the wicked?
Do you have eyes of flesh? Do you see as a mortal sees?
Are your days like the days of a mortal, or your years like the years of a man,
that you search for my guilt and seek out my sin,
though you know that I am not guilty, and there is no one to rescue me from your hand?
Your hands shaped me and made me, all of me, and now you destroy me.
Remember that you made me like clay; will you turn me back into dust?
Did you not pour me out like milk and curdle me like cheese?
You clothed me with skin and flesh and wove me together with bones and sinews.
You gave me life and faithful love, and your care has watched over my spirit.
Yet these things you hid in your heart; I know that this was your purpose.
If I sinned, you would watch me and would not acquit me of my guilt.
If I am guilty, woe to me! And if I am in the right, I cannot lift my head, so filled with shame and looking at my misery.
And if it is lifted up, you hunt me like a lion, and again you show your wondrous power against me.
You bring new witnesses against me and increase your anger toward me; fresh troops come against me in waves.
Why then did you bring me out of the womb? I should have perished before any eye saw me.
I would have been as though I had never been, carried from the womb to the grave.
Are not my days few? Stop! Leave me alone, so that I may have a little cheer
before I go, never to return, to the land of darkness and deep darkness,
a land of gloom like the blackest night, of deep darkness and disorder, where even the light is like the blackest night."
"Should a flood of words go unanswered? Should a great talker be proved right?
Should your idle talk silence people? Should you mock, and no one put you to shame?
You say, 'My teaching is pure, and I am clean in your sight.'
But oh, that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
and tell you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know then that God is exacting from you less than your guilt deserves.
Can you find out the deep things of God? Can you reach the limits of the Almighty?
They are higher than the heavens: what can you do? They are deeper than Sheol: what can you know?
Their measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
If he passes by and imprisons someone, and calls an assembly for judgment, who can stop him?
For he knows worthless people; when he sees wickedness, will he not take note of it?
An empty-headed person will get understanding when a wild donkey's colt is born human.
If you set your heart right and spread out your hands to him,
if there is wickedness in your hand, put it far away, and do not let injustice live in your tents.
Then you will lift up your face without blemish; you will stand firm and will not fear.
For you will forget your misery; you will remember it like water that has flowed past.
Your life will be brighter than noonday; its darkness will be like the morning.
You will feel secure, because there is hope; you will look around and lie down in safety.
You will lie down, and no one will make you afraid; many will seek your favor.
But the eyes of the wicked will fail; every way of escape will be gone from them, and their only hope will be to breathe their last."
"No doubt you are the people who matter, and wisdom will die with you!
But I have understanding as well as you; I am not inferior to you. Who does not know such things as these?
I have become a laughingstock to my friends, I who called on God and he answered me. A righteous, blameless man is a laughingstock!
Those at ease have contempt for disaster; it is ready for those whose feet are slipping.
The tents of robbers are at peace, and those who provoke God are secure, those who carry their god in their hand.
But ask the animals, and they will teach you, the birds of the sky, and they will tell you;
or speak to the earth, and it will teach you, and let the fish of the sea tell you.
Which of all these does not know that the hand of the LORD has done this?
In his hand is the life of every living thing and the breath of every human being.
Does not the ear test words as the palate tastes food?
Wisdom is with the aged, and understanding comes with length of days.
With him are wisdom and strength; counsel and understanding are his.
Look, what he tears down cannot be rebuilt; when he shuts someone in, no one can open.
Look, if he holds back the waters, they dry up; if he sends them out, they overturn the land.
With him are strength and sound wisdom; the one who is misled and the one who misleads are his.
He leads counselors away stripped and makes fools of judges.
He loosens the belt of kings and ties a loincloth around their waist.
He leads priests away stripped and overthrows those long established.
He silences trusted advisers and takes away the discernment of elders.
He pours contempt on nobles and loosens the belt of the strong.
He uncovers deep things out of darkness and brings deep darkness into the light.
He makes nations great, and destroys them; he enlarges nations, and leads them away.
He takes away the understanding of the leaders of the people of the earth and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
They grope in darkness without light; he makes them stagger like a drunkard.
"Look, my eye has seen all this; my ear has heard and understood it.
What you know, I also know; I am not inferior to you.
But I would speak to the Almighty; I want to argue my case with God.
But you smear over the truth with lies; you are all worthless physicians.
If only you would keep completely silent! That would be wisdom on your part.
Hear now my argument; listen to the pleadings of my lips.
Will you speak what is false on God's behalf? Will you speak deceitfully for him?
Will you take his side? Will you argue the case for God?
Would it go well with you if he examined you? Can you deceive him as one deceives a mortal?
He will surely rebuke you if you secretly take sides.
Will not his majesty terrify you, and dread of him fall on you?
Your memorable sayings are proverbs of ashes; your defenses are defenses of clay.
Be silent before me, and let me speak, and let come on me what may.
Why should I take my flesh in my teeth and put my life in my hands?
Even if he kills me, I will hope in him; yet I will argue my ways to his face.
This too will be my salvation, for no godless person would come before him.
Listen closely to my words; let my declaration be in your ears.
Look now, I have prepared my case; I know that I will be proved right.
Who is there who will contend with me? For then I would be silent and die.
Only do not do two things to me, and then I will not hide from your face:
take your hand far away from me, and do not let dread of you terrify me.
Then call, and I will answer; or let me speak, and you reply to me.
How many are my iniquities and sins? Make me know my offense and my sin.
Why do you hide your face and count me as your enemy?
Will you frighten a windblown leaf? Will you chase dry straw?
For you write bitter charges against me and make me inherit the sins of my youth.
You put my feet in the stocks and watch all my paths; you mark a line around the soles of my feet.
And so he wastes away like something rotten, like a garment eaten by moths.
"A human being, born of woman, is short of days and full of turmoil.
He comes up like a flower and withers; he flees like a shadow and does not last.
Do you really fix your eyes on such a one? Do you bring me into judgment with you?
Who can bring something clean out of something unclean? No one!
Since his days are determined, and the number of his months is with you, and you have set him limits that he cannot pass,
look away from him, and let him rest, so that he can enjoy his day like a hired worker.
For there is hope for a tree: if it is cut down, it will sprout again, and its shoots will not fail.
Though its root grows old in the earth and its stump dies in the dust,
at the scent of water it will bud and put out branches like a young plant.
But a man dies and lies powerless; a human being breathes his last, and where is he?
As water vanishes from a lake and a river dries up and is parched,
so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, people will not wake, or be roused from their sleep.
If only you would hide me in Sheol, conceal me until your anger is past, set me a fixed time, and then remember me!
If a man dies, will he live again? All the days of my hard service I would wait, until my relief should come.
You would call, and I would answer you; you would long for the work of your hands.
For then you would count my steps, but not keep watch over my sin.
My offense would be sealed up in a bag, and you would cover over my guilt.
But as a mountain falls and crumbles away, and a rock is moved from its place,
as water wears away stones and its torrents wash away the soil of the earth, so you destroy the hope of a mortal.
You overpower him forever, and he passes away; you change his appearance and send him away.
His children are honored, but he does not know it; they are brought low, but he does not notice them.
He feels only the pain of his own body, and mourns only for himself."
"Should a wise man answer with windy knowledge and fill his belly with the east wind?
Should he argue with useless talk, with words that do no good?
But you are doing away with the fear of God and hindering devotion before God.
For your guilt teaches your mouth, and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
Your own mouth condemns you, not I; your own lips testify against you.
Were you the first human being ever born? Were you brought forth before the hills?
Do you listen in on the council of God? Do you keep wisdom to yourself?
What do you know that we do not know? What do you understand that is not with us as well?
Both the gray-haired and the aged are among us, older than your father.
Are the consolations of God too small for you, or a word spoken gently to you?
Why does your heart carry you away, and why do your eyes flash,
that you turn your spirit against God and let such words come out of your mouth?
What is a mortal, that he could be pure, or one born of woman, that he could be righteous?
If God puts no trust in his holy ones, and even the heavens are not pure in his sight,
how much less one who is detestable and corrupt, a man who drinks wickedness like water!
I will explain to you; listen to me, and let me tell what I have seen,
what wise men have declared, and have not hidden, what came from their fathers,
to whom alone the land was given, when no stranger passed among them.
The wicked man writhes in pain all his days, through all the years that are stored up for the ruthless.
The sound of terrors is in his ears; in time of peace the destroyer comes upon him.
He does not believe he will come back out of darkness; he is marked out for the sword.
He wanders about for bread: 'Where is it?' He knows that a day of darkness is ready at hand.
Distress and anguish terrify him; they overpower him like a king ready for the attack.
For he has stretched out his hand against God and defied the Almighty,
charging at him headlong, with the thick bosses of his shields.
For he has covered his face with his fat and put rolls of fat on his loins,
and he has lived in ruined cities, in houses no one should live in, which are destined to become heaps of rubble.
He will not grow rich, and his wealth will not last; his possessions will not spread over the land.
He will not escape the darkness; a flame will wither his shoots, and he will be swept away by the breath of his mouth.
Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself, for emptiness will be his reward.
It will be paid in full before his time, and his branch will not be green.
He will be like a vine that drops its unripe grapes, like an olive tree that sheds its blossoms.
For the company of the godless is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery.
They conceive trouble and give birth to wickedness; their womb prepares deceit."
"I have heard many things like these; you are all miserable comforters.
Is there no end to windy words? What drives you to keep answering?
I too could talk as you do, if you were in my place. I could string together words against you and shake my head at you.
I could strengthen you with my mouth, and the comfort of my lips would bring you relief.
If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I hold back, how much of it leaves me?
But now he has worn me out. You have devastated my whole household.
You have shriveled me up, and it has become a witness; my gauntness rises up against me and testifies to my face.
His anger has torn me, and he hates me; he gnashes his teeth at me. My enemy sharpens his eyes against me.
They open their mouths wide against me; they strike my cheeks in contempt; they mass together against me.
God hands me over to the unjust and throws me into the hands of the wicked.
I was at ease, but he shattered me; he seized me by the neck and dashed me to pieces. He set me up as his target;
his archers surround me. He pierces my kidneys and does not spare; he pours out my gall on the ground.
He breaks through me, breach after breach; he charges at me like a warrior.
I have sewn sackcloth over my skin and buried my horn in the dust.
My face is red with weeping, and deep darkness is on my eyelids,
although there is no violence in my hands, and my prayer is pure.
O earth, do not cover my blood; let my cry find no resting place.
Even now, look, my witness is in heaven, and the one who testifies for me is on high.
My friends scorn me; my eye pours out tears to God.
Let him argue a man's case with God, as a person does for his friend.
For only a few years will pass, and I will go the way of no return.
"My spirit is broken; my days are snuffed out; the grave awaits me.
Surely mockers are all around me, and my eye must dwell on their provocation.
Give a pledge for me, please, with yourself. Who else will shake hands to guarantee me?
For you have closed their minds to understanding; so you will not let them triumph.
One who denounces his friends for gain, the eyes of his children will fail.
He has made me a byword among the peoples; I have become one in whose face people spit.
My eye has grown dim with grief, and all my limbs are like a shadow.
The upright are appalled at this, and the innocent are stirred up against the godless.
Yet the righteous hold to their way, and those with clean hands grow stronger and stronger.
But as for all of you, come back again, please! I will not find a wise man among you.
My days are past; my plans are broken off, the desires of my heart.
They turn night into day: 'Light is near,' they say, in the face of darkness.
If I look to Sheol as my home, if I spread out my bed in darkness,
if I say to the pit, 'You are my father,' and to the worm, 'My mother,' or 'My sister,'
where then is my hope? Who can see any hope for me?
Will it go down to the bars of Sheol? Shall we rest together in the dust?"
"How long will you hunt for words? Show some sense, and then we can talk.
Why are we counted as cattle, considered stupid in your sight?
You who tear yourself apart in your anger, is the earth to be abandoned for your sake, or the rock moved from its place?
Yes, the light of the wicked is put out, and the flame of his fire does not shine.
The light grows dark in his tent, and his lamp above him is put out.
His vigorous stride is shortened, and his own schemes bring him down.
For his own feet throw him into a net, and he walks onto its mesh.
A trap seizes him by the heel; a snare holds him fast.
A noose is hidden for him on the ground, a trap for him on the path.
Terrors frighten him on every side and chase him at every step.
His strength is starved, and disaster is ready at his side.
It eats away the parts of his skin; the firstborn of Death devours his limbs.
He is torn from the tent he trusted in and marched off to the king of terrors.
What is not his lives in his tent; sulfur is scattered over his home.
His roots dry up beneath, and his branches wither above.
The memory of him perishes from the earth, and he has no name in the land.
He is driven out of light into darkness and chased out of the world.
He has no offspring or descendant among his people, and no survivor where he used to live.
Those in the west are appalled at his fate, and those in the east are seized with horror.
Surely such are the dwellings of the unjust, and this is the place of one who does not know God."
"How long will you torment me and crush me with words?
Ten times now you have insulted me; are you not ashamed to wrong me?
Even if it is true that I have gone astray, my error remains my own concern.
If you really want to exalt yourselves over me and use my disgrace as an argument against me,
then know that God has put me in the wrong and closed his net around me.
Look, I cry out, 'Violence!' but I get no answer; I call for help, but there is no justice.
He has walled up my way so that I cannot pass, and he has set darkness on my paths.
He has stripped me of my honor and taken the crown from my head.
He tears me down on every side, and I am gone; he has uprooted my hope like a tree.
He has kindled his anger against me and counts me as one of his enemies.
His troops advance together; they build up a siege ramp against me and camp around my tent.
He has put my brothers far from me; those who know me are wholly estranged from me.
My relatives have failed me; my close friends have forgotten me.
The guests in my house and my female servants count me as a stranger; I have become a foreigner in their eyes.
I call my servant, but he does not answer, though I plead with him with my own mouth.
My breath is repulsive to my wife; I am loathsome to my own brothers.
Even young children despise me; when I get up, they speak against me.
All my intimate friends detest me; those I love have turned against me.
My bones cling to my skin and my flesh; I have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Have pity on me, have pity on me, you my friends, for the hand of God has struck me!
Why do you pursue me as God does? Will you never have enough of my flesh?
Oh, that my words were written down! Oh, that they were inscribed in a scroll,
with an iron pen and lead, carved in the rock forever!
But I know that my redeemer lives, and that at the last he will rise up upon the earth.
And after my skin has been stripped off like this, yet in my flesh I will see God.
I myself will see him, with my own eyes, I and not a stranger. My heart faints within me!
If you say, 'How we will hound him!' and that the root of the trouble is found in me,
be afraid of the sword yourselves, for wrath brings the punishment of the sword, so that you may know there is a judgment."
"So my troubled thoughts compel me to answer, because of the turmoil within me.
I hear a rebuke that insults me, and a spirit from my understanding answers me.
Do you not know this from of old, ever since humankind was placed on the earth,
that the shout of joy of the wicked is short, and the gladness of the godless lasts only a moment?
Though his pride reaches up to the heavens and his head touches the clouds,
he will perish forever like his own dung; those who saw him will say, 'Where is he?'
He flies away like a dream and cannot be found; he is chased away like a vision of the night.
The eye that saw him will see him no more, and his place will no longer behold him.
His children will seek the favor of the poor, and his own hands will give back his wealth.
His bones are full of youthful vigor, but it will lie down with him in the dust.
Though evil is sweet in his mouth, and he hides it under his tongue,
though he savors it and will not let it go, but holds it in his mouth,
his food turns sour in his stomach; it becomes the venom of cobras within him.
He swallows riches and vomits them up; God makes his belly throw them out.
He will suck the poison of cobras; the tongue of the viper will kill him.
He will not look on the streams, the rivers, the torrents of honey and curds.
He will give back what he toiled for and not swallow it; he will not enjoy the profit of his trading.
For he has crushed and abandoned the poor; he has seized a house that he did not build.
Because his greed knew no rest, he will not escape with anything he desired.
Nothing was left that he did not devour; that is why his prosperity will not last.
In the fullness of his plenty he will be in distress; the full force of misery will come upon him.
When he has filled his belly, God will send his burning anger against him and rain it down on him as his food.
He may flee from an iron weapon, but a bronze arrow will pierce him.
He pulls it out, and it comes out of his back, the glittering point out of his gall; terrors come upon him.
Total darkness lies in wait for his treasures. A fire not fanned by anyone will consume him; it will devour what is left in his tent.
The heavens will reveal his guilt, and the earth will rise up against him.
The produce of his house will be carried off, flowing away on the day of God's anger.
This is the portion of the wicked from God, the inheritance appointed for him by God."
"Listen carefully to my words, and let this be the comfort you give me.
Bear with me while I speak, and after I have spoken, mock on.
As for me, is my complaint against a human being? Why should I not be impatient?
Look at me and be appalled; put your hand over your mouth.
When I think about it I am terrified, and trembling seizes my body.
Why do the wicked live on, grow old, and even grow mighty in power?
Their offspring are established in their presence, and their descendants before their eyes.
Their houses are safe from fear, and the rod of God is not upon them.
Their bull breeds without fail; their cow gives birth and does not miscarry.
They send out their little ones like a flock, and their children dance.
They sing to the tambourine and the lyre, and rejoice to the sound of the pipe.
They spend their days in prosperity, and go down to Sheol in an instant.
Yet they say to God, 'Leave us alone! We do not want to know your ways.
Who is the Almighty, that we should serve him? What would we gain if we prayed to him?'
Look, their prosperity is not in their own hands. The counsel of the wicked is far from me.
How often is the lamp of the wicked put out? How often does disaster come upon them? How often does he deal out pains in his anger?
How often are they like straw before the wind, like chaff that the storm carries away?
God stores up his punishment for his children? Let him repay the man himself, so that he knows it!
Let his own eyes see his ruin, and let him drink of the wrath of the Almighty.
For what does he care about his household after him, when the number of his months has been cut off?
Can anyone teach God knowledge, since he judges even those on high?
One person dies in full vigor, completely at ease and secure.
His pails are full of milk, and the marrow of his bones is moist.
Another dies with a bitter soul, never having tasted anything good.
They lie down alike in the dust, and worms cover them both.
Look, I know your thoughts, the schemes by which you would wrong me.
For you say, 'Where is the house of the noble? Where is the tent in which the wicked lived?'
Have you not asked those who travel the roads? Do you not accept their accounts,
that the wicked are spared on the day of disaster, and are rescued on the day of wrath?
Who denounces his way to his face? Who repays him for what he has done?
He is carried to the grave, and watch is kept over his tomb.
The clods of the valley are sweet to him. All humankind follows after him, and those who went before him are without number.
How then can you comfort me with empty words? Nothing is left of your answers but falsehood."
"Can a man be of use to God? Even a wise man is of use only to himself.
Is it any pleasure to the Almighty if you are righteous? Is it any gain to him if you make your ways blameless?
Is it because of your fear of God that he rebukes you and enters into judgment with you?
Is not your wickedness great? Are not your iniquities endless?
For you took pledges from your brothers for no reason and stripped the naked of their clothing.
You gave no water to the weary to drink, and you withheld bread from the hungry,
while the man with power owned the land, and the man of rank lived in it.
You sent widows away empty-handed, and the arms of orphans were crushed.
That is why snares are all around you, and sudden dread terrifies you,
or darkness, so that you cannot see, and a flood of water covers you.
Is not God in the height of heaven? See the highest stars, how lofty they are!
Yet you say, 'What does God know? Can he judge through thick darkness?
Thick clouds veil him, so that he does not see, as he walks on the vault of heaven.'
Will you keep to the ancient path that wicked men have walked,
who were snatched away before their time, whose foundations were washed away by a river?
They said to God, 'Leave us alone!' and 'What can the Almighty do to us?'
Yet it was he who filled their houses with good things. But the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
The righteous see it and are glad; the innocent mock them:
'Surely our adversaries are cut off, and fire has consumed what they left.'
Come to terms with him, and be at peace; in this way good will come to you.
Accept instruction from his mouth, and lay up his words in your heart.
If you return to the Almighty, you will be restored. If you remove injustice far from your tents,
if you lay your gold in the dust, the gold of Ophir among the stones of the wadis,
then the Almighty will be your gold and your choicest silver.
For then you will delight in the Almighty and lift up your face to God.
You will pray to him, and he will hear you, and you will fulfill your vows.
You will decide on a matter, and it will be done for you, and light will shine on your ways.
When people are brought low, and you say, 'Lift them up!' he will save the downcast.
He will rescue even someone who is not innocent; he will be rescued through the cleanness of your hands."
"Even today my complaint is defiant; the hand on me is heavy in spite of my groaning.
If only I knew where to find him, so that I could come to his dwelling place!
I would set out my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
I would learn the words he would answer me, and understand what he would say to me.
Would he contend with me with his great power? No, he would surely pay attention to me.
There an upright person could reason with him, and I would escape from my judge forever.
Look, I go forward, and he is not there; backward, and I do not perceive him.
When he is at work on the left, I cannot catch hold of him; he turns aside to the right, and I do not see him.
But he knows the way I take. When he has tested me, I will come out like gold.
My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept to his way and have not turned aside.
I have not departed from the command of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily food.
But he is one, and who can turn him back? What he desires, he does.
For he will carry out what he has decreed for me, and he has many such things in mind.
That is why I am terrified in his presence; when I think about it, I am in dread of him.
God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me.
Yet I have not been silenced by the darkness, by the thick darkness that covers my face.
"Why are times not stored up by the Almighty? Why do those who know him never see his days?
Some move boundary stones; they seize flocks and pasture them.
They drive away the orphans' donkey; they take the widow's ox as a pledge.
They push the needy off the road; the poor of the land all hide themselves together.
Look, like wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, searching for food; the desert gives them bread for their children.
They harvest fodder in the field, and they glean the vineyard of the wicked.
They spend the night naked, without clothing; they have no covering in the cold.
They are drenched by the mountain downpours; with no shelter, they hug the rock.
Some snatch the orphan from the breast, and they take pledges from the poor.
They go about naked, without clothing; hungry, they carry the sheaves.
Between their terraces they press out oil; they tread the winepresses, yet they are thirsty.
From the city men groan, and the wounded cry for help, yet God does not count it as wrong.
These are among those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways, and they do not stay in its paths.
The murderer rises at daybreak; he kills the poor and the needy, and in the night he is like a thief.
The eye of the adulterer watches for the twilight. He says, 'No eye will see me,' and he puts a covering over his face.
In the dark they break into houses; by day they shut themselves in; they do not know the light.
For to all of them the morning is deep darkness, for they are well acquainted with the terrors of deep darkness.
He is swift on the surface of the waters; their portion in the land is cursed; he does not turn toward the vineyards.
Drought and heat snatch away the snow waters; so does Sheol those who have sinned.
The womb forgets him; the worm feeds on him with relish; he is remembered no more, and wickedness is broken like a tree.
He feeds on the barren woman who bears no child, and does no good to the widow.
Yet by his power he prolongs the life of the mighty; they rise up when they had no hope of living.
He lets them rest secure, and they are supported, and his eyes are on their ways.
They are exalted for a little while, and then they are gone. They are brought low and gathered up like everyone else; they are cut off like the heads of grain.
If it is not so, who can prove me a liar and reduce my words to nothing?"
"Dominion and dread are his; he makes peace in his high places.
Can his troops be counted? On whom does his light not rise?
How then can a mortal be in the right before God? How can one born of a woman be pure?
Look, even the moon is not bright, and the stars are not pure in his eyes;
how much less a mortal, who is a maggot, and a human being, who is a worm!"
"How you have helped the powerless! How you have saved the arm that has no strength!
How you have counseled one who has no wisdom, and what a wealth of sound wisdom you have made known!
With whose help have you uttered these words? Whose breath has come out of you?
The shades of the dead writhe beneath the waters, and so do those who live in them.
Sheol is naked before him, and Abaddon has no covering.
He stretches out the north over empty space and hangs the earth on nothing.
He wraps up the waters in his clouds, and the cloud does not burst under them.
He covers the face of his throne, spreading his cloud over it.
He has marked out a circle on the face of the waters, at the boundary between light and darkness.
The pillars of heaven tremble and are astounded at his rebuke.
By his power he stilled the sea; by his understanding he shattered Rahab.
By his breath the heavens became clear; his hand pierced the fleeing serpent.
Look, these are only the edges of his ways; how faint is the whisper we hear of him! But the thunder of his mighty deeds, who can understand?"
Job took up his discourse again:
"As God lives, who has denied me justice, and the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
as long as my breath is in me, and the breath of God is in my nostrils,
my lips will not speak wickedness, and my tongue will not utter deceit.
Far be it from me to declare that you are right! Until I breathe my last, I will not give up my integrity.
I hold fast to my righteousness and will not let it go; my heart does not reproach me for any of my days.
May my enemy be like the wicked, and the one who rises against me like the unjust.
For what hope does the godless have when he is cut off, when God takes away his life?
Will God hear his cry when trouble comes upon him?
Will he take delight in the Almighty? Will he call on God at all times?
I will teach you about the power of God; I will not hide what is with the Almighty.
Look, all of you have seen it yourselves. Why then do you talk such empty nonsense?
This is the portion of a wicked person from God, the inheritance that the ruthless receive from the Almighty:
If his children are many, it is for the sword, and his offspring will not have enough bread.
Those who survive him will be buried by the plague, and his widows will not weep.
Though he heaps up silver like dust and piles up clothing like clay,
he may pile it up, but the righteous will wear it, and the innocent will divide the silver.
He builds his house like a moth, like a hut that a watchman makes.
He lies down rich, but will not do so again; he opens his eyes, and it is gone.
Terrors overtake him like a flood; in the night a storm wind carries him off.
The east wind lifts him up, and he is gone; it sweeps him out of his place.
It hurls itself at him without pity; he flees headlong from its power.
It claps its hands at him and hisses at him from its place.
"Surely there is a mine for silver, and a place for the gold that people refine.
Iron is taken from the dust, and copper is smelted from stone.
People put an end to darkness; they search out the farthest limits, for the stone that lies in gloom and deep darkness.
They open a shaft far from where anyone lives, in places forgotten by any foot; far from other people they dangle and sway.
The earth, from which bread comes, is turned upside down beneath, as if by fire.
Its stones are the place of sapphires, and it holds dust of gold.
No bird of prey knows that path; the falcon's eye has not seen it.
Proud beasts have not trodden it; no lion has passed over it.
People put their hand to the flint and overturn mountains from their roots.
They cut channels through the rocks, and their eyes see every precious thing.
They dam up the sources of the rivers and bring hidden things out into the light.
But wisdom, where can it be found? Where is the place of understanding?
No mortal knows its worth; it is not found in the land of the living.
The deep says, 'It is not in me,' and the sea says, 'It is not with me.'
It cannot be bought with solid gold, and its price cannot be weighed out in silver.
It cannot be valued in the gold of Ophir, in precious onyx or sapphire.
Gold and glass cannot compare with it, nor can it be exchanged for vessels of fine gold.
Coral and crystal are not worth mentioning; the price of wisdom is above pearls.
The topaz of Cush cannot compare with it; it cannot be valued in pure gold.
Where then does wisdom come from? Where is the place of understanding?
It is hidden from the eyes of every living thing, concealed even from the birds of the sky.
Abaddon and Death say, 'With our ears we have heard a rumor of it.'
God understands the way to it; he knows its place.
For he looks to the ends of the earth; he sees everything under the heavens.
When he gave the wind its weight and measured out the waters,
when he made a decree for the rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
then he saw it and declared it; he established it and searched it out.
And he said to humankind, 'Look, the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom, and to turn away from evil is understanding.'"
Job took up his discourse again:
"If only I were as in the months gone by, as in the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone above my head, and by his light I walked through darkness;
as I was in the days of my prime, when the friendship of God was over my tent;
when the Almighty was still with me, and my children were all around me;
when my steps were bathed in cream, and the rock poured out streams of oil for me!
When I went out to the gate of the city and set up my seat in the square,
the young men saw me and drew back, and the old men rose and stood;
officials stopped talking and put their hands over their mouths;
the voices of the nobles were hushed, and their tongues stuck to the roof of their mouths.
For any ear that heard me called me blessed, and any eye that saw me spoke well of me,
because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the orphan who had no one to help him.
The blessing of the one who was perishing came upon me, and I made the widow's heart sing for joy.
I put on righteousness, and it clothed me; my justice was like a robe and a turban.
I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
I was a father to the needy, and I looked into the case of the stranger.
I broke the jaws of the unjust and made them drop their prey from their teeth.
Then I thought, 'I will die in my nest, and I will multiply my days like the sand.
My roots will be open to the water, and the dew will lie all night on my branches.
My glory will stay fresh with me, and my bow will be renewed in my hand.'
People listened to me and waited; they kept silent for my counsel.
After I had spoken, they did not speak again; my words fell on them drop by drop.
They waited for me as for the rain; they opened their mouths as for the spring rain.
When I smiled at them, they could hardly believe it; they did not let the light of my face fall.
I chose the way for them and sat as their chief; I lived like a king among his troops, like one who comforts mourners.
"But now they laugh at me, those younger than I, whose fathers I would have refused to put with the dogs of my flock.
What use to me was the strength of their hands? Their vigor had perished.
Gaunt from want and hunger, they gnaw the dry ground, in the gloom of desolation and waste.
They pluck saltwort among the bushes, and the root of the broom bush is their food.
They are driven out from the community; people shout after them as after a thief.
They have to live in the gullies of the wadis, in holes in the ground and among the rocks.
Among the bushes they bray; under the nettles they huddle together.
A senseless brood, a nameless brood, they were whipped out of the land.
And now I have become their song; I have become a byword to them.
They detest me; they keep their distance from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
Because he has loosened my cord and humbled me, they have thrown off all restraint before me.
On my right the rabble rise up; they push my feet away and build their roads of ruin against me.
They tear up my path; they profit from my disaster; no one holds them back.
As through a wide breach they come; amid the crash they roll in.
Terrors are turned against me; they chase away my dignity like the wind, and my safety has passed away like a cloud.
And now my life is poured out within me; days of affliction have taken hold of me.
At night my bones are pierced within me, and the pains that gnaw me take no rest.
With great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.
He has thrown me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.
I cry to you for help, but you do not answer me; I stand up, and you just look at me.
You have turned cruel to me; with the might of your hand you attack me.
You lift me up on the wind and make me ride it; you melt me away, and all my success.
For I know you will bring me back to death, to the house appointed for all the living.
Yet does not one in ruins stretch out a hand, and in his disaster cry for help?
Did I not weep for the one whose life was hard? Was my soul not grieved for the needy?
Yet when I hoped for good, evil came; when I waited for light, darkness came.
My insides are in turmoil and never still; days of affliction confront me.
I go about darkened, but not by the sun; I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.
I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to ostriches.
My skin has turned black and peels from me; my bones burn with fever.
My lyre is turned to mourning, and my pipe to the sound of weeping.
"I made a covenant with my eyes; how then could I gaze at a young woman?
What portion would I have from God above, what inheritance from the Almighty on high?
Is there not disaster for the unjust, and calamity for those who do wrong?
Does he not see my ways and count all my steps?
If I have walked with falsehood, or my foot has hurried after deceit,
let him weigh me on honest scales, and let God know my integrity.
If my steps have turned aside from the way, if my heart has followed my eyes, or if any stain has stuck to my hands,
then let me sow and another eat, and let my crops be uprooted.
If my heart has been enticed by a woman, or I have lain in wait at my neighbor's door,
then let my wife grind grain for another, and let other men kneel over her.
For that would be a shameful crime; it would be an offense for the judges to punish.
For it is a fire that consumes all the way to Abaddon, and it would uproot all my harvest.
If I have denied justice to my male or female servant when they brought a complaint against me,
what then could I do when God rises up? When he calls me to account, what could I answer him?
Did not the one who made me in the womb make them? Did not the same one form us in the womb?
If I have withheld from the poor what they wanted, or let the widow's eyes grow dim with longing,
or eaten my bit of bread by myself, and the orphan has not eaten any of it,
for from my youth the orphan grew up with me as with a father, and from my mother's womb I guided the widow,
if I have seen anyone perishing for lack of clothing, or the needy without covering,
if his body has not blessed me, as he was warmed by the fleece of my sheep,
if I have raised my hand against the orphan, because I saw I had support in the gate,
then let my shoulder fall from its socket, and let my arm be broken off at the elbow.
For disaster from God was a terror to me, and because of his majesty I could not do such things.
If I have made gold my confidence, or called fine gold my security,
if I have rejoiced because my wealth was great, or because my hand had gained so much,
if I have looked at the sun when it shone, or the moon moving in splendor,
and my heart has been secretly enticed, and my hand has thrown them a kiss,
this too would be an offense for the judges to punish, for I would have denied God above.
If I have rejoiced at the ruin of one who hated me, or gloated when evil found him,
I have not let my mouth sin by asking for his life with a curse.
If the men of my tent have not said, 'Who is there who has not had his fill of his meat?'
No stranger had to spend the night in the street; I opened my doors to the traveler.
If I have covered my transgressions as others do, hiding my guilt in my bosom,
because I feared the great crowd, and the contempt of the clans terrified me, so that I kept silent and did not go out of my door—
Oh, that I had someone to hear me! Here is my signature; let the Almighty answer me! Let my opponent write out his charge against me!
Surely I would carry it on my shoulder; I would bind it on like a crown.
I would give him an account of all my steps; like a prince I would approach him.
If my land has cried out against me, and its furrows have wept together,
if I have eaten its produce without paying, or made its owners breathe their last,
then let thorns grow instead of wheat, and stinking weeds instead of barley." The words of Job are ended.
So these three men stopped answering Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram, became angry. He was angry with Job because he had justified himself rather than God.
He was also angry with Job's three friends, because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job.
Elihu had waited to speak to Job, because they were older than he was.
But when Elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouths of the three men, he became angry.
So Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered: "I am young in years, and you are old. That is why I held back and was afraid to tell you what I know.
I thought, 'Age should speak, and many years should teach wisdom.'
But it is the spirit in a person, the breath of the Almighty, that gives them understanding.
It is not the old who are wise, nor the aged who understand what is right.
So I say, listen to me; let me also tell you what I know.
Look, I waited for your words; I listened to your reasoning, while you searched for what to say.
I paid close attention to you, but not one of you refuted Job or answered his words.
Do not say, 'We have found wisdom; let God drive him back, not a man.'
He has not directed his words against me, and I will not answer him with your arguments.
They are dismayed; they answer no more; words have deserted them.
Must I wait because they do not speak, because they stand there and answer no more?
I too will give my answer; I too will tell what I know.
For I am full of words; the spirit within me presses me.
Look, my belly is like wine that has no vent; like new wineskins, it is ready to burst.
Let me speak and find relief; let me open my lips and answer.
I will not show partiality to anyone or flatter any person.
For I do not know how to flatter; if I did, my Maker would soon carry me away.
"But now, Job, hear what I have to say, and listen to all my words.
Look, I open my mouth; my tongue speaks in my mouth.
My words come from an upright heart, and my lips speak sincerely what they know.
The spirit of God has made me; the breath of the Almighty gives me life.
Answer me if you can; set out your case before me; take your stand.
Look, before God I am just as you are; I too was pinched off from clay.
So no fear of me need terrify you, and my pressure will not be heavy on you.
But you have said in my hearing, and I heard the sound of your words:
'I am pure, without transgression; I am clean, and there is no guilt in me.
Look, he finds pretexts against me; he counts me as his enemy.
He puts my feet in the stocks; he watches all my paths.'
Look, in this you are not right, I answer you, for God is greater than any mortal.
Why do you contend with him, saying that he answers none of a person's words?
For God speaks in one way, and in two, though people do not notice it.
In a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls on people as they slumber on their beds,
then he opens people's ears and seals their warning,
to turn a person away from what he is doing, and to keep a man from pride.
He keeps his soul back from the pit, his life from crossing the channel of death.
A person is also disciplined with pain on his bed, while all his bones are in constant torment,
so that his life loathes bread, and his soul the food it once craved.
His flesh wastes away until it cannot be seen, and his bones, once hidden, stick out.
His soul draws near to the pit, and his life to those who bring death.
If there is an angel for him, a mediator, one among a thousand, to tell a person what is right for him,
and he is gracious to him and says, 'Spare him from going down to the pit; I have found a ransom,'
then his flesh becomes fresher than a child's; he returns to the days of his youth.
He prays to God, and God accepts him; he sees his face with a shout of joy, and he restores to the mortal his righteousness.
He sings before people and says, 'I sinned and perverted what was right, but I was not repaid as I deserved.'
He has redeemed his soul from going down to the pit, and his life will see the light.
Look, God does all these things, twice, three times, with a man,
to bring back his soul from the pit, so that he may be lit with the light of life.
Pay attention, Job, listen to me; be silent, and I will speak.
If you have anything to say, answer me; speak, for I want to prove you right.
If not, listen to me; be silent, and I will teach you wisdom."
"Hear my words, you wise men; listen to me, you who have knowledge.
For the ear tests words as the palate tastes food.
Let us choose for ourselves what is right; let us find out among ourselves what is good.
For Job has said, 'I am in the right, and God has denied me justice.
In spite of my right, I am counted a liar; my wound is incurable, though I am without transgression.'
What man is like Job, who drinks up scorn like water,
who keeps company with evildoers, and walks with wicked men?
For he has said, 'It does a man no good to be on good terms with God.'
So listen to me, you men of understanding. Far be it from God to do wickedness, and from the Almighty to do wrong!
For he repays a person for what he has done, and he brings on each one what his conduct deserves.
Truly, God will not act wickedly, and the Almighty will not pervert justice.
Who put him in charge of the earth? Who set the whole world in place?
If he were to set his heart on himself, and gather to himself his spirit and his breath,
all flesh would perish together, and humankind would return to dust.
If you have understanding, hear this; listen to what I say.
Can one who hates justice govern? Will you condemn the one who is righteous and mighty?
Is it fitting to say to a king, 'Worthless one,' or to nobles, 'Wicked'?
He shows no partiality to princes and does not favor the rich over the poor, for they are all the work of his hands.
In a moment they die; at midnight people are shaken and pass away; the mighty are removed without a hand.
For his eyes are on a person's ways, and he sees all his steps.
There is no darkness, no deep darkness, where evildoers can hide.
For he does not need to consider a person further before he comes before God in judgment.
He shatters the mighty without investigation and sets others in their place.
Because he knows their deeds, he overthrows them in the night, and they are crushed.
He strikes them for their wickedness where others can see,
because they turned aside from following him and paid no attention to any of his ways,
so that they brought the cry of the poor before him, and he hears the cry of the afflicted.
But if he keeps quiet, who can condemn him? If he hides his face, who can see him? Yet he watches over nation and individual alike,
so that the godless may not reign, and may not be snares for the people.
For has anyone said to God, 'I have borne punishment; I will not offend again.
Teach me what I cannot see; if I have done wrong, I will do it no more'?
Should he repay on your terms, when you have rejected his ways? For you must choose, not I; so tell us what you know.
Men of understanding will say to me, and any wise man who hears me:
'Job speaks without knowledge; his words are without insight.'
If only Job were tested to the end for answering like wicked men!
For he adds rebellion to his sin; he claps his hands among us and multiplies his words against God."
"Do you think this is just? You say, 'I am more in the right than God.'
For you ask, 'What use is it to you? What do I gain by not sinning?'
I will answer you, and your friends with you.
Look up at the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds, high above you.
If you have sinned, what do you do to him? If your transgressions are many, what do you do to him?
If you are righteous, what do you give him? Or what does he receive from your hand?
Your wickedness affects only someone like yourself, and your righteousness only a human being.
Because of the many oppressions, people cry out; they cry for help because of the arm of the mighty.
But no one says, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives songs in the night,
who teaches us more than the animals of the earth, and makes us wiser than the birds of the sky?'
There they cry out, but he does not answer, because of the pride of evildoers.
Surely God does not listen to an empty cry; the Almighty pays no attention to it.
How much less when you say that you do not see him, that your case is before him, and you are waiting for him!
And now, because his anger does not punish, and he does not take much notice of transgression,
Job opens his mouth in empty talk; he multiplies words without knowledge."
"Bear with me a little longer, and I will show you, for there is still more to say on God's behalf.
I will bring my knowledge from far away, and I will ascribe righteousness to my Maker.
For truly my words are not false; one who is perfect in knowledge is with you.
Look, God is mighty, and he does not despise anyone; he is mighty in strength of understanding.
He does not keep the wicked alive, but he gives justice to the afflicted.
He does not take his eyes off the righteous; he seats them with kings on the throne forever, and they are exalted.
But if they are bound in chains, caught in the cords of affliction,
then he tells them what they have done, and their transgressions, that they have behaved arrogantly.
He opens their ears to instruction and tells them to turn back from wickedness.
If they listen and serve him, they will end their days in prosperity, and their years in pleasantness.
But if they do not listen, they will cross the channel of death and die without knowledge.
The godless in heart harbor anger; they do not cry for help when he binds them.
They die in their youth, and their life ends among the shrine prostitutes.
He rescues the afflicted through their affliction and opens their ears through their distress.
He also lured you out of the jaws of distress, into a broad place where there was no constraint, and your table was set with rich food.
But you are full of the judgment due to the wicked; judgment and justice take hold of you.
Beware that wrath does not lure you into scoffing, and do not let a large ransom turn you aside.
Will your cry for help keep you out of distress, or all the efforts of your strength?
Do not long for the night, when peoples are taken away from their place.
Be careful not to turn to wickedness, for you have chosen this rather than affliction.
Look, God is exalted in his power. Who is a teacher like him?
Who has prescribed his way for him? Who can say, 'You have done wrong'?
Remember to extol his work, which people have praised in song.
All humankind has looked on it; mortals see it from afar.
Look, God is great, beyond our knowledge; the number of his years is past searching out.
For he draws up the drops of water; they distill rain from his mist,
which the skies pour down and shower on humankind in abundance.
Can anyone understand the spreading of the clouds, the thundering from his pavilion?
Look, he spreads his light around him, and he covers the roots of the sea.
For by these he judges the peoples; he gives food in abundance.
He covers his hands with lightning and commands it to strike the mark.
His thunder announces him; even the cattle tell of the storm's approach.
"At this my heart also trembles and leaps from its place.
Listen, listen to the roar of his voice, the rumbling that comes from his mouth.
He lets it loose under the whole heaven, and his lightning to the ends of the earth.
After it his voice roars; he thunders with his majestic voice, and he does not hold back the lightning when his voice is heard.
God thunders wonderfully with his voice; he does great things that we cannot understand.
For he says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth,' and to the rain shower, his mighty downpours.
He seals up the hand of every person, so that all the people he has made may know it.
The animals go into their dens and stay in their lairs.
The storm comes out from its chamber, and the cold from the scattering winds.
By the breath of God ice is given, and the broad waters are frozen solid.
He loads the thick cloud with moisture; the clouds scatter his lightning.
They turn round and round by his guidance, to do all that he commands them over the face of the inhabited earth.
Whether for punishment, or for his land, or for faithful love, he makes it happen.
Listen to this, Job; stop and consider the wonders of God.
Do you know how God directs them and makes the lightning of his cloud shine?
Do you know how the clouds are balanced, the wonders of one who is perfect in knowledge?
You, whose clothes are hot when the land lies still under the south wind,
can you, as he does, spread out the skies, hard as a mirror of cast metal?
Teach us what we should say to him; we cannot set out our case because of the darkness.
Should he be told that I want to speak? Would anyone ask to be swallowed up?
Now no one can look at the light when it is bright in the skies, when the wind has passed and swept them clean.
Out of the north comes golden splendor; around God is awesome majesty.
The Almighty: we cannot find him. He is great in power, and in justice and abundant righteousness he does not oppress.
Therefore people fear him; he does not regard any who are wise in their own heart."
Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
"Who is this who darkens counsel with words without knowledge?
Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will inform me.
Where were you when I laid the foundations of the earth? Tell me, if you have understanding.
Who fixed its measurements? Surely you know! Or who stretched the measuring line over it?
On what were its bases sunk, or who laid its cornerstone,
while the morning stars sang together and all the sons of God shouted for joy?
Who shut in the sea with doors when it burst out from the womb,
when I made the clouds its garment and thick darkness its swaddling band,
when I set my limit for it and fixed its bars and doors,
and said, 'This far you may come, and no farther; here your proud waves must stop'?
Have you ever in your life commanded the morning, or shown the dawn its place,
so that it might take hold of the edges of the earth and shake the wicked out of it?
The earth is changed like clay under a seal, and its features stand out like a garment.
Their light is withheld from the wicked, and the arm raised high is broken.
Have you entered the springs of the sea, or walked in the recesses of the deep?
Have the gates of death been revealed to you? Have you seen the gates of deep darkness?
Have you understood the breadth of the earth? Tell me, if you know all this.
Where is the way to the place where light lives? And darkness, where is its home,
that you may take it to its territory and know the paths to its house?
You know, for you were born then, and the number of your days is great!
Have you entered the storehouses of the snow, or seen the storehouses of the hail,
which I have kept for a time of trouble, for the day of battle and war?
Where is the way to the place where the light is divided, or where the east wind is scattered over the earth?
Who has cut a channel for the torrents of rain and a path for the thunderbolt,
to bring rain on a land where no one lives, on a wilderness where there are no human beings,
to satisfy the desolate wasteland and make the grass sprout?
Does the rain have a father? Who fathered the drops of dew?
From whose womb did the ice come? Who gave birth to the frost of heaven,
when the waters hide themselves as if turned to stone, and the surface of the deep is frozen?
Can you bind the chains of the Pleiades, or loosen the cords of Orion?
Can you bring out the Mazzaroth in its season, or guide the Bear with its children?
Do you know the decrees of the heavens? Can you establish their rule over the earth?
Can you lift up your voice to the clouds, so that a flood of water covers you?
Can you send out lightning bolts, so that they go and say to you, 'Here we are'?
Who has put wisdom in the ibis, or given understanding to the rooster?
Who has the wisdom to count the clouds? Who can tip over the water jars of heaven,
when the dust runs into a mass and the clods stick together?
Can you hunt prey for the lioness, or satisfy the appetite of the young lions,
when they crouch in their dens or lie in wait in the thicket?
Who provides food for the raven, when its young cry out to God and wander about for lack of food?
"Do you know when the mountain goats give birth? Do you watch over the does when they calve?
Can you count the months they must fulfill, and do you know the time when they give birth?
They crouch and bring forth their young; they are delivered of their labor pains.
Their young grow strong and grow up in the open field; they go out and do not return to them.
Who let the wild donkey go free? Who untied the ropes of the wild ass,
to which I gave the desert as its home, and the salt land as its dwelling?
It laughs at the commotion of the town; it does not hear the shouts of a driver.
It ranges the mountains as its pasture and searches for every green thing.
Will the wild ox be willing to serve you? Will it spend the night by your feeding trough?
Can you bind the wild ox in the furrow with ropes? Will it harrow the valleys behind you?
Will you rely on it because its strength is great? Will you leave your heavy work to it?
Will you trust it to bring in your grain and gather it to your threshing floor?
The wings of the ostrich flap joyfully, but are they the pinions and plumage of the stork?
For she leaves her eggs on the ground and lets them warm in the dust,
forgetting that a foot may crush them, and a wild animal may trample them.
She treats her young harshly, as if they were not hers; she does not fear that her labor may be in vain,
for God has made her forget wisdom and has given her no share of understanding.
But when she rises up to run, she laughs at the horse and its rider.
Do you give the horse its might? Do you clothe its neck with a mane?
Do you make it leap like a locust? Its majestic snorting is terrifying.
It paws in the valley and rejoices in its strength; it goes out to meet the weapons.
It laughs at fear and is not dismayed; it does not turn back from the sword.
The quiver rattles against it, the flashing spear and the javelin.
With trembling and excitement it swallows the ground; it cannot stand still when the trumpet sounds.
Whenever the trumpet sounds, it says, 'Aha!' From far away it smells the battle, the thunder of the commanders and the war cry.
Is it by your understanding that the hawk soars and spreads its wings toward the south?
Is it at your command that the eagle mounts up and makes its nest on high?
It lives on the cliff and spends the night there, on the crag of the rock, its stronghold.
From there it spies out its food; its eyes see it from far away.
Its young ones gulp down blood, and where the slain are, there it is."
"Will the one who contends with the Almighty correct him? Let the one who argues with God answer it!"
"Look, I am of small account; what can I answer you? I put my hand over my mouth.
I have spoken once, and I will not answer; twice, but I will say no more."
Then the LORD answered Job out of the storm:
"Brace yourself like a man; I will question you, and you will inform me.
Would you even annul my justice? Would you condemn me so that you may be in the right?
Do you have an arm like God's? Can you thunder with a voice like his?
Adorn yourself, then, with pride and dignity; clothe yourself with splendor and majesty.
Pour out the floods of your anger; look at everyone who is proud and bring him low.
Look at everyone who is proud and humble him; tread down the wicked where they stand.
Hide them all in the dust together; bind their faces in the hidden place.
Then I too will praise you, for your own right hand can save you.
Look now at Behemoth, which I made, as I made you; it eats grass like an ox.
Look at the strength in its loins, and the power in the muscles of its belly.
It stiffens its tail like a cedar; the sinews of its thighs are knit together.
Its bones are tubes of bronze, its limbs like bars of iron.
It is the first of the ways of God; only its Maker can bring his sword near it.
For the mountains bring it their produce, where all the wild animals play.
Under the lotus plants it lies, in the shelter of the reeds and the marsh.
The lotus plants cover it with their shade; the willows of the wadi surround it.
Look, if the river rages, it is not alarmed; it is confident, though the Jordan bursts against its mouth.
Can anyone take it by its eyes, or pierce its nose with snares?
Can you draw out Leviathan with a fishhook, or press down its tongue with a cord?
Can you put a rope of rushes through its nose, or pierce its jaw with a hook?
Will it plead with you again and again? Will it speak gentle words to you?
Will it make a covenant with you, for you to take it as your servant for life?
Will you play with it as with a bird, or put it on a leash for your young girls?
Will traders bargain over it? Will they divide it up among the merchants?
Can you fill its skin with harpoons, or its head with fishing spears?
Lay your hand on it; remember the battle, and you will not do it again!
"Look, the hope of anyone who tries is false; is one not thrown down even at the sight of it?
No one is fierce enough to rouse it. Who then can stand before me?
Who has come to me first, that I should repay him? Everything under the whole heaven is mine.
Shall I keep silent about it, about its limbs, its mighty strength and the grace of its build?
Who can strip off its outer garment? Who can come within its double bridle?
Who can open the doors of its face? All around its teeth is terror.
Its pride is its rows of shields, shut up closely as with a seal.
One is so close to another that no air can come between them.
They are joined one to another; they cling together and cannot be separated.
Its sneezes flash out light, and its eyes are like the eyelids of the dawn.
Out of its mouth go flaming torches; sparks of fire leap out.
Smoke comes out of its nostrils, as from a pot heated and boiling over burning rushes.
Its breath sets coals ablaze, and a flame comes out of its mouth.
Strength lodges in its neck, and terror dances before it.
The folds of its flesh stick together; they are firmly cast on it and cannot be moved.
Its heart is as hard as stone, hard as the lower millstone.
When it rises up, the mighty are afraid; at its crashing they are beside themselves.
The sword that reaches it does not prevail, nor does the spear, the dart or the javelin.
It counts iron as straw, and bronze as rotten wood.
The arrow does not make it flee; sling stones are turned to chaff for it.
Clubs are counted as chaff; it laughs at the rattle of the javelin.
Its underside is jagged potsherds; it spreads itself like a threshing sledge on the mud.
It makes the depths boil like a pot; it makes the sea like a pot of ointment.
Behind it, it leaves a shining wake; one would think the deep had white hair.
On earth there is nothing like it, a creature made without fear.
It looks down on everything that is lofty; it is king over all the proud beasts."
"I know that you can do all things, and that no purpose of yours can be thwarted.
'Who is this who hides counsel without knowledge?' So I have spoken of what I did not understand, things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
'Listen, and I will speak; I will question you, and you will inform me.'
I had heard of you by the hearing of the ear, but now my eye sees you.
Therefore I retract and repent in dust and ashes."

After the LORD had spoken these words to Job, the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, "My anger burns against you and against your two friends, for you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has.

So now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to my servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, for I will accept his prayer and not deal with you as your folly deserves. For you have not spoken of me what is right, as my servant Job has."
So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did as the LORD had told them, and the LORD accepted Job's prayer.
When Job had prayed for his friends, the LORD restored his fortunes, and the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then all his brothers and sisters and all who had known him before came to him and ate a meal with him in his house. They showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the trouble that the LORD had brought on him, and each of them gave him a qesitah and a gold ring.
The LORD blessed the latter part of Job's life more than the first. He had fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.
He also had seven sons and three daughters.
He named the first Jemimah, the second Keziah, and the third Keren-happuch.
In all the land no women were found as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
After this Job lived 140 years, and he saw his children and their children to the fourth generation.
And Job died, old and full of days.
Happy is the one who does not walk by the advice of the wicked, or stand in the way of sinners, or sit in the seat of mockers.
Instead, his delight is in the law of the LORD, and on his law he meditates day and night.
He is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in its season, and its leaves do not wither. In all that he does, he prospers.
Not so the wicked! They are like chaff that the wind blows away.
So the wicked will not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the assembly of the righteous.
For the LORD knows the way of the righteous, but the way of the wicked will perish.
Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers conspire together, against the LORD and against his anointed one:
"Let us break their chains, and throw off their ropes from us!"
The one who sits in heaven laughs; the Lord scoffs at them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger, and terrifies them in his fury:
"I myself have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain."
I will proclaim the decree of the LORD. He said to me, "You are my son; today I have become your father.
Ask me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, the ends of the earth your possession.
You will break them with a rod of iron; you will smash them like a potter's jar."
So now, you kings, be wise; take warning, you who rule the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.
Kiss the son, or he will be angry, and you will perish on your way, for his anger flares up quickly. Happy are all who take refuge in him.
A psalm of David, when he fled from his son Absalom.
LORD, how many are my adversaries! Many are rising up against me.
Many are saying of me, "There is no salvation for him in God." Selah.
But you, LORD, are a shield around me, my glory, the one who lifts up my head.
I cry aloud to the LORD, and he answers me from his holy mountain. Selah.
I lay down and slept; I woke again, for the LORD sustains me.
I will not be afraid of the tens of thousands of people who have taken their stand against me on every side.
Rise up, LORD! Save me, my God! For you have struck all my enemies on the jaw; you have broken the teeth of the wicked.
Salvation belongs to the LORD. May your blessing be on your people. Selah.
For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of David.
When I call, answer me, God of my righteousness! When I was in distress, you gave me room. Be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
You people, how long will you turn my honor into shame? How long will you love what is worthless and seek after lies? Selah.
Know that the LORD has set apart the faithful one for himself; the LORD hears when I call to him.
Tremble, and do not sin. Search your hearts on your beds, and be still. Selah.
Offer right sacrifices, and trust in the LORD.
Many are saying, "Who will show us good?" Let the light of your face shine on us, LORD.
You have put more joy in my heart than they have when their grain and new wine abound.
In peace I will lie down and sleep at once, for you alone, LORD, make me live in safety.
For the director. With the Nehiloth. A psalm of David.
Listen to my words, LORD; consider my sighing.
Pay attention to the sound of my cry for help, my King and my God, for to you I pray.
LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I lay out my case before you and keep watch.
For you are not a God who delights in wickedness; evil cannot stay with you as a guest.
The boastful cannot stand before your eyes; you hate all evildoers.
You destroy those who speak lies; the LORD detests the violent and the deceitful.
But I, through the greatness of your faithful love, will come into your house; I will bow down toward your holy temple in reverence for you.
LORD, lead me in your righteousness, because of those who lie in wait for me; make your way straight before me.
For there is nothing reliable in their mouth; their inner self is destruction. Their throat is an open grave; they flatter with their tongue.
Declare them guilty, God; let them fall by their own schemes. Drive them out for their many offenses, for they have rebelled against you.
But let all who take refuge in you rejoice; let them shout for joy forever. Spread your protection over them, so that those who love your name may exult in you.
For you bless the righteous, LORD; you surround him with favor as with a shield.
For the director. With stringed instruments, according to the Sheminith. A psalm of David.
LORD, do not rebuke me in your anger, or discipline me in your wrath.
Be gracious to me, LORD, for I am wasting away; heal me, LORD, for my bones are shaking with terror.
My soul is shaking with terror. But you, LORD, how long?
Turn, LORD, rescue my life; save me for the sake of your faithful love.
For in death no one remembers you; in Sheol who gives you thanks?
I am worn out with my groaning. Every night I flood my bed; I drench my couch with my tears.
My eye grows dim with grief; it grows weak because of all my adversaries.
Depart from me, all you evildoers, for the LORD has heard the sound of my weeping.
The LORD has heard my plea for mercy; the LORD accepts my prayer.
All my enemies will be ashamed and shake with terror; they will turn back and be ashamed in an instant.
A shiggaion of David, which he sang to the LORD concerning Cush, a Benjaminite.
LORD my God, in you I take refuge. Save me from all who pursue me, and rescue me,
or like a lion he will tear me to pieces, dragging me away with no one to rescue me.
LORD my God, if I have done this, if there is wrong on my hands,
if I have repaid my friend with evil, or plundered my adversary without cause,
then let the enemy pursue me and overtake me; let him trample my life to the ground, and lay my honor in the dust. Selah.
Rise up, LORD, in your anger; lift yourself up against the fury of my adversaries. Awake for me; you have decreed justice.
Let the assembly of the peoples gather around you, and over it return on high.
The LORD judges the peoples. Judge me, LORD, according to my righteousness, and according to the integrity that is in me.
Let the evil of the wicked come to an end, but establish the righteous, you who test hearts and minds, righteous God!
My shield is in God's hands, who saves the upright in heart.
God is a righteous judge, a God who is angry every day.
If someone does not turn back, he will sharpen his sword; he has bent his bow and made it ready.
He has prepared his deadly weapons; he makes his arrows into flaming shafts.
See, he is in labor with evil; he conceives trouble and gives birth to lies.
He digs a pit and hollows it out, and falls into the hole he has made.
His trouble comes back on his own head; his violence comes down on his own skull.
I will give thanks to the LORD for his righteousness, and sing praise to the name of the LORD Most High.
For the director. According to the Gittith. A psalm of David.
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your splendor above the heavens.
Out of the mouths of children and nursing infants you have established strength because of your adversaries, to silence the enemy and the avenger.
When I look at your heavens, the work of your fingers, the moon and the stars, which you have set in place,
what is a human being, that you remember him, a son of man, that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than God, and crowned him with glory and honor.
You made him ruler over the works of your hands; you put everything under his feet:
all sheep and cattle, and the wild animals too,
the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, whatever passes along the paths of the seas.
LORD, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth!
For the director. According to Muth-labben. A psalm of David.
I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart; I will tell of all your wonderful deeds.
I will rejoice and exult in you; I will sing praise to your name, Most High.
When my enemies turn back, they stumble and perish before you.
For you have upheld my right and my cause; you have sat on your throne, judging rightly.
You have rebuked the nations; you have destroyed the wicked; you have wiped out their name forever and ever.
The enemy is finished, in ruins forever; you have uprooted their cities; the very memory of them has perished.
But the LORD sits enthroned forever; he has set up his throne for judgment.
He will judge the world in righteousness; he will judge the peoples with fairness.
The LORD is a stronghold for the oppressed, a stronghold in times of trouble.
Those who know your name will trust in you, for you, LORD, have not abandoned those who seek you.
Sing praises to the LORD, who dwells in Zion; proclaim his deeds among the peoples.
For the one who avenges bloodshed remembers them; he does not forget the cry of the humble.
Be gracious to me, LORD! See how I suffer from those who hate me, you who lift me up from the gates of death,
so that I may tell of all your praises in the gates of Daughter Zion, and rejoice in your salvation.
The nations have sunk into the pit they made; their foot is caught in the net they hid.
The LORD has made himself known; he has carried out justice. The wicked are snared by the work of their own hands. Higgaion. Selah.
The wicked will return to Sheol, all the nations that forget God.
For the needy will not always be forgotten, nor will the hope of the afflicted perish forever.
Rise up, LORD! Do not let mortals prevail; let the nations be judged before you.
Strike them with terror, LORD; let the nations know that they are only mortals. Selah.
Why, LORD, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble?
