You brought us into the net; you laid a heavy burden on our backs.
You let people ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water, but you brought us out to a place of abundance.
I will come into your house with burnt offerings; I will fulfill my vows to you,
the vows my lips uttered and my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.
I will offer you burnt offerings of fat animals, with the smoke of rams; I will offer bulls with goats. Selah.
Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for me.
I cried aloud to him with my mouth, and his praise was on my tongue.
If I had cherished wickedness in my heart, the Lord would not have listened.
But truly God has listened; he has paid attention to the voice of my prayer.
Blessed be God, who has not turned away my prayer, or his faithful love from me.
For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.
May God be gracious to us and bless us; may he make his face shine on us. Selah.
May your way be known on earth, your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for you judge the peoples with fairness, and guide the nations on earth. Selah.
Let the peoples praise you, God; let all the peoples praise you.
The earth has yielded its harvest; may God, our God, bless us.
May God bless us, and let all the ends of the earth fear him.
For the director. Of David. A psalm. A song.
Let God rise up, let his enemies be scattered; let those who hate him flee before him.
As smoke is blown away, so blow them away; as wax melts before the fire, so let the wicked perish before God.
But let the righteous be glad; let them rejoice before God; let them celebrate with joy.
Sing to God, sing praises to his name; build up a road for the one who rides through the deserts. His name is the LORD; rejoice before him.
A father of the fatherless and a defender of widows is God in his holy dwelling.
God gives the lonely a home to live in; he leads prisoners out into prosperity, but the rebellious live in a parched land.
God, you went out before your people; you marched through the wasteland. Selah.
The earth shook, the heavens poured down rain before God, the One of Sinai, before God, the God of Israel.
You poured out abundant rain, God; when your inheritance was weary, you restored it.
Your people settled in it; in your goodness, God, you provided for the afflicted.
The Lord gives the word; the women who bring the good news are a great army:
"The kings of armies flee, they flee!" And the woman who stays at home divides the plunder.
Though you lie down among the sheepfolds, the wings of a dove are covered with silver, its feathers with shining gold.
When the Almighty scattered kings there, it snowed on Zalmon.
A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
Why do you look with envy, you mountains of many peaks, at the mountain God desired for his dwelling? Yes, the LORD will dwell there forever.
The chariots of God are twice ten thousand, thousands upon thousands; the Lord is among them, Sinai is in the holy place.
You went up to the heights; you led captives away; you received gifts from people, even from the rebellious, so that the LORD God might dwell there.
Blessed be the Lord, who day after day bears our burden, the God who is our salvation. Selah.
Our God is a God who saves, and to GOD the Lord belong the ways of escape from death.
Surely God will crush the heads of his enemies, the hairy crown of the one who walks in his guilt.
The Lord said, "I will bring them back from Bashan; I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so that your foot may crush them in blood, and the tongues of your dogs may have their share of the enemies."
Your processions have been seen, God, the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
The singers go in front, the musicians last, and between them young women playing tambourines.
In the assemblies bless God, the LORD, you who come from the spring of Israel.
There is little Benjamin, leading them, the princes of Judah in their throng, the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
Your God has commanded your strength. Show your strength, God, you who have acted for us.
Because of your temple at Jerusalem, kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast among the reeds, the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples, until it bows down with pieces of silver. He has scattered the peoples who delight in war.
Envoys will come from Egypt; Cush will quickly stretch out its hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God; sing praises to the Lord. Selah.
To the one who rides in the heavens, the ancient heavens! Listen, he utters his voice, a mighty voice.
Ascribe power to God, whose majesty is over Israel, and whose power is in the skies.
You are awesome, God, from your sanctuary. The God of Israel is the one who gives strength and power to his people. Blessed be God!
For the director. According to "Lilies". Of David.
Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck.
I sink in deep mire, where there is no foothold; I have come into deep waters, and the flood sweeps over me.
I am worn out with my crying; my throat is parched. My eyes grow dim as I wait for my God.
More than the hairs of my head are those who hate me without cause; mighty are those who would destroy me, my enemies without reason. What I did not steal, must I now give back?
God, you know my folly; my guilty deeds are not hidden from you.
Do not let those who hope in you be put to shame because of me, Lord GOD of Armies; do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me, God of Israel.
For it is for your sake that I have borne insults, that shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers, a foreigner to my mother's sons.
For zeal for your house has consumed me, and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
When I wept and humbled myself with fasting, it brought insults on me.
When I made sackcloth my clothing, I became a byword to them.
Those who sit at the gate talk about me, and drunkards make songs about me.
But as for me, my prayer is to you, LORD, at a time of favor. God, in your great faithful love, answer me with your sure salvation.
Rescue me from the mire, and do not let me sink; let me be rescued from those who hate me, and from the deep waters.
Do not let the flood sweep over me, or the deep swallow me up, or the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, LORD, for your faithful love is good; in your great compassion turn to me.
Do not hide your face from your servant, for I am in distress; answer me quickly.
Come near to me and redeem me; set me free because of my enemies.
You know the insults I suffer, my shame and my disgrace; all my adversaries are before you.
Insults have broken my heart, and I am sick. I looked for sympathy, but there was none, and for comforters, but I found none.
They gave me poison for food, and for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.
Let their table before them become a trap, and a snare for those at ease.
Let their eyes be darkened so that they cannot see, and make their loins tremble continually.
Pour out your fury on them, and let your burning anger overtake them.
Let their camp be desolate; let no one live in their tents.
For they persecute the one you have struck, and they talk about the pain of those you have wounded.
Add guilt to their guilt; let them have no share in your righteousness.
Let them be blotted out of the book of the living; let them not be enrolled with the righteous.
But I am afflicted and in pain; let your salvation, God, set me safe on high.
I will praise the name of God with a song, and magnify him with thanksgiving.
This will please the LORD more than an ox, a bull with its horns and hoofs.
The humble will see it and be glad; you who seek God, let your hearts revive.
For the LORD hears the needy, and does not despise his own who are prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him, the seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion and rebuild the cities of Judah; they will live there and possess it.
The descendants of his servants will inherit it, and those who love his name will live in it.
For the director. Of David. To bring to remembrance.
God, come to rescue me; LORD, come quickly to help me!
Let those who seek my life be put to shame and confounded; let those who delight in my harm be turned back and disgraced.
Let those who say, "Aha! Aha!" turn back because of their shame.
But let all who seek you rejoice and be glad in you; let those who love your salvation say always, "Great is God!"
As for me, I am afflicted and needy; God, come quickly to me! You are my help and my deliverer; LORD, do not delay.
In you, LORD, I take refuge; let me never be put to shame.
In your righteousness rescue me and deliver me; turn your ear to me and save me.
Be a rock of refuge for me, where I can always come; you have given the command to save me, for you are my rock and my fortress.
My God, rescue me from the hand of the wicked, from the grasp of the unjust and the ruthless.
For you are my hope, Lord GOD, my trust from my youth.
On you I have leaned from birth; you are the one who brought me out from my mother's womb. My praise is always of you.
I have become like a portent to many, but you are my strong refuge.
My mouth is filled with your praise, with your splendor all day long.
Do not cast me off in the time of old age; do not abandon me when my strength fails.
For my enemies speak against me; those who watch for my life plot together,
saying, "God has abandoned him; pursue him and seize him, for there is no one to rescue him."
God, do not be far from me; my God, hurry to help me!
Let my accusers be put to shame and consumed; let those who seek my harm be covered with scorn and disgrace.
But as for me, I will always hope, and I will add to all your praise.
My mouth will tell of your righteousness, of your salvation all day long, though I do not know their number.
I will come with the mighty deeds of the Lord GOD; I will make mention of your righteousness, yours alone.
God, you have taught me from my youth, and to this day I declare your wonderful deeds.
So even to old age and gray hairs, God, do not abandon me, until I declare your strength to the next generation, your might to all who are to come.
Your righteousness, God, reaches to the heights, you who have done great things. God, who is like you?
You who have made me see many troubles and calamities will give me life again; from the depths of the earth you will bring me up again.
You will increase my greatness, and turn and comfort me.
I too will praise you with the harp for your faithfulness, my God; I will sing praises to you with the lyre, Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy when I sing praises to you, and so will my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue too will speak of your righteousness all day long, for those who seek my harm have been put to shame and disgraced.
Of Solomon. God, give the king your justice, and the king's son your righteousness.
May he judge your people with righteousness, and your afflicted ones with justice.
May the mountains bring well-being to the people, and the hills, righteousness.
May he defend the cause of the afflicted among the people, save the children of the needy, and crush the oppressor.
May they fear you as long as the sun endures, and as long as the moon, through all generations.
May he be like rain falling on mown grass, like showers that water the earth.
In his days may the righteous flourish, and peace abound, until the moon is no more.
May he rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
May the desert tribes bow down before him, and his enemies lick the dust.
May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
May all kings bow down to him, and all nations serve him.
For he rescues the needy who cry for help, and the afflicted who have no one to help them.
He has pity on the poor and the needy, and saves the lives of the needy.
From oppression and violence he redeems their life, and their blood is precious in his sight.
May he live long! May gold of Sheba be given to him; may prayer be made for him continually, and may people bless him all day long.
May there be abundant grain in the land, waving on the tops of the mountains; may its fruit be like Lebanon, and may people flourish in the cities like the grass of the field.
May his name endure forever; may his name increase as long as the sun shines. May all nations be blessed in him; may they call him happy.
Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, who alone does wonderful things.
Blessed be his glorious name forever; may the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and Amen.
The prayers of David son of Jesse are ended.
A psalm of Asaph. Truly God is good to Israel, to those who are pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled; my steps had nearly slipped.
For I envied the boastful, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked.
For they have no pangs until their death; their bodies are healthy and well fed.
They are not in trouble as others are; they are not struck as other people are.
So pride is their necklace; violence covers them like a garment.
Their eyes bulge from fatness; the imaginations of their hearts overflow.
They mock and speak with malice; from on high they threaten oppression.
They set their mouths against the heavens, and their tongues strut through the earth.
So his people turn here, and drink up waters in abundance.
And they say, "How does God know? Is there knowledge in the Most High?"
See, these are the wicked; always at ease, they increase in wealth.
Surely in vain I have kept my heart clean and washed my hands in innocence.
For I have been struck all day long, and punished every morning.
If I had said, "I will speak like this," I would have betrayed the generation of your children.
But when I tried to understand this, it was troublesome in my eyes,
until I went into the sanctuary of God; then I understood their end.
Surely you set them on slippery ground; you make them fall into ruin.
How suddenly they are destroyed, swept away completely by terrors!
Like a dream when one awakes, Lord, when you rouse yourself, you will despise their image.
When my heart was bitter, and I was pierced within,
I was senseless and did not understand; I was like a beast before you.
Yet I am always with you; you hold me by my right hand.
You guide me with your counsel, and afterward you will take me into glory.
Whom have I in heaven but you? And there is nothing on earth I desire besides you.
My flesh and my heart may fail, but God is the rock of my heart and my portion forever.
For see, those who are far from you will perish; you destroy all who are unfaithful to you.
But as for me, it is good to be near God; I have made the Lord GOD my refuge, so that I may tell of all your works.
A maskil of Asaph. God, why have you rejected us forever? Why does your anger smolder against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, which you acquired long ago, the tribe of your inheritance, which you redeemed, Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
Turn your steps to the everlasting ruins; the enemy has damaged everything in the sanctuary.
Your adversaries have roared in the midst of your meeting place; they have set up their own signs as signs.
They looked like men raising axes in a thicket of trees.
And now all its carved work they smash with hatchet and hammers.
They set your sanctuary on fire; they have desecrated the dwelling place of your name, bringing it to the ground.
They said in their hearts, "Let us crush them completely!" They burned all the meeting places of God in the land.
We do not see our signs; there is no longer any prophet, and none of us knows how long.
How long, God, will the adversary taunt? Will the enemy despise your name forever?
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand? Take it from the fold of your robe and destroy them!
Yet God is my King from of old, working salvation in the midst of the earth.
You split the sea by your strength; you broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan; you gave him as food to the creatures of the desert.
You split open springs and streams; you dried up ever-flowing rivers.
Yours is the day, and yours also the night; you established the moon and the sun.
You set all the boundaries of the earth; summer and winter, you made them.
Remember this: the enemy taunts, LORD, and a foolish people despises your name.
Do not give the life of your dove to the wild beasts; do not forget the life of your afflicted forever.
Look to the covenant, for the dark places of the land are full of the haunts of violence.
Do not let the oppressed turn back in shame; let the afflicted and the needy praise your name.
Rise up, God, plead your own cause; remember how fools taunt you all day long.
Do not forget the clamor of your adversaries, the uproar of those who rise against you, which goes up continually.
For the director. According to "Do Not Destroy". A psalm of Asaph. A song.
We give thanks to you, God, we give thanks, and your name is near; people tell of your wonderful deeds.
"When I choose the appointed time, I myself will judge with fairness.
When the earth and all who live in it melt away, it is I who hold its pillars firm. Selah.
I said to the boastful, 'Do not boast,' and to the wicked, 'Do not lift up your horn.
Do not lift up your horn on high, or speak with an arrogant neck.'"
For not from the east or from the west, and not from the wilderness, comes lifting up.
For God is the judge; he puts down one and lifts up another.
For in the hand of the LORD there is a cup, with foaming wine, richly mixed; he pours from it, and all the wicked of the earth must drain it to the dregs and drink.
But as for me, I will declare it forever; I will sing praises to the God of Jacob.
All the horns of the wicked I will cut off, but the horns of the righteous will be lifted up.
For the director. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.
God is known in Judah; his name is great in Israel.
His tent is in Salem, his dwelling place in Zion.
There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow, the shield, the sword and the weapons of war. Selah.
You are radiant, majestic, more than the mountains of prey.
The stouthearted have been plundered; they have sunk into their sleep; none of the warriors could lift their hands.
At your rebuke, God of Jacob, both chariot and horse lay stunned.
You, you are awesome! Who can stand before you once your anger is roused?
From heaven you pronounced judgment; the earth feared and was still,
when God rose up to judge, to save all the humble of the earth. Selah.
Surely human wrath will praise you; with the remnant of wrath you will clothe yourself.
Make vows to the LORD your God, and fulfill them; let all around him bring gifts to the one who is to be feared.
He cuts short the spirit of princes; he is feared by the kings of the earth.
For the director. According to Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.
My voice goes up to God, and I cry out; my voice goes up to God, and he will listen to me.
In the day of my trouble I seek the Lord; at night my hand is stretched out without growing weary; my soul refuses to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan; I meditate, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
You hold my eyelids open; I am so troubled that I cannot speak.
I think about the days of old, the years long past.
I remember my song in the night; I meditate in my heart, and my spirit searches:
"Will the Lord reject forever? Will he never again show favor?
Has his faithful love ceased forever? Has his promise come to an end for all generations?
Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he in anger shut up his compassion?" Selah.
Then I said, "This is my grief: that the right hand of the Most High has changed."
I will remember the deeds of the LORD; yes, I will remember your wonders of old.
I will meditate on all your work, and ponder your mighty deeds.
God, your way is in holiness. What god is great like God?
You are the God who works wonders; you have made known your strength among the peoples.
With your arm you redeemed your people, the descendants of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
The waters saw you, God, the waters saw you and writhed; the depths too trembled.
The clouds poured down water; the skies thundered; your arrows flashed back and forth.
The sound of your thunder was in the whirlwind; lightning lit up the world; the earth trembled and shook.
Your way was through the sea, your path through the mighty waters, yet your footprints were not seen.
You led your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
A maskil of Asaph. Listen, my people, to my instruction; turn your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable; I will pour out riddles from of old,
things that we have heard and known, that our ancestors have told us.
We will not hide them from their children; we will tell the next generation the praiseworthy deeds of the LORD, his might, and the wonders he has done.
He established a statute in Jacob, and set a law in Israel, which he commanded our ancestors to make known to their children,
so that the next generation might know them, the children yet to be born, and they in turn would rise up and tell their children,
so that they would put their confidence in God, and not forget the works of God, but keep his commands,
and so that they would not be like their ancestors, a stubborn and rebellious generation, a generation whose heart was not steadfast, whose spirit was not faithful to God.
The Ephraimites, armed with bows, turned back on the day of battle.
They did not keep God's covenant, and they refused to walk in his law.
They forgot what he had done, the wonders he had shown them.
In the sight of their ancestors he did wonders in the land of Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
He split the sea and led them through; he made the waters stand up like a heap.
He led them with the cloud by day, and all night long with the light of fire.
He split rocks in the wilderness, and gave them drink as abundant as the great deep.
He brought streams out of the rock, and made water flow down like rivers.
But they went on sinning against him, rebelling against the Most High in the desert.
They put God to the test in their hearts, demanding food for their craving.
They spoke against God; they said, "Can God spread a table in the wilderness?
True, he struck the rock, and water gushed out, and streams overflowed. But can he also give bread, or provide meat for his people?"
So when the LORD heard, he was furious; a fire was kindled against Jacob, and his anger rose against Israel,
because they did not believe in God, or trust in his salvation.
Yet he commanded the skies above, and opened the doors of heaven;
he rained down manna on them to eat, and gave them the grain of heaven.
Each of them ate the bread of the mighty; he sent them food in abundance.
He let loose the east wind in the heavens, and by his power he drove out the south wind.
He rained meat on them like dust, winged birds like the sand of the seas.
He let them fall in the middle of their camp, all around their dwellings.
So they ate and were well filled, for he gave them what they craved.
But before they had turned from their craving, while the food was still in their mouths,
the anger of God rose against them; he killed the strongest of them, and struck down the young men of Israel.
In spite of all this, they went on sinning; they did not believe in his wonders.
So he made their days vanish like a breath, and their years in sudden terror.
Whenever he killed some of them, the rest would seek him; they would turn and look eagerly for God.
They remembered that God was their rock, God Most High their redeemer.
But they flattered him with their mouths, and lied to him with their tongues.
Their hearts were not steadfast toward him; they were not faithful to his covenant.
Yet he, being compassionate, forgave their iniquity and did not destroy them; again and again he held back his anger, and did not stir up all his wrath.
He remembered that they were only flesh, a breath of wind that passes and does not return.
How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, and grieved him in the wasteland!
Again and again they put God to the test, and provoked the Holy One of Israel.
They did not remember his power, the day when he redeemed them from the adversary,
when he displayed his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the region of Zoan.
He turned their rivers into blood, so that they could not drink from their streams.
He sent swarms of flies among them, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them.
He gave their crops to the grasshopper, and the fruit of their labor to the locust.
He killed their vines with hail, and their sycamore-fig trees with frost.
He gave over their cattle to the hail, and their livestock to bolts of lightning.
He let loose on them his burning anger, fury, indignation and distress, a band of destroying angels.
He cleared a path for his anger; he did not spare them from death, but gave their lives over to the plague.
He struck down every firstborn in Egypt, the firstfruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.
Then he led out his people like sheep, and guided them like a flock in the wilderness.
He led them in safety, so that they were not afraid; but the sea covered their enemies.
He brought them to his holy land, to this mountain that his right hand had won.
He drove out nations before them, and allotted their land as an inheritance by measuring line; he settled the tribes of Israel in their tents.
Yet they tested God Most High and rebelled against him, and did not keep his statutes.
They turned away and were treacherous like their ancestors; they twisted like a faulty bow.
They provoked him to anger with their high places, and made him jealous with their carved images.
When God heard, he was furious, and he utterly rejected Israel.
He abandoned the tabernacle at Shiloh, the tent where he had dwelt among human beings.
He gave up his strength to captivity, his splendor into the hand of the adversary.
He handed his people over to the sword, and he was furious with his inheritance.
Fire consumed their young men, and their young women had no wedding songs.
Their priests fell by the sword, and their widows could not weep.
Then the Lord awoke as from sleep, like a warrior shouting because of wine.
He beat back his adversaries; he put them to everlasting shame.
He rejected the tent of Joseph, and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim;
but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion, which he loves.
He built his sanctuary like the heights, like the earth, which he founded forever.
He chose David his servant, and took him from the sheepfolds;
from following the nursing ewes he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, Israel his inheritance.
He shepherded them with integrity of heart, and guided them with skillful hands.
A psalm of Asaph. God, the nations have come into your inheritance; they have defiled your holy temple; they have made Jerusalem a heap of ruins.
They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the sky, the flesh of your faithful ones to the wild animals of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.
We have become a disgrace to our neighbors, the scorn and mockery of those around us.
How long, LORD? Will you be angry forever? Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob, and laid waste his homeland.
Do not hold against us the iniquities of former times; let your compassion come quickly to meet us, for we have been brought very low.
Help us, God of our salvation, for the sake of the glory of your name; rescue us and atone for our sins, for the sake of your name.
Why should the nations say, "Where is their God?" Before our eyes, let it be known among the nations that you avenge the blood of your servants that has been poured out.
Let the groaning of the prisoner come before you; by the greatness of your arm, preserve those condemned to die.
Pay back our neighbors sevenfold into their laps for the taunts with which they have taunted you, Lord.
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture, will give thanks to you forever; from generation to generation we will tell of your praise.
For the director. According to "Lilies". A testimony of Asaph. A psalm.
Shepherd of Israel, listen, you who lead Joseph like a flock! You who are enthroned on the cherubim, shine out!
Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up your might, and come to save us.
God, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
LORD God of Armies, how long will you smolder with anger against the prayer of your people?
You have fed them the bread of tears, and made them drink tears by the measure.
You make us an object of strife for our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves.
God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
You brought a vine out of Egypt; you drove out nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground before it; it took deep root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered with its shade, and the mighty cedars with its branches.
It sent out its boughs to the Sea, and its shoots to the River.
Why have you broken down its walls, so that all who pass along the road pluck its fruit?
The boar from the forest ravages it, and all that moves in the field feeds on it.
God of Armies, turn back, please! Look down from heaven and see; take care of this vine,
the stock that your right hand planted, and the son you made strong for yourself.
It is burned with fire; it is cut down. At the rebuke of your face they perish.
Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man you made strong for yourself.
Then we will not turn away from you; give us life, and we will call on your name.
LORD God of Armies, restore us; let your face shine, and we will be saved.
For the director. According to the Gittith. Of Asaph.
Sing for joy to God our strength; shout aloud to the God of Jacob.
Raise a song and sound the tambourine, the sweet lyre with the harp.
Blow the ram's horn at the new moon, at the full moon, on the day of our festival.
For this is a decree for Israel, a ruling of the God of Jacob.
He made it a statute in Joseph when he went out against the land of Egypt. I heard a voice I did not know:
"I removed the burden from his shoulder; his hands were set free from the basket.
In distress you called, and I rescued you; I answered you from the hiding place of the thunder; I tested you at the waters of Meribah. Selah.
Hear, my people, and I will warn you; Israel, if only you would listen to me!
There shall be no strange god among you; you shall not bow down to a foreign god.
I am the LORD your God, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people did not listen to my voice, and Israel would have none of me.
So I let them go their way in the stubbornness of their hearts, to follow their own plans.
If only my people would listen to me, if only Israel would walk in my ways!
I would soon subdue their enemies, and turn my hand against their adversaries.
Those who hate the LORD would come cringing to him, and their time would last forever.
But he would feed you with the finest of the wheat, and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you."
A psalm of Asaph. God takes his stand in the divine council; in the midst of the gods he gives judgment:
"How long will you judge unjustly, and show favor to the wicked? Selah.
Give justice to the poor and the fatherless; uphold the rights of the afflicted and the destitute.
Rescue the poor and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked."
They do not know, and they do not understand; they walk about in darkness. All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
"I said, 'You are gods; you are all sons of the Most High.'
But you will die like human beings, and fall like any of the princes."
Rise up, God, judge the earth, for all the nations are your inheritance.
A song. A psalm of Asaph.
God, do not keep silent; do not be quiet, and do not be still, God.
For look, your enemies are in an uproar; those who hate you have raised their heads.
Against your people they make crafty plans; they conspire against those you shelter.
They say, "Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel will be remembered no more."
For they conspire with one mind; against you they make a covenant:
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal and Ammon and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
Assyria too has joined them; they have become the strong arm of the descendants of Lot. Selah.
Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the Kishon River,
who were destroyed at En-dor, who became dung for the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, and all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, "Let us take possession for ourselves of the pastures of God."
My God, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind.
As fire burns a forest, and as a flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with your tempest, and terrify them with your storm.
Fill their faces with shame, so that they will seek your name, LORD.
Let them be put to shame and terrified forever; let them be disgraced and perish.
Let them know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
For the director. According to the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
How lovely is your dwelling place, LORD of Armies!
My soul longs, it even faints for the courts of the LORD; my heart and my flesh sing for joy to the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home, and the swallow a nest for herself, where she may lay her young, at your altars, LORD of Armies, my King and my God.
Happy are those who live in your house; they will praise you continually. Selah.
Happy are those whose strength is in you, whose hearts are set on the highways.
As they pass through the Valley of Baca, they make it a place of springs; the early rain also covers it with blessings.
They go from strength to strength; each one appears before God in Zion.
LORD God of Armies, hear my prayer; listen, God of Jacob. Selah.
Look on our shield, God; look on the face of your anointed.
For a day in your courts is better than a thousand elsewhere. I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God than live in the tents of wickedness.
For the LORD God is a sun and a shield; the LORD gives grace and glory. He does not hold back any good thing from those who walk blamelessly.
LORD of Armies, happy is the one who trusts in you.
For the director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
LORD, you have shown favor to your land; you have restored the fortunes of Jacob.
You have forgiven the iniquity of your people; you have covered all their sin. Selah.
You have withdrawn all your fury; you have turned from your burning anger.
Restore us, God of our salvation, and put an end to your displeasure toward us.
Will you be angry with us forever? Will you drag out your anger to all generations?
Will you not give us life again, so that your people may rejoice in you?
Show us your faithful love, LORD, and grant us your salvation.
Let me hear what God, the LORD, will say, for he will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones; but let them not turn back to folly.
Surely his salvation is near to those who fear him, so that glory may dwell in our land.
Faithful love and faithfulness have met; righteousness and peace have kissed.
Faithfulness springs up from the earth, and righteousness looks down from heaven.
The LORD will indeed give what is good, and our land will yield its harvest.
Righteousness will go before him, and make a path for his steps.
A prayer of David. Turn your ear, LORD, and answer me, for I am afflicted and needy.
Guard my life, for I am faithful; you are my God; save your servant, who trusts in you.
Be gracious to me, Lord, for I call to you all day long.
Make your servant's soul glad, for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good and forgiving, abounding in faithful love to all who call on you.
Listen, LORD, to my prayer, and pay attention to the sound of my pleas for mercy.
In the day of my trouble I call on you, for you will answer me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord, and there are no works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come and bow down before you, Lord, and they will glorify your name.
For you are great, and you do wonders; you alone are God.
Teach me your way, LORD, so that I may walk in your truth; give me an undivided heart to fear your name.
I will give thanks to you, Lord my God, with all my heart, and I will glorify your name forever.
For your faithful love toward me is great; you have rescued my life from the depths of Sheol.
God, the arrogant have risen against me, and a band of ruthless men seeks my life; they do not set you before them.
But you, Lord, are a God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in faithful love and faithfulness.
Turn to me and be gracious to me; give your strength to your servant, and save the son of your female servant.
Show me a sign of your goodness, so that those who hate me may see it and be put to shame, for you, LORD, have helped me and comforted me.
Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song. The city he founded stands on the holy mountains.
The LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you, city of God. Selah.
"I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who know me; look, Philistia and Tyre, with Cush: 'This one was born there.'"
And of Zion it will be said, "Each one and every one was born in her," and the Most High himself will establish her.
The LORD will record, as he registers the peoples, "This one was born there." Selah.
Singers and dancers alike say, "All my springs are in you."
A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the director. According to Mahalath Leannoth. A maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.
LORD, God of my salvation, by day I cry out, and by night, before you.
Let my prayer come before you; turn your ear to my cry.
For my soul is full of troubles, and my life draws near to Sheol.
I am counted among those who go down to the pit; I have become like a man without strength,
left alone among the dead, like the slain who lie in the grave, whom you remember no more, for they are cut off from your hand.
You have put me in the lowest pit, in dark places, in the depths.
Your wrath lies heavy on me, and you have afflicted me with all your breakers. Selah.
You have taken my friends far from me; you have made me a horror to them. I am shut in, and I cannot get out.
My eye grows dim from affliction. I call on you, LORD, every day; I spread out my hands to you.
Do you work wonders for the dead? Do the shades rise up to praise you? Selah.
Is your faithful love told in the grave, your faithfulness in Abaddon?
Are your wonders known in the darkness, or your righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
But I cry to you for help, LORD; in the morning my prayer comes before you.
Why, LORD, do you reject my soul? Why do you hide your face from me?
I have been afflicted and close to death from my youth; I bear your terrors; I am helpless.
Your burning anger has swept over me; your terrors have destroyed me.
They surround me like water all day long; they close in on me together.
You have taken lover and friend far from me; darkness is my only companion.
A maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.
I will sing of the faithful love of the LORD forever; with my mouth I will make your faithfulness known to all generations.
For I said, "Faithful love will be built up forever; in the heavens you will establish your faithfulness."
"I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant:
'I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.'" Selah.
The heavens praise your wonders, LORD, and your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies can compare with the LORD? Who among the sons of the gods is like the LORD,
a God greatly feared in the council of the holy ones, and awesome above all who are around him?
LORD God of Armies, who is like you? You are mighty, LORD, and your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule the raging of the sea; when its waves rise, you calm them.
You crushed Rahab like one who is slain; with your strong arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours as well; the world and all that fills it, you founded them.
The north and the south, you created them; Tabor and Hermon sing for joy at your name.
Yours is an arm with might; your hand is strong, your right hand is raised high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; faithful love and faithfulness go before you.
Happy are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, LORD, in the light of your face.
In your name they rejoice all day long, and in your righteousness they are lifted up.
For you are the glory of their strength, and by your favor our horn is lifted high.
For our shield belongs to the LORD, and our king to the Holy One of Israel.
Once you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones, and said, "I have given help to a mighty man; I have raised up one chosen from the people.
I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.
My hand will be with him to support him; my arm also will strengthen him.
No enemy will get the better of him; no wicked man will humble him.
I will crush his adversaries before him, and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my faithful love will be with him, and through my name his horn will be lifted high.
I will set his hand on the sea, and his right hand on the rivers.
He will call to me, 'You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation.'
I will also make him my firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth.
I will keep my faithful love for him forever, and my covenant with him will stand firm.
I will establish his offspring forever, and his throne as long as the heavens endure.
If his sons forsake my law, and do not walk in my rulings,
if they violate my decrees, and do not keep my commands,
then I will punish their transgression with the rod, and their iniquity with blows.
But I will not take my faithful love away from him, or be false to my faithfulness.
I will not violate my covenant, or change what my lips have spoken.
Once for all I have sworn by my holiness; I will not lie to David.
His offspring will endure forever, and his throne will be like the sun before me.
Like the moon it will be established forever, a faithful witness in the skies." Selah.
But you have rejected and spurned him; you are furious with your anointed.
You have renounced the covenant with your servant; you have defiled his crown in the dust.
You have broken down all his walls; you have made his strongholds a ruin.
All who pass along the road plunder him; he has become a disgrace to his neighbors.
You have raised the right hand of his adversaries; you have made all his enemies rejoice.
You have also turned back the edge of his sword, and you have not made him stand in battle.
You have put an end to his splendor, and hurled his throne to the ground.
You have cut short the days of his youth; you have covered him with shame. Selah.
How long, LORD? Will you hide yourself forever? Will your wrath burn like fire?
Remember how short my life is! For what futility you have created all humankind!
Who can live and never see death? Who can rescue his life from the power of Sheol? Selah.
Lord, where are your former acts of faithful love, which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, how your servants are taunted, how I carry in my heart the insults of all the many peoples,
with which your enemies have taunted, LORD, with which they have taunted the footsteps of your anointed.
Blessed be the LORD forever. Amen and Amen.
A prayer of Moses, the man of God. Lord, you have been our dwelling place in every generation.
Before the mountains were born, before you brought forth the earth and the world, from everlasting to everlasting you are God.
You turn human beings back to dust, and say, "Return, children of humankind."
For a thousand years in your sight are like yesterday when it has passed, like a watch in the night.
You sweep them away; they are like a sleep. In the morning they are like grass that springs up;
in the morning it flourishes and springs up; by evening it withers and dries up.
For we are consumed by your anger, and by your wrath we are terrified.
You have set our iniquities before you, our secret sins in the light of your face.
For all our days pass away under your fury; we finish our years like a sigh.
The days of our years are seventy years, or eighty if we are strong; yet the best of them is toil and trouble, for they are soon gone, and we fly away.
Who knows the power of your anger? Your wrath is as great as the fear that is due to you.
So teach us to count our days, so that we may gain a heart of wisdom.
Turn back, LORD! How long? Have compassion on your servants.
Satisfy us in the morning with your faithful love, so that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen trouble.
Let your work be seen by your servants, and your splendor by their children.
May the favor of the Lord our God be on us. Establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
Whoever lives in the shelter of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say to the LORD, "My refuge and my fortress, my God, in whom I trust."
For he will rescue you from the snare of the fowler, and from the deadly plague.
He will cover you with his feathers, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and a wall.
You will not fear the terror of the night, or the arrow that flies by day,
or the plague that stalks in the darkness, or the destruction that lays waste at noon.
A thousand may fall at your side, and ten thousand at your right hand, but it will not come near you.
You will only look with your eyes and see the punishment of the wicked.
For you, LORD, are my refuge! You have made the Most High your dwelling place;
no harm will befall you, and no plague will come near your tent.
For he will command his angels concerning you, to guard you in all your ways.
They will lift you up in their hands, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.
You will tread on the lion and the cobra; you will trample the young lion and the serpent.
"Because he holds fast to me in love, I will rescue him; I will set him safe on high, because he knows my name.
He will call on me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will deliver him and honor him.
With long life I will satisfy him, and show him my salvation."
A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.
It is good to give thanks to the LORD, and to sing praise to your name, Most High,
to declare your faithful love in the morning, and your faithfulness by night,
on the ten-stringed instrument and on the harp, to the melody of the lyre.
For you have made me glad, LORD, by what you have done; I sing for joy at the works of your hands.
How great are your works, LORD! How very deep are your thoughts!
The senseless man does not know, and the fool does not understand this:
though the wicked sprout like grass, and all evildoers flourish, they will be destroyed forever.
But you, LORD, are on high forever.
For look, your enemies, LORD, for look, your enemies will perish; all evildoers will be scattered.
But you have raised my horn like that of the wild ox; I am anointed with fresh oil.
My eyes have looked in triumph on those who lie in wait for me; my ears have heard the downfall of the evildoers who rise against me.
The righteous will flourish like the palm tree, and grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of the LORD, they will flourish in the courts of our God.
They will still bear fruit in old age; they will stay full of sap and green,
to declare that the LORD is upright; he is my rock, and there is no injustice in him.
The LORD reigns; he is clothed with majesty. The LORD is clothed; he has wrapped himself in strength. The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved.
Your throne was established long ago; you are from everlasting.
The floods have lifted up, LORD, the floods have lifted up their voice; the floods lift up their pounding waves.
Mightier than the sound of many waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea, is the LORD, mighty on high.
Your statutes are very trustworthy; holiness befits your house, LORD, for all time to come.
God of vengeance, LORD, God of vengeance, shine out!
Rise up, Judge of the earth; pay back to the proud what they deserve.
How long will the wicked, LORD, how long will the wicked exult?
They pour out arrogant words; all the evildoers boast.
They crush your people, LORD, and afflict your inheritance.
They kill the widow and the foreigner, and murder the fatherless.
They say, "The LORD does not see; the God of Jacob pays no attention."
Understand, you senseless among the people! You fools, when will you be wise?
He who planted the ear, does he not hear? He who formed the eye, does he not see?
He who disciplines the nations, does he not punish, he who teaches humankind knowledge?
The LORD knows the thoughts of humankind, that they are only a breath.
Happy is the one you discipline, LORD, and whom you teach from your law,
to give him rest from days of trouble, until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For the LORD will not abandon his people; he will not forsake his inheritance.
For justice will again be righteous, and all the upright in heart will follow it.
Who will rise up for me against evildoers? Who will take a stand for me against evildoers?
If the LORD had not been my help, my soul would soon have lived in the land of silence.
When I said, "My foot is slipping," your faithful love, LORD, held me up.
When my anxious thoughts multiply within me, your comforts delight my soul.
Can a throne of destruction be allied with you, one that frames trouble by decree?
They band together against the life of the righteous, and condemn the innocent to death.
But the LORD has become my stronghold, and my God the rock of my refuge.
He will turn their own iniquity back on them, and destroy them for their wickedness; the LORD our God will destroy them.
Come, let us sing for joy to the LORD; let us shout aloud to the rock of our salvation.
Let us come before him with thanksgiving; let us shout aloud to him with songs of praise.
For the LORD is a great God, and a great King above all gods.
In his hand are the depths of the earth, and the peaks of the mountains are his.
The sea is his, for he made it, and his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us bow down and worship; let us kneel before the LORD our Maker.
For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, the sheep of his hand. Today, if only you would listen to his voice:
"Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
when your ancestors tested me; they put me to the test, though they had seen what I had done.
For forty years I loathed that generation, and I said, 'They are a people whose hearts go astray, and they do not know my ways.'
So I swore in my anger, 'They shall never enter my rest.'"
Sing to the LORD a new song; sing to the LORD, all the earth.
Sing to the LORD, bless his name; proclaim his salvation day after day.
Declare his glory among the nations, his wonders among all the peoples.
For the LORD is great and greatly to be praised; he is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before him; strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
Ascribe to the LORD, you families of the peoples, ascribe to the LORD glory and strength.
Ascribe to the LORD the glory due his name; bring an offering and come into his courts.
Worship the LORD in the splendor of holiness; tremble before him, all the earth.
Say among the nations, "The LORD reigns! The world is firmly established; it cannot be moved. He will judge the peoples with fairness."
Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let the sea roar, and all that fills it;
let the fields exult, and everything in them. Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before the LORD, for he comes, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with his faithfulness.
The LORD reigns! Let the earth rejoice; let the many coastlands be glad.
Clouds and thick darkness surround him; righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
Fire goes before him and burns up his adversaries all around.
His lightnings light up the world; the earth sees and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax before the LORD, before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens proclaim his righteousness, and all the peoples see his glory.
All who serve carved images are put to shame, those who boast in idols. Bow down to him, all you gods!
Zion hears and rejoices, and the daughters of Judah exult because of your judgments, LORD.
For you, LORD, are the Most High over all the earth; you are exalted far above all gods.
You who love the LORD, hate evil! He guards the lives of his faithful ones; he rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart.
Rejoice in the LORD, you righteous, and give thanks to his holy name.
A psalm. Sing to the LORD a new song, for he has done wonders; his right hand and his holy arm have won him victory.
The LORD has made his salvation known; in the sight of the nations he has revealed his righteousness.
He has remembered his faithful love and his faithfulness to the house of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.
Shout aloud to the LORD, all the earth; break out in songs of joy and sing praises.
Sing praises to the LORD with the lyre, with the lyre and the sound of song.
With trumpets and the sound of the ram's horn, shout aloud before the King, the LORD.
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it, the world and those who live in it.
Let the rivers clap their hands; let the mountains sing for joy together
before the LORD, for he comes to judge the earth. He will judge the world with righteousness, and the peoples with fairness.
The LORD reigns! Let the peoples tremble! He is enthroned on the cherubim; let the earth quake!
The LORD is great in Zion; he is exalted above all the peoples.
Let them praise your great and awesome name. Holy is he!
The King in his might loves justice. You have established fairness; you have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at his footstool. Holy is he!
Moses and Aaron were among his priests, and Samuel among those who called on his name. They called to the LORD, and he answered them.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud; they kept his statutes and the decree he gave them.
LORD our God, you answered them; you were a God who forgave them, yet you punished their misdeeds.
Exalt the LORD our God, and bow down at his holy mountain, for the LORD our God is holy.
A psalm for thanksgiving. Shout aloud to the LORD, all the earth!
Serve the LORD with gladness; come before him with songs of joy.
Know that the LORD is God. It is he who made us, and we are his; we are his people, the sheep of his pasture.
Enter his gates with thanksgiving, and his courts with praise; give thanks to him, bless his name.
For the LORD is good; his faithful love endures forever, and his faithfulness to all generations.
Of David. A psalm. I will sing of faithful love and justice; to you, LORD, I will sing praise.
I will pay attention to the blameless way. When will you come to me? I will walk with integrity of heart within my house.
I will not set anything worthless before my eyes. I hate the deeds of those who turn aside; they will not cling to me.
A crooked heart will be far from me; I will have nothing to do with evil.
Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, him I will silence; whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart, him I will not tolerate.
My eyes will be on the faithful in the land, so that they may live with me; whoever walks in the blameless way will serve me.
No one who practices deceit will live in my house; no one who tells lies will stand firm in my sight.
Morning by morning I will silence all the wicked in the land, cutting off all evildoers from the city of the LORD.
A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his complaint before the LORD.
LORD, hear my prayer; let my cry for help come to you.
Do not hide your face from me in the day of my distress; turn your ear to me; in the day I call, answer me quickly.
For my days vanish like smoke, and my bones burn like a hearth.
My heart is struck down like grass and has withered; I even forget to eat my bread.
Because of my loud groaning, my bones cling to my flesh.
I am like a pelican in the wilderness; I have become like a little owl among the ruins.
I lie awake; I have become like a lonely bird on a roof.
All day long my enemies taunt me; those who mock me use my name as a curse.
For I eat ashes like bread, and mix my drink with tears,
because of your indignation and your anger, for you have lifted me up and thrown me away.
My days are like a lengthening shadow; I wither away like grass.
But you, LORD, sit enthroned forever, and your name endures through all generations.
You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to be gracious to her; the appointed time has come.
For your servants hold her stones dear, and have pity on her dust.
The nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth your glory.
For the LORD will build up Zion; he will appear in his glory.
He will turn to the prayer of the destitute, and will not despise their prayer.
Let this be written down for a generation to come, so that a people yet to be created may praise the LORD:
that he looked down from his holy height; from heaven the LORD gazed on the earth,
to hear the groaning of the prisoner, to set free those condemned to die,
so that the name of the LORD may be declared in Zion, and his praise in Jerusalem,
when the peoples gather together, and the kingdoms, to serve the LORD.
He has broken my strength on the way; he has cut short my days.
I say, "My God, do not take me away in the middle of my days, you whose years go on through all generations.
Long ago you laid the foundation of the earth, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you will remain; they will all wear out like a garment. You will change them like clothing, and they will pass away.
But you are the same, and your years will have no end.
The children of your servants will live secure, and their offspring will be established before you."
Of David. Bless the LORD, my soul, and all that is within me, bless his holy name.
Bless the LORD, my soul, and do not forget all his benefits:
he forgives all your iniquity; he heals all your diseases;
he redeems your life from the pit; he crowns you with faithful love and compassion;
he satisfies you with good things as long as you live, so that your youth is renewed like the eagle's.
The LORD does what is right, and brings justice for all who are oppressed.
He made known his ways to Moses, his deeds to the people of Israel.
The LORD is compassionate and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love.
He will not always accuse, nor will he keep his anger forever.
He has not dealt with us according to our sins, or repaid us according to our iniquities.
For as high as the heavens are above the earth, so great is his faithful love toward those who fear him.
As far as the east is from the west, so far has he removed our transgressions from us.
As a father has compassion on his children, so the LORD has compassion on those who fear him.
For he knows how we are formed; he remembers that we are dust.
As for human beings, their days are like grass; they flourish like a flower of the field;
when the wind passes over it, it is gone, and its place knows it no more.
But the faithful love of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting on those who fear him, and his righteousness to their children's children,
to those who keep his covenant and remember to do his precepts.
The LORD has established his throne in the heavens, and his kingdom rules over all.
Bless the LORD, you his angels, you mighty ones who carry out his word, who obey the voice of his word.
Bless the LORD, all his armies, you his servants who do his will.
Bless the LORD, all his works, in all places where he rules. Bless the LORD, my soul.
Bless the LORD, my soul! LORD my God, you are very great; you are clothed with splendor and majesty.
He wraps himself in light as in a robe; he stretches out the heavens like a tent curtain.
He lays the beams of his upper rooms on the waters; he makes the clouds his chariot; he rides on the wings of the wind.
He makes the winds his messengers, flames of fire his servants.
He set the earth on its foundations, so that it will never be moved.
You covered it with the deep as with a garment; the waters stood above the mountains.
At your rebuke they fled; at the sound of your thunder they hurried away.
They went up the mountains; they went down into the valleys, to the place you appointed for them.
You set a boundary they may not pass, so that they will not return to cover the earth.
He makes springs gush out into the valleys; they flow between the hills.
They give drink to every wild animal; the wild donkeys quench their thirst.
Beside them the birds of the sky have their homes; they sing among the branches.
He waters the mountains from his upper rooms; the earth is satisfied with the fruit of your works.
He makes grass grow for the cattle, and plants for people to cultivate, to bring forth food from the earth,
and wine to gladden the human heart, oil to make faces shine, and bread to strengthen the human heart.
The trees of the LORD drink their fill, the cedars of Lebanon that he planted,
where the birds build their nests; the stork has her home in the junipers.
The high mountains are for the wild goats; the crags are a refuge for the rock badgers.
He made the moon to mark the seasons; the sun knows when to set.
You bring darkness, and it is night, when all the animals of the forest creep about.
The young lions roar for their prey, seeking their food from God.
When the sun rises, they withdraw and lie down in their dens.
People go out to their work, and to their labor until evening.
How many are your works, LORD! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
There is the sea, great and wide, teeming with creatures beyond number, living things both small and great.
There the ships go to and fro, and Leviathan, which you formed to play in it.
All of them look to you to give them their food at the right time.
When you give it to them, they gather it up; when you open your hand, they are filled with good things.
When you hide your face, they are terrified; when you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust.
When you send out your Spirit, they are created, and you renew the face of the ground.
May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in his works,
he who looks at the earth, and it trembles, who touches the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praise to my God while I have being.
May my meditation be pleasing to him; I rejoice in the LORD.
Let sinners vanish from the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the LORD, my soul! Praise the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name. Make known his deeds among the peoples.
Sing to him, sing praises to him; tell of all his wonders.
Glory in his holy name; let the hearts of those who seek the LORD rejoice.
Seek the LORD and his strength; seek his face always.
Remember the wonders he has done, his miracles and the judgments he has spoken,
you offspring of Abraham his servant, children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the LORD our God; his judgments are in all the earth.
He remembers his covenant forever, the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant he made with Abraham, his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed it to Jacob as a decree, to Israel as an everlasting covenant,
saying, "To you I will give the land of Canaan as the portion of your inheritance."
When they were few in number, very few, and foreigners in the land,
they wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no one to oppress them; he rebuked kings on their account:
"Do not touch my anointed ones; do not harm my prophets."
He called down a famine on the land; he broke every staff of bread.
He sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.
They hurt his foot with shackles; his neck was put in iron,
until the time that his word came true; the word of the LORD tested him.
The king sent and released him; the ruler of peoples set him free.
He made him lord of his household, and ruler over all his possessions,
to bind his princes as he pleased, and to teach his elders wisdom.
Then Israel came to Egypt; Jacob lived as a foreigner in the land of Ham.
The LORD made his people very fruitful, and made them stronger than their adversaries.
He turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal craftily with his servants.
He sent Moses his servant, and Aaron, whom he had chosen.
They performed his signs among them, and wonders in the land of Ham.
He sent darkness and made it dark, and they did not rebel against his word.
He turned their waters into blood, and killed their fish.
Their land swarmed with frogs, even in the chambers of their kings.
He spoke, and there came swarms of flies, and gnats throughout their country.
He gave them hail for rain, and flaming fire throughout their land.
He struck down their vines and their fig trees, and shattered the trees of their country.
He spoke, and the locusts came, and young locusts without number.
They devoured all the plants in their land, and devoured the fruit of their ground.
He struck down all the firstborn in their land, the first fruit of all their strength.
He brought them out with silver and gold, and among his tribes no one stumbled.
Egypt was glad when they left, for dread of them had fallen on the Egyptians.
He spread out a cloud as a covering, and fire to give light by night.
They asked, and he brought quail, and satisfied them with the bread of heaven.
He opened the rock, and water gushed out; it flowed through the desert like a river.
For he remembered his holy word to Abraham his servant.
He brought out his people with joy, his chosen ones with shouts of joy.
He gave them the lands of the nations, and they took possession of what the peoples had toiled for,
so that they would keep his decrees and observe his laws. Praise the LORD!
Praise the LORD! Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love endures forever.
Who can tell of the mighty deeds of the LORD, or proclaim all his praise?
Happy are those who keep justice, who do what is right at all times.
Remember me, LORD, when you show favor to your people; come to me with your salvation,
so that I may see the prosperity of your chosen ones, rejoice in the joy of your nation, and glory together with your inheritance.
We have sinned, as our ancestors did; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.
Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand your wonders; they did not remember your many acts of faithful love, but they rebelled by the sea, at the Red Sea.
Yet he saved them for the sake of his name, to make his might known.
He rebuked the Red Sea, and it dried up; he led them through the depths as through a desert.
He saved them from the hand of those who hated them, and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
The waters covered their adversaries; not one of them was left.
Then they believed his words; they sang his praise.
But they soon forgot what he had done; they did not wait for his counsel.
They gave in to their craving in the wilderness, and put God to the test in the desert.
He gave them what they asked for, but sent a wasting disease among them.
In the camp they grew jealous of Moses, and of Aaron, the holy one of the LORD.
The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram.
Fire blazed among their company; flames burned up the wicked.
They made a calf at Horeb and bowed down to a cast image.
They exchanged their Glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.
They forgot God their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham, awesome deeds by the Red Sea.
So he said he would destroy them, had not Moses, his chosen one, stood in the breach before him, to turn his wrath away from destroying them.
Then they despised the pleasant land; they did not believe his word.
They grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to the voice of the LORD.
So he raised his hand against them, to make them fall in the wilderness,
to make their offspring fall among the nations, and to scatter them through the lands.
They joined in the worship of the Baal of Peor, and ate sacrifices offered to the dead.
They provoked him to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
Then Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague was stopped.
That was credited to him as righteousness, from generation to generation forever.
They angered him at the waters of Meribah, and it went badly for Moses because of them;
for they rebelled against his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
They did not destroy the peoples, as the LORD had told them to,
but they mixed with the nations and learned their ways.
They served their idols, which became a snare to them.
They sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
They shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was defiled with blood.
They made themselves unclean by what they did, and prostituted themselves by their deeds.
So the anger of the LORD burned against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance.
He handed them over to the nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
Their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their power.
Many times he rescued them, but they kept rebelling in their plans, and they sank down in their iniquity.
Yet he looked on their distress when he heard their cry.
For their sake he remembered his covenant, and relented according to his many acts of faithful love.
He caused them to be pitied by all who held them captive.
Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, so that we may give thanks to your holy name and glory in your praise.
Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Let all the people say, "Amen!" Praise the LORD!
Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his faithful love endures forever.
Let the redeemed of the LORD say so, those he redeemed from the hand of the adversary,
and gathered from the lands, from the east and from the west, from the north and from the sea.
Some wandered in the wilderness, in the desert wastes; they found no way to a city to live in.
They were hungry and thirsty; their soul fainted within them.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he rescued them from their distress.
He led them by a straight road, to go to a city to live in.
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
For he satisfies the thirsty soul, and fills the hungry soul with good things.
Some sat in darkness and deep darkness, prisoners in misery and in iron,
because they had rebelled against the words of God, and spurned the counsel of the Most High.
So he humbled their hearts with hard labor; they stumbled, and there was no one to help.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
He brought them out of darkness and deep darkness, and snapped their chains.
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
For he shatters the doors of bronze, and cuts through the bars of iron.
Some were fools because of their rebellious ways, and suffered affliction because of their iniquities.
They loathed all food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he saved them from their distress.
He sent out his word and healed them, and rescued them from their graves.
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving, and tell of his deeds with songs of joy.
Some went down to the sea in ships, doing business on the great waters.
They saw the works of the LORD, his wonders in the deep.
For he spoke and raised a stormy wind, which lifted high the waves of the sea.
They went up to the heavens; they went down to the depths; their courage melted away in their peril.
They reeled and staggered like drunkards, and all their skill was swallowed up.
Then they cried out to the LORD in their trouble, and he brought them out of their distress.
He made the storm a calm, and its waves were still.
They were glad when it grew quiet, and he guided them to the harbor they longed for.
Let them give thanks to the LORD for his faithful love, and for his wonders for humankind.
Let them exalt him in the assembly of the people, and praise him in the council of the elders.
He turns rivers into a desert, and springs of water into thirsty ground,
a fruitful land into a salt waste, because of the wickedness of those who live there.
He turns a desert into pools of water, and dry land into springs of water.
There he settles the hungry, and they establish a city to live in.
They sow fields and plant vineyards, and gather a fruitful harvest.
He blesses them, and they become very many, and he does not let their cattle decrease.
When they are diminished and brought low through oppression, trouble and sorrow,
he pours contempt on nobles, and makes them wander in a trackless waste;
but he lifts the needy out of affliction, and makes their families like flocks.
The upright see it and are glad, and all injustice shuts its mouth.
Whoever is wise, let him heed these things, and consider the acts of faithful love of the LORD.
A song. A psalm of David.
My heart is steadfast, God; I will sing and make music, with my glory too.
Wake up, harp and lyre! I will wake the dawn.
I will give thanks to you among the peoples, LORD; I will sing praise to you among the nations.
For your faithful love is great, above the heavens, and your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be exalted above the heavens, God; let your glory be over all the earth.
So that those you love may be rescued, save by your right hand, and answer me.
God has spoken in his holiness: "I will exult; I will divide up Shechem, and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, Manasseh is mine; Ephraim is the helmet on my head; Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my washbasin; on Edom I throw my sandal; over Philistia I shout in triumph."
Who will bring me to the fortified city? Who will lead me to Edom?
Have you not rejected us, God? You no longer go out, God, with our armies.
Give us help against the adversary, for human help is worthless.
With God we will do valiantly; he will trample our adversaries.
For the director. Of David. A psalm. God of my praise, do not be silent!
For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me; they speak against me with a lying tongue.
They surround me with words of hatred, and attack me without cause.
In return for my love they accuse me, but I am in prayer.
They repay me evil for good, and hatred for my love.
Appoint a wicked man against him; let an accuser stand at his right hand.
When he is judged, let him come out guilty, and let his prayer be counted as sin.
May his days be few; may another take his office.
May his children be fatherless, and his wife a widow.
May his children wander about and beg, searching for food far from their ruined homes.
May the creditor seize all that he has; may strangers plunder the fruit of his labor.
May there be no one to show him faithful love, and no one to have pity on his fatherless children.
May his descendants be cut off; may their name be blotted out in the next generation.
May the iniquity of his ancestors be remembered before the LORD, and do not let the sin of his mother be blotted out.
Let them be before the LORD continually, and may he cut off their memory from the earth,
because he did not remember to show faithful love, but hounded the afflicted and needy man, and the brokenhearted, to put them to death.
He loved cursing, and it has come on him; he took no pleasure in blessing, and it has stayed far from him.
He clothed himself with cursing as with his robe; it has soaked into his body like water, and into his bones like oil.
May it be to him like a garment he wraps around himself, like a belt he always wears.
May this be the reward of my accusers from the LORD, of those who speak evil against my life.
But you, GOD my Lord, deal with me for the sake of your name; because your faithful love is good, rescue me.
For I am afflicted and needy, and my heart is pierced within me.
I fade away like a lengthening shadow; I am shaken off like a locust.
My knees give way from fasting; my body has grown thin and gaunt.
I have become a disgrace to them; when they see me, they shake their heads.
Help me, LORD my God; save me according to your faithful love.
Let them know that this is your hand, that you, LORD, have done it.
Let them curse, but you will bless. When they rise up, let them be put to shame, and let your servant rejoice.
May my accusers be clothed with disgrace, and wrapped in their own shame as in a cloak.
With my mouth I will give great thanks to the LORD; I will praise him in the midst of the crowd.
For he stands at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who would condemn him to death.
Of David. A psalm. The LORD says to my lord: "Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet."
The LORD will extend your mighty scepter from Zion. Rule in the midst of your enemies!
Your people will offer themselves willingly on the day of your power, in holy splendor. From the womb of the dawn, the dew of your youth is yours.
The LORD has sworn an oath and will not change his mind: "You are a priest forever, after the manner of Melchizedek."
The Lord is at your right hand; he will shatter kings on the day of his wrath.
He will judge among the nations, heaping up corpses; he will shatter heads across the wide earth.
He will drink from the stream by the way; so he will lift up his head.
Praise the LORD! I will give thanks to the LORD with all my heart, in the council of the upright and in the assembly.
Great are the works of the LORD, studied by all who delight in them.
Splendor and majesty are his work, and his righteousness endures forever.
He has made his wonders to be remembered; the LORD is gracious and compassionate.
He gives food to those who fear him; he remembers his covenant forever.
He has shown his people the power of his works, giving them the inheritance of the nations.
