I went down to the walnut grove to look at the green shoots of the valley, to see whether the vine had budded, whether the pomegranates were in bloom.
Before I knew it, my desire set me among the chariots of my noble people.
Turn back, turn back, O Shulammite! Turn back, turn back, that we may look at you! Why would you look at the Shulammite, as at the dance of the two camps?
How beautiful are your feet in sandals, O noble daughter! The curves of your thighs are like jewels, the work of a craftsman's hands.
Your navel is a rounded bowl; may it never lack mixed wine. Your belly is a heap of wheat, encircled with lilies.
Your two breasts are like two fawns, twins of a gazelle.
Your neck is like a tower of ivory. Your eyes are pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon, looking out toward Damascus.
Your head crowns you like Carmel, and the flowing hair of your head is like purple; a king is held captive in its tresses.
How beautiful you are, and how pleasant, O love, with its delights!
Your stature is like a palm tree, and your breasts are like its clusters.
I said, "I will climb the palm tree; I will take hold of its fruit." Oh, may your breasts be like clusters of the vine, and the fragrance of your breath like apples,
and your mouth like the best wine, going down smoothly for my beloved, gliding over the lips of sleepers.
I am my beloved's, and his desire is for me.
Come, my beloved, let us go out into the fields; let us spend the night in the villages.
Let us go early to the vineyards; let us see whether the vine has budded, whether its blossoms have opened, whether the pomegranates are in bloom. There I will give you my love.
The mandrakes give out their fragrance, and at our doors are all kinds of choice fruits, new as well as old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.
Oh, that you were like a brother to me, who nursed at my mother's breasts! If I found you outside, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
I would lead you, I would bring you into my mother's house; you would teach me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranates.
His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.
I make you swear, daughters of Jerusalem: do not stir up or awaken love until it is ready.
Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Under the apple tree I awakened you; there your mother was in labor with you; there she who bore you was in labor.
Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm, for love is as strong as death, its passion as unyielding as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a flame of the LORD.
Many waters cannot quench love, and rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man gave all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly despised.
We have a little sister, and she has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
If she is a wall, we will build on her a battlement of silver; but if she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers; so I have become in his eyes like one who finds peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal-hamon; he gave the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring for its fruit a thousand pieces of silver.
My vineyard, my very own, is before me. The thousand are yours, Solomon, and two hundred for those who keep its fruit.
You who sit in the gardens, companions are listening for your voice; let me hear it.
Flee, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
The vision of Isaiah son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Hear, you heavens, and listen, you earth, for the LORD has spoken: I raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me.
The ox knows its owner, and the donkey its master's feeding trough, but Israel does not know; my people do not understand.

Woe to the sinful nation, a people weighed down with guilt, offspring of evildoers, children who act corruptly! They have abandoned the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel; they have turned their backs on him.
Why will you be beaten again? Why do you keep on rebelling? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the head there is nothing sound in it: only wounds and welts and open sores. They have not been cleaned or bandaged, or soothed with oil.
Your land is a desolation; your cities are burned with fire. As for your fields, foreigners devour them before your eyes. It is desolate, as when foreigners overthrow a land.
Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege.
If the LORD of Armies had not left us a few survivors, we would have been like Sodom; we would have resembled Gomorrah.
Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Listen to the instruction of our God, you people of Gomorrah!

What are all your sacrifices to me? says the LORD. I have had more than enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals. I take no pleasure in the blood of bulls, of lambs and of goats.
When you come to appear before me, who asked you to do this, to trample my courts?
Stop bringing worthless offerings! Your incense is detestable to me. New moons and Sabbaths, the calling of assemblies: I cannot bear wickedness together with a solemn assembly.
Your new moons and your appointed festivals I hate with all my being. They have become a burden to me; I am tired of carrying them.
When you spread out your hands in prayer, I will hide my eyes from you. Even when you pray and pray, I am not listening. Your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean. Take your evil deeds out of my sight. Stop doing evil.
Learn to do good. Seek justice; correct the oppressor. Defend the rights of the fatherless; plead the widow's case.
Come now, let us settle this, says the LORD. Though your sins are like scarlet, they will be as white as snow. Though they are red as crimson, they will become like wool.
If you are willing and obey, you will eat the good things of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel, you will be eaten by the sword. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
How the faithful city has become a prostitute! She was full of justice; righteousness lived in her, but now murderers.
Your silver has become dross; your best wine is watered down.

Your rulers are rebels and companions of thieves. Every one of them loves a bribe and chases after gifts. They do not defend the rights of the fatherless, and the widow's case never comes before them.
Therefore the Lord GOD of Armies, the Mighty One of Israel, declares: Ah, I will get relief from my adversaries and take revenge on my enemies!
I will turn my hand against you. I will smelt away your dross as with lye and remove all your impurities.
I will restore your judges as at the first, and your counselors as at the beginning. After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City.
Zion will be redeemed by justice, and those in her who turn back, by righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be crushed together, and those who abandon the LORD will come to an end.
For you will be ashamed of the sacred oaks that you delighted in, and you will blush for the gardens that you chose.
For you will be like an oak whose leaves are withering, like a garden that has no water.
The strong one will become tinder, and his work a spark. Both of them will burn together, with no one to put out the fire.
This is the word that Isaiah son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
In the days to come, the mountain of the LORD's house will be established as the highest of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and all the nations will stream to it.

Many peoples will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that he may teach us his ways and we may walk in his paths." For instruction will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between the nations and settle disputes for many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.
House of Jacob, come, let us walk in the light of the LORD!

For you have abandoned your people, the house of Jacob, because they are full of things from the east and of fortune-tellers like the Philistines, and they strike hands with the children of foreigners.
Their land is filled with silver and gold, and there is no end to their treasures. Their land is filled with horses, and there is no end to their chariots.
Their land is filled with idols. They bow down to the work of their hands, to what their own fingers have made.
So humankind is brought low, and everyone is humbled. Do not forgive them!
Go into the rock and hide in the dust from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of his majesty.
The proud eyes of humankind will be brought low, and human arrogance will be humbled. The LORD alone will be exalted on that day.
For the LORD of Armies has a day against all that is proud and lofty, against all that is lifted up, and it will be brought low,
against all the cedars of Lebanon, high and lifted up, and against all the oaks of Bashan,
against all the high mountains and against all the lofty hills,
against every high tower and against every fortified wall,
against all the ships of Tarshish and against all the beautiful vessels.
Human pride will be humbled, and human arrogance brought low. The LORD alone will be exalted on that day,
and the idols will vanish completely.
People will go into caves in the rocks and holes in the ground, from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.
On that day people will throw away to the moles and the bats their idols of silver and their idols of gold, which they made for themselves to worship,
and go into the clefts of the rocks and the crevices of the cliffs, from the terror of the LORD and from the splendor of his majesty, when he rises to make the earth tremble.
Stop trusting in human beings, who have only a breath in their nostrils. For what are they worth?
For look, the Lord GOD of Armies is about to take away from Jerusalem and from Judah every support and supply, all supply of bread and all supply of water:
the warrior and the soldier, the judge and the prophet, the diviner and the elder,
the commander of fifty and the man of rank, the counselor, the skilled craftsman and the expert in charms.
I will make boys their rulers, and the reckless will govern them.
The people will oppress one another, each one his neighbor. The young will be insolent to the old, and the nobody to the honored.
A man will take hold of his brother in his father's house and say, "You have a cloak; you be our ruler! Take charge of this heap of ruins!"
On that day he will cry out, "I will not be a healer! There is no bread and no cloak in my house. Do not make me ruler of the people."
For Jerusalem has stumbled, and Judah has fallen, because their words and their deeds are against the LORD, defying his glorious presence.
The look on their faces testifies against them. They parade their sin like Sodom; they do not hide it. Woe to them! They have brought disaster on themselves.
Tell the righteous that it will go well with them, for they will eat the fruit of their deeds.
Woe to the wicked! It will go badly with them, for they will be paid back for what their hands have done.
My people! Children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. My people, your guides lead you astray; they have erased the path you should walk.
The LORD takes his place to bring charges; he stands to judge the peoples.
The LORD enters into judgment with the elders and leaders of his people: It is you who have stripped the vineyard bare. What you have stolen from the poor is in your houses.
What do you mean by crushing my people and grinding the faces of the poor? declares the Lord GOD of Armies.
The LORD said: Because the daughters of Zion are proud and walk with outstretched necks, flirting with their eyes, tripping along with mincing steps, jingling the bangles on their feet,
the Lord will cover the heads of the daughters of Zion with scabs, and the LORD will lay bare their foreheads.
On that day the Lord will take away their finery: the anklets, the headbands, the crescent ornaments,
the pendants, the bracelets, the veils,
the headdresses, the ankle chains, the sashes, the perfume boxes, the amulets,
the signet rings, the nose rings,
the festal robes, the capes, the shawls, the purses,
the mirrors, the linen garments, the turbans and the veils.
Instead of perfume there will be rot; instead of a sash, a rope; instead of well-set hair, baldness; instead of a rich robe, a wrapping of sackcloth; instead of beauty, branding.
Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
Her gates will lament and mourn; stripped bare, she will sit on the ground.
On that day seven women will take hold of one man and say, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own clothes; only let us be called by your name. Take away our disgrace!"
On that day the branch of the LORD will be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land will be the pride and splendor of the survivors of Israel.
Whoever is left in Zion and remains in Jerusalem will be called holy, everyone in Jerusalem who is recorded for life.
When the Lord has washed away the filth of the daughters of Zion and rinsed the bloodstains of Jerusalem from within her by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning,
then the LORD will create over the whole site of Mount Zion and over her assemblies a cloud by day, and smoke and the glow of a flaming fire by night. For over all the glory there will be a canopy.
It will be a shelter, a shade from the heat by day, and a refuge and hiding place from storm and rain.
Let me sing for my beloved a song of my beloved about his vineyard: My beloved had a vineyard on a very fertile hill.

He dug it up and cleared it of stones, and planted it with choice vines. He built a watchtower in the middle of it and also cut out a winepress in it. He waited for it to produce grapes, but it produced rotten grapes.
So now, you who live in Jerusalem and you people of Judah, judge between me and my vineyard.
What more could I have done for my vineyard that I have not done in it? When I waited for it to produce grapes, why did it produce rotten grapes?
Now let me tell you what I am going to do to my vineyard: I will take away its hedge, and it will be grazed bare; I will break down its wall, and it will be trampled.
I will make it a wasteland. It will not be pruned or hoed, and briers and thorns will grow up there. I will also command the clouds not to rain on it.

For the vineyard of the LORD of Armies is the house of Israel, and the people of Judah are the planting he delighted in. He waited for justice, but saw bloodshed; for righteousness, but heard an outcry.
Woe to those who join house to house and add field to field, until there is no room left, and you are left to live alone in the middle of the land!
The LORD of Armies has sworn in my hearing: Many houses will surely become desolate, large and fine houses, with no one living in them.
For ten acres of vineyard will produce only one bath, and a homer of seed will produce only an ephah.
Woe to those who rise early in the morning to chase after beer, who stay up late at night till wine sets them on fire!
They have lyre and harp, tambourine and flute, and wine at their feasts, but they pay no attention to the deeds of the LORD, and they do not see the work of his hands.
Therefore my people go into exile for lack of knowledge. Their nobles are starving, and their masses are parched with thirst.
Therefore Sheol has opened its throat wide and opened its mouth beyond measure. Down go her splendor and her masses, her noisy crowd and all who revel in her.
So humankind is brought low, and everyone is humbled, and the eyes of the proud are humbled.
But the LORD of Armies is exalted by justice, and the holy God shows himself holy by righteousness.
Lambs will graze there as in their own pasture, and strangers will eat among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who drag guilt along with cords of falsehood, and sin as if with cart ropes,
who say, "Let him hurry; let him be quick with his work, so that we may see it! Let the plan of the Holy One of Israel come near and come true, so that we may know it!"
Woe to those who call evil good and good evil, who make darkness light and light darkness, who make bitter sweet and sweet bitter!
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight!
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine, and champions at mixing strong drinks,
who acquit the guilty for a bribe and deny justice to the innocent!

Therefore, as a tongue of fire devours straw and dry grass sinks down in the flame, their root will be like rot, and their blossom will blow away like dust. For they have rejected the instruction of the LORD of Armies and despised the word of the Holy One of Israel.

That is why the anger of the LORD burns against his people. He has stretched out his hand against them and struck them down. The mountains shook, and their corpses were like garbage in the middle of the streets. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
He will raise a signal flag for the nations far away and whistle for them from the ends of the earth. And look, swiftly, speedily they come!
None of them is weary, and none stumbles; none slumbers or sleeps. Not a belt is loose at the waist, not a sandal strap is broken.
Their arrows are sharp, and all their bows are strung. Their horses' hooves seem like flint, and their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roar is like a lion's; they roar like young lions. They growl and seize their prey and carry it off, and no one can rescue it.
On that day they will growl over it like the growling of the sea. If anyone looks at the land, there is darkness and distress, and the light is darkened by its clouds.
In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hem of his robe filled the temple.
Seraphim stood above him. Each had six wings: with two he covered his face, with two he covered his feet, and with two he flew.
And they called to one another: "Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory."
The doorposts and thresholds shook at the sound of the one who called, and the house was filled with smoke.
Then I said, "Woe is me! I am ruined! For I am a man of unclean lips, and I live among a people of unclean lips, and my eyes have seen the King, the LORD of Armies!"
Then one of the seraphim flew to me, holding in his hand a glowing coal that he had taken with tongs from the altar.
He touched my mouth with it and said, "See, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is taken away, and your sin is atoned for."
Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, "Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?" And I said, "Here I am. Send me!"
He said, "Go, and say to this people: 'Keep on hearing, but do not understand; keep on seeing, but do not perceive.'

Make the heart of this people dull, make their ears heavy and shut their eyes, so that they may not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and turn back and be healed."
Then I said, "How long, Lord?" And he answered, "Until cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, and houses with no people, and the land is left utterly desolate,
until the LORD sends the people far away, and the deserted places are many in the middle of the land.
Even if a tenth remains in it, it will be burned again, like a terebinth or an oak whose stump remains when it is cut down. The holy seed is its stump."

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, marched up to Jerusalem to wage war against it, but they could not conquer it.
When the house of David was told, "Aram has joined forces with Ephraim," the heart of Ahaz and the hearts of his people shook, as the trees of the forest shake in the wind.
Then the LORD said to Isaiah, "Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the channel of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field.
Say to him, 'Be careful, keep calm, and do not be afraid. Do not lose heart because of these two smoldering stubs of firewood, because of the fierce anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah.
Aram, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted evil against you. They have said:
Let us invade Judah and terrify it, and break it open for ourselves, and make the son of Tabeel king in it.
This is what the Lord GOD says: It will not stand; it will not happen.
For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be shattered and will no longer be a people.
The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is the son of Remaliah. If you do not stand firm in faith, you will not stand firm at all.'"
Again the LORD spoke to Ahaz:
"Ask the LORD your God for a sign, whether as deep as Sheol or as high as the heavens above."
But Ahaz said, "I will not ask. I will not put the LORD to the test."
Then Isaiah said, "Listen now, house of David! Is it not enough for you to wear out the patience of people, that you wear out the patience of my God too?
Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign: Look, the young woman is pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will call him Immanuel.
He will eat curds and honey by the time he knows how to reject evil and choose good.
For before the boy knows how to reject evil and choose good, the land whose two kings you dread will be abandoned.
The LORD will bring on you, on your people and on your father's house days such as have not come since the day Ephraim broke away from Judah: the king of Assyria."
On that day the LORD will whistle for the fly that is at the far end of the streams of Egypt and for the bee that is in the land of Assyria.
They will all come and settle in the steep ravines and in the clefts of the rocks, on all the thornbushes and on all the watering places.
On that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired from beyond the River, with the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet, and it will sweep away the beard as well.
On that day a man will keep alive a young cow and two sheep.
Because they give so much milk, he will eat curds. Everyone who is left in the land will eat curds and honey.
On that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand shekels of silver, will become briers and thorns.
People will go there with bow and arrows, for all the land will be briers and thorns.
As for all the hills that used to be dug with a hoe, you will not go there for fear of the briers and thorns. They will become a place where cattle are let loose and sheep trample.
The LORD said to me, "Take a large tablet and write on it in ordinary letters: Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz."
So I took reliable witnesses to testify for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah.
Then I went to the prophetess, and she conceived and gave birth to a son. The LORD said to me, "Name him Maher-shalal-hash-baz.
For before the boy knows how to say 'My father' or 'My mother,' the wealth of Damascus and the plunder of Samaria will be carried off before the king of Assyria."
The LORD spoke to me again:
"Because this people has rejected the gently flowing waters of Shiloah and rejoices over Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
therefore, look, the Lord is bringing up against them the waters of the River, mighty and many, the king of Assyria and all his glory. It will rise over all its channels and overflow all its banks.
It will sweep on into Judah, flood it and pass through, reaching up to the neck. Its outspread wings will fill the breadth of your land, Immanuel!"
Raise the war cry, you peoples, and be shattered! Listen, all you distant lands! Arm yourselves, and be shattered! Arm yourselves, and be shattered!
Make your plans, but they will come to nothing! Give your orders, but they will not stand! For God is with us.
For this is what the LORD said to me, with his strong hand on me, when he warned me not to walk in the way of this people:
"Do not call conspiracy all that this people calls conspiracy. Do not fear what they fear, and do not dread it.
The LORD of Armies: he is the one you must regard as holy. He is the one you must fear; he is the one you must dread.
He will be a sanctuary, but for both houses of Israel he will be a stone that makes people stumble and a rock that makes them fall, and for those who live in Jerusalem a trap and a snare.
Many among them will stumble; they will fall and be broken, they will be snared and captured."
Bind up the testimony; seal the instruction among my disciples.
I will wait for the LORD, who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob. I will put my hope in him.
Here am I, and the children the LORD has given me. We are signs and portents in Israel from the LORD of Armies, who dwells on Mount Zion.
When people say to you, "Consult the spirits of the dead and the spiritists, who chirp and mutter," should not a people consult their God? Should they consult the dead on behalf of the living?
To the instruction and to the testimony! If they do not speak according to this word, there is no dawn for them.
They will pass through the land, hard-pressed and hungry. When they are hungry, they will become enraged, and they will curse their king and their God as they look upward.
Then they will look to the earth, and see only distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish, and they will be driven into thick darkness.

Yet there will be no more gloom for the land that was in anguish. In the past he brought shame on the land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, but in the future he will bring glory to the way of the sea, the land beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations.
The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. On those who lived in the land of deep darkness a light has shone.
You have made the nation great; you have increased its joy. They rejoice before you as people rejoice at harvest, as warriors rejoice when they divide the plunder.
For the yoke that weighed them down, the bar across their shoulders, the rod of their oppressor, you have shattered, as on the day of Midian.
For every boot of the warrior that tramped in the battle, and every garment rolled in blood, will be burned as fuel for the fire.
For a child has been born to us, a son has been given to us, and the government will be on his shoulder. His name will be called Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.

His government will grow, and there will be no end to peace, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to establish it and uphold it with justice and righteousness from now on and forever. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will do this.
The Lord has sent a word against Jacob, and it has fallen on Israel.
All the people will know it, Ephraim and those who live in Samaria, who say in their pride and arrogance of heart,
"The bricks have fallen, but we will rebuild with dressed stone. The sycamore-figs have been cut down, but we will put cedars in their place."
So the LORD has raised up the adversaries of Rezin against him and stirred up his enemies:
Aram from the east and the Philistines from the west have devoured Israel with open mouth. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
But the people have not turned back to him who struck them, nor have they sought the LORD of Armies.
So the LORD cut off from Israel head and tail, palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The elder and the man of rank are the head, and the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
Those who guide this people lead them astray, and those who are guided are swallowed up.

That is why the Lord takes no pleasure in their young men and has no compassion on their fatherless and widows, for everyone is godless and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks folly. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
For wickedness burns like a fire; it devours briers and thorns. It sets the thickets of the forest ablaze, and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
By the fury of the LORD of Armies the land is scorched, and the people are like fuel for the fire. No one spares his brother.
They slice meat on the right but are still hungry; they eat on the left but are not satisfied. Each of them devours the flesh of his own arm.
Manasseh devours Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh; together they turn against Judah. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
Woe to those who make unjust laws, and to the writers who keep writing oppression,
to deprive the poor of justice and rob the needy among my people of their rights, so that widows become their plunder and they prey on the fatherless!
What will you do on the day of reckoning, when ruin comes from far away? To whom will you run for help, and where will you leave your wealth?
Nothing will be left but to crouch among the prisoners or to fall among the slain. Yet for all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is still stretched out.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger! The club in their hand is my fury.
I send him against a godless nation; I command him to go against the people who provoke my wrath, to take spoil and seize plunder, and to trample them like mud in the streets.
But this is not what he intends; this is not what he has in mind. His purpose is to destroy, to cut off nations, and not a few.
For he says, "Are not my commanders all kings?
Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? Is not Samaria like Damascus?
As my hand has reached the kingdoms of the idols, whose images were greater than those of Jerusalem and Samaria,
shall I not do to Jerusalem and her images as I have done to Samaria and her idols?"
When the Lord has finished all his work on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, I will punish the fruit of the king of Assyria's proud heart and the haughty look in his eyes.

For he says: "By the strength of my hand I have done this, and by my wisdom, for I have understanding. I have removed the boundaries of peoples and plundered their treasures; like a mighty one I have brought down those who sat on thrones.
My hand has found the wealth of the peoples like a nest, and as one gathers abandoned eggs, I have gathered all the earth. Not one flapped a wing or opened its mouth to chirp."

Does the ax boast over the one who chops with it? Does the saw make itself greater than the one who saws with it? As if a rod could wield the one who lifts it, or a staff could lift the one who is not wood!
Therefore the Lord GOD of Armies will send a wasting disease among his stout warriors, and under his glory a fire will be kindled, burning like a fire.
The light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame. It will burn and devour his thorns and his briers in a single day.
The glory of his forest and his fruitful land it will destroy, both soul and body, and it will be as when a sick man wastes away.
The trees left in his forest will be so few that a child could write them down.
On that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will truly lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return, the remnant of Jacob, to the Mighty God.
For even if your people, Israel, were like the sand of the sea, only a remnant of them will return. Destruction has been decreed, overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord GOD of Armies will carry out the destruction he has decreed in the middle of all the earth.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: My people who live in Zion, do not be afraid of Assyria, though he strikes you with a rod and lifts up his staff against you, as Egypt did.
For in a very little while my fury will come to an end, and my anger will turn to their destruction.
The LORD of Armies will raise a whip against him, as when he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb. His staff will be over the sea, and he will lift it up as he did in Egypt.
On that day his burden will be lifted from your shoulder, and his yoke from your neck, and the yoke will be broken because of fatness.
He has come to Aiath; he has passed through Migron; at Michmash he leaves his baggage.
They have crossed the pass: "Geba is our camp for the night!" Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry aloud, Daughter Gallim! Listen, Laishah! Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is in flight; the people of Gebim take refuge.
This very day he will halt at Nob. He shakes his fist at the mount of Daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Look, the Lord GOD of Armies will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The tallest trees will be cut down, and the lofty will be brought low.
He will cut down the thickets of the forest with an ax, and Lebanon will fall before the Mighty One.
A shoot will come out from the stump of Jesse, and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.
The Spirit of the LORD will rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the LORD.
His delight will be in the fear of the LORD. He will not judge by what his eyes see, or decide by what his ears hear.

He will judge the poor with righteousness and decide with fairness for the humble of the earth. He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he will put the wicked to death.
Righteousness will be the belt around his waist, and faithfulness the belt around his hips.
The wolf will live with the lamb, and the leopard will lie down with the young goat. The calf and the young lion and the fattened calf will be together, and a little child will lead them.
The cow and the bear will graze; their young will lie down together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox.
The nursing child will play over the hole of the cobra, and the weaned child will put his hand into the viper's den.
They will not harm or destroy on all my holy mountain, for the earth will be full of the knowledge of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
On that day the root of Jesse will stand as a signal for the peoples. The nations will seek him, and his resting place will be glorious.

On that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time to reclaim the remnant of his people that is left, from Assyria, from Egypt, from Pathros, from Cush, from Elam, from Shinar, from Hamath and from the coastlands of the sea.
He will raise a signal flag for the nations and gather the outcasts of Israel; he will bring together the scattered people of Judah from the four corners of the earth.
The jealousy of Ephraim will depart, and the adversaries of Judah will be cut off. Ephraim will not be jealous of Judah, and Judah will not be hostile to Ephraim.
They will swoop down on the slopes of the Philistines to the west; together they will plunder the people of the east. They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab, and the Ammonites will obey them.
The LORD will utterly destroy the gulf of the Sea of Egypt. With his scorching wind he will wave his hand over the River and split it into seven streams, so that people can cross it in sandals.
There will be a highway for the remnant of his people that is left from Assyria, as there was for Israel on the day they came up from the land of Egypt.
On that day you will say, "I will praise you, LORD. Though you were angry with me, your anger has turned away, and you comfort me.
Look, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid. For the LORD, the LORD, is my strength and my song; he has become my salvation."
With joy you will draw water from the springs of salvation.
On that day you will say, "Give thanks to the LORD; call on his name. Make known his deeds among the peoples; declare that his name is exalted.
Sing praises to the LORD, for he has done glorious things; let this be known in all the earth.
Shout aloud and sing for joy, you who live in Zion, for great among you is the Holy One of Israel."
An oracle concerning Babylon, which Isaiah son of Amoz saw.
On a bare hill raise a signal flag! Shout to them; wave your hand for them to enter the gates of the nobles.
I myself have given orders to my consecrated ones; I have summoned my warriors to carry out my anger, those who exult in my triumph.
Listen! A tumult on the mountains, like that of a great people! Listen! An uproar of kingdoms, of nations gathering! The LORD of Armies is mustering an army for battle.
They come from a distant land, from the ends of the heavens, the LORD and the weapons of his wrath, to destroy the whole earth.
Wail, for the day of the LORD is near! It comes like destruction from the Almighty.
Therefore all hands will go limp, and every human heart will melt.
They will be terrified. Pains and pangs will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labor. They will look at one another in horror, their faces aflame.
Look, the day of the LORD is coming, cruel, with fury and burning anger, to make the earth a desolation and to destroy its sinners from it.
For the stars of the heavens and their constellations will not give their light. The sun will be dark when it rises, and the moon will not shed its light.
I will punish the world for its evil and the wicked for their guilt. I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant and bring low the haughtiness of tyrants.
I will make human beings scarcer than fine gold, humankind scarcer than the gold of Ophir.
Therefore I will make the heavens tremble, and the earth will be shaken from its place at the fury of the LORD of Armies, on the day of his burning anger.
Like a hunted gazelle, like sheep with no one to gather them, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land.
Whoever is found will be stabbed, and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
Their infants will be dashed to pieces before their eyes, their houses will be plundered, and their wives raped.
Look, I am stirring up the Medes against them, who have no regard for silver and take no delight in gold.
Their bows will cut down the young men. They will have no pity on the fruit of the womb; their eyes will not spare children.
Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms, the glory and pride of the Chaldeans, will be like Sodom and Gomorrah when God overthrew them.
It will never be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation. No Arab will pitch his tent there, and no shepherds will rest their flocks there.
But desert creatures will lie down there, and its houses will be full of howling creatures. Ostriches will live there, and wild goats will dance there.
Hyenas will howl in its fortresses, and jackals in its luxurious palaces. Its time is near, and its days will not be prolonged.
The LORD will have compassion on Jacob and will again choose Israel and settle them in their own land. Foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob.

Peoples will take them and bring them to their own place, and the house of Israel will possess them as male and female servants in the LORD's land. They will take captive those who took them captive, and rule over those who oppressed them.
On the day the LORD gives you rest from your pain and turmoil and from the hard labor forced on you,
you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon: "How the oppressor has come to an end! How his fury has ended!
The LORD has broken the staff of the wicked, the scepter of rulers,
that struck peoples in fury with blows that never stopped, that ruled nations in anger with relentless persecution.
The whole earth is at rest and at peace; they break into song.
Even the junipers and the cedars of Lebanon rejoice over you: 'Since you were laid low, no woodcutter comes up against us.'
Sheol below is stirred up to meet you when you come. It rouses the shades to greet you, all who were leaders of the earth. It makes all the kings of the nations rise from their thrones.
All of them answer and say to you: 'You too have become as weak as we are! You have become like us!'
Your pomp has been brought down to Sheol, with the music of your harps. Maggots are spread out as your bed, and worms are your covering.
How you have fallen from heaven, shining one, son of the dawn! How you have been cut down to the ground, you who laid the nations low!
You said in your heart, 'I will go up to heaven; above the stars of God I will set my throne on high. I will sit on the mount of assembly, in the far reaches of the north.
I will go up above the heights of the clouds; I will make myself like the Most High.'
But you are brought down to Sheol, to the depths of the Pit.
Those who see you will stare at you; they will look closely at you: 'Is this the man who made the earth tremble, who shook kingdoms,
who made the world like a wilderness and overthrew its cities, who would not let his prisoners go home?'
All the kings of the nations, all of them, lie in honor, each in his own tomb.
But you are thrown out of your grave like a rejected branch, covered with the slain, those pierced by the sword, who go down to the stones of the Pit, like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You will not join them in burial, for you have destroyed your land and killed your people. May the offspring of evildoers never be named again!
Prepare a place to slaughter his sons for the guilt of their ancestors, so that they may not rise and possess the earth and fill the face of the world with cities."
I will rise up against them, declares the LORD of Armies. I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant, offspring and descendants, declares the LORD.
I will make it a place for owls and pools of water, and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction, declares the LORD of Armies.
The LORD of Armies has sworn: Surely, as I have planned, so it will be, and as I have purposed, so it will stand:
I will break Assyria in my land and trample him on my mountains. His yoke will be removed from them, and his burden removed from their shoulder.
This is the plan that is planned for the whole earth, and this is the hand that is stretched out over all the nations.
For the LORD of Armies has planned, and who can stop him? His hand is stretched out, and who can turn it back?
In the year King Ahaz died, this oracle came:
Do not rejoice, all you Philistines, because the rod that struck you is broken. For from the root of the snake will come a viper, and its fruit will be a flying serpent.
The firstborn of the poor will graze, and the needy will lie down in safety. But I will kill your root with famine, and it will slay your survivors.
Wail, you gate! Cry out, you city! Melt in fear, all you Philistines! For smoke comes from the north, and there is no straggler in its ranks.
What answer will be given to the messengers of the nation? That the LORD has founded Zion, and in her the afflicted of his people will find refuge.
An oracle concerning Moab: Ar of Moab is devastated in a night, destroyed! Kir of Moab is devastated in a night, destroyed!
Dibon goes up to its temple, to its high places, to weep. Over Nebo and over Medeba Moab wails. Every head is shaved bald, every beard cut off.
In its streets they wear sackcloth; on its rooftops and in its squares everyone wails, streaming with tears.
Heshbon and Elealeh cry out; their voice is heard as far as Jahaz. Therefore the armed men of Moab cry out; his soul trembles within him.
My heart cries out for Moab. Her fugitives flee as far as Zoar, as far as Eglath-shelishiyah. For they go up the ascent of Luhith weeping; on the road to Horonaim they raise a cry of destruction.
For the waters of Nimrim are a desolation; the grass is withered, the new growth is gone, and nothing green is left.
So they carry the wealth they have gained and stored up away over the Wadi of the Willows.
For the cry has gone around the borders of Moab; her wailing reaches as far as Eglaim, her wailing as far as Beer-elim.
For the waters of Dimon are full of blood. Yet I will bring still more on Dimon: a lion for the survivors of Moab and for the remnant of the land.
Send lambs to the ruler of the land, from Sela, by way of the wilderness, to the mount of Daughter Zion.
Like fluttering birds, like a scattered nest, so are the daughters of Moab at the fords of the Arnon.
Give counsel; make a decision. Make your shade like night at high noon. Hide the outcasts; do not betray the fugitive.
Let my outcasts from Moab stay with you; be a refuge for them from the destroyer. When the oppressor is no more and destruction has ceased, and the one who tramples has vanished from the land,
then a throne will be established in faithful love, and on it will sit in faithfulness, in the tent of David, one who judges and seeks justice and is quick to do what is right.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, how very proud he is, of his arrogance, his pride and his insolence; his boasting is empty.
Therefore Moab wails; all of them wail for Moab. Moan for the raisin cakes of Kir-hareseth, utterly stricken.

For the fields of Heshbon wither, and the vines of Sibmah, whose choice vines laid low the lords of the nations. They reached as far as Jazer and wandered into the wilderness; their shoots spread out and crossed the sea.
So I weep with the weeping of Jazer for the vines of Sibmah. I drench you with my tears, Heshbon and Elealeh, for the battle shout has fallen on your summer fruit and your harvest.
Joy and gladness are taken away from the fruitful field; in the vineyards no one sings or shouts. No one treads out wine in the presses; I have put an end to the shout.
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like a lyre, and my inmost being for Kir-heres.
When Moab appears and wears himself out on the high place, and comes to his sanctuary to pray, it will do him no good.
This is the word that the LORD spoke concerning Moab in the past.

But now the LORD has spoken: Within three years, counted as a hired worker counts them, the glory of Moab will be brought into contempt, with all its great crowd, and its survivors will be very few and feeble.
An oracle concerning Damascus: Look, Damascus will cease to be a city; it will become a heap of ruins.
The cities of Aroer are abandoned; they will be for flocks, which will lie down with no one to frighten them.
The fortress will disappear from Ephraim, and the kingdom from Damascus. The remnant of Aram will be like the glory of the Israelites, declares the LORD of Armies.
On that day the glory of Jacob will fade, and the fat of his body will waste away.
It will be as when a reaper gathers the standing grain and his arm harvests the ears, as when someone gleans ears of grain in the Valley of Rephaim.
Gleanings will be left in it, as when an olive tree is beaten: two or three olives at the very top, four or five on its fruitful branches, declares the LORD, the God of Israel.
On that day people will look to their Maker, and their eyes will turn to the Holy One of Israel.
They will not look to the altars, the work of their hands, or regard what their fingers have made, the Asherah poles and the incense altars.
On that day their strong cities will be like the abandoned places of the woods and the hilltops, which they abandoned before the Israelites, and there will be desolation.
For you have forgotten the God of your salvation and have not remembered the Rock of your refuge. Therefore, though you plant pleasant plants and set out cuttings for a foreign god,
though on the day you plant them you make them grow, and in the morning you make your seed blossom, the harvest will vanish on the day of sickness and incurable pain.
Woe to the many peoples who roar, who roar like the roaring of the seas, and the nations who rage, who rage like the raging of mighty waters!
The nations rage like the raging of many waters, but he rebukes them, and they flee far away, chased like chaff on the mountains before the wind, like whirling dust before a storm.
At evening, look, sudden terror! Before morning, they are gone. This is the portion of those who loot us, the lot of those who plunder us.
Woe to the land of whirring wings, beyond the rivers of Cush,

which sends envoys by sea, in papyrus boats over the waters! Go, swift messengers, to a nation tall and smooth-skinned, to a people feared far and wide, a nation strong and conquering, whose land the rivers divide.
All you inhabitants of the world, you who live on the earth, when a signal flag is raised on the mountains, you will see it; when a ram's horn is blown, you will hear it.
For this is what the LORD has said to me: I will be still and look on from my dwelling place, like the shimmering heat in the sunshine, like a cloud of dew in the heat of harvest.
For before the harvest, when the blossom is over and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the shoots with pruning knives and lop off and clear away the spreading branches.
They will all be left to the birds of prey on the mountains and to the wild animals of the earth. The birds of prey will spend the summer on them, and all the wild animals of the earth the winter.

At that time gifts will be brought to the LORD of Armies from a people tall and smooth-skinned, from a people feared far and wide, a nation strong and conquering, whose land the rivers divide, to the place of the name of the LORD of Armies, Mount Zion.
An oracle concerning Egypt: Look, the LORD is riding on a swift cloud and is coming to Egypt. The idols of Egypt tremble before him, and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian; they will fight, brother against brother and neighbor against neighbor, city against city, kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be emptied out within it, and I will confuse its plans. They will consult the idols and the spirits of the dead, the mediums and the spiritists.
I will hand Egypt over to a cruel master, and a fierce king will rule over them, declares the Lord GOD of Armies.
The waters of the sea will dry up, and the river will be parched and dry.
The canals will stink; the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up; reeds and rushes will wither.
The plants along the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile, and every sown field along the Nile will dry up, blow away and be no more.
The fishermen will mourn and lament, all who cast hooks into the Nile; those who spread nets on the water will waste away.
Those who work with combed flax will be dismayed, and the weavers of white cloth.
Her foundations will be crushed, and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
The officials of Zoan are nothing but fools; the wise counselors of Pharaoh give senseless advice. How can you say to Pharaoh, "I am a son of the wise, a son of ancient kings"?
Where are your wise men now? Let them tell you and make known what the LORD of Armies has planned against Egypt.
The officials of Zoan have become fools; the officials of Memphis are deceived. The cornerstones of her tribes have led Egypt astray.
The LORD has poured into her a spirit of confusion, and they make Egypt stagger in all she does, as a drunkard staggers in his vomit.
There is nothing Egypt can do, head or tail, palm branch or reed.
On that day the Egyptians will be like women. They will tremble and be afraid before the hand that the LORD of Armies raises against them.
The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone to whom it is mentioned will be afraid because of the plan that the LORD of Armies has planned against them.
On that day there will be five cities in the land of Egypt that speak the language of Canaan and swear allegiance to the LORD of Armies. One of them will be called the City of Destruction.
On that day there will be an altar to the LORD in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a standing stone to the LORD at its border.
It will be a sign and a witness to the LORD of Armies in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to the LORD because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, who will rescue them.
The LORD will make himself known to Egypt, and the Egyptians will know the LORD on that day. They will worship with sacrifice and grain offering, and make vows to the LORD and keep them.
The LORD will strike Egypt, striking and healing. They will turn back to the LORD, and he will listen to their pleas and heal them.
On that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. The Assyrians will come to Egypt and the Egyptians to Assyria, and the Egyptians will worship with the Assyrians.
On that day Israel will be the third, with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth.
The LORD of Armies will bless them, saying, "Blessed be Egypt my people, Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance."
In the year that the commander-in-chief, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, came to Ashdod and fought against it and captured it,
at that time the LORD spoke through Isaiah son of Amoz: "Go, take off the sackcloth from your waist and remove the sandals from your feet." And he did so, walking around stripped and barefoot.
Then the LORD said, "Just as my servant Isaiah has walked stripped and barefoot for three years as a sign and a portent against Egypt and Cush,
so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, stripped and barefoot, with buttocks bared, to Egypt's shame.
They will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their pride.

On that day the people who live on this coast will say, 'Look, this is what has happened to those we hoped in, to whom we fled for help, to be rescued from the king of Assyria! How then can we escape?'"
An oracle concerning the wilderness of the sea: Like whirlwinds sweeping through the Negev, it comes from the wilderness, from a terrifying land.
A harsh vision has been shown to me: the traitor betrays, and the destroyer destroys. Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media! I put an end to all the groaning she caused.
Therefore my body is filled with anguish; pains have seized me like the pains of a woman in labor. I am bent double by what I hear; I am terrified by what I see.
My mind reels; horror overwhelms me. The twilight I longed for has become a terror to me.
They set the table, they spread the rugs, they eat, they drink! Get up, you officers, oil the shields!
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Go, post a lookout; let him report what he sees.
When he sees riders, horsemen in pairs, riders on donkeys, riders on camels, let him pay attention, close attention."
Then he called out like a lion: "Lord, I stand on the watchtower continually by day, and I am stationed at my post every night.
Look, here comes a man in a chariot, with horsemen in pairs!" Then he answered, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon! All the images of her gods lie shattered on the ground!"
My people, threshed and winnowed on my threshing floor, what I have heard from the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, I have told you.
An oracle concerning Dumah: Someone calls to me from Seir, "Watchman, what is left of the night? Watchman, what is left of the night?"
The watchman says, "Morning is coming, but also the night. If you want to ask, ask; come back again."
An oracle concerning Arabia: You caravans of Dedanites, who camp in the thickets of Arabia,
bring water to meet the thirsty! You who live in the land of Tema, meet the fugitives with bread.
For they have fled from the swords, from the drawn sword, from the bent bow, and from the heat of battle.
For this is what the Lord said to me: "Within one year, counted as a hired worker counts it, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end.
The bows of Kedar's warriors that remain will be few." For the LORD, the God of Israel, has spoken.
An oracle concerning the Valley of Vision: What is the matter with you now, that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
you city full of noise, you town of tumult and celebration? Your slain were not slain by the sword, nor did they die in battle.
All your rulers fled together; they were captured without a bow being drawn. All of you who were found were captured together, though they had fled far away.
Therefore I said, "Look away from me; let me weep bitterly. Do not try to comfort me over the destruction of my dear people."
For the Lord GOD of Armies has a day of tumult, trampling and confusion in the Valley of Vision, of battering down walls and of crying out to the mountain.
Elam took up the quiver, with chariots of men and horsemen, and Kir uncovered the shield.
Your choicest valleys were full of chariots, and the horsemen took their positions at the gate.
He removed the covering of Judah. On that day you looked to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You saw that the breaches in the walls of the City of David were many, and you collected the waters of the Lower Pool.
You counted the houses of Jerusalem and tore houses down to strengthen the wall.
You made a reservoir between the two walls for the water of the Old Pool. But you did not look to the one who made it, or consider the one who planned it long ago.
On that day the Lord GOD of Armies called for weeping and mourning, for shaving the head and putting on sackcloth.
But look, there was joy and celebration, killing cattle and slaughtering sheep, eating meat and drinking wine: "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!"
The LORD of Armies revealed himself in my hearing: Surely this guilt will not be atoned for you until you die, says the Lord GOD of Armies.
This is what the Lord GOD of Armies says: Go, go to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace:
What right do you have here, and whom do you have here, that you have cut out a tomb for yourself here, cutting out a tomb on the height, carving a resting place for himself in the rock?
Look, the LORD is about to hurl you away violently, you strong man, and grasp you firmly.
He will roll you up tightly like a ball and throw you into a wide land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will be, you disgrace to your master's house!
I will thrust you from your office, and he will pull you down from your position.
On that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah.
I will clothe him with your robe and fasten your sash around him, and I will hand your authority over to him. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah.
I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David. What he opens, no one will shut, and what he shuts, no one will open.
I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a seat of honor for his father's house.
They will hang on him all the weight of his father's house, offspring and offshoots, all the small vessels, from bowls to all the jars.
On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, the peg driven into a firm place will give way. It will be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut off. For the LORD has spoken.
An oracle concerning Tyre: Wail, you ships of Tarshish! For Tyre is destroyed, without house or harbor. From the land of Cyprus the news has reached them.
Be silent, you who live on the coast, you merchants of Sidon, whom the seafarers have made rich.
On the great waters came the grain of Shihor; the harvest of the Nile was her revenue, and she became the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon, for the sea has spoken, the stronghold of the sea: "I have not been in labor or given birth; I have not raised young men or brought up young women."
When the report reaches Egypt, they will be in anguish at the report about Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish! Wail, you who live on the coast!
Is this your joyful city, whose origin is from days of old, whose feet carried her to settle in distant places?
Who has planned this against Tyre, the giver of crowns, whose merchants are princes, whose traders are the honored of the earth?
The LORD of Armies has planned it, to defile the pride of all glory and to humble all the honored of the earth.
Go through your land as the Nile does, Daughter Tarshish; there is no longer any restraint.
He has stretched out his hand over the sea and made kingdoms tremble. The LORD has given orders concerning Canaan to destroy its strongholds.
He said, "You will no longer celebrate, you oppressed virgin Daughter Sidon! Get up, cross over to Cyprus; even there you will find no rest."
Look at the land of the Chaldeans! This is the people that is no more. Assyria assigned it to desert creatures. They set up their siege towers; they stripped its palaces bare and made it a ruin.
Wail, you ships of Tarshish, for your fortress is destroyed!
On that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the lifetime of one king. At the end of seventy years it will be with Tyre as in the song about the prostitute:
"Take a lyre, go around the city, you forgotten prostitute! Play skillfully, sing many songs, so that you will be remembered."
At the end of seventy years the LORD will come to Tyre. She will return to her fees and will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth.

But her profit and her fees will be holy to the LORD. They will not be stored up or hoarded, but her profit will go to those who live in the LORD's presence, so that they may eat their fill and wear fine clothes.
Look, the LORD is about to empty the earth and lay it waste. He will twist its surface and scatter its inhabitants.
It will be the same for people and priest, for servant and master, for maid and mistress, for buyer and seller, for lender and borrower, for creditor and debtor.
The earth will be utterly emptied and utterly plundered, for the LORD has spoken this word.
The earth dries up and withers; the world languishes and withers; the highest of the people of the earth languish.
The earth is defiled under its inhabitants, for they have broken the laws, violated the decree and broken the everlasting covenant.
Therefore a curse devours the earth, and its people bear their guilt. Therefore the inhabitants of the earth are burned up, and few people are left.
The new wine dries up; the vine languishes. All the merrymakers groan.
The joyful sound of tambourines has stopped; the noise of the revelers has ended; the joyful sound of the lyre has stopped.
They no longer drink wine with a song; beer is bitter to those who drink it.
The city of chaos is broken down; every house is shut up so that no one can enter.
In the streets there is an outcry over wine; all joy has turned to gloom; the gladness of the earth has gone into exile.
Desolation is left in the city, and its gate is battered to ruins.
For so it will be in the middle of the earth, among the peoples: as when an olive tree is beaten, as at the gleaning when the grape harvest is over.
They raise their voices and shout for joy; they cry out from the west over the majesty of the LORD.
Therefore in the east give glory to the LORD; in the coastlands of the sea, give glory to the name of the LORD, the God of Israel.
From the ends of the earth we hear songs: "Glory to the Righteous One!" But I said, "I waste away, I waste away! Woe is me! The traitors betray; with treachery the traitors betray!"
Terror and pit and snare are upon you, you who live on the earth!

Whoever flees at the sound of terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the snare. For the windows of heaven are opened, and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is utterly broken; the earth is split apart; the earth is violently shaken.
The earth staggers like a drunkard; it sways like a hut. Its rebellion lies heavy on it; it falls and will not rise again.
On that day the LORD will punish the host of heaven in heaven, and the kings of the earth on the earth.
They will be gathered together like prisoners in a pit; they will be shut up in a prison, and after many days they will be punished.
The moon will be ashamed and the sun abashed, for the LORD of Armies will reign on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, and his glory will be before his elders.
LORD, you are my God; I will exalt you; I will praise your name. For you have done wonderful things, plans formed long ago, faithful and sure.
For you have made the city a heap of rubble, the fortified town a ruin. The palace of foreigners is a city no more; it will never be rebuilt.
Therefore a strong people will honor you; the city of ruthless nations will fear you.
For you have been a refuge for the poor, a refuge for the needy in their distress, a shelter from the storm and a shade from the heat. For the breath of the ruthless is like a storm against a wall.
Like heat in a dry land, you subdue the uproar of foreigners. As heat is cooled by the shade of a cloud, so the song of the ruthless is silenced.
On this mountain the LORD of Armies will prepare for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of aged wine, of rich food full of marrow, of aged wine well refined.
On this mountain he will swallow up the shroud that covers all peoples, the sheet that is spread over all nations.
He will swallow up death forever. The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face and remove the disgrace of his people from all the earth. For the LORD has spoken.
On that day they will say, "Look, this is our God; we waited for him, and he has saved us. This is the LORD; we waited for him. Let us rejoice and be glad in his salvation."
For the hand of the LORD will rest on this mountain. But Moab will be trampled down where he stands, as straw is trampled down in a dung pit.
He will spread out his hands in it, as a swimmer spreads out his hands to swim, but he will bring down his pride, for all the skill of his hands.
The high fortress of your walls he will bring down, lay low and cast to the ground, to the dust.
On that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah: "We have a strong city; he sets up salvation as its walls and ramparts.
Open the gates, so that the righteous nation may enter, the nation that keeps faith.
You keep in perfect peace the one whose mind is steadfast, because he trusts in you.
Trust in the LORD forever, for in the LORD, the LORD, you have an everlasting Rock.
For he has brought down those who live on high, the lofty city. He lays it low, lays it low to the ground, and casts it down to the dust.
The foot tramples it, the feet of the poor, the steps of the needy."
The path of the righteous is level; you, the Upright One, make smooth the way of the righteous.
Yes, LORD, in the path of your judgments we wait for you. Your name and your renown are the desire of our soul.
My soul longs for you in the night; yes, my spirit within me seeks you at dawn. For when your judgments come upon the earth, the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.
If the wicked are shown favor, they do not learn righteousness. In a land of honesty they act unjustly and do not see the majesty of the LORD.
LORD, your hand is lifted up, but they do not see it. Let them see your zeal for your people and be ashamed; let the fire meant for your enemies consume them.
LORD, you will establish peace for us; indeed, all that we have done, you have done for us.
LORD our God, other lords besides you have ruled over us, but your name alone do we honor.
The dead do not live; the shades do not rise. That is why you punished them and destroyed them, and wiped out all memory of them.
You have enlarged the nation, LORD; you have enlarged the nation; you are glorified. You have extended all the borders of the land.
LORD, in distress they came looking for you; they poured out a whispered prayer when your discipline was on them.
As a pregnant woman about to give birth writhes and cries out in her pains, so were we because of you, LORD.
We were pregnant, we writhed, but we gave birth only to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, and no inhabitants of the world have been born.
Your dead will live; my dead bodies will rise. Wake up and shout for joy, you who dwell in the dust! For your dew is a dew of light, and the earth will give birth to the shades.
Go, my people, enter your rooms and shut your door behind you. Hide for a little while, until the wrath has passed by.
For look, the LORD is coming out from his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth for their guilt. The earth will uncover the blood shed on it and will no longer cover its slain.
On that day the LORD will punish with his sword, hard and great and strong, Leviathan the fleeing serpent, Leviathan the twisting serpent, and he will kill the dragon that is in the sea.
On that day sing of a delightful vineyard:
I, the LORD, am its keeper; I water it every moment. So that no one may harm it, I guard it night and day.
I have no anger. If only there were briers and thorns to fight against! I would march against them; I would burn them all together.
Or else let them take hold of my protection; let them make peace with me; yes, let them make peace with me.
In days to come Jacob will take root; Israel will blossom and sprout, and fill the face of the world with fruit.
Has he struck him as he struck those who struck him? Has he been killed as those who killed him were killed?
By driving her away, by sending her off, you contended with her. He removed her with his fierce wind on the day of the east wind.

Therefore by this the guilt of Jacob will be atoned for, and this will be the full fruit of the removal of his sin: when he makes all the altar stones like chalk stones crushed to pieces, no Asherah poles or incense altars will be left standing.
For the fortified city is desolate, a settlement abandoned and deserted like the wilderness. There the calf grazes, there it lies down and strips its branches.

When its twigs are dry, they are broken off; women come and make fires with them. For this is a people without understanding; therefore their Maker will have no compassion on them, and the one who formed them will show them no favor.
On that day the LORD will thresh from the flowing Euphrates to the Wadi of Egypt, and you will be gathered up one by one, people of Israel.

On that day a great ram's horn will be blown, and those who were perishing in the land of Assyria and those who were scattered in the land of Egypt will come and worship the LORD on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.
Woe to the proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim, to the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, of those overcome by wine!
Look, the Lord has one who is mighty and strong. Like a storm of hail, a destroying wind, like a storm of mighty, flooding waters, he will throw it down to the ground with his hand.
The proud crown of the drunkards of Ephraim will be trampled underfoot.

And the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which is on the head of the fertile valley, will be like a fig that ripens before the summer harvest: as soon as someone sees it, he swallows it while it is still in his hand.
On that day the LORD of Armies will be a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty for the remnant of his people,
a spirit of justice for the one who sits in judgment, and strength for those who turn back the battle at the gate.

But these too reel from wine and stagger from beer: priest and prophet reel from beer; they are swallowed up by wine; they stagger from beer; they reel when they see visions; they stumble when they give judgment.
For all the tables are covered with vomit; no place is without filth.
Whom is he trying to teach? To whom is he explaining his message? To children just weaned from milk, just taken from the breast?
For it is tsav la-tsav, tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, qav la-qav, a little here, a little there.
Very well, then: with stammering lips and in a foreign tongue he will speak to this people,
to whom he said, "This is the place of rest; give rest to the weary; this is the place of repose." But they would not listen.

So the word of the LORD will be to them tsav la-tsav, tsav la-tsav, qav la-qav, qav la-qav, a little here, a little there, so that they will go and fall backward, be broken, be snared and be captured.
Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scoffers who rule this people in Jerusalem!

For you have said, "We have made a covenant with death, and with Sheol we have made an agreement. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, it will not reach us, for we have made lies our refuge and hidden ourselves in falsehood."
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am laying in Zion a stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a firm foundation. Whoever trusts will not panic.
I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the refuge of lies, and water will flood the hiding place.
Your covenant with death will be annulled, and your agreement with Sheol will not stand. When the overwhelming scourge passes through, you will be trampled down by it.
As often as it passes through, it will take you; morning after morning it will pass through, by day and by night. To understand the message will be sheer terror.
For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap around you.
For the LORD will rise up as at Mount Perazim; he will rage as in the valley of Gibeon, to do his work, his strange work, and to perform his task, his alien task.
So now, stop your scoffing, or your chains will be made heavier. For I have heard from the Lord GOD of Armies a decree of destruction against the whole land.
Listen and hear my voice; pay attention and hear what I say.
Does the plowman plow all day to plant seed? Does he keep on breaking up and harrowing his ground?
When he has leveled its surface, does he not scatter dill and sow cumin? Does he not put wheat in rows, barley in its place, and spelt at its border?
His God instructs him and teaches him the right way.
Dill is not threshed with a threshing sledge, and a cartwheel is not rolled over cumin. Dill is beaten out with a stick, and cumin with a rod.
Grain for bread is crushed, but not endlessly; he does not keep threshing it forever. He drives the wheel of his cart and his horses over it, but he does not crush it.
This also comes from the LORD of Armies. His counsel is wonderful, and his wisdom is great.
Woe to Ariel, Ariel, the city where David camped! Add year to year; let the festivals run their round.
Yet I will bring distress on Ariel. There will be mourning and lamenting, and she will be to me like an altar hearth.
I will camp against you all around; I will besiege you with towers and set up siege works against you.
Brought low, you will speak from the ground, and your words will come muffled from the dust. Your voice will come from the ground like a ghost's, and your words will whisper from the dust.
But the horde of your foes will be like fine dust, the horde of the ruthless like chaff blowing away. Suddenly, in an instant,
you will be visited by the LORD of Armies with thunder and earthquake and great noise, with whirlwind and storm and the flame of a devouring fire.
The horde of all the nations that fight against Ariel, all who attack her and her stronghold and bring distress on her, will be like a dream, a vision in the night.

It will be as when a hungry man dreams that he is eating, but he wakes up, and his hunger is not satisfied, or as when a thirsty man dreams that he is drinking, but he wakes up faint, and his thirst is not quenched. So it will be with the horde of all the nations that fight against Mount Zion.
Be stunned and stay stunned; blind yourselves and be blind! Be drunk, but not with wine; stagger, but not with beer!
For the LORD has poured out on you a spirit of deep sleep. He has shut your eyes, the prophets, and covered your heads, the seers.
For you this whole vision has become like the words of a sealed scroll. When they give it to someone who can read and say, "Read this, please," he answers, "I cannot, for it is sealed."
Or when they give the scroll to someone who cannot read and say, "Read this, please," he answers, "I cannot read."
The Lord said: Because this people draw near with their mouth and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their fear of me is a human command learned by rote,
therefore, look, I will again do amazing things with this people, wonder upon wonder. The wisdom of their wise will perish, and the understanding of their discerning will vanish.
Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from the LORD, whose deeds are done in the dark, and who say, "Who sees us? Who knows us?"
How you turn things upside down! Should the potter be thought of as the clay? Should what is made say of its maker, "He did not make me"? Should the pot say of the potter, "He has no understanding"?
In a very little while, will not Lebanon be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field be thought of as a forest?
On that day the deaf will hear the words of a scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.
The humble will again rejoice in the LORD, and the poorest of people will exult in the Holy One of Israel.
For the ruthless will be gone, the scoffer will come to an end, and all who watch for a chance to do evil will be cut off,
those who make a person guilty with a word, who lay a trap for the one who argues for justice at the gate, and with empty claims turn aside the innocent.
Therefore this is what the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, says to the house of Jacob: Jacob will no longer be ashamed; his face will no longer grow pale.
For when he sees his children, the work of my hands, in his midst, they will treat my name as holy. They will treat the Holy One of Jacob as holy and stand in awe of the God of Israel.
Those who go astray in spirit will gain understanding, and those who grumble will accept instruction.
Woe to the rebellious children, declares the LORD, who carry out plans that are not mine, and make an alliance, but not by my Spirit, heaping sin on sin,
who set out to go down to Egypt without asking my advice, to take refuge in Pharaoh's protection and to shelter in Egypt's shade!
But Pharaoh's protection will be your shame, and shelter in Egypt's shade your disgrace.
For though his officials are in Zoan and his envoys have reached Hanes,
everyone will be put to shame because of a people who cannot help them, who bring neither help nor benefit, but only shame and disgrace.

An oracle concerning the animals of the Negev: Through a land of trouble and distress, of lioness and lion, of viper and flying serpent, they carry their wealth on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people that cannot help them.
Egypt's help is worthless and empty. Therefore I have called her "Rahab, who sits still."
Now go, write it on a tablet in their presence, and inscribe it in a scroll, so that it may be there for the time to come, forever and ever.
For they are a rebellious people, lying children, children unwilling to listen to the instruction of the LORD,
who say to the seers, "Do not see!" and to the prophets, "Do not prophesy to us what is right! Tell us smooth things; prophesy illusions!
Get out of the way; turn aside from the path; stop confronting us with the Holy One of Israel!"
Therefore this is what the Holy One of Israel says: Because you have rejected this word and trusted in oppression and deceit, and relied on them,
this guilt will be for you like a breach in a high wall, bulging out and about to fall, whose collapse comes suddenly, in an instant.
