It will break like a potter's jar, smashed so ruthlessly that among its pieces not a fragment is found to take fire from a hearth or to scoop water from a cistern.
For this is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and trust will be your strength. But you were not willing.
You said, "No! We will flee on horses." So you will flee! "We will ride on swift horses." So your pursuers will be swift!
A thousand will flee at the threat of one; at the threat of five you will all flee, until you are left like a flagpole on a mountaintop, like a signal flag on a hill.
Therefore the LORD waits to be gracious to you; therefore he rises to show you compassion. For the LORD is a God of justice. Happy are all who wait for him!
You people in Zion, who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be gracious to you at the sound of your cry; as soon as he hears it, he will answer you.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of adversity and the water of affliction, your teacher will no longer hide himself, but your eyes will see your teacher.
Your ears will hear a word behind you: "This is the way; walk in it," whenever you turn to the right or to the left.
Then you will defile your silver-plated idols and your gold-covered images. You will throw them away like a menstrual cloth and say to them, "Get out!"
He will give rain for the seed you sow in the ground, and the bread that the ground produces will be rich and plentiful. On that day your cattle will graze in broad pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the ground will eat seasoned fodder, winnowed with shovel and fork.
On every high mountain and on every lofty hill there will be streams flowing with water, on the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall.

The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be seven times brighter, like the light of seven days, on the day the LORD binds up the wounds of his people and heals the bruises from his blows.
Look, the name of the LORD comes from far away, burning with his anger, in thick, rising smoke. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like a devouring fire.
His breath is like a flooding torrent that rises up to the neck, to sift the nations in the sieve of destruction, and to put in the jaws of the peoples a bridle that leads them astray.
You will have a song as on the night when a festival is kept holy, and gladness of heart as when people go up with the flute to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will make his majestic voice heard and show his arm coming down, in raging anger and the flame of a devouring fire, with cloudburst and storm and hailstones.
For at the voice of the LORD Assyria will be shattered, when he strikes with the rod.
Every stroke of the appointed rod that the LORD lays on him will be to the sound of tambourines and lyres, as he fights against them in battle with brandished arm.

For a Topheth has long been prepared; it has been made ready for the king. Its fire pit has been made deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of sulfur, sets it ablaze.

Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many and in horsemen because they are very strong, but do not look to the Holy One of Israel or seek the LORD!
Yet he too is wise and brings disaster; he does not take back his words. He will rise up against the house of evildoers and against the helpers of those who do wrong.

The Egyptians are human beings and not God; their horses are flesh and not spirit. When the LORD stretches out his hand, the helper will stumble and the one who is helped will fall; they will all perish together.

For this is what the LORD has said to me: As a lion or a young lion growls over its prey, and though a whole band of shepherds is called out against it, it is not terrified by their shouting or daunted by their noise, so the LORD of Armies will come down to wage war on Mount Zion and on its hill.
Like birds hovering overhead, so the LORD of Armies will shield Jerusalem; he will shield and rescue it, pass over and deliver it.
Return to the one against whom the Israelites have so deeply rebelled.
For on that day each of you will reject your idols of silver and your idols of gold, which your hands have made for you in sin.
Assyria will fall by a sword not of man; a sword not of a human being will devour him. He will flee from the sword, and his young men will be put to forced labor.
His rock will pass away in terror, and his officers will be dismayed at the signal flag, declares the LORD, whose fire is in Zion and whose furnace is in Jerusalem.
Look, a king will reign in righteousness, and rulers will rule with justice.
Each of them will be like a shelter from the wind and a refuge from the storm, like streams of water in a dry land, like the shade of a great rock in a weary land.
Then the eyes of those who see will no longer be closed, and the ears of those who hear will listen.
The mind of the rash will understand and know, and the tongue of those who stammer will speak quickly and clearly.
The fool will no longer be called noble, and the scoundrel will no longer be called honorable.
For the fool speaks folly, and his mind plots evil: to practice godlessness, to spread error about the LORD, to leave the hungry empty and to deprive the thirsty of drink.
The scoundrel's ways are evil; he devises wicked schemes to ruin the poor with lies, even when the needy plead their just cause.
But the noble person makes noble plans, and by noble deeds he stands.
You women who are at ease, rise up and hear my voice! You daughters who feel secure, listen to what I say!
In little more than a year you who feel secure will tremble, for the grape harvest will fail, and the harvest of fruit will not come.
Tremble, you women who are at ease! Shudder, you who feel secure! Strip off your clothes, stand bare, and put sackcloth around your waists.
Beat your breasts for the pleasant fields, for the fruitful vine,
for the soil of my people, where thorns and briers grow up, yes, for all the houses of joy in the joyful city.
For the palace is abandoned, the busy city deserted. The hill and the watchtower will become caves forever, the delight of wild donkeys, a pasture for flocks,
until the Spirit is poured out on us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field, and the fruitful field is thought of as a forest.
Then justice will dwell in the wilderness, and righteousness will live in the fruitful field.
The work of righteousness will be peace, and the effect of righteousness will be quietness and confidence forever.
My people will live in a peaceful home, in secure dwellings and in undisturbed resting places.
But hail will fall when the forest comes down, and the city will be utterly laid low.
Happy are you who sow beside every stream, who let the ox and the donkey range free!

Woe to you, destroyer, you who have not been destroyed, you traitor, whom no one has betrayed! When you have finished destroying, you will be destroyed; when you have done with betraying, they will betray you.
LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you. Be their strength every morning, our salvation in time of distress.
At the sound of the tumult, peoples flee; when you rise up, nations scatter.
Your plunder is gathered as the caterpillar gathers; as locusts swarm, people swarm over it.
The LORD is exalted, for he dwells on high; he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.
He will be the stability of your times, a wealth of salvation, of wisdom and knowledge. The fear of the LORD is Zion's treasure.
Look, their heroes cry out in the streets; the envoys of peace weep bitterly.
The highways are deserted; no one travels the roads. He has broken the treaty and despised the cities; he has no regard for anyone.
The land mourns and languishes; Lebanon is ashamed and withers. Sharon is like the Arabah, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their leaves.
Now I will arise, says the LORD; now I will lift myself up; now I will be exalted.
You conceive chaff and give birth to straw; your breath is a fire that will consume you.
The peoples will be burned to lime, like cut thorns set on fire.
Hear, you who are far away, what I have done; and you who are near, acknowledge my might.
The sinners in Zion are terrified; trembling has seized the godless: "Who of us can live with the devouring fire? Who of us can live with everlasting burning?"

The one who walks in righteousness and speaks what is right, who rejects gain from extortion, who shakes his hands so that they hold no bribe, who stops his ears from hearing of bloodshed and shuts his eyes from looking at evil,
he will dwell on the heights; his refuge will be the fortress of the rocks. His bread will be given him; his water will not fail.
Your eyes will see the king in his beauty; they will see a land that stretches far away.
Your mind will think back on the terror: "Where is the one who counted? Where is the one who weighed the tribute? Where is the one who counted the towers?"
You will no longer see the insolent people, a people of speech too obscure to understand, with a stammering tongue that no one can make sense of.
Look at Zion, the city of our festivals! Your eyes will see Jerusalem, a peaceful dwelling, a tent that will not be moved, whose stakes will never be pulled up and none of whose ropes will be broken.
But there the LORD will be majestic for us, a place of rivers and broad streams, where no galley with oars will go, and no mighty ship will pass.
For the LORD is our judge, the LORD is our lawgiver, the LORD is our king; he will save us.
Your ropes hang loose; they cannot hold the mast firm in its place or spread the sail. Then plunder in abundance will be divided; even the lame will carry off the spoil.
No one who lives there will say, "I am sick"; the people who live there will be forgiven their guilt.
Come near, you nations, and hear! Pay attention, you peoples! Let the earth hear, and all that fills it, the world and all that comes from it.
For the LORD is angry with all the nations and furious with all their armies. He has devoted them to destruction; he has handed them over to slaughter.
Their slain will be thrown out, and the stench of their corpses will rise. The mountains will melt with their blood.

All the army of the heavens will rot away, and the heavens will be rolled up like a scroll. All their army will wither, as a leaf withers and falls from the vine, like a withered fig from the fig tree.
For my sword has drunk its fill in the heavens. Look, it comes down on Edom, on the people I have devoted to destruction, to judge them.

The LORD has a sword; it is filled with blood. It is gorged with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats, with the fat of the kidneys of rams. For the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah and a great slaughter in the land of Edom.
Wild oxen will go down with them, and young bulls with the mighty steers. Their land will drink its fill of blood, and their soil will be gorged with fat.
For the LORD has a day of vengeance, a year of repayment, to uphold the cause of Zion.
Edom's streams will be turned into pitch, and its soil into sulfur; its land will become burning pitch.
Night and day it will not be quenched; its smoke will go up forever. From generation to generation it will lie in ruins; forever and ever no one will pass through it.
The pelican and the owl will possess it; the great owl and the raven will live there. He will stretch over it the measuring line of chaos and the plumb line of emptiness.
Its nobles will have nothing there to call a kingdom, and all its princes will come to nothing.
Thorns will grow up in its fortresses, nettles and thistles in its strongholds. It will be a haunt for jackals, a home for ostriches.
Desert creatures will meet with hyenas, and the wild goat will call to its fellow. There too the night creature will settle and find for herself a place to rest.
There the owl will nest and lay eggs; it will hatch them and gather its young in its shade. There too the kites will gather, each one with its mate.
Search in the scroll of the LORD, and read: Not one of these will be missing; none will be without its mate. For it is my mouth that has commanded it, and his Spirit that has gathered them.
He has cast the lot for them, and his hand has divided the land among them with the measuring line. They will possess it forever; they will live in it from generation to generation.
The wilderness and the dry land will be glad; the desert will rejoice and blossom like the crocus.

It will blossom abundantly and rejoice, yes, rejoice with shouts of joy. The glory of Lebanon will be given to it, the splendor of Carmel and Sharon. They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God.
Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the knees that give way.
Say to those whose hearts are anxious, "Be strong, do not be afraid. Look, your God will come with vengeance; with the recompense of God he will come and save you."
Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped.
Then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will shout for joy. For water will burst out in the wilderness and streams in the desert.
The burning sand will become a pool, and the thirsty ground springs of water. In the haunts where jackals lay, grass will become reeds and papyrus.
A highway will be there, a road, and it will be called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel on it; it will be for those who walk that way, and fools will not wander onto it.
No lion will be there, and no ravenous beast will go up on it; they will not be found there. But the redeemed will walk there.
Those whom the LORD has ransomed will return and come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will be on their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
In the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria came up against all the fortified cities of Judah and captured them.
The king of Assyria sent the Rabshakeh with a large army from Lachish to King Hezekiah at Jerusalem. He stood by the channel of the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field.
Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, went out to him.
The Rabshakeh said to them, "Tell Hezekiah, 'This is what the great king, the king of Assyria, says: What is this confidence of yours? What are you trusting in?
I say that your strategy and strength for war are mere words. Now, on whom are you relying, that you have rebelled against me?
Look, you are relying on Egypt, that broken reed of a staff, which goes into the hand of anyone who leans on it and pierces it. That is what Pharaoh king of Egypt is to all who rely on him.
But if you say to me, "We are trusting in the LORD our God," isn't he the one whose high places and altars Hezekiah has removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, "You must worship before this altar"?
So now, make a wager with my master, the king of Assyria: I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able to put riders on them!
How then can you drive back even one officer, one of the least of my master's servants, when you rely on Egypt for chariots and horsemen?
And besides, have I come up against this land to destroy it without the LORD? The LORD himself said to me, "Go up against this land and destroy it."'"

Then Eliakim, Shebna and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, "Please speak to your servants in Aramaic, for we understand it. Do not speak to us in the language of Judah in the hearing of the people on the wall."

But the Rabshakeh said, "Was it to your master and to you that my master sent me to speak these words? Wasn't it to the men sitting on the wall, who, like you, will have to eat their own dung and drink their own urine?"
Then the Rabshakeh stood and called out in a loud voice in the language of Judah. He said, "Hear the words of the great king, the king of Assyria!
This is what the king says: Do not let Hezekiah deceive you, for he will not be able to rescue you.
Do not let Hezekiah make you trust in the LORD by saying, 'The LORD will surely rescue us; this city will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'

Do not listen to Hezekiah, for this is what the king of Assyria says: Make peace with me and come out to me. Then each of you will eat from his own vine and his own fig tree, and each of you will drink water from his own cistern,
until I come and take you to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards.
Do not let Hezekiah mislead you by saying, 'The LORD will rescue us.' Has any of the gods of the nations rescued his land from the hand of the king of Assyria?
Where are the gods of Hamath and Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim? Did they rescue Samaria from my hand?
Who among all the gods of these lands has rescued his land from my hand, that the LORD should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?"
But they kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, "Do not answer him."

Then Eliakim son of Hilkiah, the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and Joah son of Asaph, the recorder, came to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and they told him the words of the Rabshakeh.
When King Hezekiah heard it, he tore his clothes, covered himself with sackcloth and went into the house of the LORD.
He sent Eliakim the palace administrator, Shebna the secretary and the senior priests, all wearing sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
They said to him, "This is what Hezekiah says: Today is a day of distress, of rebuke and of disgrace. Children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to deliver them.

Perhaps the LORD your God will hear the words of the Rabshakeh, whom his master the king of Assyria has sent to mock the living God, and will rebuke him for the words that the LORD your God has heard. So pray for the remnant that is left."
When King Hezekiah's servants came to Isaiah,
Isaiah said to them, "Say this to your master: 'This is what the LORD says: Do not be afraid of the words you have heard, with which the king of Assyria's lackeys have insulted me.
I am going to put a spirit in him, so that he will hear a rumor and go back to his own land, and I will make him fall by the sword in his own land.'"
The Rabshakeh went back and found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he had heard that the king had left Lachish.
Then the king heard that Tirhakah king of Cush had set out to fight against him. When he heard it, he sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
"Say this to Hezekiah king of Judah: Do not let your God, in whom you trust, deceive you by saying, 'Jerusalem will not be handed over to the king of Assyria.'
Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, destroying them completely. And will you be rescued?
Did the gods of the nations that my predecessors destroyed rescue them, the nations of Gozan, Haran and Rezeph, and the people of Eden who were in Telassar?
Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena and of Ivvah?"
Hezekiah took the letter from the hand of the messengers and read it. Then he went up to the house of the LORD, and Hezekiah spread it out before the LORD.
Hezekiah prayed to the LORD and said,
"The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, enthroned above the cherubim, you alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the heavens and the earth.
Turn your ear, LORD, and hear. Open your eyes, LORD, and see. Hear all the words that Sennacherib has sent to mock the living God.
It is true, LORD, that the kings of Assyria have laid waste all the countries and their lands.
They have thrown their gods into the fire, for they were not gods but only the work of human hands, wood and stone. So they destroyed them.
Now, LORD our God, save us from his hand, so that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you alone are the LORD."
Then Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Because you have prayed to me about Sennacherib king of Assyria,
this is the word that the LORD has spoken against him: The virgin daughter Zion despises you and mocks you. Daughter Jerusalem tosses her head behind your back.
Whom have you mocked and insulted? Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride? Against the Holy One of Israel!

Through your servants you have mocked the Lord. You have said, 'With my many chariots I have gone up to the heights of the mountains, to the farthest reaches of Lebanon. I cut down its tallest cedars, its choicest junipers. I came to its farthest heights, its densest forest.
I dug wells and drank water, and with the soles of my feet I dried up all the streams of Egypt.'
Have you not heard? Long ago I planned it. From days of old I formed it. Now I have brought it about, that you should turn fortified cities into heaps of ruins.
Their people, drained of strength, are dismayed and put to shame. They are like plants of the field and tender green shoots, like grass on the rooftops, like a field before the grain is grown.
I know when you sit down, when you go out and when you come in, and how you rage against me.
Because you rage against me and your arrogance has reached my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and my bit in your mouth, and I will turn you back by the way you came.

And this will be the sign for you: This year you will eat what grows by itself, and in the second year what springs up from that. But in the third year, sow and reap, plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
The survivors of the house of Judah who are left will again take root below and bear fruit above.
For from Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Armies will do this.

Therefore this is what the LORD says concerning the king of Assyria: He will not come into this city or shoot an arrow there. He will not come before it with a shield or build a siege ramp against it.
By the way that he came, he will go back. He will not come into this city, declares the LORD.
I will defend this city and save it, for my own sake and for the sake of my servant David."
Then the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 in the camp of Assyria. When people got up early in the morning, there were all the dead bodies.
So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and went back home, and he stayed in Nineveh.

One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of Nisroch his god, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esarhaddon became king in his place.

In those days Hezekiah became ill and was at the point of death. The prophet Isaiah son of Amoz came to him and said to him, "This is what the LORD says: Give instructions to your household, for you are going to die. You will not recover."
Then Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the LORD.
He said, "Please, LORD, remember how I have walked before you faithfully and with my whole heart, and have done what is good in your eyes." And Hezekiah wept bitterly.
Then the word of the LORD came to Isaiah:
"Go and say to Hezekiah, 'This is what the LORD, the God of your ancestor David, says: I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. I am going to add fifteen years to your life.
I will rescue you and this city from the power of the king of Assyria, and I will defend this city.
This is the sign to you from the LORD that the LORD will do what he has promised:
I am going to make the shadow on the stairway of Ahaz, which has gone down with the sun, go back ten steps.'" So the sun went back ten steps on the stairway it had gone down.
A writing of Hezekiah king of Judah, after he had been ill and had recovered from his illness:
I said, "In the prime of my days I must go through the gates of Sheol; I am robbed of the rest of my years."
I said, "I will not see the LORD, the LORD in the land of the living. I will no longer look on any human being, when I am among those who live where life has ceased."
My dwelling is pulled up and taken away from me like a shepherd's tent. Like a weaver I have rolled up my life; he cuts me off from the loom. From day to night you bring me to an end.
I composed myself until morning, but like a lion he breaks all my bones. From day to night you bring me to an end.
Like a swift or a thrush I chirp; I moan like a dove. My eyes grow weak from looking upward. Lord, I am oppressed; be my security!
What can I say? He has spoken to me, and he himself has done it. I will walk slowly all my years because of the bitterness of my soul.
Lord, by these things people live, and in all of them is the life of my spirit. You restore my health and let me live!
Look, it was for my good that I had such bitter grief. In your love you have kept my life from the pit of destruction, for you have thrown all my sins behind your back.
For Sheol cannot thank you; death cannot praise you. Those who go down to the Pit cannot hope for your faithfulness.
The living, the living, they thank you, as I do today. Fathers make known your faithfulness to their children.
The LORD will save me, and we will play my songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD.
Isaiah said, "Let them take a cake of figs and spread it on the boil, and he will recover."
And Hezekiah said, "What is the sign that I will go up to the house of the LORD?"
At that time Merodach-baladan son of Baladan king of Babylon sent letters and a gift to Hezekiah, for he had heard that he had been ill and had recovered.

Hezekiah was glad because of them and showed them his treasure house: the silver, the gold, the spices and the fine oil, his whole armory, and everything that was found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his palace or in all his realm that Hezekiah did not show them.
Then the prophet Isaiah came to King Hezekiah and said to him, "What did these men say? And where did they come to you from?" Hezekiah said, "They came to me from a distant land, from Babylon."
He asked, "What did they see in your palace?" Hezekiah said, "They saw everything in my palace. There is nothing in my treasuries that I did not show them."
Then Isaiah said to Hezekiah, "Hear the word of the LORD of Armies.
The days are coming when everything in your palace, and all that your ancestors have stored up until this day, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left, says the LORD.
And some of your sons, your own descendants whom you will father, will be taken away, and they will be officials in the palace of the king of Babylon."
Hezekiah said to Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." For he thought, "There will be peace and security in my days."
Comfort, comfort my people, says your God.
Speak tenderly to Jerusalem, and call out to her that her hard service is over, that her guilt has been paid for, that she has received from the hand of the LORD double for all her sins.
A voice is shouting: "In the wilderness prepare the way for the LORD; make straight in the desert a highway for our God.
Every valley will be raised up, and every mountain and hill made low. The uneven ground will become level, and the rugged places a plain.
Then the glory of the LORD will be revealed, and all people will see it together. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken."
A voice says, "Shout!" And I said, "What shall I shout?" All people are grass, and all their faithfulness is like the flower of the field.
The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the LORD blows on it. Surely the people are grass.
The grass withers, the flower fades, but the word of our God will stand forever.

Go up on a high mountain, you who bring good news to Zion! Raise your voice with strength, you who bring good news to Jerusalem! Raise it; do not be afraid! Say to the towns of Judah, "Here is your God!"
Look, the Lord GOD comes with might, and his arm rules for him. Look, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him.
Like a shepherd he tends his flock. He gathers the lambs in his arm and carries them close to his heart; he gently leads the ewes that have young.

Who has measured the waters in the hollow of his hand, and marked off the heavens with the span of his hand? Who has held the dust of the earth in a measure, and weighed the mountains on scales and the hills in a balance?
Who has measured the Spirit of the LORD, or instructed him as his counselor?
Whom did he consult to give him understanding? Who taught him the path of justice, taught him knowledge, and showed him the way of understanding?
Look, the nations are like a drop from a bucket; they are counted as dust on the scales. Look, he lifts up the coastlands like fine dust.
Lebanon is not enough for fuel, nor are its animals enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are as nothing before him; he counts them as less than nothing and emptiness.
To whom, then, will you compare God? What likeness will you set beside him?
An idol? A craftsman casts it, and a goldsmith overlays it with gold and casts silver chains for it.
One too poor for such an offering chooses wood that will not rot. He looks for a skilled craftsman to set up an idol that will not topple.
Do you not know? Have you not heard? Has it not been told you from the beginning? Have you not understood how the earth was founded?
He is the one who sits enthroned above the circle of the earth, and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers. He stretches out the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He brings rulers to nothing and makes the judges of the earth like emptiness.
Scarcely are they planted, scarcely are they sown, scarcely has their stem taken root in the ground, when he blows on them and they wither, and the storm carries them off like straw.
To whom, then, will you compare me, that I should be like him? says the Holy One.
Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He brings out their army by number and calls them all by name. Because of his great strength and mighty power, not one of them is missing.
Why do you say, Jacob, and why do you declare, Israel, "My way is hidden from the LORD, and my God pays no attention to my cause"?
Do you not know? Have you not heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the Creator of the ends of the earth. He does not grow tired or weary; his understanding cannot be searched out.
He gives strength to the weary, and to those who have no power he gives great might.
Even young men grow tired and weary, and strong young men stumble and fall.
But those who wait for the LORD will renew their strength. They will rise up on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not grow tired.
Be silent before me, you coastlands! Let the peoples renew their strength! Let them come near and then speak; let us come together for judgment.
Who has stirred up one from the east, whom victory meets at every step? He hands nations over to him and makes him trample kings. His sword makes them like dust, his bow like driven straw.
He pursues them and passes on unharmed, by a path his feet have never traveled.
Who has done this and carried it out, calling the generations from the beginning? I, the LORD, am the first, and with the last I am he.
The coastlands have seen it and are afraid; the ends of the earth tremble. They have drawn near and come.
Each one helps his neighbor and says to his brother, "Be strong!"

The craftsman encourages the goldsmith, and the one who smooths with the hammer encourages the one who strikes the anvil. He says of the soldering, "It is good." He fastens the idol with nails so that it will not topple.
But you, Israel, my servant, Jacob, whom I have chosen, offspring of Abraham my friend,
you whom I took hold of from the ends of the earth and called from its farthest corners, and to whom I said, "You are my servant; I have chosen you and have not rejected you":
Do not be afraid, for I am with you; do not be dismayed, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will help you; I will uphold you with my righteous right hand.
Look, all who rage against you will be put to shame and disgraced. Those who contend with you will be as nothing and will perish.
You will look for those who quarrel with you, but you will not find them. Those who make war against you will be as nothing, nothing at all.
For I, the LORD your God, take hold of your right hand and say to you, "Do not be afraid; I will help you."
Do not be afraid, you worm Jacob, you little band of Israel! I will help you, declares the LORD; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Look, I will make you into a threshing sledge, new and sharp, with many teeth. You will thresh the mountains and crush them, and make the hills like chaff.
You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the storm will scatter them. But you will rejoice in the LORD; you will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy look for water, but there is none; their tongues are parched with thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them; I, the God of Israel, will not abandon them.
I will open rivers on the bare heights, and springs in the middle of the valleys. I will turn the wilderness into pools of water, and the dry land into springs of water.
I will put in the wilderness the cedar, the acacia, the myrtle and the olive. I will set in the desert the juniper, the plane tree and the pine together,
so that people may see and know, may consider and understand together, that the hand of the LORD has done this, and the Holy One of Israel has created it.
Present your case, says the LORD; bring forward your arguments, says the King of Jacob.
Let them come forward and tell us what is going to happen. Tell us the former things, what they were, so that we may consider them and know how they turned out. Or announce to us the things to come.
Tell us what is coming hereafter, so that we may know that you are gods. Yes, do something, good or bad, so that we may be dismayed and see it together.
Look, you are less than nothing, and your work is less than nothing. Whoever chooses you is detestable.
I stirred up one from the north, and he has come, one from the rising of the sun who calls on my name. He will tread on rulers as on mortar, as a potter treads clay.
Who announced this from the beginning, so that we could know, and beforehand, so that we could say, "He is right"? No one announced it; no one proclaimed it; no one heard any words from you.
I was the first to say to Zion, "Look, here they are!" and I give Jerusalem a messenger of good news.
But I look, and there is no one; among these there is no counselor who can give an answer when I ask them.
Look, all of them are a delusion; their works are nothing; their cast images are wind and emptiness.
Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one, in whom I delight. I have put my Spirit on him; he will bring justice to the nations.
He will not cry out or raise his voice, or make his voice heard in the street.
A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. He will faithfully bring justice.
He will not grow dim or be bruised until he has established justice on the earth, and the coastlands wait for his instruction.

This is what God, the LORD, says, who created the heavens and stretched them out, who spread out the earth and all that comes from it, who gives breath to the people on it and spirit to those who walk on it:
I, the LORD, have called you in righteousness; I will take hold of your hand. I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people, a light for the nations,
to open eyes that are blind, to bring prisoners out of the dungeon, and those who sit in darkness out of the prison.
I am the LORD; that is my name. I will not give my glory to another, or my praise to idols.
Look, the former things have come to pass, and new things I now declare. Before they spring up, I tell you of them.
Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise from the end of the earth, you who go down to the sea, and all that is in it, you coastlands and those who live in them.
Let the wilderness and its towns raise their voices, the villages where Kedar lives. Let the people of Sela sing for joy; let them shout from the tops of the mountains.
Let them give glory to the LORD and declare his praise in the coastlands.
The LORD goes out like a warrior; like a man of war he stirs up his zeal. He shouts, yes, he roars; he shows his might against his enemies.
For a long time I have kept silent; I have been still and held myself back. Now, like a woman in labor, I will cry out; I will gasp and pant.
I will lay waste mountains and hills and dry up all their plants. I will turn rivers into dry land and dry up the pools.

I will lead the blind by a way they do not know; I will guide them on paths they have not known. I will turn the darkness before them into light, and the rough places into level ground. These are the things I will do, and I will not abandon them.
They will be turned back and utterly put to shame, those who trust in idols, who say to cast images, "You are our gods."
Listen, you deaf! Look, you blind, so that you may see!
Who is blind but my servant, or deaf like my messenger whom I send? Who is blind like the one at peace with me, blind like the servant of the LORD?
You see many things, but you do not take note of them; his ears are open, but he does not hear.
The LORD was pleased, for the sake of his righteousness, to make his instruction great and glorious.
But this is a people plundered and looted, all of them trapped in holes and hidden away in prisons. They have become plunder with no one to rescue them, loot with no one to say, "Give it back!"
Who among you will listen to this, pay attention and hear it for the time to come?
Who handed Jacob over to be looted, and Israel to plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we have sinned? They would not walk in his ways, and they did not obey his instruction.
So he poured out on him his burning anger and the fury of battle. It set him on fire all around, but he did not understand; it burned him, but he did not take it to heart.
But now, this is what the LORD says, he who created you, Jacob, he who formed you, Israel: Do not be afraid, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name; you are mine.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they will not sweep over you. When you walk through fire, you will not be burned, and the flame will not consume you.
For I am the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. I give Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba in exchange for you.
Because you are precious in my eyes, and honored, and I love you, I give people in exchange for you, and nations in exchange for your life.
Do not be afraid, for I am with you. I will bring your offspring from the east and gather you from the west.
I will say to the north, "Give them up!" and to the south, "Do not hold them back! Bring my sons from far away and my daughters from the end of the earth,
everyone who is called by my name, whom I created for my glory, whom I formed and made."
Bring out the people who are blind, though they have eyes, who are deaf, though they have ears.

Let all the nations gather together, and let the peoples assemble. Who among them can declare this and tell us the former things? Let them bring their witnesses to prove they are right, so that others may hear and say, "It is true."

You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and my servant whom I have chosen, so that you may know and believe me and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, and after me there will be none.
I, I am the LORD, and apart from me there is no savior.
I declared and saved and proclaimed, and there was no foreign god among you. You are my witnesses, declares the LORD, and I am God.
From this day on I am he. No one can rescue from my hand. I act, and who can turn it back?
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I am sending to Babylon. I will bring them all down as fugitives, and the Chaldeans in the ships they shouted over.
I am the LORD, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.
This is what the LORD says, who makes a way through the sea, a path through the mighty waters,
who brings out chariot and horse, army and warrior together. They lie down, never to rise again; they are snuffed out, quenched like a wick.
Do not remember the former things, or consider the things of old.
Look, I am doing a new thing! Now it springs up; do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the wasteland.
The wild animals will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I give water in the wilderness, rivers in the wasteland, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
the people I formed for myself, so that they may declare my praise.
Yet you have not called on me, Jacob; you have grown weary of me, Israel.
You have not brought me sheep for your burnt offerings, or honored me with your sacrifices. I have not burdened you with grain offerings, or wearied you with demands for frankincense.
You have not bought me sweet cane with silver, or filled me with the fat of your sacrifices. Instead you have burdened me with your sins; you have wearied me with your wrongdoing.
I, I am he who wipes out your rebellious acts for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
Remind me; let us go to court together. State your case, so that you may be proved right.
Your first ancestor sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against me.
So I profaned the princes of the sanctuary; I handed Jacob over to destruction and Israel to scorn.
But now listen, Jacob my servant, Israel whom I have chosen.
This is what the LORD says, who made you, who formed you from the womb and will help you: Do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
For I will pour water on the thirsty land and streams on the dry ground. I will pour out my Spirit on your offspring and my blessing on your descendants.
They will spring up among the grass, like willows by streams of water.
One will say, "I belong to the LORD"; another will call himself by the name of Jacob; another will write on his hand, "The LORD's," and take the name of Israel as his title.
This is what the LORD says, the King of Israel and its Redeemer, the LORD of Armies: I am the first and I am the last; apart from me there is no God.
Who is like me? Let him proclaim it; let him declare it and set it out before me, since I established my ancient people. Let them declare what is coming, and what is going to happen.
Do not tremble or be afraid. Did I not tell you long ago and declare it? You are my witnesses. Is there any God apart from me? There is no other Rock; I know of none.
All who make idols are nothing, and the things they delight in do no good. Their witnesses neither see nor know, so they will be put to shame.
Who would fashion a god or cast an idol that can do no good?
Look, all who join themselves to it will be put to shame; the craftsmen are only human. Let them all gather and take their stand; they will be terrified and put to shame together.

The blacksmith takes a tool and works it over the coals. He shapes the idol with hammers and forges it with his strong arm. He also grows hungry and loses his strength; he drinks no water and grows faint.
The carpenter stretches out a line and marks it out with a stylus. He shapes it with chisels and marks it with compasses. He makes it in the form of a man, with human beauty, to live in a shrine.
He cuts down cedars for himself, or takes a cypress or an oak. He lets it grow strong among the trees of the forest. He plants a laurel, and the rain makes it grow.
Then it becomes fuel for people to burn. He takes some of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread. He also makes a god and worships it; he makes it an idol and bows down to it.
Half of it he burns in the fire. Over that half he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied. He also warms himself and says, "Ah! I am warm; I have seen the fire!"
And the rest of it he makes into a god, his idol. He bows down to it and worships; he prays to it and says, "Save me, for you are my god!"
They do not know or understand, for their eyes are plastered over so that they cannot see, and their minds so that they cannot understand.

No one stops to think; no one has the knowledge or understanding to say, "Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread on its coals; I roast meat and eat it. Shall I make the rest of it a detestable thing? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?"
He feeds on ashes. A deceived heart has led him astray, and he cannot save himself or say, "Is not this thing in my right hand a lie?"
Remember these things, Jacob, Israel, for you are my servant. I formed you; you are my servant. Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
I have wiped out your rebellious acts like a cloud, and your sins like mist. Return to me, for I have redeemed you.

Sing for joy, you heavens, for the LORD has done it! Shout aloud, you depths of the earth! Break into song, you mountains, you forest and every tree in it! For the LORD has redeemed Jacob, and he shows his glory in Israel.
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am the LORD, who made all things, who alone stretched out the heavens, who spread out the earth by myself,
who frustrates the signs of false prophets and makes fools of diviners, who turns back the wise and makes their knowledge foolish,

who carries out the word of his servant and fulfills the counsel of his messengers, who says of Jerusalem, "She will be inhabited," and of the towns of Judah, "They will be rebuilt, and I will raise up her ruins,"
who says to the deep, "Be dry! I will dry up your rivers,"
who says of Cyrus, "He is my shepherd, and he will carry out all that I desire," saying of Jerusalem, "She will be rebuilt," and of the temple, "Its foundations will be laid."

This is what the LORD says to his anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have grasped to subdue nations before him and to strip kings of their armor, to open doors before him, so that gates will not be shut:
I will go before you and level the mountains. I will break down doors of bronze and cut through bars of iron.
I will give you treasures hidden in darkness, riches stored in secret places, so that you may know that I am the LORD, the God of Israel, who calls you by name.
For the sake of Jacob my servant, and Israel my chosen, I call you by your name; I give you a title of honor, though you do not know me.
I am the LORD, and there is no other; apart from me there is no God. I will arm you, though you do not know me,
so that people may know, from the rising of the sun to its setting, that there is none besides me. I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I form light and create darkness; I make well-being and create disaster. I, the LORD, do all these things.

Rain down from above, you heavens, and let the clouds pour down righteousness. Let the earth open, so that salvation may bear fruit, and let righteousness spring up with it. I, the LORD, have created it.
Woe to the one who quarrels with his Maker, a pot among the pots of earth! Does the clay say to the one who forms it, "What are you making?" or "Your work has no handles"?
Woe to the one who says to a father, "What are you fathering?" or to a woman, "What are you giving birth to?"
This is what the LORD says, the Holy One of Israel, and its Maker: Would you question me about things to come, about my children, or give me orders about the work of my hands?
It was I who made the earth and created humankind on it. My own hands stretched out the heavens, and I commanded all their army.
I myself have stirred him up in righteousness, and I will make all his ways straight. He will rebuild my city and set my exiles free, not for a price or a bribe, says the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD says: The wealth of Egypt and the merchandise of Cush, and the Sabeans, men of great height, will come over to you and be yours. They will walk behind you, coming over in chains. They will bow down to you and plead with you: "Surely God is with you, and there is no other; there is no other god."
Truly you are a God who hides himself, the God of Israel, the Savior.
They will be put to shame and disgraced, all of them; the makers of idols go off together in disgrace.
But Israel is saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. You will not be put to shame or disgraced, to ages everlasting.

For this is what the LORD says, who created the heavens (he is God), who formed the earth and made it (he established it; he did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited): I am the LORD, and there is no other.
I did not speak in secret, somewhere in a land of darkness. I did not say to the offspring of Jacob, "Seek me in vain." I, the LORD, speak what is right; I declare what is true.
Gather together and come; draw near together, you survivors of the nations! They have no knowledge, those who carry around their wooden idols and keep praying to a god who cannot save.

Declare it and present your case; let them take counsel together. Who announced this long ago, who declared it from of old? Was it not I, the LORD? There is no other god apart from me, a righteous God and a Savior; there is none besides me.
Turn to me and be saved, all the ends of the earth! For I am God, and there is no other.
By myself I have sworn; a word has gone out from my mouth in righteousness, and it will not turn back: To me every knee will bow, every tongue will swear allegiance.
"Only in the LORD," it will be said of me, "are righteousness and strength." All who raged against him will come to him and be put to shame.
In the LORD all the offspring of Israel will be found righteous and will glory.
Bel bows down; Nebo stoops. Their idols are loaded on animals and cattle. The things you used to carry in procession are loaded as a burden on weary animals.
They stoop and bow down together; they cannot rescue the burden. They themselves go into captivity.
Listen to me, house of Jacob, all the remnant of the house of Israel, you whom I have carried since birth, whom I have borne since you were in the womb.
Even to your old age I am he, and to your gray hairs I will carry you. I have made you, and I will bear you; I will carry you and rescue you.
To whom will you compare me and make me equal? With whom will you liken me, that we may be alike?
Those who pour out gold from the bag and weigh out silver on the scale hire a goldsmith, and he makes it into a god; they bow down and worship it.

They lift it to their shoulders and carry it; they set it in its place, and it stands there; it cannot move from its place. Even when someone cries out to it, it does not answer; it cannot save anyone from his trouble.
Remember this and stand firm; take it to heart, you rebels.
Remember the former things of long ago, for I am God, and there is no other; I am God, and there is none like me.
I declare the end from the beginning, and from ancient times what has not yet been done. I say, "My plan will stand, and I will do all that I please."
I call a bird of prey from the east, the man of my plan from a far country. I have spoken, and I will bring it about; I have planned it, and I will do it.
Listen to me, you stubborn of heart, who are far from righteousness.
I am bringing my righteousness near; it is not far off, and my salvation will not be delayed. I will give salvation in Zion, and my glory to Israel.
Go down and sit in the dust, virgin daughter Babylon! Sit on the ground without a throne, daughter of the Chaldeans! For you will no longer be called tender and delicate.
Take millstones and grind flour. Remove your veil; strip off your skirt; bare your legs and wade through the rivers.
Your nakedness will be exposed; your shame will be seen. I will take vengeance, and I will spare no one.
Our Redeemer, whose name is the LORD of Armies, is the Holy One of Israel.
Sit in silence and go into darkness, daughter of the Chaldeans, for you will no longer be called the queen of kingdoms.
I was angry with my people; I profaned my inheritance and handed them over to you. You showed them no mercy; even on the old you made your yoke very heavy.
You said, "I will be queen forever." You did not take these things to heart or think about how it would end.
So now hear this, you lover of pleasure, who sit secure, who say in your heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me. I will never sit as a widow or know the loss of children."
Both of these will come on you in a moment, in a single day: loss of children and widowhood. They will come on you in full measure, in spite of your many sorceries and the great power of your spells.
You trusted in your wickedness; you said, "No one sees me." Your wisdom and your knowledge led you astray, and you said in your heart, "I am, and there is no one besides me."
But disaster will come on you, and you will not know how to charm it away. Ruin will fall on you that you cannot buy off; catastrophe will come on you suddenly, which you do not foresee.
Keep on, then, with your spells and your many sorceries, which you have labored at since your youth. Perhaps you will succeed; perhaps you will cause terror.
You are worn out by all your counsel. Let them stand up and save you, those who divide up the heavens, who gaze at the stars, who make known at each new moon what is coming on you.
Look, they are like straw; the fire burns them up. They cannot save themselves from the power of the flame. This is no coal to warm oneself by, no fire to sit in front of!
That is what they are to you, those you have labored with, those who have traded with you since your youth. Each one wanders off his own way; there is no one to save you.

Hear this, house of Jacob, you who are called by the name of Israel and have come from the waters of Judah, you who swear by the name of the LORD and invoke the God of Israel, but not in truth or righteousness.
For they call themselves after the holy city and lean on the God of Israel; the LORD of Armies is his name.
The former things I declared long ago; they went out from my mouth, and I announced them. Then suddenly I acted, and they came to pass.
Because I knew that you are stubborn, your neck an iron sinew and your forehead bronze,
I declared them to you long ago; before they came to pass I announced them to you, so that you could not say, "My idol did them; my carved image and my cast image commanded them."
You have heard it; now see it all. Will you not declare it? From now on I announce to you new things, hidden things that you have not known.
They are created now, not long ago; before today you have not heard of them, so that you could not say, "Look, I knew them."
You have never heard, you have never known; from of old your ear has not been opened. For I knew that you would surely act treacherously, and that you were called a rebel from birth.
For the sake of my name I hold back my anger; for the sake of my praise I restrain it for you, so as not to cut you off.
Look, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have chosen you in the furnace of affliction.
For my own sake, for my own sake, I do it; for how can my name be profaned? I will not give my glory to another.
Listen to me, Jacob, Israel whom I called: I am he; I am the first, and I am also the last.
My own hand laid the foundation of the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens. When I call to them, they stand up together.
Gather, all of you, and listen! Who among them declared these things? The one the LORD loves will carry out his purpose against Babylon, and his arm will be against the Chaldeans.
I, I have spoken; I have called him. I have brought him, and he will succeed in his way.
Come near to me and hear this: From the beginning I have not spoken in secret; from the time it came to be, I have been there. And now the Lord GOD has sent me, and his Spirit.
This is what the LORD says, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: I am the LORD your God, who teaches you what is for your good, who leads you in the way you should go.
If only you had paid attention to my commands! Then your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like the waves of the sea.
Your offspring would have been like the sand, and your descendants like its grains. Their name would never be cut off or destroyed from before me.
Go out from Babylon! Flee from the Chaldeans! With a shout of joy declare this, proclaim it, send it out to the end of the earth. Say, "The LORD has redeemed his servant Jacob!"
They did not thirst when he led them through the deserts. He made water flow for them from the rock; he split the rock, and the water gushed out.
There is no peace, says the LORD, for the wicked.
Listen to me, you coastlands; pay attention, you peoples far away! The LORD called me before I was born; from my mother's body he named me.
He made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand he hid me. He made me a polished arrow; in his quiver he concealed me.
He said to me, "You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will show my glory."
But I said, "I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing and emptiness. Yet surely my cause is with the LORD, and my reward with my God."

And now the LORD says, he who formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob back to him, so that Israel might be gathered to him (for I am honored in the eyes of the LORD, and my God has become my strength),

he says, "It is too small a thing for you to be my servant, to raise up the tribes of Jacob and bring back the survivors of Israel. I will also make you a light for the nations, so that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth."

This is what the LORD says, the Redeemer of Israel and his Holy One, to the one who is deeply despised, abhorred by the nation, the servant of rulers: Kings will see and rise up; princes will bow down, because of the LORD, who is faithful, the Holy One of Israel, who has chosen you.

This is what the LORD says: In a time of favor I have answered you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you. I will keep you and make you a covenant for the people, to restore the land and to give out again the desolate inheritances,
saying to the prisoners, "Come out," and to those in darkness, "Show yourselves." They will graze along the roads, and their pasture will be on all the bare heights.
They will not hunger or thirst; the scorching heat and the sun will not strike them. For he who has compassion on them will lead them and guide them to springs of water.
I will make all my mountains into a road, and my highways will be raised up.
Look, these will come from far away; look, these from the north and from the west, and these from the land of Sinim.
Shout for joy, you heavens! Rejoice, you earth! Break into song, you mountains! For the LORD has comforted his people and will have compassion on his afflicted ones.
But Zion said, "The LORD has abandoned me; the Lord has forgotten me."
Can a woman forget her nursing child, or have no compassion on the son of her womb? Even if these forget, I will not forget you.
Look, I have engraved you on the palms of my hands; your walls are always before me.
Your children hurry back; those who destroyed you and laid you waste go away from you.
Lift up your eyes and look around: they all gather and come to you. As surely as I live, declares the LORD, you will put them all on like jewelry; you will tie them on as a bride does.
For your ruins and your desolate places and your devastated land—now you will be too small for your inhabitants, and those who swallowed you up will be far away.
The children born in your time of bereavement will yet say in your hearing, "This place is too cramped for me; make room for me to live."
Then you will say in your heart, "Who bore me these? I was bereaved and barren, exiled and turned away. Who brought these up? Look, I was left all alone; where have these come from?"

This is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I will lift up my hand to the nations and raise my signal flag to the peoples. They will bring your sons in their arms, and your daughters will be carried on their shoulders.

Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers. They will bow down to you with their faces to the ground and lick the dust of your feet. Then you will know that I am the LORD; those who hope in me will not be put to shame.
Can plunder be taken from a warrior, or captives be rescued from a righteous one?

But this is what the LORD says: Even the captives of the warrior will be taken, and the plunder of the tyrant will be rescued. I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children.

I will make your oppressors eat their own flesh, and they will be drunk on their own blood as on new wine. Then all people will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.

This is what the LORD says: Where is your mother's certificate of divorce, with which I sent her away? Or to which of my creditors did I sell you? Look, it was for your sins that you were sold, and for your rebellious acts that your mother was sent away.

Why was there no one when I came? Why was there no one to answer when I called? Is my hand too short to redeem? Have I no power to rescue? Look, with a rebuke I dry up the sea; I turn rivers into a wilderness. Their fish rot for lack of water and die of thirst.
I clothe the heavens with darkness and make sackcloth their covering.
The Lord GOD has given me the tongue of one who is taught, so that I may know how to sustain the weary with a word. Morning by morning he wakens, he wakens my ear to listen like one who is taught.
The Lord GOD has opened my ear, and I did not rebel; I did not turn back.
I gave my back to those who struck me, and my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard. I did not hide my face from insults and spitting.
But the Lord GOD helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced. Therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I will not be put to shame.
He who proves me right is near. Who will bring charges against me? Let us stand up together. Who is my accuser? Let him come near me.
Look, the Lord GOD helps me; who will declare me guilty? Look, they will all wear out like a garment; the moth will eat them up.
Who among you fears the LORD and obeys the voice of his servant? Whoever walks in darkness and has no light, let him trust in the name of the LORD and rely on his God.

But look, all of you who kindle a fire, who arm yourselves with burning arrows, walk in the light of your fire and among the burning arrows you have lit! This is what you will receive from my hand: you will lie down in torment.
Listen to me, you who pursue righteousness, you who seek the LORD: Look to the rock from which you were cut and to the quarry from which you were dug.
Look to your ancestor Abraham and to Sarah who gave birth to you. For he was only one when I called him, and I blessed him and made him many.

For the LORD will comfort Zion; he will comfort all her ruins. He will make her wilderness like Eden, her desert like the garden of the LORD. Joy and gladness will be found in her, thanksgiving and the sound of singing.
Pay attention to me, my people; listen to me, my nation. For instruction will go out from me, and I will set my justice as a light for the peoples.
My righteousness draws near; my salvation has gone out, and my arms will judge the peoples. The coastlands will hope in me and wait for my arm.

Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look at the earth beneath. For the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment, and its inhabitants will die like gnats. But my salvation will last forever, and my righteousness will never fail.
Listen to me, you who know what is right, you people who have my instruction in your hearts. Do not fear the reproach of mere mortals, or be dismayed by their insults.
For the moth will eat them like a garment, and the worm will eat them like wool. But my righteousness will last forever, and my salvation through all generations.
Awake, awake, put on strength, arm of the LORD! Awake, as in days of old, in generations long ago. Was it not you who cut Rahab to pieces, who pierced the dragon?
Was it not you who dried up the sea, the waters of the great deep, who made the depths of the sea a road for the redeemed to cross?
Those whom the LORD has ransomed will return and come to Zion with singing. Everlasting joy will be on their heads. Gladness and joy will overtake them, and sorrow and sighing will flee away.
I, I am he who comforts you. Who are you that you are afraid of mortals who die, of human beings who are made like grass?

You have forgotten the LORD your Maker, who stretched out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. You live in constant fear all day long because of the fury of the oppressor, as he prepares to destroy. But where is the fury of the oppressor?
The one bowed down in chains will soon be set free. He will not die and go down to the Pit, and he will not lack bread.
For I am the LORD your God, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar. The LORD of Armies is his name.
I have put my words in your mouth and covered you with the shadow of my hand, to plant the heavens and lay the foundations of the earth, and to say to Zion, "You are my people."
Wake up, wake up! Stand up, Jerusalem, you who have drunk from the hand of the LORD the cup of his fury, you who have drained to the dregs the bowl, the cup that makes people stagger.
There is no one to guide her among all the children she bore; there is no one to take her by the hand among all the children she brought up.
These two things have happened to you (who will grieve with you?): ruin and destruction, famine and sword. How can I comfort you?
Your children have fainted; they lie at the head of every street like an antelope caught in a net. They are full of the fury of the LORD, the rebuke of your God.
Therefore hear this, you afflicted one, drunk, but not with wine.

This is what your Lord, the LORD, says, your God, who defends his people: Look, I have taken from your hand the cup that makes people stagger, the bowl, the cup of my fury. You will never drink it again.
I will put it into the hands of your tormentors, who said to you, "Bow down, so that we may walk over you." And you made your back like the ground, like a street for them to walk over.
Awake, awake, put on your strength, Zion! Put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city! For the uncircumcised and the unclean will never enter you again.
Shake yourself free from the dust; rise up and take your seat, Jerusalem! Loose the bonds from your neck, captive Daughter Zion!
For this is what the LORD says: You were sold for nothing, and you will be redeemed without silver.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: At first my people went down to Egypt to live there as foreigners; then Assyria oppressed them for nothing.
And now what do I have here? declares the LORD. For my people have been taken away for nothing. Their rulers wail, declares the LORD, and all day long my name is continually despised.
Therefore my people will know my name; therefore on that day they will know that I am he who speaks: Here I am.
How beautiful on the mountains are the feet of the one who brings good news, who proclaims peace, who brings good news of good things, who proclaims salvation, who says to Zion, "Your God reigns!"
Listen! Your watchmen raise their voices; together they shout for joy. For with their own eyes they will see the LORD return to Zion.
Break into singing together, you ruins of Jerusalem! For the LORD has comforted his people; he has redeemed Jerusalem.
The LORD has bared his holy arm before the eyes of all the nations, and all the ends of the earth will see the salvation of our God.
Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch nothing unclean. Go out from the middle of her; purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the LORD.
But you will not go out in haste or leave in flight. For the LORD will go before you, and the God of Israel will be your rear guard.
Look, my servant will act wisely; he will be raised and lifted up and greatly exalted.
Just as many were appalled at you, so disfigured was his appearance, beyond that of any man, and his form beyond that of human beings,
so he will sprinkle many nations. Kings will shut their mouths because of him. For what they were not told, they will see, and what they have not heard, they will understand.
Who has believed what we have heard? And to whom has the arm of the LORD been revealed?
He grew up before him like a young plant, like a root out of dry ground. He had no form or majesty that we should look at him, no appearance that we should desire him.
He was despised and rejected by others, a man of pains, who knew what sickness was. Like one from whom people hide their faces, he was despised, and we held him in no regard.
Surely he has carried our sicknesses and borne our pains. Yet we thought of him as stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
But he was pierced for our rebellious acts; he was crushed for our wrongdoings. The punishment that brought us peace was on him, and by his wounds we are healed.
We all, like sheep, have gone astray; we have each turned to his own way. And the LORD has laid on him the guilt of us all.

He was oppressed, and he let himself be afflicted, yet he did not open his mouth. Like a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and like a sheep that is silent before its shearers, he did not open his mouth.
By oppression and judgment he was taken away. And who of his generation considered that he was cut off from the land of the living, struck down for the rebellion of my people?
They made his grave with the wicked, and with a rich man in his death, although he had done no violence, and there was no deceit in his mouth.
Yet it was the LORD's will to crush him; he made him sick. When you make his life a guilt offering, he will see offspring and prolong his days, and the will of the LORD will prosper in his hand.
Out of the anguish of his soul he will see and be satisfied. By his knowledge my righteous servant will make many righteous, and he will bear their wrongdoings.

Therefore I will give him a portion among the many, and he will divide the plunder with the strong, because he poured out his life to death and was counted among the rebels. Yet he bore the sin of many and made intercession for the rebels.

Sing, barren woman, you who have not given birth! Break into song and shout, you who have not been in labor! For the children of the desolate woman will be more than the children of the married woman, says the LORD.
Enlarge the place of your tent; let the curtains of your dwellings be stretched out; do not hold back. Lengthen your ropes and strengthen your stakes.
For you will spread out to the right and to the left. Your offspring will possess the nations and will settle the desolate cities.

Do not be afraid, for you will not be put to shame; do not be disgraced, for you will not be humiliated. You will forget the shame of your youth, and you will no longer remember the disgrace of your widowhood.
For your husband is your Maker; the LORD of Armies is his name. Your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel; he is called the God of all the earth.
For the LORD has called you back like a wife abandoned and grieved in spirit, like a wife married in her youth who has been rejected, says your God.
For a brief moment I abandoned you, but with great compassion I will gather you.
In a flood of anger I hid my face from you for a moment, but with everlasting faithful love I will have compassion on you, says the LORD, your Redeemer.
For this is like the waters of Noah to me: as I swore that the waters of Noah would never again pass over the earth, so I have sworn that I will not be angry with you or rebuke you.
For the mountains may depart and the hills be shaken, but my faithful love will not depart from you, and my covenant of peace will not be shaken, says the LORD, who has compassion on you.
Afflicted one, storm-tossed and not comforted, look, I will set your stones in black mortar and lay your foundations with sapphires.
I will make your battlements of rubies, your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
All your children will be taught by the LORD, and great will be the peace of your children.
You will be established in righteousness. You will be far from oppression, for you will have nothing to fear, and from terror, for it will not come near you.
If anyone stirs up trouble, it will not be from me; whoever stirs up trouble against you will fall because of you.
Look, I have created the smith who blows on the coals and produces a weapon fit for its work. I have also created the destroyer to wreak havoc.

No weapon forged against you will succeed, and you will refute every tongue that rises against you in judgment. This is the heritage of the servants of the LORD, and their vindication comes from me, declares the LORD.
Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters! And you who have no money, come, buy grain and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost.
Why do you spend money on what is not bread, and your earnings on what does not satisfy? Listen carefully to me, and eat what is good, and you will delight in rich food.
Turn your ear and come to me; listen, so that you may live. I will make an everlasting covenant with you, my faithful love promised to David.
Look, I made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples.
Look, you will call a nation you do not know, and a nation that does not know you will run to you, because of the LORD your God, the Holy One of Israel, for he has glorified you.
Seek the LORD while he may be found; call on him while he is near.
Let the wicked abandon his way, and the evildoer his thoughts. Let him turn back to the LORD, and he will have compassion on him, to our God, for he will freely forgive.
For my thoughts are not your thoughts, and your ways are not my ways, declares the LORD.
For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.
For as the rain and the snow come down from the heavens and do not return there without watering the earth and making it bear and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
so will my word be that goes out from my mouth: it will not return to me empty, without accomplishing what I desire and succeeding in the purpose for which I sent it.
For you will go out with joy and be led out in peace. The mountains and the hills will break into singing before you, and all the trees of the field will clap their hands.
Instead of the thornbush the juniper will grow, and instead of the brier the myrtle will grow. This will make a name for the LORD, an everlasting sign that will not be cut off.
This is what the LORD says: Keep justice and do what is right, for my salvation is about to come, and my righteousness to be revealed.
Blessed is the person who does this, the human being who holds fast to it, who keeps the Sabbath without profaning it and keeps his hand from doing any evil.
Let no foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD say, "The LORD will surely separate me from his people." And let no eunuch say, "Look, I am only a dry tree."
For this is what the LORD says: To the eunuchs who keep my Sabbaths, who choose what pleases me and hold fast to my covenant,
I will give within my house and within my walls a memorial and a name better than sons and daughters. I will give them an everlasting name that will not be cut off.
And the foreigners who join themselves to the LORD to serve him, to love the name of the LORD, and to be his servants, all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it and hold fast to my covenant,

I will bring to my holy mountain and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar, for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
The Lord GOD declares, he who gathers the outcasts of Israel: I will gather still others to them besides those already gathered.
All you wild animals of the field, come and devour, all you wild animals in the forest!
Its watchmen are blind; none of them knows anything. They are all mute dogs that cannot bark. They lie around dreaming; they love to sleep.

The dogs have a mighty appetite; they never know when they have had enough. And they are shepherds who have no understanding. They have all turned to their own way, each to his own gain, every one of them.
"Come," they say, "let me get wine, and let us fill ourselves with beer! Tomorrow will be like today, only far better!"
The righteous one perishes, and no one takes it to heart. The faithful are taken away, and no one understands that the righteous one is taken away from the evil to come.
He enters into peace; they rest on their beds, all who walk uprightly.
But you, come here, you children of a sorceress, offspring of an adulterer and a prostitute!
Whom are you mocking? At whom do you open your mouth wide and stick out your tongue? Are you not children of rebellion, offspring of deceit?
You inflame yourselves among the oaks, under every green tree; you slaughter children in the ravines, under the clefts of the rocks.
Among the smooth stones of the ravine is your portion; they, they are your lot. To them you have poured out drink offerings and brought up grain offerings. Should I relent because of these things?
On a high and lofty mountain you have made your bed; there too you went up to offer sacrifice.

Behind the door and the doorpost you have set up your sign. For, deserting me, you uncovered your bed, climbed up into it and opened it wide. You made a bargain for yourself with them; you loved their bed; you gazed on their nakedness.
You went to the king with oil and gave him many perfumes. You sent your envoys far away; you sent them down even to Sheol.
You were wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, "It is hopeless." You found new strength, so you did not grow faint.
Whom did you dread and fear, that you lied, and did not remember me or take it to heart? Is it not because I have kept silent, and for a long time, that you do not fear me?
I will expose your righteousness and your deeds, and they will not help you.

When you cry out, let your collection of idols save you! The wind will carry them all off; a breath will take them away. But whoever takes refuge in me will inherit the land and possess my holy mountain.
And it will be said, "Build it up, build it up, prepare the road! Remove every obstacle from the way of my people."

For this is what the High and Lofty One says, who lives forever, whose name is Holy: I live in a high and holy place, and also with the one who is crushed and humble in spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble and to revive the heart of the crushed.
For I will not accuse forever, nor will I always be angry. For then the spirit would grow faint before me, the breath of life that I have made.
Because of the guilt of his greed I was angry, and I struck him; I hid my face and was angry. But he went on turning away, in the way of his own heart.
I have seen his ways, but I will heal him. I will lead him and repay him with comfort, him and those who mourn for him,
