creating praise on their lips: Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says the LORD, and I will heal him.
But the wicked are like the tossing sea, which cannot be still; its waters toss up mud and mire.
There is no peace, says my God, for the wicked.
Shout aloud; do not hold back! Raise your voice like a ram's horn! Declare to my people their rebellion, and to the house of Jacob their sins.

Yet day after day they seek me and delight to know my ways, as if they were a nation that did what is right and had not abandoned the justice of its God. They ask me for righteous judgments; they delight in drawing near to God.
"Why have we fasted," they say, "and you do not see? Why have we denied ourselves, and you do not notice?" Look, on the day of your fast you pursue your own business and drive all your workers hard.
Look, you fast only to quarrel and fight and to strike with a wicked fist. You cannot fast as you do today and make your voice heard on high.

Is this the kind of fast I choose, a day for a person to deny himself? Is it to bow one's head like a reed and to lie on sackcloth and ashes? Is this what you call a fast, a day acceptable to the LORD?
Is not this the fast that I choose: to loosen the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and to break every yoke?
Is it not to share your bread with the hungry and to bring the homeless poor into your house, to cover the naked when you see them, and not to turn away from your own flesh and blood?
Then your light will break out like the dawn, and your healing will spring up quickly. Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.
Then you will call, and the LORD will answer; you will cry for help, and he will say, "Here I am." If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing finger and wicked speech,
if you pour yourself out for the hungry and satisfy the needs of the afflicted, then your light will rise in the darkness, and your gloom will be like noon.
The LORD will guide you always and satisfy your needs in parched places and strengthen your bones. You will be like a watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.
Your people will rebuild the ancient ruins; you will raise up the foundations of many generations. You will be called the Repairer of the Breach, the Restorer of Streets to Live In.

If you keep your feet from trampling the Sabbath, from doing as you please on my holy day; if you call the Sabbath a delight and the holy day of the LORD honored; if you honor it by not going your own ways, not pursuing your own business or speaking idle words,
then you will find your delight in the LORD, and I will make you ride on the heights of the earth and feed you with the inheritance of your ancestor Jacob. For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.
Look, the hand of the LORD is not too short to save, nor his ear too dull to hear.
But your wrongdoings have separated you from your God, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he does not hear.
For your hands are defiled with blood and your fingers with guilt. Your lips have spoken lies; your tongue mutters wickedness.
No one brings a case justly; no one goes to law honestly. They trust in empty words and speak lies; they conceive trouble and give birth to evil.
They hatch the eggs of vipers and weave spiders' webs. Whoever eats their eggs dies, and when one is crushed, a snake hatches out.
Their webs will not become clothing; they cannot cover themselves with what they make. Their works are works of evil, and acts of violence are in their hands.
Their feet run to evil, and they hurry to shed innocent blood. Their thoughts are thoughts of evil; ruin and destruction are on their highways.
They do not know the way of peace, and there is no justice in their tracks. They have made their paths crooked; no one who walks on them knows peace.
That is why justice is far from us, and righteousness does not reach us. We hope for light, but look, there is darkness; for brightness, but we walk in gloom.
We grope along the wall like the blind; we grope like those who have no eyes. We stumble at noon as in the twilight; among the strong we are like the dead.
We all growl like bears; we moan and moan like doves. We hope for justice, but there is none; for salvation, but it is far from us.
For our rebellious acts are many before you, and our sins testify against us. Our rebellious acts are with us, and we know our wrongdoings:
rebelling and denying the LORD, turning away from following our God, speaking oppression and revolt, conceiving and uttering lies from the heart.
So justice is driven back, and righteousness stands far away. Truth has stumbled in the public square, and honesty cannot enter.
Truth is missing, and whoever turns away from evil makes himself a prey. The LORD saw it, and it was evil in his eyes that there was no justice.
He saw that there was no one; he was appalled that there was no one to intervene. So his own arm brought him salvation, and his righteousness upheld him.
He put on righteousness as a breastplate, and the helmet of salvation on his head. He put on garments of vengeance for clothing and wrapped himself in zeal as in a cloak.
According to what they have done, so he will repay: fury to his adversaries, retribution to his enemies; to the coastlands he will repay retribution.
So from the west they will fear the name of the LORD, and from the rising of the sun his glory. For he will come like a rushing river, driven by the wind of the LORD.
A Redeemer will come to Zion, to those in Jacob who turn from rebellion, declares the LORD.

As for me, this is my covenant with them, says the LORD: My Spirit, who is on you, and my words that I have put in your mouth will not depart from your mouth, or from the mouths of your children, or from the mouths of your children's children, says the LORD, from now on and forever.
Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen on you.
For look, darkness covers the earth, and thick darkness the peoples. But the LORD rises on you, and his glory appears over you.
Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
Lift up your eyes and look around: they all gather and come to you. Your sons will come from far away, and your daughters will be carried on the hip.
Then you will see and be radiant; your heart will throb and swell with joy, for the abundance of the sea will be turned to you, and the wealth of the nations will come to you.
A multitude of camels will cover you, young camels of Midian and Ephah. All those from Sheba will come, bringing gold and frankincense and proclaiming the praises of the LORD.
All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered to you; the rams of Nebaioth will serve you. They will go up as acceptable offerings on my altar, and I will make my glorious house more glorious still.
Who are these that fly like a cloud, like doves to their windows?

Surely the coastlands wait for me, with the ships of Tarshish in the lead, to bring your sons from far away, their silver and gold with them, for the name of the LORD your God, for the Holy One of Israel, because he has glorified you.
Foreigners will rebuild your walls, and their kings will serve you. For in my anger I struck you, but in my favor I have had compassion on you.
Your gates will always stand open; day and night they will not be shut, so that people may bring you the wealth of the nations, with their kings led in procession.
For the nation or kingdom that will not serve you will perish; those nations will be utterly ruined.
The glory of Lebanon will come to you, the juniper, the plane tree and the pine together, to beautify the place of my sanctuary, and I will make the place of my feet glorious.

The sons of those who oppressed you will come bowing low to you, and all who despised you will bow down at the soles of your feet. They will call you the City of the LORD, the Zion of the Holy One of Israel.
Instead of being abandoned and hated, with no one passing through, I will make you an everlasting pride, a joy from generation to generation.
You will drink the milk of nations and nurse at the breasts of kings. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am your Savior, your Redeemer, the Mighty One of Jacob.
Instead of bronze I will bring gold, and instead of iron I will bring silver; instead of wood, bronze, and instead of stones, iron. I will make peace your overseer and righteousness your ruler.
Violence will no longer be heard in your land, nor ruin or destruction within your borders. You will call your walls Salvation and your gates Praise.
The sun will no longer be your light by day, nor will the brightness of the moon shine on you. But the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your God will be your glory.
Your sun will never set again, and your moon will not wane, for the LORD will be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning will be over.
Your people will all be righteous; they will possess the land forever. They are the shoot I planted, the work of my hands, so that I may be glorified.
The least of them will become a thousand, and the smallest a mighty nation. I am the LORD; when the time comes, I will do this quickly.

The Spirit of the Lord GOD is on me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim freedom for the captives and release for the prisoners,
to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor and the day of vengeance of our God, to comfort all who mourn,

to provide for those who mourn in Zion: to give them a garland instead of ashes, the oil of gladness instead of mourning, a garment of praise instead of a fainting spirit. They will be called oaks of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, so that he may be glorified.
They will rebuild the ancient ruins and raise up the places long desolate. They will renew the ruined cities, the places desolate for generations.
Strangers will stand and tend your flocks, and foreigners will be your plowmen and vinedressers.
But you will be called priests of the LORD; you will be named ministers of our God. You will eat the wealth of the nations, and you will glory in their riches.

Instead of your shame you will have a double portion, and instead of disgrace they will rejoice in their lot. Therefore in their land they will possess a double portion; everlasting joy will be theirs.
For I, the LORD, love justice; I hate robbery and wrongdoing. I will faithfully give them their reward and make an everlasting covenant with them.
Their offspring will be known among the nations, and their descendants among the peoples. All who see them will recognize that they are offspring the LORD has blessed.

I will greatly rejoice in the LORD; my soul will exult in my God. For he has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom puts on a garland like a priest, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
For as the earth brings out its sprouts, and as a garden makes what is sown in it spring up, so the Lord GOD will make righteousness and praise spring up before all the nations.
For the sake of Zion I will not keep silent, and for the sake of Jerusalem I will not rest, until her righteousness goes out like brightness, and her salvation like a burning torch.
The nations will see your righteousness, and all kings your glory. You will be called by a new name that the mouth of the LORD will give you.
You will be a crown of beauty in the hand of the LORD, a royal diadem in the palm of your God.

You will no longer be called Abandoned, and your land will no longer be called Desolate. But you will be called My Delight Is in Her, and your land Married; for the LORD delights in you, and your land will be married.
For as a young man marries a young woman, so your sons will marry you; and as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you.
On your walls, Jerusalem, I have posted watchmen; all day and all night they will never be silent. You who call on the LORD to remember, take no rest for yourselves,
and give him no rest until he establishes Jerusalem and makes it the praise of the earth.
The LORD has sworn by his right hand and by his mighty arm: I will never again give your grain as food to your enemies, and foreigners will never again drink the new wine for which you have labored.
But those who harvest it will eat it and praise the LORD, and those who gather it will drink it in the courts of my sanctuary.
Go through, go through the gates! Prepare the way for the people! Build up, build up the highway! Clear it of stones! Raise a signal flag over the peoples!
Look, the LORD has proclaimed to the end of the earth: Say to Daughter Zion, "Look, your salvation is coming! Look, his reward is with him, and his recompense goes before him."
They will be called the Holy People, the Redeemed of the LORD; and you will be called Sought After, the City Not Abandoned.

"Who is this coming from Edom, in crimson garments from Bozrah, this one splendid in his clothing, striding forward in the greatness of his strength?" "It is I, speaking in righteousness, mighty to save."
"Why is your clothing red, and your garments like those of one who treads in the winepress?"
"I have trodden the winepress alone; from the peoples no one was with me. I trod them in my anger and trampled them in my fury. Their lifeblood spattered my garments, and I stained all my clothing.
For the day of vengeance was in my heart, and the year of my redemption had come.
I looked, but there was no one to help; I was appalled that there was no one to support me. So my own arm brought me salvation, and my fury upheld me.
I trampled the peoples in my anger and made them drunk in my fury, and I poured out their lifeblood on the ground."

I will tell of the faithful love of the LORD, the praises of the LORD, for all that the LORD has done for us, the great goodness to the house of Israel that he has shown them in his compassion and in his abundant faithful love.
He said, "Surely they are my people, children who will not be false." So he became their Savior.
In all their distress he too was distressed, and the angel of his presence saved them. In his love and in his pity he redeemed them; he lifted them up and carried them all the days of old.
But they rebelled and grieved his holy Spirit. So he turned and became their enemy; he himself fought against them.
Then his people remembered the days of old, the days of Moses: Where is he who brought them up out of the sea, with the shepherds of his flock? Where is he who put his holy Spirit among them,
who sent his glorious arm to go at the right hand of Moses, who split the waters before them to make for himself an everlasting name,
who led them through the depths? Like a horse in the wilderness, they did not stumble.
Like cattle that go down into the valley, the Spirit of the LORD gave them rest. So you led your people, to make for yourself a glorious name.
Look down from heaven and see, from your holy and glorious dwelling. Where are your zeal and your mighty deeds? The yearning of your heart and your compassion are held back from me.
For you are our Father, though Abraham does not know us and Israel does not acknowledge us. You, LORD, are our Father; "Our Redeemer from of old" is your name.
Why, LORD, do you make us wander from your ways and harden our hearts so that we do not fear you? Return for the sake of your servants, the tribes of your inheritance.
Your holy people possessed it for only a little while; our adversaries have trampled down your sanctuary.

We have become like those you have never ruled, like those who were never called by your name. If only you would tear open the heavens and come down, so that the mountains would quake at your presence!
As when fire kindles brushwood, and fire makes water boil, make your name known to your adversaries, so that the nations may tremble at your presence!
When you did awesome things that we did not expect, you came down; the mountains quaked at your presence.
From ages past no one has heard, no ear has perceived, no eye has seen any God besides you, who acts for those who wait for him.
You meet those who gladly do what is right, who remember you in your ways. Look, you were angry, and we sinned. We have been in them a long time; can we be saved?
We have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like a filthy cloth. We all wither like a leaf, and our wrongdoings carry us away like the wind.
No one calls on your name or rouses himself to take hold of you. For you have hidden your face from us and made us melt away in the grip of our wrongdoings.
But now, LORD, you are our Father. We are the clay, and you are our potter; we are all the work of your hand.
Do not be so very angry, LORD, and do not remember our wrongdoing forever. Look, please, we are all your people.
Your holy cities have become a wilderness; Zion has become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation.
Our holy and beautiful house, where our ancestors praised you, has been burned with fire, and all that we treasured has become ruins.
After all this, LORD, will you hold back? Will you keep silent and afflict us so very much?
I let myself be sought by those who did not ask for me; I let myself be found by those who did not seek me. I said, "Here I am, here I am," to a nation that was not called by my name.
All day long I have held out my hands to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, following their own thoughts,
a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens and burning incense on bricks,
who sit among the graves and spend the night in secret places, who eat the flesh of pigs, with broth of spoiled meat in their pots,
who say, "Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am too holy for you!" These are smoke in my nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.
Look, it is written before me: I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will repay into their laps

both your wrongdoings and the wrongdoings of your ancestors together, says the LORD, because they burned incense on the mountains and insulted me on the hills. I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.

This is what the LORD says: As when new wine is found in a cluster of grapes and someone says, "Do not destroy it, for there is a blessing in it," so I will do for the sake of my servants, so as not to destroy them all.
I will bring out offspring from Jacob, and from Judah heirs to my mountains. My chosen ones will possess them, and my servants will live there.
Sharon will become a pasture for flocks, and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, for my people who have sought me.
But you who abandon the LORD, who forget my holy mountain, who set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny,

I will destine you for the sword, and all of you will bow down to be slaughtered, because I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen. You did what was evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me.

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, my servants will eat, but you will go hungry; look, my servants will drink, but you will go thirsty; look, my servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.
Look, my servants will sing for joy with gladness of heart, but you will cry out with pain of heart and wail with a broken spirit.
You will leave your name to my chosen ones as a curse, and the Lord GOD will put you to death, but he will call his servants by another name.

So whoever invokes a blessing in the land will be blessed by the God of truth, and whoever swears an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth. For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from my eyes.
For look, I am creating new heavens and a new earth. The former things will not be remembered or come to mind.
But be glad and rejoice forever in what I am creating, for look, I am creating Jerusalem to be a delight and its people a joy.
I will rejoice over Jerusalem and delight in my people; the sound of weeping and the sound of crying will no longer be heard in it.

There will no longer be in it an infant who lives only a few days, or an old man who does not live out his days. For one who dies at a hundred years will be thought a youth, and one who falls short of a hundred years will be thought accursed.
They will build houses and live in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.
They will not build for others to live in, or plant for others to eat. For like the days of a tree will be the days of my people, and my chosen ones will long enjoy the work of their hands.
They will not labor in vain or bear children for sudden disaster, for they will be offspring blessed by the LORD, and their descendants with them.
Before they call, I will answer; while they are still speaking, I will hear.
The wolf and the lamb will graze together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox, and dust will be the serpent's food. They will not harm or destroy on all my holy mountain, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. Where is the house you would build for me? Where is the place of my rest?
My hand made all these things, and so they came to be, declares the LORD. But this is the one I will look to: the one who is humble and contrite in spirit, and who trembles at my word.

Whoever slaughters an ox is like one who kills a person; whoever sacrifices a lamb, like one who breaks a dog's neck; whoever presents a grain offering, like one who offers pig's blood; whoever burns incense as a memorial, like one who blesses an idol. They have chosen their own ways, and they delight in their detestable things.

So I too will choose harsh treatment for them and bring on them what they dread. For I called, and no one answered; I spoke, and they did not listen. They did what was evil in my eyes and chose what does not please me.

Hear the word of the LORD, you who tremble at his word: Your brothers who hate you and cast you out for my name's sake have said, "Let the LORD show his glory, so that we may see your joy!" But they will be put to shame.
Listen! An uproar from the city! A sound from the temple! It is the sound of the LORD repaying his enemies what they deserve.
Before she went into labor, she gave birth; before her pains came on her, she delivered a son.
Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Can a land be born in one day, or a nation be brought forth in a moment? Yet as soon as Zion went into labor, she gave birth to her children.
Shall I bring to the moment of birth and not cause delivery? says the LORD. Shall I, who cause delivery, close the womb? says your God.
Rejoice with Jerusalem and be glad for her, all you who love her! Rejoice greatly with her, all you who mourn over her,
so that you may nurse and be satisfied at her comforting breasts, so that you may drink deeply and delight in her overflowing abundance.

For this is what the LORD says: Look, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the wealth of the nations like an overflowing stream. You will nurse and be carried on her hip and bounced on her knees.
As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you will be comforted in Jerusalem.
You will see, and your heart will rejoice; your bones will flourish like grass. The hand of the LORD will be made known to his servants, but his fury to his enemies.
For look, the LORD will come in fire, and his chariots like the whirlwind, to repay his anger with fury and his rebuke with flames of fire.
For with fire the LORD will execute judgment, and with his sword, on all people, and those slain by the LORD will be many.
Those who consecrate and purify themselves to go into the gardens, following one in the middle, who eat the flesh of pigs and vile things and mice, will come to an end together, declares the LORD.
As for me, I know their deeds and their thoughts, and the time is coming to gather all nations and languages. They will come and see my glory.

I will set a sign among them, and I will send survivors from them to the nations: to Tarshish, Pul and Lud (who draw the bow), to Tubal and Javan, to the distant coastlands that have not heard of my fame or seen my glory. They will declare my glory among the nations.

They will bring all your brothers from all the nations as an offering to the LORD, on horses, in chariots and wagons, on mules and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says the LORD, just as the Israelites bring a grain offering in a clean vessel to the house of the LORD.
And I will also take some of them to be priests and Levites, says the LORD.
For as the new heavens and the new earth that I am making will endure before me, declares the LORD, so your offspring and your name will endure.
From new moon to new moon, and from Sabbath to Sabbath, all people will come to bow down before me, says the LORD.
They will go out and look on the corpses of the people who rebelled against me. For their worm will not die, and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a horror to all people.
The words of Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the LORD came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
It came also in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, until the end of the eleventh year of Zedekiah son of Josiah king of Judah, until Jerusalem went into exile in the fifth month.
The word of the LORD came to me:
"Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I set you apart. I appointed you a prophet to the nations."
I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I don't know how to speak, for I am only a boy."
But the LORD said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a boy.' You will go to everyone I send you to, and you will say whatever I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to rescue you, declares the LORD."
Then the LORD stretched out his hand and touched my mouth, and the LORD said to me, "Look, I have put my words in your mouth.
See, today I appoint you over nations and over kingdoms, to uproot and to tear down, to destroy and to overthrow, to build and to plant."
The word of the LORD came to me: "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "I see a branch of an almond tree."
The LORD said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my word to carry it out."
The word of the LORD came to me a second time: "What do you see?" I said, "I see a boiling pot, and it is tipped away from the north."
The LORD said to me, "From the north disaster will be let loose on all who live in the land.

For I am about to summon all the clans of the kingdoms of the north, declares the LORD. They will come, and each of them will set up his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, against all its walls around it, and against all the cities of Judah.
I will pronounce my judgments on my people for all their evil, because they have abandoned me. They have burned incense to other gods and bowed down to the works of their own hands.
But you, get ready for action. Stand up and tell them everything I command you. Do not be shattered with fear before them, or I will shatter you before them.
And I, look, today I have made you a fortified city, an iron pillar and bronze walls against the whole land: against the kings of Judah, its officials, its priests and the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you, declares the LORD, to rescue you."
The word of the LORD came to me:
Go and proclaim in the hearing of Jerusalem: This is what the LORD says: I remember the faithful love of your youth, your love as a bride, how you followed me in the wilderness, in a land not sown.
Israel was holy to the LORD, the firstfruits of his harvest. All who ate of it were held guilty; disaster came on them, declares the LORD.
Hear the word of the LORD, house of Jacob, and all the clans of the house of Israel.
This is what the LORD says: What wrong did your ancestors find in me, that they went far from me? They followed what is worthless and became worthless themselves.

They did not say, "Where is the LORD, who brought us up from the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a land of deserts and pits, through a land of drought and deep darkness, a land that no one travels through, where no human being lives?"
I brought you into a fruitful land, to eat its fruit and its good things. But you came in and defiled my land, and made my inheritance detestable.
The priests did not say, "Where is the LORD?" Those who handle the law did not know me. The shepherds rebelled against me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed things that do not profit.
Therefore I will still bring charges against you, declares the LORD, and against your children's children I will bring charges.
Cross over to the coasts of Kittim and look; send to Kedar and consider carefully; see if there has ever been anything like this.
Has a nation ever exchanged its gods, even though they are not gods? But my people have exchanged their Glory for what does not profit.
Be appalled at this, you heavens; shudder and be utterly desolate, declares the LORD.
For my people have done two evils: they have abandoned me, the spring of living water, to dig out cisterns for themselves, cracked cisterns that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Was he born a slave in the household? Then why has he become plunder?
Young lions have roared over him; they have raised their voices. They have made his land a desolation; his cities are burned, with no one living in them.
The people of Memphis and Tahpanhes have also shaved your head.
Have you not brought this on yourself by abandoning the LORD your God, when he was leading you on the way?
So now, what good is it for you to take the road to Egypt, to drink the waters of the Shihor? What good is it for you to take the road to Assyria, to drink the waters of the River?

Your own evil will discipline you, and your faithlessness will rebuke you. Know and see how evil and bitter it is for you to abandon the LORD your God, and to have no fear of me, declares the Lord GOD of Armies.
For long ago I broke your yoke and tore off your bonds, and you said, "I will not transgress." Yet on every high hill and under every leafy tree you lay down as a prostitute.
I had planted you as a choice vine, wholly of true seed. How then have you turned against me into the wild shoots of a foreign vine?
Even if you wash yourself with lye and use much soap, the stain of your guilt is still before me, declares the Lord GOD.
How can you say, "I am not defiled; I have not gone after the Baals"? Look at your way in the valley; know what you have done, you swift young camel running here and there,
a wild donkey used to the wilderness, sniffing the wind in her desire! In her season of heat, who can turn her back? None who look for her need to tire themselves; in her month they will find her.
Keep your feet from going bare and your throat from thirst! But you said, "It's hopeless! No! For I love strangers, and I will go after them."
As a thief is put to shame when he is caught, so the house of Israel is put to shame: they, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets.

They say to a tree, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave birth to us." For they have turned their backs to me, not their faces. Yet in the time of their trouble they say, "Get up and save us!"
But where are your gods that you made for yourself? Let them get up, if they can save you in the time of your trouble! For you have as many gods as you have cities, Judah.
Why do you bring charges against me? All of you have rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
In vain I have struck your children; they accepted no discipline. Your own sword has devoured your prophets like a ravaging lion.
You people of this generation, consider the word of the LORD! Have I been a wilderness to Israel, or a land of thick darkness? Why do my people say, "We roam free; we will not come to you again"?
Does a young woman forget her jewelry, or a bride her sash? Yet my people have forgotten me for days without number.
How well you set your course to seek love! So you have even taught your ways to wicked women.
Even on your skirts is found the lifeblood of the innocent poor. You did not catch them breaking in. Yet in spite of all this
you say, "I am innocent; surely his anger has turned away from me." Look, I will bring you to judgment because you say, "I have not sinned."
How lightly you go about changing your way! You will be put to shame by Egypt, as you were put to shame by Assyria.
From there too you will go out with your hands on your head, for the LORD has rejected those you trust, and you will not prosper with them.

If a man sends his wife away, and she leaves him and becomes another man's wife, will he go back to her again? Would that land not be utterly defiled? But you have prostituted yourself with many lovers, and would you return to me? declares the LORD.

Lift up your eyes to the bare heights and look: where have you not been lain with? You sat by the roads waiting for them, like a nomad in the desert. You have defiled the land with your prostitution and your wickedness.
So the showers have been held back, and the spring rain has not come. Yet you have the brazen look of a prostitute; you refuse to be ashamed.
Have you not just now called to me, "My father, you are the companion of my youth!
Will he stay angry forever? Will he keep his anger to the end?" Look, that is how you have spoken, yet you have done all the evil you could.
The LORD said to me in the days of King Josiah: Have you seen what Faithless Israel has done? She went up on every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and prostituted herself there.
I thought, "After she has done all this, she will return to me." But she did not return, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.
I saw that, though I had sent Faithless Israel away and given her a certificate of divorce for all her adulteries, her treacherous sister Judah had no fear. She too went and prostituted herself.
Because her prostitution meant so little to her, she defiled the land, committing adultery with stone and tree.
Yet for all this her treacherous sister Judah did not return to me with all her heart, but only in pretense, declares the LORD.
The LORD said to me: Faithless Israel has shown herself more righteous than treacherous Judah.

Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say: Return, Faithless Israel, declares the LORD. I will not look on you in anger, for I am faithful, declares the LORD; I will not stay angry forever.

Only acknowledge your guilt, that you have rebelled against the LORD your God. You have spread your favors to strangers under every leafy tree, and you have not listened to my voice, declares the LORD.
Return, faithless children, declares the LORD, for I am your master. I will take you, one from a city and two from a clan, and bring you to Zion.
I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will feed you with knowledge and understanding.

When you have multiplied and become fruitful in the land in those days, declares the LORD, people will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the LORD." It will not come to mind. They will not remember it or miss it, and another will not be made.

At that time they will call Jerusalem "The Throne of the LORD," and all the nations will gather to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. They will no longer follow the stubbornness of their evil hearts.
In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the land of the north to the land I gave your ancestors as an inheritance.

I myself said: How I would set you among my sons, and give you a pleasant land, the most beautiful inheritance among the nations! I thought you would call me "My father," and would not turn back from following me.
But as a woman is unfaithful to her lover, so you have been unfaithful to me, house of Israel, declares the LORD.
A voice is heard on the bare heights, the weeping and pleading of the Israelites, because they have twisted their way; they have forgotten the LORD their God.
Return, faithless children; I will heal your faithlessness. "Here we are; we come to you, for you are the LORD our God.
Surely the hills are a delusion, the uproar on the mountains. Surely in the LORD our God is the salvation of Israel.
But the Shameful Thing has devoured what our ancestors worked for since our youth: their flocks and their herds, their sons and their daughters.

Let us lie down in our shame, and let our disgrace cover us. For we have sinned against the LORD our God, we and our ancestors, from our youth until this day, and we have not listened to the voice of the LORD our God."
If you return, Israel, declares the LORD, return to me. If you put your detestable idols out of my sight and do not stray,
and if you swear, "As surely as the LORD lives," in truth, in justice and in righteousness, then the nations will bless themselves by him, and in him they will glory.
For this is what the LORD says to the people of Judah and to Jerusalem: Break up your unplowed ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to the LORD; remove the foreskins of your hearts, people of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem, or my wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to put it out, because of the evil of your deeds.
Declare it in Judah, proclaim it in Jerusalem, and say: Blow the ram's horn throughout the land! Shout aloud and say, "Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities!"
Raise a signal flag toward Zion! Run for safety; do not stand still! For I am bringing disaster from the north, and great destruction.
A lion has come up from its thicket; a destroyer of nations has set out. He has left his place to make your land a desolation. Your cities will be ruined, with no one living in them.
So put on sackcloth, mourn and wail, for the fierce anger of the LORD has not turned away from us.
On that day, declares the LORD, the king and the officials will lose heart. The priests will be appalled, and the prophets will be astounded.
Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Surely you have utterly deceived this people and Jerusalem, saying, 'You will have peace,' when the sword is at our throat!"
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: A scorching wind from the bare heights in the wilderness is coming toward my dear people, not to winnow and not to cleanse,
a wind too strong for that, coming at my command. Now I myself will pronounce judgments against them.
Look, he comes up like clouds, his chariots like the whirlwind; his horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we are ruined!
Wash the evil from your heart, Jerusalem, so that you may be saved. How long will your wicked thoughts lodge within you?
For a voice is declaring from Dan, and proclaiming disaster from the hill country of Ephraim.
Tell the nations, "Look!" Proclaim against Jerusalem: Besiegers are coming from a distant land; they raise their voices against the cities of Judah.
Like men guarding a field, they surround her on every side, because she has rebelled against me, declares the LORD.
Your own way and your deeds have brought this on you. This is your evil. How bitter it is! How it reaches your heart!
My insides, my insides! I writhe in pain! The walls of my heart! My heart pounds within me; I cannot keep silent. For you have heard, my soul, the sound of the ram's horn, the battle cry.
Disaster follows disaster; the whole land is devastated. Suddenly my tents are devastated, my tent curtains in a moment.
How long must I see the signal flag and hear the sound of the ram's horn?
For my people are foolish; they do not know me. They are senseless children; they have no understanding. They are skilled at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and it was formless and empty; at the heavens, and their light was gone.
I looked at the mountains, and they were quaking; all the hills were swaying.
I looked, and there were no human beings, and all the birds of the sky had fled.
I looked, and the fruitful land was a wilderness, and all its cities were torn down before the LORD, before his fierce anger.
For this is what the LORD says: The whole land will be a desolation, yet I will not make a full end of it.
Because of this the earth will mourn, and the heavens above will grow dark, because I have spoken, I have purposed, and I have not relented, nor will I turn back from it.
At the noise of horsemen and archers the whole city flees. They go into the thickets and climb up among the rocks. Every city is abandoned; no one lives in them.

And you, devastated one, what are you doing? Though you dress in scarlet, though you put on gold jewelry, though you enlarge your eyes with paint, you make yourself beautiful in vain. Your lovers despise you; they seek your life.

For I hear a cry like that of a woman in labor, the anguish of one bearing her first child, the cry of daughter Zion gasping for breath, stretching out her hands: "Woe is me! My life is fainting before the killers!"
Roam through the streets of Jerusalem; look around and take note. Search her squares to see if you can find one person, anyone who does justice and seeks to be faithful, so that I may forgive her.
Though they say, "As surely as the LORD lives," they are still swearing falsely.

LORD, do your eyes not look for faithfulness? You struck them, but they felt no pain; you crushed them, but they refused to accept discipline. They made their faces harder than rock; they refused to turn back.
I thought, "These are only the poor. They are foolish, for they do not know the way of the LORD, what their God requires.
I will go to the great men and speak to them, for surely they know the way of the LORD, what their God requires." But they too, all of them, had broken the yoke and torn off the bonds.

So a lion from the forest will strike them down, a wolf from the desert will destroy them, and a leopard is watching their cities. Everyone who goes out of them will be torn to pieces, for their rebellions are many, their acts of faithlessness are numerous.

How can I forgive you for this? Your children have abandoned me and sworn by gods that are not gods. I fed them until they were full, and they committed adultery and thronged to the house of a prostitute.
They are well-fed, lusty stallions; each one neighs for his neighbor's wife.
Should I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Should I not avenge myself on a nation like this?
Go up through her vineyard rows and destroy, but do not make a full end. Strip away her branches, for they do not belong to the LORD.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been utterly unfaithful to me, declares the LORD.
They have denied the LORD and said, "He will do nothing! No disaster will come on us; we will not see sword or famine.
The prophets are only wind; the word is not in them. So may it be done to them!"
Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, says: Because you people have spoken this word, I am going to make my words in your mouth a fire, and this people wood, and it will consume them.

I am going to bring against you a nation from far away, house of Israel, declares the LORD. It is an enduring nation, an ancient nation, a nation whose language you do not know, and you will not understand what they say.
Their quiver is like an open grave; all of them are warriors.

They will devour your harvest and your food; they will devour your sons and your daughters. They will devour your flocks and your herds; they will devour your vines and your fig trees. With the sword they will shatter the fortified cities you trust in.
Yet even in those days, declares the LORD, I will not make a full end of you.

And when you ask, "Why has the LORD our God done all these things to us?" you are to say to them, "As you have abandoned me and served foreign gods in your land, so you will serve strangers in a land that is not yours."
Declare this in the house of Jacob, and proclaim it in Judah:
Hear this, you foolish and senseless people, who have eyes but do not see, who have ears but do not hear.

Do you not fear me? declares the LORD. Do you not tremble before me? I placed the sand as a boundary for the sea, a permanent limit that it cannot cross. Its waves toss, but they cannot prevail; they roar, but they cannot cross it.
But this people has a stubborn and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away.
They do not say in their hearts, "Let us fear the LORD our God, who gives the rain, the autumn rain and the spring rain, in its season, who keeps for us the weeks appointed for the harvest."
Your wrongdoings have turned these away; your sins have kept good things from you.
For among my people are found wicked men. They watch like fowlers lying in wait; they set a trap; they catch human beings.
Like a cage full of birds, their houses are full of deceit. That is how they have become great and rich.
They have grown fat and sleek. They have even gone beyond all bounds in evil. They do not plead the cause, the cause of the fatherless, yet they prosper; they do not defend the rights of the needy.
Should I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Should I not avenge myself on a nation like this?
An appalling and horrible thing has happened in the land:
the prophets prophesy falsely, and the priests rule as they direct, and my people love it so. But what will you do when the end comes?
Run for safety, people of Benjamin, out of the midst of Jerusalem! Blow the ram's horn in Tekoa, and raise a signal fire over Beth-hakkerem! For disaster looms from the north, and great destruction.
Daughter Zion, so lovely and delicate, I will destroy.
Shepherds with their flocks will come to her. They will pitch their tents against her all around; each will graze his own part.
"Prepare for war against her! Up, let us attack at noon! Woe to us, for the day is fading; the evening shadows are lengthening.
Up, let us attack by night and destroy her fortresses!"
For this is what the LORD of Armies says: Cut down her trees and pile up a siege ramp against Jerusalem. This is the city that must be punished; there is nothing but oppression within her.
As a well keeps its water fresh, so she keeps her wickedness fresh. Violence and destruction are heard in her; sickness and wounds are always before me.
Take warning, Jerusalem, or I will turn from you in disgust and make you a desolation, a land where no one lives.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: They will glean the remnant of Israel as thoroughly as a vine. Pass your hand over the branches again, like a grape picker.

To whom can I speak and give warning, so that they will listen? Look, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot pay attention. Look, the word of the LORD has become an object of scorn to them; they take no pleasure in it.

But I am full of the wrath of the LORD; I am weary of holding it in. Pour it out on the children in the street, and on the young men gathered together. For husband and wife alike will be caught, the old and those full of years.
Their houses will be turned over to others, their fields and their wives together, for I will stretch out my hand against those who live in the land, declares the LORD.
For from the least of them to the greatest, every one is greedy for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, every one deals falsely.
They have treated the wound of my people as though it were nothing, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.

They acted shamefully, for they did detestable things, yet they were not at all ashamed; they did not even know how to blush. So they will fall among those who fall; when I punish them, they will stumble, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: Stand by the roads and look, and ask for the ancient paths, where the good way is, and walk in it, and you will find rest for yourselves. But they said, "We will not walk in it."
I appointed watchmen over you: "Listen to the sound of the ram's horn!" But they said, "We will not listen."
Therefore hear, you nations, and know, you assembly, what will happen to them.
Hear, you earth: I am going to bring disaster on this people, the fruit of their own schemes, because they have not paid attention to my words, and they have rejected my instruction.
What use to me is frankincense that comes from Sheba, or sweet cane from a distant land? Your burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices do not please me.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to put obstacles before this people. Fathers and sons together will stumble over them; neighbor and friend will perish.
This is what the LORD says: Look, a people is coming from the land of the north; a great nation is being stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
They grasp bow and javelin; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound is like the roaring sea; they ride on horses, drawn up like warriors for battle against you, daughter Zion.
We have heard the report of them; our hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped us, pain like that of a woman in labor.
Do not go out into the field or walk on the road, for the enemy has a sword. Terror is on every side.
My dear people, put on sackcloth and roll in ashes. Mourn as for an only son, with bitter wailing, for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.
I have made you a tester of metals among my people, a fortress, so that you may know and test their ways.
They are all the most stubborn of rebels, going about with slander. They are bronze and iron; all of them act corruptly.
The bellows blow fiercely; the lead is consumed by the fire. The refining goes on in vain; the wicked are not drawn off.
They are called rejected silver, for the LORD has rejected them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Stand in the gate of the LORD's house and proclaim this word there. Say: Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who come in through these gates to worship the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Make your ways and your deeds good, and I will let you live in this place.
Do not trust in deceptive words: "This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD!"
For if you truly make your ways and your deeds good, if you truly do justice between one person and another,
if you do not oppress the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods to your own harm,
then I will let you live in this place, in the land I gave your ancestors, for all time.
But look, you are trusting in deceptive words that are worthless.
Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal and follow other gods you have not known,
and then come and stand before me in this house, which bears my name, and say, "We are safe!", only to go on doing all these detestable things?
Has this house, which bears my name, become a den of robbers in your eyes? But I, look, I have seen it, declares the LORD.
Go now to my place that was in Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, declares the LORD, and though I spoke to you again and again, you did not listen, and when I called you, you did not answer,
I will do to the house that bears my name, the house you trust in, the place I gave to you and your ancestors, just what I did to Shiloh.
I will throw you out of my sight, just as I threw out all your relatives, all the descendants of Ephraim.
As for you, do not pray for this people. Do not raise a cry or a prayer for them, and do not plead with me, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
The children gather wood, the fathers light the fire, and the women knead dough to make cakes for the Queen of Heaven. They pour out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.
But is it I they are provoking? declares the LORD. Is it not themselves, to their own shame?

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: My anger and my wrath will be poured out on this place, on human beings and animals, on the trees of the field and the produce of the ground. It will burn and not be put out.
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Add your burnt offerings to your sacrifices, and eat the meat yourselves!
For when I brought your ancestors out of the land of Egypt, I did not speak to them or command them about burnt offerings and sacrifices.
But this is what I commanded them: "Listen to my voice, and I will be your God, and you will be my people. Walk in all the way that I command you, so that it may go well with you."
But they did not listen or pay attention. They followed their own plans, in the stubbornness of their evil hearts. They went backward and not forward.
From the day your ancestors came out of the land of Egypt until this day, I have sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them again and again, day after day.
But they did not listen to me or pay attention. They stiffened their necks; they did more evil than their ancestors.
When you tell them all these things, they will not listen to you. When you call to them, they will not answer you.
So say to them: This is the nation that has not listened to the voice of the LORD its God and has not accepted discipline. Truth has perished; it has been cut off from their mouths.
Cut off your hair and throw it away; raise a lament on the bare heights, for the LORD has rejected and abandoned the generation that has roused his fury.
For the people of Judah have done what is evil in my eyes, declares the LORD. They have set up their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, and defiled it.
They have built the high places of Topheth in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire, something I did not command, nor did it ever enter my mind.

Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when it will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no room left.
The corpses of this people will be food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth, with no one to frighten them away.

I will put an end to the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem, for the land will become a ruin.

At that time, declares the LORD, the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of its officials, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will be brought out of their graves.

They will be spread out before the sun and the moon and all the host of heaven, which they have loved and served, which they have followed, consulted and worshiped. They will not be gathered up or buried; they will be like dung on the surface of the ground.
Death will be chosen rather than life by all the remnant that is left of this evil family, in all the places where I have driven them, declares the LORD of Armies.
Say to them: This is what the LORD says: When people fall, do they not get up? When someone turns away, does he not turn back?
Why then has this people, Jerusalem, turned away in endless faithlessness? They hold fast to deceit; they refuse to turn back.
I have listened carefully, but they do not speak what is right. No one repents of his wickedness, saying, "What have I done?" Each of them turns to his own course, like a horse charging into battle.
Even the stork in the sky knows her seasons, and the dove, the swift and the thrush keep the time of their coming. But my people do not know what the LORD requires.
How can you say, "We are wise, and the law of the LORD is with us"? But look, the lying pen of the scribes has turned it into a lie.
The wise will be put to shame; they will be dismayed and caught. Look, they have rejected the word of the LORD, so what wisdom do they have?
Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to new owners. For from the least to the greatest, every one is greedy for unjust gain; from prophet to priest, every one deals falsely.
They have treated the wound of my dear people as though it were nothing, saying, "Peace, peace," when there is no peace.

They acted shamefully, for they did detestable things, yet they were not at all ashamed; they did not know how to blush. So they will fall among those who fall; at the time of their punishment they will stumble, says the LORD.

I will gather them and make an end of them, declares the LORD. There will be no grapes on the vine, no figs on the fig tree, and even the leaves will wither. What I gave them will pass away from them.

"Why are we sitting here? Gather together! Let us go into the fortified cities and perish there. For the LORD our God has doomed us to perish and given us poisoned water to drink, because we have sinned against the LORD.
We hoped for peace, but no good has come; for a time of healing, but there is only terror."

From Dan the snorting of his horses is heard; at the sound of the neighing of his stallions the whole land quakes. They come and devour the land and everything in it, the city and those who live in it.
For I am sending snakes among you, vipers that no charm can stop, and they will bite you, declares the LORD.
My joy is gone; grief has come upon me; my heart is sick within me.

Listen! The cry of my dear people from a land far and wide: "Is the LORD not in Zion? Is her King not in her?" Why have they provoked me to anger with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?
"The harvest is past, the summer has ended, and we are not saved."
Because my dear people are broken, I am broken. I go about in mourning; horror has gripped me.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has no new skin grown over the wound of my dear people?
Oh, that my head were water and my eyes a fountain of tears, so that I could weep day and night for the slain of my dear people!
Oh, that I had in the wilderness a travelers' shelter, so that I could leave my people and go away from them! For they are all adulterers, a crowd of traitors.
They bend their tongues like bows to shoot lies. It is not by faithfulness that they have grown strong in the land, for they go from evil to evil, and they do not know me, declares the LORD.
Let everyone be on guard against his neighbor, and do not trust any brother. For every brother is a cheat like Jacob, and every neighbor goes about slandering.
Each one deceives his neighbor, and no one speaks the truth. They have taught their tongues to speak lies; they wear themselves out doing wrong.
You live in the midst of deceit; in their deceit they refuse to know me, declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to refine them and test them, for what else can I do because of my dear people?
Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth each one speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets an ambush for him.
Should I not punish them for these things? declares the LORD. Should I not avenge myself on a nation like this?

For the mountains I will take up weeping and wailing, and a lament for the pastures of the wilderness, because they are laid waste, with no one passing through, and the lowing of cattle is not heard. Both the birds of the sky and the animals have fled; they are gone.
I will make Jerusalem a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, with no one living there.

Who is wise enough to understand this? To whom has the mouth of the LORD spoken, so that he can explain it? Why has the land perished and been laid waste like a wilderness, with no one passing through?
The LORD said: Because they have abandoned my instruction, which I set before them, and have not listened to my voice or walked by it,
but have followed the stubbornness of their hearts and gone after the Baals, as their ancestors taught them,
therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to feed this people with wormwood and give them poisoned water to drink.
I will scatter them among nations that neither they nor their ancestors have known, and I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Consider, and call for the mourning women to come; send for the most skilled of them to come.
Let them hurry and raise a lament over us, so that our eyes may run with tears and our eyelids flow with water.
For a sound of wailing is heard from Zion: "How we are ruined! We are utterly put to shame, for we have left the land, because they have torn down our homes."
Now hear the word of the LORD, you women; let your ears receive the word of his mouth. Teach your daughters a lament, and each woman her neighbor a funeral song.
For death has climbed in through our windows; it has entered our fortresses, to cut off the children from the streets and the young men from the squares.
Speak: This is what the LORD declares: Human corpses will fall like dung on the open field, like sheaves behind the reaper, with no one to gather them.
This is what the LORD says: Let not the wise boast of their wisdom, or the strong boast of their strength, or the rich boast of their riches.

But let the one who boasts boast of this: that he understands and knows me, that I am the LORD, who acts with faithful love, justice and righteousness on the earth, for in these I delight, declares the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish all who are circumcised only in the flesh:

Egypt, Judah, Edom, the Ammonites, Moab, and all who clip the hair on their temples and live in the desert. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
Hear the word that the LORD speaks to you, house of Israel.
This is what the LORD says: Do not learn the way of the nations, and do not be terrified by the signs in the heavens, though the nations are terrified by them.
For the customs of the peoples are worthless. A tree is cut from the forest and shaped with a chisel by a craftsman's hands.
They adorn it with silver and gold; they fasten it with nails and hammers so that it will not totter.
Like a scarecrow in a cucumber field, they cannot speak. They have to be carried, because they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they can do no harm, and they cannot do any good either.
There is no one like you, LORD. You are great, and your name is great in might.
Who would not fear you, King of the nations? It is your due. For among all the wise of the nations and in all their kingdoms there is no one like you.
They are all stupid and foolish alike; the teaching of worthless idols is only wood!
Hammered silver is brought from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz, the work of a craftsman and of a goldsmith's hands. Their clothing is violet and purple; they are all the work of skilled workers.
But the LORD is the true God; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes, and the nations cannot endure his fury.
This is what you are to say to them: The gods who did not make the heavens and the earth will perish from the earth and from under these heavens.
He made the earth by his power; he established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
When he thunders, there is a roar of waters in the heavens; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every human being is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol. For his cast images are a lie; there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work of mockery. At the time of their punishment they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the maker of all things, and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance. The LORD of Armies is his name.
Gather up your bundle from the ground, you who live under siege!
For this is what the LORD says: This time I am going to sling out the inhabitants of the land. I will bring distress on them, so that they will feel it.
Woe is me because of my injury! My wound is incurable. But I said, "Surely this is my sickness, and I must bear it."
My tent is destroyed, and all my tent ropes are snapped. My children have gone from me and are no more. There is no one left to pitch my tent again or to set up my tent curtains.
For the shepherds are stupid; they have not sought the LORD. So they have not prospered, and all their flock is scattered.
Listen! A report is coming, a great commotion from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a desolation, a haunt of jackals.
I know, LORD, that a human being's way is not in his own control; it is not for anyone who walks to direct his own steps.
Correct me, LORD, but only with justice, not in your anger, or you will reduce me to nothing.

Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the clans that do not call on your name. For they have devoured Jacob; they have devoured him and consumed him, and laid waste his homeland.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak them to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
Say to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Cursed is anyone who does not listen to the words of this covenant,

which I commanded your ancestors when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron-smelting furnace: "Listen to my voice and do them, everything I command you. Then you will be my people, and I will be your God,"
so that I may keep the oath I swore to your ancestors, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is today. I answered, "Amen, LORD."
The LORD said to me: Proclaim all these words in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem: Hear the words of this covenant and do them.
For I solemnly warned your ancestors when I brought them up from the land of Egypt, and I have warned them again and again until this day, saying, "Listen to my voice."

But they did not listen or pay attention; each of them followed the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this covenant, which I had commanded them to do, but they did not do them.
The LORD said to me: A conspiracy has been found among the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have gone back to the wrongdoings of their ancestors of old, who refused to listen to my words. They too have followed other gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant that I made with their ancestors.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to bring on them a disaster they cannot escape. They will cry out to me, but I will not listen to them.
Then the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods they burn incense to, but these will not save them at all in the time of their trouble.
For you have as many gods as you have cities, Judah, and as many altars as Jerusalem has streets you have set up to the Shameful Thing, altars to burn incense to Baal.
As for you, do not pray for this people, or raise a cry or a prayer for them, for I will not listen when they call to me because of their trouble.
What right does my beloved have in my house, when she has carried out so many evil schemes? Can sacred meat take away your disaster from you? Then you could rejoice.
The LORD once named you "A leafy olive tree, beautiful with well-formed fruit." But with the roar of a great storm he will set fire to it, and its branches will be broken.

The LORD of Armies, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you, because of the evil that the house of Israel and the house of Judah have done, provoking me to anger by burning incense to Baal.
The LORD made it known to me, and I knew it. Then you showed me what they were doing.

But I was like a trusting lamb led to the slaughter. I did not know it was against me they had made their plans: "Let us destroy the tree with its fruit; let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name will be remembered no more."
But the LORD of Armies, who judges righteously, who tests the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance on them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Therefore this is what the LORD says about the people of Anathoth, who seek your life and say, "Do not prophesy in the name of the LORD, or you will die by our hand":
therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to punish them. The young men will die by the sword; their sons and their daughters will die by famine.
Not even a remnant will be left to them, for I will bring disaster on the people of Anathoth, the year of their punishment.
You are always in the right, LORD, when I bring a case against you. Yet I would speak with you about justice: Why does the way of the wicked prosper? Why do all the treacherous live at ease?
You planted them, and they have taken root; they grow and bear fruit. You are near in their mouths but far from their hearts.
But you, LORD, know me; you see me and test my heart toward you. Drag them off like sheep to be slaughtered; set them apart for the day of killing.

How long will the land mourn and the grass of every field wither? Because of the wickedness of those who live in it, the animals and the birds are swept away. For they have said, "He will not see what becomes of us."
If you have raced with men on foot and they have worn you out, how will you compete with horses? If you feel secure only in a peaceful land, how will you manage in the thickets of the Jordan?
For even your brothers and your own family, even they have betrayed you; even they are shouting loudly after you. Do not trust them, even when they speak kindly to you.
I have abandoned my house; I have deserted my inheritance. I have given the one I dearly love into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become to me like a lion in the forest. She has roared at me; therefore I hate her.
Has my inheritance become to me like a speckled bird of prey, with birds of prey all around her? Go, gather all the wild animals; bring them to devour.
Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have trampled down my portion. They have turned my pleasant portion into a desolate wilderness.
They have made it a desolation; desolate, it mourns before me. The whole land has been made desolate, but no one takes it to heart.
Over all the bare heights in the wilderness destroyers have come, for the sword of the LORD devours from one end of the land to the other. No living thing has peace.
They have sown wheat but reaped thorns; they have worn themselves out but gained nothing. Be ashamed of your harvests, because of the fierce anger of the LORD.

This is what the LORD says about all my evil neighbors who strike at the inheritance I gave my people Israel: I am going to uproot them from their land, and I will uproot the house of Judah from among them.
But after I have uprooted them, I will again have compassion on them, and I will bring them back, each one to his inheritance and each one to his land.
And if they diligently learn the ways of my people, to swear by my name, "As surely as the LORD lives," just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they will be built up among my people.
But if any nation will not listen, I will completely uproot that nation and destroy it, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD said to me: "Go and buy yourself a linen loincloth and put it around your waist, but do not put it in water."
So I bought a loincloth, as the LORD had told me, and put it around my waist.
The word of the LORD came to me a second time:
"Take the loincloth you bought, the one around your waist, and set out for Perath. Hide it there in a crevice in the rock."
So I went and hid it at Perath, as the LORD had commanded me.
After many days the LORD said to me, "Set out for Perath, and take from there the loincloth I commanded you to hide there."
So I went to Perath and dug, and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it. And look, the loincloth was ruined; it was good for nothing.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"This is what the LORD says: In the same way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

This evil people, who refuse to listen to my words, who follow the stubbornness of their hearts and have gone after other gods to serve them and worship them, will be like this loincloth, which is good for nothing.

For as a loincloth clings to a man's waist, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to me, declares the LORD, to be my people, for my renown, my praise and my glory. But they did not listen."

Say this word to them: This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Every jar should be filled with wine. And when they say to you, "Don't we know very well that every jar should be filled with wine?"

then say to them: This is what the LORD says: I am going to fill all the inhabitants of this land with drunkenness: the kings who sit on David's throne, the priests, the prophets and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
I will smash them one against another, fathers and sons together, declares the LORD. I will not show pity or spare them or have compassion; nothing will keep me from destroying them.
Hear and pay attention; do not be proud, for the LORD has spoken.
Give glory to the LORD your God before he brings darkness, before your feet stumble on the mountains at dusk. You will look for light, but he will turn it into deep darkness and make it thick gloom.
But if you will not listen, I will weep in secret because of your pride. My eyes will weep bitterly and run with tears, because the flock of the LORD has been taken captive.
Say to the king and to the queen mother, "Take a lowly seat, for your glorious crowns have come down from your heads."
The cities of the Negev are shut up, and there is no one to open them. All Judah has been carried into exile, carried into exile completely.
Lift up your eyes and see those coming from the north. Where is the flock that was given to you, your beautiful flock?
What will you say when he sets over you as rulers those you yourself trained to be your friends? Will not pains seize you like a woman in labor?
And if you say in your heart, "Why have these things happened to me?" it is because of your many sins that your skirts have been stripped off and your body violated.
Can a Cushite change his skin, or a leopard its spots? Then you also can do good, you who are trained to do evil.
I will scatter them like chaff blown away by the desert wind.
This is your lot, the portion I have measured out to you, declares the LORD, because you have forgotten me and trusted in the Lie.
I myself will pull your skirts up over your face, and your shame will be seen.

Your adulteries and your lustful neighing, your shameless prostitution on the hills in the countryside: I have seen your detestable acts. Woe to you, Jerusalem! You will not be made clean. How long will it still be?
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah about the drought:
Judah mourns, and her gates languish; her people sit in black on the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.
Their nobles send their servants for water. They come to the cisterns but find no water; they return with their jars empty. They are ashamed and dismayed, and they cover their heads.
Because the ground is cracked, for there has been no rain in the land, the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
Even the doe in the field gives birth and abandons her fawn, because there is no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights and pant for air like jackals; their eyes fail because there is no vegetation.
Though our wrongdoings testify against us, LORD, act for the sake of your name. For our acts of faithlessness are many; we have sinned against you.
Hope of Israel, its Savior in time of trouble, why are you like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who stops only for a night?
Why are you like a man taken by surprise, like a warrior who cannot save? Yet you are among us, LORD, and we bear your name. Do not abandon us!
This is what the LORD says about this people: How they love to wander! They do not restrain their feet. So the LORD does not accept them; now he will remember their wrongdoing and punish their sins.
The LORD said to me: Do not pray for the good of this people.
Though they fast, I will not listen to their cry; though they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them. Instead I will make an end of them by sword, famine and plague.
Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! Look, the prophets keep telling them, 'You will not see the sword, and you will not have famine. I will give you lasting peace in this place.'"

The LORD said to me: The prophets are prophesying lies in my name. I did not send them or command them or speak to them. They are prophesying to you false visions, divination, worthless things and the delusions of their own minds.

Therefore this is what the LORD says about the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I did not send them, and who say, "Sword and famine will not come on this land": By sword and famine those prophets will meet their end.

And the people they are prophesying to will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, with no one to bury them, them, their wives, their sons and their daughters. I will pour out on them their own wickedness.
Say this word to them: Let my eyes run with tears night and day, and let them not stop, for the virgin daughter of my people has been struck a crushing blow, a very grievous wound.
If I go out into the field, look, those killed by the sword! If I enter the city, look, those sick with famine! For both prophet and priest wander through a land they do not know.

Have you utterly rejected Judah? Do you loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that there is no healing for us? We hoped for peace, but no good has come; for a time of healing, but there is only terror.
We acknowledge our wickedness, LORD, the wrongdoing of our ancestors, for we have sinned against you.
For the sake of your name, do not spurn us; do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember your covenant with us, and do not break it.
Can any of the worthless idols of the nations bring rain? Can the heavens give showers by themselves? Is it not you, LORD our God? So we hope in you, for you are the one who does all these things.
Then the LORD said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my heart would not turn toward this people. Send them away from my presence, and let them go!

And if they ask you, "Where shall we go?" tell them: This is what the LORD says: Those destined for death, to death; those destined for the sword, to the sword; those destined for famine, to famine; and those destined for captivity, to captivity.
I will appoint over them four kinds of destroyers, declares the LORD: the sword to kill, the dogs to drag away, and the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth to devour and destroy.
I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, because of what Manasseh son of Hezekiah king of Judah did in Jerusalem.
