Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve for you? Who will turn aside to ask how you are?
You have rejected me, declares the LORD; you keep going backward. So I have stretched out my hand against you and destroyed you; I am tired of relenting.
I have winnowed them with a winnowing fork in the gates of the land. I have bereaved them, I have destroyed my people, for they did not turn back from their ways.

Their widows have become more numerous before me than the sand of the seas. At noon I have brought a destroyer against the mothers of young men; I have suddenly brought down on them anguish and terror.

The mother of seven grows faint; she breathes out her life. Her sun has set while it is still day; she is shamed and humiliated. And the rest of them I will give to the sword before their enemies, declares the LORD.
Woe is me, my mother, that you gave birth to me, a man of strife and contention to the whole land! I have not lent, and no one has lent to me, yet all of them curse me.
The LORD said: Surely I will set you free for good. Surely I will make the enemy plead with you in the time of disaster and the time of distress.
Can anyone break iron, iron from the north, and bronze?
Your wealth and your treasures I will give away as plunder, without price, because of all your sins throughout all your territory.
I will make you go with your enemies into a land you do not know, for a fire has been kindled by my anger; it will burn against you.
You know, LORD. Remember me and take care of me, and take vengeance for me on my persecutors. Do not let your patience with them sweep me away. Know that for your sake I bear insult.
When your words were found, I ate them, and your word became a joy to me and the delight of my heart, for I bear your name, LORD, God of Armies.
I did not sit in the company of those who make merry, or celebrate with them. Because your hand was on me I sat alone, for you had filled me with indignation.
Why is my pain unending, and my wound incurable, refusing to be healed? Will you truly be to me like a deceptive brook, like waters that cannot be relied on?

Therefore this is what the LORD says: If you turn back, I will bring you back, and you will stand before me. If you bring out what is precious and not what is worthless, you will be my mouth. Let them turn to you, but you must not turn to them.
I will make you to this people a fortified wall of bronze. They will fight against you, but they will not overcome you, for I am with you to save you and rescue you, declares the LORD.
I will rescue you from the hand of the wicked and redeem you from the grasp of the ruthless.
The word of the LORD came to me:
You must not take a wife, or have sons or daughters in this place.
For this is what the LORD says about the sons and daughters born in this place, and about the mothers who bear them and the fathers who father them in this land:

They will die of deadly diseases. They will not be mourned or buried; they will be like dung on the surface of the ground. They will perish by sword and famine, and their corpses will be food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

For this is what the LORD says: Do not enter a house where there is a funeral feast, and do not go to mourn or to grieve for them, for I have withdrawn my peace from this people, declares the LORD, my faithful love and my compassion.
Both great and small will die in this land. They will not be buried, and no one will mourn for them; no one will gash himself or shave his head for them.
No one will break bread for the mourner, to comfort him for the dead, and no one will give them a cup of consolation to drink for a father or a mother.
Do not enter a house where there is feasting, to sit with them and eat and drink.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to put an end in this place, before your eyes and in your days, to the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

When you tell this people all these things, and they ask you, "Why has the LORD pronounced all this great disaster against us? What is our wrongdoing? What is the sin we have committed against the LORD our God?"
then say to them: It is because your ancestors abandoned me, declares the LORD, and followed other gods and served them and worshiped them. They abandoned me and did not keep my law.
And you have done worse than your ancestors. Look, each of you is following the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of listening to me.
So I will hurl you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your ancestors have known, and there you will serve other gods day and night, for I will show you no favor.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt,"

but, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where he had driven them." For I will bring them back to their land, which I gave to their ancestors.

I am going to send for many fishermen, declares the LORD, and they will catch them. After that I will send for many hunters, and they will hunt them down on every mountain and every hill, and in the crevices of the rocks.
For my eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from me, and their wrongdoing is not concealed from my eyes.

First I will repay them double for their wrongdoing and their sin, because they have defiled my land with the corpses of their detestable idols, and filled my inheritance with their detestable things.

LORD, my strength and my stronghold, my refuge in the day of trouble, to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, "Our ancestors inherited nothing but lies, worthless things that did them no good.
Can human beings make gods for themselves? Such things are not gods!"
Therefore, look, I will teach them. This time I will make them know my power and my might, and they will know that my name is the LORD.
The sin of Judah is written with an iron pen; with a diamond point it is engraved on the tablet of their hearts and on the horns of their altars.
Their children remember their altars and their Asherah poles beside the leafy trees, on the high hills,
my mountain in the open country. Your wealth and all your treasures I will give away as plunder, along with your high places, because of sin throughout all your territory.

Through your own fault you will lose your hold on the inheritance I gave you. I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know, for you have kindled a fire in my anger that will burn forever.
This is what the LORD says: Cursed is the one who trusts in human beings, who makes mere flesh his strength, and whose heart turns away from the LORD.
He will be like a shrub in the desert; he will not see when good comes. He will live in the parched places of the wilderness, in a salt land where no one lives.
Blessed is the one who trusts in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD.

He will be like a tree planted by water, that sends out its roots by a stream. It does not see when heat comes; its leaves stay green. In a year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not stop bearing fruit.
The heart is more deceitful than anything, and desperately sick. Who can understand it?
I, the LORD, search the heart and test the mind, to give each one according to his ways, according to the fruit of his deeds.
Like a partridge that hatches eggs it did not lay is the one who gains riches unjustly. In the middle of his life his riches will leave him, and at his end he will be a fool.
A glorious throne, exalted from the beginning, is the place of our sanctuary.
LORD, the hope of Israel, all who abandon you will be put to shame. Those who turn away from me will be written in the dust, for they have abandoned the LORD, the spring of living water.
Heal me, LORD, and I will be healed; save me, and I will be saved, for you are my praise.
Look, they keep saying to me, "Where is the word of the LORD? Let it come now!"
But I have not run away from being a shepherd who follows you, nor have I longed for the day of disaster. You know what came from my lips; it was before you.
Do not become a terror to me; you are my refuge in the day of disaster.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, but do not let me be put to shame. Let them be terrified, but do not let me be terrified. Bring on them the day of disaster; shatter them with double destruction.
This is what the LORD said to me: Go and stand in the People's Gate, through which the kings of Judah come in and go out, and in all the gates of Jerusalem.
Say to them: Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah, all Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem who come in through these gates.
This is what the LORD says: For your lives' sake, be careful not to carry a load on the Sabbath day or bring it in through the gates of Jerusalem.
Do not carry a load out of your houses on the Sabbath day or do any work, but keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your ancestors.
Yet they did not listen or pay attention. They stiffened their necks so as not to listen or accept discipline.
But if you listen carefully to me, declares the LORD, and bring no load in through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, but keep the Sabbath day holy and do no work on it,

then kings and officials who sit on David's throne will come in through the gates of this city, riding in chariots and on horses, they and their officials, the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. And this city will be inhabited forever.

People will come from the cities of Judah and the area around Jerusalem, from the land of Benjamin, from the western foothills, from the hill country and from the Negev, bringing burnt offerings and sacrifices, grain offerings and frankincense, and bringing thanksgiving sacrifices to the house of the LORD.

But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath day holy and not carry a load as you come in through the gates of Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, then I will kindle a fire in its gates that will consume the fortresses of Jerusalem, and it will not be put out.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Get up and go down to the potter's house, and there I will let you hear my words."
So I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, working at the wheel.
Whenever the vessel he was making from the clay was spoiled in the potter's hand, he would make it again into another vessel, as seemed right to the potter.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"House of Israel, can I not do with you as this potter does? declares the LORD. Look, like the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in my hand, house of Israel.
At one moment I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, to uproot it, tear it down and destroy it.
But if that nation I have spoken against turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster I intended to bring on it.
At another moment I may speak about a nation or a kingdom, to build it and to plant it.
But if it does evil in my eyes and does not listen to my voice, I will relent of the good I had said I would do for it.

So now, say to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: 'This is what the LORD says: Look, I am shaping disaster against you and devising a plan against you. Turn back, each of you, from his evil way, and make your ways and your deeds good.'
But they will say, 'It's hopeless! We will follow our own plans; each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart.'"
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Ask among the nations: Who has ever heard anything like this? The virgin Israel has done a most horrible thing.
Does the snow of Lebanon ever vanish from the rocks of the field? Do the cold waters flowing from afar ever run dry?
Yet my people have forgotten me; they burn incense to what is worthless. They have stumbled in their ways, the ancient paths, to walk in bypaths, on a road not built up.
Their land will become a horror, a thing to hiss at forever. All who pass by it will be appalled and shake their heads.
Like the east wind I will scatter them before the enemy. I will show them my back and not my face in the day of their disaster.

Then they said, "Come, let us make plans against Jeremiah, for instruction will not be lost from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike at him with our tongues, and pay no attention to anything he says."
Pay attention to me, LORD, and hear what my accusers are saying.
Should good be repaid with evil? Yet they have dug a pit for me. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, to turn your wrath away from them.

So hand their children over to famine, and give them over to the power of the sword. Let their wives be made childless and widowed; let their men be killed by plague, their young men struck down by the sword in battle.
Let a cry be heard from their houses when you suddenly bring raiders against them, for they have dug a pit to capture me and hidden snares for my feet.
But you, LORD, know all their plotting to kill me. Do not forgive their wrongdoing, or blot out their sin from your sight. Let them be overthrown before you; deal with them in the time of your anger.
This is what the LORD says: Go and buy a potter's clay jar. Take with you some of the elders of the people and some of the senior priests,
and go out to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, at the entrance of the Potsherd Gate. There proclaim the words I tell you.

Say: Hear the word of the LORD, you kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring such a disaster on this place that the ears of everyone who hears of it will tingle.

For they have abandoned me and made this place a foreign place, burning incense in it to other gods that neither they nor their ancestors nor the kings of Judah ever knew, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocent.
They have built the high places of Baal to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to Baal, something I did not command or speak of, nor did it ever enter my mind.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when this place will no longer be called Topheth or the Valley of Ben-hinnom, but the Valley of Slaughter.

In this place I will empty out the plans of Judah and Jerusalem. I will make them fall by the sword before their enemies, by the hand of those who seek their lives, and I will give their corpses as food to the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.
I will make this city a horror and a thing to hiss at; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.

I will make them eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and they will eat one another's flesh, in the siege and the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their lives will press them hard.
Then break the jar in the sight of the men who go with you,

and say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies says: So I will break this people and this city, as one breaks a potter's vessel so that it can never be mended. They will bury the dead in Topheth until there is no room left to bury.
This is what I will do to this place and to its inhabitants, declares the LORD: I will make this city like Topheth.

The houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the kings of Judah will be defiled like the place of Topheth, all the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods.
Then Jeremiah came from Topheth, where the LORD had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the LORD's house and said to all the people,

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring on this city and on all its towns all the disaster I have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their necks so as not to listen to my words."
When the priest Pashhur son of Immer, who was chief officer in the house of the LORD, heard Jeremiah prophesying these things,
Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and put him in the stocks at the Upper Gate of Benjamin in the house of the LORD.
The next day, when Pashhur released Jeremiah from the stocks, Jeremiah said to him, "The LORD has not named you Pashhur, but Terror-on-Every-Side.

For this is what the LORD says: I am going to make you a terror to yourself and to all your friends. They will fall by the sword of their enemies before your eyes. I will hand all Judah over to the king of Babylon, and he will carry them into exile to Babylon or strike them down with the sword.

I will hand over to their enemies all the wealth of this city, all the fruit of its labor, all its valuables and all the treasures of the kings of Judah. They will plunder them, seize them and carry them off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, and everyone who lives in your house will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon; there you will die, and there you will be buried, you and all your friends to whom you have prophesied lies."
You deceived me, LORD, and I was deceived; you overpowered me, and you prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
For whenever I speak, I cry out; I shout, "Violence and destruction!" For the word of the LORD has brought me insult and scorn all day long.
If I say, "I will not mention him or speak any more in his name," then it is in my heart like a burning fire, shut up in my bones. I am worn out holding it in, and I cannot.

For I hear many whispering, "Terror on every side! Denounce him! Let us denounce him!" All my close friends are watching for me to stumble: "Perhaps he will be deceived, and then we will prevail over him and take our revenge on him."
But the LORD is with me like a mighty warrior. So my persecutors will stumble and not prevail. They will be utterly put to shame, for they will not succeed. Their disgrace will never be forgotten.
LORD of Armies, you who test the righteous, who see the heart and mind, let me see your vengeance on them, for to you I have committed my cause.
Sing to the LORD! Praise the LORD! For he has rescued the life of the needy from the hand of evildoers.
Cursed be the day I was born! May the day my mother gave birth to me not be blessed!
Cursed be the man who brought the news to my father, "A son is born to you, a boy!" and made him very glad.
May that man be like the cities that the LORD overthrew without relenting. May he hear a cry in the morning and a battle shout at noon,
because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have been my grave, her womb pregnant forever.
Why did I ever come out of the womb to see trouble and sorrow, and to end my days in shame?
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and the priest Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, saying,

"Please inquire of the LORD for us, because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon is making war against us. Perhaps the LORD will act for us in keeping with all his wonderful deeds, and make him withdraw from us."
Jeremiah said to them, "Say this to Zedekiah:

'This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I am going to turn back the weapons of war in your hands, with which you are fighting the king of Babylon and the Babylonians who are besieging you outside the wall, and I will gather them into the middle of this city.
I myself will fight against you with an outstretched hand and a strong arm, in anger, in fury and in great wrath.
I will strike down the inhabitants of this city, both human beings and animals; they will die of a great plague.

After that, declares the LORD, I will hand over Zedekiah king of Judah, his servants and the people in this city who survive the plague, the sword and the famine, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, to their enemies and to those who seek their lives. He will strike them down with the edge of the sword; he will not spare them, or have pity or compassion.'"
And to this people you are to say: This is what the LORD says: I am setting before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine or plague. But whoever goes out and surrenders to the Babylonians who are besieging you will live; he will escape with his life.
For I have set my face against this city for harm and not for good, declares the LORD. It will be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
And to the royal house of Judah: Hear the word of the LORD,

house of David. This is what the LORD says: Do justice every morning, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor, or my wrath will break out like fire and burn with no one to put it out, because of the evil of your deeds.
Look, I am against you, you who are enthroned above the valley, rock of the plain, declares the LORD, you who say, "Who can come down against us? Who can enter our dwellings?"
I will punish you according to the fruit of your deeds, declares the LORD. I will kindle a fire in her forest, and it will consume everything around her.
This is what the LORD says: Go down to the palace of the king of Judah and speak this word there.
Say: Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne, you and your servants and your people who come in through these gates.

This is what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the oppressor. Do not wrong or mistreat the foreigner, the fatherless or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you truly carry out this word, then kings who sit on David's throne will come in through the gates of this palace, riding in chariots and on horses, each with his servants and his people.
But if you do not listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that this palace will become a ruin.
For this is what the LORD says about the palace of the king of Judah: You are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon, yet I will surely make you a wilderness, cities where no one lives.
I will set apart destroyers against you, each with his weapons, and they will cut down your choicest cedars and throw them into the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city, and they will say to one another, "Why has the LORD done such a thing to this great city?"
And they will answer, "Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God, and worshiped other gods and served them."
Do not weep for the dead, or mourn for him. Weep bitterly instead for the one who is going away, for he will never come back to see his native land.
For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah king of Judah, who became king in place of his father Josiah and who has gone away from this place: He will never come back here.
He will die in the place where they have taken him into exile, and he will never see this land again.
Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not pay him his wages,
who says, "I will build myself a spacious house with roomy upper rooms," who cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar and paints it red.
Does it make you a king, that you compete in cedar? Did your father not eat and drink, and do justice and righteousness? Then it went well with him.
He defended the cause of the poor and needy; then it went well. Is that not what it means to know me? declares the LORD.
But your eyes and your heart are set only on your dishonest gain, on shedding innocent blood, on oppression and extortion.

Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah: They will not mourn for him, "Alas, my brother! Alas, sister!" They will not mourn for him, "Alas, master! Alas, his majesty!"
He will be buried with the burial of a donkey, dragged off and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers are crushed.
I spoke to you when you were at ease, but you said, "I will not listen." This has been your way from your youth: you have not listened to my voice.
The wind will shepherd away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
You who live in Lebanon, nestled among the cedars, how pitiable you will be when pangs come on you, pain like that of a woman in labor!
As surely as I live, declares the LORD, even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah were the signet ring on my right hand, I would still pull you off it.
I will hand you over to those who seek your life, to those you fear, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Babylonians.
I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another country, where neither of you was born, and there you will die.
They will never return to the land they long to return to.
Is this man Coniah a despised, broken pot, a jar that no one wants? Why have he and his children been hurled out and thrown into a land they do not know?
Land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
This is what the LORD says: Record this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his lifetime. For none of his descendants will prosper; none will sit on David's throne or rule again in Judah.
Woe to the shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! declares the LORD.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds who shepherd my people: You have scattered my flock and driven them away, and you have not cared for them. So I am going to deal with you for the evil of your deeds, declares the LORD.
I myself will gather the remnant of my flock from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will be fruitful and multiply.
I will raise up shepherds over them who will shepherd them, and they will no longer be afraid or dismayed, and none will be missing, declares the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will raise up for David a righteous Branch. He will reign as king and act wisely, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will live in safety. And this is the name by which he will be called: The LORD Is Our Righteousness.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when people will no longer say, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought the Israelites up out of the land of Egypt,"

but, "As surely as the LORD lives, who brought up and led the descendants of the house of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where I had driven them." Then they will live on their own land.
Concerning the prophets: My heart is broken within me; all my bones tremble. I am like a drunk man, like a man overcome by wine, because of the LORD and because of his holy words.
For the land is full of adulterers; because of the curse the land mourns, and the pastures of the wilderness are dried up. Their course is evil, and their might is not right.
Both prophet and priest are godless; even in my house I have found their wickedness, declares the LORD.
Therefore their way will be to them like slippery paths in the darkness; they will be driven on and fall there. For I will bring disaster on them, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.
Among the prophets of Samaria I saw something offensive: they prophesied by Baal and led my people Israel astray.

But among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen something horrible: they commit adultery and walk in lies. They strengthen the hands of evildoers, so that no one turns from his wickedness. All of them have become like Sodom to me, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says about the prophets: I am going to feed them wormwood and make them drink poisoned water, for from the prophets of Jerusalem godlessness has spread throughout the land.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you. They are filling you with empty hopes. They speak visions from their own minds, not from the mouth of the LORD.
They keep saying to those who despise me, "The LORD has said, 'You will have peace.'" And to everyone who follows the stubbornness of his heart they say, "No disaster will come on you."
But which of them has stood in the council of the LORD, to see and hear his word? Who has paid attention to his word and listened?
Look, the storm of the LORD! Wrath has gone out, a whirling tempest; it will whirl down on the heads of the wicked.
The anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has done and carried out the purposes of his heart. In the days to come you will understand it clearly.
I did not send these prophets, yet they ran. I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
But if they had stood in my council, they would have proclaimed my words to my people and turned them back from their evil way and from the evil of their deeds.
Am I a God who is near, declares the LORD, and not a God far off?
Can anyone hide in secret places so that I cannot see him? declares the LORD. Do I not fill heaven and earth? declares the LORD.
I have heard what the prophets say who prophesy lies in my name: "I had a dream! I had a dream!"
How long? Is there anything in the minds of the prophets who prophesy lies, the prophets of the deceit of their own minds?
They plan to make my people forget my name by the dreams they tell one another, just as their ancestors forgot my name for Baal.
Let the prophet who has a dream tell his dream, but let the one who has my word speak my word faithfully. What does straw have to do with grain? declares the LORD.
Is not my word like fire, declares the LORD, and like a hammer that shatters rock?
Therefore I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who steal my words from one another.
I am against the prophets, declares the LORD, who use their own tongues and declare, "He declares."

I am against those who prophesy lying dreams, declares the LORD, who tell them and lead my people astray with their lies and their recklessness. I did not send them or command them, and they do this people no good at all, declares the LORD.
When this people, or a prophet or a priest, asks you, "What is the burden of the LORD?" say to them, "What burden? I will cast you off, declares the LORD."
And if a prophet or a priest or anyone else says, "The burden of the LORD," I will punish that man and his household.
This is what each of you is to say to his neighbor and to his brother: "What has the LORD answered?" or "What has the LORD spoken?"
But you must no longer mention "the burden of the LORD," for each man's own word will become his burden, and you twist the words of the living God, the LORD of Armies, our God.
This is what you are to say to the prophet: "What has the LORD answered you?" or "What has the LORD spoken?"

But if you say, "The burden of the LORD," then this is what the LORD says: Because you have used these words, "The burden of the LORD," though I sent word to you, "You must not say, 'The burden of the LORD,'"
therefore I will surely forget you and cast you away from my presence, you and the city I gave to you and your ancestors.
I will bring on you everlasting disgrace and everlasting shame that will never be forgotten.

The LORD showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the LORD. This was after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken into exile from Jerusalem Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah, the officials of Judah, the craftsmen and the metalworkers, and had brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very good figs, like figs that ripen early, and the other basket had very bad figs, so bad they could not be eaten.
The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" I said, "Figs. The good figs are very good, and the bad ones are very bad, so bad they cannot be eaten."
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Like these good figs, so I will regard as good the exiles of Judah, whom I have sent away from this place to the land of the Babylonians.
I will set my eyes on them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the LORD. They will be my people, and I will be their God, for they will return to me with all their heart.

But like the bad figs, which are so bad they cannot be eaten, this is what the LORD says, so I will treat Zedekiah king of Judah, his officials, and the remnant of Jerusalem who remain in this land and those who live in the land of Egypt.
I will make them a horror, a disaster, to all the kingdoms of the earth, a disgrace and a byword, a taunt and a curse, in all the places where I will drive them.
I will send the sword, famine and plague against them until they are wiped out from the land I gave to them and their ancestors."
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke it to all the people of Judah and to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem:

For twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah until this day, the word of the LORD has come to me, and I have spoken to you again and again, but you have not listened.
The LORD has sent you all his servants the prophets, sending them again and again, but you have not listened or paid any attention.
They said, "Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and your evil deeds, and you will live in the land the LORD gave to you and your ancestors for all time.
Do not follow other gods to serve them and worship them, and do not provoke me to anger with what your hands have made. Then I will not harm you."
But you did not listen to me, declares the LORD, and so you provoked me to anger with what your hands have made, to your own harm.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies says: Because you have not listened to my words,

I am going to send for all the clans of the north, declares the LORD, and for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I will bring them against this land and its inhabitants and against all these nations around it. I will destroy them completely and make them a horror, a thing to hiss at, and an everlasting ruin.
I will banish from them the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones and the light of the lamp.
This whole land will become a ruin and a desolation, and these nations will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.

But when the seventy years are complete, I will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their wrongdoing, declares the LORD, and the land of the Babylonians, and I will make it a desolation forever.
I will bring on that land all the words I have spoken against it, all that is written in this book, which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations.
For many nations and great kings will make slaves of them too, and I will repay them according to their deeds and the work of their hands.
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, said to me: Take from my hand this cup of the wine of wrath, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.
They will drink and stagger and go mad because of the sword I am sending among them.
So I took the cup from the LORD's hand and made all the nations to whom the LORD sent me drink it:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, its kings and its officials, to make them a ruin, a horror, a thing to hiss at and a curse, as they are today;
Pharaoh king of Egypt, his servants, his officials and all his people;
all the mixed peoples; all the kings of the land of Uz; all the kings of the land of the Philistines: Ashkelon, Gaza, Ekron and what remains of Ashdod;
all the kings of Tyre, all the kings of Sidon, and the kings of the coastlands across the sea;
Dedan, Tema, Buz and all who clip the hair on their temples;
all the kings of Arabia and all the kings of the mixed peoples who live in the desert;
all the kings of Zimri, all the kings of Elam and all the kings of Media;
all the kings of the north, near and far, one after another; and all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth. And after them the king of Sheshach will drink.
Then say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Drink, get drunk and vomit; fall and rise no more, because of the sword I am sending among you.
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand and drink, say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies says: You must drink it!

For look, I am beginning to bring disaster on the city that bears my name, and will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for I am summoning a sword against all the inhabitants of the earth, declares the LORD of Armies.

As for you, prophesy all these words against them, and say to them: The LORD roars from on high; from his holy dwelling he raises his voice. He roars mightily against his pasture; he shouts like those who tread grapes, against all who live on the earth.

The uproar resounds to the ends of the earth, for the LORD has a case against the nations; he is entering into judgment with all humankind. The wicked he will hand over to the sword, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Look, disaster is spreading from nation to nation; a great storm is being stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
On that day those slain by the LORD will lie from one end of the earth to the other. They will not be mourned or gathered up or buried; they will be like dung on the surface of the ground.
Wail, you shepherds, and cry out! Roll in the dust, you leaders of the flock! For the days of your slaughter and your scattering have come, and you will fall like a precious vessel.
There will be no escape for the shepherds, no way out for the leaders of the flock.
Listen! The cry of the shepherds, the wailing of the leaders of the flock, for the LORD is destroying their pasture.
The peaceful meadows are laid waste because of the fierce anger of the LORD.
Like a lion he has left his lair, for their land has become a desolation because of the fury of the oppressor, and because of his fierce anger.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:

"This is what the LORD says: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak to all the people of the towns of Judah who come to worship in the LORD's house. Tell them all the words I command you to speak to them; do not leave out a word.
Perhaps they will listen, and each of them will turn from his evil way. Then I will relent of the disaster I am planning to bring on them because of their evil deeds.
Say to them: 'This is what the LORD says: If you do not listen to me and walk in my instruction, which I have set before you,
and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I send to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.'"
The priests, the prophets and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
When Jeremiah had finished speaking everything that the LORD had commanded him to speak to all the people, the priests, the prophets and all the people seized him and said, "You must die!

Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD, 'This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be laid waste, with no one living in it'?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
When the officials of Judah heard these things, they came up from the king's palace to the house of the LORD and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.

Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves the death sentence, because he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and to all the people, "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all the words you have heard.
So now make your ways and your deeds good, and listen to the voice of the LORD your God. Then the LORD will relent of the disaster he has pronounced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do with me whatever seems good and right to you.

But know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city and on its inhabitants, for in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve the death sentence, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."
Some of the elders of the land stood up and said to the whole assembly of the people,

"Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah. He said to all the people of Judah, 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a wooded height.'

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek the LORD's favor? And the LORD relented of the disaster he had pronounced against them. But we are about to bring a great disaster on ourselves!"
There was also a man who prophesied in the name of the LORD, Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land just as Jeremiah did.
When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and was afraid, and he fled to Egypt.
Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor and some men with him.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his body into the burial ground of the common people.
But Ahikam son of Shaphan protected Jeremiah, so that he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD said to me: "Make yourself straps and yoke bars, and put them on your neck.
Then send them to the king of Edom, the king of Moab, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre and the king of Sidon, by the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah king of Judah.
Give them a message for their masters: 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: This is what you are to say to your masters:
By my great power and my outstretched arm I made the earth, and the human beings and the animals on the face of the earth, and I give it to whomever I see fit.
Now I have handed all these lands over to my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. I have given him even the wild animals to serve him.
All the nations will serve him and his son and his grandson, until the time comes for his own land too. Then many nations and great kings will make him their slave.

But if any nation or kingdom will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon or put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish that nation with the sword, famine and plague, declares the LORD, until I have destroyed it by his hand.
So do not listen to your prophets, your diviners, your dreamers, your soothsayers or your sorcerers, who keep telling you, "You will not serve the king of Babylon."
For they are prophesying lies to you, so that you will be removed far from your land; I will drive you out, and you will perish.
But the nation that puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave on its own land, declares the LORD, to farm it and live there.'"
I spoke the same message to Zedekiah king of Judah: "Put your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon; serve him and his people, and you will live.
Why should you and your people die by the sword, famine and plague, as the LORD has spoken against any nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the words of the prophets who say to you, 'You will not serve the king of Babylon,' for they are prophesying lies to you.
I have not sent them, declares the LORD. They are prophesying falsely in my name, so that I will drive you out and you will perish, you and the prophets who prophesy to you."

Then I spoke to the priests and to all this people: "This is what the LORD says: Do not listen to the words of your prophets who prophesy to you, 'Look, the vessels of the LORD's house will very soon be brought back from Babylon,' for they are prophesying lies to you.
Do not listen to them. Serve the king of Babylon and live. Why should this city become a ruin?

If they are prophets and if the word of the LORD is with them, let them plead with the LORD of Armies that the vessels still left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem may not go to Babylon.
For this is what the LORD of Armies says about the pillars, the Sea, the stands and the rest of the vessels still left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon did not take when he carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon, along with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem:
this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about the vessels left in the house of the LORD, in the palace of the king of Judah and in Jerusalem:
They will be taken to Babylon, and there they will stay until the day I attend to them, declares the LORD. Then I will bring them up and restore them to this place."

In that same year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the fifth month of the fourth year, the prophet Hananiah son of Azzur, from Gibeon, spoke to me in the house of the LORD in the presence of the priests and all the people:
"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have broken the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Within two years I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the LORD's house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.
I will also bring back to this place Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah and all the exiles from Judah who went to Babylon, declares the LORD, for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon."
Then the prophet Jeremiah answered the prophet Hananiah in the presence of the priests and all the people who were standing in the house of the LORD.
The prophet Jeremiah said, "Amen! May the LORD do so! May the LORD fulfill the words you have prophesied, and bring back the vessels of the LORD's house and all the exiles from Babylon to this place.
But listen now to this word that I speak in your hearing and in the hearing of all the people.
The prophets who were before you and me from ancient times prophesied war, disaster and plague against many countries and great kingdoms.
As for the prophet who prophesies peace, when the word of that prophet comes true, then it will be known that the LORD has truly sent him."
Then the prophet Hananiah took the yoke bar from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah and broke it.

And Hananiah said in the presence of all the people, "This is what the LORD says: In the same way I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon from the neck of all the nations within two years." Then the prophet Jeremiah went on his way.
After the prophet Hananiah had broken the yoke bar from the neck of the prophet Jeremiah, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"Go and tell Hananiah: 'This is what the LORD says: You have broken wooden yoke bars, but you have made iron yoke bars in their place.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I have put an iron yoke on the neck of all these nations, to serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and they will serve him. I have given him even the wild animals.'"
Then the prophet Jeremiah said to the prophet Hananiah, "Listen, Hananiah! The LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to send you off the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have preached rebellion against the LORD."
And the prophet Hananiah died that same year, in the seventh month.

These are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the surviving elders of the exiles, to the priests, to the prophets and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had deported from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the officials of Judah and Jerusalem, the craftsmen and the metalworkers had left Jerusalem.
He sent it by Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. It said:
This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles whom I deported from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their produce.
Take wives and have sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons and give your daughters to husbands, so that they may bear sons and daughters. Multiply there; do not decrease.
Seek the well-being of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD for it, for in its well-being you will have well-being.
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Do not let your prophets who are among you and your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to the dreams that you dream.
For they are prophesying lies to you in my name. I did not send them, declares the LORD.
For this is what the LORD says: When seventy years are completed for Babylon, I will come to you, and I will fulfill for you my good promise to bring you back to this place.
For I know the plans I have for you, declares the LORD, plans for well-being and not for disaster, to give you a future and a hope.
Then you will call on me and come and pray to me, and I will listen to you.
You will seek me and find me, when you search for me with all your heart.

I will let myself be found by you, declares the LORD. I will restore your fortunes and gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have driven you, declares the LORD, and I will bring you back to the place from which I sent you into exile.
Because you have said, "The LORD has raised up prophets for us in Babylon,"
this is what the LORD says about the king who sits on David's throne, and about all the people who live in this city, your relatives who did not go out with you into exile:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to send against them the sword, famine and plague, and I will make them like rotten figs that are too bad to be eaten.

I will pursue them with the sword, famine and plague, and I will make them a horror to all the kingdoms of the earth, and a curse, a horror, a thing to hiss at and a disgrace among all the nations where I have driven them,
because they did not listen to my words, declares the LORD, which I sent to them through my servants the prophets, sending them again and again. But you did not listen, declares the LORD.
So you, hear the word of the LORD, all you exiles whom I sent from Jerusalem to Babylon.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says about Ahab son of Kolaiah and about Zedekiah son of Maaseiah, who are prophesying lies to you in my name: I am going to give them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will strike them down before your eyes.
Because of them all the exiles of Judah who are in Babylon will use this curse: "May the LORD make you like Zedekiah and Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire,"

because they have done an outrageous thing in Israel. They have committed adultery with their neighbors' wives, and they have spoken lies in my name, words I did not command them. I am the one who knows, and I am a witness, declares the LORD.
To Shemaiah the Nehelamite you are to say:

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Because you sent letters in your own name to all the people in Jerusalem, to Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest and to all the priests, saying,
"The LORD has made you priest in place of Jehoiada the priest, to have overseers in the house of the LORD for every madman who prophesies, to put him in the stocks and the collar.
So now, why have you not rebuked Jeremiah of Anathoth, who is prophesying to you?
For he has sent word to us in Babylon, saying, 'It will be a long time. Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their produce.'"
Zephaniah the priest read this letter in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Send to all the exiles: This is what the LORD says about Shemaiah the Nehelamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, though I did not send him, and has made you trust in a lie,

therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to punish Shemaiah the Nehelamite and his descendants. He will have no one left living among this people, and he will not see the good that I am going to do for my people, declares the LORD, for he has preached rebellion against the LORD.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Write in a scroll all the words I have spoken to you.

For look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel and Judah, says the LORD. I will bring them back to the land I gave their ancestors, and they will take possession of it.
These are the words the LORD spoke concerning Israel and Judah.
For this is what the LORD says: We have heard a cry of terror, of dread and not of peace.
Ask now, and see: can a male give birth? Why then do I see every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor? Why has every face turned deathly pale?
Woe! For that day is great; there is none like it. It is a time of distress for Jacob, yet he will be saved out of it.
On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, I will break his yoke from off your neck, and I will tear off your bonds. Foreigners will no longer make him their slave.
Instead they will serve the LORD their God and David their king, whom I will raise up for them.

As for you, do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, declares the LORD; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I am going to save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace and secure, and no one will make him afraid.

For I am with you, declares the LORD, to save you. I will make a full end of all the nations among which I have scattered you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you with justice, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
For this is what the LORD says: Your injury is incurable; your wound is beyond healing.
There is no one to plead your cause, no remedy for your sore, no new skin for you.
All your lovers have forgotten you; they do not seek you. For I have struck you as an enemy strikes, with the punishment of a cruel one, because your guilt is great and your sins are many.
Why do you cry out over your injury? Your pain is incurable. Because your guilt is great and your sins are many, I have done these things to you.
Therefore all who devour you will be devoured, and all your foes, every one of them, will go into captivity. Those who plunder you will become plunder, and all who prey on you I will give up as prey.
For I will restore you to health and heal you of your wounds, declares the LORD, because they have called you an outcast: "That is Zion; no one seeks her."

This is what the LORD says: I am going to restore the fortunes of the tents of Jacob and have compassion on his dwellings. The city will be rebuilt on its mound, and the palace will stand in its rightful place.
From them will come songs of thanksgiving and the sound of people celebrating. I will multiply them, and they will not decrease; I will bring them honor, and they will not be made small.
His children will be as they were long ago, and his community will be established before me. I will punish all who oppress him.
His leader will be one of their own, and his ruler will come out from among them. I will bring him near, and he will approach me, for who would otherwise dare to approach me? declares the LORD.
So you will be my people, and I will be your God.
Look, the storm of the LORD! Wrath has gone out, a sweeping storm. It will whirl down on the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of the LORD will not turn back until he has carried out and accomplished the purposes of his heart. In the days to come you will understand this.
At that time, declares the LORD, I will be the God of all the clans of Israel, and they will be my people.
This is what the LORD says: The people who survived the sword found favor in the wilderness, when Israel went to find its rest.
The LORD appeared to me from far away: I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you with faithful love.
Again I will build you, and you will be built, virgin Israel. Again you will take up your tambourines and go out in the dances of those who celebrate.
Again you will plant vineyards on the hills of Samaria; the planters will plant and enjoy the fruit.
For there will be a day when watchmen will call out on the hills of Ephraim, "Come, let us go up to Zion, to the LORD our God!"
For this is what the LORD says: Sing with joy for Jacob; shout for the chief of the nations. Proclaim it, give praise and say, "Save your people, LORD, the remnant of Israel!"

Look, I am going to bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the farthest parts of the earth. Among them will be the blind and the lame, the pregnant woman and the woman in labor together. A great company will return here.

They will come with weeping, and with pleas for mercy I will lead them. I will lead them beside streams of water, on a level path where they will not stumble. For I am a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn.
Hear the word of the LORD, you nations, and declare it in the coastlands far away. Say, "He who scattered Israel will gather him and watch over him as a shepherd watches over his flock."
For the LORD has ransomed Jacob and redeemed him from the hand of one stronger than he.

They will come and sing for joy on the heights of Zion, and they will be radiant over the goodness of the LORD: over the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and over the young of the flock and the herd. Their life will be like a well-watered garden, and they will never languish again.
Then young women will rejoice in the dance, and young men and old men together. I will turn their mourning into gladness; I will comfort them and give them joy in place of their sorrow.
I will satisfy the priests with abundance, and my people will be filled with my goodness, declares the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: A voice is heard in Ramah, lamentation and bitter weeping. Rachel is weeping for her children; she refuses to be comforted for her children, because they are no more.
This is what the LORD says: Keep your voice from weeping and your eyes from tears, for your work will be rewarded, declares the LORD. They will return from the land of the enemy.
There is hope for your future, declares the LORD. Your children will return to their own territory.
I have surely heard Ephraim rocking in grief: "You disciplined me, and I was disciplined, like a calf not trained to the yoke. Bring me back, so that I may come back, for you are the LORD my God.
For after I turned away, I repented; after I was made to understand, I struck my thigh. I was ashamed and humiliated, because I bore the disgrace of my youth."
Is Ephraim my dear son, my delightful child? For whenever I speak against him, I still remember him. Therefore my heart yearns for him; I will surely have compassion on him, declares the LORD.
Set up road markers for yourself; put up signposts. Set your mind on the highway, the road you traveled. Return, virgin Israel; return to these cities of yours.
How long will you waver, faithless daughter? For the LORD has created something new on the earth: a woman will surround a man.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Once more they will use these words in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I restore their fortunes: "May the LORD bless you, home of righteousness, holy mountain!"
Judah and all its cities will live there together, the farmers and those who move about with the flocks.
For I will refresh the weary and satisfy all who languish.
At this I woke up and looked, and my sleep had been sweet to me.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of human beings and the seed of animals.
Just as I watched over them to uproot and to tear down, to overthrow and to destroy and to bring disaster, so I will watch over them to build and to plant, declares the LORD.
In those days they will no longer say, "The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge."
Instead, each will die for his own guilt. Everyone who eats the sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah.

It will not be like the covenant I made with their ancestors on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, my covenant that they broke, though I was their husband, declares the LORD.

For this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, declares the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.

No longer will each one teach his neighbor and each his brother, saying, "Know the LORD," for they will all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, declares the LORD. For I will forgive their wrongdoing, and I will remember their sin no more.
This is what the LORD says, who gives the sun for light by day, and decrees the moon and the stars for light by night, who stirs up the sea so that its waves roar; the LORD of Armies is his name:
If these decrees ever depart from before me, declares the LORD, then the descendants of Israel will also cease to be a nation before me for all time.

This is what the LORD says: If the heavens above can be measured and the foundations of the earth below can be searched out, then I will also reject all the descendants of Israel for all that they have done, declares the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the city will be rebuilt for the LORD from the Tower of Hananel to the Corner Gate.
The measuring line will go out again straight ahead to the hill of Gareb, and then turn to Goah.

The whole valley of the corpses and the ashes, and all the terraces as far as the Wadi Kidron, to the corner of the Horse Gate toward the east, will be holy to the LORD. It will never again be uprooted or torn down.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar.
At that time the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was confined in the courtyard of the guard, which was in the palace of the king of Judah.

For Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'This is what the LORD says: I am going to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Babylonians, but he will certainly be given into the hand of the king of Babylon. He will speak with him face to face and see him eye to eye.
He will take Zedekiah to Babylon, and he will remain there until I attend to him, declares the LORD. Though you fight against the Babylonians, you will not succeed'?"
Jeremiah said: The word of the LORD came to me:
"Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle is going to come to you and say, 'Buy my field in Anathoth, for the right of redemption is yours to buy it.'"

Then Hanamel my cousin came to me in the courtyard of the guard, just as the LORD had said, and he said to me, "Please buy my field in Anathoth, in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession and of redemption is yours. Buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.
So I bought the field in Anathoth from Hanamel my cousin, and I weighed out the money for him, seventeen shekels of silver.
I signed the deed and sealed it, had witnesses attest it, and weighed the money on scales.
Then I took the deed of purchase, the sealed copy containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy,

and I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah in the presence of Hanamel my cousin, and of the witnesses who had signed the deed of purchase, and of all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
In their presence I charged Baruch:

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Take these documents, this deed of purchase, both the sealed copy and this open copy, and put them in a clay jar, so that they will last for a long time.
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Houses and fields and vineyards will again be bought in this land."
After I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the LORD:
"Ah, Lord GOD! You made the heavens and the earth by your great power and your outstretched arm. Nothing is too hard for you.
You show faithful love to thousands, but you repay the guilt of the fathers into the laps of their children after them. Great and mighty God, whose name is the LORD of Armies,
great in counsel and mighty in deed, your eyes are open to all the ways of human beings, to give each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds.
You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this day you have done so in Israel and among all humankind, and you have made a name for yourself, as it is today.
You brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and an outstretched arm, and with great terror.
You gave them this land, which you swore to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
They came in and took possession of it, but they did not listen to your voice or walk in your law. They did nothing of all you commanded them to do, so you have brought all this disaster on them.

Look, the siege ramps have reached the city to capture it. Because of the sword, famine and plague, the city has been given into the hand of the Babylonians who are fighting against it. What you said has happened, and now you see it.
Yet you, Lord GOD, have said to me, 'Buy the field with money and call witnesses,' though the city has been given into the hand of the Babylonians."
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Look, I am the LORD, the God of all humankind. Is anything too hard for me?
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to give this city into the hand of the Babylonians and into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

The Babylonians who are fighting against this city will come and set this city on fire and burn it, with the houses on whose roofs they have burned incense to Baal and poured out drink offerings to other gods to provoke me to anger.

For the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done nothing but evil in my eyes from their youth. The people of Israel have done nothing but provoke me to anger by the work of their hands, declares the LORD.
This city has roused my anger and my wrath from the day they built it until this day, so that I must remove it from my sight,

because of all the evil that the people of Israel and the people of Judah have done to provoke me to anger, they, their kings, their officials, their priests and their prophets, the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They have turned their backs to me and not their faces. Though I taught them again and again, they would not listen and accept discipline.
They set up their detestable idols in the house that bears my name, to defile it.

They built the high places of Baal in the Valley of Ben-hinnom, to hand over their sons and their daughters to Molech, something I did not command them, nor did it enter my mind, that they should do this detestable thing and cause Judah to sin.
Now therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says concerning this city, of which you say, "It has been given into the hand of the king of Babylon by sword, famine and plague":
I am going to gather them from all the lands where I have driven them in my anger, my wrath and great fury. I will bring them back to this place and let them live in safety.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them one heart and one way, so that they will fear me always, for their own good and the good of their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from them, but will do them good. I will put the fear of me in their hearts, so that they will not turn away from me.
I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in faithfulness, with all my heart and with all my soul.
For this is what the LORD says: Just as I have brought all this great disaster on this people, so I am going to bring on them all the good that I promise them.
Fields will again be bought in this land of which you say, "It is a desolation, without human beings or animals; it has been given into the hand of the Babylonians."

People will buy fields for money, sign deeds, seal them and call witnesses, in the land of Benjamin, in the places around Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah and in the cities of the Negev, for I will restore their fortunes, declares the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still confined in the courtyard of the guard:
This is what the LORD says, who made it, the LORD who formed it to establish it, the LORD is his name:
Call to me, and I will answer you and tell you great and hidden things that you have not known.

For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the houses of the kings of Judah that have been torn down to make defenses against the siege ramps and against the sword:

They are coming to fight the Babylonians, only to fill these houses with the corpses of the people I have struck down in my anger and my wrath, for I have hidden my face from this city because of all their evil.
Look, I am going to bring it new flesh and healing. I will heal them and reveal to them an abundance of peace and faithfulness.
I will restore the fortunes of Judah and the fortunes of Israel, and I will rebuild them as they were at first.
I will cleanse them from all the guilt of their sin against me, and I will forgive all the guilt of their sin and their rebellion against me.

This city will be to me a name of joy, a praise and a glory before all the nations of the earth, who will hear of all the good I do for them. They will fear and tremble because of all the good and all the peace that I provide for it.

This is what the LORD says: In this place, of which you say, "It is a ruin, without human beings or animals," in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem that are desolate, without human beings, without inhabitants and without animals, there will be heard again

the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the voices of those who say, "Give thanks to the LORD of Armies, for the LORD is good; his faithful love endures forever!" as they bring thank offerings to the house of the LORD. For I will restore the fortunes of the land as they were at first, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: In this place that is a ruin, without human beings or animals, and in all its cities, there will again be pasture for shepherds resting their flocks.

In the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah and in the cities of the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, in the places around Jerusalem and in the cities of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, says the LORD.
Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will fulfill the good promise I made to the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will cause a righteous Branch to sprout for David, and he will do justice and righteousness in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name by which she will be called: The LORD Is Our Righteousness.
For this is what the LORD says: David will never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel,
and the Levitical priests will never lack a man before me to offer burnt offerings, to burn grain offerings and to make sacrifices for all time.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
This is what the LORD says: If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer come at their appointed time,
then my covenant with David my servant can also be broken, so that he will have no son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the Levitical priests, my ministers.
As the host of heaven cannot be counted and the sand of the sea cannot be measured, so I will multiply the descendants of David my servant and the Levites who minister to me.
The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
Have you not seen what this people have been saying: "The two clans that the LORD chose, he has rejected"? So they despise my people, and no longer regard them as a nation.
This is what the LORD says: If I have not established my covenant with day and night, and the decrees of heaven and earth,

then I will also reject the descendants of Jacob and of David my servant, and will not choose rulers from his descendants over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. For I will restore their fortunes and have compassion on them.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army, all the kingdoms of the earth under his rule and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and all its cities:

This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: Go and speak to Zedekiah king of Judah and say to him: This is what the LORD says: I am going to give this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.

You will not escape from his hand, but you will certainly be captured and given into his hand. You will see the king of Babylon eye to eye, and he will speak with you face to face. And you will go to Babylon.
Yet hear the word of the LORD, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the LORD says about you: You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace. As they burned spices for your ancestors, the former kings who were before you, so they will burn spices for you and mourn for you, "Alas, master!" For I myself have spoken the word, declares the LORD.
Jeremiah the prophet spoke all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem,

while the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah that were left, against Lachish and against Azekah. For these were the only fortified cities left of the cities of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD after King Zedekiah had made a covenant with all the people in Jerusalem to proclaim liberty to them,
that each should set free his Hebrew slaves, male and female, so that no one would keep a fellow Judean as a slave.

All the officials and all the people who had entered into the covenant agreed that each would set free his male and female slaves and not keep them as slaves any longer. They obeyed and set them free.
But afterward they turned around and took back the male and female slaves they had set free, and forced them to be slaves again.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I made a covenant with your ancestors when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. I said,

"At the end of seven years each of you must set free his fellow Hebrew who has sold himself to you. He is to serve you six years, and then you must set him free from your service." But your ancestors did not listen to me or pay attention.
Recently you yourselves turned back and did what is right in my eyes, each of you proclaiming liberty to his neighbor. You made a covenant before me in the house that bears my name.
But then you turned back and profaned my name. Each of you took back his male and female slaves, whom you had set free to go where they wished, and you forced them to be your slaves again.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: You have not listened to me and proclaimed liberty, each to his brother and each to his neighbor. So I am going to proclaim liberty for you, declares the LORD, liberty to the sword, to plague and to famine. I will make you an object of terror to all the kingdoms of the earth.
As for the men who transgressed my covenant, who did not keep the terms of the covenant they made before me, I will make them like the calf they cut in two and passed between its pieces,
the officials of Judah and the officials of Jerusalem, the court officials, the priests and all the people of the land who passed between the pieces of the calf.
I will give them into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives. Their corpses will be food for the birds of the sky and the animals of the earth.

Zedekiah king of Judah and his officials I will give into the hand of their enemies and into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, which has withdrawn from you.

I am going to give the command, declares the LORD, and I will bring them back to this city. They will fight against it, capture it and burn it with fire. I will make the cities of Judah a desolation, with no one living in them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
"Go to the house of the Rechabites and speak with them. Bring them to the house of the LORD, into one of the rooms, and give them wine to drink."
So I took Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah son of Habazziniah, his brothers and all his sons, the whole house of the Rechabites.

I brought them into the house of the LORD, into the room of the sons of Hanan son of Igdaliah, the man of God. It was next to the room of the officials, above the room of Maaseiah son of Shallum, the keeper of the threshold.
Then I set before the men of the house of the Rechabites bowls full of wine, and cups, and I said to them, "Drink wine."
But they said, "We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our ancestor, commanded us, 'You must never drink wine, neither you nor your children.

You must not build houses, sow seed or plant vineyards, or own any of these. Instead you must live in tents all your days, so that you may live a long time in the land where you are staying as foreigners.'
