We have obeyed the voice of Jonadab son of Rechab, our ancestor, in all that he commanded us. We have not drunk wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons or our daughters,
and we have not built houses to live in. We have no vineyard or field or seed.
We have lived in tents, and we have obeyed and done everything that Jonadab our ancestor commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said, 'Come, let us go into Jerusalem to escape the army of the Babylonians and the army of the Arameans.' So we are living in Jerusalem."
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:

"This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Go and say to the people of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: 'Will you not accept discipline and listen to my words? declares the LORD.

The words of Jonadab son of Rechab, who commanded his descendants not to drink wine, have been kept. They have not drunk wine to this day, because they have obeyed their ancestor's command. But I have spoken to you again and again, and you have not listened to me.

I have sent you all my servants the prophets, sending them again and again, to say: Turn now, each of you, from his evil way, and make your deeds good. Do not follow other gods to serve them. Then you will live in the land I gave to you and your ancestors. But you did not pay attention or listen to me.
The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab have kept the command their ancestor gave them, but this people has not listened to me.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring on Judah and on all the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the disaster I have pronounced against them, because I spoke to them, but they did not listen, and I called to them, but they did not answer.'"

To the house of the Rechabites Jeremiah said, "This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Because you have obeyed the command of Jonadab your ancestor, and kept all his commands, and done everything he commanded you,
therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me for all time."
In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD:
"Take a scroll and write on it all the words I have spoken to you concerning Israel and Judah and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, in the days of Josiah, until today.
Perhaps when the house of Judah hears of all the disaster I intend to bring on them, each of them will turn from his evil way, and I will forgive their wrongdoing and their sin."
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah instructed Baruch, "I am restricted; I cannot go into the house of the LORD.

So you are to go, and on a fast day read the words of the LORD from the scroll you have written at my dictation, in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD. Read them also in the hearing of all the people of Judah who come in from their cities.
Perhaps their plea will come before the LORD, and each of them will turn from his evil way, for great is the anger and the wrath that the LORD has pronounced against this people."
Baruch son of Neriah did everything Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading the words of the LORD from the scroll in the house of the LORD.

In the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, in the ninth month, all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who had come from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem proclaimed a fast before the LORD.

Then Baruch read from the scroll the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the room of Gemariah son of Shaphan the secretary, in the upper courtyard at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the scroll,

he went down to the king's palace, into the secretary's room, and all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the secretary, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah and all the other officials.
Micaiah told them all the words he had heard when Baruch read from the scroll in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch to say, "Take in your hand the scroll you read in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
They said to him, "Sit down, please, and read it to us." So Baruch read it to them.
When they heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear, and they said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."
Then they asked Baruch, "Tell us, please, how did you write all these words at his dictation?"
Baruch said to them, "He dictated all these words to me, and I wrote them in ink on the scroll."
Then the officials said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and do not let anyone know where you are."
They went in to the king in the courtyard, after leaving the scroll in the room of Elishama the secretary, and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king.
The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the room of Elishama the secretary. Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and of all the officials who stood beside the king.
The king was sitting in the winter house, for it was the ninth month, with a fire burning in the brazier before him.

Whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with a scribe's knife and throw them into the fire in the brazier, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire in the brazier.
Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid, and they did not tear their clothes.
Even when Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
The king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel and Shelemiah son of Abdeel to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD had hidden them.
After the king had burned the scroll with the words that Baruch had written at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah:
"Take another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you are to say: 'This is what the LORD says: You burned this scroll, saying: Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will certainly come and destroy this land and wipe out from it both human beings and animals?
Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his corpse will be thrown out to the heat by day and the frost by night.

I will punish him and his descendants and his servants for their wrongdoing. I will bring on them, on the inhabitants of Jerusalem and on the people of Judah all the disaster I pronounced against them, but they did not listen.'"

So Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it at Jeremiah's dictation all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire. And many similar words were added to them.
Zedekiah son of Josiah reigned as king in place of Coniah son of Jehoiakim; Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made him king in the land of Judah.
But neither he nor his servants nor the people of the land listened to the words of the LORD that he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest to Jeremiah the prophet to say, "Please pray to the LORD our God for us."
Now Jeremiah was still coming and going among the people, for they had not yet put him in prison.
Pharaoh's army had come out of Egypt, and when the Babylonians who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah the prophet:

"This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: This is what you are to say to the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire of me: 'Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, is going back to its own land, to Egypt.
The Babylonians will come back and fight against this city. They will capture it and burn it with fire.
This is what the LORD says: Do not deceive yourselves, saying: The Babylonians will surely go away from us. For they will not go away.

Even if you were to strike down the whole army of the Babylonians who are fighting against you, and only wounded men were left among them, each in his tent, they would get up and burn this city with fire.'"
When the army of the Babylonians had withdrawn from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah set out from Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to receive his share of property there among the people.

When he reached the Benjamin Gate, a captain of the guard named Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah was there, and he arrested Jeremiah the prophet, saying, "You are deserting to the Babylonians!"
Jeremiah said, "That is a lie! I am not deserting to the Babylonians." But he would not listen to him. Irijah arrested Jeremiah and brought him to the officials.
The officials were furious with Jeremiah. They beat him and put him in prison in the house of Jonathan the secretary, for they had made it into a prison.
So Jeremiah was put into the cistern house, into the vaulted cells, and Jeremiah remained there many days.

Then King Zedekiah sent for him and had him brought, and the king questioned him secretly in his palace. He said, "Is there any word from the LORD?" Jeremiah said, "There is." And he said, "You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon."
Then Jeremiah said to King Zedekiah, "What wrong have I done to you or your servants or this people, that you have put me in prison?
Where are your prophets who prophesied to you, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
Now please listen, my lord the king. Let my plea come before you: do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the secretary, or I will die there."

So King Zedekiah gave orders, and they committed Jeremiah to the courtyard of the guard. He was given a loaf of bread each day from the bakers' street, until all the bread in the city was gone. So Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.
Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jucal son of Shelemiah and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people:
"This is what the LORD says: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, famine and plague, but whoever goes out to the Babylonians will live. He will escape with his life, and live.
This is what the LORD says: This city will certainly be given into the hand of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it."

Then the officials said to the king, "This man must be put to death, for he is discouraging the soldiers who are left in this city, and all the people, by speaking such words to them. This man is not seeking the well-being of this people, but their harm."
King Zedekiah said, "He is in your hands, for the king can do nothing against you."

So they took Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah the king's son, which was in the courtyard of the guard. They let Jeremiah down by ropes. There was no water in the cistern, only mud, and Jeremiah sank into the mud.
Ebed-melech the Cushite, an official in the king's palace, heard that they had put Jeremiah into the cistern. The king was sitting in the Benjamin Gate.
Ebed-melech went out from the king's palace and spoke to the king:

"My lord the king, these men have done evil in all they have done to Jeremiah the prophet. They have thrown him into the cistern, and he will die where he is of hunger, for there is no more bread in the city."
Then the king commanded Ebed-melech the Cushite, "Take thirty men with you from here, and pull Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies."

So Ebed-melech took the men with him and went into the king's palace, to a place under the storeroom. He took from there some worn-out rags and worn-out clothes, and let them down by ropes to Jeremiah in the cistern.
Ebed-melech the Cushite said to Jeremiah, "Put these worn-out rags and clothes under your armpits, under the ropes." Jeremiah did so.
Then they pulled Jeremiah up with the ropes and brought him out of the cistern. And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard.

King Zedekiah sent and had Jeremiah the prophet brought to him at the third entrance of the house of the LORD. The king said to Jeremiah, "I am going to ask you something. Do not hide anything from me."
Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you advice, you will not listen to me."
But King Zedekiah swore an oath to Jeremiah in secret: "As surely as the LORD lives, who has given us this life, I will not put you to death or hand you over to these men who seek your life."

Then Jeremiah said to Zedekiah, "This is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: If you surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, your life will be spared and this city will not be burned with fire; you and your household will live.

But if you do not surrender to the officials of the king of Babylon, this city will be given into the hand of the Babylonians, and they will burn it with fire, and you yourself will not escape from their hand."
King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "I am afraid of the Judeans who have deserted to the Babylonians, that I may be handed over to them and they will mistreat me."
Jeremiah said, "They will not hand you over. Please obey the voice of the LORD in what I am telling you, and it will go well with you, and your life will be spared.
But if you refuse to surrender, this is what the LORD has shown me:

All the women who are left in the palace of the king of Judah will be brought out to the officials of the king of Babylon, and they will say, 'Your trusted friends misled you and overcame you. Now that your feet are sunk in the mud, they have turned back.'

All your wives and your children will be brought out to the Babylonians, and you yourself will not escape from their hand. You will be seized by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire."
Then Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, "Let no one know about this conversation, and you will not die.

If the officials hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us what you said to the king. Do not hide it from us, and we will not put you to death. And what did the king say to you?'
then say to them, 'I was presenting my plea to the king not to send me back to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
All the officials did come to Jeremiah and question him, and he told them just what the king had commanded. So they said no more to him, for no one had heard the conversation.
And Jeremiah remained in the courtyard of the guard until the day Jerusalem was captured. This is what happened when Jerusalem was captured:
In the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army and besieged it.
In the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the city wall was broken through.

Then all the officials of the king of Babylon came in and sat in the Middle Gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samgar-nebo, Sarsechim the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag, and all the rest of the officials of the king of Babylon.

When Zedekiah king of Judah and all the soldiers saw them, they fled. They went out of the city by night by way of the king's garden, through the gate between the two walls, and he went off in the direction of the Arabah.

But the Babylonian army pursued them and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho. They captured him and brought him up to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah's sons at Riblah before his eyes, and the king of Babylon slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze shackles to take him to Babylon.
The Babylonians burned the king's palace and the houses of the people with fire, and they tore down the walls of Jerusalem.
Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard deported to Babylon the rest of the people who were left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to him, and the rest of the people who were left.
But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left in the land of Judah some of the poor people, who owned nothing, and at that time he gave them vineyards and fields.
Now Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had given orders about Jeremiah through Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard:
"Take him and look after him. Do him no harm, but do for him whatever he tells you."
So Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, Nebushazban the Rab-saris, Nergal-sharezer the Rab-mag and all the chief officers of the king of Babylon sent
and had Jeremiah taken from the courtyard of the guard. They entrusted him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, to take him home. So he stayed among the people.
While Jeremiah was still confined in the courtyard of the guard, the word of the LORD had come to him:

"Go and say to Ebed-melech the Cushite: 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to bring my words against this city for harm and not for good, and they will take place before your eyes on that day.
But I will rescue you on that day, declares the LORD, and you will not be given into the hand of the men you fear.
For I will surely save you, and you will not fall by the sword. You will escape with your life, because you have trusted in me, declares the LORD.'"

The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD, after Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had released him at Ramah. He had taken him there in chains, among all the exiles of Jerusalem and Judah who were being taken into exile to Babylon.
The commander of the guard took Jeremiah and said to him, "The LORD your God pronounced this disaster against this place.
Now the LORD has brought it about; he has done as he said. Because you people sinned against the LORD and did not obey his voice, this has happened to you.

But now, look, today I am freeing you from the chains on your hands. If you wish to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you. But if you do not wish to come with me to Babylon, then don't. See, the whole land is before you; go wherever you think good and right."

When Jeremiah still had not turned to go, he said, "Go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah, and stay with him among the people, or go wherever you think right." Then the commander of the guard gave him provisions and a gift, and let him go.
So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land.

All the commanders of the armed forces who were in the open country, they and their men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had put in his charge men, women and children, those of the poorest of the land who had not been deported to Babylon.

So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan the sons of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and Jezaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore an oath to them and their men, and he said, "Do not be afraid to serve the Babylonians. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.

As for me, I will stay at Mizpah to represent you before the Babylonians who come to us. But you, gather wine, summer fruit and oil, store them in your jars, and live in the towns you have taken over."

Likewise all the Judeans who were in Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judah, and that he had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over them.
Then all the Judeans returned from all the places where they had been scattered and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah. And they gathered wine and summer fruit in great abundance.
Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces who were in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
and said to him, "Do you know that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

Then Johanan son of Kareah said to Gedaliah in secret at Mizpah, "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and no one will know. Why should he take your life, so that all the Judeans who have gathered around you would be scattered and the remnant of Judah would perish?"
But Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for what you are saying about Ishmael is a lie."

In the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, who was of royal descent and one of the king's chief officers, came with ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah. As they were eating a meal together there at Mizpah,

Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him got up and struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword and killed him, the man the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
Ishmael also struck down all the Judeans who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and the Babylonians who were there, the soldiers.
On the day after Gedaliah was killed, before anyone knew of it,

eighty men came from Shechem, from Shiloh and from Samaria, with their beards shaved off, their clothes torn and their bodies gashed, bringing grain offerings and frankincense to present at the house of the LORD.
Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went. When he met them, he said to them, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
But when they came into the city, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the men who were with him slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern.

But there were ten men among them who said to Ishmael, "Do not kill us, for we have stores of wheat and barley, oil and honey hidden in the field." So he held back and did not kill them with their companions.

Now the cistern into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had struck down because of Gedaliah was the one King Asa had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael son of Nethaniah filled it with the slain.

Then Ishmael took captive all the rest of the people who were in Mizpah, the king's daughters and all the people who were left at Mizpah, whom Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had put in the charge of Gedaliah son of Ahikam. Ishmael son of Nethaniah took them captive and set out to cross over to the Ammonites.
When Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces who were with him heard of all the evil Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done,
they took all their men and went to fight against Ishmael son of Nethaniah. They found him by the great pool in Gibeon.
When all the people who were with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces who were with him, they were glad.
All the people Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned around and went back to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Then Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces who were with him took all the rest of the people from Mizpah whom he had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah, after Ishmael had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam: the men who were soldiers, the women, the children and the court officials whom he had brought back from Gibeon.
They went and stayed at Geruth-chimham, near Bethlehem, intending to go on into Egypt
to escape the Babylonians. They were afraid of them, because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
Then all the commanders of the armed forces, with Johanan son of Kareah and Jezaniah son of Hoshaiah, and all the people from the least to the greatest, came near
and said to Jeremiah the prophet, "Please let our plea come before you, and pray to the LORD your God for us, for all this remnant. For we are only a few left out of many, as your own eyes can see.
Pray that the LORD your God will tell us the way we should go and the thing we should do."
Jeremiah the prophet said to them, "I have heard you. I will pray to the LORD your God as you ask, and whatever the LORD answers you I will tell you. I will keep nothing back from you."
Then they said to Jeremiah, "May the LORD be a true and faithful witness against us if we do not do everything the LORD your God sends you to tell us.
Whether it is good or bad, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may go well with us when we obey the voice of the LORD our God."
At the end of ten days the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.
He called Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces who were with him, and all the people from the least to the greatest,
and said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to present your plea before him, says:
If you will stay in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down; I will plant you and not uproot you, for I relent of the disaster I have brought on you.
Do not be afraid of the king of Babylon, whom you now fear. Do not be afraid of him, declares the LORD, for I am with you to save you and to rescue you from his hand.
I will show you compassion, so that he will have compassion on you and let you return to your own land.
But if you say, 'We will not stay in this land,' and so disobey the voice of the LORD your God,
and say, 'No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war or hear the sound of the ram's horn or be hungry for bread, and there we will live,'
then hear the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: If you are determined to go to Egypt, and you go to live there,
then the sword you fear will overtake you there in the land of Egypt, and the famine you dread will follow close after you there in Egypt, and there you will die.
All the men who are determined to go to Egypt to live there will die by the sword, famine and plague. Not one of them will survive or escape the disaster I am going to bring on them.

For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: As my anger and my wrath were poured out on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my wrath will be poured out on you when you go to Egypt. You will become a curse, a horror, a curse and a disgrace, and you will never see this place again.
The LORD has spoken to you, remnant of Judah: Do not go to Egypt. Know for certain that I have warned you today
that you have gone astray at the cost of your lives. For you sent me to the LORD your God, saying, 'Pray for us to the LORD our God, and tell us whatever the LORD our God says, and we will do it.'
So I have told you today, but you have not obeyed the voice of the LORD your God in anything he has sent me to tell you.
Now know for certain that you will die by the sword, famine and plague in the place where you want to go to live."
When Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the LORD their God, all these words that the LORD their God had sent him to tell them,
Azariah son of Hoshaiah, Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men said to Jeremiah, "You are telling a lie! The LORD our God has not sent you to say, 'Do not go to Egypt to live there.'
Baruch son of Neriah is inciting you against us, to hand us over to the Babylonians, so that they will kill us or take us into exile in Babylon."
So Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the armed forces and all the people did not obey the voice of the LORD to stay in the land of Judah.

Instead, Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armed forces took the whole remnant of Judah, who had come back to live in the land of Judah from all the nations where they had been scattered:

the men, the women, the children, the king's daughters and everyone whom Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and also Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah.
They came into the land of Egypt, for they did not obey the voice of the LORD, and they went as far as Tahpanhes.
Then the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes:
"Take some large stones in your hands and bury them in the mortar of the brick pavement at the entrance of Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes, while the men of Judah watch.

Then say to them: 'This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to send for my servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and I will set his throne over these stones I have buried, and he will spread his canopy over them.
He will come and strike the land of Egypt, giving over to death those destined for death, to captivity those destined for captivity, and to the sword those destined for the sword.

I will set fire to the temples of the gods of Egypt, and he will burn them and carry their gods away captive. He will wrap himself in the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his cloak, and he will go away from there in peace.
He will smash the sacred pillars of Beth-shemesh in the land of Egypt, and he will burn the temples of the gods of Egypt with fire.'"
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Judeans living in the land of Egypt, those living at Migdol, at Tahpanhes, at Memphis and in the land of Pathros:

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You have seen all the disaster I brought on Jerusalem and on all the cities of Judah. Look, today they are a ruin, with no one living in them,
because of the evil they did to provoke me to anger, by going to burn incense and to serve other gods that they had not known, neither they, nor you, nor your ancestors.
I sent you all my servants the prophets again and again, saying, "Do not do this detestable thing that I hate!"
But they did not listen or pay attention; they did not turn from their evil and stop burning incense to other gods.
So my wrath and my anger were poured out and burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, and they became a ruin and a desolation, as they are today.

And now this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Why are you doing such great harm to yourselves, cutting off from Judah man and woman, child and infant, so that you leave yourselves no remnant?

Why do you provoke me to anger with the works of your hands, burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt where you have come to live, so that you will be cut off and become a curse and a disgrace among all the nations of the earth?

Have you forgotten the evil deeds of your ancestors, the evil deeds of the kings of Judah and the evil deeds of their wives, your own evil deeds and the evil deeds of your wives, which they committed in the land of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?
To this day they have not humbled themselves, nor have they shown fear or walked in my law and my decrees that I set before you and your ancestors.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to set my face against you for harm, to cut off all Judah.

I will take the remnant of Judah who set their faces to go to the land of Egypt to live there, and they will all come to an end. In the land of Egypt they will fall; by the sword and by famine they will come to an end. From the least to the greatest they will die by the sword and by famine. They will become a curse, a horror, a curse and a disgrace.
I will punish those who live in the land of Egypt as I punished Jerusalem, with the sword, famine and plague.

None of the remnant of Judah who have come to live in the land of Egypt will escape or survive to return to the land of Judah, where they long to return to live. For none will return except a few fugitives.

Then all the men who knew that their wives were burning incense to other gods, and all the women who stood by, a great assembly, and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in Pathros, answered Jeremiah:
"As for the word you have spoken to us in the name of the LORD, we will not listen to you.

Instead we will certainly do everything we have vowed: we will burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her, as we did, we and our ancestors, our kings and our officials, in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem. For then we had plenty of food, and we were well off and saw no disaster.
But since we stopped burning incense to the Queen of Heaven and pouring out drink offerings to her, we have lacked everything, and we have been consumed by the sword and by famine.

And when we burned incense to the Queen of Heaven and poured out drink offerings to her, was it without our husbands' consent that we made cakes for her bearing her image, and poured out drink offerings to her?"
Then Jeremiah said to all the people, to the men and the women and all the people who had given him this answer,

"As for the incense you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your ancestors, your kings, your officials and the people of the land, did not the LORD remember it? Did it not come into his mind?
The LORD could no longer bear your evil deeds and the detestable things you did. So your land became a ruin, a horror and a curse, without inhabitant, as it is today.

It is because you burned incense and sinned against the LORD, and did not obey the voice of the LORD or walk in his law, his decrees and his statutes, that this disaster has come upon you, as it is today."
Then Jeremiah said to all the people and to all the women, "Hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt.

This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled it with your hands, saying, 'We will certainly carry out the vows we have made, to burn incense to the Queen of Heaven and pour out drink offerings to her.' Go ahead then, keep your vows! Carry out your vows!

Therefore hear the word of the LORD, all you people of Judah who live in the land of Egypt: I have sworn by my great name, says the LORD, that my name will never again be invoked by any man of Judah in all the land of Egypt, saying, 'As surely as the Lord GOD lives.'
I am watching over them for harm and not for good. All the people of Judah who are in the land of Egypt will come to an end by the sword and by famine until they are all gone.

Those who escape the sword will return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. Then the whole remnant of Judah who came to the land of Egypt to live there will know whose word will stand, mine or theirs.
This will be the sign to you, declares the LORD, that I will punish you in this place, so that you will know that my words against you will surely stand for harm:

This is what the LORD says: I am going to give Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt into the hand of his enemies, into the hand of those who seek his life, just as I gave Zedekiah king of Judah into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, his enemy who sought his life."
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a scroll at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
You said, "Woe is me! For the LORD has added sorrow to my pain. I am worn out with my groaning, and I find no rest."
This is what you are to say to him: This is what the LORD says: What I have built I am tearing down, and what I have planted I am uprooting, the whole land.
And you, are you seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For I am going to bring disaster on all humankind, declares the LORD, but I will let you escape with your life wherever you go.
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

Concerning Egypt. About the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was by the Euphrates River at Carchemish, and which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah:
Prepare shield and buckler, and advance to battle!
Harness the horses; mount, you horsemen! Take your positions with helmets on! Polish the spears; put on your armor!
Why do I see them terrified, falling back? Their warriors are beaten down; they flee headlong and do not look back. Terror on every side! declares the LORD.
The swift cannot flee, nor the warrior escape. In the north, by the Euphrates River, they stumble and fall.
Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge?
Egypt rises like the Nile, like rivers whose waters surge. He says, "I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy cities and those who live in them."
Go up, you horses! Drive furiously, you chariots! Let the warriors go out: Cush and Put, who carry the shield, and the Ludim, who draw the bow.

That day belongs to the Lord GOD of Armies, a day of vengeance, to avenge himself on his foes. The sword will devour and be satisfied, and drink its fill of their blood. For the Lord GOD of Armies holds a sacrifice in the land of the north, by the Euphrates River.
Go up to Gilead and get balm, virgin daughter Egypt! In vain you have used many medicines; there is no healing for you.
The nations have heard of your shame; your cry fills the earth. For warrior has stumbled against warrior; both have fallen together.
The word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
Declare it in Egypt, proclaim it in Migdol, proclaim it in Memphis and in Tahpanhes. Say: Take your stand and get ready, for the sword devours those around you.
Why has your mighty one been swept away? He did not stand, because the LORD drove him down.
He made many stumble; they fell, each against the other. They said, "Get up, let us go back to our own people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor."
There they cried out, "Pharaoh king of Egypt is only a noise; he has let the appointed time pass by."
As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies, one will come like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea.
Pack your bags for exile, you who live there, daughter Egypt, for Memphis will become a desolation, burned and empty of inhabitants.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north has come, has come!

Even her hired soldiers in her midst are like fattened calves. They too have turned and fled together; they did not stand. For the day of their calamity has come upon them, the time of their punishment.
Her sound is like a snake slithering away, for they march on in force; they come against her with axes, like those who cut down trees.
They will cut down her forest, declares the LORD, though it cannot be searched through, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
Daughter Egypt is put to shame; she is given into the hand of the people of the north.
The LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish Amon of Thebes, and Pharaoh and Egypt, her gods and her kings, Pharaoh and those who trust in him.

I will give them into the hand of those who seek their lives, into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his servants. But afterward Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.

As for you, do not be afraid, Jacob my servant; do not be dismayed, Israel. For I am going to save you from far away, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and be at peace and secure, and no one will make him afraid.

As for you, do not be afraid, Jacob my servant, declares the LORD, for I am with you. I will make a full end of all the nations where I have driven you, but of you I will not make a full end. I will discipline you with justice, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before Pharaoh struck Gaza.

This is what the LORD says: Look, waters are rising from the north; they will become an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and everything in it, the city and those who live in it. People will cry out, and all who live in the land will wail.
At the sound of the stamping hooves of his stallions, at the rumble of his chariots and the clatter of their wheels, fathers will not turn back for their children, because their hands hang limp.
For the day is coming to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper who survives. For the LORD is destroying the Philistines, the remnant of the coastland of Caphtor.
Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is silenced. Remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?
Alas, sword of the LORD! How long until you are quiet? Go back into your sheath; rest and be still.
How can it be quiet, when the LORD has given it a command? Against Ashkelon and against the seacoast, there he has appointed it.
Concerning Moab. This is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Woe to Nebo, for it is devastated! Kiriathaim is put to shame and captured; the stronghold is put to shame and shattered.
Moab's renown is no more. In Heshbon they have planned disaster against her: "Come, let us cut her off from being a nation." You too, Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.
Listen! A cry from Horonaim: "Devastation and great destruction!"
Moab is shattered; her little ones raise a cry.
For on the ascent of Luhith they go up weeping bitterly; for on the descent to Horonaim they have heard the anguished cry of destruction.
Flee! Save your lives! Be like a juniper in the wilderness.
Because you trusted in your works and your treasures, you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into exile, together with his priests and his officials.
The destroyer will come against every city, and no city will escape. The valley will perish, and the plateau will be destroyed, as the LORD has said.
Give wings to Moab, for she will surely fly away. Her cities will become a desolation, with no one living in them.
Cursed is anyone who does the work of the LORD carelessly; cursed is anyone who keeps his sword from bloodshed!

Moab has been at ease from his youth, settled like wine on its dregs. He has not been poured from jar to jar; he has not gone into exile. So his flavor has stayed in him, and his aroma has not changed.
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send him pourers, and they will pour him out. They will empty his jars and smash his jugs.
Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, in which they trusted.
How can you say, "We are warriors, mighty men for battle"?
Moab is devastated, and his cities have been invaded; the best of his young men have gone down to the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.
Moab's calamity is near at hand; his disaster is coming quickly.
Mourn for him, all you who are around him, all who know his name. Say, "How the mighty scepter is broken, the glorious staff!"
Come down from your glory and sit on the parched ground, you who live there, daughter Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come up against you; he has ruined your strongholds.
Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer. Ask the man who flees and the woman who escapes; say, "What has happened?"
Moab is put to shame, for it is shattered. Wail and cry out! Proclaim by the Arnon that Moab is devastated.
Judgment has come to the land of the plateau: to Holon, to Jahzah and to Mephaath,
to Dibon, to Nebo and to Beth-diblathaim,
to Kiriathaim, to Beth-gamul and to Beth-meon,
to Kerioth and to Bozrah, and to all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, declares the LORD.
Make him drunk, for he has made himself great against the LORD. Let Moab wallow in his vomit, and let him also become a laughingstock.
Was not Israel a laughingstock to you? Was he caught among thieves, that whenever you spoke of him you shook your head?
Leave the cities and live among the rocks, you who live in Moab! Be like a dove that nests on the sides of the mouth of a gorge.
We have heard of the pride of Moab, how very proud he is: his loftiness, his pride, his arrogance and his haughty heart.
I know his insolence, declares the LORD, but it is empty; his boasts accomplish nothing.
Therefore I wail for Moab; for all Moab I cry out; for the men of Kir-heres one moans.

More than the weeping for Jazer I weep for you, vine of Sibmah! Your tendrils crossed over the sea; they reached as far as the sea of Jazer. On your summer fruit and on your grape harvest the destroyer has fallen.
Joy and gladness have been taken away from the orchard and from the land of Moab. I have stopped the wine from the winepresses; no one treads them with shouts of joy. The shouting is no shout of joy.
From the outcry at Heshbon as far as Elealeh, as far as Jahaz they raise their voice, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah. For even the waters of Nimrim have become desolate.
I will put an end in Moab, declares the LORD, to those who offer sacrifices on the high place and burn incense to their gods.
Therefore my heart moans for Moab like a flute; my heart moans like a flute for the men of Kir-heres. Therefore the wealth they gained has perished.
For every head is shaved bald and every beard cut off; on every hand are gashes, and around the waist is sackcloth.
On all the roofs of Moab and in its squares there is nothing but mourning, for I have broken Moab like a jar that no one wants, declares the LORD.
How it is shattered! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become a laughingstock and an object of terror to all those around him.
For this is what the LORD says: Look, one swoops down like an eagle and spreads his wings over Moab.
Kerioth is captured, and the strongholds are seized. On that day the hearts of Moab's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Moab will be destroyed and be a people no more, because he made himself great against the LORD.
Terror, pit and trap are before you, you who live in Moab, declares the LORD.

Whoever flees from the terror will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs out of the pit will be caught in the trap. For I will bring upon her, upon Moab, the year of their punishment, declares the LORD.

In the shadow of Heshbon the fugitives stand without strength. For fire has gone out from Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon. It has devoured the forehead of Moab and the skulls of the boasters.
Woe to you, Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished, for your sons have been taken into captivity, and your daughters into exile.
Yet I will restore the fortunes of Moab in the days to come, declares the LORD. Thus far the judgment on Moab.
Concerning the Ammonites. This is what the LORD says: Has Israel no sons? Has he no heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad, and why do his people live in its cities?

Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will make the battle cry heard against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a desolate mound, and its villages will be burned with fire. Then Israel will take possession of those who took possession of him, says the LORD.

Wail, Heshbon, for Ai is devastated! Cry out, daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth among the walls, for Milcom will go into exile, together with his priests and his officials.
Why do you boast of your valleys, your valley overflowing, faithless daughter, who trusted in her treasures, saying, "Who will come against me?"
I am going to bring terror on you, declares the Lord GOD of Armies, from all who are around you. You will be driven away, each one headlong, with no one to gather the fugitives.
But afterward I will restore the fortunes of the Ammonites, declares the LORD.
Concerning Edom. This is what the LORD of Armies says: Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom gone bad?
Flee, turn back, hide deep down, you who live in Dedan! For I will bring disaster on Esau, the time when I punish him.
If grape pickers came to you, they would leave no gleanings. If thieves came by night, they would destroy all they wanted.
But I have stripped Esau bare; I have uncovered his hiding places, and he cannot hide himself. His offspring are destroyed, his brothers and his neighbors, and he is no more.
Leave your orphans; I will keep them alive. Let your widows trust in me.
For this is what the LORD says: If those who did not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, will you go unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you will surely drink it.
For I have sworn by myself, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a horror, a disgrace, a ruin and a curse, and all her cities will be ruins forever.
I have heard a report from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Gather together and come against her; rise up for battle!"
For look, I will make you small among the nations, despised among human beings.

The terror you inspire and the pride of your heart have deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, who hold the height of the hill. Though you build your nest as high as the eagle's, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
Edom will become a horror; everyone who passes by it will be appalled and hiss at all its wounds.
As when Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors were overthrown, says the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will stay in it.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to a pasture that is always green, I will suddenly chase them from it, and I will appoint over it whoever is chosen. For who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Edom, and the purposes he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
At the sound of their fall the earth quakes; their cry is heard at the Red Sea.
Look, like an eagle he will rise and swoop down and spread his wings over Bozrah. On that day the hearts of Edom's warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They melt in fear; there is anxiety like the sea, which cannot be calm.
Damascus has grown weak; she has turned to flee, and panic has seized her. Distress and pangs have gripped her like a woman in labor.
How is it that the city of praise has not been abandoned, the town of my joy?
Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD of Armies.
I will set fire to the wall of Damascus, and it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.
Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck down. This is what the LORD says: Rise up, go up against Kedar, and destroy the people of the east.
Their tents and their flocks will be taken, their tent curtains and all their goods; their camels will be carried off from them. People will shout to them, "Terror on every side!"
Flee, wander far away, hide deep down, you who live in Hazor, declares the LORD. For Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has made a plan against you; he has formed a purpose against you.
Rise up, go up against a nation at ease, that lives in security, declares the LORD, that has no gates or bars; they live alone.

Their camels will become plunder, and their great herds spoil. I will scatter to every wind those who clip the hair at their temples, and I will bring disaster on them from every side, declares the LORD.
Hazor will become a haunt of jackals, a desolation forever. No one will live there; no human being will stay in it.
The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to break the bow of Elam, the mainstay of their might.
I will bring against Elam the four winds from the four ends of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will be no nation to which the outcasts of Elam will not come.

I will shatter Elam before their enemies, before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster on them, my fierce anger, declares the LORD. I will send the sword after them until I have made an end of them.
I will set my throne in Elam and destroy from there its king and officials, declares the LORD.
But in the days to come I will restore the fortunes of Elam, declares the LORD.
The word that the LORD spoke concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Babylonians, through Jeremiah the prophet:

Declare it among the nations and proclaim it; raise a signal flag and proclaim it; hide nothing. Say: Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered. Her images are put to shame; her idols are shattered.
For a nation from the north has come up against her; it will make her land a desolation, and no one will live in it. Both human beings and animals have fled; they are gone.
In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the people of Israel will come, they and the people of Judah together. They will come weeping as they go, and they will seek the LORD their God.
They will ask the way to Zion, with their faces turned toward it: "Come, let us join ourselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten."
My people have been lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray, making them roam on the mountains. They have wandered from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
All who found them have devoured them, and their foes have said, "We are not guilty, because they sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their ancestors."
Flee from the midst of Babylon; go out from the land of the Babylonians, and be like male goats that go before the flock.

For look, I am stirring up and bringing against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will draw up their lines against her; from there she will be captured. Their arrows are like those of a skilled warrior who does not return empty-handed.
Babylonia will become plunder; all who plunder her will be satisfied, declares the LORD.
Though you rejoice, though you exult, you who plunder my inheritance, though you frisk about like a heifer threshing grain and neigh like stallions,
your mother will be greatly ashamed; she who bore you will be disgraced. Look, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land and a desert.
Because of the wrath of the LORD she will not be inhabited, but will be completely desolate. Everyone who passes by Babylon will be appalled and hiss at all her wounds.
Draw up your lines around Babylon, all you who bend the bow! Shoot at her; spare no arrows, for she has sinned against the LORD.

Raise the battle cry against her on every side! She has surrendered; her towers have fallen; her walls are torn down. For this is the vengeance of the LORD. Take vengeance on her; do to her as she has done.

Cut off from Babylon the sower and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. Because of the sword of the oppressor, they will each turn back to their own people; they will each flee to their own land.
Israel is a scattered sheep, chased away by lions. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and now at the last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has gnawed his bones.
Therefore this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: I am going to punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I punished the king of Assyria.
I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and in Bashan, and his appetite will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, search will be made for Israel's guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah's sins, but none will be found, for I will forgive those I leave as a remnant.
Go up against the land of Merathaim, against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod. Put them to the sword and devote them to destruction, declares the LORD; do all that I have commanded you.
The noise of battle is in the land, and great destruction!
How the hammer of the whole earth is cut down and broken! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
I set a trap for you, Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and seized, because you challenged the LORD.
The LORD has opened his armory and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for the Lord GOD of Armies has work to do in the land of the Babylonians.
Come against her from every side; open her granaries; pile her up like heaps of grain and devote her to destruction. Let her have no remnant left.
Put all her young bulls to the sword; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, the time of their punishment.
Listen! Fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon are declaring in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, vengeance for his temple.

Summon archers against Babylon, all who bend the bow. Camp all around her; let none of hers escape. Repay her for her deeds; do to her just as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
Therefore her young men will fall in her squares, and all her soldiers will be silenced on that day, declares the LORD.
Look, I am against you, Arrogant One, declares the Lord GOD of Armies, for your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
The Arrogant One will stumble and fall, with no one to raise him up. I will set fire to his cities, and it will consume everything around him.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: The people of Israel are oppressed, and the people of Judah with them. All who took them captive hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.
But their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Armies is his name. He will surely plead their cause, so that he may give rest to the earth, but unrest to the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword against the Babylonians, declares the LORD, and against the inhabitants of Babylon, against her officials and against her wise men!
A sword against her false prophets, and they will become fools! A sword against her warriors, and they will be shattered!
A sword against his horses and his chariots, and against all the foreign troops in her midst, and they will become like women! A sword against her treasures, and they will be plundered!
A drought on her waters, and they will dry up! For it is a land of idols, and they go mad over their terrifying images.
Therefore desert creatures will live there with hyenas, and ostriches will live in her. She will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors, declares the LORD, no one will live there; no human being will stay in it.
Look, a people is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are being stirred up from the farthest parts of the earth.
They grasp bow and javelin; they are cruel and show no mercy. Their sound is like the roaring sea; they ride on horses, drawn up like warriors for battle against you, daughter Babylon.
The king of Babylon has heard the report of them, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor.

Look, like a lion coming up from the thickets of the Jordan to a pasture that is always green, I will suddenly chase them from it, and I will appoint over it whoever is chosen. For who is like me? Who can summon me? What shepherd can stand before me?

Therefore hear the plan that the LORD has made against Babylon, and the purposes he has formed against the land of the Babylonians: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; surely the pasture will be made desolate because of them.
At the sound of Babylon's capture the earth quakes, and a cry is heard among the nations.
This is what the LORD says: I am going to stir up a destroying wind against Babylon and against the people who live in Leb-kamai.
I will send foreigners to Babylon, and they will winnow her and empty her land, for they will come against her from every side on the day of disaster.
Against the archer let the archer bend his bow, and against the one who stands up in his armor. Do not spare her young men; devote her whole army to destruction.
They will fall slain in the land of the Babylonians, pierced through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed by their God, by the LORD of Armies, though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon! Save your lives, each of you! Do not be destroyed because of her guilt. For this is the time of the LORD's vengeance; he is repaying her what she deserves.
Babylon was a golden cup in the LORD's hand, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad.
Suddenly Babylon has fallen and is shattered. Wail for her! Get balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
"We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Leave her, and let us each go to our own land, for her judgment reaches to the heavens and rises as high as the clouds.
The LORD has brought our vindication to light. Come, let us tell in Zion the work of the LORD our God."

Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because his purpose is to destroy Babylon. For this is the vengeance of the LORD, vengeance for his temple.

Raise a signal flag against the walls of Babylon! Strengthen the watch; post the watchmen; prepare the ambushes! For the LORD has both planned and done what he spoke concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who live by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the measure of your life is cut off.
The LORD of Armies has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with people like a swarm of locusts, and they will raise the shout of victory over you.
He made the earth by his power; he established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
When he thunders, there is a roar of waters in the heavens; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth. He makes lightning for the rain, and brings out the wind from his storehouses.
Every human being is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol. For his cast images are a lie; there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work of mockery. At the time of their punishment they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the maker of all things, and of the tribe that is his inheritance. The LORD of Armies is his name.
You are my war club, my weapon for battle: with you I shatter nations; with you I destroy kingdoms;
with you I shatter the horse and its rider; with you I shatter the chariot and its driver;
with you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter the old and the young; with you I shatter the young man and the young woman;
with you I shatter the shepherd and his flock; with you I shatter the farmer and his team; with you I shatter governors and deputies.
I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Babylonia for all the evil they have done in Zion before your eyes, declares the LORD.

Look, I am against you, destroying mountain, declares the LORD, you who destroy the whole earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the cliffs and make you a burned-out mountain.
No stone will be taken from you for a cornerstone, nor any stone for a foundation, for you will be desolate forever, declares the LORD.

Raise a signal flag in the land! Blow the ram's horn among the nations! Prepare the nations for war against her; summon against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni and Ashkenaz. Appoint a commander against her; bring up horses like bristling locusts.
Prepare the nations for war against her, the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their deputies, and every land under their rule.
The earth quakes and writhes, for the LORD's purposes against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a desolation, with no one living in it.
Babylon's warriors have stopped fighting; they stay in their strongholds. Their strength has failed; they have become like women. Her dwellings are set on fire; the bars of her gates are broken.
Runner runs to meet runner, and messenger to meet messenger, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end,
the fords have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified.
For this is what the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, says: Daughter Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trodden; in a little while the time of her harvest will come.

"Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has crushed me; he has set me down like an empty jar. He has swallowed me like a sea monster; he has filled his belly with my delicacies and rinsed me out."
"May the violence done to me and to my flesh be on Babylon," the people of Zion will say. "May my blood be on the inhabitants of Babylonia," Jerusalem will say.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: I am going to plead your cause and take vengeance for you. I will dry up her sea and make her spring run dry.
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, a horror and a thing to hiss at, with no one living there.
They roar together like young lions; they growl like lion cubs.
While they are heated, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they celebrate, then sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake, declares the LORD.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
How Sheshach is captured, the praise of the whole earth seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon; she is covered with its roaring waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry land and a desert, a land where no one lives, through which no human being passes.
I will punish Bel in Babylon and make him spit out what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him. Even the wall of Babylon has fallen.
Go out from her midst, my people! Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD!
Do not lose heart or be afraid at the rumors heard in the land, when one rumor comes this year and another the next, with violence in the land and ruler against ruler.
Therefore, look, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall in her midst.
Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for the destroyers will come against her from the north, declares the LORD.
Babylon must fall because of the slain of Israel, as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go! Do not stand still! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to your mind.
"We are ashamed, for we have heard insults; disgrace has covered our faces, for foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD's house."
Therefore, look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
Though Babylon should climb to the heavens, and though she should fortify her lofty stronghold, destroyers will come against her from me, declares the LORD.
Listen! A cry from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Babylonians!
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and silencing her great noise. Their waves roar like many waters; the sound of their voice resounds.
For a destroyer has come against her, against Babylon. Her warriors are captured; their bows are shattered. For the LORD is a God of retribution; he will surely repay.
I will make her officials and her wise men drunk, her governors, her deputies and her warriors; they will sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Armies.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: The thick wall of Babylon will be leveled to the ground, and her high gates set on fire. The peoples exhaust themselves for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the fire.

This is the command that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
Jeremiah had written on one scroll all the disaster that would come on Babylon, all these words that are written concerning Babylon.
Jeremiah said to Seraiah, "When you come to Babylon, see that you read all these words aloud.
Then say, 'LORD, you have said concerning this place that you will cut it off, so that no one will live in it, neither human beings nor animals, for it will be desolate forever.'
When you finish reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates.
Then say, 'So will Babylon sink and never rise again, because of the disaster I am going to bring on her. And they will grow weary.'" Thus far the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done.
For it was because of the LORD's anger that all this happened to Jerusalem and Judah, until he cast them out of his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

So in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem with his whole army. They camped against it, and they built siege works all around it.
The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine in the city was so severe that there was no food for the people of the land.

Then the city wall was broken through, and all the soldiers fled and went out of the city by night by way of the gate between the two walls, near the king's garden, though the Babylonians were all around the city. They went off in the direction of the Arabah.
But the Babylonian army pursued the king and overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and all his army was scattered from him.
They captured the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed sentence on him.
The king of Babylon slaughtered Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, and he also slaughtered all the officials of Judah at Riblah.
Then he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in bronze shackles, and the king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in prison until the day of his death.

In the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, which was the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
He burned the house of the LORD, the king's palace and all the houses of Jerusalem. Every great house he burned with fire.
The whole Babylonian army that was with the commander of the guard tore down all the walls around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard deported some of the poorest of the people, the rest of the people who were left in the city, the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the craftsmen.
But Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard left some of the poorest people of the land to work the vineyards and the fields.
The Babylonians broke up the bronze pillars that belonged to the house of the LORD, and the stands and the bronze Sea that were in the house of the LORD, and they carried all the bronze to Babylon.
They also took away the pots, the shovels, the wick trimmers, the sprinkling bowls, the dishes and all the bronze articles used in the temple service.

The commander of the guard took away the basins, the firepans, the sprinkling bowls, the pots, the lampstands, the dishes and the bowls for drink offerings, whatever was made of gold and whatever was made of silver.

As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the twelve bronze bulls that were under the stands, which King Solomon had made for the house of the LORD, the bronze of all these articles was beyond weighing.
As for the pillars, each pillar was eighteen cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits went around it. It was four fingers thick, and hollow.
The bronze capital on top of it was five cubits high, with a network and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its pomegranates, was the same.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on the sides; all the pomegranates around the network numbered a hundred.
The commander of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest and the three doorkeepers.

From the city he took an official who was in charge of the soldiers, and seven of the king's advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.
Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
The king of Babylon struck them down and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.
These are the people whom Nebuchadnezzar deported: in the seventh year, 3,023 Judeans;
in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, 832 people from Jerusalem;
in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the commander of the guard deported 745 Judeans. In all there were 4,600 people.

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-fifth day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and brought him out of prison.
He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.
So Jehoiachin took off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he regularly ate at the king's table.
As for his allowance, a regular allowance was given him by the king of Babylon, a portion for each day, until the day of his death, for as long as he lived.
How lonely sits the city that was full of people! She has become like a widow, she who was great among the nations. The princess among the provinces has been put to forced labor.
She weeps bitterly in the night, with tears on her cheeks. Among all her lovers she has no one to comfort her. All her friends have betrayed her; they have become her enemies.
Judah has gone into exile after affliction and harsh servitude. She lives among the nations, but finds no resting place. All her pursuers have overtaken her in the narrow places.
The roads to Zion mourn, for no one comes to the festivals. All her gates are desolate; her priests groan; her young women grieve, and she herself is in bitterness.
Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease. For the LORD has made her suffer for her many rebellions. Her little children have gone into captivity before the foe.
All her splendor has departed from Daughter Zion. Her princes have become like deer that find no pasture; they have gone on without strength before the pursuer.

In the days of her affliction and her homelessness, Jerusalem remembers all the precious things that were hers in days of old. When her people fell into the hand of the foe, and there was no one to help her, the foes looked at her; they laughed at her ruin.
Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become a thing to scorn. All who honored her despise her, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away.
Her uncleanness is in her skirts; she did not consider her end. Her fall was astonishing; there is no one to comfort her. Look, LORD, at my affliction, for the enemy has triumphed!
The foe has stretched out his hand over all her precious things; for she has seen the nations enter her sanctuary, those you commanded not to enter your assembly.
All her people groan as they search for bread; they give their treasures for food to keep themselves alive. Look, LORD, and see, for I am despised.
Is it nothing to you, all you who pass by on the road? Look and see if there is any pain like my pain, which was dealt out to me, which the LORD inflicted on the day of his burning anger.
From on high he sent fire into my bones, and it overcame them. He spread a net for my feet; he turned me back. He has made me desolate, sick all day long.

The yoke of my rebellions has been bound on; by his hand they were woven together. They have come up on my neck; he has made my strength fail. The Lord has given me into the hands of those I cannot withstand.
The Lord has rejected all my mighty men in my midst; he has called an assembly against me to crush my young men. The Lord has trodden Virgin Daughter Judah as in a winepress.
For these things I weep; my eye, my eye runs down with water, for a comforter is far from me, one to revive my soul. My children are desolate, for the enemy has prevailed.
Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her. The LORD has commanded against Jacob that his neighbors should be his foes. Jerusalem has become an unclean thing among them.
The LORD is in the right, for I rebelled against his word. Hear now, all peoples, and see my pain! My young women and my young men have gone into captivity.
I called to my lovers, but they deceived me. My priests and my elders perished in the city as they searched for food to keep themselves alive.
Look, LORD, for I am in distress! My insides churn; my heart is overturned within me, for I have been very rebellious. Outside, the sword bereaves; inside, there is death.

They have heard that I groan; there is no one to comfort me. All my enemies have heard of my trouble; they rejoice that you have done it. Bring on the day you have announced, and let them become like me.
Let all their evil come before you, and deal with them as you have dealt with me because of all my rebellions. For my groans are many, and my heart is faint.
How the Lord in his anger has covered Daughter Zion with a cloud! He has thrown down from heaven to earth the splendor of Israel; he has not remembered his footstool in the day of his anger.

The Lord has swallowed up without pity all the dwellings of Jacob. In his fury he has torn down the strongholds of Daughter Judah; he has brought them down to the ground. He has profaned the kingdom and its princes.
