In his burning anger he has cut off every horn of Israel. He has drawn back his right hand in the face of the enemy. He has burned against Jacob like a flaming fire that consumes all around.
He has bent his bow like an enemy; his right hand is set like a foe's. He has killed all who were pleasing to the eye. On the tent of Daughter Zion he has poured out his wrath like fire.
The Lord has become like an enemy; he has swallowed up Israel. He has swallowed up all her palaces; he has destroyed his strongholds. He has multiplied mourning and moaning in Daughter Judah.
He has wrecked his booth like a garden; he has destroyed his place of meeting. The LORD has made Zion forget festival and Sabbath, and in his fierce anger he has spurned king and priest.
The Lord has rejected his altar and disowned his sanctuary. He has handed over to the enemy the walls of her palaces. They raised a shout in the house of the LORD as on a festival day.
The LORD determined to destroy the wall of Daughter Zion. He stretched out the measuring line; he did not hold back his hand from destroying. He made rampart and wall lament; together they languish.
Her gates have sunk into the ground; he has ruined and broken her bars. Her king and her princes are among the nations; there is no instruction, and her prophets find no vision from the LORD.
The elders of Daughter Zion sit on the ground in silence. They have thrown dust on their heads and put on sackcloth. The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads to the ground.
My eyes are worn out with tears; my insides churn. My heart is poured out on the ground because of the destruction of my dear people, because children and infants faint in the streets of the city.
They say to their mothers, "Where is the grain and the wine?" as they faint like the wounded in the streets of the city, as their life is poured out on their mothers' laps.
What can I say for you? To what can I compare you, Daughter Jerusalem? What can I liken to you, to comfort you, Virgin Daughter Zion? For your ruin is as vast as the sea; who can heal you?
Your prophets have seen for you visions that were empty and false; they did not expose your guilt to restore your fortunes. They have seen for you oracles that were empty and misleading.
All who pass along the road clap their hands at you. They hiss and shake their heads at Daughter Jerusalem: "Is this the city that was called the perfection of beauty, the joy of all the earth?"
All your enemies open their mouths against you; they hiss and grind their teeth. They say, "We have swallowed her up! Ah, this is the day we hoped for; we have found it, we have seen it!"

The LORD has done what he planned; he has carried out his word, which he commanded in days of old. He has torn down without pity; he has let the enemy rejoice over you; he has raised up the horn of your foes.
Their heart cried out to the Lord. O wall of Daughter Zion, let your tears run down like a torrent day and night! Give yourself no relief; do not let your eyes rest.

Arise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the night watches! Pour out your heart like water before the face of the Lord. Lift up your hands to him for the lives of your children, who faint with hunger at the head of every street.
Look, LORD, and consider: to whom have you done this? Should women eat their offspring, the children they have cared for? Should priest and prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?
Young and old lie on the ground in the streets; my young women and my young men have fallen by the sword. You have killed them on the day of your anger; you have slaughtered without pity.
You summoned, as for a festival day, my terrors from all around. On the day of the LORD's anger, no one escaped or survived. Those I cared for and raised, my enemy has destroyed.
I am the man who has seen affliction under the rod of his wrath.
He has driven me away and made me walk in darkness, not light.
Surely against me he turns his hand again and again, all day long.
He has worn away my flesh and my skin; he has broken my bones.
He has besieged me and surrounded me with bitterness and hardship.
He has made me live in dark places, like those long dead.
He has walled me in so that I cannot get out; he has made my chains heavy.
Though I call out and cry for help, he shuts out my prayer.
He has walled up my ways with hewn stone; he has made my paths crooked.
He is to me a bear lying in wait, a lion in hiding.
He has turned aside my ways and torn me to pieces; he has made me desolate.
He bent his bow and set me up as a target for his arrow.
He has shot into my heart the arrows of his quiver.
I have become a laughingstock to all my people, their mocking song all day long.
He has filled me with bitter herbs; he has made me drink my fill of wormwood.
He has broken my teeth with gravel; he has pressed me down in the ashes.
My soul has been rejected from peace; I have forgotten what good is.
So I said, "My strength has perished, and my hope from the LORD."
Remember my affliction and my homelessness, the wormwood and the bitterness.
My soul remembers it continually and is bowed down within me.
But this I call to mind, and therefore I have hope:
Because of the LORD's faithful love we are not finished, for his compassion does not fail.
It is new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
"The LORD is my portion," says my soul, "therefore I will hope in him."
The LORD is good to those who wait for him, to the soul who seeks him.
It is good to wait in silence for the salvation of the LORD.
It is good for a man to bear the yoke in his youth.
Let him sit alone in silence, for he has laid it on him.
Let him put his mouth in the dust; perhaps there may yet be hope.
Let him offer his cheek to the one who strikes him; let him be filled with disgrace.
For the Lord will not reject forever.
Though he brings grief, he will have compassion according to the greatness of his faithful love.
For he does not afflict willingly, or bring grief to human beings.
To crush underfoot all the prisoners of the land,
to deny a man his rights before the Most High,
to wrong a person in his lawsuit: the Lord does not approve.
Who has spoken and it came to pass, unless the Lord has commanded it?
Is it not from the mouth of the Most High that both evil and good come?
Why should any living person complain, any man, about his sins?
Let us search and examine our ways, and return to the LORD.
Let us lift up our hearts with our hands to God in heaven:
We have rebelled and disobeyed, and you have not forgiven.
You have wrapped yourself in anger and pursued us; you have killed without pity.
You have wrapped yourself in a cloud, so that no prayer can pass through.
You have made us scum and refuse among the peoples.
All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
Panic and pit have come upon us, devastation and destruction.
My eye runs down with streams of water because of the destruction of my dear people.
My eye flows and does not stop, without any rest,
until the LORD looks down from heaven and sees.
My eye brings grief to my soul because of all the daughters of my city.
Those who are my enemies without cause have hunted me down like a bird.
They tried to end my life in a pit, and they threw stones at me.
Water flowed over my head; I said, "I am cut off!"
I called on your name, LORD, from the depths of the pit.
You heard my voice; do not close your ear to my cry for relief, to my cry for help!
You came near on the day I called to you; you said, "Do not fear!"
You have taken up my case, Lord; you have redeemed my life.
You have seen the wrong done to me, LORD; judge my case!
You have seen all their vengeance, all their plots against me.
You have heard their taunts, LORD, all their plots against me,
the lips of those who rise against me, and their muttering against me all day long.
Look at them, sitting or standing: I am their mocking song.
Pay them back, LORD, according to the work of their hands.
Give them a hardened heart; may your curse be on them!
Pursue them in anger and destroy them from under the heavens of the LORD.
How the gold has grown dim, how the pure gold has changed! The holy stones lie scattered at the head of every street.
The precious children of Zion, worth their weight in fine gold, how they are regarded as clay jars, the work of a potter's hands!
Even jackals offer the breast and nurse their young, but my dear people has become cruel, like ostriches in the wilderness.
The tongue of the nursing infant sticks to the roof of its mouth for thirst. Little children ask for bread, but no one breaks it for them.
Those who used to eat delicacies are desolate in the streets. Those brought up in scarlet now cling to ash heaps.
The punishment of my dear people is greater than the punishment of Sodom, which was overthrown in a moment, with no hand laid on it.
Her princes were purer than snow, whiter than milk; their bodies were ruddier than coral, their form like sapphire.
Now their appearance is blacker than soot; they are not recognized in the streets. Their skin has shriveled on their bones; it has become as dry as wood.
Better off were those killed by the sword than those killed by hunger, who waste away, pierced through by the lack of the produce of the field.
The hands of compassionate women have boiled their own children; they became their food in the destruction of my dear people.
The LORD has spent his wrath; he has poured out his burning anger. He has kindled a fire in Zion, and it has consumed her foundations.
The kings of the earth did not believe, nor did any of the inhabitants of the world, that foe and enemy could enter the gates of Jerusalem.
It happened because of the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests, who shed in her midst the blood of the righteous.
They wandered blind through the streets, so defiled with blood that no one could touch their garments.
"Go away! Unclean!" people cried to them. "Go away, go away! Do not touch!" So they fled and wandered, and people among the nations said, "They shall not stay here any longer."
The LORD himself has scattered them; he will no longer look on them. No one showed respect to the priests, or favor to the elders.
Our eyes still wear themselves out, looking in vain for help. From our watchtower we watched for a nation that could not save us.
They dogged our steps so that we could not walk in our streets. Our end drew near; our days were numbered, for our end had come.
Our pursuers were swifter than the eagles in the sky. They chased us on the mountains; they lay in wait for us in the wilderness.
The breath of our nostrils, the LORD's anointed, was caught in their pits, the one of whom we said, "Under his shadow we will live among the nations."
Rejoice and be glad, Daughter Edom, you who live in the land of Uz! To you also the cup will pass; you will become drunk and strip yourself naked.
Your punishment is complete, Daughter Zion; he will not keep you in exile any longer. But he will punish your iniquity, Daughter Edom; he will expose your sins.
Remember, LORD, what has happened to us; look and see our disgrace.
Our inheritance has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners.
We have become orphans, without a father; our mothers are like widows.
We must pay silver for the water we drink; our wood comes to us at a price.
Our pursuers are at our necks; we are weary and are given no rest.
We have given our hand to Egypt, and to Assyria, to get enough bread.
Our ancestors sinned and are no more, and we bear their iniquities.
Slaves rule over us; there is no one to rescue us from their hand.
We get our bread at the risk of our lives, because of the sword in the wilderness.
Our skin is hot as an oven from the burning heat of hunger.
Women have been raped in Zion, young women in the towns of Judah.
Princes have been hung up by their hands; elders are shown no respect.
Young men carry the millstone, and boys stagger under loads of wood.
The elders have left the city gate; the young men have stopped their music.
The joy of our hearts has ceased; our dancing has turned to mourning.
The crown has fallen from our head. Woe to us, for we have sinned!
Because of this our heart is faint; because of these things our eyes have grown dim:
because Mount Zion lies desolate, with foxes prowling over it.
But you, LORD, reign forever; your throne endures from generation to generation.
Why do you forget us forever? Why do you forsake us for so long?
Bring us back to you, LORD, so that we may return; renew our days as of old,
unless you have utterly rejected us, and are angry with us beyond measure.
In the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, while I was among the exiles by the river Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.
On the fifth day of the month, in the fifth year of the exile of King Jehoiachin,
the word of the LORD came to Ezekiel son of Buzi, the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chebar, and the hand of the LORD came on him there.

I looked, and I saw a storm wind coming from the north: a great cloud, with fire flashing, and brightness all around it. In the middle of it, in the middle of the fire, was something like the gleam of amber.
In the middle of it was the likeness of four living creatures. This was their appearance: they had a human form.
Each had four faces, and each of them had four wings.
Their legs were straight, and the soles of their feet were like the sole of a calf's foot. They gleamed like the gleam of polished bronze.
Under their wings on their four sides they had human hands. As for the faces and the wings of the four of them,
their wings touched one another. They did not turn as they went; each of them went straight ahead.

The likeness of their faces was this: each had the face of a human being; the four of them had the face of a lion on the right side; the four of them had the face of an ox on the left side; and the four of them had the face of an eagle.
Such were their faces. Their wings were spread out above. Each had two wings touching those of another, and two covering their bodies.
Each of them went straight ahead. Wherever the spirit would go, they went. They did not turn as they went.

As for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like burning coals of fire, like the appearance of torches. Fire moved back and forth among the living creatures. The fire was bright, and lightning came out of the fire.
The living creatures darted back and forth like the appearance of a flash of lightning.
As I looked at the living creatures, I saw a wheel on the ground beside the living creatures, one for each of their four faces.

The appearance of the wheels and the way they were made was like the gleam of beryl, and the four of them had the same likeness. Their appearance and the way they were made were like a wheel within a wheel.
When they went, they went in any of their four directions; they did not turn as they went.
As for their rims, they were high and awesome, and the rims of all four were full of eyes all around.
When the living creatures went, the wheels went beside them, and when the living creatures rose from the ground, the wheels rose.
Wherever the spirit would go, they went, wherever the spirit would go, and the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.

When they went, the wheels went; when they stood still, the wheels stood still; and when they rose from the ground, the wheels rose along with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in the wheels.
Over the heads of the living creatures there was the likeness of a dome, gleaming like awesome crystal, spread out over their heads above.
Under the dome their wings were stretched out straight, one toward another. Each of them had two wings that covered it; each of them had two that covered their bodies.

When they went, I heard the sound of their wings, like the sound of many waters, like the voice of the Almighty, a sound of tumult like the noise of an army camp. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.
And there came a voice from above the dome that was over their heads. When they stood still, they let their wings drop.

Above the dome that was over their heads was something that looked like lapis lazuli, in the likeness of a throne, and on the likeness of the throne, high above it, was a likeness with the appearance of a human being.

I saw that from what looked like his waist upward he was like the gleam of amber, like the appearance of fire enclosed all around; and from what looked like his waist downward I saw something like the appearance of fire, and there was brightness all around him.

Like the appearance of the rainbow in the clouds on a day of rain, so was the appearance of the brightness all around. This was the appearance of the likeness of the glory of the LORD. When I saw it, I fell on my face, and I heard the voice of someone speaking.
He said to me, "Son of man, stand on your feet, and I will speak with you."
As he spoke to me, the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet, and I heard him speaking to me.
He said to me, "Son of man, I am sending you to the Israelites, to rebellious nations that have rebelled against me. They and their ancestors have revolted against me to this very day.
The children are hard-faced and stubborn-hearted. I am sending you to them, and you are to say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.'
And whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are a rebellious house, they will know that a prophet has been among them.

And you, son of man, do not be afraid of them or of their words, though briers and thorns are all around you and you live among scorpions. Do not be afraid of their words, and do not be terrified by their looks, for they are a rebellious house.
You are to speak my words to them, whether they listen or refuse to listen, for they are rebellious.
But you, son of man, listen to what I am saying to you. Do not be rebellious like that rebellious house. Open your mouth and eat what I am giving you."
Then I looked, and I saw a hand stretched out to me, and in it was a scroll.
He spread it out in front of me. It had writing on the front and on the back, and written on it were laments, mourning and woe.
He said to me, "Son of man, eat what you find. Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel."
So I opened my mouth, and he fed me this scroll.
He said to me, "Son of man, feed your stomach and fill your belly with this scroll that I am giving you." So I ate it, and in my mouth it was as sweet as honey.
He said to me, "Son of man, go to the house of Israel and speak my words to them.
For you are not being sent to a people of strange speech and difficult language, but to the house of Israel,
not to many peoples of strange speech and difficult language, whose words you cannot understand. Surely, if I sent you to them, they would listen to you.
But the house of Israel will not be willing to listen to you, for they are not willing to listen to me. For the whole house of Israel is hard-headed and stubborn-hearted.
Look, I have made your face as hard as their faces, and your forehead as hard as their foreheads.
I have made your forehead like diamond, harder than flint. Do not be afraid of them, and do not be terrified by their looks, for they are a rebellious house."
He said to me, "Son of man, take to heart all my words that I speak to you, and listen with your ears.
Go to the exiles, to your own people, and speak to them. Say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says,' whether they listen or refuse to listen."
Then the Spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rumbling: "Blessed be the glory of the LORD from his place!"
It was the sound of the wings of the living creatures brushing against one another, and the sound of the wheels beside them, the sound of a great rumbling.
The Spirit lifted me up and took me away, and I went in bitterness, my spirit burning, and the hand of the LORD was strong on me.
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib, who lived by the river Chebar, and I sat where they were living. I sat there among them for seven days, overwhelmed.
At the end of seven days the word of the LORD came to me:
"Son of man, I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel. Whenever you hear a word from my mouth, you are to warn them from me.

When I say to the wicked, 'You will surely die,' and you do not warn him, and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his wicked way so as to save his life, that wicked person will die for his guilt, but I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn the wicked, and he does not turn from his wickedness or from his wicked way, he will die for his guilt, but you will have saved your life.

And when a righteous person turns from his righteousness and does wrong, and I put a stumbling block in front of him, he will die. Because you did not warn him, he will die for his sin, and the righteous deeds he has done will not be remembered, but I will hold you responsible for his blood.
But if you warn the righteous person not to sin, and he does not sin, he will surely live, because he took the warning, and you will have saved your life."
The hand of the LORD was on me there, and he said to me, "Get up, go out to the plain, and there I will speak with you."
So I got up and went out to the plain, and there was the glory of the LORD standing there, like the glory I had seen by the river Chebar, and I fell on my face.
Then the Spirit came into me and set me on my feet. He spoke with me and said to me, "Go, shut yourself inside your house.
And you, son of man, look, they will put ropes on you and tie you up with them, so that you cannot go out among them.
I will make your tongue stick to the roof of your mouth, so that you will be unable to speak and unable to rebuke them, for they are a rebellious house.

But when I speak with you, I will open your mouth, and you are to say to them, 'This is what the Lord GOD says.' Whoever will listen, let him listen, and whoever refuses, let him refuse, for they are a rebellious house.
"And you, son of man, take a brick and put it in front of you, and draw a city on it, Jerusalem.
Lay siege to it: build a siege wall against it, pile up a ramp against it, set up camps against it, and place battering rams against it all around.
Then take an iron griddle and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city. Set your face toward it, so that it is under siege, and besiege it. This is a sign for the house of Israel.
Then lie on your left side, and lay the guilt of the house of Israel on it. For the number of days that you lie on it, you will bear their guilt.
I have assigned you the years of their guilt as a number of days, 390 days. So you will bear the guilt of the house of Israel.
When you have completed these, lie down a second time, on your right side, and bear the guilt of the house of Judah for 40 days. I have assigned you a day for each year, a day for each year.
Set your face toward the siege of Jerusalem, with your arm bared, and prophesy against it.
Look, I will put ropes on you, so that you cannot turn from one side to the other until you have completed the days of your siege.

Take wheat and barley, beans and lentils, millet and spelt. Put them in one container and make bread for yourself from them. You are to eat it for the number of days that you lie on your side, 390 days.
The food you eat is to be weighed out, twenty shekels a day; you are to eat it at set times.
You are to drink water by measure, a sixth of a hin; you are to drink it at set times.
You are to eat it as a barley cake, and bake it in their sight over human dung."
The LORD said, "This is how the Israelites will eat their bread, unclean, among the nations where I will drive them."

Then I said, "Ah, Lord GOD! I have never made myself unclean. From my youth until now I have never eaten anything that died by itself or was torn by wild animals, and no foul meat has ever come into my mouth."
He said to me, "See, I will let you have cow dung instead of human dung. You may make your bread over it."
He said to me, "Son of man, I am going to cut off the supply of bread in Jerusalem. They will eat bread by weight and with anxiety, and drink water by measure and in dismay,
so that they will lack bread and water, and they will look at one another in dismay, and waste away in their guilt.
"And you, son of man, take a sharp sword and use it as a barber's razor: pass it over your head and over your beard. Then take scales for weighing, and divide the hair.

A third of it you are to burn in the fire in the middle of the city, when the days of the siege are completed. A third you are to take and strike with the sword all around the city. And a third you are to scatter to the wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
Take a few hairs from there and tie them up in the hem of your robe.
Take some of these again, throw them into the fire, and burn them in the fire. From there a fire will spread to the whole house of Israel.
This is what the Lord GOD says: This is Jerusalem. I set her in the middle of the nations, with countries all around her.
But she has rebelled against my rulings more wickedly than the nations, and against my decrees more than the countries around her. For they have rejected my rulings and have not walked in my decrees.

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have been more unruly than the nations around you, and have not walked in my decrees or kept my rulings, and have not even acted according to the rulings of the nations around you,
therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I, even I, am against you. I will carry out judgments in your midst in the sight of the nations.
Because of all your detestable practices, I will do to you what I have never done before, and the like of which I will never do again.
Therefore fathers will eat their children in your midst, and children will eat their fathers. I will carry out judgments on you, and I will scatter all who are left of you to every wind.

Therefore, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, because you have defiled my sanctuary with all your vile idols and with all your detestable practices, I too will cut you down. My eye will not pity, and I will not spare.
A third of you will die of plague and perish by famine in your midst; a third will fall by the sword all around you; and a third I will scatter to every wind, and I will draw a sword after them.
Then my anger will be spent, and I will satisfy my fury on them, and I will be appeased. Then they will know that I, the LORD, have spoken in my jealousy, when I have spent my fury on them.
I will make you a ruin and a disgrace among the nations around you, in the sight of everyone who passes by.
You will be a disgrace and a taunt, a warning and a horror to the nations around you, when I carry out judgments on you in anger and in fury and with furious punishments. I, the LORD, have spoken.
When I send against them the deadly arrows of famine, arrows for destruction, which I will send to destroy you, I will bring more and more famine on you, and I will cut off your supply of bread.
I will send famine and wild animals against you, and they will leave you childless. Plague and bloodshed will sweep through you, and I will bring the sword against you. I, the LORD, have spoken."
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, set your face toward the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them.

Say: Mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord GOD. This is what the Lord GOD says to the mountains and the hills, to the ravines and the valleys: Look, I myself am bringing a sword against you, and I will destroy your high places.
Your altars will be made desolate, and your incense altars will be smashed. I will make your slain fall in front of your idols.
I will lay the corpses of the Israelites in front of their idols, and I will scatter your bones around your altars.

Wherever you live, the cities will be laid waste and the high places made desolate, so that your altars will be laid waste and held guilty, your idols smashed and brought to an end, your incense altars cut down, and your works wiped out.
The slain will fall among you, and you will know that I am the LORD.
But I will leave some of you alive: some of you will escape the sword among the nations, when you are scattered through the countries.

Then those of you who escape will remember me among the nations where they have been taken captive, how I was broken by their heart, which played the prostitute and turned away from me, and by their eyes, which played the prostitute after their idols. They will loathe themselves for the evil they have done, for all their detestable practices.
And they will know that I am the LORD. It was not for nothing that I said I would bring this disaster on them.

This is what the Lord GOD says: Clap your hands and stamp your feet, and say "Alas!" over all the evil, detestable practices of the house of Israel, for they will fall by the sword, by famine and by plague.
Whoever is far away will die of plague, whoever is near will fall by the sword, and whoever is left and spared will die of famine. So I will spend my fury on them.

And you will know that I am the LORD, when their slain lie among their idols around their altars, on every high hill, on all the mountaintops, under every green tree and under every leafy oak, the places where they offered a pleasing aroma to all their idols.
I will stretch out my hand against them and make the land a desolate waste, from the wilderness to Diblah, wherever they live. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
And you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says to the land of Israel: An end! The end has come on the four corners of the land.
Now the end is on you. I will let loose my anger against you; I will judge you according to your ways, and I will bring on you the penalty for all your detestable practices.
My eye will not pity you, and I will not spare. I will bring your ways down on you, and your detestable practices will be in your midst. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
This is what the Lord GOD says: Disaster! A disaster like no other! Look, it is coming!
An end has come! The end has come! It has awakened against you. Look, it is coming!
Doom has come to you, you who live in the land. The time has come; the day is near: tumult, and not joyful shouting on the mountains.
Now, very soon, I will pour out my fury on you and spend my anger against you. I will judge you according to your ways, and I will bring on you the penalty for all your detestable practices.
My eye will not pity, and I will not spare. I will repay you according to your ways, and your detestable practices will be in your midst. Then you will know that I, the LORD, am the one who strikes.
Look, the day! Look, it is coming! Doom has gone out. The rod has blossomed; arrogance has budded.
Violence has grown into a rod of wickedness. Nothing will be left of them, nothing of their crowds, nothing of their wealth, and there will be no splendor among them.
The time has come; the day has arrived. Let the buyer not rejoice, and let the seller not mourn, for wrath is on all her crowds.

For the seller will not go back to what he sold, even while they are still alive. For the vision concerning all her crowds will not be turned back, and because of his guilt, no one will keep hold of his life.
They have blown the trumpet and made everything ready, but no one goes out to battle, for my wrath is on all her crowds.
The sword is outside, and plague and famine are inside. Whoever is in the field will die by the sword, and whoever is in the city, famine and plague will devour him.
Those of them who escape and survive will be on the mountains like doves of the valleys, all of them moaning, each for his guilt.
All hands will hang limp, and all knees will turn to water.
They will put on sackcloth, and horror will cover them. Shame will be on every face, and every head will be shaved bald.

They will throw their silver into the streets, and their gold will be like something unclean. Their silver and their gold will not be able to save them on the day of the LORD's wrath. They will not satisfy their hunger or fill their stomachs with it, for it made them stumble into guilt.
Their beautiful jewelry they turned into a source of pride, and with it they made their detestable images, their vile idols. Therefore I will make it something unclean for them.
I will hand it over to foreigners as plunder and to the wicked of the earth as spoil, and they will profane it.
I will turn my face away from them, and they will profane my treasured place. Robbers will enter it and profane it.
Make the chain, for the land is full of bloody crimes, and the city is full of violence.
I will bring the worst of the nations, and they will take possession of their houses. I will put an end to the pride of the strong, and their holy places will be profaned.
Anguish is coming! They will seek peace, but there will be none.
Disaster will come on disaster, and rumor will follow rumor. They will seek a vision from a prophet, but instruction will perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders.

The king will mourn, the prince will be clothed with despair, and the hands of the people of the land will tremble. I will deal with them according to their ways, and by their own standards I will judge them. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
In the sixth year, in the sixth month, on the fifth day of the month, as I was sitting in my house, with the elders of Judah sitting in front of me, the hand of the Lord GOD fell on me there.

I looked, and I saw a likeness with the appearance of fire. From what looked like his waist downward was fire, and from his waist upward was something like the appearance of brightness, like the gleam of amber.

He stretched out the form of a hand and took me by a lock of my hair, and the Spirit lifted me up between earth and heaven and brought me in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the inner gate that faces north, where the image of jealousy stood, the image that provokes jealousy.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, like the vision that I had seen in the plain.
He said to me, "Son of man, lift up your eyes toward the north." So I lifted up my eyes toward the north, and there, north of the altar gate, in the entrance, was this image of jealousy.

He said to me, "Son of man, do you see what they are doing, the great detestable practices that the house of Israel is committing here, to drive me far from my sanctuary? But you will see yet more great detestable practices."
He brought me to the entrance of the court, and I looked, and there was a hole in the wall.
He said to me, "Son of man, dig through the wall." So I dug through the wall, and there was an entrance.
He said to me, "Go in and see the evil, detestable practices that they are committing here."
So I went in and looked, and there, carved on the wall all around, were all kinds of creeping things and unclean animals, and all the idols of the house of Israel.

Seventy of the elders of the house of Israel were standing in front of them, with Jaazaniah son of Shaphan standing among them. Each had his censer in his hand, and a fragrant cloud of incense was rising.

He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen what the elders of the house of Israel are doing in the dark, each in the room of his carved images? For they say, 'The LORD does not see us. The LORD has abandoned the land.'"
He said to me, "You will see yet more great detestable practices that they are committing."
Then he brought me to the entrance of the north gate of the house of the LORD, and there were the women, sitting and weeping for Tammuz.
He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? You will see still greater detestable practices than these."

Then he brought me into the inner court of the house of the LORD, and there at the entrance of the temple of the LORD, between the porch and the altar, were about twenty-five men, with their backs to the temple of the LORD and their faces toward the east, bowing down to the sun in the east.

He said to me, "Have you seen this, son of man? Is it a trivial thing for the house of Judah to commit the detestable practices they have committed here, that they must also fill the land with violence and provoke me to anger again and again? Look, they are putting the branch to their nose!
Therefore I too will act in fury. My eye will not pity, and I will not spare. Though they cry in my ears with a loud voice, I will not listen to them."
Then he called out in my hearing with a loud voice, "Come near, you who are to punish the city, each with his weapon of destruction in his hand!"

And six men came from the direction of the upper gate, which faces north, each with his weapon for smashing in his hand. Among them was a man clothed in linen, with a writing case at his waist. They came in and stood beside the bronze altar.
Now the glory of the God of Israel had gone up from the cherub on which it had been, to the threshold of the house. He called to the man clothed in linen, who had the writing case at his waist.
The LORD said to him, "Go through the city, through Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the people who sigh and groan over all the detestable practices that are committed in it."
To the others he said in my hearing, "Go through the city after him and strike. Do not let your eye pity, and do not spare.

Kill old men, young men and young women, little children and women, until they are destroyed. But do not come near anyone who has the mark on him. Begin at my sanctuary." So they began with the elders who were in front of the house.
He said to them, "Defile the house, and fill the courts with the slain. Go!" So they went out and struck down people in the city.
While they were striking them down, and I was left alone, I fell on my face and cried out, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you destroy all the remnant of Israel when you pour out your fury on Jerusalem?"

He said to me, "The guilt of the house of Israel and Judah is very, very great. The land is full of bloodshed, and the city is full of injustice. For they say, 'The LORD has abandoned the land, and the LORD does not see.'
As for me, my eye will not pity, and I will not spare. I will bring their ways down on their heads."
Then the man clothed in linen, with the writing case at his waist, brought back word: "I have done everything you commanded me."
I looked, and there on the dome above the heads of the cherubim was something like lapis lazuli, with the appearance of the likeness of a throne, which appeared above them.

He spoke to the man clothed in linen and said, "Go in between the whirling wheels underneath the cherub. Fill your hands with burning coals from among the cherubim and scatter them over the city." And he went in as I watched.
Now the cherubim were standing on the south side of the house when the man went in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
Then the glory of the LORD rose from the cherub to the threshold of the house. The house was filled with the cloud, and the court was full of the brightness of the glory of the LORD.
The sound of the wings of the cherubim could be heard as far as the outer court, like the voice of God Almighty when he speaks.
When he commanded the man clothed in linen, "Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from among the cherubim," the man went in and stood beside a wheel.

Then a cherub stretched out his hand from among the cherubim to the fire that was among the cherubim. He took some of it and put it into the hands of the man clothed in linen, who took it and went out.
The cherubim appeared to have the form of human hands under their wings.
I looked, and there were four wheels beside the cherubim, one wheel beside each cherub, and the appearance of the wheels was like the gleam of beryl.
As for their appearance, the four of them had the same likeness, like a wheel within a wheel.
When they went, they went in any of their four directions; they did not turn as they went. In whatever direction the head faced, they went after it; they did not turn as they went.
Their whole body, their backs, their hands and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes all around, the wheels of all four of them.
As for the wheels, they were called in my hearing "the whirling wheels".
Each one had four faces: the first face was the face of the cherub, the second face was a human face, the third the face of a lion, and the fourth the face of an eagle.
Then the cherubim rose up. These were the living creatures that I had seen by the river Chebar.
When the cherubim went, the wheels went beside them, and when the cherubim lifted their wings to rise from the ground, the wheels did not turn from beside them either.
When the cherubim stood still, the wheels stood still, and when they rose, the wheels rose with them, for the spirit of the living creatures was in them.
Then the glory of the LORD went out from over the threshold of the house and stood over the cherubim.

The cherubim lifted their wings and rose from the ground before my eyes as they went out, with the wheels beside them. They stopped at the entrance of the east gate of the house of the LORD, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
These were the living creatures that I had seen beneath the God of Israel by the river Chebar, and I knew that they were cherubim.
Each had four faces and each had four wings, and under their wings was the likeness of human hands.
As for the likeness of their faces, they were the same faces that I had seen by the river Chebar. Each of them went straight ahead.

Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the east gate of the house of the LORD, the gate that faces east. There at the entrance of the gate were twenty-five men, and I saw among them Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah, leaders of the people.
He said to me, "Son of man, these are the men who are planning wickedness and giving evil advice in this city.
They say, 'The time is not near to build houses. This city is the pot, and we are the meat.'
Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, son of man."
Then the Spirit of the LORD fell on me, and he said to me, "Say: This is what the LORD says: That is what you have said, house of Israel, but I know the things that come into your mind.
You have killed many people in this city and filled its streets with the slain.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: The slain whom you have laid in the middle of it, they are the meat, and this city is the pot. But you I will bring out of it.
You have feared the sword, and the sword is what I will bring on you, declares the Lord GOD.
I will bring you out of the middle of it and hand you over to foreigners, and I will carry out judgments on you.
You will fall by the sword; I will judge you at the border of Israel. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
This city will not be your pot, and you will not be the meat in it. I will judge you at the border of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the LORD, whose decrees you have not walked in and whose rulings you have not kept, but you have acted according to the rulings of the nations around you."
While I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died. Then I fell on my face and cried out with a loud voice, "Ah, Lord GOD! Will you make a complete end of the remnant of Israel?"
The word of the LORD came to me:

"Son of man, your brothers, your own brothers, your relatives who have the right to redeem you, and the whole house of Israel, all of them, are those of whom the people living in Jerusalem have said, 'Keep far away from the LORD. This land was given to us as a possession.'

Therefore say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Though I have sent them far away among the nations, and though I have scattered them among the countries, yet I have been a sanctuary for them for a little while in the countries where they have gone.
Therefore say: This is what the Lord GOD says: I will gather you from the peoples and assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.
They will come there and remove from it all its vile idols and all its detestable practices.
I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you. I will remove the heart of stone from their bodies and give them a heart of flesh,
so that they will walk in my decrees and keep my rulings and do them. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God.
But as for those whose heart goes after their vile idols and their detestable practices, I will bring their ways down on their heads, declares the Lord GOD."
Then the cherubim lifted their wings, with the wheels beside them, and the glory of the God of Israel was over them above.
The glory of the LORD went up from the middle of the city and stood on the mountain east of the city.
The Spirit lifted me up and brought me to the exiles in Chaldea, in the vision, by the Spirit of God. Then the vision that I had seen left me.
And I told the exiles all the things that the LORD had shown me.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, you are living in the middle of a rebellious house. They have eyes to see but do not see, and ears to hear but do not hear, for they are a rebellious house.

As for you, son of man, pack your belongings for exile, and go into exile by day in their sight. Go into exile from your place to another place in their sight. Perhaps they will see, though they are a rebellious house.
Bring out your belongings by day in their sight, like belongings for exile, and in the evening go out in their sight like people going out into exile.
In their sight dig through the wall, and carry your belongings out through it.
In their sight carry them on your shoulder, and take them out in the dark. Cover your face, so that you cannot see the land, for I have made you a sign for the house of Israel.

So I did as I was commanded. I brought out my belongings by day, like belongings for exile, and in the evening I dug through the wall with my hand. I took them out in the dark, carrying them on my shoulder in their sight.
In the morning the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, said to you, "What are you doing?"
Say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: This oracle concerns the prince in Jerusalem and the whole house of Israel who are there.
Say: I am a sign for you. As I have done, so it will be done to them. They will go into exile, into captivity.

The prince who is among them will carry his things on his shoulder in the dark and go out. They will dig through the wall to bring him out through it. He will cover his face, so that he will not see the land with his eyes.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, yet he will not see it, and there he will die.
I will scatter to every wind all those around him, his helpers and all his troops, and I will draw a sword after them.
Then they will know that I am the LORD, when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them through the countries.
But I will let a few of them escape the sword, famine and plague, so that they may tell about all their detestable practices among the nations where they go. Then they will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, eat your bread with trembling, and drink your water with shuddering and anxiety.

Say to the people of the land: This is what the Lord GOD says about those who live in Jerusalem, in the land of Israel: They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in dismay, so that their land will be stripped of everything in it, because of the violence of all who live in it.
The cities that are now inhabited will be laid waste, and the land will become desolate. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, what is this proverb you have about the land of Israel: "The days drag on, and every vision comes to nothing"?

Therefore say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: I will put an end to this proverb, and they will no longer use it as a proverb in Israel. Instead say to them: "The days are near, and so is the fulfillment of every vision."
For there will no longer be any false vision or flattering divination within the house of Israel.
For I am the LORD. I will speak, and the word that I speak will be done. It will no longer be delayed. In your own days, rebellious house, I will speak the word and do it, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, look, the house of Israel is saying, "The vision that he sees is for many days from now, and he prophesies about times far off."
Therefore say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: None of my words will be delayed any longer. Whatever word I speak will be done, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, prophesy against the prophets of Israel who are prophesying. Say to those who prophesy out of their own imagination: Hear the word of the LORD.
This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the foolish prophets, who follow their own spirit and have seen nothing!
Your prophets, Israel, have been like foxes among ruins.
You have not gone up into the breaches or built up a wall around the house of Israel, so that it might stand in the battle on the day of the LORD.
They have seen false visions and lying divination. They say, "declares the LORD," when the LORD has not sent them, and yet they expect him to fulfill their word.
Have you not seen a false vision and spoken a lying divination, when you say, "declares the LORD," though I have not spoken?
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Because you have spoken falsehood and seen lies, therefore, look, I am against you, declares the Lord GOD.

My hand will be against the prophets who see false visions and give lying divinations. They will not be in the council of my people, or be written in the register of the house of Israel, or enter the land of Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord GOD.
Because, yes, because they have led my people astray, saying, "Peace," when there is no peace, and when someone builds a flimsy wall, they cover it with whitewash,
say to those who cover it with whitewash that it will fall. There will be a flooding rain, and you, great hailstones, will fall, and a stormy wind will break out.
When the wall has fallen, will people not say to you, "Where is the whitewash you covered it with?"
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: In my fury I will make a stormy wind break out; in my anger there will be a flooding rain, and in fury, hailstones to destroy it.

I will tear down the wall that you covered with whitewash and bring it down to the ground, so that its foundation is laid bare. When it falls, you will perish in the middle of it. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
So I will spend my fury on the wall and on those who covered it with whitewash. And I will say to you, "The wall is gone, and so are those who whitewashed it":
the prophets of Israel who prophesied to Jerusalem and saw visions of peace for her when there was no peace, declares the Lord GOD.
And you, son of man, set your face against the daughters of your people who prophesy out of their own imagination. Prophesy against them,

and say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Woe to the women who sew bands on every wrist and make veils for the heads of people of every height, to hunt down lives! Will you hunt down the lives of my people and keep your own lives alive?

You have profaned me among my people for handfuls of barley and scraps of bread, putting to death people who should not die and keeping alive people who should not live, by your lies to my people, who listen to lies.

Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Look, I am against your bands with which you hunt down lives there like birds. I will tear them from your arms, and I will set free the lives that you hunt down like birds.
I will tear off your veils and rescue my people from your hands, and they will no longer be prey in your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
Because you have disheartened the righteous with lies, when I had not brought him grief, and you have encouraged the wicked not to turn from his evil way and save his life,
therefore you will no longer see false visions or practice divination. I will rescue my people from your hands. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
Some of the elders of Israel came to me and sat down in front of me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, these men have set up their idols in their hearts and put the stumbling block of their guilt in front of their faces. Should I let myself be consulted by them at all?

Therefore speak to them and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: Anyone of the house of Israel who sets up his idols in his heart and puts the stumbling block of his guilt in front of his face, and then comes to the prophet, I, the LORD, will answer him myself as he comes with his many idols,
so that I may take hold of the house of Israel by their hearts, for they have all turned away from me through their idols.
Therefore say to the house of Israel: This is what the Lord GOD says: Turn back! Turn away from your idols, and turn your faces away from all your detestable practices.

For anyone of the house of Israel, or of the foreigners who live in Israel, who separates himself from me, sets up his idols in his heart, and puts the stumbling block of his guilt in front of his face, and then comes to the prophet to consult me through him, I, the LORD, will answer him myself.
I will set my face against that man and make him a sign and a byword, and I will cut him off from among my people. Then you will know that I am the LORD.
And if the prophet is deceived and speaks a word, it is I, the LORD, who have deceived that prophet, and I will stretch out my hand against him and destroy him from among my people Israel.
They will bear their guilt; the guilt of the one who consults will be the same as the guilt of the prophet,
so that the house of Israel will no longer stray from me or defile themselves anymore with all their transgressions. Then they will be my people, and I will be their God, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, if a land sins against me by acting unfaithfully, and I stretch out my hand against it, cut off its supply of bread, send famine on it, and cut off from it both people and animals,
even if these three men, Noah, Daniel and Job, were in it, they would save only themselves by their righteousness, declares the Lord GOD.
If I send wild animals through the land and they leave it childless, and it becomes so desolate that no one passes through it because of the animals,
even if these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they could not save their sons or their daughters. They alone would be saved, and the land would be desolate.
Or if I bring a sword against that land and say, "Let a sword pass through the land," and I cut off from it both people and animals,
even if these three men were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they could not save their sons or their daughters; they alone would be saved.
Or if I send a plague into that land and pour out my fury on it in bloodshed, to cut off from it both people and animals,
even if Noah, Daniel and Job were in it, as I live, declares the Lord GOD, they could not save son or daughter. They would save only themselves by their righteousness.

For this is what the Lord GOD says: How much worse will it be when I send my four terrible judgments against Jerusalem, sword and famine and wild animals and plague, to cut off from it both people and animals!

Yet look, some survivors will be left in it, sons and daughters who will be brought out. Look, they will come out to you, and when you see their ways and their deeds, you will be consoled for the disaster I have brought on Jerusalem, for everything I have brought on it.
They will console you when you see their ways and their deeds, and you will know that it was not without cause that I did all that I did in it, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, how is the wood of the vine better than any other wood, the vine branch that is among the trees of the forest?
Is wood taken from it to make anything useful? Or do people take a peg from it to hang any vessel on?
Look, it is put into the fire for fuel. When the fire has consumed both its ends and its middle is charred, is it any use for anything?
Look, even when it was whole, it could not be made into anything useful. How much less, when the fire has consumed it and it is charred, can it still be made into anything useful!
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Like the wood of the vine among the trees of the forest, which I have given to the fire for fuel, so I will give up the people who live in Jerusalem.
I will set my face against them. Though they have come out of the fire, the fire will still consume them. Then you will know that I am the LORD, when I set my face against them.
I will make the land desolate, because they have acted unfaithfully, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, make known to Jerusalem her detestable practices.
Say: This is what the Lord GOD says to Jerusalem: Your origin and your birth were in the land of the Canaanites. Your father was an Amorite, and your mother a Hittite.
As for your birth, on the day you were born your cord was not cut, you were not washed with water to clean you, you were not rubbed with salt, and you were not wrapped in cloths.
No eye pitied you enough to do any one of these things for you out of compassion for you. Instead you were thrown out into the open field, because you were despised, on the day you were born.
Then I passed by you and saw you kicking about in your blood, and I said to you in your blood, "Live!" I said to you in your blood, "Live!"
I made you grow like a plant of the field. You grew up and became tall, and you came to the age of full beauty: your breasts were formed and your hair had grown, but you were naked and bare.

Then I passed by you and saw you, and look, your time was the time for love. I spread the corner of my garment over you and covered your nakedness. I swore an oath to you and entered into a covenant with you, declares the Lord GOD, and you became mine.
Then I bathed you with water, washed your blood off you, and anointed you with oil.
I clothed you with embroidered cloth and put sandals of fine leather on your feet. I wrapped you in fine linen and covered you with silk.
I adorned you with jewelry: I put bracelets on your arms and a necklace around your neck.
I put a ring in your nose, earrings in your ears, and a beautiful crown on your head.
So you were adorned with gold and silver, and your clothing was fine linen, silk and embroidered cloth. You ate fine flour, honey and oil. You became very, very beautiful, and you rose to be a queen.
Your fame spread among the nations because of your beauty, for it was perfect through the splendor that I had put on you, declares the Lord GOD.
But you trusted in your beauty and played the prostitute because of your fame. You poured out your acts of prostitution on everyone who passed by; it was his.
You took some of your clothes and made colorful high places for yourself, and on them you played the prostitute. Such things should not come about, and they should never be.
You also took your beautiful jewels, made of my gold and my silver that I had given you, and made for yourself male images, and you played the prostitute with them.
You took your embroidered clothes to cover them, and you set my oil and my incense before them.
Also my food that I gave you, the fine flour, the oil and the honey I fed you, you set before them as a pleasing aroma. That is what happened, declares the Lord GOD.
You took your sons and your daughters, whom you had borne to me, and sacrificed them to the images as food. Was your prostitution not enough?
You slaughtered my children and gave them up, offering them to the images.
In all your detestable practices and your acts of prostitution you did not remember the days of your youth, when you were naked and bare, kicking about in your blood.
After all your wickedness (woe, woe to you, declares the Lord GOD!)
you built yourself a mound and made yourself a lofty place in every square.
At the head of every street you built your lofty place and made your beauty detestable. You spread your legs for everyone who passed by and multiplied your acts of prostitution.
You played the prostitute with the Egyptians, your neighbors with their large genitals, and multiplied your prostitution to provoke me to anger.

So I stretched out my hand against you and cut down your allotted portion. I handed you over to the will of those who hate you, the daughters of the Philistines, who were ashamed of your lewd conduct.
You played the prostitute with the Assyrians too, because you were never satisfied. You played the prostitute with them, and still you were not satisfied.
You multiplied your prostitution with the land of traders, Chaldea, and even with this you were not satisfied.
How sick your heart is, declares the Lord GOD, that you did all these things, the deeds of a brazen prostitute!
When you built your mound at the head of every street and made your lofty place in every square, you were not like a prostitute, for you scorned payment.
You adulterous wife, who takes strangers instead of her husband!
All prostitutes are given gifts, but you gave your gifts to all your lovers, and bribed them to come to you from all around for your acts of prostitution.
So in your prostitution you were the opposite of other women. No one chased after you for prostitution, and you gave payment, while no payment was given to you. So you were the opposite.
Therefore, you prostitute, hear the word of the LORD.

This is what the Lord GOD says: Because your lust was poured out and your nakedness was uncovered in your prostitution with your lovers, and because of all your detestable idols, and because of the blood of your children whom you gave to them,

therefore, look, I am going to gather all your lovers whom you pleased, all those you loved along with all those you hated. I will gather them against you from all around and uncover your nakedness to them, and they will see all your nakedness.
I will judge you as women who commit adultery and shed blood are judged, and I will bring on you the bloodshed of fury and jealousy.
I will hand you over to them, and they will tear down your mound and demolish your lofty places. They will strip you of your clothes, take your beautiful jewels, and leave you naked and bare.
They will bring up a mob against you, and they will stone you with stones and hack you to pieces with their swords.
They will burn your houses with fire and carry out judgments on you in the sight of many women. I will put an end to your prostitution, and you will no longer give payment.
Then I will satisfy my fury on you, and my jealousy will turn away from you. I will be calm and no longer angry.

Because you did not remember the days of your youth, but provoked me with all these things, I in turn will bring your ways down on your head, declares the Lord GOD. Did you not commit this lewdness on top of all your detestable practices?
Look, everyone who uses proverbs will use this proverb about you: "Like mother, like daughter."

You are your mother's daughter, who loathed her husband and her children, and you are the sister of your sisters, who loathed their husbands and their children. Your mother was a Hittite and your father an Amorite.
Your older sister is Samaria, who lives with her daughters to your north, and your younger sister, who lives to your south, is Sodom with her daughters.
You not only walked in their ways and acted according to their detestable practices; in a very short time you became more corrupt than they in all your ways.
As I live, declares the Lord GOD, your sister Sodom and her daughters never did what you and your daughters have done.
Look, this was the guilt of your sister Sodom: she and her daughters had pride, plenty of food and carefree ease, but she did not help the poor and needy.
They were haughty and did detestable things before me, so I removed them when I saw it.
Samaria did not commit half your sins. You have done more detestable things than they did, and you have made your sisters seem righteous by all the detestable things you have done.

You too must bear your disgrace, for you have pleaded your sister's case. Because of your sins, in which you acted more detestably than they, they are more in the right than you. So you too be ashamed and bear your disgrace, for you have made your sisters seem righteous.
I will restore their fortunes, the fortunes of Sodom and her daughters and the fortunes of Samaria and her daughters, and I will restore your fortunes along with theirs,
so that you may bear your disgrace and be ashamed of all that you have done, when you bring them comfort.
Your sisters, Sodom and her daughters, will return to their former state; Samaria and her daughters will return to their former state; and you and your daughters will return to your former state.
You would not even mention your sister Sodom in the day of your pride,

before your wickedness was exposed, as it is now that you have become the scorn of the daughters of Aram and all her neighbors, and of the daughters of the Philistines, those all around who despise you.
You must bear the penalty of your lewdness and your detestable practices, declares the LORD.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: I will deal with you as you have done, you who despised the oath by breaking the covenant.
Yet I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and I will establish with you an everlasting covenant.
Then you will remember your ways and be ashamed when you receive your sisters, those older than you and those younger, and I give them to you as daughters, but not on the basis of your covenant.
I will establish my covenant with you, and you will know that I am the LORD,
so that you will remember and be ashamed, and never again open your mouth because of your disgrace, when I make atonement for you for all that you have done, declares the Lord GOD.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, pose a riddle and tell a parable to the house of Israel.
Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: A great eagle, with great wings and long pinions, full of feathers of many colors, came to Lebanon and took the top of the cedar.
He broke off the topmost of its young shoots and carried it to a land of traders, and set it in a city of merchants.
Then he took some of the seed of the land and put it in a fertile field. He set it like a willow beside abundant waters.
It sprouted and became a spreading vine, low in height. Its branches turned toward him, and its roots remained beneath him. So it became a vine, and it produced shoots and sent out leafy branches.

But there was another great eagle, with great wings and thick plumage. And look, this vine bent its roots toward him and stretched out its branches to him, away from the beds where it was planted, so that he might water it.
It had been planted in good soil beside abundant waters, so that it could produce branches, bear fruit and become a splendid vine.

Say: This is what the Lord GOD says: Will it prosper? Will he not pull up its roots and strip off its fruit, so that it withers, so that all its fresh sprouting leaves wither? It will not take a strong arm or many people to pull it up by its roots.
Look, it is planted, but will it prosper? Will it not wither completely when the east wind strikes it? It will wither on the beds where it sprouted.
The word of the LORD came to me:
Say to the rebellious house: Do you not know what these things mean? Say: Look, the king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and took its king and its officials and brought them to himself in Babylon.
He took one of the royal family and made a covenant with him, putting him under an oath. He also took away the leading men of the land,
so that the kingdom would be humble and not lift itself up, and would keep his covenant in order to survive.

But he rebelled against him by sending his envoys to Egypt, so that they would give him horses and a large army. Will he prosper? Will a man who does such things escape? Can he break a covenant and escape?
As I live, declares the Lord GOD, he will die in Babylon, in the land of the king who made him king, whose oath he despised and whose covenant he broke, there with him in Babylon.
Pharaoh with his mighty army and great horde will not help him in the war, when ramps are thrown up and siege walls built to cut off many lives.
He despised the oath by breaking the covenant. Though he had given his hand in pledge, he did all these things. He will not escape.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: As I live, I will surely bring down on his head my oath that he despised and my covenant that he broke.
I will spread my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon and enter into judgment with him there for the unfaithfulness he committed against me.
All the fugitives among all his troops will fall by the sword, and those who are left will be scattered to every wind. Then you will know that I, the LORD, have spoken.

This is what the Lord GOD says: I myself will take a sprig from the lofty top of the cedar and set it out. I will break off a tender shoot from the topmost of its young shoots, and I myself will plant it on a high and lofty mountain.

On the high mountain of Israel I will plant it, and it will put out branches and bear fruit and become a majestic cedar. Birds of every kind will nest under it; they will nest in the shade of its branches.

All the trees of the field will know that I am the LORD. I bring down the high tree and make the low tree high; I dry up the green tree and make the dry tree flourish. I, the LORD, have spoken, and I will do it.
The word of the LORD came to me:
What do you mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: "The fathers eat sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge"?
As I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer use this proverb in Israel.
Look, all lives are mine. The life of the father, like the life of the son, is mine. The person who sins is the one who will die.
Suppose a man is righteous and does what is just and right.
He does not eat on the mountains or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife or come near a woman during her menstrual impurity.
He does not oppress anyone. He returns what was given him in pledge for a debt. He does not commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
He does not lend at interest or take any profit. He keeps his hand from wrongdoing and judges fairly between one person and another.
He walks in my decrees and keeps my rulings, acting faithfully. Such a man is righteous; he will surely live, declares the Lord GOD.
But suppose he fathers a son who is violent, who sheds blood, and who does any one of these things
(though the father did none of them). He eats on the mountains and defiles his neighbor's wife.
He oppresses the poor and needy, commits robbery, and does not return a pledge. He lifts up his eyes to the idols and does detestable things.
He lends at interest and takes profit. Will he live? He will not live! He has done all these detestable things; he will surely be put to death. His blood will be on his own head.
But suppose this son fathers a son who sees all the sins his father has done. He sees them, and does not do the like.
He does not eat on the mountains or lift up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel. He does not defile his neighbor's wife.
He does not oppress anyone, does not take anything in pledge, and does not commit robbery. He gives his bread to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
He keeps his hand from harming the poor, and does not take interest or profit. He keeps my rulings and walks in my decrees. He will not die for his father's guilt; he will surely live.
As for his father, because he practiced extortion, robbed his brother, and did what was not good among his people, look, he dies for his guilt.
Yet you say, "Why does the son not bear the guilt of the father?" When the son has done what is just and right, and has kept all my decrees and done them, he will surely live.

The person who sins is the one who will die. The son will not bear the guilt of the father, nor will the father bear the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous will be on him, and the wickedness of the wicked will be on him.
But if the wicked person turns away from all the sins he has committed, and keeps all my decrees and does what is just and right, he will surely live; he will not die.
None of the transgressions he has committed will be remembered against him. Because of the righteousness he has done, he will live.
Do I take any pleasure in the death of the wicked, declares the Lord GOD? Do I not rather want him to turn from his ways and live?

But if a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does wrong, doing all the same detestable things that the wicked person does, will he live? None of the righteous deeds he has done will be remembered. Because of the unfaithfulness he has committed and the sin he has committed, he will die for them.
Yet you say, "The way of the Lord is not fair." Hear now, house of Israel: Is my way not fair? Is it not your ways that are not fair?
When a righteous person turns away from his righteousness and does wrong and dies because of it, he dies for the wrong he has done.
And when a wicked person turns away from the wickedness he has committed and does what is just and right, he will save his life.
Because he considers and turns away from all the transgressions he has committed, he will surely live; he will not die.
Yet the house of Israel says, "The way of the Lord is not fair." Are my ways not fair, house of Israel? Is it not your ways that are not fair?
Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, each according to his ways, declares the Lord GOD. Turn back, and turn away from all your transgressions, so that guilt will not be your downfall.
Throw off all the transgressions you have committed, and make for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. Why should you die, house of Israel?
For I take no pleasure in the death of anyone who dies, declares the Lord GOD. So turn back and live!
As for you, take up a lament for the princes of Israel,
and say: What a lioness your mother was! She lay down among lions; among young lions she reared her cubs.
She brought up one of her cubs, and he became a young lion. He learned to tear prey; he devoured people.
The nations heard about him; he was caught in their pit. They brought him with hooks to the land of Egypt.
When she saw that she had waited in vain, that her hope was lost, she took another of her cubs and made him a young lion.
He prowled among the lions; he became a young lion. He learned to tear prey; he devoured people.
He knew their widows and laid waste their cities. The land and everything in it was appalled at the sound of his roaring.
Then the nations from the provinces all around set themselves against him. They spread their net over him; he was caught in their pit.
With hooks they put him in a cage and brought him to the king of Babylon. They brought him into strongholds, so that his voice would no longer be heard on the mountains of Israel.
Your mother was like a vine in your blood, planted by the water. It was fruitful and full of branches because of the abundant water.
It had strong branches, fit for the scepters of rulers. It grew tall among the thick boughs; it stood out in its height, with its many branches.
But it was uprooted in fury and thrown to the ground. The east wind dried up its fruit. Its strong branch was torn off and withered; fire consumed it.
Now it is planted in the wilderness, in a dry and thirsty land.
Fire has gone out from its branch and consumed its fruit. No strong branch is left on it, no scepter for ruling. This is a lament, and it has become a lament.
In the seventh year, in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, some of the elders of Israel came to consult the LORD, and they sat down in front of me.
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
Son of man, speak to the elders of Israel and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: Have you come to consult me? As I live, I will not let myself be consulted by you, declares the Lord GOD.
Will you judge them? Will you judge them, son of man? Make known to them the detestable practices of their ancestors,

and say to them: This is what the Lord GOD says: On the day I chose Israel, I raised my hand to the descendants of the house of Jacob and made myself known to them in the land of Egypt. I raised my hand to them and said, "I am the LORD your God."

On that day I raised my hand to them, swearing that I would bring them out of the land of Egypt into a land I had searched out for them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands.
And I said to them, "Each of you, throw away the vile idols you set your eyes on, and do not defile yourselves with the idols of Egypt. I am the LORD your God."

But they rebelled against me and were not willing to listen to me. None of them threw away the vile idols they set their eyes on, nor did they abandon the idols of Egypt. Then I said I would pour out my fury on them and spend my anger against them in the middle of the land of Egypt.

But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations among whom they lived, in whose sight I had made myself known to them by bringing them out of the land of Egypt.
So I brought them out of the land of Egypt and led them into the wilderness.
I gave them my decrees and made known to them my rulings, by which a person who does them will live.
I also gave them my Sabbaths, to be a sign between me and them, so that they might know that I am the LORD who makes them holy.

But the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness. They did not walk in my decrees, and they rejected my rulings, by which a person who does them will live, and they greatly profaned my Sabbaths. Then I said I would pour out my fury on them in the wilderness to make an end of them.
But I acted for the sake of my name, so that it would not be profaned in the sight of the nations in whose sight I had brought them out.
I also raised my hand to them in the wilderness, swearing that I would not bring them into the land I had given them, a land flowing with milk and honey, the most beautiful of all lands,
because they rejected my rulings and did not walk in my decrees, and they profaned my Sabbaths, for their hearts went after their idols.
Yet my eye spared them, and I did not destroy them; I did not make an end of them in the wilderness.
I said to their children in the wilderness, "Do not walk in the decrees of your fathers or keep their rulings, and do not defile yourselves with their idols.
I am the LORD your God. Walk in my decrees, and keep my rulings and do them.
Keep my Sabbaths holy, and they will be a sign between me and you, so that you may know that I am the LORD your God."
