They will not need to gather wood from the field or cut it from the forests, because they will make their fires with the weapons. They will plunder those who plundered them and loot those who looted them, declares the Lord GOD.

On that day I will give Gog a burial place there in Israel, the Valley of the Travelers, east of the sea. It will block the way of travelers. There they will bury Gog and all his hordes, and they will call it the Valley of Hamon-gog.
For seven months the house of Israel will be burying them, in order to cleanse the land.
All the people of the land will bury them, and it will bring them renown on the day I display my glory, declares the Lord GOD.

They will set apart men to go through the land continually and bury, with those who pass through, the bodies that remain on the face of the land, so as to cleanse it. At the end of the seven months they will make their search.
As they pass through the land, whenever anyone sees a human bone, he will set up a marker beside it, until the gravediggers have buried it in the Valley of Hamon-gog.
A city will also be named Hamonah. So they will cleanse the land.

As for you, son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: Say to the birds of every kind and to all the wild animals, "Assemble and come! Gather from all around to my sacrifice, which I am sacrificing for you, a great sacrifice on the mountains of Israel, and you will eat flesh and drink blood.
You will eat the flesh of the mighty and drink the blood of the princes of the earth, as if they were rams, lambs and goats, and bulls, all of them fattened animals of Bashan.
You will eat fat until you are full and drink blood until you are drunk, at my sacrifice, which I have sacrificed for you.
At my table you will eat your fill of horses and charioteers, of mighty men and warriors of every kind, declares the Lord GOD."
I will display my glory among the nations, and all the nations will see the judgment I have carried out and my hand that I have laid on them.
From that day on, the house of Israel will know that I am the LORD their God.

And the nations will know that the house of Israel went into exile for their guilt, because they were unfaithful to me. So I hid my face from them and handed them over to their enemies, and they all fell by the sword.
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and their transgressions, and I hid my face from them.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: Now I will restore the fortunes of Jacob and have compassion on the whole house of Israel, and I will be jealous for my holy name.
They will bear their disgrace and all the unfaithfulness they showed toward me, when they live securely on their own land with no one to make them afraid,
when I bring them back from the peoples and gather them from the lands of their enemies, and show myself holy through them in the sight of many nations.
Then they will know that I am the LORD their God, because I sent them into exile among the nations and then gathered them back to their own land. I will not leave any of them there any longer.
I will no longer hide my face from them, for I will have poured out my Spirit on the house of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.

In the twenty-fifth year of our exile, at the beginning of the year, on the tenth day of the month, in the fourteenth year after the city was struck down, on that very day the hand of the LORD was on me, and he brought me there.
In visions of God he brought me to the land of Israel and set me down on a very high mountain, and on it, to the south, was something like the structure of a city.
He brought me there, and there was a man whose appearance was like bronze, with a linen cord and a measuring reed in his hand. He was standing in the gateway.

The man said to me, "Son of man, look with your eyes, hear with your ears, and pay attention to everything I am going to show you, for you have been brought here so that I may show it to you. Tell the house of Israel everything you see."

There was a wall all around the outside of the house. In the man's hand was a measuring reed six cubits long, each cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth. He measured the thickness of the wall: one reed; and its height: one reed.
Then he went to the gate that faced east. He climbed its steps and measured the threshold of the gate: one reed wide; and the other threshold: one reed wide.
Each alcove was one reed long and one reed wide, and between the alcoves were five cubits. The threshold of the gate beside the porch of the gate, on the inside, was one reed.
He measured the porch of the gate on the inside: one reed.
Then he measured the porch of the gate: eight cubits; and its jambs: two cubits. The porch of the gate was on the inside.
The alcoves of the east gate were three on one side and three on the other. The three had the same measurements, and the jambs on either side had the same measurements.
He measured the width of the entrance of the gate: ten cubits; and the length of the gate: thirteen cubits.
There was a barrier of one cubit in front of the alcoves, one cubit on either side; and the alcoves were six cubits on one side and six cubits on the other.
He measured the gate from the roof of one alcove to the roof of the other: the width was twenty-five cubits, from doorway to opposite doorway.
He made the jambs sixty cubits, and the gate reached all around to the jamb of the court.
From the front of the entrance gate to the front of the porch of the inner gate was fifty cubits.
The alcoves and their jambs had narrow windows all around, on the inside of the gate, and so did the porches. There were windows all around on the inside, and on the jambs were palm trees.
Then he brought me into the outer court, and there were rooms and a pavement made for the court all around. Thirty rooms faced the pavement.
The pavement ran beside the gates, corresponding to the length of the gates. This was the lower pavement.
Then he measured the distance from the front of the lower gate to the front of the inner court, outside: a hundred cubits, on the east and on the north.
As for the gate of the outer court that faced north, he measured its length and its width.
Its alcoves, three on one side and three on the other, its jambs and its porches had the same measurements as the first gate: fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its windows, its porches and its palm trees had the same measurements as those of the gate that faced east. Seven steps led up to it, and its porches were in front of them.
The inner court had a gate opposite the north gate, as it had for the east gate. He measured from gate to gate: a hundred cubits.
Then he led me toward the south, and there was a gate facing south. He measured its jambs and its porches; they had the same measurements as the others.
It and its porches had windows all around, like those other windows. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Seven steps led up to it, and its porches were in front of them. It had palm trees on its jambs, one on either side.
The inner court had a gate toward the south, and he measured from gate to gate toward the south: a hundred cubits.
Then he brought me into the inner court through the south gate, and he measured the south gate. It had the same measurements as the others.
Its alcoves, its jambs and its porches had the same measurements as the others. It and its porches had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
There were porches all around, twenty-five cubits long and five cubits wide.
Its porches faced the outer court, and there were palm trees on its jambs. Its stairway had eight steps.
Then he brought me into the inner court on the east side, and he measured the gate. It had the same measurements as the others.
Its alcoves, its jambs and its porches had the same measurements as the others. It and its porches had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its porches faced the outer court, and there were palm trees on its jambs on either side. Its stairway had eight steps.
Then he brought me to the north gate, and he measured it. It had the same measurements as the others,
with its alcoves, its jambs and its porches, and it had windows all around. It was fifty cubits long and twenty-five cubits wide.
Its jambs faced the outer court, and there were palm trees on its jambs on either side. Its stairway had eight steps.
There was a room with its doorway by the jambs of the gates, where the burnt offering was to be washed.
In the porch of the gate were two tables on one side and two tables on the other, on which the burnt offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering were to be slaughtered.
At the outer side, as one goes up to the entrance of the north gate, were two tables; and on the other side of the porch of the gate were two tables.
So there were four tables on one side and four tables on the other, beside the gate: eight tables on which they were to slaughter.

There were also four tables of dressed stone for the burnt offering, a cubit and a half long, a cubit and a half wide and a cubit high. On them they were to lay the instruments with which they slaughtered the burnt offering and the sacrifice.
Hooks, a handbreadth long, were fastened all around on the inside, and the meat of the offering was to be laid on the tables.
Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, were rooms for the singers, one beside the north gate, facing south, and one beside the east gate, facing north.
He said to me, "This room that faces south is for the priests who have charge of the house,
and the room that faces north is for the priests who have charge of the altar. These are the sons of Zadok, who alone among the sons of Levi may come near to the LORD to serve him."
He measured the court: a hundred cubits long and a hundred cubits wide, a square. The altar was in front of the house.

Then he brought me to the porch of the house and measured the jambs of the porch: five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. The width of the gate was three cubits on one side and three cubits on the other.
The porch was twenty cubits long and eleven cubits wide, and it was reached by steps. There were pillars beside the jambs, one on either side.
Then he brought me into the main hall and measured the jambs: six cubits wide on one side and six cubits wide on the other, the width of the tent.
The entrance was ten cubits wide, and the side walls of the entrance were five cubits on one side and five cubits on the other. He measured its length: forty cubits; and its width: twenty cubits.
Then he went inside and measured the jambs of the entrance: two cubits; the entrance: six cubits; and the width of the entrance: seven cubits.
He measured its length: twenty cubits; and its width: twenty cubits, at the far end of the main hall. He said to me, "This is the most holy place."
Then he measured the wall of the house: six cubits thick; and the width of the side rooms all around the house: four cubits.

The side rooms were one above another, thirty-three of them. There were ledges in the wall of the house all around for the side rooms, so that they would be supported, but they were not fastened into the wall of the house.

The side rooms grew wider as they went around, story by story upward, for the structure around the house went up story by story all around the house. So the house was wider at the top, and one went up from the lowest story to the highest by way of the middle one.
I saw that the house had a raised platform all around. The foundations of the side rooms were a full reed, six cubits to the edge.
The thickness of the outer wall of the side rooms was five cubits. There was an open area beside the side structure of the house.
Between the rooms there was a width of twenty cubits all around the house, on every side.
The doorways of the side rooms opened onto the open area, one doorway toward the north and one doorway toward the south. The width of the open area was five cubits all around.
The building that faced the separate yard on the west side was seventy cubits wide. The wall of the building was five cubits thick all around, and its length was ninety cubits.
Then he measured the house: a hundred cubits long; and the separate yard and the building with its walls: a hundred cubits long.
The width of the front of the house and of the separate yard on the east was a hundred cubits.

He measured the length of the building facing the separate yard at the back of the house, with its galleries on either side: a hundred cubits. The main hall, the inner room and the porches of the court,

the thresholds, the narrow windows and the galleries all around the three of them, opposite the threshold, were paneled with wood all around, from the floor up to the windows; and the windows were covered.
Above the entrance, as far as the inner room and on the outside, and on all the walls all around, inside and outside, were measured panels.
They were carved with cherubim and palm trees, with a palm tree between cherub and cherub. Each cherub had two faces:
a human face toward the palm tree on one side, and a lion's face toward the palm tree on the other side. They were carved on the whole temple all around.
From the floor to above the entrance, cherubim and palm trees were carved on the wall of the main hall.
The doorposts of the main hall were square. In front of the holy place was something that looked like this:
an altar of wood, three cubits high and two cubits long, with its corners. Its length and its walls were of wood. He said to me, "This is the table that is before the LORD."
The main hall and the holy place each had a double door.
Each door had two leaves, two leaves that swung: two leaves for one door and two leaves for the other.
On the doors of the main hall were carved cherubim and palm trees like those carved on the walls. There was a canopy of wood on the front of the porch outside.
There were narrow windows and palm trees on either side, on the side walls of the porch, and on the side rooms of the house and on the canopies.
Then he brought me out into the outer court, by the way toward the north, and he brought me to the rooms opposite the separate yard and opposite the building on the north.
Their length along the front, where the doorway faced north, was a hundred cubits, and the width was fifty cubits.
Opposite the twenty cubits that belonged to the inner court, and opposite the pavement that belonged to the outer court, was gallery facing gallery, in three stories.
In front of the rooms was a passage ten cubits wide, on the inner side, a way of one cubit, and their doorways were on the north.
The upper rooms were narrower, for the galleries took more space from them than from the lower and the middle rooms of the building.
For they were in three stories and had no pillars like the pillars of the courts. So the upper rooms were set back from the ground more than the lower and the middle ones.
There was an outer wall parallel to the rooms, toward the outer court, in front of the rooms; it was fifty cubits long.
For the rooms on the side of the outer court were fifty cubits long, while those facing the main hall were a hundred cubits.
Below these rooms was the entryway from the east, as one enters them from the outer court.
Along the width of the wall of the court toward the east, facing the separate yard and facing the building, were rooms,
with a passage in front of them. They looked like the rooms on the north side; they had the same length and width, with all the same exits, arrangements and doorways.
Like the doorways of the rooms on the south side was a doorway at the head of the passage, the passage in front of the matching wall, toward the east, as one enters them.

Then he said to me, "The north rooms and the south rooms facing the separate yard are the holy rooms, where the priests who come near to the LORD are to eat the most holy offerings. There they are to put the most holy offerings, the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering, for the place is holy.

When the priests enter, they must not go out of the holy place into the outer court. They are to leave there the garments in which they minister, for these are holy, and they are to put on other garments before they go near the area for the people."
When he had finished measuring the inner house, he brought me out by the gate that faced east and measured the area all around.
He measured the east side with the measuring reed: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the north side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed, all around.
He measured the south side: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He turned to the west side and measured: five hundred reeds by the measuring reed.
He measured it on the four sides. It had a wall all around, five hundred long and five hundred wide, to separate the holy from the common.
Then he led me to the gate, the gate that faces east.
And there was the glory of the God of Israel, coming from the east. Its sound was like the sound of many waters, and the earth shone with his glory.
The vision I saw was like the vision I had seen when I came to destroy the city, and the visions were like the vision I had seen by the river Chebar. And I fell on my face.
The glory of the LORD came into the house by the gate that faces east.
Then the Spirit lifted me up and brought me into the inner court, and there the glory of the LORD filled the house.
I heard someone speaking to me from the house, while a man was standing beside me.

He said to me, "Son of man, this is the place of my throne and the place of the soles of my feet, where I will live among the Israelites forever. The house of Israel will no longer defile my holy name, neither they nor their kings, by their prostitution and by the corpses of their kings at their death.

When they set their threshold by my threshold and their doorpost beside my doorpost, with only a wall between me and them, they defiled my holy name by the detestable practices they committed. So I consumed them in my anger.
Now let them put their prostitution and the corpses of their kings far away from me, and I will live among them forever.
As for you, son of man, describe the house to the house of Israel, so that they will be ashamed of their guilt. Let them measure its plan.

If they are ashamed of all they have done, make known to them the design of the house, its arrangement, its exits and its entrances, all its forms and all its decrees, all its forms and all its laws. Write it down before their eyes, so that they may keep its whole design and all its decrees and carry them out.
This is the law of the house: on the top of the mountain, the whole area all around will be most holy. Yes, this is the law of the house."

These are the measurements of the altar in cubits, the cubit being a cubit and a handbreadth: its base is a cubit deep and a cubit wide, with a rim of one span around its edge. And this is the height of the altar:
From the base on the ground to the lower ledge it is two cubits, and the width is one cubit; and from the smaller ledge to the larger ledge it is four cubits, and the width is one cubit.
The altar hearth is four cubits high, and from the hearth four horns project upward.
The altar hearth is square, twelve cubits long and twelve wide, square on its four sides.
The ledge is square, fourteen cubits long and fourteen wide on its four sides, with a rim around it of half a cubit, and its base is a cubit all around. Its steps face east.
Then he said to me, "Son of man, this is what the Lord GOD says: These are the decrees for the altar on the day it is made, for offering burnt offerings on it and for splashing blood against it.
You are to give a young bull as a sin offering to the Levitical priests who are descendants of Zadok, who come near to me to serve me, declares the Lord GOD.
You are to take some of its blood and put it on the four horns of the altar, on the four corners of the ledge and on the rim all around. So you will purify it from sin and make atonement for it.
You are to take the bull of the sin offering and burn it in the appointed place of the house, outside the sanctuary.
On the second day you are to offer a male goat without defect as a sin offering, and they are to purify the altar as they purified it with the bull.
When you have finished purifying it, you are to offer a young bull without defect and a ram from the flock without defect.
You are to present them before the LORD, and the priests are to throw salt on them and offer them up as a burnt offering to the LORD.
For seven days you are to provide a goat for a sin offering each day. A young bull and a ram from the flock, without defect, are also to be provided.
For seven days they are to make atonement for the altar and cleanse it, and so consecrate it.
When they have completed these days, from the eighth day on, the priests are to offer your burnt offerings and your fellowship offerings on the altar, and I will accept you, declares the Lord GOD."
Then he brought me back by way of the outer gate of the sanctuary, the one facing east, and it was shut.
The LORD said to me, "This gate is to remain shut. It must not be opened, and no one may enter by it, because the LORD, the God of Israel, has entered by it. So it is to remain shut.
Only the prince, because he is the prince, may sit in it to eat bread before the LORD. He is to enter by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way."
Then he brought me by way of the north gate to the front of the house. I looked, and the glory of the LORD filled the house of the LORD, and I fell on my face.

The LORD said to me, "Son of man, pay attention, look with your eyes and listen with your ears to all that I tell you about all the decrees of the house of the LORD and all its laws. Pay attention to the entrance of the house and all the exits of the sanctuary.
Say to the rebellious, to the house of Israel, 'This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough of all your detestable practices, house of Israel!

You brought foreigners, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, into my sanctuary, to be in it and to profane my house, when you offered my food, the fat and the blood. They have broken my covenant, on top of all your detestable practices.
You have not kept charge of my holy things yourselves; instead you have set them to keep my charge in my sanctuary for you.
This is what the Lord GOD says: No foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, of all the foreigners who are among the Israelites, may enter my sanctuary.
But the Levites who went far from me when Israel went astray, who went astray from me after their idols, will bear their guilt.

They will serve in my sanctuary, having charge of the gates of the house and serving the house. They will slaughter the burnt offering and the sacrifice for the people, and they will stand before the people to serve them.

Because they served them before their idols and became a stumbling block of guilt for the house of Israel, therefore I have raised my hand against them, declares the Lord GOD, swearing that they will bear their guilt.
They must not come near me to serve me as priests, or come near any of my holy things, the most holy things. They will bear their shame for the detestable practices they have committed.
Yet I will appoint them to keep charge of the house, for all its service and for all that is to be done in it.

But the Levitical priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept charge of my sanctuary when the Israelites went astray from me, they will come near to me to serve me. They will stand before me to offer me fat and blood, declares the Lord GOD.
They will enter my sanctuary, and they will come near to my table to serve me and keep my charge.
When they enter the gates of the inner court, they are to wear linen garments. They must have nothing woolen on them while they serve in the gates of the inner court and inside the house.
They are to have linen turbans on their heads and linen undergarments around their waists. They must not wear anything that makes them sweat.

When they go out into the outer court, into the outer court to the people, they are to take off the garments in which they have been serving and leave them in the holy rooms, and put on other garments, so that they do not make the people holy by their garments.
They must not shave their heads or let their hair grow long. They are to keep the hair of their heads trimmed.
No priest may drink wine when he enters the inner court.
They must not marry a widow or a divorced woman, but only virgins of the descendants of the house of Israel, or a widow who is the widow of a priest.
They are to teach my people the difference between the holy and the common, and show them how to tell the unclean from the clean.
In a dispute they are to stand as judges, and they are to judge it by my rulings. They are to keep my laws and my decrees at all my appointed festivals, and they are to keep my Sabbaths holy.
A priest must not go near a dead person and so become unclean, except that for a father or mother, son or daughter, brother, or sister who has no husband, they may make themselves unclean.
After he has been cleansed, seven days are to be counted for him.
On the day he enters the holy place, into the inner court, to serve in the holy place, he is to offer his sin offering, declares the Lord GOD.
This is to be their inheritance: I am their inheritance. You are to give them no property in Israel; I am their property.
They are to eat the grain offering, the sin offering and the guilt offering, and everything devoted in Israel will be theirs.

The best of all the firstfruits of every kind, and every contribution of every kind from all your contributions, will belong to the priests. You are to give the priest the first of your dough, so that a blessing may rest on your house.
The priests must not eat anything, bird or animal, that has died by itself or been torn by wild animals.

"'When you allot the land as an inheritance, you are to set apart a contribution for the LORD, a holy portion of the land, twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide. It will be holy throughout its whole area all around.
Of this, a square of five hundred by five hundred is to be for the sanctuary, with fifty cubits of open land around it.
From this measured area you are to measure off a section twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide, and in it will be the sanctuary, the most holy place.
It is the holy portion of the land. It will be for the priests who serve in the sanctuary, who come near to serve the LORD. It will be a place for their houses and a holy area for the sanctuary.
An area twenty-five thousand long and ten thousand wide will belong to the Levites who serve the house, as their property, for twenty rooms.
Alongside the holy contribution you are to assign as the city's property an area five thousand wide and twenty-five thousand long. It will belong to the whole house of Israel.

The prince is to have the land on both sides of the holy contribution and the city's property, alongside the holy contribution and the city's property, on the west side westward and on the east side eastward. Its length will correspond to one of the tribal portions, from the western border to the eastern border.
This land will be his property in Israel. My princes will no longer oppress my people, but will give the rest of the land to the house of Israel according to their tribes.
This is what the Lord GOD says: Enough, you princes of Israel! Put away violence and oppression, and do what is just and right. Stop evicting my people, declares the Lord GOD.
You are to have honest scales, an honest ephah and an honest bath.
The ephah and the bath are to be the same size, the bath holding a tenth of a homer and the ephah a tenth of a homer. The homer is to be the standard measure for both.
The shekel is to be twenty gerahs. Twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels and fifteen shekels are to be your mina.
This is the contribution you are to present: a sixth of an ephah from each homer of wheat, and a sixth of an ephah from each homer of barley.
The prescribed portion of oil, measured by the bath, is a tenth of a bath from each kor. Ten baths make a homer, for ten baths are a homer.

And one sheep is to be given from every flock of two hundred, from the well-watered pastures of Israel, for grain offerings, burnt offerings and fellowship offerings, to make atonement for the people, declares the Lord GOD.
All the people of the land are to give this contribution to the prince in Israel.

It will be the prince's duty to provide the burnt offerings, the grain offerings and the drink offerings at the festivals, the new moons and the Sabbaths, at all the appointed festivals of the house of Israel. He is to provide the sin offering, the grain offering, the burnt offering and the fellowship offerings, to make atonement for the house of Israel.
This is what the Lord GOD says: In the first month, on the first day of the month, you are to take a young bull without defect and purify the sanctuary from sin.

The priest is to take some of the blood of the sin offering and put it on the doorposts of the house, on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the doorposts of the gate of the inner court.
You are to do the same on the seventh day of the month for anyone who sins unintentionally or through ignorance. So you will make atonement for the house.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, you are to celebrate the Passover, a festival lasting a week, when unleavened bread is to be eaten.
On that day the prince is to provide, for himself and for all the people of the land, a bull as a sin offering.

During the seven days of the festival he is to provide as a burnt offering to the LORD seven bulls and seven rams without defect, each day for the seven days, and a male goat each day as a sin offering.
As a grain offering he is to provide an ephah for each bull and an ephah for each ram, with a hin of oil for each ephah.
In the seventh month, on the fifteenth day of the month, at the festival, he is to provide the same for seven days: the same sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain offerings and oil.

"'This is what the Lord GOD says: The gate of the inner court that faces east is to be shut on the six working days, but on the Sabbath day it is to be opened, and on the day of the new moon it is to be opened.

The prince is to enter by way of the porch of the gate from outside and stand by the doorpost of the gate. The priests are to offer his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings, and he is to bow down at the threshold of the gate and then go out. But the gate is not to be shut until evening.
The people of the land are to bow down at the entrance of that gate before the LORD on the Sabbaths and the new moons.
The burnt offering that the prince presents to the LORD on the Sabbath day is to be six lambs without defect and a ram without defect.
The grain offering is to be an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he wishes to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
On the day of the new moon he is to offer a young bull without defect, and six lambs and a ram, which are to be without defect.
As a grain offering he is to provide an ephah with the bull and an ephah with the ram, and with the lambs as much as he can afford, and a hin of oil for each ephah.
When the prince enters, he is to come in by way of the porch of the gate and go out the same way.

When the people of the land come before the LORD at the appointed festivals, whoever enters by the north gate to worship is to go out by the south gate, and whoever enters by the south gate is to go out by the north gate. No one is to go back through the gate by which he came in; each is to go out straight ahead.
The prince is to be among them: when they come in, he is to come in, and when they go out, they are to go out.
At the festivals and the appointed times, the grain offering is to be an ephah with a bull and an ephah with a ram, and with the lambs as much as he wishes to give, and a hin of oil for each ephah.

When the prince provides a freewill offering, a burnt offering or fellowship offerings as a freewill offering to the LORD, the gate that faces east is to be opened for him, and he is to offer his burnt offering and his fellowship offerings as he does on the Sabbath day. Then he is to go out, and after he has gone out the gate is to be shut.
You are to provide a year-old lamb without defect as a burnt offering to the LORD every day. Morning by morning you are to provide it.

With it, morning by morning, you are to provide a grain offering of a sixth of an ephah, with a third of a hin of oil to moisten the fine flour, a grain offering to the LORD. These are permanent decrees, to be kept continually.
So they are to provide the lamb, the grain offering and the oil morning by morning, as a regular burnt offering.
This is what the Lord GOD says: If the prince gives a gift to one of his sons, it is that son's inheritance and will belong to his sons. It is their property by inheritance.

But if he gives a gift from his inheritance to one of his servants, it will belong to the servant until the year of liberty, and then it will return to the prince. His inheritance belongs to his sons alone; it is theirs.

The prince must not take any of the people's inheritance, driving them off their property. He is to give his sons their inheritance from his own property, so that none of my people will be driven from his property.'"
Then he brought me through the entrance at the side of the gate to the holy rooms for the priests, which faced north. There I saw a place at the far end, on the west side.

He said to me, "This is the place where the priests are to boil the guilt offering and the sin offering, and where they are to bake the grain offering, so that they do not bring them out into the outer court and make the people holy."
Then he brought me out into the outer court and led me around to the four corners of the court, and in each corner of the court there was a court.
In the four corners of the court were enclosed courts, forty long and thirty wide. The four corner courts had the same measurements.
Around each of the four of them was a row of stonework, and hearths for cooking were built under the rows all around.
He said to me, "These are the kitchens where those who serve the house will boil the sacrifices of the people."

Then he brought me back to the entrance of the house, and there was water flowing out from under the threshold of the house toward the east, for the house faced east. The water was flowing down from under the south side of the house, south of the altar.
He brought me out by way of the north gate and led me around on the outside to the outer gate that faces east, and there the water was trickling out from the south side.
As the man went out toward the east with a measuring line in his hand, he measured a thousand cubits and led me through the water, and it was ankle-deep.
He measured another thousand and led me through the water, and it was knee-deep. He measured another thousand and led me through, and it was waist-deep.
He measured another thousand, and it was a river that I could not cross, for the water had risen. It was deep enough to swim in, a river that could not be crossed.
He said to me, "Son of man, have you seen this?" Then he led me back along the bank of the river.
When I came back, there on the bank of the river were very many trees on both sides.
He said to me, "This water flows out toward the eastern region and goes down into the Arabah, and it enters the sea. When it flows into the sea, the water of the sea will become fresh.

Wherever the river goes, every living creature that swarms will live. There will be very many fish, because this water goes there and makes the water of the sea fresh; so everything will live where the river goes.
Fishermen will stand beside it from En-gedi to En-eglaim; it will be a place for spreading nets. Its fish will be of many kinds, like the fish of the Great Sea, very many.
But its swamps and marshes will not become fresh; they will be left for salt.

On both banks of the river every kind of tree for food will grow. Their leaves will not wither, and their fruit will not fail. They will bear fresh fruit every month, because their water flows from the sanctuary. Their fruit will be for food and their leaves for healing."
"This is what the Lord GOD says: These are the boundaries by which you are to divide the land as an inheritance among the twelve tribes of Israel, with two portions for Joseph.
You are to divide it equally among you, the land I raised my hand to give to your ancestors. This land will fall to you as an inheritance.
This is to be the boundary of the land: On the north side, from the Great Sea by the way of Hethlon, as one goes to Zedad,
Hamath, Berothah and Sibraim, which lies between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath, as far as Hazer-hatticon, which is on the border of Hauran.
So the boundary will run from the sea to Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus, with the border of Hamath to the north. This is the north side.

On the east side, the boundary will run between Hauran and Damascus, and along the Jordan between Gilead and the land of Israel. You are to measure from the northern boundary to the eastern sea. This is the east side.
On the south side, toward the Negev, it will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Wadi to the Great Sea. This is the south side, toward the Negev.
On the west side, the Great Sea will be the boundary, as far as a point opposite Lebo-hamath. This is the west side.
You are to divide this land among yourselves according to the tribes of Israel.

You are to allot it as an inheritance for yourselves and for the foreigners who live among you and have had children among you. They are to be to you like native-born Israelites; with you they are to be allotted an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
In whatever tribe the foreigner lives, there you are to give him his inheritance, declares the Lord GOD.

"These are the names of the tribes: At the northern end, beside the way of Hethlon to Lebo-hamath, as far as Hazar-enan, at the border of Damascus, with Hamath to the north beside it, and extending from the east side to the west side, Dan will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Dan, from the east side to the west side, Asher will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Asher, from the east side to the west side, Naphtali will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Naphtali, from the east side to the west side, Manasseh will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Manasseh, from the east side to the west side, Ephraim will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Ephraim, from the east side to the west side, Reuben will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Reuben, from the east side to the west side, Judah will have one portion.

Next to the territory of Judah, from the east side to the west side, will be the contribution you are to set apart, 25,000 wide, and as long as one of the tribal portions, from the east side to the west side, with the sanctuary in the middle of it.
The contribution you are to set apart for the LORD will be 25,000 long and 10,000 wide.

This will be the holy contribution for the priests: on the north side 25,000 long, on the west side 10,000 wide, on the east side 10,000 wide, and on the south side 25,000 long. The sanctuary of the LORD will be in the middle of it.
It will be for the consecrated priests, the sons of Zadok, who kept my charge and did not go astray when the Israelites went astray, as the Levites did.
It will be a special portion for them from the holy contribution of the land, a most holy place, next to the territory of the Levites.
Alongside the territory of the priests, the Levites will have an area 25,000 long and 10,000 wide. The whole length will be 25,000 and the width 10,000.
They must not sell any of it or exchange it, and this choicest part of the land must not pass to others, for it is holy to the LORD.
The remaining area, 5,000 wide and 25,000 long, will be for the common use of the city, for houses and for open land. The city will be in the middle of it.
These will be its measurements: the north side 4,500, the south side 4,500, the east side 4,500 and the west side 4,500.
The city will have open land: 250 on the north, 250 on the south, 250 on the east and 250 on the west.

The rest of the area, along the length beside the holy contribution, will be 10,000 on the east and 10,000 on the west. It will lie beside the holy contribution, and its produce will be food for the workers of the city.
The workers of the city, from all the tribes of Israel, will farm it.
The whole contribution will be 25,000 by 25,000. You are to set apart the holy contribution as a square, together with the city's property.

What remains on both sides of the holy contribution and of the city's property will belong to the prince. It will extend eastward from the 25,000 of the contribution to the eastern border, and westward from the 25,000 to the western border, alongside the tribal portions. It will belong to the prince. The holy contribution and the sanctuary of the house will be in the middle of it.

The property of the Levites and the property of the city will lie in the middle of what belongs to the prince; the land between the territory of Judah and the territory of Benjamin will belong to the prince.
As for the rest of the tribes: from the east side to the west side, Benjamin will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Benjamin, from the east side to the west side, Simeon will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Simeon, from the east side to the west side, Issachar will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Issachar, from the east side to the west side, Zebulun will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Zebulun, from the east side to the west side, Gad will have one portion.
Next to the territory of Gad, on the south side, toward the Negev, the boundary will run from Tamar to the waters of Meribath-kadesh, and along the Wadi to the Great Sea.
This is the land you are to allot as an inheritance to the tribes of Israel, and these will be their portions, declares the Lord GOD.
These are the exits of the city: On the north side, which measures 4,500,
the gates of the city will be named after the tribes of Israel. There will be three gates on the north: one gate for Reuben, one gate for Judah and one gate for Levi.
On the east side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Joseph, one gate for Benjamin and one gate for Dan.
On the south side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Simeon, one gate for Issachar and one gate for Zebulun.
On the west side, which measures 4,500, there will be three gates: one gate for Gad, one gate for Asher and one gate for Naphtali.
The distance all around will be 18,000. And from that day on the name of the city will be 'The LORD Is There.'"
In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of God. He brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he put the vessels in the treasury of his god.
Then the king told Ashpenaz, his chief court official, to bring some of the Israelites, from the royal family and from the nobles:

young men without any defect, good-looking, skilled in all wisdom, well informed and quick to learn, who had the ability to serve in the king's palace. He was to teach them the literature and language of the Babylonians.
The king assigned them a daily ration from the king's food and from the wine he drank. They were to be educated for three years, and at the end of that time they were to enter the king's service.
Among them, from the people of Judah, were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah.
The chief official gave them names. He named Daniel Belteshazzar, Hananiah Shadrach, Mishael Meshach, and Azariah Abednego.
But Daniel made up his mind not to defile himself with the king's food or with the wine he drank, and he asked the chief official to let him not defile himself.
God caused the chief official to show Daniel kindness and compassion.

The chief official said to Daniel, "I am afraid of my lord the king, who has assigned your food and your drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men of your age? You would put my head in danger with the king."
Then Daniel said to the guard whom the chief official had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,
"Please test your servants for ten days. Let us be given vegetables to eat and water to drink.
Then compare our appearance with the appearance of the young men who eat the king's food, and deal with your servants according to what you see."
He agreed to this and tested them for ten days.
At the end of the ten days they looked better and healthier than all the young men who were eating the king's food.
So the guard took away their food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.
To these four young men God gave knowledge and skill in all literature and wisdom. And Daniel had understanding of visions and dreams of every kind.
At the end of the time the king had set for bringing them in, the chief official brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.
The king talked with them, and among them all no one was found to equal Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah. So they entered the king's service.
In every matter of wisdom and understanding that the king asked them about, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his whole kingdom.
And Daniel remained there until the first year of King Cyrus.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and he could not sleep.
So the king gave orders to summon the magicians, the enchanters, the sorcerers and the Chaldeans, to tell the king his dreams. They came in and stood before the king.
The king said to them, "I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream."
Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: "O king, live forever! Tell your servants the dream, and we will give its interpretation."
The king answered the Chaldeans, "This is my firm decision: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb, and your houses will be made a dunghill.
But if you tell me the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, a reward and great honor. So tell me the dream and its interpretation."
They answered a second time, "Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will give its interpretation."
The king answered, "I know for certain that you are trying to gain time, because you see that my decision is firm.

If you do not make the dream known to me, there is only one sentence for you. You have agreed together to speak lying and corrupt words before me until the situation changes. So tell me the dream, and I will know that you can give me its interpretation."

The Chaldeans answered the king, "There is no one on earth who can tell the king what he asks. That is why no king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter or Chaldean.
What the king asks is too difficult. There is no one who can tell it to the king except the gods, and they do not live among mortals."
At this the king became furious and very angry, and he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed.
So the decree went out that the wise men were to be killed, and they looked for Daniel and his companions to kill them.
Then Daniel spoke with prudence and discretion to Arioch, the captain of the king's guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
He said to Arioch, the king's officer, "Why is the decree from the king so harsh?" Then Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
So Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, and he would tell the king the interpretation.
Then Daniel went to his house and told the matter to his companions Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah,
so that they would seek mercy from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night, and Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
Daniel said, "Blessed be the name of God forever and ever, for wisdom and power belong to him.
He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and sets up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who have understanding.
He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light lives with him.
To you, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and power. Now you have made known to me what we asked of you; you have made known to us what the king asked."

So Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said to him, "Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will tell the king the interpretation."
Then Arioch quickly brought Daniel in before the king and said to him, "I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can make known the interpretation to the king."
The king said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, "Are you able to make known to me the dream I saw and its interpretation?"
Daniel answered the king, "No wise men, enchanters, magicians or diviners can tell the king the mystery he has asked about.

But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in the last days. This is your dream, the visions that passed through your head as you lay on your bed:
As for you, O king, as you lay on your bed your thoughts turned to what would happen after this, and the revealer of mysteries has made known to you what will happen.

As for me, this mystery has been revealed to me not because I have more wisdom than anyone else alive, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king, and so that you may understand the thoughts of your heart.
You were looking, O king, and there before you was a great statue. That statue was huge, and its brightness was extraordinary. It stood in front of you, and its appearance was terrifying.
The head of the statue was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
its legs of iron, and its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.
As you watched, a stone was cut out, not by human hands. It struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and smashed them.

Then the iron, the clay, the bronze, the silver and the gold were all smashed together and became like chaff on the threshing floors in summer. The wind carried them away, and not a trace of them could be found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
This was the dream, and now we will tell the king its interpretation.
You, O king, are the king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, the power, the might and the glory.
He has given into your hand human beings, the wild animals and the birds of the sky, wherever they live, and he has made you ruler over them all. You are that head of gold.
After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you, and then a third kingdom, of bronze, which will rule over the whole earth.
Then there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron. Just as iron smashes and shatters everything, and as iron crushes things, it will smash and crush all these.

As you saw, the feet and toes were partly of potter's clay and partly of iron. So it will be a divided kingdom, but some of the strength of iron will be in it, just as you saw the iron mixed with the wet clay.
As the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
And as you saw the iron mixed with the wet clay, so they will mix with one another by marriage, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.

In the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be left to another people. It will smash all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will stand forever.

That is the meaning of the stone you saw cut out of the mountain, not by human hands, that smashed the iron, the bronze, the clay, the silver and the gold. A great God has made known to the king what will happen after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy."
Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell on his face and bowed down to Daniel, and he gave orders to present an offering and incense to him.
The king said to Daniel, "Truly your God is the God of gods, the Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, for you have been able to reveal this mystery."
Then the king gave Daniel a high position and many great gifts. He made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
At Daniel's request, the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king's court.
King Nebuchadnezzar made a statue of gold, sixty cubits high and six cubits wide, and he set it up on the plain of Dura in the province of Babylon.

Then King Nebuchadnezzar sent word to gather the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates and all the officials of the provinces, to come to the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.

So the satraps, the prefects, the governors, the counselors, the treasurers, the judges, the magistrates and all the officials of the provinces gathered for the dedication of the statue that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up, and they stood in front of the statue that Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
Then the herald called out loudly, "This is the command to you, peoples, nations and languages:

As soon as you hear the sound of the horn, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the zither, the bagpipe and every kind of music, you must fall down and worship the statue of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar has set up.
Whoever does not fall down and worship will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire."

So as soon as all the peoples heard the sound of the horn, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the zither and every kind of music, all the peoples, nations and languages fell down and worshiped the statue of gold that King Nebuchadnezzar had set up.
At that time some Chaldeans came forward and denounced the Jews.
They said to King Nebuchadnezzar, "O king, live forever!

You, O king, have issued a decree that everyone who hears the sound of the horn, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the zither, the bagpipe and every kind of music must fall down and worship the statue of gold,
and that whoever does not fall down and worship will be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire.

There are some Jews whom you appointed over the administration of the province of Babylon: Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. These men pay no attention to you, O king. They do not serve your gods, and they do not worship the statue of gold that you have set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar, in a furious rage, ordered Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego to be brought in. So these men were brought before the king.
Nebuchadnezzar said to them, "Is it true, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, that you do not serve my gods, and that you do not worship the statue of gold that I have set up?

Now if you are ready, as soon as you hear the sound of the horn, the pipe, the lyre, the harp, the zither, the bagpipe and every kind of music, to fall down and worship the statue I have made, well and good. But if you do not worship, you will immediately be thrown into a furnace of blazing fire. And who is the god who will rescue you from my hands?"
Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego answered the king, "Nebuchadnezzar, we have no need to give you an answer in this matter.
If our God whom we serve is able to rescue us, he will rescue us from the furnace of blazing fire and from your hand, O king.
But even if he does not, be it known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods, and we will not worship the statue of gold that you have set up."
Then Nebuchadnezzar was filled with fury, and the look on his face changed toward Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego. He gave orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than it was usually heated.
He commanded some of the strongest men in his army to tie up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego and to throw them into the furnace of blazing fire.
So these men were tied up in their cloaks, their tunics, their hats and their other clothes, and they were thrown into the furnace of blazing fire.
Because the king's order was so harsh and the furnace so extremely hot, the flame of the fire killed the men who carried Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego up.
And these three men, Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, fell, tied up, into the furnace of blazing fire.
Then King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished and jumped up in alarm. He said to his advisers, "Didn't we throw three men, tied up, into the fire?" They answered the king, "Certainly, O king."
He said, "Look! I see four men, untied, walking in the middle of the fire, and they are unharmed. And the fourth looks like a son of the gods."

Then Nebuchadnezzar came near the door of the furnace of blazing fire and said, "Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, servants of the Most High God, come out! Come here!" Then Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego came out of the fire.

The satraps, the prefects, the governors and the king's advisers gathered around and saw these men. The fire had had no power over their bodies. The hair of their heads was not singed, their cloaks were not harmed, and there was no smell of fire on them.

Nebuchadnezzar said, "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego, who has sent his angel and rescued his servants who trusted in him. They defied the king's command and gave up their bodies rather than serve or worship any god except their own God.

So I issue a decree: anyone of any people, nation or language who says anything against the God of Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego will be torn limb from limb, and his house will be made a dunghill, for there is no other god who is able to rescue like this."
Then the king promoted Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego in the province of Babylon.
King Nebuchadnezzar, to all peoples, nations and languages who live in all the earth: May your peace be great!
It is my pleasure to make known the signs and wonders that the Most High God has done for me.
How great are his signs! How mighty are his wonders! His kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and his rule lasts from generation to generation.
I, Nebuchadnezzar, was at ease in my house and flourishing in my palace.
I had a dream, and it made me afraid. As I lay on my bed, the images and the visions that passed through my head terrified me.
So I issued a decree that all the wise men of Babylon should be brought in before me to make known to me the interpretation of the dream.
Then the magicians, the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners came in, and I told them the dream, but they did not make known to me its interpretation.
At last Daniel came in before me. His name is Belteshazzar, after the name of my god, and the spirit of the holy gods is in him. I told him the dream:

"Belteshazzar, chief of the magicians, I know that the spirit of the holy gods is in you, and that no mystery is too difficult for you. Tell me the visions of my dream that I saw, and its interpretation.
These were the visions that passed through my head as I lay on my bed: I was looking, and there was a tree in the middle of the earth, and its height was great.
The tree grew large and strong. Its top reached to the sky, and it could be seen to the ends of the whole earth.

Its leaves were beautiful and its fruit plentiful, and on it was food for all. Under it the wild animals found shade, and in its branches the birds of the sky lived, and from it every living creature was fed.
In the visions that passed through my head as I lay on my bed, I looked, and there was a watcher, a holy one, coming down from heaven.
He called out loudly and said, 'Cut down the tree and cut off its branches! Strip off its leaves and scatter its fruit! Let the animals flee from under it and the birds from its branches.

But leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his share be with the animals in the grass of the earth.
Let his mind be changed from a human mind, and let him be given the mind of an animal. And let seven periods of time pass over him.

The sentence is by the decree of the watchers, and the decision by the word of the holy ones, so that the living may know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of human beings. He gives it to whomever he wishes, and he sets over it the lowliest of people.'

This is the dream that I, King Nebuchadnezzar, saw. Now you, Belteshazzar, tell me its interpretation, for none of the wise men of my kingdom can make known to me its interpretation. But you can, because the spirit of the holy gods is in you."

Then Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, was dismayed for a while, and his thoughts terrified him. The king said, "Belteshazzar, do not let the dream or its interpretation alarm you." Belteshazzar answered, "My lord, may the dream be for those who hate you, and its interpretation for your enemies!
The tree that you saw, which grew large and strong, whose top reached to the sky and which could be seen through the whole earth,
whose leaves were beautiful and whose fruit was plentiful, on which was food for all, under which the wild animals lived, and in whose branches the birds of the sky nested,
it is you, O king! You have grown great and strong. Your greatness has grown and reaches to the sky, and your rule to the ends of the earth.

And as for the watcher, a holy one, whom the king saw coming down from heaven and saying, 'Cut down the tree and destroy it, but leave the stump with its roots in the ground, bound with iron and bronze, in the grass of the field. Let him be drenched with the dew of heaven, and let his share be with the wild animals, until seven periods of time pass over him,'
this is the interpretation, O king, and it is the decree of the Most High that has come upon my lord the king:

You will be driven away from people, and you will live with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like oxen and be drenched with the dew of heaven, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of human beings and gives it to whomever he wishes.
And as it was commanded to leave the stump with the roots of the tree, your kingdom will be secure for you from the time you know that Heaven rules.
Therefore, O king, may my advice be acceptable to you. Break off your sin by doing what is right, and your iniquities by showing mercy to the oppressed. Perhaps your prosperity will be prolonged."
All this came upon King Nebuchadnezzar.
At the end of twelve months he was walking on the roof of the royal palace of Babylon.
The king said, "Is this not great Babylon, which I have built as a royal residence by my mighty power and for the glory of my majesty?"
The words were still in the king's mouth when a voice came down from heaven: "To you it is declared, King Nebuchadnezzar: the kingdom has departed from you.

You will be driven away from people, and you will live with the wild animals. You will be fed grass like oxen, and seven periods of time will pass over you, until you know that the Most High rules over the kingdom of human beings and gives it to whomever he wishes."

At that very moment the word was fulfilled against Nebuchadnezzar. He was driven away from people and ate grass like oxen, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until his hair grew long like eagles' feathers and his nails like birds' claws.

At the end of that time, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted my eyes to heaven, and my reason returned to me. I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored the one who lives forever, for his rule is an everlasting rule, and his kingdom lasts from generation to generation.
All who live on the earth are counted as nothing. He does as he wishes with the host of heaven and with those who live on the earth. No one can hold back his hand or say to him, "What have you done?"

At that time my reason returned to me, and for the glory of my kingdom my majesty and splendor returned to me. My advisers and my nobles sought me out, and I was restored to my kingdom, and still greater majesty was added to me.
Now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, exalt and honor the King of heaven, for all his works are true and his ways are just, and he is able to humble those who walk in pride.
King Belshazzar gave a great feast for a thousand of his nobles, and he drank wine in front of the thousand.

Under the influence of the wine, Belshazzar gave orders to bring in the vessels of gold and silver that his father Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, so that the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines could drink from them.
So they brought in the vessels of gold that had been taken from the temple, the house of God in Jerusalem, and the king and his nobles, his wives and his concubines drank from them.
They drank wine and praised the gods of gold and silver, bronze, iron, wood and stone.
At that moment the fingers of a human hand appeared and wrote on the plaster of the wall of the king's palace, opposite the lampstand. And the king watched the hand as it wrote.
Then the king's face turned pale, and his thoughts terrified him. His legs gave way, and his knees knocked together.

The king called out loudly to bring in the enchanters, the Chaldeans and the diviners. The king said to the wise men of Babylon, "Whoever reads this writing and tells me its interpretation will be clothed in purple and have a chain of gold around his neck, and he will rule as third in the kingdom."
Then all the king's wise men came in, but they could not read the writing or make known its interpretation to the king.
Then King Belshazzar was greatly terrified, and his face turned pale, and his nobles were bewildered.
Because of the words of the king and his nobles, the queen came into the banquet hall. The queen said, "O king, live forever! Do not let your thoughts terrify you or your face turn pale.

There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods. In the days of your father, light, insight and wisdom like the wisdom of the gods were found in him. King Nebuchadnezzar your father, your father the king, made him chief of the magicians, enchanters, Chaldeans and diviners,

because an extraordinary spirit, knowledge and insight, and the ability to interpret dreams, explain riddles and solve problems were found in this Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will tell the interpretation."
Then Daniel was brought in before the king. The king said to Daniel, "Are you that Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, whom the king my father brought from Judah?
I have heard of you that the spirit of the gods is in you, and that light, insight and extraordinary wisdom are found in you.
Now the wise men and the enchanters were brought in before me to read this writing and make known to me its interpretation, but they could not tell the interpretation of the words.

But I have heard of you that you can give interpretations and solve problems. Now if you can read the writing and make known to me its interpretation, you will be clothed in purple and have a chain of gold around your neck, and you will rule as third in the kingdom."
Then Daniel answered the king, "Keep your gifts for yourself, and give your rewards to someone else. But I will read the writing to the king and make known to him the interpretation.
O king, the Most High God gave Nebuchadnezzar your father the kingdom, greatness, glory and majesty.

Because of the greatness he gave him, all peoples, nations and languages trembled in fear before him. Whomever he wished he killed, and whomever he wished he kept alive; whomever he wished he raised up, and whomever he wished he brought low.
But when his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened so that he acted proudly, he was brought down from his royal throne, and his glory was taken from him.

He was driven away from human beings, and his mind was made like that of an animal. He lived with the wild donkeys, he was fed grass like oxen, and his body was drenched with the dew of heaven, until he knew that the Most High God rules over the kingdom of human beings and sets over it whomever he wishes.
But you, his son Belshazzar, have not humbled your heart, though you knew all this.

You have lifted yourself up against the Lord of heaven. The vessels of his house were brought before you, and you and your nobles, your wives and your concubines have drunk wine from them. You have praised the gods of silver and gold, bronze, iron, wood and stone, which do not see or hear or know. But the God who holds in his hand your breath and all your ways, you have not honored.
So he sent the hand, and this writing was inscribed.
This is the writing that was inscribed: Mene, mene, tekel, u-pharsin.
This is the interpretation of the words: Mene: God has numbered your kingdom and brought it to an end.
Tekel: you have been weighed on the scales and found lacking.
Peres: your kingdom is divided and given to the Medes and Persians."
Then at Belshazzar's command they clothed Daniel in purple, put a chain of gold around his neck, and proclaimed that he would rule as third in the kingdom.
That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed.
And Darius the Mede received the kingdom, when he was about sixty-two years old.
It pleased Darius to appoint 120 satraps over the kingdom, to be throughout the whole kingdom,
and over them three chief officials, of whom Daniel was one. The satraps were to give account to them, so that the king would not suffer loss.
Then this Daniel distinguished himself above the chief officials and the satraps, because an extraordinary spirit was in him, and the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

Then the chief officials and the satraps tried to find grounds for a charge against Daniel in his conduct of the kingdom's affairs, but they could find no grounds and no corruption, because he was trustworthy, and no negligence or corruption was found in him.
Then these men said, "We will not find any grounds for a charge against this Daniel unless we find something against him in the law of his God."
Then these chief officials and satraps came as a group to the king and said to him, "King Darius, live forever!

All the chief officials of the kingdom, the prefects and the satraps, the advisers and the governors have agreed that the king should issue a decree and enforce a ban: anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, will be thrown into the lions' pit.
Now, O king, issue the ban and sign the document, so that it cannot be changed, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked."
So King Darius signed the document, the ban.

When Daniel knew that the document had been signed, he went into his house. In its upper room were windows open toward Jerusalem. Three times a day he knelt down, prayed and gave thanks before his God, just as he had done before.
Then these men came as a group and found Daniel making his request and pleading for mercy before his God.

So they came near and spoke before the king about the king's ban: "Did you not sign a ban that anyone who makes a request of any god or human being for thirty days, except of you, O king, will be thrown into the lions' pit?" The king answered, "The matter stands firm, according to the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be revoked."
Then they said before the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the ban that you have signed. Three times a day he makes his request."
When the king heard this, he was greatly distressed, and he set his mind on rescuing Daniel. Until the sun went down he did all he could to save him.
Then these men came as a group to the king and said to the king, "Know, O king, that it is a law of the Medes and Persians that no ban or decree that the king issues can be changed."
So the king gave the order, and Daniel was brought and thrown into the lions' pit. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!"
A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the pit, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the signet rings of his nobles, so that nothing might be changed concerning Daniel.
Then the king went to his palace and spent the night fasting. No entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
Then at dawn, as soon as it was light, the king got up and went in haste to the lions' pit.

When he came near the pit, he called to Daniel in an anguished voice. The king said to Daniel, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"
Then Daniel spoke with the king: "O king, live forever!
My God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. And before you too, O king, I have done no harm."
Then the king was overjoyed, and he ordered that Daniel be lifted out of the pit. So Daniel was lifted out of the pit, and no harm was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

At the king's command, the men who had denounced Daniel were brought and thrown into the lions' pit, they, their children and their wives. Before they reached the bottom of the pit, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations and languages who live in all the earth: "May your peace be great!

I issue a decree that in all the dominion of my kingdom people are to tremble with fear before the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, and he endures forever. His kingdom will never be destroyed, and his rule will last to the end.
He rescues and saves, and he does signs and wonders in heaven and on earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."
So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
In the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon, Daniel had a dream, and visions passed through his head as he lay on his bed. Then he wrote down the dream and told the main points of the account.
Daniel said, "I was looking in my vision by night, and there were the four winds of heaven stirring up the great sea.
Four great beasts came up out of the sea, each different from the others.

The first was like a lion and had eagle's wings. As I watched, its wings were plucked off, and it was lifted up from the ground and made to stand on two feet like a human being, and a human mind was given to it.
Then there was another beast, a second one, like a bear. It was raised up on one side, and it had three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. It was told, 'Get up, devour much flesh!'
After this I looked, and there was another, like a leopard. It had four wings of a bird on its back, and the beast had four heads, and it was given authority to rule.

After this I was looking in the visions of the night, and there was a fourth beast, terrifying and dreadful and extremely strong. It had great iron teeth. It devoured and crushed, and it trampled what was left with its feet. It was different from all the beasts before it, and it had ten horns.

While I was considering the horns, there was another horn, a small one, coming up among them, and three of the first horns were uprooted before it. This horn had eyes like human eyes and a mouth speaking arrogant words.

As I looked, thrones were set in place, and the Ancient of Days took his seat. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool. His throne was flames of fire, and its wheels were burning fire.

A river of fire was flowing, coming out from before him. Thousands upon thousands served him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him. The court sat in judgment, and the books were opened.
Then I kept looking because of the sound of the arrogant words that the horn was speaking. As I watched, the beast was killed, and its body destroyed and given over to the burning fire.
As for the rest of the beasts, their authority was taken away, but their lives were prolonged for a season and a time.
I was looking in the visions of the night, and there, with the clouds of heaven, one like a son of man was coming. He came to the Ancient of Days and was presented before him.

He was given authority, glory and kingship, so that all peoples, nations and languages would serve him. His authority is an everlasting authority that will not pass away, and his kingdom is one that will not be destroyed.
As for me, Daniel, my spirit was distressed within me, and the visions that passed through my head terrified me.
I approached one of those standing there and asked him the truth about all this. So he told me and made known to me the interpretation of these things:
'These great beasts, which are four, are four kings who will arise from the earth.
But the holy ones of the Most High will receive the kingdom, and they will possess the kingdom forever, forever and ever.'

Then I wanted to know the truth about the fourth beast, which was different from all the others, extremely terrifying, with teeth of iron and claws of bronze, which devoured and crushed and trampled what was left with its feet,
and about the ten horns on its head, and the other horn that came up, before which three fell: the horn that had eyes and a mouth speaking arrogant words, and that looked greater than the others.
As I watched, this horn was making war against the holy ones and was prevailing over them,
until the Ancient of Days came and judgment was given in favor of the holy ones of the Most High, and the time came when the holy ones took possession of the kingdom.
This is what he said: 'The fourth beast will be a fourth kingdom on earth, which will be different from all the kingdoms. It will devour the whole earth, trample it down and crush it.
As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings will arise, and another will arise after them. He will be different from the earlier ones, and he will bring down three kings.

He will speak words against the Most High and wear down the holy ones of the Most High. He will try to change the sacred seasons and the law, and they will be given into his hand for a time, times and half a time.
But the court will sit in judgment, and his authority will be taken away, to be destroyed and abolished forever.

Then the kingship and the authority and the greatness of the kingdoms under the whole heaven will be given to the people of the holy ones of the Most High. Their kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom, and all rulers will serve and obey them.'
