Here is the end of the account. As for me, Daniel, my thoughts greatly terrified me, and my face turned pale, but I kept the matter in my heart."
In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, after the one that had appeared to me before.
I looked in the vision, and as I looked, I was in the fortress of Susa, in the province of Elam. I looked in the vision, and I was beside the Ulai Canal.
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a ram standing beside the canal. It had two horns. Both horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one came up last.
I saw the ram charging westward, northward and southward. No beast could stand before it, and there was no one who could rescue from its power. It did as it pleased and made itself great.
As I was considering this, a male goat came from the west across the face of the whole earth, without touching the ground. The goat had a conspicuous horn between its eyes.
It came to the ram with the two horns, which I had seen standing beside the canal, and it charged at it in furious strength.

I saw it reach the ram. It was enraged against it, and it struck the ram and broke its two horns. The ram had no strength to stand before it. It threw the ram to the ground and trampled on it, and there was no one who could rescue the ram from its power.
The male goat made itself very great. But at the height of its power the great horn was broken, and in its place four conspicuous horns came up toward the four winds of heaven.
Out of one of them came another horn, a small one, which grew exceedingly great toward the south, toward the east and toward the beautiful land.
It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it threw down to the earth some of the host and some of the stars, and trampled on them.
It made itself great, even up to the commander of the host. The regular offering was taken away from him, and the place of his sanctuary was thrown down.
Because of transgression, the host was given over, together with the regular offering. It threw truth to the ground, and it acted and succeeded.

Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to the one who was speaking, "How long will the vision last, concerning the regular offering, the transgression that makes desolate, and the giving over of both the sanctuary and the host to be trampled?"
He said to me, "For 2,300 evenings and mornings. Then the sanctuary will be restored to its rightful state."
While I, Daniel, was seeing the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one who looked like a man.
And I heard a human voice from between the banks of the Ulai, and it called out, "Gabriel, make this man understand the vision."
He came near where I stood, and when he came I was terrified and fell on my face. He said to me, "Understand, son of man, that the vision is for the time of the end."
While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep with my face to the ground. Then he touched me and set me on my feet.
He said, "I am going to make known to you what will happen at the end of the time of wrath, for it concerns the appointed time of the end.
The ram that you saw with the two horns: these are the kings of Media and Persia.
The shaggy male goat is the king of Greece, and the great horn between its eyes is the first king.
As for the horn that was broken and the four that arose in its place: four kingdoms will arise from his nation, but not with his power.
At the end of their rule, when the transgressors have reached their full measure, a king will arise, fierce-looking and skilled in intrigue.
His power will be mighty, but not by his own power. He will cause astonishing destruction, and he will succeed in what he does. He will destroy the mighty and the people of the holy ones.

By his cunning he will make deceit succeed under his hand, and in his heart he will make himself great. Without warning he will destroy many. He will even stand up against the Prince of princes, but he will be broken, and not by human hand.
The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been told is true. But you, keep the vision secret, for it refers to many days from now."
And I, Daniel, was overcome and lay sick for some days. Then I got up and went about the king's business. But I was appalled by the vision, and no one could explain it.
In the first year of Darius son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by descent, who was made king over the kingdom of the Babylonians,

in the first year of his reign, I, Daniel, understood from the books the number of years that, according to the word of the LORD to Jeremiah the prophet, must pass until the desolation of Jerusalem came to an end: seventy years.
So I turned my face to the Lord God, to seek him by prayer and pleas for mercy, with fasting, sackcloth and ashes.
I prayed to the LORD my God and made confession. I said, "Ah, Lord, the great and awesome God, who keeps covenant and faithful love with those who love him and keep his commands,
we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled, turning away from your commands and your rulings.
We have not listened to your servants the prophets, who spoke in your name to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, and to all the people of the land.

To you, Lord, belongs righteousness, but to us open shame, as it is this day: to the people of Judah, to those who live in Jerusalem, and to all Israel, those near and those far away, in all the lands to which you have driven them because of the unfaithfulness they have committed against you.
LORD, to us belongs open shame: to our kings, our officials and our ancestors, because we have sinned against you.
To the Lord our God belong compassion and forgiveness, though we have rebelled against him.
We have not obeyed the voice of the LORD our God by living according to his instructions, which he set before us through his servants the prophets.

All Israel has broken your law and turned away, refusing to obey your voice. So the curse and the oath written in the Law of Moses, the servant of God, have been poured out on us, because we have sinned against him.

He has carried out his word that he spoke against us and against our rulers who ruled us, by bringing on us a great disaster. Under the whole heaven nothing has ever been done like what has been done to Jerusalem.
Just as it is written in the Law of Moses, all this disaster has come on us. Yet we have not sought the favor of the LORD our God by turning from our iniquities and paying heed to your truth.
So the LORD kept watch over the disaster and brought it on us, for the LORD our God is righteous in all the works he has done, and we have not obeyed his voice.
And now, Lord our God, who brought your people out of the land of Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for yourself, as it is this day, we have sinned, we have acted wickedly.

Lord, in keeping with all your righteous acts, let your anger and your wrath turn away from your city Jerusalem, your holy mountain. Because of our sins and the iniquities of our ancestors, Jerusalem and your people have become a disgrace to all who are around us.
Now, our God, listen to the prayer of your servant and to his pleas for mercy. For the Lord's sake, make your face shine on your desolate sanctuary.

Turn your ear, my God, and hear. Open your eyes and see our desolations and the city that is called by your name. We do not lay our pleas before you because of our righteous acts, but because of your great compassion.
Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, listen and act! Do not delay, for your own sake, my God, for your city and your people are called by your name."
While I was still speaking and praying, confessing my sin and the sin of my people Israel, and laying my plea before the LORD my God for the holy mountain of my God,
while I was still speaking in prayer, the man Gabriel, whom I had seen in the vision at the first, came to me in swift flight at about the time of the evening offering.
He gave me understanding and spoke with me. He said, "Daniel, I have now come out to give you insight and understanding.
At the beginning of your pleas for mercy a word went out, and I have come to tell it to you, for you are greatly loved. So consider the word and understand the vision.

Seventy weeks are decreed for your people and your holy city, to finish the transgression, to put an end to sin, to atone for iniquity, to bring in everlasting righteousness, to seal up vision and prophet, and to anoint a most holy place.

Know and understand this: from the going out of the word to restore and rebuild Jerusalem until an anointed one, a ruler, there will be seven weeks. Then for sixty-two weeks it will be built again, with square and moat, but in troubled times.

After the sixty-two weeks, an anointed one will be cut off and will have nothing. The people of a ruler who is to come will destroy the city and the sanctuary. Its end will come with a flood, and to the end there will be war. Desolations are decreed.

He will make a firm covenant with many for one week, and for half of the week he will put a stop to sacrifice and offering. And on a wing of abominations will come one who makes desolate, until the end that is decreed is poured out on the one who makes desolate."

In the third year of Cyrus king of Persia, a word was revealed to Daniel, who was called Belteshazzar. The word was true, and it concerned a great conflict. He understood the word and had understanding of the vision.
At that time I, Daniel, had been mourning for three whole weeks.
I ate no rich food, no meat or wine entered my mouth, and I did not anoint myself at all until the three whole weeks were over.
On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was on the bank of the great river, the Tigris.
I lifted my eyes and looked, and there was a man dressed in linen, with a belt of fine gold from Uphaz around his waist.

His body was like beryl, his face like the appearance of lightning, his eyes like flaming torches, his arms and his legs like the gleam of polished bronze, and the sound of his words like the sound of a multitude.
I, Daniel, was the only one who saw the vision. The men who were with me did not see the vision, but great terror fell on them, and they fled and hid themselves.
So I was left alone, and I saw this great vision. No strength was left in me. My face turned deathly pale, and I retained no strength.
Then I heard the sound of his words, and as I heard the sound of his words, I fell into a deep sleep on my face, with my face to the ground.
Then a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and the palms of my hands.

He said to me, "Daniel, greatly loved man, understand the words that I am speaking to you, and stand up where you are, for I have now been sent to you." When he had spoken this word to me, I stood up trembling.

Then he said to me, "Do not be afraid, Daniel, for from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to humble yourself before your God, your words have been heard, and I have come because of your words.
The prince of the kingdom of Persia stood against me for twenty-one days. Then Michael, one of the chief princes, came to help me, and I was left there with the kings of Persia.
Now I have come to make you understand what will happen to your people in the last days, for the vision is for days yet to come."
While he was speaking these words with me, I turned my face toward the ground and was speechless.

Then one who looked like a human being touched my lips. I opened my mouth and spoke, and I said to the one standing before me, "My lord, because of the vision pains have come over me, and I retain no strength.
How can my lord's servant speak with my lord? As for me, no strength remains in me now, and no breath is left in me."
Then the one who looked like a human being touched me again and strengthened me.
He said, "Do not be afraid, greatly loved man. Peace be with you. Be strong, be strong!" As he spoke with me, I was strengthened, and I said, "Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me."
Then he said, "Do you know why I have come to you? Now I will go back to fight against the prince of Persia, and when I go out, the prince of Greece will come.
But I will tell you what is written in the book of truth. There is no one who stands firmly with me against these except Michael, your prince.
"And as for me, in the first year of Darius the Mede, I stood up to support and strengthen him.

Now I will tell you the truth. Three more kings will arise in Persia, and the fourth will be far richer than all of them. When he has grown strong through his riches, he will stir up everyone against the kingdom of Greece.
Then a mighty king will arise, who will rule with great authority and do as he pleases.

But as soon as he has arisen, his kingdom will be broken and divided toward the four winds of heaven. It will not go to his descendants, nor will it have the power with which he ruled, for his kingdom will be uprooted and given to others besides these.
The king of the south will grow strong, but one of his commanders will grow stronger than he and will rule, and his dominion will be a great dominion.

After some years they will make an alliance. The daughter of the king of the south will come to the king of the north to make an agreement, but she will not keep her power, and he and his power will not last. She will be given up, together with those who brought her, her father and the one who supported her in those times.
A shoot from her roots will arise in his place. He will come against the army and enter the fortress of the king of the north. He will deal with them and prevail.
He will also carry off to Egypt their gods, with their cast images and their precious vessels of silver and gold. Then for some years he will keep away from the king of the north.
Then the king of the north will come into the realm of the king of the south, but he will return to his own land.
His sons will prepare for war and assemble a multitude of great forces. One of them will keep coming, overflow and pass through, and again he will wage war as far as his fortress.
Then the king of the south will be enraged and go out and fight against him, the king of the north. He will raise a great multitude, but the multitude will be given into his hand.
When the multitude has been carried off, his heart will be lifted up. He will bring down tens of thousands, but he will not prevail.
For the king of the north will again raise a multitude, greater than the first, and after some years he will come on with a great army and much equipment.
In those times many will rise up against the king of the south. Violent men from among your own people will lift themselves up to fulfill the vision, but they will stumble.
Then the king of the north will come and pile up a siege ramp and capture a fortified city. The forces of the south will not stand, not even his chosen troops, and there will be no strength to stand.
The one who comes against him will do as he pleases, and no one will stand before him. He will stand in the beautiful land, and destruction will be in his hand.

He will set his face to come with the strength of his whole kingdom, and he will make an agreement with him and carry it out. He will give him a daughter in marriage in order to destroy the kingdom, but she will not stand by him or be on his side.
Then he will turn his face to the coastlands and capture many. But a commander will put an end to his insolence; indeed, he will turn his insolence back on him.
Then he will turn his face back toward the fortresses of his own land, but he will stumble and fall and be found no more.
In his place will arise one who sends an oppressor through the glory of the kingdom. But within a few days he will be broken, though not in anger or in battle.
In his place will arise a contemptible person, who has not been given royal majesty. He will come in without warning and seize the kingdom through intrigue.
Overwhelming forces will be swept away before him and broken, and also a prince of the covenant.
After an alliance is made with him, he will act deceitfully. He will rise to power with only a small nation.

Without warning he will come into the richest parts of the province and do what neither his ancestors nor their ancestors had done: he will scatter plunder, spoil and goods among them. He will devise plans against fortresses, but only for a time.

He will stir up his strength and his courage against the king of the south with a great army, and the king of the south will wage war with a very great and powerful army, but he will not stand, because of the plots devised against him.
Those who eat his food will destroy him. His army will be swept away, and many will fall slain.
The two kings, their hearts set on evil, will sit at one table and speak lies to each other, but it will not succeed, for the end is still to come at the appointed time.
He will return to his land with great wealth, but his heart will be set against the holy covenant. He will take action and return to his own land.
At the appointed time he will come again into the south, but this time it will not be as it was before.

Ships of Kittim will come against him, and he will lose heart. He will turn back and rage against the holy covenant and take action. He will return and pay heed to those who abandon the holy covenant.
Forces sent by him will rise up and profane the sanctuary, the fortress. They will take away the regular offering and set up the abomination that causes desolation.
Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will corrupt with flattery, but the people who know their God will stand firm and take action.
Those among the people who are wise will give understanding to many, though for some days they will fall by sword and flame, by captivity and plunder.
When they fall, they will receive a little help, and many will join them insincerely.
Some of the wise will fall, so that they may be refined, purified and made white, until the time of the end, for it is still to come at the appointed time.

The king will do as he pleases. He will exalt himself and make himself greater than every god, and he will say astonishing things against the God of gods. He will succeed until the wrath is completed, for what has been decreed will be done.
He will pay no attention to the gods of his ancestors, or to the one desired by women, or to any god, for he will make himself greater than them all.
Instead, he will honor a god of fortresses in their place. A god whom his ancestors did not know he will honor with gold and silver, with precious stones and costly gifts.
He will deal with the strongest fortresses with the help of a foreign god. Those who acknowledge him he will greatly honor. He will make them rulers over many and distribute land as a reward.

At the time of the end the king of the south will engage him in battle, but the king of the north will storm against him with chariots and horsemen and many ships. He will invade countries, overflow and pass through.
He will enter the beautiful land, and many will fall. But these will escape from his hand: Edom, Moab and the leaders of the Ammonites.
He will stretch out his hand against countries, and the land of Egypt will not escape.
He will gain control of the treasures of gold and silver and all the precious things of Egypt, and the Libyans and the Cushites will follow in his steps.
But reports from the east and the north will alarm him, and he will go out in great fury to destroy many and devote them to destruction.
He will pitch his royal tents between the seas and the beautiful holy mountain. Yet he will come to his end, and no one will help him.

"At that time Michael, the great prince who stands guard over your people, will arise. There will be a time of distress such as has never been since there was a nation until that time. But at that time your people will be delivered, everyone who is found written in the book.
Many of those who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, and some to disgrace and everlasting contempt.
Those who are wise will shine like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever.
But you, Daniel, keep the words secret and seal the book until the time of the end. Many will run to and fro, and knowledge will increase."
Then I, Daniel, looked, and there stood two others, one on this bank of the river and one on that bank of the river.
One of them said to the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river, "How long will it be until the end of these wonders?"

I heard the man dressed in linen, who was above the waters of the river. He raised his right hand and his left hand toward heaven and swore by the one who lives forever that it would be for a time, times and half a time, and that when the shattering of the power of the holy people comes to an end, all these things will be completed.
I heard, but I did not understand. So I said, "My lord, what will be the outcome of these things?"
He said, "Go your way, Daniel, for the words are kept secret and sealed until the time of the end.
Many will be purified, made white and refined, but the wicked will act wickedly. None of the wicked will understand, but those who are wise will understand.
From the time that the regular offering is taken away and the abomination that causes desolation is set up, there will be 1,290 days.
Blessed is the one who waits and reaches 1,335 days.
But you, go your way to the end. You will rest, and you will rise to receive your allotted share at the end of the days."
The word of the LORD that came to Hosea son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash, king of Israel.

When the LORD first spoke through Hosea, the LORD said to Hosea, "Go, take for yourself a wife given to prostitution, and children of prostitution, for the land is committing flagrant prostitution by turning away from the LORD."
So he went and married Gomer daughter of Diblaim, and she conceived and bore him a son.
The LORD said to him, "Name him Jezreel, for in a little while I will punish the house of Jehu for the bloodshed of Jezreel, and I will put an end to the kingdom of the house of Israel.
On that day I will break the bow of Israel in the Valley of Jezreel."
She conceived again and bore a daughter. The LORD said to him, "Name her Lo-ruhamah, for I will no longer have compassion on the house of Israel, that I should forgive them at all.
But I will have compassion on the house of Judah, and I will save them by the LORD their God. I will not save them by bow or sword or battle, by horses or horsemen."
After she had weaned Lo-ruhamah, she conceived and bore a son.
The LORD said, "Name him Lo-ammi, for you are not my people, and I will not be yours."

Yet the number of the Israelites will be like the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured or counted. And in the place where it was said to them, "You are not my people," it will be said to them, "Children of the living God."
The people of Judah and the people of Israel will be gathered together. They will appoint for themselves one head, and they will go up from the land, for great will be the day of Jezreel.
Say to your brothers, "Ammi," and to your sisters, "Ruhamah."
Bring charges against your mother, bring charges, for she is not my wife, and I am not her husband. Let her remove her prostitution from her face and her adultery from between her breasts,
or I will strip her naked and expose her as on the day she was born. I will make her like a wilderness, turn her into a parched land, and kill her with thirst.
I will have no compassion on her children, because they are children of prostitution.

For their mother has prostituted herself; she who conceived them has acted shamefully. For she said, "I will go after my lovers, who give me my bread and my water, my wool and my flax, my oil and my drink."
Therefore I am going to hedge up your way with thorns, and I will build a wall against her, so that she cannot find her paths.
She will pursue her lovers but not overtake them; she will look for them but not find them. Then she will say, "I will go back to my first husband, for it was better for me then than now."
She did not know that it was I who gave her the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and who lavished on her the silver and gold that they used for Baal.
Therefore I will take back my grain in its time and my new wine in its season, and I will snatch away my wool and my flax, which were to cover her nakedness.
Now I will uncover her shame before the eyes of her lovers, and no one will rescue her from my hand.
I will put an end to all her celebrations: her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths and all her appointed feasts.
I will lay waste her vines and her fig trees, of which she said, "These are my wages, which my lovers gave me." I will turn them into a thicket, and the wild animals will devour them.

I will punish her for the feast days of the Baals, when she burned incense to them and decked herself with her nose ring and her jewelry, and went after her lovers, but me she forgot, declares the LORD.
Therefore I am going to win her back. I will lead her into the wilderness and speak tenderly to her.
There I will give her back her vineyards, and make the Valley of Achor a door of hope. There she will respond as in the days of her youth, as on the day she came up out of the land of Egypt.
On that day, declares the LORD, you will call me "My husband," and you will no longer call me "My Baal."
I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, and they will no longer be remembered by name.

On that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals, the birds of the sky and the creatures that creep on the ground. I will break bow and sword and battle and banish them from the land, and I will let them lie down in safety.
I will betroth you to myself forever. I will betroth you to myself in righteousness and justice, in faithful love and compassion.
I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the LORD.
On that day I will answer, declares the LORD. I will answer the heavens, and they will answer the earth.
The earth will answer the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, and they will answer Jezreel.
I will sow her for myself in the land. I will have compassion on Lo-ruhamah, and I will say to Lo-ammi, "You are my people," and he will say, "My God."
The LORD said to me, "Go again, love a woman who is loved by another man and is an adulteress, just as the LORD loves the Israelites, though they turn to other gods and love raisin cakes."
So I bought her for myself for fifteen shekels of silver and a homer and a lethech of barley.
Then I said to her, "You are to live with me for many days. You must not be a prostitute or belong to any man, and I too will be faithful to you."
For the Israelites will live for many days without king or official, without sacrifice or standing stone, without ephod or household gods.
Afterward the Israelites will return and seek the LORD their God and David their king. They will come trembling to the LORD and to his goodness in the last days.
Hear the word of the LORD, you Israelites, for the LORD has a case against those who live in the land. There is no faithfulness, no faithful love, no knowledge of God in the land.
There is cursing, lying, murder, stealing and adultery. They break all bounds, and bloodshed follows bloodshed.
Therefore the land mourns, and all who live in it waste away, along with the wild animals and the birds of the sky, and even the fish of the sea are swept away.
Yet let no one bring a charge, and let no one accuse, for your people are like those who bring charges against a priest.
You will stumble by day, and the prophet will stumble with you by night, and I will destroy your mother.

My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I reject you from serving as my priest. Since you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children.
The more they increased, the more they sinned against me. I will change their glory into shame.
They feed on the sin of my people, and they long for their iniquity.
It will be like people, like priest. I will punish them for their ways and repay them for their deeds.
They will eat but not be satisfied; they will prostitute themselves but not increase, for they have abandoned the LORD and stopped heeding him.
Prostitution, wine and new wine take away understanding.
My people consult their piece of wood, and their staff gives them answers. For a spirit of prostitution has led them astray, and they have prostituted themselves and left their God.

They sacrifice on the tops of the mountains and burn incense on the hills, under oak, poplar and terebinth, because their shade is pleasant. That is why your daughters turn to prostitution and your daughters-in-law commit adultery.

I will not punish your daughters when they turn to prostitution, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, for the men themselves go off with prostitutes and sacrifice with shrine prostitutes. A people without understanding will come to ruin.
Though you, Israel, play the prostitute, do not let Judah become guilty. Do not go to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear, "As the LORD lives!"
For Israel is stubborn, like a stubborn heifer. Can the LORD now pasture them like a lamb in a broad meadow?
Ephraim is joined to idols; leave him alone!
When their drinking is over, they give themselves to prostitution. Her rulers dearly love shame.
A wind has wrapped her up in its wings, and they will be put to shame because of their sacrifices.
Hear this, you priests! Pay attention, house of Israel! Listen, house of the king! For the judgment is for you, because you have been a snare at Mizpah and a net spread out on Tabor.
The rebels have gone deep into slaughter, but I will discipline them all.
I know Ephraim, and Israel is not hidden from me. For now, Ephraim, you have prostituted yourself; Israel is defiled.
Their deeds do not allow them to return to their God, for a spirit of prostitution is within them, and they do not know the LORD.
Israel's pride testifies against him. Israel and Ephraim will stumble in their iniquity, and Judah also will stumble with them.
With their flocks and their herds they will go to seek the LORD, but they will not find him; he has withdrawn from them.
They have been unfaithful to the LORD, for they have borne children who are not his. Now the new moon will devour them along with their fields.
Blow the horn in Gibeah, the trumpet in Ramah! Sound the alarm in Beth-aven! Behind you, Benjamin!
Ephraim will become a desolation on the day of punishment. Among the tribes of Israel I make known what is certain.
The officials of Judah have become like those who move a boundary stone. I will pour out my fury on them like water.
Ephraim is oppressed, crushed in judgment, because he was determined to follow a command.
I am like a moth to Ephraim, like rot to the house of Judah.
When Ephraim saw his sickness and Judah his wound, Ephraim went to Assyria and sent to the great king. But he cannot heal you or cure you of your wound.
For I will be like a lion to Ephraim, like a young lion to the house of Judah. I myself will tear them to pieces and go away; I will carry them off, and no one will rescue them.
I will go back to my place until they admit their guilt and seek my face. In their distress they will earnestly seek me.
"Come, let us return to the LORD. For he has torn us, but he will heal us; he has struck us, but he will bind up our wounds.
After two days he will revive us; on the third day he will raise us up, so that we may live before him.
Let us know, let us press on to know the LORD. His coming is as sure as the dawn. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth."
What shall I do with you, Ephraim? What shall I do with you, Judah? Your faithful love is like the morning mist, like the dew that goes away early.
That is why I have cut them to pieces by the prophets; I have killed them by the words of my mouth, and my judgment goes out like light.
For I desire faithful love, not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
But like Adam they have broken the covenant; there they have been unfaithful to me.
Gilead is a city of evildoers, tracked with bloody footprints.
As bands of robbers lie in wait for someone, so the company of priests murder on the road to Shechem. Indeed, they have committed shameful crimes.
In the house of Israel I have seen a horrible thing. Ephraim's prostitution is there; Israel is defiled.
For you also, Judah, a harvest is appointed, when I restore the fortunes of my people.
When I would heal Israel, the iniquity of Ephraim is exposed, and the wicked deeds of Samaria. For they practice deceit; a thief breaks in, and a band of raiders attacks in the street.
But they do not consider that I remember all their wickedness. Now their deeds surround them; they are before my face.
They make the king glad with their wickedness, and the officials with their lies.
They are all adulterers. They are like an oven heated by a baker, who stops stirring the fire from the kneading of the dough until it is leavened.
On the day of our king, the officials became sick with the heat of wine; he joined hands with mockers.
For they draw near with their hearts like an oven in their plotting. All night their baker sleeps; in the morning it blazes like a flaming fire.
All of them are hot as an oven, and they devour their rulers. All their kings have fallen, and none of them calls on me.
Ephraim mixes himself with the peoples. Ephraim is a flat cake not turned over.
Foreigners devour his strength, but he does not know it. Gray hair is sprinkled on him, but he does not know it.
Israel's pride testifies against him, yet they do not return to the LORD their God or seek him in spite of all this.
Ephraim is like a dove, easily fooled and without sense. They call to Egypt; they go to Assyria.
As they go, I will spread my net over them; I will bring them down like the birds of the sky. I will discipline them according to the report to their assembly.
Woe to them, for they have strayed from me! Destruction to them, for they have rebelled against me! I would redeem them, but they speak lies about me.
They do not cry out to me from their hearts when they wail on their beds. For grain and new wine they gather together; they turn away from me.
Though I trained and strengthened their arms, they plot evil against me.

They turn, but not to the Most High; they are like a faulty bow. Their officials will fall by the sword because of the insolence of their tongues. This will make them a laughingstock in the land of Egypt.
Put the horn to your lips! An eagle is over the house of the LORD, because they have broken my covenant and rebelled against my law.
They cry out to me, "My God, we, Israel, know you!"
Israel has rejected what is good; an enemy will pursue him.
They set up kings, but not through me; they appointed officials, but without my knowledge. With their silver and their gold they made idols for themselves, so that they will be cut off.
He has rejected your calf, Samaria! My anger burns against them. How long will they be incapable of innocence?
For it is from Israel! A craftsman made it; it is not God. The calf of Samaria will be broken to pieces.
For they sow the wind, and they will reap the whirlwind. The standing grain has no head; it will produce no flour. Even if it should produce, foreigners would swallow it up.
Israel is swallowed up. Now they are among the nations like a worthless vessel.
For they have gone up to Assyria, a wild donkey wandering alone. Ephraim has hired lovers.
Even though they hire them among the nations, I will now gather them together. Soon they will writhe under the burden of the king of princes.
Because Ephraim has multiplied altars for sinning, they have become to him altars for sinning.
Though I write for him the many things of my law, they are regarded as something strange.
They sacrifice meat as gifts to me and eat it, but the LORD does not accept them. Now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins. They will return to Egypt.
Israel has forgotten his Maker and built palaces, and Judah has multiplied fortified cities. But I will send fire on his cities, and it will devour their strongholds.
Do not rejoice, Israel; do not exult like the peoples. For you have prostituted yourself and left your God. You have loved a prostitute's wages on every threshing floor of grain.
Threshing floor and winepress will not feed them, and the new wine will fail her.
They will not remain in the land of the LORD. Ephraim will return to Egypt, and in Assyria they will eat unclean food.

They will not pour out wine offerings to the LORD, and their sacrifices will not please him. They will be like the bread of mourners to them; all who eat it will be defiled. For their bread will be for themselves alone; it will not come into the house of the LORD.
What will you do on the day of the appointed festival, on the day of the LORD's feast?

For look, they have gone away from destruction, but Egypt will gather them, and Memphis will bury them. Nettles will take possession of their precious things of silver, and thorns will grow in their tents.

The days of punishment have come; the days of repayment have come. Let Israel know it! "The prophet is a fool, the man of the spirit is mad!" So it is because of your great iniquity, and your hostility is great.
The prophet is a watchman over Ephraim with my God, yet a fowler's snare is on all his ways, and hostility in the house of his God.
They have sunk deep into corruption, as in the days of Gibeah. He will remember their iniquity; he will punish their sins.

Like grapes in the wilderness I found Israel; like the first fruit on the fig tree in its first season I saw your ancestors. But they came to Baal-peor and dedicated themselves to the Shameful Thing, and they became detestable, like the thing they loved.
Ephraim's glory will fly away like a bird: no birth, no pregnancy, no conception.
Even if they raise children, I will bereave them until no one is left. Woe to them indeed when I turn away from them!
Ephraim, as I saw, was like Tyre, planted in a pleasant meadow; but Ephraim will bring out his children to the slayer.
Give them, the LORD—what will you give? Give them a womb that miscarries and breasts that are dry.
All their wickedness is in Gilgal; there I came to hate them. Because of their wicked deeds I will drive them out of my house. I will love them no more; all their officials are rebels.
Ephraim is struck down; their root is dried up; they will bear no fruit. Even if they give birth, I will kill the precious offspring of their womb.
My God will reject them, because they have not listened to him, and they will be wanderers among the nations.
Israel is a luxuriant vine that yields its fruit. The more his fruit increased, the more altars he built; the better his land became, the finer he made his standing stones.
Their heart is false; now they must bear their guilt. He will break down their altars and destroy their standing stones.
For now they will say, "We have no king, because we did not fear the LORD. And the king, what could he do for us?"
They speak mere words, swear empty oaths and make covenants. So lawsuits spring up like poisonous weeds in the furrows of a field.
The inhabitants of Samaria fear for the calf of Beth-aven. Its people mourn over it, and its idolatrous priests wail over it, over its glory, because it has gone into exile from them.
It too will be carried to Assyria as tribute to the great king. Ephraim will be put to shame, and Israel will be ashamed of his own plans.
Samaria and her king will be cut off like a twig on the surface of the water.
The high places of Aven, the sin of Israel, will be destroyed. Thorns and thistles will grow up over their altars. Then they will say to the mountains, "Cover us!" and to the hills, "Fall on us!"
Since the days of Gibeah you have sinned, Israel. There they have remained. Will not war overtake them in Gibeah, war against the wicked?
When I choose, I will discipline them. Nations will be gathered against them, when they are bound for their double iniquity.
Ephraim was a trained heifer that loved to thresh, and I spared her fair neck. But now I will harness Ephraim; Judah must plow; Jacob must harrow for himself.
Sow for yourselves righteousness; reap the fruit of faithful love. Break up your unplowed ground, for it is time to seek the LORD, until he comes and rains righteousness on you.
You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; you have eaten the fruit of lies. Because you have trusted in your own way and in the great number of your warriors,

the roar of battle will rise among your people, and all your fortresses will be destroyed, as Shalman destroyed Beth-arbel on the day of battle, when mothers were dashed to pieces with their children.
This is what Bethel will do to you, because of your great wickedness. At dawn the king of Israel will be utterly cut off.
When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son.
The more they were called, the more they went away from them. They kept sacrificing to the Baals and burning incense to carved images.
Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them by their arms, but they did not know that I healed them.
I led them with cords of human kindness, with bands of love. I was to them like those who lift a yoke from their jaws, and I bent down to them and fed them.
He will not return to the land of Egypt, but Assyria will be his king, because they refused to return to me.
The sword will whirl through his cities; it will destroy the bars of his gates and devour them because of their schemes.
My people are bent on turning away from me. They call him upward, but he will not raise them up at all.
How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over, Israel? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned over within me; all my compassion is stirred.
I will not carry out my burning anger; I will not again destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not a human being, the Holy One among you, and I will not come in wrath.
They will follow the LORD; he will roar like a lion. When he roars, his children will come trembling from the west.
They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, like doves from the land of Assyria, and I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.
Ephraim has surrounded me with lies, and the house of Israel with deceit. But Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.
Ephraim feeds on the wind and pursues the east wind all day long. He multiplies lies and violence. They make a covenant with Assyria, and olive oil is carried to Egypt.
The LORD has a case against Judah; he will punish Jacob according to his ways and repay him according to his deeds.
In the womb he grasped his brother's heel, and in his manhood he struggled with God.
He struggled with the angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with him. He found him at Bethel, and there he spoke with us.
The LORD, the God of Armies, the LORD is his name!
As for you, return to your God with his help. Keep faithful love and justice, and wait for your God continually.
A merchant, in whose hands are false scales, he loves to oppress.
Ephraim says, "Surely I have become rich; I have found wealth for myself. In all my labor they will find in me no iniquity that is sin."
But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. I will make you live in tents again, as in the days of the appointed festival.
I spoke to the prophets; it was I who multiplied visions, and through the prophets I spoke in parables.
If Gilead is wicked, surely they are worthless. In Gilgal they sacrifice bulls; their altars will be like heaps of stones in the furrows of a field.
Jacob fled to the country of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept sheep.
By a prophet the LORD brought Israel up from Egypt, and by a prophet Israel was kept.
Ephraim has provoked bitter anger, so his Lord will leave his bloodguilt on him and repay him for his contempt.
When Ephraim spoke, there was trembling; he was exalted in Israel. But he incurred guilt through Baal and died.
Now they sin more and more. They make for themselves cast images from their silver, idols skillfully made, all of them the work of craftsmen. They say of them, "Let those who sacrifice kiss calves!"
Therefore they will be like the morning mist, like the dew that goes away early, like chaff that swirls from a threshing floor, like smoke from a window.
But I am the LORD your God from the land of Egypt. You know no God but me, and there is no savior except me.
It was I who knew you in the wilderness, in the land of drought.
When they had pasture, they were filled; they were filled, and their hearts were lifted up. That is why they forgot me.
So I will be like a lion to them; like a leopard I will lurk by the road.
I will meet them like a bear robbed of her cubs, and I will tear open their chests. There I will devour them like a lioness; the wild animals will rip them apart.
It is your destruction, Israel, that you are against me, against your helper.
Where now is your king, that he may save you in all your cities? And where are your rulers, of whom you said, "Give me a king and officials"?
I gave you a king in my anger, and I took him away in my wrath.
Ephraim's iniquity is bound up; his sin is stored away.
The pains of childbirth come on him, but he is an unwise child, for when the time comes he does not present himself at the opening of the womb.
Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? Shall I redeem them from death? Where, O death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your destruction? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.

Though he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come, the wind of the LORD rising from the wilderness. His spring will dry up, and his fountain will fail. He will plunder his treasury of every precious thing.
Samaria will bear her guilt, because she has rebelled against her God. They will fall by the sword; their little ones will be dashed to pieces, and their pregnant women ripped open.
Return, Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled because of your iniquity.
Take words with you and return to the LORD. Say to him, "Take away all iniquity and accept what is good, and we will offer our lips as bulls.
Assyria will not save us; we will not ride on horses. We will never again say 'Our God' to the work of our hands, for in you the orphan finds compassion."
I will heal their unfaithfulness; I will love them freely, for my anger has turned away from him.
I will be like the dew to Israel; he will blossom like the lily, and he will strike roots like Lebanon.
His shoots will spread out; his splendor will be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.
Those who live in his shade will return. They will flourish like grain; they will blossom like the vine. His fame will be like the wine of Lebanon.
Ephraim, what more have I to do with idols? It is I who answer and watch over him. I am like a luxuriant cypress; your fruit comes from me.
Who is wise? Let him understand these things. Who is discerning? Let him know them. For the ways of the LORD are right, and the righteous walk in them, but rebels stumble in them.
The word of the LORD that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, you elders! Listen, all who live in the land! Has anything like this happened in your days, or in the days of your ancestors?
Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children the next generation.
What the cutting locust left, the swarming locust has eaten; what the swarming locust left, the hopping locust has eaten; and what the hopping locust left, the destroying locust has eaten.
Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! Wail, all you wine drinkers, because of the sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.
For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number. Its teeth are a lion's teeth, and it has the fangs of a lioness.
It has laid waste my vine and splintered my fig tree. It has stripped off their bark and thrown it away; their branches are left white.
Mourn like a young woman dressed in sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of the LORD. The priests mourn, those who serve the LORD.
The fields are ruined; the ground mourns, for the grain is ruined, the new wine dries up, and the olive oil fails.
Be dismayed, you farmers; wail, you vinedressers, over the wheat and the barley, because the harvest of the field is lost.
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withers. Pomegranate, palm and apple tree, all the trees of the field have dried up. Surely joy has dried up and left the people.

Put on sackcloth and lament, you priests! Wail, you who serve at the altar! Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God! For grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
Set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly. Gather the elders and all who live in the land to the house of the LORD your God, and cry out to the LORD.
Alas for the day! For the day of the LORD is near; it comes like destruction from the Almighty.
Has not food been cut off before our eyes, joy and gladness from the house of our God?
The seeds shrivel under their clods. The storehouses are desolate; the granaries are torn down, for the grain has dried up.
How the animals groan! The herds of cattle wander in confusion, because there is no pasture for them. Even the flocks of sheep suffer punishment.
To you, LORD, I call, for fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness, and flame has burned up all the trees of the field.
Even the wild animals long for you, because the streams of water have dried up, and fire has devoured the pastures of the wilderness.
Blow the horn in Zion; sound the alarm on my holy mountain! Let all who live in the land tremble, for the day of the LORD is coming; it is near:

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness. Like dawn spreading over the mountains a great and mighty people comes. There has never been anything like it, and there will never be again after it, through the years of all generations.
Before them fire devours, and behind them a flame blazes. Before them the land is like the garden of Eden, and behind them a desolate wilderness. Nothing escapes them.
Their appearance is like the appearance of horses, and they run like war horses.
With a noise like chariots they leap on the tops of the mountains, like the crackling of a flame of fire devouring stubble, like a mighty people drawn up for battle.
Before them peoples are in anguish; every face turns pale.
They charge like warriors; they climb the wall like soldiers. Each goes on his way, and they do not swerve from their paths.
They do not jostle one another; each goes in his own track. They burst through the weapons and are not stopped.
They rush on the city; they run along the wall; they climb into the houses; they enter through the windows like a thief.
Before them the earth quakes, the heavens tremble. Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their shining.
The LORD raises his voice before his army. His camp is very great; mighty is the one who carries out his word. For the day of the LORD is great and very terrible. Who can endure it?
Yet even now, declares the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping and with mourning.
Tear your hearts and not your garments. Return to the LORD your God, for he is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love, and he relents from sending disaster.
Who knows? He may turn and relent, and leave behind him a blessing: a grain offering and a drink offering for the LORD your God.
Blow the horn in Zion! Set apart a fast; call a solemn assembly.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Assemble the elders; gather the children, even nursing infants. Let the bridegroom leave his room and the bride her bridal chamber.

Between the porch and the altar let the priests, who serve the LORD, weep and say, "Spare your people, LORD. Do not make your inheritance a disgrace, a byword among the nations. Why should they say among the peoples, 'Where is their God?'"
Then the LORD became jealous for his land and took pity on his people.
The LORD answered his people, "I am sending you grain, new wine and olive oil, and you will be satisfied with them. I will never again make you a disgrace among the nations.

I will drive the northerner far from you, and banish him into a parched and desolate land, his front into the eastern sea and his rear into the western sea. His stench will rise; his foul smell will rise. For he has done great things!"
Do not be afraid, land; rejoice and be glad, for the LORD has done great things!
Do not be afraid, you wild animals, for the pastures of the wilderness are turning green. The tree bears its fruit; the fig tree and the vine give their full yield.
Children of Zion, rejoice and be glad in the LORD your God, for he has given you the autumn rain in righteousness. He has poured down rain for you, the autumn rain and the spring rain, as before.
The threshing floors will be full of grain; the vats will overflow with new wine and olive oil.
I will repay you for the years that the swarming locust has eaten, the hopping locust, the destroying locust and the cutting locust, my great army that I sent against you.
You will eat your fill and be satisfied, and you will praise the name of the LORD your God, who has dealt wonderfully with you. My people will never again be put to shame.
Then you will know that I am in the middle of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and there is no other. My people will never again be put to shame.
After this I will pour out my Spirit on all people. Your sons and your daughters will prophesy; your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
Even on the male and female servants in those days I will pour out my Spirit.
I will show wonders in the heavens and on the earth: blood and fire and columns of smoke.
The sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.

And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved, for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be those who escape, as the LORD has said, and among the survivors will be those whom the LORD calls.
For look, in those days and at that time, when I restore the fortunes of Judah and Jerusalem,

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will enter into judgment with them on behalf of my people, my inheritance Israel, whom they scattered among the nations, and because they divided up my land.
They cast lots for my people. They traded a boy for a prostitute, and sold a girl for wine and drank it.
What are you to me, Tyre and Sidon and all the regions of Philistia? Are you paying me back for something? If you are paying me back, I will swiftly and speedily return your deeds on your own heads.
For you took my silver and my gold, and carried my rich treasures into your temples.
You sold the people of Judah and Jerusalem to the Greeks, to remove them far from their own territory.
Look, I am going to rouse them from the place where you sold them, and I will return your deeds on your own heads.
I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans, to a nation far away, for the LORD has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: Prepare for war! Rouse the warriors! Let all the soldiers draw near and come up!
Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning knives into spears. Let the weak say, "I am a warrior!"
Hurry and come, all you nations around, and gather there. Bring down your warriors, LORD!
Let the nations rouse themselves and come up to the Valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit to judge all the nations around.
Swing the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come, tread the grapes, for the winepress is full. The vats overflow, for their wickedness is great.
Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision! For the day of the LORD is near in the valley of decision.
Sun and moon grow dark, and the stars withdraw their shining.
The LORD roars from Zion and raises his voice from Jerusalem, and the heavens and the earth shake. But the LORD is a refuge for his people, a stronghold for the Israelites.
Then you will know that I am the LORD your God, who lives in Zion, my holy mountain. Jerusalem will be holy, and foreigners will never again pass through it.

On that day the mountains will drip sweet wine, and the hills will flow with milk. All the streambeds of Judah will flow with water, and a spring will come out from the house of the LORD and water the Valley of Shittim.
Egypt will become a desolation, and Edom a desolate wilderness, because of the violence done to the people of Judah, in whose land they shed innocent blood.
But Judah will be inhabited forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I will avenge their blood, which I have not yet avenged. The LORD lives in Zion.

The words of Amos, who was one of the sheep breeders of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah and in the days of Jeroboam son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
He said: The LORD roars from Zion and raises his voice from Jerusalem. The pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the top of Carmel withers.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they threshed Gilead with threshing sledges of iron.
So I will send fire on the house of Hazael, and it will devour the fortresses of Ben-hadad.

I will break the gate bar of Damascus. I will cut off the one who sits enthroned in the Valley of Aven, and the one who holds the scepter in Beth-eden. The people of Aram will go into exile to Kir, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they carried away whole communities into exile, to hand them over to Edom.
So I will send fire on the wall of Gaza, and it will devour its fortresses.

I will cut off the one who sits enthroned in Ashdod, and the one who holds the scepter in Ashkelon. I will turn my hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines will perish, says the Lord GOD.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Tyre, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they handed over whole communities to Edom and did not remember the covenant of brothers.
So I will send fire on the wall of Tyre, and it will devour its fortresses.

This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Edom, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled all pity. His anger tore without end, and he kept his fury forever.
So I will send fire on Teman, and it will devour the fortresses of Bozrah.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of the Ammonites, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead to enlarge their territory.
So I will kindle a fire on the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its fortresses, with a battle cry on the day of battle, with a storm on the day of the whirlwind.
Their king will go into exile, he and his officials together, says the LORD.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Moab, and for four, I will not turn it back, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
So I will send fire on Moab, and it will devour the fortresses of Kerioth. Moab will die amid the uproar, with a battle cry and the sound of the ram's horn.
I will cut off the ruler from within her and kill all her officials with him, says the LORD.

This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Judah, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they rejected the instruction of the LORD and did not keep his decrees. Their lies, which their ancestors followed, have led them astray.
So I will send fire on Judah, and it will devour the fortresses of Jerusalem.
This is what the LORD says: For three crimes of Israel, and for four, I will not turn it back, because they sell the innocent for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals.
They trample the heads of the poor into the dust of the ground and push the humble out of the way. A man and his father go to the same young woman, and so they profane my holy name.
They stretch out beside every altar on garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their God they drink wine taken from those they have fined.
Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, though he was as tall as the cedars and as strong as the oaks. I destroyed his fruit above and his roots below.
It was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt and led you forty years in the wilderness, to take possession of the land of the Amorite.
I raised up some of your sons to be prophets, and some of your young men to be Nazirites. Is it not so, people of Israel? declares the LORD.
But you made the Nazirites drink wine, and you commanded the prophets, "Do not prophesy."
Look, I am going to crush you down where you stand, as a cart crushes when it is full of sheaves.
The swift will have nowhere to flee; the strong will not hold on to his strength, and the warrior will not save his life.
The one who handles the bow will not stand his ground, the swift of foot will not escape, and the one who rides the horse will not save his life.
Even the bravest of the warriors will flee naked on that day, declares the LORD.
Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, people of Israel, against the whole clan that I brought up from the land of Egypt:
You alone have I known of all the clans of the earth. Therefore I will punish you for all your wrongdoing.
Do two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
Does a lion roar in the forest when it has no prey? Does a young lion growl from its den unless it has caught something?
Does a bird fall into a trap on the ground when no snare is set for it? Does a trap spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing?
If a ram's horn is blown in a city, are the people not afraid? If disaster comes to a city, has the LORD not done it?
Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing his plan to his servants the prophets.
The lion has roared; who will not be afraid? The Lord GOD has spoken; who can do anything but prophesy?

Proclaim it to the fortresses in Ashdod and to the fortresses in the land of Egypt, and say: "Gather on the mountains of Samaria, and see the great turmoil within her and the oppression in her midst."
They do not know how to do what is right, declares the LORD, those who store up violence and destruction in their fortresses.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: An enemy will surround the land. He will strip you of your strength, and your fortresses will be plundered.

This is what the LORD says: As a shepherd rescues from the lion's mouth two legs or a piece of an ear, so the people of Israel who live in Samaria will be rescued, with the corner of a couch and a piece of a bed.
Hear, and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Armies.
On the day I punish Israel for its crimes, I will punish the altars of Bethel. The horns of the altar will be cut off and fall to the ground.
I will strike the winter house together with the summer house. The houses of ivory will perish, and the great houses will come to an end, declares the LORD.
Hear this word, you cows of Bashan on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to your husbands, "Bring us something to drink!"
The Lord GOD has sworn by his holiness: Look, the days are coming on you when you will be carried away with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks.
You will go out through the breaches in the wall, each woman straight ahead, and you will be thrown out toward Harmon, declares the LORD.
Come to Bethel and rebel; go to Gilgal and rebel all the more! Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every third day.
Burn a thanksgiving offering of bread made with yeast, and proclaim your freewill offerings; announce them! For that is what you love to do, people of Israel, declares the Lord GOD.
I gave you clean teeth in all your cities and a lack of bread in all your places, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

I also held back the rain from you when there were still three months to the harvest. I sent rain on one city and sent no rain on another city. One field had rain, and the field that had no rain dried up.
Two or three cities staggered to one city to drink water, and could not drink their fill, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I struck you with blight and mildew. Your many gardens and vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees, the cutting locust devoured, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.

I sent a plague among you as I did in Egypt. I killed your young men with the sword, and your horses were captured. I made the stench of your camps rise into your nostrils, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
I overthrew some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a burning stick snatched from the fire, yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD.
Therefore this is what I will do to you, Israel. Because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, Israel!

For look, he who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who tells human beings what his thoughts are, who turns the dawn into darkness, and treads on the heights of the earth: the LORD, the God of Armies, is his name.
Hear this word, which I take up over you as a lament, house of Israel:
Fallen, never to rise again, is the virgin Israel. She lies abandoned on her land, with no one to raise her up.
For this is what the Lord GOD says: The city that marches out a thousand strong will have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred strong will have ten left, for the house of Israel.
For this is what the LORD says to the house of Israel: Seek me and live!
But do not seek Bethel, do not go to Gilgal, and do not cross over to Beersheba. For Gilgal will surely go into exile, and Bethel will come to nothing.
Seek the LORD and live, or he will break out like fire on the house of Joseph, and it will devour, with no one to put it out for Bethel.
You who turn justice into wormwood and throw righteousness to the ground!

He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns deep darkness into morning and darkens day into night, who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the LORD is his name.
He makes destruction flash out against the strong, and destruction comes on the fortress.
They hate the one who gives correction in the gate, and they detest the one who speaks with integrity.

Therefore, because you trample on the poor and take from them a levy of grain, you have built houses of cut stone, but you will not live in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, but you will not drink their wine.
For I know how many your crimes are and how great your sins: you who harass the innocent, who take bribes, and who turn aside the needy in the gate.
Therefore the prudent will keep silent at such a time, for it is an evil time.
Seek good and not evil, so that you may live. Then the LORD, the God of Armies, will be with you, as you say he is.
Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate. Perhaps the LORD, the God of Armies, will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.

Therefore this is what the LORD, the God of Armies, the Lord, says: There will be wailing in all the squares, and in all the streets they will say, "Alas! Alas!" They will call the farmer to mourning, and those skilled in lament to wailing.
In all the vineyards there will be wailing, for I will pass through your midst, says the LORD.
Woe to you who long for the day of the LORD! Why would you want the day of the LORD? It is darkness, and not light.
It will be as when someone flees from a lion and a bear meets him, or goes into the house and leans his hand against the wall, and a snake bites him.
Is not the day of the LORD darkness, and not light, gloom with no brightness in it?
I hate, I reject your festivals; I take no delight in your solemn assemblies.
Even though you offer me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them; I will not look at the fellowship offerings of your fattened animals.
Take away from me the noise of your songs; I will not listen to the music of your harps.
But let justice roll on like waters, and righteousness like a stream that never runs dry.
Did you bring me sacrifices and grain offerings in the wilderness for forty years, house of Israel?
You will carry Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your god, which you made for yourselves,
and I will send you into exile beyond Damascus, says the LORD, whose name is the God of Armies.
Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who feel secure on the mountain of Samaria, the notable men of the first of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
Cross over to Calneh and look; go from there to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are they better than these kingdoms? Is their territory larger than yours?
You push away the day of disaster, yet you bring near the reign of violence.
They lie on beds of ivory and sprawl on their couches. They eat lambs from the flock and calves from the stall.
They improvise to the sound of the harp; like David, they invent musical instruments for themselves.
They drink wine by the bowlful and anoint themselves with the finest oils, but they do not grieve over the ruin of Joseph.
Therefore they will now go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the feasting of those who sprawl will come to an end.
The Lord GOD has sworn by himself, declares the LORD, the God of Armies: I loathe the pride of Jacob and hate his fortresses. I will hand over the city and everything in it.
If ten men are left in one house, they will die.

And when a relative, the one who burns the dead, picks up a body to carry the bones out of the house, he will say to someone in the back of the house, "Is anyone else with you?" He will say, "No one." Then he will say, "Hush! We must not mention the name of the LORD."
For look, the LORD is giving the command, and he will strike the great house into fragments and the small house into splinters.
Do horses run on rock? Does anyone plow there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.
You who rejoice over Lo-debar, who say, "Did we not take Karnaim for ourselves by our own strength?"
For look, I am raising up a nation against you, house of Israel, declares the LORD, the God of Armies, and they will oppress you from Lebo-hamath to the Wadi of the Arabah.
This is what the Lord GOD showed me: he was forming a swarm of locusts when the late crop was beginning to come up. It was the late crop after the king's mowings.
When they had finished eating the plants of the land, I said, "Lord GOD, forgive, please! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "It will not happen," said the LORD.
This is what the Lord GOD showed me: the Lord GOD was calling for judgment by fire. It devoured the great deep and was devouring the land.
Then I said, "Lord GOD, stop, please! How can Jacob survive? He is so small."
The LORD relented concerning this. "This too will not happen," said the Lord GOD.
This is what he showed me: the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, with a plumb line in his hand.
The LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Look, I am setting a plumb line among my people Israel. I will not pass them by again.
The high places of Isaac will be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste. I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent a message to Jeroboam king of Israel: "Amos has conspired against you in the very heart of the house of Israel. The land cannot bear all his words.
For this is what Amos has said: 'Jeroboam will die by the sword, and Israel will surely go into exile away from its land.'"
Amaziah said to Amos, "Seer, go! Run away to the land of Judah. Earn your living there, and prophesy there.
But never prophesy at Bethel again, for it is the king's sanctuary and a royal temple."
Amos answered Amaziah, "I am not a prophet, and I am not a prophet's son. I am a herdsman and a tender of sycamore figs.
But the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to my people Israel.'
So now hear the word of the LORD. You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'

Therefore this is what the LORD says: Your wife will become a prostitute in the city, and your sons and your daughters will fall by the sword. Your land will be divided up with a measuring line, and you yourself will die in an unclean land. And Israel will surely go into exile away from its land."
This is what the Lord GOD showed me: a basket of summer fruit.
He said, "What do you see, Amos?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come for my people Israel. I will not pass them by again.
On that day the songs of the temple will become wailing, declares the Lord GOD. So many corpses, thrown out everywhere! Hush!"
Hear this, you who trample the needy and bring the poor of the land to an end,

who say, "When will the new moon be over, so that we can sell grain, and the Sabbath, so that we can open the stores of wheat? We will make the ephah small and the shekel heavy and cheat with dishonest scales,
buying the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and selling even the sweepings of the wheat."
The LORD has sworn by the Pride of Jacob: I will never forget anything they have done.
Will not the land tremble because of this, and everyone who lives in it mourn? All of it will rise like the Nile, be tossed about, and sink again like the river of Egypt.
On that day, declares the Lord GOD, I will make the sun go down at noon and darken the earth in broad daylight.

I will turn your festivals into mourning and all your songs into a lament. I will put sackcloth on every waist and shave every head bald. I will make it like the mourning for an only son, and its end like a bitter day.
Look, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land: not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.
People will stagger from sea to sea and wander from north to east, running back and forth to seek the word of the LORD, but they will not find it.
On that day the beautiful young women and the young men will faint from thirst.
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria, who say, "As your god lives, Dan," and "As the way to Beersheba lives," will fall and never rise again.

I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and he said: Strike the tops of the pillars so that the thresholds shake, and shatter them on the heads of all the people. Those who are left of them I will kill with the sword. Not one of them will get away; not one will escape.
If they dig down into Sheol, from there my hand will take them. If they climb up to the heavens, from there I will bring them down.
If they hide on the top of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them. If they hide from my sight on the floor of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it will bite them.
If they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it will kill them. I will set my eyes on them for harm and not for good.
The Lord GOD of Armies touches the earth, and it melts, and all who live in it mourn. All of it rises like the Nile and sinks again like the river of Egypt.
He builds his upper rooms in the heavens and sets the foundations of his vault on the earth. He calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out on the face of the earth: the LORD is his name.
Are you not like the Cushites to me, people of Israel? declares the LORD. Did I not bring Israel up from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Arameans from Kir?
Look, the eyes of the Lord GOD are on the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth. Yet I will not completely destroy the house of Jacob, declares the LORD.
For look, I am giving the command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as grain is shaken in a sieve, and not a pebble falls to the ground.
All the sinners among my people will die by the sword, those who say, "Disaster will not come near us or overtake us."
On that day I will raise up the fallen shelter of David. I will repair its broken walls and raise up its ruins, and I will rebuild it as it was in days of old,
so that they may take possession of what is left of Edom and of all the nations that are called by my name, declares the LORD, who will do this.

Look, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when the one who plows will overtake the one who reaps, and the one who treads grapes the one who sows the seed. The mountains will drip sweet wine, and all the hills will flow with it.
I will restore the fortunes of my people Israel. They will rebuild the ruined cities and live in them; they will plant vineyards and drink their wine; they will make gardens and eat their fruit.
I will plant them on their land, and they will never again be uprooted from the land that I have given them, says the LORD your God.

The vision of Obadiah. This is what the Lord GOD says concerning Edom: We have heard a report from the LORD, and an envoy has been sent among the nations: "Rise up! Let us rise against her for battle!"
Look, I will make you small among the nations; you will be utterly despised.
The pride of your heart has deceived you, you who live in the clefts of the rock, whose dwelling is on the heights, who say in your heart, "Who will bring me down to the ground?"
Though you build as high as the eagle, though your nest is set among the stars, from there I will bring you down, declares the LORD.
If thieves came to you, if robbers by night (how you will be destroyed!), would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape pickers came to you, would they not leave gleanings?
How Esau has been searched out, his hidden treasures hunted down!

All your allies have driven you to the border. The men who were at peace with you have deceived you and overpowered you. Those who eat your bread set a trap under you. There is no understanding in him.
On that day, declares the LORD, will I not destroy the wise from Edom, and understanding from the mountain of Esau?
Your warriors will be terrified, Teman, so that everyone will be cut off from the mountain of Esau by slaughter.
Because of the violence done to your brother Jacob, shame will cover you, and you will be cut off forever.
On the day you stood aloof, on the day strangers carried off his wealth and foreigners entered his gates and cast lots for Jerusalem, you too were like one of them.
Do not gloat over your brother on the day of his misfortune. Do not rejoice over the people of Judah on the day of their ruin. Do not boast on the day of distress.
