Do not enter the gate of my people on the day of their disaster. Do not gloat, you too, over his suffering on the day of his disaster. Do not lay hands on his wealth on the day of his disaster.
Do not stand at the crossroads to cut off his fugitives. Do not hand over his survivors on the day of distress.
For the day of the LORD is near, against all the nations. As you have done, it will be done to you; what you have dealt out will come back on your own head.
For just as you drank on my holy mountain, so all the nations will drink without ceasing. They will drink and gulp it down, and be as though they had never been.
But on Mount Zion there will be those who escape, and it will be holy. The house of Jacob will take possession of their own possessions.

The house of Jacob will be a fire, the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau stubble. They will set it ablaze and consume it, and there will be no survivor of the house of Esau, for the LORD has spoken.

The people of the Negev will possess the mountain of Esau, and the people of the Shephelah the land of the Philistines. They will possess the territory of Ephraim and the territory of Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
The exiles of this army of the Israelites will possess what belongs to the Canaanites as far as Zarephath, and the exiles of Jerusalem who are in Sepharad will possess the cities of the Negev.
Deliverers will go up on Mount Zion to rule the mountain of Esau, and the kingdom will belong to the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah son of Amittai:
"Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and cry out against it, for their evil has come up before me."

But Jonah got up to run away to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD. He went down to Joppa and found a ship going to Tarshish. He paid the fare and went down into the ship to go with them to Tarshish, away from the presence of the LORD.
But the LORD hurled a great wind on the sea, and there was a great storm on the sea, and the ship was about to break up.

The sailors were afraid, and each one cried out to his own god. They hurled the cargo that was in the ship into the sea to lighten it for themselves. But Jonah had gone down into the hold of the ship, and he lay there, fast asleep.
The captain came to him and said to him, "How can you be sleeping? Get up, call on your god! Perhaps the god will give a thought to us, and we will not perish."
Then they said to one another, "Come, let us cast lots, so that we may know on whose account this disaster has come on us." So they cast lots, and the lot fell on Jonah.
They said to him, "Tell us, you on whose account this disaster has come on us: what is your work? Where do you come from? What is your country? From what people are you?"
He said to them, "I am a Hebrew. I fear the LORD, the God of heaven, who made the sea and the dry land."
The men were terrified and said to him, "What is this you have done?" For the men knew that he was running away from the presence of the LORD, because he had told them.
They said to him, "What should we do to you, so that the sea will calm down for us?" For the sea was growing more and more stormy.
He said to them, "Pick me up and hurl me into the sea, and the sea will calm down for you. For I know that it is on my account that this great storm has come on you."
But the men rowed hard to get back to dry land, and they could not, because the sea was growing more and more stormy against them.
Then they called out to the LORD: "Please, LORD, do not let us perish for this man's life, and do not hold us guilty of innocent blood. For you, LORD, have done as you pleased."
Then they picked Jonah up and hurled him into the sea, and the sea stopped raging.
The men greatly feared the LORD. They offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows.
The LORD appointed a great fish to swallow Jonah, and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
Jonah prayed to the LORD his God from the belly of the fish.
He said: "I called to the LORD out of my distress, and he answered me. From the belly of Sheol I cried for help, and you heard my voice.
You threw me into the deep, into the heart of the seas, and the current surrounded me. All your breakers and your waves swept over me.
I said, 'I have been driven away from your sight. Yet I will look again toward your holy temple.'
The waters closed around me up to my neck; the deep surrounded me; seaweed was wrapped around my head.
I went down to the roots of the mountains; the earth with its bars closed behind me forever. But you brought my life up from the pit, LORD my God.
When my life was ebbing away, I remembered the LORD, and my prayer came to you, to your holy temple.
Those who cling to worthless idols abandon their faithful love.
But I, with a song of thanksgiving, will sacrifice to you. What I have vowed I will pay. Salvation belongs to the LORD!"
Then the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah out onto the dry land.
The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time:
"Get up, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the message that I tell you."
So Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, as the LORD had said. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, a three days' walk across.
Jonah began to go into the city, going a day's walk, and he proclaimed, "Forty days more, and Nineveh will be overthrown!"
The people of Nineveh believed God. They proclaimed a fast and put on sackcloth, from the greatest of them to the least.
When the news reached the king of Nineveh, he got up from his throne, took off his robe, covered himself with sackcloth, and sat in the ashes.
He had this proclaimed in Nineveh: "By the decree of the king and his nobles: No human being or animal, no herd or flock, is to taste anything. They are not to graze or drink water.
Let human beings and animals be covered with sackcloth, and let them call out to God with all their strength. Let each one turn from his evil way and from the violence that is in his hands.
Who knows? God may turn and relent, and turn from his burning anger, so that we do not perish."
When God saw what they did, that they turned from their evil way, God relented concerning the disaster that he had said he would bring on them, and he did not do it.
But to Jonah this seemed very wrong, and he was angry.

He prayed to the LORD and said, "Please, LORD, isn't this what I said while I was still in my own country? That is why I hurried to run away to Tarshish. For I knew that you are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger and abounding in faithful love, and that you relent from sending disaster.
So now, LORD, please take my life from me, for it is better for me to die than to live."
The LORD said, "Is it right for you to be angry?"
Jonah went out of the city and sat down to the east of the city. He made a shelter for himself there and sat under it in the shade, until he could see what would happen to the city.
Then the LORD God appointed a plant, and it grew up over Jonah to be a shade over his head, to save him from his misery. Jonah was very glad about the plant.
But at dawn the next day God appointed a worm, and it attacked the plant, so that it withered.
When the sun rose, God appointed a scorching east wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah's head, so that he grew faint. He asked to die, saying, "It is better for me to die than to live."
But God said to Jonah, "Is it right for you to be angry about the plant?" He said, "It is right for me to be angry, angry enough to die!"
The LORD said, "You were concerned about the plant, for which you did not labor and which you did not make grow. It came up in a night and perished in a night.
And should I not be concerned about Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than 120,000 people who do not know their right hand from their left, and many animals as well?"
The word of the LORD that came to Micah of Moresheth in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.
Hear, you peoples, all of you; listen, earth, and all that is in it! Let the Lord GOD be a witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.
For look, the LORD is coming out of his place. He will come down and tread on the heights of the earth.
The mountains will melt under him, and the valleys will split open, like wax before the fire, like water poured down a slope.

All this is because of the rebellion of Jacob, because of the sins of the house of Israel. What is the rebellion of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what are the high places of Judah? Are they not Jerusalem?
So I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open country, a place for planting vineyards. I will pour her stones down into the valley and lay bare her foundations.

All her carved images will be smashed, all her prostitute's wages will be burned with fire, and I will make all her idols a desolation. For she gathered them from a prostitute's wages, and to a prostitute's wages they will return.
Because of this I will mourn and wail; I will go barefoot and naked. I will mourn like the jackals, and lament like the ostriches.
For her wound is incurable; it has come to Judah. It has reached the gate of my people, Jerusalem itself.
Tell it not in Gath; do not weep at all. In Beth-leaphrah, roll yourself in the dust.
Pass on your way, you who live in Shaphir, in shameful nakedness. Those who live in Zaanan do not come out. Beth-ezel is wailing; it will take its support away from you.
For those who live in Maroth writhe in anguish, waiting for good, because disaster has come down from the LORD to the gate of Jerusalem.
Harness the horses to the chariot, you who live in Lachish. She was the beginning of sin for Daughter Zion, for in you were found the rebellions of Israel.
Therefore you will give parting gifts to Moresheth-gath. The houses of Achzib will be a deception to the kings of Israel.
I will yet bring a conqueror against you, you who live in Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
Shave your head bald and cut off your hair for the children you delight in. Make yourself as bald as the vulture, for they have gone from you into exile.
Woe to those who plan wickedness and work out evil on their beds! When morning dawns they carry it out, because it is in their power.
They covet fields and seize them, and houses, and take them. They oppress a man and his household, a person and his inheritance.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Look, I am planning disaster against this clan, from which you cannot free your necks. You will no longer walk proudly, for it will be an evil time.

On that day they will take up a taunt song against you and lament with a bitter lament, saying, "We are utterly ruined! He changes the portion of my people. How he takes it away from me! He divides our fields among traitors."
Therefore you will have no one to cast the measuring line by lot in the assembly of the LORD.
"Do not preach," they preach. "No one should preach about such things. Disgrace will not overtake us."
Should this be said, house of Jacob? Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these the things he does? Do not my words do good to the one who walks uprightly?
But lately my people have risen up as an enemy. You strip the robe from off the garment of those who pass by trustingly, like men returning from war.
You drive the women of my people out of the homes they delight in. From their young children you take away my splendor forever.
Get up and go, for this is no place of rest, because of the uncleanness that destroys with a painful destruction.
If a man went about with wind and lies and deceived, saying, "I will preach to you about wine and beer," he would be the preacher for this people!

I will surely gather all of you, Jacob; I will surely bring together the remnant of Israel. I will put them together like sheep in a fold, like a flock in the middle of its pasture. The place will hum with people.
The one who breaks open the way will go up before them. They will break through, pass through the gate and go out by it. Their king will pass on before them, the LORD at their head.
And I said: Listen, you heads of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel! Is it not for you to know justice?
You hate good and love evil. You tear the skin off my people and the flesh off their bones.
You eat the flesh of my people and strip their skin off them. You break their bones in pieces and chop them up like meat for the pot, like flesh in a cauldron.
Then they will cry out to the LORD, but he will not answer them. He will hide his face from them at that time, because of the evil they have done.

This is what the LORD says about the prophets who lead my people astray, who cry "Peace!" when they have something to bite with their teeth, but declare war on anyone who puts nothing in their mouths:
Therefore it will be night for you, with no vision, and darkness for you, with no divination. The sun will go down on the prophets, and the day will turn black over them.
The seers will be ashamed and the diviners disgraced. They will all cover their lips, because there is no answer from God.
But as for me, I am filled with power, with the Spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might, to declare to Jacob his rebellion and to Israel his sin.
Hear this, you heads of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who detest justice and twist everything that is straight,
who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with injustice.

Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean on the LORD and say, "Is not the LORD among us? No disaster will come on us."
Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a wooded height.
In the days to come, the mountain of the LORD's house will be established as the highest of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and peoples will stream to it.

Many nations will come and say, "Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, so that he may teach us his ways and we may walk in his paths." For instruction will go out from Zion, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.

He will judge between many peoples and settle disputes for strong nations far away. They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning knives. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, and they will not learn war anymore.
Each of them will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, and no one will make them afraid, for the mouth of the LORD of Armies has spoken.
For all the peoples walk, each in the name of its god, but we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever.
On that day, declares the LORD, I will gather the lame and bring together those who have been driven away, those whom I have afflicted.
I will make the lame a remnant, and those driven far away a strong nation. The LORD will reign over them on Mount Zion from now on and forever.
And you, watchtower of the flock, stronghold of Daughter Zion, to you it will come: the former dominion will come, the kingdom of Daughter Jerusalem.
Now why do you cry aloud? Is there no king in you? Has your counselor perished, that pain has seized you like a woman in labor?

Writhe and groan, Daughter Zion, like a woman in labor, for now you will go out from the city and camp in the open country. You will go to Babylon. There you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies.
But now many nations have gathered against you. They say, "Let her be defiled, and let our eyes gloat over Zion."
But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD, and they do not understand his plan: he has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.

Rise and thresh, Daughter Zion, for I will make your horn iron and your hooves bronze, and you will crush many peoples. You will devote their plunder to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of the whole earth.
Now gather your troops, daughter of troops! A siege has been laid against us. With a rod they will strike the judge of Israel on the cheek.
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, too small to be among the clans of Judah, from you one will come out for me to be ruler in Israel, whose origins are from of old, from ancient days.
Therefore he will give them up until the time when she who is in labor has given birth. Then the rest of his brothers will return to the people of Israel.
He will stand and shepherd his flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majesty of the name of the LORD his God. And they will live secure, for now he will be great to the ends of the earth.
And he will be our peace. When Assyria comes into our land and treads on our fortresses, we will raise up against it seven shepherds, eight leaders of men.
They will shepherd the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod at its gates. He will rescue us from Assyria when it comes into our land and treads within our borders.
The remnant of Jacob will be among many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for anyone or depend on human beings.

The remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, among many peoples, like a lion among the animals of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it goes, and there is no one to rescue.
Your hand will be raised over your adversaries, and all your enemies will be cut off.
On that day, declares the LORD, I will cut off your horses from among you and destroy your chariots.
I will cut off the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
I will cut off sorceries from your hand, and you will have no more fortune-tellers.
I will cut off your carved images and your standing stones from among you, and you will no longer bow down to the work of your hands.
I will uproot your Asherah poles from among you and destroy your cities.
In anger and wrath I will take vengeance on the nations that have not obeyed.
Hear what the LORD is saying: Rise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
Hear, you mountains, the LORD's case, you enduring foundations of the earth! For the LORD has a case against his people, and he will argue it with Israel.
My people, what have I done to you? How have I wearied you? Answer me!
For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses, Aaron and Miriam ahead of you.
My people, remember what Balak king of Moab planned and what Balaam son of Beor answered him, and what happened from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may know the saving acts of the LORD.
"With what shall I come before the LORD and bow down before God on high? Shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves a year old?
Will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I give my firstborn for my rebellion, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?"
He has told you, mortal, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, to love faithful love, and to walk humbly with your God?
Listen! The LORD is calling to the city, and it is wisdom to fear your name: Hear of the rod, and of the one who appointed it.
Can I forget the treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and the short ephah, which is cursed?
Can I acquit someone with wicked scales, with a bag of false weights?
Her rich men are full of violence; her inhabitants speak lies, and their tongues in their mouths are deceitful.
So I have struck you with a painful wound, to make you desolate because of your sins.
You will eat but not be satisfied; your hunger will remain inside you. You will carry things away but not save them, and what you do save I will give to the sword.
You will sow but not reap; you will tread olives but not anoint yourself with oil, and tread grapes but not drink wine.

For the decrees of Omri are kept, and all the practices of the house of Ahab, and you have followed their advice. So I will make you a desolation, and the city's inhabitants an object of hissing; you will bear the scorn of my people.
Woe is me! For I have become like one who gathers summer fruit, like one who gleans after the grape harvest. There is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I long for.
The faithful have vanished from the land, and there is no one upright among human beings. All of them lie in wait to shed blood; each hunts his brother with a net.
Their hands are skilled at doing evil. The official asks for gifts, and the judge judges for a bribe. The powerful man speaks out what he craves, and so they weave it together.
The best of them is like a briar, the most upright worse than a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, the day of your punishment, has come; now their confusion will come.
Do not trust a neighbor; do not rely on a friend. Guard the doors of your mouth from the woman who lies in your arms.
For the son treats his father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, and the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man's enemies are the people of his own household.
But as for me, I will watch for the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.
I will bear the anger of the LORD, because I have sinned against him, until he pleads my case and gives me justice. He will bring me out into the light; I will see his righteousness.
Then my enemy will see it, and shame will cover her, she who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will look on her; now she will be trampled down like mud in the streets.
A day for building your walls! On that day the boundary will be extended far.
On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.
But the earth will become a desolation because of those who live in it, as the fruit of their deeds.
Shepherd your people with your staff, the flock that is your inheritance, which lives alone in a forest in the middle of a fruitful land. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.
As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them wonders.
The nations will see and be ashamed of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths; their ears will be deaf.

They will lick the dust like a snake, like creatures that crawl on the ground. They will come trembling out of their strongholds. They will turn in fear to the LORD our God, and they will be afraid of you.
Who is a God like you, who forgives wrongdoing and passes over the rebellion of the remnant of his inheritance? He does not hold on to his anger forever, because he delights in faithful love.
He will again have compassion on us; he will tread our wrongdoings underfoot. You will hurl all their sins into the depths of the sea.
You will show faithfulness to Jacob and faithful love to Abraham, as you swore to our ancestors in the days of old.
An oracle concerning Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries and keeps his anger for his enemies.
The LORD is slow to anger and great in power, and he will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD's way is in the whirlwind and the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
He rebukes the sea and dries it up; he makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the blossom of Lebanon fades.
The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth heaves at his presence, the world and all who live in it.
Who can stand before his fury? Who can endure the heat of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are shattered before him.
The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress. He knows those who take refuge in him.
But with an overwhelming flood he will make a complete end of her place, and he will pursue his enemies into darkness.
What are you plotting against the LORD? He will make a complete end; distress will not rise up a second time.
For like tangled thorns, and drunk as with their drink, they will be consumed like dry stubble, completely.
From you has come one who plots evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
This is what the LORD says: Though they are at full strength and many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
And now I will break his yoke from off you and tear off your bonds.

The LORD has given a command concerning you: No more descendants will bear your name. From the house of your gods I will cut off the carved image and the cast idol. I will prepare your grave, for you are worthless.

Look, on the mountains, the feet of the one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your festivals, Judah; fulfill your vows. For never again will the wicked one pass through you; he is completely cut off.
One who scatters has come up against you. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourself! Gather all your strength!
For the LORD is restoring the pride of Jacob, like the pride of Israel, for plunderers have plundered them and ruined their vine branches.
The shields of his warriors are red; his soldiers are clothed in scarlet. The chariots flash like fire on the day he prepares for battle, and the spears are brandished.
The chariots race madly through the streets; they rush back and forth in the squares. They look like torches; they dart about like lightning.
He summons his nobles; they stumble as they go. They hurry to her wall, and the siege shield is set up.
The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace melts away.
It is decided: she is stripped and carried away. Her slave women moan like the sound of doves and beat their breasts.
Nineveh is like a pool of water whose waters are draining away. "Stop! Stop!" they cry, but no one turns back.
Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold! There is no end to the treasure, the wealth of every kind of precious thing.
Emptiness, desolation and ruin! Hearts melt, knees give way, every waist trembles, and every face turns pale.
Where is the lions' den now, the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness went, and the lion's cub, with no one to make them afraid?
The lion tore enough for his cubs and strangled prey for his lionesses. He filled his caves with prey and his dens with torn flesh.

Look, I am against you, declares the LORD of Armies. I will burn your chariots in smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will be heard no more.
Woe to the city of bloodshed, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey!
The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, the galloping horse and the jolting chariot!
Horsemen charging, flashing swords and glittering spears! Many slain, heaps of corpses, bodies without end! They stumble over the bodies.
All because of the endless prostitution of the prostitute, so charming, the mistress of sorceries, who sells nations by her prostitution and peoples by her sorceries.
Look, I am against you, declares the LORD of Armies. I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
I will throw filth on you, treat you with contempt, and make you a spectacle.
Everyone who sees you will run from you and say, "Nineveh is devastated! Who will mourn for her?" Where can I find anyone to comfort you?
Are you better than Thebes, which sat by the Nile, with water all around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?
Cush and Egypt were her strength, without limit; Put and the Libyans were among her helpers.
Yet she too went into exile; she went into captivity. Her infants too were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her nobles, and all her great men were bound in chains.
You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding. You too will seek refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, the figs fall into the mouth of the eater.
Look, your troops are women in your midst. The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire has devoured your gate bars.
Draw water for the siege! Strengthen your fortresses! Go into the clay and tread the mortar! Take hold of the brick mold!
There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you off. It will devour you as the hopping locust does. Multiply like the hopping locust! Multiply like the swarming locust!
You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The hopping locust strips the land and flies away.
Your guards are like the swarming locust, your officials like swarms of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where they are.
Your shepherds are asleep, king of Assyria; your nobles lie down to rest. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
There is no relief for your injury; your wound is fatal. All who hear the news about you clap their hands over you, for who has not felt your endless cruelty?
The oracle that Habakkuk the prophet saw.
How long, LORD, must I cry for help, and you do not listen? I cry out to you, "Violence!" but you do not save.
Why do you make me see wickedness, and why do you look on trouble? Destruction and violence are before me; there is strife, and conflict rises up.
So the law grows numb, and justice never goes out. For the wicked surround the righteous, so justice goes out twisted.
"Look among the nations and see! Be astonished, be amazed! For I am doing a deed in your days that you would not believe if you were told.
For look, I am raising up the Babylonians, that bitter and hasty nation, which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings that are not its own.
They are dreaded and feared; their justice and their dignity come from themselves.
Their horses are swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves at evening. Their horsemen gallop on; their horsemen come from far away. They fly like an eagle swooping to devour.
They all come for violence; their faces press forward like the east wind, and they gather captives like sand.
They scoff at kings, and rulers are a joke to them. They laugh at every fortress; they heap up earth and capture it.
Then they sweep past like the wind and go on, guilty men, whose own strength is their god."
Are you not from of old, LORD, my God, my Holy One? We will not die. LORD, you have appointed them to execute judgment; Rock, you have established them to punish.
Your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and you cannot look on wrongdoing. Why then do you look on the treacherous and keep silent when the wicked swallow up those more righteous than they?
You have made human beings like the fish of the sea, like creeping things that have no ruler.
He brings all of them up with a hook; he drags them out with his net and gathers them in his dragnet. So he rejoices and is glad.
That is why he sacrifices to his net and burns incense to his dragnet, for by them his portion is rich and his food is plentiful.
Will he therefore keep emptying his net and go on killing nations without mercy?
I will stand at my watch post and station myself on the rampart. I will watch to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
Then the LORD answered me: "Write down the vision; make it plain on tablets, so that the one who reads it may run.
For the vision is still for the appointed time. It hurries toward the end, and it will not lie. If it seems slow, wait for it; it will surely come, it will not delay.
Look, his soul is puffed up; it is not upright within him. But the righteous will live by his faithfulness.

Moreover, wine is treacherous; the arrogant man will not rest. He opens his throat as wide as Sheol; like death, he is never satisfied. He gathers all the nations for himself and collects all the peoples for himself.
Will not all of them take up a taunt against him, with mocking riddles about him, and say: 'Woe to him who heaps up what is not his own (how long?) and loads himself with goods taken in pledge!
Will not your creditors suddenly rise up, and those who make you tremble wake up? Then you will become plunder for them.
Because you have plundered many nations, all the rest of the peoples will plunder you, because of the blood of human beings and violence done to the earth, to the city and all who live in it.
Woe to him who gets evil gain for his house, to set his nest on high and escape from the grasp of disaster!
You have planned shame for your house by cutting off many peoples; you have sinned against your own life.
For the stone will cry out from the wall, and the beam will answer it from the woodwork.
Woe to him who builds a city with bloodshed and founds a town on injustice!
Is it not from the LORD of Armies that peoples wear themselves out only for the fire, and nations exhaust themselves for nothing?
For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of the glory of the LORD, as the waters cover the sea.
Woe to him who makes his neighbors drink, pouring out your wrath and making them drunk, in order to gaze on their nakedness!
You will be filled with shame instead of glory. Drink, you too, and show your foreskin! The cup in the LORD's right hand will come around to you, and utter disgrace will cover your glory.

For the violence done to Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of the animals will terrify you, because of the blood of human beings and violence done to the earth, to the city and all who live in it.
What use is a carved image, once its maker has carved it, or a cast image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in what he has made himself, when he makes idols that cannot speak.
Woe to him who says to a piece of wood, "Wake up!" and to a silent stone, "Get up!" Can it teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, but there is no breath in it at all.'
But the LORD is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him."
A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet. According to Shigionoth.
LORD, I have heard the report of you; I stand in awe, LORD, of your work. In the midst of the years revive it; in the midst of the years make it known. In wrath, remember mercy.
God came from Teman, the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah. His splendor covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.
His brightness was like the light; rays came from his hand, and there his power was hidden.
Plague went before him, and pestilence followed at his heels.
He stood and measured the earth; he looked and made the nations tremble. The ancient mountains were shattered; the everlasting hills sank down. His ways are as of old.
I saw the tents of Cushan in distress; the tent curtains of the land of Midian trembled.
Was your anger against the rivers, LORD? Was your wrath against the rivers, or your fury against the sea, when you rode on your horses, on your chariots of victory?
Your bow was laid bare; arrows were sworn by your word. Selah. You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw you and writhed; a torrent of water swept by. The deep gave its voice; it lifted its hands on high.
Sun and moon stood still in their dwelling at the light of your arrows as they flew, at the flash of your glittering spear.
In fury you marched through the earth; in anger you trampled the nations.
You went out to save your people, to save your anointed one. You crushed the head of the house of the wicked, laying it bare from foundation to neck. Selah.
With his own arrows you pierced the head of his warriors, who stormed out to scatter me, gloating as if about to devour the poor in secret.
You trampled the sea with your horses, churning the mighty waters.

I heard, and my body trembled; my lips quivered at the sound. Rottenness entered my bones, and my legs trembled beneath me. Yet I will wait quietly for the day of distress to come on the people who invade us.

Though the fig tree does not blossom, and there is no fruit on the vines, though the olive crop fails, and the fields produce no food, though the flock is cut off from the fold, and there are no cattle in the stalls,
yet I will rejoice in the LORD; I will be joyful in the God of my salvation.
GOD, the Lord, is my strength. He makes my feet like the feet of a deer, and makes me walk on my heights. For the director. With my stringed instruments.
The word of the LORD that came to Zephaniah son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon king of Judah.
I will sweep away everything, completely, from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.

I will sweep away human beings and animals; I will sweep away the birds of the sky and the fish of the sea, and the things that make the wicked stumble. I will cut off humankind from the face of the earth, declares the LORD.
I will stretch out my hand against Judah and against all who live in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place what is left of Baal, and the name of the idol priests along with the priests,
those who bow down on the rooftops to the host of heaven, and those who bow down and swear allegiance to the LORD but also swear by Milcom,
and those who turn back from following the LORD, who do not seek the LORD or inquire of him.
Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near. The LORD has prepared a sacrifice; he has consecrated his guests.
On the day of the LORD's sacrifice I will punish the officials and the king's sons, and all who dress in foreign clothing.
On that day I will punish everyone who leaps over the threshold, who fill their master's house with violence and deceit.
On that day, declares the LORD, a cry will be heard from the Fish Gate, wailing from the Second Quarter, and a great crash from the hills.
Wail, you who live in the Mortar, for all the traders are destroyed; all who weigh out silver are cut off.
At that time I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the people who sit complacent, like wine left on its dregs, who say in their hearts, "The LORD will do nothing, good or bad."
Their wealth will be plundered and their houses made a desolation. They will build houses but not live in them; they will plant vineyards but not drink their wine.
The great day of the LORD is near, near and coming very quickly. Listen! The day of the LORD! There the warrior cries out bitterly.
That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of ruin and devastation, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and thick darkness,
a day of the ram's horn and the battle cry against the fortified cities and against the high corner towers.
I will bring such distress on humankind that they will walk like the blind, because they have sinned against the LORD. Their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung.

Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to save them on the day of the LORD's wrath. In the fire of his jealousy the whole earth will be consumed, for he will make an end, a sudden and terrible end, of all who live on the earth.
Gather yourselves together, gather together, you shameless nation,
before the decree takes effect and the day blows past like chaff, before the burning anger of the LORD comes on you, before the day of the LORD's anger comes on you.
Seek the LORD, all you humble of the land, who do what he commands. Seek righteousness; seek humility. Perhaps you will be sheltered on the day of the LORD's anger.
For Gaza will be abandoned, and Ashkelon will become a desolation. Ashdod will be driven out at noon, and Ekron will be uprooted.
Woe to you who live by the seacoast, you nation of the Cherethites! The word of the LORD is against you, Canaan, land of the Philistines: I will destroy you until no one is left living there.
The seacoast will become pastures, with meadows for shepherds and pens for flocks.

The coast will belong to the remnant of the house of Judah; they will graze their flocks there. In the houses of Ashkelon they will lie down in the evening, for the LORD their God will care for them and restore their fortunes.
I have heard the taunts of Moab and the insults of the Ammonites, how they taunted my people and made boasts against their territory.

Therefore, as I live, declares the LORD of Armies, the God of Israel, Moab will become like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah, a place overgrown with weeds, a salt pit and a desolation forever. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the survivors of my nation will possess them.
This is what they will get for their pride, because they taunted and made boasts against the people of the LORD of Armies.
The LORD will be terrible against them, for he will starve all the gods of the earth. And all the coastlands of the nations will bow down to him, each in its own place.
You too, Cushites, will be slain by my sword.
And he will stretch out his hand against the north and destroy Assyria. He will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as the desert.

Flocks will lie down in her midst, all kinds of wild animals. Both the desert owl and the screech owl will roost on the tops of her pillars. A voice will hoot in the window; desolation will be on the threshold, for her cedar paneling has been stripped bare.

This is the exultant city that lived in security, that said in her heart, "I am, and there is no one else." How she has become a desolation, a lair for wild animals! Everyone who passes by her hisses and shakes his fist.
Woe to the rebellious and defiled one, the oppressing city!
She does not listen to the voice; she does not accept correction. She does not trust in the LORD; she does not draw near to her God.
Her officials within her are roaring lions; her judges are wolves at evening, who leave nothing until the morning.
Her prophets are reckless, treacherous men. Her priests profane what is holy; they do violence to the law.
The LORD within her is righteous; he does no wrong. Morning by morning he brings his justice to light; he never fails. But the unjust know no shame.
I have cut off nations; their corner towers are desolate. I have laid waste their streets, so that no one walks in them. Their cities are ruined, with no one in them, no one living there.

I said, "Surely you will fear me; you will accept correction." Then her dwelling would not be cut off, in spite of all the punishment I have brought on her. But they rose early to make all their deeds corrupt.

Therefore wait for me, declares the LORD, for the day when I rise up as a witness. For my decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out on them my indignation, all my burning anger. In the fire of my jealousy the whole earth will be consumed.
For then I will change the speech of the peoples to a pure speech, so that all of them may call on the name of the LORD and serve him shoulder to shoulder.
From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers, my scattered people, will bring me offerings.

On that day you will not be put to shame for all the deeds by which you rebelled against me, for then I will remove from your midst those who exult in their pride, and you will never again be haughty on my holy mountain.
But I will leave in your midst a people humble and poor, and they will take refuge in the name of the LORD.
The remnant of Israel will do no wrong and tell no lies, and no deceitful tongue will be found in their mouths. They will graze and lie down, with no one to make them afraid.
Sing aloud, Daughter Zion! Shout, Israel! Rejoice and exult with all your heart, Daughter Jerusalem!
The LORD has taken away the judgments against you; he has turned back your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is in your midst; you will never again fear disaster.
On that day it will be said to Jerusalem: "Do not be afraid, Zion; do not let your hands hang limp.
The LORD your God is in your midst, a warrior who saves. He will rejoice over you with gladness; he will be quiet in his love; he will delight in you with singing."
I will gather those who grieve for the appointed festivals, who were away from you, a burden on her and a disgrace.
Look, at that time I will deal with all who oppress you. I will save the lame and gather the outcast, and I will give them praise and renown in every land where they were put to shame.

At that time I will bring you home, at the time when I gather you. For I will give you renown and praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says the LORD.

In the second year of King Darius, on the first day of the sixth month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: These people say, "The time has not come, the time for the house of the LORD to be rebuilt."
Then the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:
Is it a time for you yourselves to live in your paneled houses, while this house lies in ruins?
Now this is what the LORD of Armies says: Consider your ways.

You have sown much, but harvested little. You eat, but never have enough; you drink, but never have your fill; you put on clothes, but no one is warm. And whoever earns wages earns them to put into a bag with holes.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Consider your ways.
Go up into the hills, bring wood and build the house, so that I may take pleasure in it and be honored, says the LORD.

You looked for much, but see, it came to little. When you brought it home, I blew it away. Why? declares the LORD of Armies. Because of my house, which lies in ruins, while each of you runs off to his own house.
Therefore, because of you, the heavens have held back the dew, and the earth has held back its produce.
I have called for a drought on the land and on the hills, on the grain, the new wine and the olive oil, on what the ground produces, on human beings and animals, and on all the work of your hands.

Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the rest of the people obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, because the LORD their God had sent him. And the people feared the LORD.
Then Haggai, the LORD's messenger, gave the LORD's message to the people: "I am with you, declares the LORD."

So the LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people. They came and began work on the house of the LORD of Armies, their God,
on the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet:
Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people, and say:
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How does it look to you now? Does it not seem to you like nothing at all?

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, declares the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, declares the LORD, and work, for I am with you, declares the LORD of Armies,
as I promised you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.
For this is what the LORD of Armies says: Once more, in a little while, I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD of Armies.
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, declares the LORD of Armies.
The glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former, says the LORD of Armies. And in this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of Armies.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Haggai the prophet:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Ask the priests for a ruling:
"If someone carries consecrated meat in the fold of his garment, and with the fold he touches bread or stew or wine or oil or any other food, does it become holy?" The priests answered, "No."
Then Haggai said, "If someone who is unclean from contact with a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?" The priests answered, "It becomes unclean."
Then Haggai answered, "So it is with this people, and so it is with this nation before me, declares the LORD, and so with all the work of their hands. Whatever they offer there is unclean.
Now consider from this day onward. Before stone was laid on stone in the temple of the LORD,
how did you fare? When someone came to a heap of twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures from the press, there were only twenty.
I struck you, all the work of your hands, with blight and mildew and hail, yet you did not turn to me, declares the LORD.
Consider from this day onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day when the foundation of the temple of the LORD was laid. Consider:
Is there still seed in the barn? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not yet borne fruit. From this day on I will bless you."
The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am about to shake the heavens and the earth.

I will overturn the thrones of kingdoms and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots and their riders; horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his comrade.

On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declares the LORD, and I will make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of Armies.
In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet:
The LORD was very angry with your ancestors.
So say to them: This is what the LORD of Armies says: Return to me, declares the LORD of Armies, and I will return to you, says the LORD of Armies.

Do not be like your ancestors, to whom the earlier prophets proclaimed, "This is what the LORD of Armies says: Turn back from your evil ways and your evil deeds." But they did not listen or pay attention to me, declares the LORD.
Your ancestors, where are they now? And the prophets, do they live forever?

But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, did they not overtake your ancestors? Then they repented and said, "The LORD of Armies has dealt with us as he planned to do, according to our ways and our deeds."
On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, the month of Shebat, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, the prophet.
I saw in the night, and there was a man riding on a red horse! He was standing among the myrtle trees in the ravine, and behind him were red, sorrel and white horses.
I asked, "What are these, my lord?" The angel who was speaking with me said to me, "I will show you what they are."
Then the man who was standing among the myrtle trees answered, "These are the ones the LORD has sent to patrol the earth."
They answered the angel of the LORD who was standing among the myrtle trees, "We have patrolled the earth, and the whole earth is still and at rest."
Then the angel of the LORD said, "LORD of Armies, how long will you withhold your compassion from Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, with which you have been angry these seventy years?"
The LORD answered the angel who was speaking with me with kind and comforting words.
Then the angel who was speaking with me said to me, "Proclaim: 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am very jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion,
and I am very angry with the nations that are at ease. For I was only a little angry, but they made the disaster worse.

Therefore this is what the LORD says: I have returned to Jerusalem with compassion. My house will be rebuilt in it, declares the LORD of Armies, and a measuring line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.'
Proclaim again: 'This is what the LORD of Armies says: My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and the LORD will again comfort Zion and again choose Jerusalem.'"
Then I looked up and saw four horns.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these?" He said to me, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, Israel and Jerusalem."
Then the LORD showed me four craftsmen.

I asked, "What are these coming to do?" He said, "These are the horns that scattered Judah, so that no one could lift up his head. But these craftsmen have come to terrify them, to throw down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it."
Then I looked up and saw a man with a measuring line in his hand.
I asked, "Where are you going?" He said to me, "To measure Jerusalem, to see how wide it is and how long."
Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward, and another angel came out to meet him.
He said to him, "Run, tell that young man: 'Jerusalem will be inhabited like open villages without walls, because of the great number of people and animals in it.
And I myself will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD, and I will be the glory within it.'"
Come! Come! Flee from the land of the north, declares the LORD, for I have scattered you like the four winds of the heavens, declares the LORD.
Come, Zion! Escape, you who live with Daughter Babylon!
For this is what the LORD of Armies says, he who sent me after glory to the nations that plundered you: Whoever touches you touches the pupil of his eye.
For look, I am going to wave my hand against them, and they will become plunder for those who served them. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me.
Sing and rejoice, Daughter Zion, for look, I am coming, and I will live among you, declares the LORD.
Many nations will join themselves to the LORD on that day and become my people. I will live among you, and you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
The LORD will take possession of Judah as his portion in the holy land, and he will again choose Jerusalem.
Be silent, all humankind, before the LORD, for he has roused himself from his holy dwelling.
Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and the Accuser standing at his right hand to accuse him.
The LORD said to the Accuser, "The LORD rebuke you, Accuser! The LORD, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you! Is not this man a burning stick snatched from the fire?"
Now Joshua was dressed in filthy clothes as he stood before the angel.
The angel said to those who were standing before him, "Take the filthy clothes off him." And to Joshua he said, "See, I have taken your guilt away from you, and I will clothe you in festal robes."
Then I said, "Let them put a clean turban on his head." So they put a clean turban on his head and clothed him with garments, while the angel of the LORD stood by.
Then the angel of the LORD solemnly charged Joshua:

"This is what the LORD of Armies says: If you walk in my ways and keep my charge, then you will govern my house and have charge of my courts, and I will give you the right to come and go among these who are standing here.
Listen, Joshua the high priest, you and your colleagues who sit before you, for they are men who are a sign: I am going to bring my servant the Branch.

For look, the stone that I have set before Joshua: on one stone there are seven eyes. I am going to engrave an inscription on it, declares the LORD of Armies, and I will remove the guilt of this land in a single day.
On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, each of you will invite his neighbor to sit under his vine and under his fig tree."
Then the angel who was speaking with me came back and woke me, as someone is woken from sleep.
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a lampstand all of gold, with a bowl on top of it. It has seven lamps on it, with seven spouts for each of the lamps on top of it.
There are two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and the other on its left."
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
The angel who was speaking with me answered, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
Then he said to me, "This is the word of the LORD to Zerubbabel: Not by might and not by power, but by my Spirit, says the LORD of Armies.
What are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you will become a plain. He will bring out the top stone amid shouts of 'Grace, grace to it!'"
Then the word of the LORD came to me:
The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house, and his hands will complete it. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you.
For who has despised the day of small things? They will rejoice when they see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These seven are the eyes of the LORD, which range over the whole earth.
Then I asked him, "What are these two olive trees on the right and on the left of the lampstand?"
And a second time I asked him, "What are these two branches of the olive trees, beside the two gold pipes, which pour out the golden oil from themselves?"
He said to me, "Do you not know what these are?" I said, "No, my lord."
Then he said, "These are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of the whole earth."
Again I looked up, and I saw a flying scroll.
He asked me, "What do you see?" I said, "I see a flying scroll, twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

He said to me, "This is the curse that is going out over the whole land. For according to what is written on one side, every thief will be swept away, and according to what is written on the other side, everyone who swears falsely will be swept away.

I will send it out, declares the LORD of Armies, and it will enter the house of the thief and the house of the one who swears falsely by my name. It will stay inside his house and destroy it, both its timbers and its stones."
Then the angel who was speaking with me came forward and said to me, "Look up and see what this is that is going out."
I asked, "What is it?" He said, "This is the ephah basket that is going out." And he said, "This is their iniquity in all the land."
Then a round cover of lead was lifted, and there was a woman sitting inside the basket.
He said, "This is Wickedness." He thrust her back into the basket and pushed the lead weight down over its mouth.
Then I looked up and saw two women coming out, with the wind in their wings. They had wings like the wings of a stork, and they lifted up the basket between earth and heaven.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "Where are they taking the basket?"
He said to me, "To build a house for it in the land of Shinar. When the house is ready, the basket will be set down there on its stand."
Again I looked up, and I saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains, and the mountains were mountains of bronze.
The first chariot had red horses, the second chariot black horses,
the third chariot white horses, and the fourth chariot dappled horses, all of them strong.
I asked the angel who was speaking with me, "What are these, my lord?"
The angel answered me, "These are the four winds of heaven, going out after presenting themselves before the Lord of the whole earth.
The chariot with the black horses is going out toward the land of the north, the white ones have gone out after them, and the dappled ones have gone out toward the land of the south."
When the strong ones went out, they were eager to go and patrol the earth. He said, "Go, patrol the earth!" So they patrolled the earth.
Then he called to me and said to me, "Look, those going out toward the land of the north have given my Spirit rest in the land of the north."
The word of the LORD came to me:
Take an offering from the exiles, from Heldai, Tobijah and Jedaiah, who have come from Babylon. Go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
Take silver and gold and make crowns, and set the crown on the head of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest.
Say to him: This is what the LORD of Armies says: Here is a man whose name is the Branch. He will branch out from his place, and he will build the temple of the LORD.

It is he who will build the temple of the LORD. He will be clothed with majesty, and he will sit and rule on his throne. There will be a priest on his throne, and there will be a counsel of peace between the two of them.
The crown will be a memorial in the temple of the LORD for Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah and Hen son of Zephaniah.

Those who are far away will come and help to build the temple of the LORD. Then you will know that the LORD of Armies has sent me to you. This will happen if you carefully obey the voice of the LORD your God.
In the fourth year of King Darius, the word of the LORD came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Kislev.
Now the people of Bethel had sent Sharezer and Regem-melech and their men to seek the favor of the LORD,
and to ask the priests of the house of the LORD of Armies and the prophets, "Should I weep in the fifth month and abstain, as I have done for so many years?"
Then the word of the LORD of Armies came to me:
Say to all the people of the land and to the priests: When you fasted and mourned in the fifth month and in the seventh month for these seventy years, was it really for me that you fasted?
And when you eat and when you drink, are you not eating and drinking for yourselves?

Are not these the words that the LORD proclaimed through the earlier prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and at peace, with its towns around it, and when the Negev and the Shephelah were inhabited?
The word of the LORD came to Zechariah:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Judge with true justice; show faithful love and compassion to one another.
Do not oppress the widow or the fatherless, the foreigner or the poor, and do not plot evil against one another in your hearts.
But they refused to pay attention. They turned a stubborn shoulder and stopped their ears so as not to hear.

They made their hearts as hard as flint, so as not to hear the law and the words that the LORD of Armies had sent by his Spirit through the earlier prophets. So great anger came from the LORD of Armies.
Just as I called and they would not listen, so they called and I would not listen, says the LORD of Armies.
I scattered them with a storm among all the nations they had not known, and the land was left desolate behind them, with no one coming or going. So they made the pleasant land a desolation.
The word of the LORD of Armies came:
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am very jealous for Zion; I am jealous for her with great fury.

This is what the LORD says: I have returned to Zion, and I will live in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called the City of Faithfulness, and the mountain of the LORD of Armies the Holy Mountain.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Old men and old women will again sit in the squares of Jerusalem, each with a staff in hand because of great age.
And the squares of the city will be full of boys and girls playing there.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: If it seems too wonderful in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, must it also seem too wonderful in my eyes? declares the LORD of Armies.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: I am going to save my people from the land of the east and from the land of the setting sun.
I will bring them to live in the middle of Jerusalem. They will be my people, and I will be their God, in faithfulness and righteousness.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: Let your hands be strong, you who in these days are hearing these words from the mouth of the prophets who spoke on the day the foundation was laid for the house of the LORD of Armies, so that the temple might be built.
For before those days there were no wages for people or for animals, and no one who went out or came in was safe from the enemy, for I set everyone against his neighbor.
But now I will not treat the remnant of this people as in the former days, declares the LORD of Armies.

For there will be a sowing in peace: the vine will give its fruit, the earth will give its produce, and the heavens will give their dew. I will give the remnant of this people all these things to possess.
As you have been a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so I will save you, and you will be a blessing. Do not be afraid; let your hands be strong.
For this is what the LORD of Armies says: Just as I planned to bring disaster on you when your ancestors made me angry, says the LORD of Armies, and I did not relent,
so now in these days I have again planned to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Do not be afraid.
These are the things you are to do: Speak the truth to one another; in your gates give judgments that are true and make for peace.
Do not plot evil against one another in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for all these are things that I hate, declares the LORD.
The word of the LORD of Armies came to me:

This is what the LORD of Armies says: The fasts of the fourth month, the fifth, the seventh and the tenth will become times of joy and gladness and cheerful festivals for the house of Judah. So love truth and peace.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: Peoples will yet come, the inhabitants of many cities.
The inhabitants of one city will go to another and say, "Let us go at once to seek the favor of the LORD and to seek the LORD of Armies. I am going too."
Many peoples and strong nations will come to seek the LORD of Armies in Jerusalem and to seek the favor of the LORD.

This is what the LORD of Armies says: In those days ten men from nations of every language will take hold, they will take hold of the hem of a Jew and say, "Let us go with you, for we have heard that God is with you."
An oracle. The word of the LORD is against the land of Hadrach, and Damascus is where it comes to rest. For the eyes of humankind and of all the tribes of Israel are on the LORD.
It is against Hamath too, which borders on it, and against Tyre and Sidon, though they are very wise.
Tyre has built herself a fortress and heaped up silver like dust and gold like the mud of the streets.
But look, the Lord will take possession of her and strike down her power on the sea, and she will be devoured by fire.
Ashkelon will see it and be afraid; Gaza too will writhe in anguish, and Ekron, for her hope will be put to shame. Gaza will lose her king, and Ashkelon will be uninhabited.
A people of mixed race will live in Ashdod, and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
I will take the blood out of his mouth and the detestable food from between his teeth. He too will be a remnant for our God. He will be like a clan in Judah, and Ekron like the Jebusites.
I will camp around my house as a guard, against those who march back and forth. No oppressor will overrun them again, for now I have seen with my own eyes.
Rejoice greatly, Daughter Zion! Shout, Daughter Jerusalem! Look, your king is coming to you, righteous and victorious, humble and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.

I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim and the war horse from Jerusalem, and the battle bow will be cut off. He will proclaim peace to the nations. His rule will be from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth.
As for you, because of the blood of my covenant with you, I will set your prisoners free from the waterless pit.
Return to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope. Even today I declare that I will give back to you double.
For I will bend Judah as my bow; I will fill it with Ephraim as its arrow. I will rouse your sons, Zion, against your sons, Greece, and make you like a warrior's sword.
Then the LORD will appear over them, and his arrow will flash like lightning. The Lord GOD will blow the ram's horn and march out in the storms of the south.
The LORD of Armies will shield them. They will devour and trample the sling stones; they will drink and roar as if with wine. They will be full like a bowl, like the corners of the altar.
On that day the LORD their God will save them, as the flock of his people. For like the jewels of a crown they will sparkle over his land.
How good and how beautiful it will be! Grain will make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women.
Ask the LORD for rain in the season of the spring rain. It is the LORD who makes the storm clouds, and he will give them showers of rain, and plants in the field for everyone.
For the household gods speak nonsense, and the diviners see lies. They tell false dreams and give empty comfort. So the people wander like sheep; they suffer for lack of a shepherd.
My anger burns against the shepherds, and I will punish the leaders. For the LORD of Armies cares for his flock, the house of Judah, and he will make them like his majestic horse in battle.
From Judah will come the cornerstone, from Judah the tent peg, from Judah the battle bow, from Judah every ruler, all together.
They will be like warriors trampling the enemy into the mud of the streets in battle. They will fight, because the LORD is with them, and they will put the horsemen to shame.

I will strengthen the house of Judah and save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back because I have compassion on them, and they will be as though I had never rejected them. For I am the LORD their God, and I will answer them.
Ephraim will be like a warrior, and their hearts will be glad as with wine. Their children will see it and be glad; their hearts will rejoice in the LORD.
I will whistle for them and gather them in, for I have redeemed them, and they will be as many as they were before.
Though I scattered them like seed among the peoples, in far countries they will remember me. They and their children will live, and they will return.
I will bring them back from the land of Egypt and gather them from Assyria. I will bring them to the land of Gilead and to Lebanon, until there is no room left for them.
He will pass through the sea of distress and strike the waves of the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up. The pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
I will strengthen them in the LORD, and they will walk in his name, declares the LORD.
Open your doors, Lebanon, so that fire may devour your cedars!
Wail, you cypress, for the cedar has fallen, for the mighty trees are ruined! Wail, you oaks of Bashan, for the dense forest has come down!
Listen! The wailing of the shepherds, for their glory is ruined! Listen! The roaring of young lions, for the thickets of the Jordan are ruined!
This is what the LORD my God said: "Shepherd the flock marked for slaughter.
Those who buy them kill them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, 'Blessed be the LORD, for I am rich!' And their own shepherds have no pity on them.

For I will no longer have pity on the people of the land, declares the LORD. Look, I am going to hand over everyone to his neighbor and to his king. They will crush the land, and I will not rescue anyone from their hand."
So I shepherded the flock marked for slaughter, the most afflicted of the flock. I took two staffs. One I called Favor and the other I called Union, and I shepherded the flock.
In one month I got rid of the three shepherds. I lost patience with them, and they also detested me.
Then I said, "I will not be your shepherd. Let the dying die, and let the perishing perish, and let those who are left devour one another's flesh."
Then I took my staff Favor and broke it, to revoke the covenant I had made with all the peoples.
So it was revoked on that day, and the afflicted of the flock, who were watching me, knew that it was the word of the LORD.
Then I said to them, "If it seems good to you, give me my wages; if not, keep them." So they weighed out my wages, thirty pieces of silver.
Then the LORD said to me, "Throw it to the potter, that magnificent price at which they valued me!" So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the house of the LORD, to the potter.
Then I broke my second staff, Union, to revoke the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.
Then the LORD said to me, "Take once more the equipment of a foolish shepherd.

For look, I am going to raise up a shepherd in the land who will not care for those that are perishing or seek the young or heal the injured or feed the healthy, but will eat the flesh of the fat ones and tear off their hooves.
Woe to my worthless shepherd, who abandons the flock! May the sword strike his arm and his right eye! May his arm wither completely, and his right eye go totally blind!"
An oracle. The word of the LORD concerning Israel. Declares the LORD, who stretches out the heavens, lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the human spirit within a person:
Look, I am going to make Jerusalem a cup that makes all the surrounding peoples reel. Judah too will be under siege, as Jerusalem is.
On that day I will make Jerusalem a heavy stone for all the peoples. All who lift it will be badly injured, and all the nations of the earth will gather against her.

On that day, declares the LORD, I will strike every horse with panic and its rider with madness. But I will keep my eyes open over the house of Judah, when I strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.
Then the clans of Judah will say in their hearts, "The people who live in Jerusalem are our strength, through the LORD of Armies, their God."

On that day I will make the clans of Judah like a fire pot in a pile of wood, like a flaming torch among sheaves. They will devour all the surrounding peoples, right and left, while Jerusalem will remain in its place, in Jerusalem.
The LORD will save the tents of Judah first, so that the glory of the house of David and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem will not be raised above Judah.

On that day the LORD will shield the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the feeblest among them on that day will be like David, and the house of David will be like God, like the angel of the LORD going before them.
On that day I will set out to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.

I will pour out on the house of David and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem a spirit of grace and of pleading. They will look on me, the one they have pierced, and they will mourn for him as one mourns for an only child, and weep bitterly over him as one weeps over a firstborn.
On that day the mourning in Jerusalem will be as great as the mourning for Hadad-rimmon in the plain of Megiddo.
The land will mourn, each clan by itself: the clan of the house of David by itself and their wives by themselves; the clan of the house of Nathan by itself and their wives by themselves;
the clan of the house of Levi by itself and their wives by themselves; the clan of the Shimeites by itself and their wives by themselves;
and all the clans that are left, each clan by itself and their wives by themselves.
On that day a fountain will be opened for the house of David and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, to cleanse them from sin and impurity.

On that day, declares the LORD of Armies, I will cut off the names of the idols from the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also remove from the land the prophets and the spirit of impurity.

If anyone still prophesies, his father and mother who bore him will say to him, "You will not live, for you have spoken lies in the name of the LORD." And his father and mother who bore him will pierce him when he prophesies.
On that day every prophet will be ashamed of his vision when he prophesies. He will not put on a hairy cloak in order to deceive.
He will say, "I am not a prophet. I am a man who works the soil, for the land has been my livelihood since my youth."
And if someone asks him, "What are these wounds on your chest?" he will say, "I was wounded in the house of my friends."

Awake, sword, against my shepherd, against the man who stands next to me, declares the LORD of Armies. Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered, and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
In the whole land, declares the LORD, two thirds will be cut off and die, and a third will be left in it.

I will bring this third into the fire. I will refine them as silver is refined and test them as gold is tested. They will call on my name, and I will answer them. I will say, "They are my people," and they will say, "The LORD is my God."
Look, a day is coming for the LORD, when the plunder taken from you will be divided in your midst.

For I will gather all the nations against Jerusalem for battle. The city will be captured, the houses plundered and the women raped. Half of the city will go into exile, but the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city.
Then the LORD will go out and fight against those nations, as he fights on a day of battle.

On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, which lies east of Jerusalem, and the Mount of Olives will be split in two from east to west by a very wide valley. Half of the mountain will move north, and half of it south.

You will flee by the valley of my mountains, for the valley of the mountains will reach as far as Azel. You will flee as you fled from the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. Then the LORD my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.
On that day there will be no light, neither brightness nor frost.
It will be one unbroken day, known to the LORD, neither day nor night, and at evening time there will be light.
On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem, half of it to the eastern sea and half of it to the western sea. It will flow in summer and in winter.
The LORD will be king over all the earth. On that day the LORD will be one, and his name one.

The whole land will be changed into a plain like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon, south of Jerusalem. But Jerusalem will be raised up and will remain in its place, from the Benjamin Gate to the place of the First Gate and to the Corner Gate, and from the Tower of Hananel to the king's winepresses.
People will live in it, and there will never again be a curse of destruction. Jerusalem will live in security.

This will be the plague with which the LORD will strike all the peoples who have made war on Jerusalem: their flesh will rot while they are still standing on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.
On that day a great panic from the LORD will fall on them. Each will seize the hand of his neighbor, and they will raise their hands against each other.
Judah too will fight at Jerusalem. The wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered: gold, silver and clothing in great abundance.
A plague like this will also strike the horses, the mules, the camels, the donkeys and all the animals in those camps.
Then all who are left of all the nations that came against Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, and to celebrate the Festival of Booths.
If any of the clans of the earth do not go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, the LORD of Armies, there will be no rain on them.
